title: Alliance Contribution Rating in Contention of Relics: What the Ranking Actually Tells You
summary: The Alliance Contribution Rating in Contention of Relics is one of those Infinity Kingdom statistics that looks more straightforward than it really is.
markdown:
## Introduction

The **Alliance Contribution Rating** in Contention of Relics is one of those Infinity Kingdom statistics that looks more straightforward than it really is.

Open the alliance ranking and every member has a number beside their name. Naturally, players tend to read the list as a performance ranking: first place contributed the most, second place contributed the second most, and so on. That interpretation needs some context - especially for players managing an alliance and who are deciding what players to award the big CoR reward bundles!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-148-1024x443.png)

Contribution Rating is useful for measuring **activity during CoR**, but different activities can generate contribution points while having very different effects on the alliance's actual objectives. One of the clearest examples is **Chaos Beast farming**.

A player can accumulate substantial Contribution Rating by repeatedly killing Chaos Beasts for personal Valor Marks. Meanwhile, another player may spend much of CoR gathering Energy Nodes, attending Relic sieges, fighting around objectives, or helping with the World Heart.

The important principle is:

> **Alliance Contribution Rating measures contribution points earned. It should not automatically be treated as a ranking of who contributed most toward winning CoR.**

Understanding that distinction is particularly important for R4 and R5 players deciding how alliance rewards should be distributed.

---

## What Is Alliance Contribution Rating?

During Contention of Relics, participating players accumulate **Contribution Rating** from various event activities.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-147-1024x305.png)

The resulting ranking is visible from the alliance interface and provides an easy overview of member activity. There is nothing inherently wrong with using this ranking.

A player sitting at 10,000+ Contribution Rating has clearly been doing CoR activities. Someone sitting at zero clearly has not.

The problem appears when we try to infer **what kind of contribution produced those points**.

Not every contribution point represents the same strategic value.

---

## Chaos Beasts Generate a Lot of Contribution Rating

Chaos Beasts provide the easiest example.

Based on current in-game testing, defeating Chaos Beasts awards:

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-146-1024x141.png)

Level 3 farming adds up particularly quickly.

Ten kills produce **1,590 Contribution Rating**.

Twenty produce **3,180**.

Thirty produce **4,770**.

Forty produce **6,360**.

At 159 points per kill, roughly 76 Level 3 Chaos Beast kills would generate just over **12,000 Contribution Rating**.

This does **not** mean that someone with 12,000 rating killed 76 Chaos Beasts. Contribution Rating comes from multiple CoR activities.

It demonstrates why the final number cannot tell us how that player spent their time.

---

## Why Players Farm Chaos Beasts

There is a perfectly good reason to kill them: **Valor Marks**.

Valor Marks are used to purchase items from the CoR Mystery Shop. The game identifies several ways of earning them, including defeating Chaos Beasts, capturing Energy Nodes, fighting enemy Lords, and rewards connected to Relics and the World Heart.

For individual progression, Chaos Beast farming is therefore useful.

If the battlefield is quiet and your alliance does not need your march somewhere else, there is little reason to leave it idle. Farming Chaos Beasts turns that downtime into additional Valor Marks.

The distinction is between **personal value** and **alliance value**.

A Chaos Beast farmer receives personal Valor Marks while also generating Contribution Rating.

An Energy Node player is helping generate Energy Cubes.

A siege player may be spending troops and healing speedups so the alliance can capture or retain a Relic.

All three can increase their Contribution Rating, but their effect on the wider CoR campaign is not identical.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-145-1024x523.png)

---

## Contribution Rating Is Best Treated as an Activity Indicator

This is how I have found the ranking most useful in practice.

**Contribution Rating answers:**
*"Has this player been active in CoR?"*

It is much worse at answering:
*"How important was this player to our alliance's CoR performance?"*

At the extremes, the leaderboard remains informative. A player with zero rating has obviously done little or nothing that generates contribution. A player with a very high score has clearly invested time into event activities. The ambiguity lies between active players.

Suppose Player A has **8,000 Contribution Rating** and Player B has **5,000**.

The ranking tells us that Player A accumulated 3,000 more contribution points. It does not tell us that Player A was 60% more useful to the alliance.

Player A may have spent substantial time farming Chaos Beasts. Player B may have been occupying Energy Nodes and immediately moving whenever leadership called for a siege.

Without knowing the activities behind the numbers, the comparison is incomplete.

---

## Energy Cubes Are the More Important Strategic Context

The reason this distinction matters is that **Contention of Relics is ultimately decided around Energy Cubes and objective control**.

The in-game rules state that kingdoms are ranked according to the Energy Cubes they obtain during CoR. Relics, the World Heart, and Energy Nodes are therefore not merely alternative ways to increase a personal statistic; they feed into the wider competition.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-149-1024x407.png)

Energy Cubes also matter at the alliance level because reaching specific thresholds produces enormous pools of Valor Marks.

The current thresholds shown in-game are:

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-150-1024x388.png)

These numbers provide much better context for evaluating certain kinds of participation.

A player who helps push an alliance across the **200,000 Energy Cube threshold**, for example, is helping move its Valor Mark pool from 1.5 million to **2.2 million**.

Reaching 300,000 increases the pool to **3.6 million Valor Marks**.

That contribution benefits the alliance as a whole.

---

## Contribution Rating and Reward Distribution

Contribution Rating is useful, but I would never distribute CoR rewards purely from the leaderboard. It tells you that someone was active; it does not tell you how useful that activity was to the alliance.

When distributing Valor Marks, I care more about who **showed up for Relic and World Heart sieges, collected Energy Nodes, completed alliance objectives, and responded when help was needed**. Roles matter too. A strong PvP player may spend most of CoR clearing enemies rather than gathering, while a smaller account can contribute far more by consistently collecting nodes. Both are doing useful work.

Chaos Beasts are where the leaderboard gets deceptive. Farming them is perfectly worthwhile during downtime because you earn personal Valor Marks and Contribution Rating at the same time. However, someone farming Level 3 Beasts for hours can end up above a player who spent the event gathering cubes and burning troops at sieges. I would not automatically give the Beast farmer a larger share of the alliance Valor pool just because the final number is higher. They have already been earning personal Valor from that farming, while the other player was helping create the alliance reward being distributed.

This is also why I dislike rigid systems where Rank 1 gets the most, Rank 2 gets the second-most, and so on. Players quickly figure out what produces Contribution Rating efficiently and optimize around it. You can unintentionally encourage people to farm Beasts while the alliance actually needs marches on nodes or objectives. **Reward the activity you want people to repeat next CoR.**

You do not need a spreadsheet tracking every march to accomplish that. R4s and R5s generally know who attended sieges, who consistently gathered nodes, and who answered calls. Use Contribution Rating as supporting information rather than the final verdict, and make the reward criteria clear before CoR starts.

None of this means players should stop farming Chaos Beasts. I farm them whenever objectives are covered and there is nothing more useful for my march to be doing. The problem is only when personal Valor farming takes priority over alliance objectives.

There is another layer to all of this because the alliance Valor rewards scale with Energy Cubes: **400,000 Valor at 10,000 cubes, 900,000 at 50,000, 1.5 million at 100,000, 2.2 million at 200,000, and 3.6 million at 300,000**. An organized kingdom can actually exploit those thresholds by splitting active players between farm alliances, pushing several alliances through efficient cube milestones, banking the Valor, and moving players around for distribution.

That gets considerably more complicated, though. **It is probably a guide of its own.** Stay tuned!

---

## Conclusion

Contribution Rating is best treated as a rough measure of CoR activity, not a final judgment of who contributed the most. Chaos Beasts alone can generate thousands of points while mainly rewarding the player with personal Valor Marks, so the number needs context.

For alliance rewards, look at what players actually did: **who collected nodes, attended sieges, completed alliance objectives, fought when needed, and helped generate the Energy Cubes behind the alliance's Valor pool**.

And keep farming Chaos Beasts. They are good value whenever there is downtime. Just don't mistake a high Contribution Rating from Beast farming for the same thing as helping the alliance win CoR.

**Use the leaderboard as a reference, not the reward sheet.**

---

markdown:
Alliance technology is a crucial aspect of Infinity Kingdom that can significantly increase the power and development of an alliance. By investing in the right technology, alliances can gain important buffs and upgrades that can help them in both growth and war aspects of the game. In this article, we will provide you with a tier list of the most important growth technologies that alliances should prioritize.

**Having rapid tech development in a new alliance on new servers is absolutely crucial and all members should be encourage to gem alliance technology daily. For new alliances gemming is cheap and should be done by everyone to get a nice boost at the beginning of a new server/alliance.**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/image-12.png)

## Technology tiers

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-142-1024x411.png)

### S Tier:

The top tier of growth technologies includes Big Family, Brothers-In-Arms, AP Recovery, Rapid March, Lower Attack Cost, Knife Through Butter, and Garrison Attack. These technologies are essential for any alliance looking to grow quickly and effectively.

**Big Family**: This technology increases the maximum number of alliance members, allowing for a larger pool of players to help with development and defense.

**Brothers-In-Arms**: This technology increases the speed at which alliance members can help each other. This is particularly important for speeding up construction and research tasks.

**AP Recovery**: This technology increases the speed at which alliance members can recover their action points, allowing for more tasks to be completed each day.

**Rapid March**: This technology increases the marching speed of alliance members, making it easier to move troops around the map and respond to threats quickly.

**Lower Attack Cost**: This technology reduces the amount of attack resources required to attack other players, making it easier to launch attacks and gain resources.

**Knife Through Butter**: This technology increases the damage dealt by troops to enemy walls, making it easier to penetrate enemy defenses.

**Garrison Attack**: This technology increases the damage dealt by troops defending a garrison, making it harder for enemies to capture your buildings.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-143-1024x436.png)

### A tier:

The second tier of growth technologies includes Wall Breaker, Quick Response, Assembly Charge, and Bowmen Load. These technologies are also important for alliance growth, but not as essential as those in the S tier.

**Wall Breaker**: This technology increases the damage dealt by troops to enemy walls, making it easier to penetrate city defenses.

**Quick Response**: This technology reduces the time it takes for troops to return to the city after an attack or defense, allowing for quicker recovery and response times.

**Assembly Charge**: This technology increases the marching speed of troops, making it easier to move troops around the map and respond to threats quickly.

**Bowmen Load**: This technology increases the number of resources bowmen can carry. Since we are running two bowmen in every march you get double value from this load tech.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-144-1024x488.png)

### B tier:

The third tier of growth technologies includes SP Recovery, Iron, Food, Wood, Stone Gatherer, Shieldmen Load, Spearmen Load, and Cavalry Load. These technologies are helpful for alliance growth, but not as essential as those in the S and A tiers.

**SP Recovery**: This technology increases the speed at which SP are recovered, allowing for more Well of Time raids to be completed each day.

**Resource Gatherer:** These technologies increase the amount of resources gathered from resource nodes, making it easier to accumulate resources for development.

**Shieldmen Load, Spearmen Load, and Cavalry Load**: These technologies increase the carrying capacity of different types of troops, allowing for more resources to be gathered or more troops to be deployed.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-145-1024x475.png)

### C tier:

The fourth tier of growth technologies includes Iron, Food, Wood, and Stone Tax, Lower Garrison Cost, and Fast Garrison. These technologies are not as important as those in the S, A, and B tiers, but can still be useful for alliance growth.

**Iron, Food, Wood, and Stone Tax**: These technologies increase the amount of resources gained from taxes, providing a small boost to overall resource accumulation.

**Lower Garrison Cost**: This technology reduces the resources required to place troops in a friendly players garrison.

**Fast Garrison**: This technology increases the speed at which troops are garrisoned. It is a nice quality-of-life improvement, but not a top priority.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-146-1024x478.png)

### F tier:

**Fortification Damage**: This technology increases the damage dealt by your alliance's structures when defending against enemy attacks. While it may seem useful, it is not a high priority. It is better to focus on improving the power of your troops through other technologies.

**Win the Peace**: This technology provides a small increase city shields after a siege. It is not a high priority, and should only be invested in if there are no other more important technologies left to research.

**Guard the Peace**: This technology provides a small increase in the rewards gained from defending a city siege. It is also not a high priority, and should only be invested in if there are no other more important technologies left to research.

## Conclusion

In conclusion, investing in the right Alliance Development Technology is crucial for both the growth and success of your alliance in Infinity Kingdom. By prioritizing the S and A tiers, your alliance will see significant improvements in various areas, including troop power, resource management, and battle effectiveness. It is important to communicate with your alliance members and come up with a plan for which technologies to prioritize based on your alliance's specific needs and goals. With the right strategy, your alliance can become a force to be reckoned with in the world of Infinity Kingdom.

Infinity Kingdom is a popular game where players build and manage their kingdoms. A big part of the game is forming alliances with other players and working together towards common goals. One of the most important aspects of alliance management is upgrading alliance technology. In this article, we'll provide a guide on how to progress alliance technology in the most effective way.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-124.png)

**There are two main types of alliances in Infinity Kingdom, each with different end goals: Main alliances and Alt alliances**. The first type is a main alliance, which needs as much combat power as possible. The second type is an "alt-alliance" focused on resource farming. We'll provide separate guides for each type.

## Guide for Main Alliances

The first step towards progress for a main alliance is to unlock and upgrade the Alliance Core tech: Big Family. This will allow you to fill more members into the alliance and upgrade alliance technology faster. The alliance leader and members should work together to donate resources towards upgrading the Alliance technology.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-122.png)

Once the Alliance tech Big Family is upgraded, the focus should be on upgrading alliance troop technology. The goal is to improve the combat power of the alliance, which will come in handy during battles. The troop technology that should be prioritized are bowmen, shieldmen, and cavalry.

**Bowmen should be the first priority** as they are used by two immortal types in any army. Shieldmen and cavalry are the next most commonly used troops and should be the focus after bowmen.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-126-1024x435.png)

In addition to troop technology, main alliances also need vast territory and continuously upgrading Big Family for more members. It's important to unlock and upgrade alliance core tech that increase territory and roster. This allows the alliance to expand its territory and collect more resources. The alliance leader should also recruit new members and work on increasing the overall power of the alliance.

### We recommend progressing in two stages:

Stage 1: Focus on upgrading the Alliance **core**and unlocking all alliance territories and the full roster size. Donate resources towards upgrading the Alliance.

Stage 2: Focus on upgrading **troop**technology, starting with bowmen, then shieldmen and cavalry.

## Guide for Alt-Alliances

The focus of an alt-alliance is on farming resources. Unlike main alliances, alt-alliances do not need as much combat power. Instead, the focus should be on upgrading resource collection. The first step is to unlock and upgrade the Alliance core tech.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-127.png)

Once the Alliance Center is upgraded, the focus should be on upgrading alliance technology that increases resource collection. The two most important technology upgrades for alt-alliances are Tax Collection and Player Resource Node Collection. Tax Collection allows the alliance to collect taxes from members' kingdoms, while Player Resource Node Collection allows alliance members to collect resources from each other's resource nodes.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-128-1024x134.png)

In addition to upgrading resource collection technology, alt-alliances should focus on increasing the number of resource nodes owned by alliance members. This can be done by upgrading the Resource Node structure and by recruiting members who have a lot of resource nodes.

### We recommend progressing in three stages:

Stage 1: Focus on upgrading the Alliance core tech and unlocking all alliance roster slots. Donate resources towards upgrading the Alliance and get Vast Territory and Big Family asap.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-131.png)

Stage 2: Focus on upgrading Tax Collection and Player Resource Node Collection. Upgrade the Resource Node structure to increase the number of resource nodes owned by alliance members.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-129-1024x450.png)

Stage 3: Continue upgrading resource collection technology and alliance structures. Work on recruiting members who have a lot of resource nodes.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-130-1024x486.png)

## Rewards as an Alliance member

### 1. Earn Alliance Coins by participating in Alliance activities, upgrading cities, and donating daily.

These coins can be used to purchase Immortal Fragments (build new Immortals or turn it into a stream of [Purple Crystals](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/combat/passives/purple-crystal-maximum-efficiency-2/))

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/image-20.png)

You can also spend your alliance coins on other highly usefull rewards like Space Portals, Territorial Teleports, Random Teleports, Protection Barriers (bubbels), Contract Builders and Speedups.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/image-21-1024x367.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/image-22-1024x366.png)

### 2. Buffs and more buffs

**Alliance technology**offers insanely strong buffs to all its members. **Defense**, **Attack**and **HP**upgrades boosts your troops by up to 20% each!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/121231231-1024x336.png)

### 3. Positions and Cities Boosts

Cities provide very strong buffs to alliance members.

- You can get strong development buffs to Dragon Upgrade speed, Building speed, Technology Reseach speed, Healing speed, etc.
- You can also get powerful combat buffs to increase the damage of your troops, Immortals, or boost their defenses.

These buffs are crucial to any alliance that wishes to compete. Moreover, it gives members of strong alliances a big boost in power and the ability to deal more easily with rogue players.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/image-24-1024x485.png)

### 4. Rallying

You and your alliance allies can rally against a particular powerful foe. By rallying you setup a bombardment of attacks (capped at 5 for each rally) against your enemy. Each march in the rally will hit right after each other.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/image-25-1024x565.png)

This is how smaller players are able to defeat stronger whales - and how a bunch of smaller whales are able to kill even the biggest whales of the game!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/image-26.png)

markdown:
### Alliance Supremacy Event Guide

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-52-1024x554.png)

Alliance Supremacy is one of those cross-server competition modes where your whole alliance gets to show what it’s really made of. Instead of live fighting or frantic troop swaps, this mode is about preparation, simple force of power and lineup strength, but also a bit of strategy as to how well your alliance can coordinate across three lanes. If you’ve ever wanted to see what 20 stacked marches in a rally looks like, this is it.

It runs in a league format, starting with a group stage and finishing in elimination rounds, and the rewards scale pretty nicely depending on which battlegroup you’re in (Season 1, Season 2, or Conquest/Legendary).

---

## Event Format

The whole competition is split into a multi-stage tournament:

### General Structure

- **48 alliances** enter each battlegroup.
- The flow goes:
**Regular Season → Round of 16 → Quarterfinals → Semifinals → Finals.**
- All battles are scheduled matches, not free-for-all fights.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-54-1024x698.png)

### Battlegroups

There are essentially **three separate battlegroups**:

1. **Season 1** – Top 48 alliances of that season.
2. **Season 2** – Another completely separate bracket of 48 alliances.
3. **Conquest & Legendary servers** – Top 48 alliances from these advanced server eras.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-53-1024x568.png)

All of these run the same event, but each battlegroup has its own progression and reward structure.

---

## Regular Season Breakdown

The Regular Season lasts **5 days**, and this part is basically a group stage.

- **48 alliances** are divided into **8 groups of 6**.
- Each group plays **three matches per day**.
- Alliances earn points based on match victories.
- After the 5-day grind, the **top 16 alliances** (by points) advance to the knockout stage.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-55-1024x183.png)

It’s fast-paced — you’re basically playing at the same three times every day — but since the fighting isn’t live, the pressure is more about getting your setups right.

---

## Gameplay Mechanics

Alliance Supremacy uses **pre-battle deployment**, not manual combat. Once the match starts, you just watch the lanes play out.

### Team Limits & Lanes

- Every participating member can set **up to 2 marches**.
- The battlefield has **3 lanes**: Upper, Mid, Lower.
- **Each lane can host 20 marches**, so in a full alliance, you’ll be cherry-picking the strongest.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-57-1024x649.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-58-1024x590.png)

Most alliances will mix and match lanes depending on enemy strengths, but high-end alliances usually coordinate heavily to stack their best 60 marches cleanly. **Once you are done with the days preperation those marches will stay in the lane for the fights of the day.**

### Battle Resolution

- Battles are fully automatic.
- A march that wins continues fighting in relay style, but **each march can win a maximum of 5 consecutive battles**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-62-1024x600.png)

- Each lane fight closely resembles two large rallies going against each other. Winning **2 out of the 3 lanes** wins the match.
- The fights basically look like three mega-rallies happening at once.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-59-1024x609.png)

### Match Times

Matches run at fixed daily slots:

- **13:01–13:30 UTC**
- **14:01–14:30 UTC**
- **15:01–15:30 UTC**

You don’t need to be online, but you *do* need your marches set before the match starts.

### Scouting Your Opponent

During prep time, you can inspect enemy lineups:

- Just click the **Inspect** icon.
- You’ll see their marches ranked by **STP**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-60.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-61-1024x576.png)

---

## Strategy Tips

This mode rewards alliances that coordinate rather than just throw random teams in lanes.

- **Lane stacking matters**, especially in knockout rounds. By that I mean that alliances should not have just anyone sending any march, small second marches will NOT win. Coordination matter!
Alliances should group their **top 60 marches** and decide which two lanes they want to fully control.
- **Securing two lanes is all that matters.**
Sometimes having a “sacrifice lane” is deliberate — it lets you put all main marches into two lanes for guaranteed wins.

---

## Rewards

Rewards follow the same logic across battlegroups, but the contents scale higher in later server eras.

Every match gives:

- **Single Victory Reward** – Only given when your alliance wins that match.
- **Placement Rewards** – Paid out at the end of the whole event based on your final ranking.
- *Only members who actually participate in the match get rewards.*

---

## Single Victory Rewards

### Season 1 , season 2 and Conquest battlegroups all have the same single victory rewards:

- **12 random Immortal Fragments** per victory.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-63-1024x206.png)

Note again, only for participating members of the alliance.

---

## Placement Rewards

### Season 1 Rewards

- **1st:** 240 random Immortal Fragments + 240 Stardust
- **2nd:** 180 frags + 180 Stardust
- **3rd:** 120 frags + 150 Stardust
- **Top 4:** 90 frags + 120 Stardust
- **Top 8:** 75 frags + 90 Stardust
- **Top 16:** 60 frags + 60 Stardust

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-64-1024x461.png)

---

### Season 2 Rewards

**Holy/Shadow fragments** are added starting in Season 2.

- **1st:** 90 Holy/Shadow + 180 frags + 240 Stardust
- **2nd:** 75 Holy/Shadow + 150 frags + 180 Stardust
- **3rd:** 60 Holy/Shadow + 120 frags + 150 Stardust
- **Top 4:** 45 Holy/Shadow + 90 frags + 120 Stardust
- **Top 8:** 30 Holy/Shadow + 75 frags + 90 Stardust
- **Top 16:** 15 Holy/Shadow + 60 frags + 60 Stardust

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-66-1024x579.png)

---

### Conquest & Legendary Rewards

Same as Season 2 but with **Chaos Immortal** fragments added.

- **1st:** 60 Chaos + 90 Holy/Shadow + 180 frags + 240 Stardust
- **2nd:** 45 Chaos + 75 Holy/Shadow + 150 frags + 180 Stardust
- **3rd:** 30 Chaos + 60 Holy/Shadow + 120 frags + 150 Stardust
- **Top 4:** 25 Chaos + 45 Holy/Shadow + 90 frags + 120 Stardust
- **Top 8:** 20 Chaos + 30 Holy/Shadow + 75 frags + 90 Stardust
- **Top 16:** 15 Chaos + 15 Holy/Shadow + 60 frags + 60 Stardust

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-65-1024x473.png)

---

## Player Perspective

There are some interesting aspects to this event as to alliance coordination of who sends what where and the rewards - especially in conquest - is quite nice! That being said, the event being fully automated and without interaction was a bit of let down for me personally. Others may prefer this type of auto-play in their mobile games, as it dosent require you to coordinate a lot of online players at the same time. But for me personally, I had hopes for a MOBA-style battleground, think MOBA (Dota, League of Legends, etc.) meets IBL. However, its not so bad. Its one more thing for players to do and pay interest too which is almost always good.

---

title: Alliance War Technology Priority (tiered)
summary: Alliance Technology is a key aspect of Infinity Kingdom, and the War Technology section is no exception. Having the right technology in your alliance can make a huge difference in combat, providing crucial buffs that…
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-147-1024x479.png)

Alliance Technology is a key aspect of Infinity Kingdom, and the War Technology section is no exception. Having the right technology in your alliance can make a huge difference in combat, providing crucial buffs that increase your power significantly and improve the chances of victory. In this article, we will take a closer look at the War Technology tier list, and provide some tips on how you can invest in the right technology to make your alliance a force to be reckoned with on the battlefield.

## S-Tier:

**Bowmen Attack and HP**: These technologies provide a significant boost to your Bowmen, which are one of the most important units in the game. A strong Bowmen unit can easily decimate enemy armies, making this technology a must-have for any alliance that wants to dominate in combat. This is the only S-tier war technology simply because you always run two bowmen Immortals in any army composition.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-148.png)

## A-Tier:

**Cavalry and Shieldmen Attack and HP:** These technologies are similar to Bowmen Attack and HP, but for Cavalry and Shieldmen instead. Cavalry and Shieldmen are also essential units in any army, and these technologies will help them deal more damage and last longer in combat.

**Bowmen Defense**: While offense is important, defense is equally important in any battle. Bowmen Defense technology will help your Bowmen units survive enemy attacks and deal damage in return.

**Cavalry and Shieldmen Defense:** Like Bowmen Defense, this technology provides a boost to your cavalry and shieldmen units, making them more resilient in battle.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-149-1024x428.png)

## B-Tier:

**Home Turf**: This technology provides a significant increase to the power of your Immortals when defending your own city. This is a great technology to have when you are under attack, as it can help you fend off enemy armies more easily.

**Fight Side by Side**: This technology provides a buff to your troops when fighting alongside allies, making it a must-have for any alliance that wants to dominate in team battles.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-150-1024x431.png)

## C-Tier:

**Spearmen HP, Attack, and Defense:** Spearmen are not as commonly used as Bowmen, Cavalry, and Shieldmen, so these technologies are not as important as others. However, if your alliance relies heavily on spearmen Immortals, then investing in these technologies may be worthwhile.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-151-1024x186.png)

## F-Tier:

**Quick Response:** This technology provides a significant boost to the speed of your marches, which can be incredibly useful for both attacking and defending.

**Assembly Charge**: This technology increases the damage dealt by your troops when they charge into battle, making it a great choice for aggressive alliances.

**Garrison Defense**: This technology provides a significant boost to your Immortals when defending your city's garrison, making it easier to fend off enemy attacks.

**Minimize Losses**: This technology reduces the amount of troops lost in battle, which can be a lifesaver if you are struggling to maintain your army's numbers.

**Wall Durability**: This technology increases the durability of your city walls, making it harder for enemies to breach them and attack your city.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-152-1024x388.png)

Overall, investing in the right War Technology is essential for any alliance that wants to be successful in combat. By prioritizing the right technologies, you can make your troops more powerful, resilient, and deadly, increasing your chances of victory on the battlefield.

In conclusion, investing in war technology is crucial for an alliance's success in Infinity Kingdom. Choosing which technology to prioritize can be a difficult decision, but with this tier list as a guide, alliances can ensure they are putting their resources into the most effective areas. Remember, focusing on a few key technologies rather than trying to level everything up at once can lead to faster overall growth and improvement. So work together with your alliance, strategize, and prioritize wisely to become a dominant force on the battlefield!

title: Alt daily routine - what to do and what to skip
summary: Running a lot of alts is very time consuming - it is therefore very important to know what things you need to do on a daily basis and what you should skip. The more things we can skip, the more alts we can manage in the…
markdown:
Running a lot of alts is very time consuming - it is therefore very important to know what things you need to do on a daily basis and what you should skip. The more things we can skip, the more alts we can manage in the same time window.

Running 14 alts takes around 2 hours of combined gametime for me daily - including rss node farming and castle attacks.

## Create a routine with 2 daily logins

You want to time out your farming nodes and your troop production close to each other. Then make sure your second daily login matches both node farms and troop production finishing.

This is my personal routine.

### First daily login:

1. **Spend your AP farming ressources from dead-castles.**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-66-1024x561.png)

2. **Production**

- Begin troop training and healing
- Make sure you have all builders working
- Make sure you have Academy researching (read more about best alt-tech below).

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-68.png)

3. **Spend all your SP**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-70-1024x571.png)

### Second login (times out to be anytime after troop-production ends).

1. **Use all of your main's Rank Advancement attacks.**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-69-1024x364.png)

### 2. Collect daily rewards

- Daily missions. You want to complete the first daily bonus every day. Training speedups are your most important speedup since you will be farming your own troops as hard as you can during events ([for instance KoH, read more here](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/events/king-of-the-hill/complete-guide-for-all-stages/)).
- If you are focusing on growing your alt, you want to spend the extra 5 minutes and unlock the second bonus too. If you have your alt maxed, skip it.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-64.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-65-1024x416.png)

- Make sure you use up all your wishes (and if close to a new bonus, spend a few gems).

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-71-1024x617.png)

- Sign-in rewards, make sure you get them at least everytime it is gems, speedups, shields and random TP. You need these for alt farming, growth and SvS.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-72-1024x545.png)

3. **Collect alliance rewards**

Get ressources

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-82-1024x170.png)

Get alliance coins

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-83.png)

3**. Spend all your AP again on ressources (see above)**

4. **Begin troop production again (see above)**

5. **Spend all your SP again (see above)**

markdown:
### Alt Account Management for Feeding Main Account in Infinity Kingdom

Managing alt accounts effectively is a strategic aspect of Infinity Kingdom that can significantly boost your main account's honor and resources. This guide outlines the essential priorities for building your alt accounts with the goal of maximizing their utility in supporting your main account, especially when you can only afford to log in once a day.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-94-1024x397.png)

## Priority List for Alt Account Management

### 1. Spend Action Points (AP) Wisely

- **Objective**: Raid low-level gnomes with one march to minimize troop loss while still gaining experience.
- **Strategy**: Target gnomes much below your march's capability to ensure little to no troop loss. This method ensures a steady buildup of troop count through levels gained from the experience.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-95.png)

### 2. Utilize Skill Points (SP) Effectively

- **Objective**: Increase rank to boost troop count.
- **Strategy**: Allocate all available SP to advance your rank, directly contributing to an increased troop count, enhancing your account's capability to feed honor to your main account.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-96.png)

### 3. Focus on Key Technological Advancements

- **Objective**: Enhance troop count and training capacity.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-97-1024x573.png)

- **Strategy**: Prioritize technology that increases your troop count and the number of troops you can train in a single session. Given the once-a-day login constraint, maximizing training output is crucial.  - (a) Prioritize technologies that expand troop count.
- (b) Focus on technologies that allow for greater training amounts per session.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-98-1024x585.png)

### 4. Optimize Honor and Resource Farming

- **Objective**: Farm honor and resources efficiently.
- **Strategy**: Regularly send out marches to farm resources and gather honor. This consistent effort contributes significantly to your main account's growth.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-99-1024x550.png)

### 5. Streamline Building Focus

- **Objective**: Increase barracks capacity without unnecessary upgrades.
- **Strategy**: Concentrate on upgrading barracks to boost your troop production capabilities. Avoid upgrading buildings not directly related to troop production to conserve resources and focus.

## Tips for Efficient Honor Farming

### Maximizing Honor Gains

- Utilize the double honor talent strategically by consolidating your largest troops into one alt and then attacking it with your main. This approach doubles the honor gained from each successful attack.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-100-1024x595.png)

- Implement the instant healing talent defensively to maximize troop survival during honor farming sessions. This tactic ensures you get the most value out of each troop when attacking with your main account.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-101-1024x350.png)

### Legion of Frostborne Specific Strategy

During the Legion of Frostborne event, the healing talent extends to all marches within the castle, including garrisons. To optimize, ensure:

- Stack your attacks in one-on-one alt scenarios. This method allows you to use one talent stack for a comprehensive 5-march hit, maximizing the efficiency of your talent usage and honor gain.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-102.png)

## Conclusion

Managing alt accounts requires a strategic approach focused on troop production, technology advancement, and efficient resource and honor farming. By prioritizing the key areas outlined above and utilizing the tips for honor farming, you can significantly enhance the support your alt accounts provide to your main account. This disciplined approach ensures your main account receives the maximum possible benefit, helping to accelerate your progress and competitive standing in Infinity Kingdom.

title: Alt technology development
summary: Upgrading alts technology is very different from upgrading your main. We do not want to boost the power of our alt to make it strong. Instead our goal is to grow as quickly as possible, produce as much ressource as…
markdown:
Upgrading alts technology is very different from upgrading your main. We do not want to boost the power of our alt to make it strong. Instead our goal is to grow as quickly as possible, produce as much ressource as possible and train as many troops as possible. Therefore our tech development on alts should be as follow:

1. **Growth**

You want to build as quickly as possible.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-74-1024x426.png)

2. **Ressource production**

You want to upgrade the first row in development quickly. Boosting your ressource production help growing quickly as well as creating more plunder for your main. If you sometimes are unable to consistently login 2 times a day, you want to upgrade the extensions too.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-75-1024x696.png)

3. **Troop production**

You want as many troops as quickly as possible since one of the main points of alts is being farmed for honor. Therefore, you want to upgrade the troop tech training nodes as much as you can. Focus on bowmen, since you need more of those.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-76-1024x585.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-77-1024x621.png)

Later on, you want to get Medical specialist upgraded too, since your hospitals quickly become stacked with troops (remember to balance hitting your alt with main and your main with alt so you keep low training grounds and hospital in balance).

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-78-1024x578.png)

title: Ambush
summary: In the strategic landscape of Infinity Kingdom, the \"Ambush\" skill emerges as a unique asset for Range immortals, blending both offensive might and defensive agility. Available at Tower of Knowledge (ToK) level 53 and…
markdown:
### Mastering the "Ambush" Skill in Infinity Kingdom

In the strategic landscape of Infinity Kingdom, the "Ambush" skill emerges as a unique asset for Range immortals, blending both offensive might and defensive agility. Available at Tower of Knowledge (ToK) level 53 and during the Triss Blessing Event, "Ambush" offers a dual advantage on the battlefield, making it a prized skill for players seeking to enhance their combat capabilities.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-38-1024x528.png)

## Concept and Execution

"Ambush" operates on a sophisticated mechanism that alternates between making the user untargetable and unleashing devastating attacks. Every 12 seconds, there's a 50% chance for the immortal wielding this skill to enter stealth mode, becoming both inactive and immune to targeting for 3 seconds. Upon re-emergence from stealth, the immortal inflicts significant physical damage across the enemy lineup.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-37.png)

For optimal skill sequencing, positioning "Ambush" in the far right slot of your skill lineup is advisable. This placement ensures that other skills are triggered before entering stealth, maximizing your offensive output before momentarily stepping out of the battlefield.

## Damage Potential

In terms of damage output, "Ambush" ranks impressively, with a high damage dealt among skills. Its capacity to deliver substantial physical damage to all opponents makes it a formidable addition to any Range immortal's arsenal.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-39-1024x595.png)

While "Ambush" is universally compatible with Range immortals, offering no specific synergy that favors one over another, its effectiveness is undeniable. However, players must exercise caution in matchups against certain immortals like Tutankhamon or Hippolytta, especially when paired with Himiko. The stealth aspect of "Ambush" can inadvertently aid Tutankhamon by narrowing his target options, potentially boosting his damage output through repeated ultimate attacks. Likewise, having Hippolytta hit one immortal many times completly destroys the energy bar of that immortal - but it also protects the energy bar of the immortal with ambush!

The stealth aspect can be both a powerful defensive mechanic protecting the troop count of your Immortal but it can also be a double edged sword!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-40.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-41.png)

The dual nature of "Ambush" as both a protective and aggressive skill necessitates strategic deployment. It's a skill that rewards timing and placement, demanding players to be mindful of the battlefield dynamics and the composition of both their own and the enemy's forces. Understanding when to leverage its stealth mode for defensive purposes versus timing its damage output for maximum impact is key to mastering "Ambush."

## Conclusion

"Ambush" stands out as a skill that embodies the essence of strategic flexibility, offering Range immortals in Infinity Kingdom a potent blend of survivability and offensive prowess. Its introduction into your strategic repertoire can significantly alter the course of battle, providing moments of invulnerability coupled with bursts of devastating damage. As with any skill, the effectiveness of "Ambush" is amplified when integrated thoughtfully into your overall battle strategy, making it a valuable addition for those looking to dominate the skies of Infinity Kingdom.

title: Ancient Altars (Special KVK Event)
summary: The Ancient Altars event is a supplemental KVK activity available only in Conquest Seasons Plus within Infinity Kingdom. It opens with Zone 2 and runs until the end of KVK. The event doesn’t redefine the season on its…
markdown:
### Introduction

The **Ancient Altars** event is a supplemental KVK activity available **only in Conquest Seasons Plus** within **Infinity Kingdom**. It opens with **Zone 2** and runs until the end of KVK. The event doesn’t redefine the season on its own, but when coordinated properly it can provide meaningful point acceleration at key moments—especially for alliances pushing tight rankings.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-11-1024x444.png)

You’ll find the overview under **Alliance → Ancient Altar**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-12-1024x328.png)

---

## Event Structure and Core Objective

At its core, the event is split into two phases:

1. **Collect clues by scouting Ancient Ruins**
2. **Summon and purify an Ancient Altar to activate an alliance-wide buff**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-14-1024x584.png)

Clues are obtained exclusively through ruins scattered across the KVK map. There is **no auto-search**—manual scouting is required.

---

## Ancient Ruins: How They Work

- Ruins function similarly to **no-harm ruins**.
- Send scouts to explore them for:  - Event points
- Random rewards
- A **chance at gems**
- **Each ruin can be explored only once**, so speed and coordination matter.
- Ruins **refresh every other day** during the event.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-13-1024x561.png)

### Ruin Levels by Zone

- **Zone 1** → Level 1 Ruins
- **Zone 2** → Level 2 Ruins

Higher-level ruins provide noticeably better rewards. In practice, once Zone 2 opens, it’s worth shifting scout attention there unless your alliance is still cleaning up missed Zone 1 ruins for achievements.

---

## Summoning the Ancient Altar

Once your alliance gathers enough clues:

- **R5 or R6** can summon the Ancient Altar
- The altar can be placed **anywhere on the map**, but **must be adjacent to an alliance Thermal Tower**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-15.png)

This flexibility allows leadership to time altar placement as it fits your alliance relative to e.g.:

- Spider Boss spawns
- PvP push windows
- Other events

---

## Purification Mechanics

Purification is straightforward:

- The altar is attacked **like a city or checkpoint**
- There are **no personal rewards** for dealing damage
- Missing the fight is not a loss—what matters is the buff activation

Once purified, the alliance receives **one random buff** for **24 hours**.

---

## Available Ancient Altar Buffs

Each purification grants **one** of the following alliance-wide effects:

- **+50% points from defeating known bosses**
- **+20% points from defeating players**
- **100% conversion of city points into alliance points**
- **+100% gathering speed**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-16.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-17.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-18.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-19.png)

## Ancient Altar Siege Mechanics

One point worth clarifying—because it’s often overthought—is how the **Ancient Altar itself actually works in combat**.

Mechanically, the Altar behaves **like a City Siege without any garrison**. There are no defending marches, no immortals to counter, and no combat scaling to worry about. You are simply **burning down wall fortification and durability**. Once both are reduced to zero, the purification completes and the alliance buff is granted.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-20-1024x486.png)

Because of this, the Altar is **not a difficult siege**, despite having a fairly large durability pool.

A few practical implications from experience:

- **Buffs are unnecessary** for the Altar fight itself. March attack, siege, or damage buffs are overkill unless leadership is deliberately using the Altar as a rally point to get players online before a PvP push.
- **Gnome-optimized or siege-focused builds are wasted here.** There is no efficiency gain from specialized siege setups—the Altar doesn’t reward that kind of optimization.
- Any reasonably built march will contribute effectively. This is why alliances can clear the Altar quickly even with casual participation.

Where buffs *do* make sense is **after** purification. Many alliances intentionally time the Altar attack to:

1. Get members online for a simple, low-risk objective
2. Immediately transition into PvP, boss hunting, or point farming while momentum is high

In short: the Ancient Altar looks intimidating, but it’s closer to a durability check than a real fight. Treat it as a coordination trigger, not a combat challenge, and you’ll get more strategic value out of it.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-21-1024x477.png)

---

## Achievements and Minimum Participation

Make sure your members don’t miss the basics:

- **Alliance achievement**: Purify the altar at least once
- **Personal achievement**: Explore **10 ruins**

Even casual participation covers these, and there’s no reason to leave them incomplete.

---

## Overall Assessment

The Ancient Altars event is **not a headline KVK feature**, but it’s far from pointless:

- It offers **extra alliance points** that can matter in close seasons
- It provides **steady gem income** for players willing to scout consistently
- It rewards alliances that communicate and time buffs intelligently

If you treat it as background noise, you’ll miss value. If you integrate it into your alliance’s KVK rhythm, it becomes a quiet but reliable contributor.

---

### Final Takeaway

Ancient Altars won’t carry your KVK—but disciplined scouting, timely purification, and smart buff usage can give your alliance an edge when margins are thin. If you have spare time to hunt ruins, the gem returns alone often justify the effort.

---

title: Ancient Tribe
summary: Infinity Kingdom has a ton of cool city skins. You get skins from purchases during events, performance from in game activities such as contention of relics and/or Legion of Frostborne, Throne of the Supreeme, and so on.…
markdown:
Infinity Kingdom has a ton of cool city skins. You get skins from purchases during events, performance from in game activities such as contention of relics and/or Legion of Frostborne, Throne of the Supreeme, and so on. Castle Skins serve two purposes: (1) they provide unique buff effects to specific activities such as e.g. tech speed, dragon speed, combat buffs, recovery speed, resource collection rate, etc. and (2) they provide unique cosmetic effects that change the way your castle looks inside the game. The cosmetic effects work in all aspects of the game, any game mode, and provides some awesome customization to make youself more unique and your castle look.. well.. more awesome!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-89-1024x520.png)

In this article we shall look to one of my personal favorite cosmetic skins in all of **Infinity Kingdom: Ancient Tribe**

## What does Ancient Tribe do?

Every castle skin has unique beneficial effects, from building speed to rss gathering and troop HP. The Ancient Tribe provides you a 3% increase to your Action Point recovery rate. AP is the most limited resource we have in Infinity Kingdom and as such having more AP simple mean you can do more things throughout your day in Infinity Kingdom!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-90.png)

That being said, this skin is not one of the "best" skins purely based on it's effect. 3% increased AP means that while you would normally regen 1 AP every 30 seconds. Translating into 120 AP / hour or 2880 AP per day without the skin effect active. With the skin you instead regen 123.6 AP / hour with the skin on a daily total of 2966.4 and thus only a 86.4 AP more with the skin active.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-91.png)

86 AP is not a lot, translates into roughly a single action more per day, which is very neglectable and not really worth using this skin when you compare it to the effects offered by other castle skins. However, this skin is still one of my favorites simple because the look and feel of it is awesome!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-92.png)

## How to get it?

There is only one way to obtain this skin**: (1) Hunting Festival and (2) Golden Path seasonal shop**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-93.png)

This skin was first released with the very first version of the Hunting Festival which occur every **May**in Infinity Kingdom. During this seasonal event, players have been able to complete quests and practice with your bow and arrow to become Legendary Hunter and earn the Tribe Casle Skin. You should beware that these seasonal events tends to change every year, and as such I cannot give any guarantees as to how or if you will be able to collect this skin from the seasonal even when May comes around again.

However, lucky for you guys there is a place where you can be sure to collect this skin - in the Golden Path seasonal shop!

## Golden Path

Ancient Tribe can be found in the last and first rotation of the Golden Path shop. You will be able to find it there somewhere around the december-february timeframe (changes slightly ever year and based on server).

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-94.png)

This skin is available in the golden path rotation! **[Check out my article here to read more about the Castle skins offered via Golden Path as well as the full rotation](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/development/market/golden-path/)**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-95.png)

Published: 23-03-23

title: Annihilation

markdown:
### Unleashing Power with Annihilation: A Player's Guide to Dominating in Infinity Kingdom

Welcome, fellow lords and ladies, to a deep dive into one of Infinity Kingdom's most formidable powers: the Tower of Knowledge skill, "Annihilation." As a beacon for free-to-play (F2P) players seeking to amplify their magical onslaught, Annihilation stands out as a quintessential skill for any mage looking to leave a mark on the battlefield. Let's explore how to harness this skill to its full potential, turning your magical immortals into unstoppable forces of destruction.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-136-1024x536.png)

#### Overview of Annihilation

Annihilation is a skill that, by its very nature, promises devastation. With a 45% chance every 6 seconds to unleash 300% magical damage to all four enemy immortals, it epitomizes the essence of "area of effect" (AOE) prowess. This translates to an astronomical 1200% magical damage output each time the skill activates, positioning Annihilation as a top-tier choice for any player keen on maximizing damage.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-143-1024x383.png)

#### Synergy with Critical Builds

The true beauty of Annihilation lies in its compatibility with critical hit-based builds, particularly those emphasizing fire elements. The skill not only delivers massive damage but also serves as a catalyst for the "Chase" skill. Since Chase is triggered by critical hits and Annihilation targets all enemies, it significantly heightens the probability of activating Chase on every Annihilation proc. This synergy is not just effective; it's a game-changer, making Annihilation a cornerstone for any crit-based magical damage setup.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-138-1024x455.png)

#### Optimal Usage of Annihilation

**Choosing the Right Immortal:** Annihilation should be the crown jewel in the arsenal of your most potent mage. Immortals like Himiko, Empress Wu, Baldwin, Hammurabi, and Merlin are prime candidates for this skill, as their inherent strengths and capabilities are magnified through its use.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-139.png)

**Pairing with Chase:** For those committed to a crit-based approach, integrating Chase alongside Annihilation can transform your mages into harbingers of doom. This combination not only ensures high damage output but also leverages the crit mechanism to disrupt and decimate enemy ranks efficiently.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-140.png)

**Strategic Considerations:** Deploying Annihilation demands a strategic mindset. Given its significant impact and the timing of its activation, positioning your mage and timing their attacks in sync with other skills and immortals on your roster can maximize the devastation inflicted upon your adversaries.

#### Building Around Annihilation

To truly capitalize on Annihilation, your strategy should extend beyond skill selection. Consider the following:

- **Gear and Artifacts:** Equip items that enhance magical damage, critical hit rate, and speed. These will ensure that Annihilation's effects are felt more frequently and with greater intensity.
- **Supporting Skills:** Beyond Chase, look for skills that complement Annihilation's damage potential or that provide buffs to your mage's critical hit capabilities.
- **Team Composition:** Surround your Annihilation-wielding mage with immortals who can benefit from the chaos it creates—be it through additional AOE skills, debuffs on enemies, or buffs for your team.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-141.png)

#### Conclusion

Annihilation is not just a skill; it's a statement—a declaration of your intent to dominate the magical battlefield in Infinity Kingdom. By strategically incorporating Annihilation into your lineup, pairing it with synergistic skills like Chase, and optimizing your immortal's build, you can unlock unparalleled levels of magical destruction. Remember, in the hands of a savvy player, Annihilation is more than just a skill; it's the key to turning the tide of battle in your favor. Embrace its power, and let the annihilation begin!

title: Arena rewards - Immortals and their rotation by season
summary: The Arena in Infinity Kingdom is one of the most important features for progressing and strengthening your army. Each season, new Immortals become available as placement rewards and in the Arena Shop.
markdown:
The *Arena* in *Infinity Kingdom* is one of the most important features for progressing and strengthening your army. Each season, new **Immortals** become available as placement rewards and in the Arena Shop.

These Immortals are some of the most powerful units in the game, and planning ahead to obtain them is crucial for optimizing your gameplay. This guide will help you understand the seasonal rotation of Immortals and how to use the Arena effectively to build a top-tier army.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/image-112-1024x473.png)

---

### Why Arena Immortals Matter

Arena Immortals are unique units that can dramatically enhance your army’s performance. They are not only strong individually but often come with powerful synergies for specific elemental builds. Knowing when your desired Immortal will be available allows you to plan, save Arena coins, and make strategic decisions to improve your lineup.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/image-113-1024x526.png)

---

### Seasonal Immortal Rewards Overview

Each Arena season lasts a limited time, offering both **placement rewards** and Immortals for purchase in the **Arena Shop**. Here's the breakdown of Immortals for each season:

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/Single-InfoGrafic-Portals-2-1024x508.png)

#### Season 1

- **Placement Reward:** Empress Wu
- **Arena Shop Slot 1:** Harald
- **Arena Shop Slot 2:** Hippolyta

#### Season 2

- **Placement Reward:** Attila
- **Arena Shop Slot 1:** Cleopatra
- **Arena Shop Slot 2:** Harald

#### Season 3

- **Placement Reward:** Alexander the Great
- **Arena Shop Slot 1:** Richard I
- **Arena Shop Slot 2:** Cleopatra

#### Season 4

- **Placement Reward:** Peter the Great
- **Arena Shop Slot 1:** Emperor Qin
- **Arena Shop Slot 2:** Richard I

#### Season 5

- **Placement Reward:** Hannibal Barca
- **Arena Shop Slot 1:** Hippolyta
- **Arena Shop Slot 2:** Emperor Qin

---

### How to Earn Immortals in the Arena

#### 1. Placement Rewards

At the end of each Arena season, your rank determines your placement reward. Immortals given as placement rewards are rare and often pivotal for specific elemental teams, so aiming for a high rank is essential.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/image-114-1024x556.png)

#### 2. Arena Coins and Arena Shop

- **Earn Arena Coins** by participating in and winning Arena battles. You earn through the victory point bar in the bottom of the screen as well as 10x victory points as insignias per battle won.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/image-115-1024x550.png)

- Use these coins to purchase Immortals from the **Arena Shop**, where two Immortals are available for each season.
- Immortals in the Arena Shop can often complement or enhance your elemental strategy, so prioritize those that fit your team’s needs.

---

### Tips for Arena Immortal Selection

1. **Plan Ahead:**
Since the rotation of Immortals in the Arena is predictable, you can save Arena coins for when a specific Immortal you need becomes available. For example, if you're building a **hybrid team**, you might want to save for **Qin** or **Alexander the Great**.
2. **Optimize for Your Elemental Build:**
Each Immortal aligns with a specific elemental affinity. Research how the Immortal synergizes with your current lineup. For instance:  - **Harald** (water): Strong for physical damage based water teams.
- **Empress Wu** (Fire): Must have for offensive Fire builds.
- **Hippolyta** (fire): Must have for fire teams with her control and ability proc capabilities.
3. **Balance Offense and Defense:**
While some Immortals like **Attila** masters control and **Hannibal Barca** excel in offense, others like **Richard I** are better for defense and control. Think about your strategy and the role your desired Immortal will play in it when picking which immortals and fits with your setup. Read guides here on this website to see builds for all stages of development.
4. **Use Arena Coins Wisely:**
Avoid spending Arena coins impulsively. Immortals in the shop will rotate out, so having enough coins banked ensures you won’t miss out on key units.

---

### How to Succeed in the Arena

1. **Build a Strong Lineup:**
Focus on strengthening your team to climb the Arena leaderboard. Maximize synergies between your Immortals and dragons to dominate battles.
2. **Participate Regularly:**
Consistent participation in Arena battles earns more Arena coins and improves your chances of securing high placement rewards.
***Tip:**I would make sure to always get the 10 victory point bonus, even if that means spending gems for a ticket. Getting 240 Insignia + rewards from the ticket-win battle every day stacks up very quickly.*
3. **Track Seasonal Immortals:**
Keep this guide handy to know which Immortals are coming up and when to aim for specific rewards or shop purchases.

---

### Conclusion

Arena Immortals are a cornerstone of success in *Infinity Kingdom*. By carefully tracking their seasonal availability and planning your purchases, you can strengthen your elemental teams and dominate in both PvP and PvE content.

Save your Arena coins, aim for high placements, and target the Immortals that best fit your strategy. With the right approach, the Arena will become a key tool in building your dream army.

Happy battling, and may the Immortal rewards be ever in your favor! 🏆✨

title: Ares (Chaos)
summary: Ares, the god of war, joined Infinity Kingdom with Patch 2.8.5 on July 10th, entering as the newest Chaos Immortal.
markdown:
## Ares – The God of War (Chaos, Cavalry)

Ares, the god of war, joined Infinity Kingdom with Patch 2.8.5 on **July 10th**, entering as the newest **Chaos Immortal**.

Unlike **Apollo**, who combines burst damage, healing suppression, and scaling durability, **Ares** represents pure, relentless aggression. His signature trait is a **permanent +50% Attack Speed bonus**, making him one of the fastest cavalry Immortals from the moment combat begins.

What truly sets Ares apart, however, is his ability to **remove Control Immunity** and **weaken Barriers**—two defensive mechanics that once defined the durability meta. Teams that rely on shield stacking or immunity rotations quickly crumble against him. In turn, he enables allies’ control skills—stuns, silences, confusions, roots—to land with full effect.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-10.png)

This dual function gives Ares a rare identity among frontliners: he is both a **high-pressure attacker** and a **team enabler** who opens the way for allies to capitalize on control and burst windows.

Ares is designed for tempo play. He sets the pace early, cracks defensive layers open, and lets the rest of the team flood through. Players who prefer fast, decisive battles will find him a powerful addition to Chaos lineups.

---

## Core Strengths & Battle Identity

### Skill: Battlefield Trample

- **Passive:** Increases Normal Attack Speed by 50% permanently.
- **Active:** Deals physical damage to all enemies (scaling 150–500%) and has a 50% chance to apply **Frighten** for 6 seconds, which:  - Removes the target’s **Control Immunity**
- Reduces the effectiveness of **Barriers** by 30%

Ares thrives on momentum. The permanent speed boost ensures he begins outputting damage immediately, while Frighten opens defensive gaps that allow allied control effects and damage to land unhindered. This makes him one of the most aggressive openers in the Chaos roster.

While his early tempo is unmatched, his impact declines slightly in prolonged battles without sustain or scaling. For players focused on early dominance and team coordination, however, Ares provides a distinct advantage.

---

## Battlefield Trample – Mechanics & Energy Flow

Battlefield Trample defines Ares’ combat rhythm:

- **+50% Attack Speed (passive)**
- **AoE Physical Damage (150–500% scaling)**
- **50% chance to apply "Frighten" on enemies which strip them of any Control Immunity (e.g. Fountain of Life or Fu Fei) and weaken Barriers by 30% for 6 seconds**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-8.png)

### Why It Matters

- **Anti-Barrier Utility:** Ares doesn’t just pierce shields—he destabilizes them. Barrier-heavy teams, especially those relying on sustain or timing-based protection, lose their key advantage.
- **CC Enablement:** Removing Control Immunity allows allied controllers—such as **Tomyris**, **Himiko**, and **Loki**—to land disables that previously failed. Once these effects connect, the fight shifts heavily in your favor.
- **Damage Conversion:** Each CC connection opens a punishment window for high-damage allies like Apollo or Anubis to exploit.

### Energy Regen & Ultimate Timing

Ares also benefits from above-average energy regeneration, starting at **93.3/s** base. With equipment and boosts, he can reach 105–130/s, letting him cast Battlefield Trample frequently—crucial for maintaining his debuff uptime.

| Regen Rate | Time to 1000 Energy | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 93.3/s | ~10.7s | Baseline |
| 105/s | ~9.5s | Smooth cycle |
| 130/s | ~7.7s | Near-continuous pressure |

Ares’ debuff lasts **6 seconds**. At **105/s**, there’s a ~3.5s gap between effects; at **130/s**, the downtime narrows to ~1.7s. In live battles, even minor boosts (on-hit energy gain, ally support, etc.) can create near-continuous debuff pressure—transforming him into a constant disruptor.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-7-1024x559.png)

The most impactful element of his kit is not the AoE damage itself, but the **immunity removal** that changes how entire lineups interact.

---

## Optimal Builds – Artifact, Specialization & Skills

### Best Artifact

### War Spear·Surge

Prioritize **Physical Damage %** as the main attribute. The Surge effect aligns with Ares’ short ultimate cycle, helping him refresh Battlefield Trample faster and maintain pressure.

### Best Specialization

**Knight’s Spirit** — Offers +21–70% Damage and +9–30% Attack Speed.
This specialization amplifies his aggressive playstyle and keeps him effective from the opening seconds.

### Recommended Skills

- **Last Stand:** Provides vital survivability during the opening exchange, ensuring Ares stays alive to apply his debuffs.
- **Wind Rage:** Doubles down on his attack speed, turning him into a relentless source of auto-attack and skill pressure.
- **Knife Through Butter:** Excellent synergy. Every 6 attacks trigger AoE cleaves that cut enemy energy regen by 300. With Ares’ speed, this procs often, crippling sustain teams.
- **Optional alternatives:**  - **Assembly Charge:** For early snowball.
- **Battle Frenzy:** For pure offense.
- **Corrosive Power:** For smoother ult rotations.

### Essential Team Skill

**Fountain of Life** on an ally is strongly recommended. It prevents Ares from being silenced during his initial charge, preserving his tempo advantage.
**Spring of Life** is also useful for sustain-based setups, reducing incoming damage when healed.

The optimal skill trio for Ares is **Knife Through Butter + Wind Rage + Last Stand**—a balance of speed, disruption, and durability that lets him sustain aggression while amplifying team control.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-6.png)

---

## Team Synergies

Ares excels when paired with allies who can exploit his immunity removal and barrier reduction. The best combinations pair him with high-burst or control-heavy Immortals.

- **Loki:** With Ares removing immunity, Loki’s **Confusion** connects reliably, causing enemies to attack themselves. This combo revives CC-heavy compositions and can dismantle coordinated teams.
- **Apollo:** Once barriers are weakened, Apollo’s **Corona Godstrike** and healing reduction dominate. Together, they crush sustain-based defenses in seconds.
- **Anubis:** A dependable frontline bruiser who absorbs damage and amplifies incoming damage. Pairs well for sustained pressure setups.
- **Fu Fei:** Provides critical sustain and control immunity, allowing Ares to survive long enough to cycle multiple ultimates. A must-have for balanced compositions.

Ares functions best as an **enabler**—he doesn’t carry fights alone, but his debuffs allow his team to deal far greater damage and control than they otherwise could.

---

## Battle Performance Examples

### Case 1 – Ares + Apollo

**Duration:** ~40 seconds
**Result:** Ares enabled Apollo to reach **56.6M damage**, compared to the enemy Apollo’s (who did just **12.1M**).
Ares’ barrier breaking and immunity stripping allowed uninterrupted damage rotations, while Fu Fei’s healing kept the frontline intact. The opposing team’s sustain collapsed under the combined healing reduction and CC pressure.

### Below images are the two sides of the chaos-whale fight:

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-1024x615.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-3-1024x619.png)

**Takeaway:** Ares amplified Apollo’s damage potential and crippled the enemy’s sustain. The match ended quickly due to overwhelming early tempo.

---

### Case 2 – Ares + Loki

**Duration:** ~1 minute 10 seconds
**Result:** Ares contributed **32.6M damage**, while Loki added **20.4M**.
The fight was slower but heavily controlled. Continuous debuffs allowed **Confusion** and other CC effects to land consistently. Fu Fei’s healing sustained Ares through prolonged exchanges, leading to a gradual victory.

### Below images are the two sides of the chaos-whale fight:

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-2-1024x614.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-4-1024x614.png)

**Takeaway:** Ares transitioned into a semi-carry role within a CC-heavy setup. While less explosive than the Apollo variant, this composition offered steady control and reliable wins through attrition.

---

## Conclusion

Ares redefines Chaos frontline play. His strength lies not in raw damage numbers but in **meta disruption**—breaking barriers, removing control immunity, and letting allies dictate the tempo.

He fits perfectly into teams focused on **early aggression**, **tempo control**, and **crowd control synergy**. Pair him with **Apollo** for explosive offense or **Loki** for sustained CC dominance.

However, players favoring **slow, sustain-based battles** may find his impact tapering off over time. Ares is not a wall—he’s a hammer built to break them.

**Bottom Line:**
Ares is a meta-shifting Immortal who changes how fights are played. He doesn’t just deal damage—he changes the rules of engagement. For players who want to resurrect CC comps, dismantle barrier-heavy teams, and seize control from the first second, Ares delivers exactly that.
