***Upgrade Materials for Artifacts in Infinity Kingdom*** - *Harnessing the Power of Sun and Spirit*

In the ever-expanding realm of Infinity Kingdom, where powerful Immortals clash for supremacy, artifacts stand as essential tools that can tip the balance in battles and strategic conquests. To wield artifacts at their maximum potential, commanders must delve into the realm of upgrades, a process that requires the rare and potent Upgrade Materials. This article delves into the world of Infinity Kingdom's upgrade materials, shedding light on how to acquire them and the significance they hold.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/image-6-1024x547.png)

## How Artifacts Ascend: The Upgrade Process

Artifacts, imbued with mystic power, can be upgraded to enhance their effects and attributes. This process unfolds in the sacred chambers of the Forge building, where Sun Crystals and Empowered Sun Crystals serve as the catalysts for transformation. To navigate the upgrade journey, commanders traverse three tiers of quality: bronze, silver, and gold. Each level promises increased might and versatility.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/image-8-1024x573.png)

- **Bronze to Silver:** To elevate an artifact from its humble bronze state to the more formidable silver quality, commanders require 40 Sun Crystals. This initial leap forms the foundation for the artifact's enhanced capabilities.
- **Silver to Gold:** The zenith of an artifact's potential lies in its golden incarnation. Elevating a silver artifact to this eminent state calls for 40 Empowered Sun Crystals. Through this investment of resources, commanders can truly harness the artifact's full potential, turning the tide of battle in their favor.

In the pursuit of commanding an unstoppable Immortal force, a total of 160 Sun Crystals and 160 Empowered Sun Crystals is needed to equip the four Immortals of the main march with Gold artifacts, a feat that symbolizes true mastery of artifact enhancement.

## Gathering the Prized Crystals: Sources of Upgrade Materials

The journey to acquire the essential Upgrade Materials takes commanders through various paths, each offering opportunities to bolster their arsenal and solidify their dominion.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/image-10-300x225.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/image-9-300x228.png)

- **Rebel Camps Event:** Engaging in the Rebel Camps event presents a chance to amass both regular Sun Crystals and Empowered Sun Crystals. The battlefield yields more than just victory; it gifts the commanders the means to strengthen their Immortals.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/image-13.png)

- **Wheel of Fortune Events:** Fortuna herself smiles upon those who spin the Wheel of Fortune. Within its rotations lie the possibility of securing both types of Sun Crystals, further enhancing the odds of prevailing in the tumultuous battles that characterize Infinity Kingdom.
- **Seasonal Sales:** The strategic-minded can seize the chance presented by the Seasonal Sales to acquire Sun Crystals and Empowered Sun Crystals. These special bundles offer an efficient and direct path to amassing the resources needed to empower artifacts.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/image-11-1024x533.png)

- **Pearl Shop:** The Pearl Shop, a burgeoning emporium of mystical artifacts and rare resources, holds the key to unlocking upgraded power. Both Empowered Sun Crystals and Spiritual Crystals can be acquired here, shaping the destinies of commanders willing to invest.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/image-45-1024x535.png)

## Chaos Immortals and Spiritual Crystals: A Special Path

In the tapestry of Infinity Kingdom, Chaos Immortals occupy a unique space, demanding a distinct approach to artifact enhancement. These enigmatic beings require the infusion of Spiritual Crystals and Empowered Spiritual Crystals to ascend from obscurity to silver and, ultimately, to gold quality.

- **Spiritual Crystals:** Elevating Chaos artifacts from bronze to silver necessitates the use of Spiritual Crystals, available in the Pearl Shop and through the Seasonal Sale bundles. These ethereal resources bridge the gap between the mundane and the exceptional.
- **Empowered Spiritual Crystals:** The zenith of Chaos artifact prowess is achieved through Empowered Spiritual Crystals. This refined material, attainable through select avenues, underlines the investment commanders must make to steer Chaos Immortals toward supremacy.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/image-16-1024x503.png)

### Embrace the Path of Upgrade Mastery

In Infinity Kingdom, artifacts are more than mere trinkets; they are conduits of power, capable of altering the course of battles and determining the fate of realms. The journey toward fully realized artifact potential is a path riddled with challenges and rewards, where Sun Crystals, Empowered Sun Crystals, Spiritual Crystals, and Empowered Spiritual Crystals serve as the pivotal keys. As commanders wield these materials wisely, their Immortals ascend to greatness, and the legacy of their dominion takes shape amidst the chaotic tapestry of Infinity Kingdom.

markdown:
## Introduction

Assembly Charge is one of those KvK skills that looks inconsistent at first glance, but performs reliably once you understand how it interacts with normal attacks. It isn’t about single big bursts—it’s about stacking value over time through repeated triggers.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-104-1024x376.png)

If you’re running physical DPS, especially attack-speed-based setups, this skill can quietly become one of your top damage contributors.

---

## Skill Overview and Acquisition

### Where to Get Assembly Charge

- **KvK Shop** (priority source — grab it when available from Conquest and onwards)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-105.png)

If you’re planning to build physical DPS marches long-term, it’s worth securing this skill early.

---

### Skill Effect Breakdown

- **Trigger Condition**: 60% chance on *each normal attack*
- **Effect**:  - Deals physical damage to the target + 2 nearby enemies
- Grants **+10% physical damage** for 6 seconds

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-106.png)

**Key Insight:**
The 60% chance is deceptive. It applies per normal attack, so heroes with high attack frequency effectively “roll the dice” many times, resulting in consistent uptime and damage.

---

## Best Users and Core Synergy

### Primary User: Alexander

Assembly Charge fits naturally on Alexander because:

- His kit revolves around frequent normal attacks
- He doesn’t rely on long cooldown skills
- He benefits directly from sustained physical damage scaling

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-107-1024x590.png)

In practice, when I tested this in multiple KvK fights, Assembly Charge consistently landed **top 1–2 damage contribution** on Alexander, especially in longer engagements.

---

### Alternative Users

- **Hannibal** (if sufficiently upgraded)  - Similar normal attack reliance
- Works well in secondary or experimental marches

More broadly:

- Any **physical DPS hero with high attack frequency** can use it effectively
- It’s less effective on burst or skill-dependent heroes

---

## Recommended Combinations

### Normal Attack Trigger-Based DPS Build (High Consistency)

- Assembly Charge
- Berserk
- Wind Rage

### Why it works:

- **Berserk** increases attack speed (more trigger chances)
- **Wind Rage** adds additional normal attack triggers
- Assembly Charge benefits from both → more procs, more AoE damage

### Getting into legendary skills:

- Swap out Berserk for Knife Through Butter

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-108-1024x609.png)

This combination turns Alexander into a **multi-trigger engine**, stacking damage across the entire enemy formation.

---

## Performance Observations

From actual combat logs:

- Assembly Charge can trigger easily ever single second
- Frequently ranks:  - **Top damage source**
- Or **second highest contributor**
- Performs better in:  - Longer fights
- Multi-target engagements
- Second marches where fights aren’t instantly decided

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-110-1024x458.png)

It’s not flashy, but over time it consistently adds pressure.

---

## Conclusion Summary

- Assembly Charge is a **high-value sustained DPS skill**, not a burst tool
- Best used on **fast-attacking physical heroes**, especially Alexander
- Its effectiveness scales with:  - Attack speed
- Number of normal attacks
- Strongest synergy comes from:  - **Berserk**
- **Wind Rage**
- Expect it to become a **top damage contributor in longer fights**

If you treat it as a trigger engine rather than a proc gamble, it becomes one of the more reliable KvK damage skills available.

---

### Player Guide: Mastering the "Assist" Skill in Infinity Kingdom

"Assist" is one of the foundational skills in Infinity Kingdom, known for its strategic depth and versatility. Although its popularity has fluctuated over the years, "Assist" remains a crucial skill in many top-tier builds due to its ability to manipulate damage distribution effectively. This guide explores how to best utilize the "Assist" skill to protect key immortals and enhance your overall battle strategy.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/image-163.png)

## What Does "Assist" Do?

"Assist" is a defensive skill that activates every 10 seconds, targeting one random backrow allied unit. The mechanics of the skill are as follows:

- **Damage Transfer**: When activated, all damage received by the assisted unit is transferred to the immortal equipped with "Assist."
- **Damage Reduction**: The immortal with "Assist" will receive 25% less damage for 6 seconds when the skill activates.

This skill is particularly valuable in protecting vital backline units, ensuring they can continue to deal damage or provide support without the risk of being quickly eliminated.

## Strategic Implementation of Assist

## 1. Protecting Key Backline Immortals

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/image-165.png)

- **Dual Backline Setup**: In formations where two immortals are positioned in the back, equipping "Assist" on one ensures that the other, typically a crucial damage dealer or controller, receives protection. This setup is ideal when you rely heavily on a specific backline immortal for your strategy's success.

## 2. Utilizing "Assist" on Support Immortals

- **Damage Redistribution**: Use "Assist" on a support immortal whose troop count is less critical to their function, such as Tomyris. This strategy keeps more essential immortals like Himiko safer, as Tomyris’s contributions to the battle are not heavily dependent on her troop count.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/image-166.png)

## 3. Combining "Assist" with Defensive Skills

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/image-164-1024x583.png)

- **Enhanced Protection**: When using "Assist" on immortals whose effectiveness depends on their troop count (e.g., healers like Zenobia or Theodora), it’s beneficial to pair "Assist" with additional defensive skills:  - **Absolute Defense** and **Void Realm**: These skills provide robust damage mitigation, enhancing the survivability of immortals taking transferred damage.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/image-167-1024x594.png)

In the above you see 3.3 million damage shielded by Absolute Defense, may not seem overly much but it is given the relative short duration and our overall mitigation build, it actually is quite significant. Comparatively the top tier skill Energy Shield provided us 4m shielding in the same fight. Absolute Defensive giving good value in synergy with assist!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/image-168-1024x395.png)

- **Life Link**: This skill can be particularly synergistic, as it not only helps in reducing incoming damage but also transfers some of the absorbed damage back to the enemy, further leveraging the defensive setup.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/image-169.png)

## Effective Builds with Assist

- **Support-Heavy Build**: Equip "Assist" on a durable support immortal in a formation that includes high-value targets requiring protection. This setup allows your primary units to operate with decreased risk.
- **Balanced Defense Build**: In a balanced team, "Assist" can protect your strategic assets while diversified defensive skills across your team manage the redistributed damage effectively.

## Conclusion

"Assist" offers a unique strategic advantage by allowing players to control where damage is directed within their formation. This capability is critical in protecting key units and maintaining the integrity of your battle strategy. Whether shielding a high-impact damage dealer or ensuring the longevity of your support immortals, "Assist" provides the flexibility and protection needed to adapt and overcome various battle challenges. Proper utilization of this skill can significantly enhance your team’s performance in both offensive and defensive aspects of the game.

## Introduction

After being absent from Infinity Kingdom for years, Asteria has finally returned in patch 2.9.5 alongside the new Affinity system. From early testing, the relaunch looks extremely close to the original version mechanically, especially regarding progression structure and alliance boss behavior. The biggest difference is clearly the reward design, which is now heavily tied into Affinity progression through the new Otherworld Crystal currency.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/image-4-1024x553.png)

Players who experienced the original Asteria event will probably recognize the flow immediately:

- Push progressively harder personal camps
- Unlock alliance-wide bosses
- Coordinate alliance participation carefully
- Optimize contribution without accidentally ending encounters too early

The old strategies still appear highly relevant.

---

## How the New Asteria Works - Individual Challenges

The personal side of the event revolves around clearing increasingly difficult Shadow Rogue camps.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/image-5-1024x574.png)

### Key mechanics

- Camps scale upward after each clear
- Maximum difficulty is Level 30
- Enemy strength increases quite aggressively near the top
- Clearing higher levels contributes toward unlocking alliance bosses
- Even the highest level (6) challenge at camp level 30 seems doable by most everyone, which is quite good!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/image-6-1024x604.png)

From testing on the final personal stage:

- Level 30 Challenge Level 6
- Conquest season account
- Battle duration: ~33 seconds
- Casualties: only ~100 troops

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/image-8-1024x570.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/image-7-1024x613.png)

That battle length is important because it confirms the enemies are not simply paper targets. They survive long enough to interact with sustain and debuff setups properly. However, despite the longer fight duration, the incoming damage remains manageable with optimized PvE control builds.

## Recommended PvE Utility Skills

Two skills stand out immediately:

### No Escape

Excellent for extending control windows and stabilizing harder camps.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/image-9.png)

### Weakening Curse

Still one of the strongest PvE mitigation tools because reducing enemy output scales extremely well in prolonged boss-style encounters.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/image-10.png)

In practice, those two together noticeably smooth out the later stages. When I tested the final challenge, sustain remained stable throughout most of the encounter despite the longer combat duration.

---

## Alliance Challenges – Why 1-Troop Marches Matter

## The old strategy is probably still mandatory

The alliance bosses appear structurally identical to the original implementation:

- Bosses unlock after enough members complete personal stages
- R5/R6 summon the boss
- Entire alliance attacks collectively
- Multiple boss levels exist

The critical issue is boss durability.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/image-12.png)

Based on current scaling, alliance bosses are almost certainly too fragile for modern server power levels. Even moderately developed conquest alliances are likely capable of deleting bosses extremely quickly.

That creates the same problem older servers had years ago: Players miss participation rewards because the boss died too fast

## Recommended alliance procedure

The safest method is still the classic approach:

### Step-by-step

1. Gather entire alliance at one location
2. Summon the boss
3. Every player sends a 1-unit march first
4. Wait until everyone tags the boss
5. Kill the boss normally afterward

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/image-11-1024x562.png)

This minimizes accidental burst damage while ensuring everyone qualifies for rewards.

In older Asteria cycles, alliances that ignored this coordination routinely lost rewards for slower or offline members. Given current troop scaling and immortal power creep, the issue is probably even worse now than it was originally.

Large conquest alliances especially need strict coordination here.

---

## The Biggest Change – Rewards

## Old Asteria vs New Asteria

The original event was valuable mainly because of:

- Artifact rewards
- Resources
- Some progression materials

At the time, artifacts were enormous progression accelerators.

The new reward structure is significantly stronger overall and it ties directly into the Affinity system while also supplying universally useful account progression resources.

---

## Personal Rewards

Current rewards include:

- Otherworld Crystals
- Speedups
- Dragon Chest Keys

The Dragon Chest Key income is actually surprisingly generous considering how frequently those become bottlenecks during progression stretches.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/image-13-1024x604.png)

The speedups are also meaningful enough that active players will notice the gain immediately over a full event cycle.

---

## Alliance Rewards

Alliance-side rewards currently include:

- Additional Otherworld Crystals
- Philosopher Stones
- Random immortal fragments

That combination gives the event value for both:

- Affinity progression
- General immortal development

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/image-14-1024x659.png)

---

## Total Crystal Income

The rewards from Asteria are actually quite generous this time around. If you fully complete both the personal and alliance challenges, you end up with 6,000 Otherworld Crystals in total — 3,000 from personal rewards and another 3,000 from alliance rewards. Considering the current shop prices, that is a pretty significant amount of currency.

---

## Asteria Shop Pricing

Right now, buying out the entire Asteria shop costs 1,950 crystals per day. Since the event runs for three days, a maxed run technically gives enough crystals to clear the whole shop every day.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/image-15-1024x597.png)

Still, **that probably is not**the smartest long-term approach...

---

## Why Buying Everything May Be Inefficient

The important thing to remember is that the crystals are rewarded at the end of the event, while the shop itself stays open afterward. There is no real reason to rush into spending everything immediately.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/image-16.png)

The smarter play will most likely be figuring out which items give the best Affinity value for the crystal cost.

That is the part we still need proper testing on. Until we know exactly how much Affinity each item provides, it is hard to say what the optimal purchases are.

---

## Affinity Material Observations

One thing already seems fairly clear though. Chaos, Holy, and Shadow immortals appear to content for the same Affinity items — mainly Nectar, Silk, and Letters. These can be used on any immortal type, whereas the rest of the items available are tied to elemental specific immortals! So you want to use the universals on your chaos, holy or shadow immortals if you run any of these. Using them on an elemental immortal will most likely be inefficient (depending on actual affinity rates yet to be released). Stay tuned for more!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/image-17-1024x425.png)

The remaining materials seem tied to the elemental factions instead:

- Pearls for Water
- Amber for Earth
- Zircon for Fire
- Gem for Lightning
- Bouquet for Wind

If that turns out to be correct, it could become a fairly important bottleneck later on, **but for now I think the main takeaway is that you should not be spending universally applicable items on standard element immortals**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/image-18-1024x272.png)

---

## Player Perspective

Mechanically, this feels very close to classic Asteria. The progression pacing, boss structure, and alliance coordination requirements all resemble the original implementation closely enough that veteran alliances already know how to optimize it.

The difference is reward relevance.

Old Asteria helped account growth through artifact progression, new Asteria looks positioned as a core Affinity progression system.

That makes participation much more important than before!

The alliance coordination aspect is also likely underestimated right now. On high-power conquest servers, bosses may disappear almost instantly unless **leadership actively organizes low-damage participation tagging first**.

I would strongly recommend alliances establish procedures immediately before players start wasting summon opportunities!

---

## Conclusion Summary

Asteria’s return in patch 2.9.5 is less of a redesign and more of a modernization of the original event structure.

### Early conclusions:

- Personal challenges are manageable with proper PvE utility skills
- No Escape and Weakening Curse remain extremely effective
- Alliance bosses will likely require strict 1-troop coordination
- Rewards are dramatically better than the original version
- Otherworld Crystals appear generous relative to current shop costs
- Affinity item efficiency will become the real optimization layer

The next important step is testing the Affinity gain values from each shop item to determine the true crystal efficiency hierarchy. Once players can measure exact Affinity values per item, the optimal spending paths should become much clearer.

title: Asteria Otherworldly Shop
summary: Otherworldly Shop Guide – What to Buy and How the Affinity Gifts Work
markdown:
## Introduction

Otherworldly Shop Guide – What to Buy and How the Affinity Gifts Work

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-11-1024x626.png)

The Otherworldly Shop is the new currency shop tied to Asteria and the Immortal Affinity system. Players earn Otherworld Crystals by completing Asteria's personal and alliance challenges, and those crystals can then be exchanged for Affinity gifts used to increase relationships with immortals.

At first glance, the shop looks like it contains a lot of different items with different values. After testing the Affinity gains, however, the shop is actually surprisingly well balanced. The important thing is not finding the highest-value item, but understanding which gifts should be used on which immortals.

---

## Universal Affinity Gifts

These gifts can be used on any immortal and always provide their full value regardless of faction or element.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-12-1024x203.png)

### Spiritfont Nectar

Spiritfont Nectar is the most expensive universal gift in the shop.

- Cost: 80 Otherworld Crystals
- Daily Limit: 1
- Affinity: 800

This works out to exactly 10 Affinity per crystal.

Because of its high point value, this will likely become one of the primary purchases for players building Chaos, Holy, and Shadow immortals.

### Starweave Silk

Starweave Silk provides a mid-tier option.

- Cost: 40 Otherworld Crystals
- Daily Limit: 3
- Affinity: 400

Like Nectar, it provides exactly 10 Affinity per crystal.

### Letter of Blessing

Letter of Blessing is the cheapest universal gift.

- Cost: 20 Otherworld Crystals
- Daily Limit: 5 (plus an additional letter earned from daily activities)
- Affinity: 200

Again, the efficiency remains identical at 10 Affinity per crystal.

Although the point value is lower, it provides excellent flexibility when you only need a small amount of Affinity to reach the next level.

---

## Elemental Affinity Gifts

Elemental gifts work a little differently from the universal gifts. Every elemental gift provides a base amount of Affinity that can be given to any immortal, but also includes a bonus when used on an immortal of the matching element.

For example, a Water gift can be given to any immortal, but only Water immortals receive the additional elemental bonus. This means elemental players can gain significantly more Affinity from these items than Chaos, Holy, or Shadow immortals.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-13-1024x319.png)

### Purple Elemental Gifts

Purple gifts cost **50 Otherworld Crystals** and provide **200 base Affinity** to any immortal. When given to the correct element, they grant an additional **300 bonus Affinity**, for a total of **500 Affinity**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-10.png)

When used on the matching immortal, every purple gift provides **10 Affinity per crystal spent**.

---

### Blue Elemental Gifts

Blue gifts cost **30 Otherworld Crystals** and provide **100 base Affinity** to any immortal. Matching the gift to the correct element grants an additional **200 bonus Affinity**, bringing the total to **300 Affinity**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-9.png)

Just like the purple gifts, the blue gifts also provide **10 Affinity per crystal** when used on the correct element.

### What This Means

After testing all of the Affinity gifts currently available in the Otherworldly Shop, **there does not appear to be a "best value" elemental gift.**Both the blue and purple versions are balanced around the same Affinity-per-crystal ratio. The only real difference is the amount of Affinity gained per purchase and the daily purchase limits.

As long as you are matching gifts to the correct element, every elemental gift converts crystals into Affinity at the same efficiency. The real optimization comes from making sure you never waste the elemental bonus by giving the wrong gift to the wrong immortal.

---

## The Most Important Thing to Understand

After running the numbers, one thing becomes immediately clear: the shop is balanced around a simple 10-to-1 conversion ratio.

Whether you buy:

- Nectar
- Silk
- Letters
- Purple elemental gifts
- Blue elemental gifts

the efficiency remains exactly the same when the item is used correctly. There is no secret "best value" item hiding in the shop.

---

## Chaos, Holy, and Shadow Immortals

One important thing to understand is that Chaos, Holy, and Shadow immortals do not receive elemental Affinity bonuses. Unlike Water, Earth, Fire, Lightning, and Wind immortals, they only gain the base Affinity value from elemental gifts.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-14-1024x335.png)

For example, an Abyssal Pearl provides a total of 500 Affinity when given to a Water immortal. That same gift only provides 200 Affinity when given to a Chaos, Holy, or Shadow immortal because the 300-point elemental bonus does not apply.

This makes elemental gifts a very inefficient way to increase Affinity on those factions. The crystal cost remains exactly the same, but a large portion of the item's value is effectively wasted.

As a result, players focusing on Chaos, Holy, or Shadow immortals should prioritize the universal gifts instead. Spiritfont Nectar, Starweave Silk, and Letter of Blessing always provide their full Affinity value regardless of the immortal receiving them, making them the most efficient use of Otherworld Crystals for these factions.

This also means that Chaos, Holy, and Shadow players are largely dependent on the same small pool of universal gifts, while elemental players can spread their purchases across both universal and elemental gift categories. Over time, that may make Affinity progression considerably more expensive for players investing heavily into premium factions.

---

## What Should You Buy?

For elemental immortals, the answer is straightforward. Purchase gifts matching the element of the immortals you are actively building. Whether you choose the blue or purple versions makes little difference from an efficiency perspective since both provide the same Affinity-per-crystal ratio.

For Chaos, Holy, and Shadow immortals, focus almost entirely on the universal gifts. They provide substantially better value than elemental gifts because they do not rely on bonus Affinity triggers.

If you are building multiple marches, especially a mix of elemental and premium factions, it is worth planning purchases ahead of time. Elemental teams can draw from several different gift pools, while Chaos, Holy, and Shadow teams are largely restricted to the same universal resources.

---

## Final Thoughts

The Otherworldly Shop initially looks like a complicated collection of Affinity items, but the underlying design is actually very simple. Every gift is balanced around the same efficiency ratio, and the real optimization comes from matching gifts to the correct immortals.

For elemental players, that means taking advantage of the elemental bonus system whenever possible. For Chaos, Holy, and Shadow players, it means treating Nectar, Silk, and Letters as your primary progression resources.

As more players begin pushing higher Affinity levels, understanding this distinction will likely become far more important than simply buying whatever happens to be available in the shop each day.

title: Atalanta (wind) - post rework patch 2.9.3
summary: Atalanta has always occupied an unusual position within the Wind roster. Historically, she struggled to maintain relevance due to inconsistent targeting and limited overall impact compared to more reliable ranged damage…
markdown:
### Introduction

Atalanta has always occupied an unusual position within the Wind roster. Historically, she struggled to maintain relevance due to inconsistent targeting and limited overall impact compared to more reliable ranged damage dealers. Most players who experimented with her eventually moved on, largely because her performance did not match her theoretical output.

With the current rework, her design is much clearer. She is no longer trying to function as a traditional burst bowman. Instead, she operates as a **hybrid between a sniper and a sustained normal-attack damage dealer**, built around a defined damage window rather than a single impactful cast.

Understanding this distinction is key. If she is evaluated purely by Ultimate damage, she appears average. If evaluated by **total output during Sniper Stance**, her value becomes much more apparent.

---

### Immortal Presentation – Role, Skill, and Function

#### Ultimate ability

Atalanta’s Ultimate, *Sniper Stance*, looks like a simple 800% hit at first. With the artifact, that goes up to about 1040%, which is decent—but honestly, that’s not where her value comes from.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-129-1024x637.png)

The important part is what happens after you trigger it. Once the stance is active, she gets 10 seconds where every normal attack hits twice, guaranteed. That’s the real damage. So instead of thinking of her Ultimate as a burst skill, it’s better to see it as a **trigger for her damage window**.

The artifact works the same way. It boosts the initial hit, which is nice for a bit more pressure, especially if you’re trying to snipe something early—but it doesn’t increase the piercing-hit autos, which is where most of her damage actually comes from.

So in practice, you’re not relying on her Ultimate to win the fight. You’re using it to **start her real damage cycle**. The better uptime you get during that window, the more value you actually get out of her kit.

#### Core Role

Atalanta functions as:

- **Single-target priority sniper**
- **Sustained physical DPS through normal attacks**
- **Backline pressure unit via pierce mechanics**

She is not designed for:

- Wide AoE damage
- Fast burst cycles
- Independent carry potential

Instead, her role is to **apply continuous, targeted pressure**, particularly against high-value enemy units.

---

## Signature Skill and How It Actually Functions

At first glance, Sniper Stance reads like a fairly standard damage skill: a single hit followed by a temporary buff. Most players stop there and evaluate it as “800% damage plus some extra effect,” which is where the misunderstanding usually begins.

In reality, the initial hit is the least important part of the skill.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-131.png)

What matters is what happens after.

Once Sniper Stance activates, Atalanta enters a 10-second window where every normal attack **pierces and hits a second target behind the first**. There is no randomness here—every single attack during that window effectively becomes a double hit as you strike the frontline target, then the target directly behind that target.

That immediately changes how you should think about her kit. She is not casting a skill to deal damage—she is casting a skill to **change how her basic attacks behave**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-130-1024x550.png)

This is why she feels closer to Alexander or Hannibal Barca than to traditional bowmen. The skill is not the damage source—it is the enabler of her real damage.

In longer fights, her damage ramps in a steady and predictable way. There’s no spike-and-drop pattern like burst bowmen. Instead, it’s consistent pressure that holds as long as she keeps attacking.

---

## How to Evaluate Her Damage Properly

The most common mistake is isolating the 800% multiplier and comparing it directly to other ranged physical damage dealers. On paper, that puts her behind units like Seondeok or Gilgamesh. And if the fight ended right after the Ultimate cast, that comparison would be fair. But that’s not how her damage is delivered.

A better way to evaluate her is to treat Sniper Stance as a **conversion window**:

- For 10 seconds, every auto attack gains piercing, hitting two immortal on a direct line.
- Her total output becomes tied to **attack frequency, uptime, and survival**, not just skill scaling

So instead of asking: “How strong is her Ultimate?” The more accurate question is: “How much damage does she generate during her stance window?”. When you look at it this way, her numbers start to make more sense. Her listed DPS may look average, but it doesn’t fully capture the fact that she is consistently applying damage to two targets at once, often including the enemy backline.

---

## Relative Position Among Ranged Physical Immortals

Compared to other ranged physical options, Atalanta sits in an unusual middle ground.

She does not compete well in pure burst scenarios. Units like Seondeok will always feel stronger in short fights because they frontload their damage. You see immediate impact, which is exactly what PvP often rewards.

However, in sustained environments, the gap closes—and in some cases, reverses.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-132-1024x332.png)

Because Atalanta’s damage is tied to repeated piercing-hit attacks, she scales with time in a way burst units do not. The longer she remains active and attacking, the more value she extracts from each stance cycle.

There is also a layer of **targeting value** that is easy to overlook. Most bowmen lose efficiency when stuck on frontline units. Atalanta doesn’t. Her damage naturally carries through to the backline, meaning she contributes to killing priority targets even when she isn’t directly targeting them.

In practice, this often translates into fights where:

- Her raw DPS looks average
- But her **impact on key enemy units is disproportionately high**

---

## How You Should Think About Atalanta

The simplest way to understand her is this: She is not a burst ranged attacker like Khan. She is a **window-based sustained DPS sniper**.

Everything in her kit revolves around that idea.

You are not picking her to win fights quickly. You are picking her to:

- Apply consistent pressure over time
- Reach targets other units struggle to hit
- Convert stable fights into favorable outcomes through sustained damage

This also explains why she feels inconsistent across different game modes. In fast, chaotic PvP fights, she often doesn’t get enough time to fully utilize her stance. In controlled environments like boss fights or longer PvE encounters, her value becomes much clearer.

From experience, once you start evaluating her based on **uptime and positioning rather than raw skill damage**, her performance becomes much easier to understand—and much easier to use effectively.

---

## Team Setups – How to Build Around Atalanta

When you start building around Atalanta, the first thing to accept is that she cannot carry fights on her own. Even with the rework, she’s still fundamentally limited by targeting one lane and, at best, applying pressure to two units through pierce. That’s not enough to break teams by itself.

What she needs is support—specifically from the frontline.

The most important piece is a **frontline damage dealer**, not just a tank. You’re looking for someone who actively pressures the enemy front row while Atalanta works through them and into the backline. Without that, her damage just doesn’t convert into kills fast enough.

In practice, the most natural pairings are:

- **Hannibal Barca**, especially in sustain setups
- **Alexander**, for stable and consistent frontline presence
- **Ares**, if you want a more aggressive approach

Hannibal in particular stands out because he does two things Atalanta really benefits from: he keeps the team alive longer and he maintains constant pressure. That extra uptime matters a lot, since her damage depends on getting full value from her stance window.

Once that frontline is in place, the rest of the team depends on what you’re aiming for.

If you’re leaning toward more control or chaos effects, adding something like **Anubis**, **Fu Fei**, or **Nine-Tail** can round out the setup. These help disrupt the enemy while Atalanta continues applying steady damage in the background. It’s not about boosting her directly—it’s about making sure the fight lasts long enough and stays stable enough for her to do her job.

The general idea is simple:

- Frontline applies pressure and holds formation
- Atalanta converts that into **consistent piercing-hit damage**
- Support units either extend the fight or disrupt the enemy

From testing and reports, this kind of setup performs particularly well in **Elemental Domain** (in legendary season) and other boss content, where fights naturally last longer. In PvP, it can work, but it’s less reliable. Faster fights and heavy control comps tend to limit her uptime, which directly lowers her value.

So when you build around Atalanta, you’re not trying to force a meta comp. You’re building a **stable, pressure-based team** where she has time and space to operate. If you get that right, her performance becomes much more consistent—and much more impactful than her raw numbers suggest.

---

### Boss Performance – Where She Really Shines

Atalanta is genuinely one of the more interesting options for bossing, and this is where her kit makes the most sense. Boss fights give her exactly what she needs: **long duration, stable positioning, and full uptime on her stance**.

This is from player VictorSeven with the (far as I have seen) best use of Atalanta - as an insane boss-sniper!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-133-1024x618.png)

---

## PvP Viability and Meta Context – Where She Actually Fits

Atalanta is one of those Immortals that sits in an awkward but interesting spot in PvP. She is absolutely usable, and in the right setup she can perform well—but she doesn’t align with what the current meta tends to reward.

The main issue is tempo. Most PvP fights, especially in KvK or higher-tier Arena, are decided quickly. You either win through burst, heavy control, or overwhelming early pressure. Atalanta doesn’t provide any of those. Her value comes **after** she activates Sniper Stance, and more importantly, after she’s allowed to stay active for the full duration of that window.

That creates a very specific requirement: She needs a **stable, sustained fight** to perform.

If you can give her that—usually through a strong frontline like Hannibal or Alexander and a more durable team structure—she will contribute consistent damage and apply meaningful pressure to backline targets. In those situations, she can hold her own, even in PvP. But she also wont bring anything especially unique to the table besides her ability to "snipe" aka target the enemy you want hit the hardest. Problem is she has; no wounds like Khan, no control like Himiko, no hyper-scaling like Baldwin, no crit-scaling like Wu/Seon.

Furthermore, in faster fights, or against control-heavy teams, things fall apart quickly. If she gets interrupted, loses uptime, or the fight ends before her stance cycle really matters, her impact feels minimal compared to more explosive units.

This ties directly into her position in the meta. The current meta favors Immortals that:

- Deliver **immediate multi-target damage**
- Provide **control or utility**
- Can swing fights **within the first few seconds**

Atalanta does none of that. What she offers instead is:

- **Consistent, sustained damage**
- **Backline pressure through pierce**
- Strong performance in **longer, controlled fights**

That’s valuable—but it’s not broadly optimal, which is why she isn’t widely used.

From a practical standpoint, she ends up being the kind of Immortal that rewards players who build around her intentionally. You’re not picking her because she’s the strongest option in a vacuum. You’re picking her because you understand how to create the conditions where her kit actually works.

So the honest assessment is: She is **viable in PvP, but not meta**. And more importantly, she’s **not**plug-and-play. While I havn't been able to find anyone running her succesfully outside of Open Arena, I have a feeling that some player much more clever than me will be able to figure out builds for Atalanta that can go toe-to-toe with the meta builds that everyone does.

---

## Conclusion

Atalanta is not a burst carry and doesn’t fit the current PvP meta—but that’s not what she’s built for.

She’s a **sustained DPS sniper** who gets her value from uptime, piercing-hit autos, and consistent pressure over time. In longer fights, especially bossing and PvE, she performs very well.

The trade-off is that she needs support and proper setup. If you build around her, she delivers. If you don’t, she feels underwhelming.

So overall: **not meta, but definitely viable—and very strong in the right conditions.**

title: Athena after patch 2.9.4 - a strategic counterpick
summary: Athena Guide (Post Patch 2.9.4) - A Shift from General Tank to Strategic Counterpick
markdown:
***Athena Guide (Post Patch 2.9.4)** - **A Shift from General Tank to Strategic Counterpick***

## Introduction

Athena’s position in Infinity Kingdom has always been somewhat unstable. She has strong defensive tools on paper, but in practice, she struggled to compete with more consistent frontline options due to her slow energy cycle.

Patch 2.9.4 doesn’t directly “buff” Athena in the traditional sense. Instead, it redefines her role entirely. By removing her +200 starting energy and replacing it with full immunity to *Seriously Wound*, the developers have shifted her away from being a general-purpose tank and into a **specialized counter unit**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-26-1024x515.png)

To understand whether she can return to the meta, you have to look beyond her individual kit and consider the broader systems she interacts with—especially wounds, sustain, and the ongoing shift toward longer, more durable fights.

---

## Athena’s Kit After 2.9.4

The key change is straightforward but impactful.

Athena no longer gains 200 initial energy at the start of battle. Instead, she now provides complete **immunity to *Seriously Wound* effects** for all allies. Everything else in her kit remains unchanged. She is still a defensive frontline tank with access to damage reduction, sustain through her active skill, and relatively low energy regeneration.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-21-edited-1.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-22.png)

This means her identity has not been rebuilt from the ground up, but the way you evaluate her has changed significantly. The removed energy directly affects her consistency, while the added immunity introduces a new layer of strategic value.

---

## What This Means in Practice

This adjustment introduces a clear trade-off that defines Athena’s current role.

Previously, the additional starting energy acted as a stabilizer. It allowed her to reach her first skill activation earlier, which partially compensated for her slow energy regeneration. While it did not fully solve her issues, it made her more reliable in the early stages of a fight.

With that removed, her weaknesses are more exposed. She takes longer to contribute, and in faster engagements, that delay can be the difference between stabilizing a fight and falling behind.

In exchange, she now offers something that no other frontline provides as consistently: complete prevention of wound effects. This shifts her value away from general performance and toward matchup-specific impact. Instead of asking whether Athena is a strong tank overall, the more relevant question becomes whether the enemy relies on wounds.

---

## The Importance of Wound Mechanics

Wound effects remain one of the most influential mechanics in the current state of the game, particularly outside of top-end whale environments.

The strength of wounds lies in their ability to shut down healing. In sustained fights, healing is often what allows a team to stabilize and outlast the opponent. When that is removed, even moderate damage becomes lethal over time.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-27.png)

This is why immortals like Genghis Khan and Qin continue to perform well. Their value is not limited to raw damage output. Instead, they create pressure by preventing recovery, forcing fights into a one-sided attrition where only one side can sustain itself.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-29-1024x840.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-30-1024x880.png)

The developers have already shown awareness of this issue. Previous attempts to address wounds focused on reactive solutions, such as improving cleanse effects. However, these approaches tend to struggle because they rely on timing and consistency. If wounds are constantly reapplied, removing them after the fact does not fully solve the problem.

Athena’s new design takes a different approach. By preventing wounds entirely, she removes the mechanic before it can influence the fight. This is a much more reliable form of counterplay, especially in prolonged engagements.

---

## Athena’s New Role in the Meta

Athena now occupies a clearly defined niche. She is no longer a generalist tank competing on raw efficiency. Instead, she is a **counter unit designed to neutralize wound-based strategies**.

This role becomes most relevant in environments where players are combining elemental cores with Chaos immortals. In these setups, wound application is often used to quickly build momentum as you counter enemy sustain.

When Athena is present in these matchups, that advantage disappears. Healing becomes consistent again, and sustain-based strategies regain their intended effectiveness. This can fundamentally change how a fight plays out, particularly in drawn-out engagements where resource management and recovery determine the outcome.

In fights where the enemy relies on wound effects, her presence can immediately shift the balance. Teams that would normally struggle to maintain health can now operate as intended, allowing healing and mitigation to scale over time.

This makes her particularly effective in sustained combat scenarios. When fights extend beyond the initial burst phase, the ability to maintain health becomes increasingly valuable. Athena enables that by removing one of the main tools used to prevent it.

---

## Weaknesses and Limitations

Despite her new utility, Athena’s core weaknesses remain and are, in some ways, more pronounced.

Her low energy regeneration continues to limit her consistency. Without the initial energy boost, her first activation is delayed, which reduces her early impact. In fast-paced fights or against high burst compositions, this can make her feel unresponsive.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-31-1024x732.png)

Additionally, her lower magical defense is still a concern. While the meta is gradually shifting, magic-based damage has not disappeared. Against those teams, Athena requires additional support or investment to avoid becoming a liability.

These limitations reinforce her role as a situational counter pick rather than a universal solution.

Athena is best used in teams that are built with a clear purpose. She fits naturally into sustain-focused compositions, where healing and mitigation are central to the strategy. In these setups, her wound immunity allows the team to function without interruption.

She also works well in double tank formations, where the slower pace of combat reduces the impact of her delayed activation. In these environments, her defensive contributions become more meaningful over time.

However, she is less effective in flexible or general-purpose builds. She does not offer the immediate impact or consistency required to replace more traditional frontline options in every situation.

---

## Potential Return to the Meta

Athena’s return to the meta is not something that happens automatically because of this change. It depends heavily on the environment around her and how players adapt to the tools introduced in recent patches.

The most important factor is whether wound-based strategies remain common. As long as players continue to rely on immortals like Genghis Khan and Qin to control fights through healing denial, there will be a need for reliable counters. Athena is currently one of the most direct answers to that problem, and that alone gives her a pathway back into relevance.

However, this is not just about countering a single mechanic. It is also about how players build their teams in response to that mechanic. In mid- to high-spender environments, where players are often working with hybrid compositions, wounds are used as a way to gain efficiency. Athena disrupts that approach, which can force players to reconsider how they construct their marches.

If enough players begin to adapt by incorporating Athena or similar counters, it can create a feedback loop. Wound-based strategies become less effective, which in turn increases the value of sustain-based compositions. In that kind of environment, Athena’s role becomes more central rather than situational.

That said, in full whale environments, the situation is different. Those players typically rely less on wounds and more on raw scaling and optimized synergies. In those cases, Athena’s utility does not address the primary threats, which limits her impact. This is why her potential return to the meta is more likely to occur in the broader player base rather than at the very top.

---

## Shift Toward Sustained Combat

To fully understand Athena’s potential, it’s important to look at the broader direction of the game.

Recent updates suggest that the developers are moving away from burst-heavy combat toward a model that favors sustained engagements. Skills like Arcane Hunter reinforce this direction by providing consistent damage over time rather than immediate impact. At the same time, the gradual shift toward physical damage compositions has reduced the dominance of high-burst magical setups.

In a sustained combat environment, fights are decided less by who deals the most damage upfront and more by who can maintain pressure over time. This places greater importance on healing, damage reduction, and consistency. Mechanics that interfere with these systems, such as wounds, become even more influential.

By introducing a reliable way to counter wounds, Athena fits directly into this evolving structure. She enables the kind of gameplay the developers appear to be encouraging: longer fights where positioning, composition, and resource management matter more than immediate burst.

This does not mean that burst strategies will disappear, but it does suggest that the overall balance is shifting. As that happens, units that support sustained combat—especially those that remove key counters to it—become more valuable.

---

## Player Perspective

From a practical standpoint, Athena feels more defined but less flexible than before.

Previously, she struggled because she lacked a clear advantage over other tanks. Now, she has a specific purpose, but that purpose only matters in certain matchups.

When used correctly, her impact is noticeable. When used without considering the opponent, her weaknesses remain apparent.

This makes her a more strategic choice. She rewards players who understand the meta and can anticipate what they are facing, rather than those looking for a simple, all-purpose solution.

---

## Conclusion Summary

Athena in Patch 2.9.4 is not a straightforward upgrade. She is a repositioned unit designed to address a specific problem within the game.

She loses early tempo due to the removal of initial energy but gains full immunity to *Seriously Wound*, allowing her to enable sustain-based strategies in matchups where they would normally fail.

Her return to the meta depends on how the game continues to evolve. If wound-based strategies remain common and the shift toward sustained combat continues, she has a strong case for becoming a relevant and widely used counterpick.

She is unlikely to become a universal frontline option, but she no longer needs to be. In the right context, her value is clear—and in Infinity Kingdom, that is often what defines whether an immortal truly belongs in the meta.

---

title: Athena Aigis Unique Artifact
summary: Athena is a powerhouse among the Chaos Immortals in Infinity Kingdom, consistently ranking as one of the top three Immortals in the game. Her strength is further amplified by her unique artifact, Aigis, which, although…
markdown:
### Player Guide: Athena's Unique Artifact - Aigis

Athena is a powerhouse among the Chaos Immortals in Infinity Kingdom, consistently ranking as one of the top three Immortals in the game. Her strength is further amplified by her unique artifact, Aigis, which, although it may seem simple at first glance, provides an immense boost to her and her team's survivability. In this guide, we will delve into what makes Athena so formidable and why her unique artifact, Aigis, is incredibly powerful.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/image-75-1024x596.png)

## Athena: A Top-Tier Immortal

Athena's role as a Chaos Immortal is vital in any high-level team composition. Her abilities and stats make her a key player in both offensive and defensive strategies. Athena's primary strength lies in her ability to sustain and protect her team, which is further enhanced by her unique artifact. Moreover, her unique ability to consistenly remove all negative effects makes her sustain power unrivaled. Many players are not very impressed with her, simply because she show quite low healing compared to being an expensive Chaos Immortal. However, it is important to note that the main strength from Athena comes from who mechanics which are not shown anywhere in your battle report!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/image-77.png)

1. She consistently removes all wounding and all **negative effects**from your team, making her one of very few things in the entire game to be able to counter the strongest ultimate abilities and tower of knowledge skills in the game.
2. Her Unique Artifact is the second mechanic that people are not seeing in reports and therefore underestimating. The power here comes from her ability to bolster the entire teams physical defense attribute.

While the first effect is something I may explore further in it's own guide (check under the hard-counter sections, I hope to get it out soon). The unique artifact mechanis is something we are going to talk about here today.

## Athena’s Unique Artifact: Aigis

### Description and Effect

Aigis provides a substantial physical defense boost to Athena and her allies. The artifact's effect is described as:

"Increases physical defense for 12 seconds equal to 20% of Athena's physical defense."

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/image-72.png)

### Why is Aigis So Powerful?

At first glance, giving 20% of Athena's physical defense to allies might not seem like a game-changer. However, when you consider the high attribute levels that Athena can achieve in the end-game, this becomes a massive boost.

#### Insane Physical Defense Boost

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/image-73-1024x607.png)

Athena can easily reach 9,000 to 10,000 physical defense. This means that Aigis provides an additional 1,800 to 2,000 physical defense to her allies for 12 seconds. To put this into perspective, this boost is equivalent to 22-24 fully upgraded physical defense nodes in the dragon talent tree, which is considered one of the best defensive nodes available.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/image-74-1024x450.png)

Such a significant increase in physical defense cannot be underestimated. It dramatically reduces the damage taken by your team, allowing them to survive longer and sustain their attacks. This defensive boost is crucial in high-stakes battles where every bit of defense counts.

#### End-Game Attribute Levels

At the end-game, attributes play a crucial role in determining the outcome of battles. The boost provided by Aigis scales exceptionally well with the high attribute levels that players achieve. This scaling makes Aigis one of the best artifacts in the game, providing both immediate and sustained value in combat situations.

### Synergy with Other Skills and Artifacts

Athena's Aigis works exceptionally well in conjunction with other defensive skills. Consider pairing Aigis with skills that further enhance defense or provide additional healing and shielding to maximize the survivability of your team.

## How to obtain Aigis?

It is quite streight forward actually. You obtain Athena fragments via the Chaos Roulette event, and as you progress through the 25 spins each time you clear the wheel, you are getting unique artifact fragments as the second most rare drop - usually coming around just before you get the Athena Immortal fragments. On average, maxing out your Athena Immortal in the Chaos Roulette will also net you 720 unique artifact fragments (avg. drop) meaning a solid 8 artifacts crafted when you max her. While this is far from the 15 it takes to max out an artifact, it is plenty to make a good chance at a decent roll and a good bonus upgrade for your Athena.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/image-76.png)

## Conclusion

Athena's unique artifact, Aigis, is a deceptively simple yet incredibly powerful tool in Infinity Kingdom. By providing a massive boost to physical defense, it ensures that Athena and her team can withstand even the most formidable opponents. Understanding and leveraging Aigis's power can significantly enhance your team's performance, making Athena an invaluable asset in your lineup.

As you progress in the game and face tougher challenges, remember to prioritize the acquisition and upgrading of Aigis. Its impact on your team's survivability and overall effectiveness in battle cannot be overstated. Equip Athena with Aigis and watch as your team becomes a nearly unstoppable force on the battlefield.

title: Athena's Outfit - New best tank? Let us compare with meta dominant tank YSS
summary: Athena Summer Skin vs. Yi Sun-sin (YSS): Is the New Skin Really an Upgrade?
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-60-1024x626.png)

## Introduction

***Athena Summer Skin vs. Yi Sun-sin (YSS): Is the New Skin Really an Upgrade?***

Athena has long been one of the strongest defensive support Immortals in Infinity Kingdom, particularly against physical damage compositions. Her Holy Grace provides powerful sustain, her Exclusive Artifact increases her durability against physical attackers, and her built-in Wound resistance makes her a natural counter to heroes like Khan.

The release of Athena's Summer Skin introduced several balance changes that initially looked like a significant upgrade. On paper, increased Energy Regeneration, stronger healing, and an earlier activation threshold all appear to make her considerably stronger.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-61.png)

After testing the changes in a variety of matchups, however, the picture becomes more nuanced. The skin certainly improves Athena in some situations, but it also weakens one of the mechanics that previously made her so difficult to kill. More importantly, it does very little to address her biggest weakness: magic damage.

As a result, Yi Sun-sin (YSS) remains the stronger choice in many battles despite Athena's apparent buffs.

---

## Understanding Athena's Summer Skin Changes

The Summer Skin introduces four notable adjustments to Athena's kit.

### New Passive: +40% Energy Regeneration Speed

The first addition is a passive bonus granting 40% Energy Regeneration Speed.

At first glance, this appears to be a major improvement. In practice, its impact is more modest because Energy Regeneration Speed scales from an Immortal's base regeneration value rather than acting as a flat increase.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-62-1024x560.png)

Athena's base Energy Regeneration is only **65.7**, one of the slowest values among support Immortals. By comparison, many offensive Immortals, for example quick fire immortals like Wu, sit at **120+** regeneration.

Because of that low starting point, the additional 40% increases her energy gain, but not nearly as dramatically as many players initially expected. It is still a buff, just not one that fundamentally changes how quickly she reaches her Ultimate.

---

### Holy Grace Healing Increased

Holy Grace's recovery rate increases from **80 to 100** at maximum level.

This is a straightforward improvement.

Whenever Holy Grace activates, Athena now restores significantly more health, making prolonged fights against physical teams even more favourable.

---

### Damage Reduction Activates Earlier

The activation threshold for Holy Grace's damage reduction increases from **60% HP to 70% HP**.

This means Athena begins protecting her team sooner during sustained physical engagements.

Earlier activation generally translates into better survivability because damage reduction comes online before large amounts of health have already been lost.

---

### Damage Reduction Reduced

The trade-off is easy to overlook.

Holy Grace's damage reduction falls from **40% to 30%**.

Although the effect activates earlier, the protection itself is weaker once it is active.

Whether this is an improvement depends entirely on the matchup.

---

## Where Athena Excels

Athena has always been designed to counter physical damage, and the Summer Skin reinforces that identity.

Against physical teams, several parts of her kit work together exceptionally well:

- Holy Grace activates consistently.
- Increased healing restores more health every trigger.
- Wound resistance reduces the effectiveness of heroes like Khan.
- Earlier damage reduction helps stabilize the team sooner.

When fighting physical-heavy compositions, Holy Grace often activates repeatedly throughout the battle. Every activation now provides more healing than before, allowing Athena to sustain her frontline through extended engagements.

This is where the Summer Skin performs exactly as intended.

---

## Why Magic Teams Are Still a Problem

The changes become much less impressive once magic damage enters the equation.

Athena's Exclusive Artifact primarily increases **Physical Defense**, providing little protection against magic-based attackers. More importantly, **Holy Grace only activates when Athena's team receives physical damage**.

Against teams built around Merlin, Baldwin, Empress Wu, Loki, or other magic carries, Holy Grace may activate very few times—or not at all.

That creates a significant problem. The improved healing cannot trigger. The earlier threshold becomes irrelevant. Even the increased Energy Regeneration has less impact because the core mechanic driving Athena's sustain simply isn't being used.

The Summer Skin strengthens Athena's existing specialty without solving the matchup she has traditionally struggled with.

---

## Why Yi Sun-sin Often Performs Better

This is where Yi Sun-sin deserves serious consideration.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-63-1024x666.png)

Unlike Athena, YSS provides immediate value regardless of the damage type your opponent uses.

His Ultimate grants:

- 30% damage reduction immediately
- Increased healing received
- No HP threshold requirement
- No dependency on physical damage

Those differences are more important than they initially appear.

Mage compositions are built around early burst damage. Infinite Fire powers, and similar abilities begin dealing heavy damage almost immediately after combat starts. YSS's protection is already active before much of that burst lands.

Athena, by comparison, may still be waiting for Holy Grace to activate. In many battles, that timing alone determines whether your frontline survives the opening seconds.

---

## Healing Comparison

One common argument in favour of Athena's Summer Skin is that Holy Grace now heals considerably more. That is true - however, YSS improves every healing source on your team rather than a single ability.

This includes effects such as:

- Fountain of Life
- Vitality Touch
- Bjorn's healing
- Fou Fei's Ultimate
- Any additional healing provided by your support setup

Instead of increasing one recovery skill, YSS amplifies your entire sustain package.

Against opponents without reliable Wound effects, that global healing bonus often produces more overall value than Athena's stronger Holy Grace alone.

---

## Timing Matters More Than Raw Numbers

One of the easiest mistakes when comparing support Immortals is focusing only on percentages.

A larger heal does not necessarily make an Immortal stronger. The timing of that heal is often far more important. During testing, YSS's Ultimate consistently activated early enough to reduce incoming burst damage before the team's health dropped into dangerous territory.

Athena's protection, even with the improved 70% threshold, frequently became relevant only after significant damage had already been taken. Against physical teams, that delay usually isn't an issue because Holy Grace activates repeatedly throughout the fight.

Against magic burst teams, those first few seconds are often the most dangerous part of the battle. If your frontline survives the opening burst, healing has time to work. If it doesn't, stronger healing values become irrelevant.

---

## Should You Replace YSS?

Not necessarily. The Summer Skin does not make Athena universally stronger than Yi Sun-sin. Instead, it pushes Athena further into the role she already performed well.

A simple way to think about the two Immortals is this:

### Choose Athena when:

- Facing physical-heavy teams
- Countering Khan or other Wound-based compositions
- Expecting long, sustained fights

### Choose Yi Sun-sin when:

- Facing mage-heavy teams
- Expecting early burst damage
- Running healing-heavy support compositions
- You need immediate damage reduction regardless of damage type

Many experienced players keep both Immortals built and simply switch between them depending on the opponent.

That flexibility often produces better results than trying to force one support into every matchup.

---

## Final Thoughts

Athena's Summer Skin is best described as a **conditional buff** rather than a universal upgrade.

The increased healing, earlier activation threshold, and Energy Regeneration all improve her performance against physical damage, reinforcing her role as one of the game's strongest anti-physical supports.

At the same time, reducing Holy Grace's damage reduction from 40% to 30% limits her effectiveness in situations where raw mitigation matters most, and the changes do little to improve her performance against magic-heavy teams.

Yi Sun-sin remains one of the most reliable defensive supports in the game because his protection works immediately, applies regardless of damage type, and enhances every source of healing your team receives.

Rather than asking which Immortal is stronger overall, the better question is which one is stronger for the matchup in front of you.

In most cases, the answer depends less on your own team than on the type of damage your opponent intends to deal.

---

title: Attack and Defense (legendary)
summary: Among the earliest Chaos skills introduced through the first iteration of the Well of Time event and now available as one of only two skills as early as Preparation Season, Attack & Defense has holds its own remarkably…
markdown:
## Introduction

Among the earliest Chaos skills introduced through the first iteration of the Well of Time event and now available as one of only two skills as early as Preparation Season, **Attack & Defense** has holds its own remarkably well through each season.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-43.png)

Many early skills eventually fell behind newer Conquest- and Legendary-era mechanics, but this one remained relevant because it combines two things physical teams value more than almost anything else:

- damage burst pressure
- huge survivability against physical damage

In the current physical-heavy meta shaped by Medusa, Apollo, revived Alexander builds, and modern Khan setups, the defensive half of the skill often matters even more than the damage itself. That balance is what keeps Attack & Defense viable all the way into high-end Legendary Season play.

---

## Official Skill Description

> “After battle starts, has a 60% chance to deal Physical Damage every 6s (Damage Rate 400%) and increase own Physical Defense by 100% for 6s.”

At first glance, the skill reads fairly simply. In practice, there is more going on here than many players initially realize.

---

## Damage Performance - Proc Rate and Timing

The main weakness of Attack & Defense is in its damage consistency.. or well in-consistency.

A **60% trigger chance every 6 seconds** is noticeably less reliable than some of the more stable top-tier physical skills. In shorter fights especially, poor proc timing can heavily reduce value. There will absolutely be battles where the skill underperforms due to RNG.

That said, the **400% damage rate** is genuinely strong.

In repeated testing on physical carries like Medusa, the skill commonly lands within the same overall damage contribution range usually somewhere around:

- **20–30% of total damage**
- depending on fight length, proc timing, and enemy mitigation

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-44-1024x607.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-45-1024x620.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-46-1024x617.png)

That is already enough to make the skill viable offensively.

The important distinction is that Attack & Defense is not competing purely as a damage skill. If it only dealt damage, it would still be good — but probably not elite. What elevates it is the second effect.

---

## The Real Value: 100% Physical Defense - Why the Defense Buff Matters So Much

The physical defense increase is enormous. A flat **100% Physical Defense increase for 6 seconds** is one of the strongest defensive buffs attached to any offensive Chaos skill. In older mage-dominated metas, players often underestimated this effect because magical burst bypassed much of its value. That environment has changed significantly.

Modern high-level PvP revolves heavily around physical pressure, Medusa, Apollo, Alexander, Khan, all are amongst the top used and best performing immortals in the current meta. That is why this skill is so incredible. Against these teams, physical mitigation becomes one of the most valuable stats in the game.

---

## Upgrade Requirements - Wisdom Well Requirement

Because this is a Legendary/Chaos Tower of Knowledge skill, upgrading requires the **Wisdom Well** system.

### Upgrade Costs

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-47.png)

### Total Cost to Max = 240 legendary skill stones

### Realistic Spending Expectations:

In practice, most players report averages closer to roughly **4 fragments per 25 coins**. Using that average, reaching Level 8 generally requires approximately **1500 total coins**.

With standard Well of Time pacing:

- roughly **80 coins per week**
- approximately **19 weeks**
- around **$950 USD equivalent spending pace**

Realistically:

- unlocking alone often lands around **$400 USD**
- fully maxing commonly ranges between **$900–1500 USD**
- RNG can shift this significantly

This is one of the reasons Chaos skill investment decisions matter so much. Attack & Defense is expensive, but unlike many niche Chaos skills, it remains relevant deep into endgame play. **[Read more about legendary skill upgrading and cost estimates here.](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/tower-of-knowledge-passives/tok-basics/chaos-tok-skills-legendary-and-pricing-to-upgrade-and-max-2-8-5/)**

---

## Player Perspective

Attack & Defense is one of those skills that looks merely “good” on paper but consistently overperforms in real PvP environments.

The damage contribution is respectable, though somewhat RNG-dependent. The real strength is how effectively it mitigates physical carries against the current meta. Once physical-focused teams became dominant again, the value of doubling up on physical defense during combat became extremely difficult to ignore.

In many high-end fights, surviving one additional rotation matters more than squeezing out slightly higher burst damage. That is exactly where this skill shines.

For players investing long-term into physical carry teams, especially Medusa-based compositions, Attack & Defense remains one of the safest Chaos skill investments available from the early Well of Time pool.

---

## Conclusion Summary

Attack & Defense remains one of the strongest early Chaos Tower of Knowledge skills because it successfully combines:

- meaningful physical damage
- exceptional defensive utility
- long-term meta relevance

While the proc consistency can occasionally feel unreliable, the combination of a 400% damage rate and a massive 100% physical defense boost gives the skill value far beyond raw DPS numbers.

In the modern physical-heavy meta, that defensive effect alone is often enough to justify the investment. For sustained physical carries like Medusa, Alexander, and Khan setups, Attack & Defense continues to perform at a level worthy of endgame play years after its original release.

---

categoryPath: How to get ALL Immortal Unique Artifacts
markdown:
In this guide we are going to have a look at all of the Attack Immortals that populate Infinity Kingdoms vast battlegrounds. Moreover, we are going to look at each and every single Immortal's Unique Artifact to let you know where and how you can obtain it!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/image-102-1024x570.png)

## Unique Artifacts - how to obtain

| Immortal | Unique Artifact | Where you can obtain Fragments for this Unique Artifact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wukong | Heart of Spiritual Stone | Chaos Roulette |
| Louis IX | Justice Grasp | Blessings of Triss Event |
| Tutankhamun | Meteoric Dagger | Blessings of Triss Event |
| Khubilai Khan | The Code of Yuan | Blessings of Triss Event |
| Manco | Barricade of Light | Blessings of Triss Event |
| Alexander | Homer's Epic | 5-day bundles + Blessings of Triss Event + Seasonal Events + Stellar Compass |
| Hippolyta | Godesses' Waist Belt | Throne of the Supreme + Supreme's Seal + Pinball |
| William | The Domesday Book | Pinball Event |
| Attila | Celestial's Blade | 5-day bundles + Blessings of Triss Event + Seasonal Events + Stellar Compass |
| Saladin | Wings of War | 5-day bundles + Blessings of Triss Event + Seasonal Events + Stellar Compass |
| Muhammed ll | Code of Order | Blessings of Triss Event |
| Siegfried | Dark Dragon's Blood | Blessings of Triss Event + Shadow Pinball + Sparks of Galaxy |
| Peter | Justice Grasp | Throne of the Supreme + Stellar Compass |
| Ramesses ll | The Sun's Gift | Triss Bundles + Supreme's Seal |
| Hannibal Barca | The War Colossus | Triss Bundles + Pinball Event + Supreme's Seal |
| Herald | Figurehead of War Dragon | Pinball Event |
| Frederick | Crown of Flame | Pinball Event |

## These UA-Events explained

We have a few different events in play here. Mainly we are getting drops from **Triss Event** but also from the **Throne of the Supreme**, **Sparks of Galaxy**, **Stellar Compass, 5-day bundles, Supreme's Seal**, **Pinball**and from **Chaos Roulette**.

Let's dive on in a learn a bit about these 7 different events.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/image-72.png)

## 1 Blessings of Triss Event

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/image-73-1024x580.png)

Blessings of Triss is perhaps the purest whale-event of all in Infinity Kingdom. It is a huge gamle making wishes with relative poor chance for useful rewards spending wish coins only available through spender shop. However, it is an important event for Infinity Kingdom, since it is where most of the unique artifacts are available.

You will get one free wish per day over the three day event period. With each event there will be 6x different Unique Artifacts available, you obtain 30 fragments at a time when you get lucky on a wish.

The chance to get Fragments on a free spin is precisely 6%. Per default you have a 1% chance to obtain each fragment jackpot (hence 6x1% = 6%).
