title: City / CoR Relic siege movements
summary: Attacking cities in Norheim and in Legion of Frostborne gives you Bloody Rage debuff, leaving you unable to move again for 10 min. You do not want to wait out this debuff before moving to the next city when you are…
categoryPath: Strategies for Managing Blood Rage Debuff
markdown:
Attacking cities in Norheim and in Legion of Frostborne gives you **Bloody Rage debuff**, leaving you unable to move again for 10 min. You do not want to wait out this debuff before moving to the next city when you are sieging relics in CoR of quickly capturing objectives in Legion of Frostborn, the last thing you want to do is sitting still waiting for debuffs to come off before you move to the next objective!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/image-16.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Skaermbillede-2022-09-02-140817.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Skaermbillede-2022-09-02-144654.png)

1. **Begin relocation to the next objective**
2. **Siege the city**
3. **Complete relocation**
4. **Siege the city IF this is the last objective, otherwise wait the relo cooldown here.**
5. **Repeat.**

## Other relevant knowledge for siege movements

![](https://www.levelwinner.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/infinity-kingdom-attacking-strategy-800x385-1.jpg)

**Dont be like these guys**, leaving spaces everywhere and parking your city in rediculess ways, means longer marchtimes, slower sieges and much largers strain on the few who got a space within reasonable range.

## How to siege a city – the right way

I shall not spend a lot of time on this, as there is really only two things you need to do.

1. **Set your siege schematic right**
2. **Adjust your talents if you are doing a difficult siege**

## Siege Schematics

(**A) Norheim Cities – CoR Relics – SvS Cities**

These are 4×4 making it easy mode to position.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image.png)

**(B) Norheim Capitals – CoR World Heart** **– SvS Ymir**

These are 5×5, an odd number for our 2×2 castles.
Beware! Don’t just park next to it without thinking first, otherwise you end up with gaps.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-2-1024x421.png)

## Remember talents

You obviously want military talents increasing your fighting power when you are sieging a difficult city – oh and remember them buffs!

**Important talents are**: Ruin, Survival Methods and Shock

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/image-20.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/image-17.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/image-21.png)

title: City Siege Talent build
summary: There are three types of talents. Some talents makes the most sense to run in any combat scenario, some depend on your army composition and then there are some you only want in very specific situations. In this guide we…
markdown:
There are three types of talents. Some talents makes the most sense to run in any combat scenario, some depend on your army composition and then there are some you only want in very specific situations. In this guide we will ONLY focus on city sieges. If you need a combo siege-PvP build, you can read my PvP talents guide and create a hybrid.

In this article I shall go through the Military talent tree step by step and explain what you want to put in your **Siege loadout**.

### 1. Crit versus dodge

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-102.png)

Unless you are playing without a magic damage dealer (and therefore not using the passive “Chase”) you always want crit.

### 2. Physical versus Magic attack

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-103.png)

This choice dosen't matter for the siege. So you want to choose something that works with your army just in case PvP will occur. I run Knife Through Butter (phys). If you are relying on e.g. Merlin to deal the damage in your water or wield double mage fire (Baldwin + Wu) you want to use Rage (magic).

### 3. AP conservation versus March speed

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-104.png)

You always want march speed. Life it too short to save 3-4 AP per hit. Also speed is important to make sure you defeat city walls and garrisons before siege timer ends!

**4. Attack** **versus defend**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/image.png)

You want to run **Ruin** here always. It is a very strong siege talent that allow you to melt garrisons.

### 5. Relocation speed versus reduced troop losses

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-108.png)

Per default you want to be running **Survival Methods**for the reduction in troop losses. Only in an [IB scenario](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/lord-lady/talents/ib-talents-illusion-battle/) is relocation speed important.

### 6. Berserking versus healing versus honor

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-110.png)

This talent **doesn't matter for our siege**. So choose based on other activies you might want to do before you shift out of this build.

(6.1.) If you are fightning in a closely matched battle, **Last Stand**is a VERY powerful talent adding streight up 8% more damage to your army. This means you can beat opponent even at a significant power disadvantage! However, it comes at a properity cost you must be wary of. It is my go to talent in heavy PvP situations (SvS or Norheim). **Last Stand** is also a must have, if you are [ratting](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/pvp/lord-combat-strategies/rat-pack-playstyle/).

(6.2.) **Aid**is a decent defensive talent if you are taking a lot of hits as the target of rallies or just the center of enemy frenzy. If you are low on healing speedups, this talent can save you a lot of trouble. I never run this per default, but see its value.

(6.3.) **Rank Advancement** is an amazing talent! If you overpower your opponent you want to run this talent to maximize your honor gain and climb that Nobility Ranking. It is a must-have when you [farm honor, e.g. using alts](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/lord-lady/nobility-honor/using-alts-to-farm-honor/).

### 7. Weaken enemies versus boosting defense

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-111.png)

You want to default to running **Domination** and weaken your enemies.

### 8. Another attack versus defend

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/image-1.png)

*The talent "Shock" is a must have for siege talent loadouts. Dealing a high amount of damage to the city walls before you hit it is awesome as the walls are cumbersome to overcome. We like free damage!*

### 9. Energy regen versus attack speed

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-113.png)

You want to run **Owl Guardian** for its energy regen. All Immortals benefit greatly from increased energy regen, where as only very few and highly specific builds values attack speed over regen.

### 10. Another attack versus defend choice

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-115.png)

**Dosen't matter for sieges.** The first talent it weakest, so exclude that one. Making it a decision on when you want the power of increased energy regen. If you are attacking more than defending you want **Excitation**(marked above), if you are on the defense **Energy Burst**can be activated with the same buff (plus a debuff if your attacker runs a tactic in the attack).

### 11. Resilience versus Accuracy

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-116.png)

You want to run accuracy most of the time. Versus garrisons we need consistency. We are trying to beat as many garrison marches as possible, and don't want RNG dodges to mess it up. If you rely on physical damage = run **Target Locked** and boost our accuracy.

In very specific cases where you have built an army that relies solely on magic damage, you want to run **Strong Will** (e.g. running double mage fire with Hippo and William as supports) OR if you are playing a niche defense-prolong team.

**12. Hospital queues versus scaling walls versus defense energy reg.**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-117.png)

This is an odd choice and useless for your siege loadout - I personally think all three talents are terrible. I default to the third option, **Skillful**because it is the only one I find slightly useful in PvP (energy regen in defense battles).

Honestly, I usually spend my talent point in **development** instead – this way I can maintain 5/5 **Plentiful Gold** even while waging war or in SvS.

title: Cleave
summary: The \"Cleave\" skill is a formidable tool in the arsenal of Infinity Kingdom players, known for its ability to deal splash damage to multiple enemy units. With a 75% chance to trigger extra Physical Damage (Damage Factor…
markdown:
### Player Guide: Optimizing the "Cleave" Skill in Infinity Kingdom

The "Cleave" skill is a formidable tool in the arsenal of Infinity Kingdom players, known for its ability to deal splash damage to multiple enemy units. With a 75% chance to trigger extra Physical Damage (Damage Factor 75%) to 2 nearby enemy units on every normal attack, "Cleave" significantly enhances the battlefield efficacy of physical damage dealers. This guide explores the strategic implementation of "Cleave," highlighting its synergies and optimal use cases.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-129-1024x468.png)

## The Mechanics of "Cleave"

"Cleave" operates by extending the impact of a normal attack beyond the primary target, hitting additional enemies with splash damage. This capability is particularly valuable in densely packed combat scenarios where the positioning of enemy units amplifies the potential for collateral damage.

### Key Features:

- **High Trigger Chance**: With a 75% chance to activate, "Cleave" reliably delivers splash damage in most combat encounters.
- **Physical Damage Enhancement**: The skill boosts the overall damage output of physical attackers, making it essential for maximizing their contribution to the battle.

## Strategic Applications

### Hybrid Setup Synergy

In a hybrid setup featuring immortals like Hannibal and Alexander, "Cleave" can be strategically employed to distribute damage more evenly across enemy lines. By equipping Hannibal with "Cleave," you augment his ability to support Alexander's single-target onslaught by spreading additional pressure to adjacent enemies. This tandem approach can overwhelm opponents with a balanced mix of focused and splash damage.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-130.png)

### Enhancing AOE Damage

For compositions prioritizing Area of Effect (AOE) damage, "Cleave" adds another layer of destructive potential. When combined with immortals known for their AOE capabilities, such as those in Khan-earth setups, "Cleave" ensures that even normal attacks contribute to the strategy's overall damage output. This is particularly effective in scenarios where the goal is to rapidly diminish the enemy's frontline, paving the way for a decisive victory.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-131-1024x597.png)

## Unlocking and Leveraging "Cleave"

"Cleave" is accessible to all players, making it a versatile skill for a wide range of strategies. To fully harness its power:

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-132-1024x353.png)

1. **Prioritize Attack Speed**: Given that "Cleave's" effectiveness scales with attack speed, equip it on immortals who can frequently trigger normal attacks. This maximizes the instances of splash damage, significantly enhancing your army's damage distribution.
2. **Strategic Immortal Placement**: Position your "Cleave"-equipped immortals to maximize their engagement with enemy units. Proper placement ensures optimal usage of the skill, leveraging its splash damage potential to its fullest.
3. **Synergy with Other Skills**: Pair "Cleave" with skills that augment physical damage or attack speed, such as "Combo," to create a formidable physical attacker capable of dealing extensive damage to multiple targets simultaneously.
4. **Consider Your Overall Strategy**: Integrate "Cleave" into team compositions that benefit from its splash damage, whether to bolster a hybrid approach or to complement AOE-centric tactics.

## Conclusion

The "Cleave" skill is a powerful addition to any Infinity Kingdom player's toolkit, offering significant splash damage capabilities that can turn the tide of battle. By strategically incorporating "Cleave" into your lineup and synergizing it with other skills and immortal abilities, you can effectively amplify your physical damage dealers' impact on the battlefield. Whether part of a focused hybrid setup or a broader AOE strategy, "Cleave" ensures that your forces wield an extra edge in combat, making it a skill worthy of consideration for any aspiring conqueror in the realm of Norheim.

title: Club 1000 daily login - huge gifts!
summary: So you’ve been logging into Infinity Kingdom for 1000 days straight — that’s almost three years. If you’ve been this loyal, the devs have a special thank-you waiting for you… but the catch is, it’s not something you’ll…
markdown:
So you’ve been logging into Infinity Kingdom for 1000 days straight — that’s almost three years. If you’ve been this loyal, the devs have a special thank-you waiting for you… but the catch is, it’s not something you’ll ever see inside the game itself.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-141.png)

This reward isn’t part of the standard in-game login chain. It’s part of the **IKVIP program**, a special perk for verified spenders who’ve been around since the early days. Once you hit your **1000-day login milestone**, you can claim a one-time veteran reward — and depending on what you choose, it could be one of the rarest power boosts in the game.

---

### How It Works

You can check your total logins by going to:

> **Profile → Statistics → Logins** // **or via the Daily Login screen (VIP number on name plate)**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-141.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-142-1024x591.png)

That’ll show your total number of logins and your current chain. When you reach 1000, head to the **IKVIP Discord** and message the official **IKVIP account** (make sure you’re verified as VIP first — check their verification channel or see the separate guide on that). They’ll confirm your account and give you your choice of reward.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-143-1024x228.png)

### Dont panic if you miss one day..

While it used to be believed that you needed *1000 consecutive* logins, reports from verified players show that **having 1000 total logins** is enough. So if you missed a few days here and there, don’t panic — players with solid chains and 1000+ total logins have still received the reward.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-144-634x1024.png)

Make sure you send the IKVIP a screenshot of your logins statistics as well as your Lord ID.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-145-1024x100.png)

## How do you become "verified VIP?"

verified as VIP means you have spent more than 2000 USD since your account was created. Contacting IKVIP can get you a full account of your spending on your account if you are curious to know. Once you hit 2000 you are eligible for the secret veteran reward at 1000 day login chain!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-148-1024x747.png)

---

### What You Get

You’ll be offered **one of the following rewards:**

- 60x **Ability Stones** for *any* **Epic-quality Tower of Knowledge skill** (except Legendary skills)
- 60x **Immortal Fragments** for *any* **non-Chaos Immortal**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-146-1024x472.png)

Basically, you can unlock or upgrade *one full Epic skill* of your choice — or grab 60 fragments for an Epic or lower Immortal.

But let’s be real here — if you’re VIP verified, you already have access to a ton of Immortal fragments through regular events, shop bundles, and summons. So don’t waste this reward on Immortals. The real gold here is the **rare skill stones**.

**[Read more about all the skills here.](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/tower-of-knowledge-passives/ability-stones-availability-season-1-2-and-conquest/complete-guide-on-all-skill-stones-available-in-conquest-and-how-to-get-them/)**

---

### Best Use: Rare Epic Skills

The most valuable pick from this reward is absolutely one of the rare Epic skills found only in the **“Ability Stone Selection Chest I”**. These are the ones that don’t drop anywhere else except through the extremely RNG-heavy **Wisdom Well** during Conquest season.

Those hard-to-get skills are:

- **Unforeseen Attack**
- **Abundant Spirit**
- **Assembly Charge**
- **Psionic Tide**
- **Blood Frenzy**
- **Chaos Storm**
- **Time to Shine**
- **Corrosive Power**

Most players don’t realize how brutal the drop rate is for these. You’re looking at roughly **a 2% drop rate per wish** for *a single stone* of these rarities. And since you need 60 stones to max one, the math looks like this:

**[More details here.](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/events/blessings-of-triss/wisdom-well-pricing-of-skills-and-value-guide-season-1-2-and-conquest/)**

> **60 stones / (2% drop rate for 1)** = **~3000 wishes on average**

That’s roughly double the average cost of maxing a Legendary skill (which takes about **1663 wishes**). So yeah — these are *insanely* rare. Most endgame players will have several maxed Legendary skills *before* even unlocking one of these.

That’s why the 1000-day veteran reward is so special: **you get one of these completely for free**, no RNG, no wasted Wisdom Crystals.

---

### What to Choose

If you’re not sure what to grab, here’s my honest take after testing and seeing tons of builds over the years:

- **Corrosive Power** is probably the single best choice for most players. It performs insanely well across many top-tier setups, especially in sustained fights and against high-resistance teams. It’s one of those “always useful” skills.
- **Assembly Charge**, **Chaos Storm**, **Time to Shine**, **Abundant Spirit**, and **Psionic Tide** are all top-tier too, depending on what you run. If you’re heavily invested in certain comps or specific Immortal synergies, one of these might edge out Corrosive Power for you.

That said — this is a *once-in-a-lifetime* pick. Don’t rush it. Hop on the **official IK Discord** or one of the major community servers and ask around. Show your current march setups and let experienced players weigh in. Every veteran has slightly different advice based on synergy, and you really don’t get a do-over on this one.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-147.png)

**[Discord link here.](https://discord.gg/FnQhFUvSA5)**

---

### Player Perspective

If it were me, I’d 100% take **Corrosive Power** unless you already have it. It’s ridiculously strong and works in many builds. The regen is crazy and it stacks with other skills of its kind for massive regen-synergy and some insane build comps (see build guides for more).

---

title: Cold Coins in KvK – Can You Unlock a Full Skill in a Single Season?
summary: One of the most common questions I see every KvK season — in alliance chat, faction planning discussions, and Discord — is simple:
markdown:
One of the most common questions I see every KvK season — in alliance chat, faction planning discussions, and Discord — is simple:

### “Can I get a full skill from this KvK?”

The confusion usually comes from how the rewards are structured. Many players assume that winning the season or ranking first automatically guarantees enough Cold Coins for a full skill. In practice, the system is more specific than that.

This guide breaks down the Cold Coin structure clearly and shows, with concrete numbers, when a full skill is realistic — and when it is not.

---

## Understanding the Cold Coin Structure

A full skill requires:

- **60 Skill Shards**
- **800 Cold Coins per shard**
- **48,000 Cold Coins total**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-34-1024x568.png)

So the real question becomes:

**Can your KvK performance reach 48,000 Cold Coins?**

To answer that, we need to look at the reward sources individually.

---

## Fixed Income: The Base You Control

These rewards are largely within your control if you are active.

## Personal Contribution

- **25,000 Cold Coins**

This is stable and achievable with consistent participation.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-39-1024x564.png)

## Alliance Reputation Rewards

Alliance Reputation thresholds determine additional Cold Coins:

- 12,000,000+ reputation = 10,000
- 9,600,000 = 9,000
- 8,400,000 = 8,000
- 7,200,000 = 7,000
- 6,000,000 = 6,000

In organized alliances that actively farm gates and push faction reputation, reaching 9.6M–12M is realistic.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-37.png)

If you hit the maximum threshold:

25,000 (Personal)

- 10,000 (Alliance Reputation)
= **35,000 Cold Coins**

This is your stable baseline.

### Summary

- 35,000 coins is achievable without winning the season.
- Reputation farming is critical.
- This is not enough for a full skill on its own.

---

## Alliance Ranking Rewards

Ranking rewards are performance-based:

- 1st place (winners only) – 6,000
- 2nd – 5,000
- 3rd – 4,000
- 4th–8th – 4,500
- 9th–50th – 3,000

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-38.png)

The important detail is the spread:

The difference between first place and minimal ranking is only **3,000 Cold Coins**.

Let’s assume best case ranking without objectives:

25,000 (Personal)
10,000 (Reputation)
6,000 (Rank 1)

= **41,000 Cold Coins**

41,000 ÷ 800 = 51 shards

Even as Rank 1, you are still short of 60 shards.

This is why some alliances win KvK by reputation but still cannot unlock a full skill.

### Summary

- Ranking helps, but the difference is relatively small.
- Rank 1 without objectives is not enough.
- Ranking alone does not decide skill completion.

---

## Objective Control: The Real Deciding Factor

## Ymir

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-40.png)

Holding Ymir at the end of KvK grants:

- **9,000 Cold Coins**

This is the single largest variable reward.

If we add Ymir to the previous Rank 1 scenario:

25,000 (Personal)
10,000 (Reputation)
6,000 (Rank 1)
9,000 (Ymir)

= **50,000 Cold Coins**

50,000 ÷ 800 = 62 shards

Now you unlock a full skill and have shards remaining.

The difference between “almost” and “guaranteed” is entirely Ymir.

## Citadel

Holding a Citadel grants:

- **3,000 Cold Coins**

If we add just a Citadel but not Ymir to the previous Rank 1 scenario:

25,000 (Personal)
10,000 (Reputation)
6,000 (Rank 1)
3,000 (Citadel)

= **44,000 Cold Coins**

44,000 ÷ 800 = 55 shards. You are short 5 shards!

And just in case you are thinking, *'well rank one must mean Ymir is yours?*' Nope.. I literally just finished our first Conquest P1 season in first place but without Ymir.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-33-1024x505.png)

---

## Practical Player Perspective

After tracking Cold Coin totals across multiple seasons, the pattern is consistent:

- Personal activity guarantees steady progress.
- Reputation farming builds a strong foundation.
- Ranking matters, but not decisively.
- Ymir determines whether you unlock a full skill in a single season.

Many players focus on leaderboard placement. In practice, the more important question is strategic:

**Can your faction secure and hold Ymir at the end of the season?**

That single objective swings your Cold Coin income more than ranking ever will.

---

## Final Conclusion

If you are asking:

### “Can I get a full skill from my KvK season?”

The answer depends on this checklist:

- Did you max personal contribution?
- Did your alliance reach high reputation thresholds?
- Did your faction hold Ymir at the end?

If the answer to all three is yes, then one full skill per KvK is realistic and repeatable.

If Ymir is missing, even a Rank 1 finish is usually not enough.

Over multiple seasons, this difference compounds significantly. Choosing a faction capable of controlling Ymir consistently is one of the most important long-term progression decisions you can make in KvK.

---

### Guide to the Colosseum Castle Skin in Infinity Kingdom

The Colosseum Castle Skin, the latest addition to the aesthetic and functional customization options in Infinity Kingdom, offers players both a visually striking theme inspired by Roman architecture and valuable gameplay buffs. This guide delves into the benefits of the Colosseum skin, its unique features, and its strategic implications for players looking to maximize their in-game advantages.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-133-1024x335.png)

## Features of the Colosseum Castle Skin

### Honor Boost

The Colosseum skin grants a significant 5% increase in honor gained from battles. This enhancement is particularly beneficial for players focused on climbing the ranks and securing their position within the game's competitive landscape. The incremental gains from this 5% boost can accumulate over time, leading to substantial long-term benefits.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-135.png)

### Marching Speed Increase

A novel feature introduced with this skin is the 5% increase in marching speed. This buff can have strategic implications across various aspects of the game, potentially including Infinity Battlefield (IB) and Infinity Battlefield League (IBL), where rapid troop mobilization can be crucial for securing objectives and reacting to enemy movements. It is not known to me if it works in IB and IBL, but if it does it has the potential to make a huge difference for well coordinated teams.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-138-1024x455.png)

## Strategic Implications

The combination of increased honor and marching speed makes the Colosseum skin an attractive option for players aiming to optimize their gameplay efficiency. The honor boost is aligned with other top-tier skins, such as those associated with the earth and holy dragons, making it a valuable asset for honor accumulation.

The addition of marching speed, however, introduces new tactical possibilities. Faster marches can allow players to engage in battles more quickly, reinforce allies, or respond to threats, providing a tactical edge in time-sensitive situations.

## Acquisition and Considerations

### Pay to Play Only

The Colosseum Castle Skin is exclusively available to players willing to invest in the game, requiring the purchase of 62,500 gems. This requirement places the skin in a high price range, estimated at approximately $500-600 USD, marking it as a luxury item within the game's ecosystem.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-136-1024x519.png)

you do also get some holy/shadow dragon crystals which is great (500 total). But all in all it's a very expensive skin to collect. a

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-137-1024x389.png)

### Strategic Value vs. Cost

While the buffs provided by the Colosseum skin are undeniably beneficial, players should weigh the cost against the potential strategic advantages. The honor boost and increased marching speed offer tangible benefits, but the significant financial investment means this skin is likely most appealing to players who are already inclined to spend substantially on the game.

## Conclusion

The Colosseum Castle Skin emerges as a powerful addition to Infinity Kingdom, blending aesthetic appeal with gameplay enhancements that can significantly impact honor accumulation and troop mobility. For players prepared to make the investment, this skin not only signifies status but also provides practical benefits that can influence the course of play, particularly in competitive formats. As with any premium in-game item, the decision to acquire the Colosseum skin should be made with consideration of both its immediate appeal and its long-term value in your strategic planning.

markdown:
### Player Guide: Harnessing the "Combo" Skill in Infinity Kingdom

In the vast strategic landscape of Infinity Kingdom, the "Combo" skill emerges as a potent force, especially notable for its accessibility and impact despite being a purple (none epic) rank skill. This guide will delve into how to obtain and optimally utilize "Combo" to its fullest potential, highlighting its mechanics, strategic value, and the immortals best suited to wield this power.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-85-1024x569.png)

## Obtaining "Combo"

"Combo" is a skill that becomes available to players at mid-level, offering a powerful tool that's easily accessible for both free-to-play and paying players alike. Its early availability means players can integrate this skill into their strategies sooner, providing a significant advantage in various battle scenarios.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-86-1024x283.png)

## Skill Mechanics

The official description of "Combo" states: **"Every normal attack has a 30% chance of causing extra Physical Damage (Damage rate 250%) to the target."** This skill triggers exclusively on normal attacks targeting the single enemy in front of your immortal, excluding cleave effects. Its reliance on normal attacks makes it especially powerful for immortals with high attack speeds and physical damage outputs.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-84.png)

## Why "Combo" Is Good

"Combo" excels in setups that favor rapid, high-damage output, offering a 30% chance to inflict an additional 250% physical damage on normal hits. This capability makes it particularly effective for focusing down key enemy front-liners, allowing players to quickly eliminate pivotal threats on the battlefield. The skill's efficiency grows with immortals that have a high frequency of normal attacks, maximizing the chances of activating the extra damage effect.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-87-1024x477.png)

### Strategic Application

Beyond its raw damage output, "Combo" enables targeted strategic plays. By equipping it on immortals positioned to attack high-value enemy units, players can swiftly take out significant threats, such as a frontline Hippolyta in a hyper-regen setup. However, it's essential to be mindful of potential counters, such as defensive or thorns builds, which can mitigate "Combo's" effectiveness.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-88-1024x430.png)

## Recommended Immortals

Given its mechanics, "Combo" shines brightest on immortals with a blend of high physical attack power and attack speed. The skill finds its niche within wind-earth hybrid builds, where it can be leveraged to its utmost:

- **Alexander**: With inherent high damage and attack speed, Alexander is an ideal candidate for "Combo," particularly in wind-earth hybrid setups where his capabilities are further amplified.
- **Hannibal Barca & Peter**: While primarily an exceptional fit for Alexander, "Combo" can also enhance Hannibal Barca in wind setups and Peter in lightning configurations, provided these immortals are tailored towards specific strategic builds focusing on rapid, focused damage output.

## Conclusion

"Combo" presents a formidable skill choice for players aiming to maximize their impact in the early to mid-game phases of Infinity Kingdom. Its power to significantly enhance the damage output of suitable immortals makes it a valuable asset in player arsenals, especially when strategically applied against key enemy targets. As with any skill, the key to "Combo's" success lies in thoughtful immortal selection, positioning, and synergy with other skills, such as "Wind Rage" and "Berserker," to create a devastatingly effective battle strategy. With "Combo" in your toolkit, the potential to swiftly turn the tides of battle in your favor becomes a tangible reality.

markdown:
## A New Creator Event Begins – Community Emoji Design Contest

Infinity Kingdom has moved straight from the success of the Creator Frame event into its next community-driven challenge, and this one leans even further into everyday player interaction. The **「Community Emoji Design Contest」** is now live, and it’s one of the more practical and engaging creator events we’ve seen so far.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-65-1024x577.png)

Where the frame event focused on identity and presentation, this contest shifts toward something players actually use constantly—communication. The goal is simple on paper, but it opens up a lot of room for creativity: design emojis that feel like they truly belong to the Infinity Kingdom community.

---

## What This Event Is About

At its core, this event asks players to create a **set of emojis based on Infinity Kingdom’s Immortals**, designed for regular social use. That distinction matters. These are not just decorative assets—they’re meant to function in real conversations across Discord and community spaces.

There are a few key requirements to keep in mind:

- Your emojis should be **based on IK Immortals**
- They need to be **clear, readable, and stylistically consistent**
- A set of **3–5 emojis is considered optimal**, though more are allowed
- You can use **Photoshop, AI tools, or other software**, but the work must be **original**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-67.png)

This naturally pushes designs toward something that works at small scale, similar to how frame readability mattered in the previous event. Overly detailed designs tend to lose clarity, while strong silhouettes and expressions stand out immediately.

---

## How to Participate

Joining is straightforward:

- Create your emoji set following the guidelines
- Submit your work through the [**official Discord event channel**](https://discord.gg/kps7gK9gxY)
- Ensure your submission follows the required format

The event runs **until April 29**, which gives enough time to iterate if you want to refine your work after seeing other submissions.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-66.png)

### Design requirements:

- Create a set of emojis based on the Immortals of IK, suitable for everyday social use.
- Ensure clear visuals and a consistent style, with no limit on the number of emojis in the set (3-5 is optimal).
- Support PS creation or AI assistance, must be original and compliant, with no restrictions on form.

---

## Rewards and Recognition

Like previous creator events, this one balances accessibility with meaningful incentives:

- **All participants** receive in-game item rewards
- High-quality entries may be featured in the official **Community Emoji Selection**, with proper credit
- The **most interesting emoji** will be voted on by players and added to the Discord server

There’s also long-term value tied to participation:

- Taking part in **three creator theme events** earns a **creator-exclusive avatar frame**

That structure makes it worthwhile even if you’re not aiming for the top spot.

---

## Why This Event Is Worth Joining

From a player perspective, this is one of the more approachable creator events. Designing emojis doesn’t require the same level of structural precision as frames, but it does reward a good understanding of expression and clarity.

In practice, the strongest entries will likely focus on:

- **Recognizable Immortal traits** exaggerated into simple expressions
- Clean, bold visuals that remain readable at small sizes
- A consistent style across the entire emoji set

If you’ve spent time in alliance chat or Discord, you already know how quickly certain reactions become part of daily communication. This event is essentially giving players the chance to define that “emoji language” for the community.

---

## More Than Just a Contest

Just like the frame event, a big part of the value here comes from browsing the submissions themselves. These creator channels tend to develop into a mix of:

- Well-crafted, highly polished designs
- Creative or unexpected interpretations of Immortals
- Lighthearted or humorous entries that reflect community culture

Even if you don’t plan to submit anything, it’s worth joining the channel just to see what others are creating.

---

## Final Thoughts

The **Community Emoji Design Contest** builds directly on the momentum of the previous creator events, but shifts the focus toward something more interactive and widely used. It’s not just about creating something that looks good—it’s about creating something players will actually use.

If you want to see more events like this continue, participation matters. Submit a design, experiment with ideas, or at the very least follow the event and engage with the community. These creator contests are starting to define a new layer of Infinity Kingdom, and this is exactly the kind of event that benefits from broad player involvement.

---

Note that gift codes often have expiration dates, so be sure to use them as soon as possible to avoid missing out on the rewards. Also, some codes may be limited to one use per account, so make sure you're using them on your main account.

In addition to using the gift codes above and joining the Infinity Kingdom Wiki Discord, keep an eye out for future codes that may be released by the developers. You can follow Infinity Kingdom on social media or join the official Discord server to stay up-to-date on the latest news and announcements.

Using gift codes is a great way to get some free rewards in Infinity Kingdom, so be sure to take advantage of them when they're available. Happy gaming!

title: Community Voting Is Now Live for the 6th Infinity Kingdom Immortal Outfit Design Contest
summary: The community has spoken through its creativity—now it's time to decide the winner.
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-16-1024x422.png)

The community has spoken through its creativity—now it's time to decide the winner.

After receiving a wide range of incredible submissions, the Infinity Kingdom team has narrowed the field down to **10 outstanding finalist designs** for the **6th Immortal Outfit Design Contest**. The final decision is no longer in the hands of the judges—it's in yours.

Whether you've been following the contest from the beginning or you're just discovering these amazing concepts, now is the perfect time to support the artists who help make the Infinity Kingdom community so creative and passionate.

---

## Your Vote Matters

Community events like this are one of the best examples of what makes Infinity Kingdom special. Rather than simply introducing new cosmetics, the developers invite players to imagine what their favorite Immortals could become. Every concept represents hours of artwork, planning, and imagination from fellow players.

Now those creators need your support.

From elegant imperial robes and celestial guardians to powerful warlords and mystical sorcerers, this year's finalists offer a fantastic variety of styles. Every design brings its own unique interpretation of an Immortal, and choosing a favorite won't be easy.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-17-1024x368.png)

---

## Meet the Finalists

The ten finalists are:

- **Enexis**
- **Presidente**
- **Kala**
- **KRYON**
- **MechBaron**
- **Nay-Sovereign**
- **Everest**
- **KARAN**
- **OKJ**
- **AXATION**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-18-1024x409.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-19-1024x334.png)

Each artist has taken a different approach, with inspirations ranging from historical royalty and mythology to magical fantasy and battlefield legends. Whether you're drawn to Merlin's arcane elegance, Himiko's mystical power, Genghis Khan's commanding presence, or Zenobia's radiant redesign, there's something here for every Infinity Kingdom player.

---

## How to Vote

Casting your vote only takes a minute.

Simply:

1. Open the official voting form.
2. Enter your **Role ID (UID)**.
3. Select your favorite design.
4. Submit your vote.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-20-1024x557.png)

If you don't know your Role ID, open Infinity Kingdom and tap your **profile portrait** to access the **Lord Info** screen. Your unique ID is displayed at the top of the window, alongside a handy **Copy** button that lets you copy it directly to your clipboard before pasting it into the voting form.

Remember that **each UID can vote only once**, so make your choice carefully.

Voting closes on **8 September at 23:59 UTC**.

---

## Every Vote Earns a Reward

There's another good reason to participate besides supporting your favorite artist.

According to the official announcement, **all eligible players who participate in the vote will receive the event's voting reward** once the event concludes. It only takes a few moments to cast your vote, making it an easy way to support the community while earning a little something in return.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-21-1024x52.png)

---

## Community Events Help Shape Infinity Kingdom

Events like the Immortal Outfit Design Contest highlight one of the strongest parts of Infinity Kingdom—the creativity of its players.

These contests give artists a chance to showcase their ideas, inspire future in-game cosmetics, and celebrate the characters that make Infinity Kingdom memorable. The more players who participate, whether by creating artwork or simply voting, the stronger these community-driven events become.

Even if your favorite design doesn't take first place, your participation helps demonstrate that the community values these creative competitions and wants to see more of them in the future.

So take a few minutes, explore all ten incredible finalists, cast your vote, and show your support for the talented creators who continue to bring fresh ideas to Infinity Kingdom.

### Claim your spot as King of the Hill

### Day 1 - Troops Cooking

Tier 5 soldiers yield a measly 64 points each. This is the most point efficient way to spend universal speedups if you are planning to use these during KoH. Bare in mind tho, you will need to be deleting the troops you train and thus not gain value in the long term, whereas researching technology and upgrading dragons are high value.

With tier 5 barracks **training**1 soldier is: 64 points = 5 seconds. I.e. **12.8 points per second**.
**Research**(day 4) is: 480 points / 60 seconds = **8 points per second.**

Use the calculator to count your speedups available: [https://ik-wiki.com/speedup-calculator/](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/development/speedup-calculator/calculator/)

### Day 2 - Gnome camping

### Day 3 - Resource Farmvile

This is a simple day: **2 ressource gatheres yields 1 point.**

- Always have gatheres out, and remember to use both **gathering buffs and production buffs!**

- You should also make sure not to collect resources from your castles farms on day 2. **This way, you can reap capped farms at reset to day 3 and get optimal points from your castles farms**.

**Pro tip:** If you hit another players node (on peaceful server an alt) the ressources collected will count as gathered and therefore yield points towards this stage.

### Day 4 - Building and Technology

You will gain **480 points per min**. spend on building and/or technology research.

This is not the most efficient way to gain points, but unlike troop training, the value gained is long term.

With tier 5 barracks **training**1 soldier is: 64 points = 5 seconds. I.e. **12.8 points per second**.
**Research**(day 4) is: 480 points / 60 seconds = **8 points per second.**

Use the calculator to count your speedups available: [https://ik-wiki.com/speedup-calculator/](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/development/speedup-calculator/calculator/)

### Day 5 and 6 - Kill Event

You gain **25 points per 1 honor point** gained during the two-day Kill Event.

During Kill Event days, honor farming is all the rage. To be efficient during these days, you must either have many strong **alts**or group up with other players on your server. This is because the talent **"Rank Advancement"**. The absolute no. 1 to gain honor in Infinity Kingdom is to stack high ranked marches in a single castle and hitting them with one strong march and the talent. If you are able to do this right, t5 stacks can earn you as much as 250.000 honor in a single attack.

### How to max honor gain

1. Gather 5 marches (can be from a min of 2 Castles/Lords)
2. Remove dragons and passives from the marches
3. Garrison the Target Castle
4. Assist garrison with 4x marches to the Target Castle from the assisting Lord
5. Attack with strongest march you can muster and use Rank Advancement

title: Complete guide on all skill stones available in Season 1 and how to get them
summary: Season 1 is where players first meet the Wisdom Well, the Cinder Shop, and KvK stones. The trick isn’t just “what’s strong,” it’s timing. You can buy early to spike power in S1, but a lot of these stones are easier or…
categoryPath: Ability Stones Availability - season 1, 2 and Conquest
markdown:
Season 1 is where players first meet the **Wisdom Well**, the **Cinder Shop**, and **KvK** stones. The trick isn’t just “what’s strong,” it’s **timing**. You *can* buy early to spike power in S1, but a lot of these stones are easier or cheaper to get later. If you’re planning long-term, read the **[Season 2](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/tower-of-knowledge-passives/ability-stones-availability-season-1-2-and-conquest/complete-guide-on-all-skill-stones-available-in-season-2-and-how-to-get-them/)** and **[Conquest](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/tower-of-knowledge-passives/ability-stones-availability-season-1-2-and-conquest/complete-guide-on-all-skill-stones-available-in-conquest-and-how-to-get-them/)**guides too; for now, this page is strictly **what’s available in Season 1** and how to use it without wasting currency. Skill value depends on your march, so cross-check with build guides before you commit.

[Embedded media](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/2025-10-04-14-30-04.mkv)

## What’s in Season 1 (at a glance)

- **Wisdom Well (Jackpot Pool)** in S1 includes: **Weakening Curse, Siren’s Gaze, Weakness Protection, Berserker, Wind Rage, Overpower, Smite, Spring of Life, Battle Stance, Fear of Domination, Desire of Life, Unyielding, Storm Strike, Armageddon, Implosion, Energy Shield.**
- **Cinder Shop (S1)** sells: **Toxin Barrier, Blade Vortex, Full Coverage, Victorious Pursuit, Snipe, Stormeye, Spell Disintegrator, Guard, Vitality Touch, Purification, Jade Barrier, Spear Impale, Void Realm, Demonic Contract.**
- **KvK (S1)**: **Snipe** is in the **Cold Coin shop**; **Full Coverage** and **Snipe** can drop from **KvK chests**.

---

## Season 1 Skill Stone Availability (Overview Table)

Columns are **Wisdom Well – Jackpot**, **Cinder Shop**, **KvK Shop**, **KvK Chests**.

| Skill | Wisdom Well – Jackpot | Cinder Shop | KvK Shop | KvK Chests |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Weakening Curse | YES | NO | NO | NO |
| Siren’s Gaze | YES | NO | NO | NO |
| Weakness Protection | YES | NO | NO | NO |
| Berserker | YES | NO | NO | NO |
| Wind Rage | YES | NO | NO | NO |
| Overpower | YES | NO | NO | NO |
| Smite | YES | NO | NO | NO |
| Spring of Life | YES | NO | NO | NO |

| Desire of Life | YES | NO | NO | NO |
| Unyielding | YES | NO | NO | NO |

| Demonic Contract | NO | YES | NO | NO |

---

## Wisdom Well (Season 1)

**What’s inside:** the first jackpot pool (list above). When you hit jackpot, you pull **one of those stones** in a meaningful chunk, which can absolutely turbo a Season 1 march.

In season one you get the first iterations of the Wisdom Well. As the jackpot reward in season 1 you are able to get: Weakening curse, Siren’s gaze, Weakness Protection, Berserker, Wind Rage, Overpower, Smite, Spring of Life, Battle Stance, Fear of Domination, Desire of Life, Unyielding, Storm Strike, Armageddon, Implosion, Energy Shield.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-105.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-104.png)

**How to use it:**

- If you’re pushing **now**, rolling for things like **Weakening Curse** for most setups or **Wind Rage** for hybrids can flip fights fast (check build guides for details).
- If you’re more budget-minded, don’t over-commit. A lot of these stones show up in easier lanes later, so S1 Well pulls are basically you paying a premium for getting key skills early.

**My take:** I keep Well spending **targeted**. If a single stone changes my matchups this season, I go for it. Otherwise I hold and build via Cinder Shop picks.

---

## Cinder Wish Shop (Season 1)

**What you can buy:** **Toxin Barrier, Blade Vortex, Full Coverage, Victorious Pursuit, Snipe, Stormeye, Spell Disintegrator, Guard, Vitality Touch, Purification, Jade Barrier, Spear Impale, Void Realm, Demonic Contract.**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-106-1024x419.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-107-1024x561.png)

### Why it matters in S1:

- This is your **reliable** way to finish a march without gambling and to even get skills for free by selling KvK stone rewards and buying using cinders in the wish shop.
- If you pull something from KvK (or Well I guess) you don’t need, you can **sell it for Cinders** and convert into exactly what your lineup is missing from this list.

---

## KvK Shop (Season 1)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-108-1024x586.png)

**What’s in the shop:** **Snipe**.
**Should you buy?** Sure, but you wont be needing it since the skill is not particularly strong. But you can still purchase these just fine! Why? Because you turn them into Cinders (more below).

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-109.png)

All skill stones can be **sold for Cinders**. So you can:

1. Pick up a stone from **KvK** using **Cold Coins**,
2. **Sell** that stone for **Cinders**,
3. **Buy** something else from the **Cinder Shop** instead.

The **ratio** you get here is **1:1** between “KvK skill stone → Cinder Shop skill stone.” That’s huge for flexibility. If KvK is offering something you don’t actually want to run, you can still turn it into a Cinder Shop pick that you *do* need. This is how budget and F2P players quietly fix holes in a march without swiping.

---

## KvK Chests (Season 1)

**What can drop:** **Full Coverage** and **Snipe**. **I don’t recommend heavy spending gems here in S1.** **Full Coverage** can be cute if you’re running a **super niche high-regen build**, but Conquest gives you better tools in both the **KvK Shop** and **Cinder Shop**. For almost everyone, the efficient move is to **bank Cold Coins** in S1/S2 for Conquest.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-111-1024x427.png)

---

## Player Perspective (how I play S1)

If I’m trying to win S1 server fights, I’ll take a **surgical** shot at the Well for a stone that fixes my worst matchup. If you are running an earth himiko spender build going for things like **Weakening Curse**, **Spring of Life**in the well and spending cinders on **Vitality or Purification or Jade Barrier**will provide you with top tier skills for season 1 and season 2. However these will NOT hold top tier ranking going into conquest and later Legendary seasons. Personally, the tricky part is not getting baited into finishing every shiny set—you’ll keep them going in season 1 and season 2 but you will replace them in conquest and legendary where the jackpot rewards are legendary skills and where many new more powerful skills are available.

In essence, if you want to be top dog contender for season 1 and 2, buy the best key skills for your chosen main build. If you are going for max long term efficiency, grind as many KvK Cold Coins as you can, skip Wisdom well skills until conquest and use KvK rewards to turn into free cinders to buy a key single skill if possible.

---

title: Complete guide on all skill stones available in Season 2 and how to get them
summary: A ton of players burn cash in seasons because they see shiny skill stones at painful prices and think, “If I don’t buy now, I’ll fall behind.” You do get a big power bump if you spend early—but most of those stones…
categoryPath: Ability Stones Availability - season 1, 2 and Conquest
markdown:
A ton of players burn cash in seasons because they see shiny skill stones at painful prices and think, “If I don’t buy now, I’ll fall behind.” You *do* get a big power bump if you spend early—but most of those stones either get cheaper, move to free-to-play paths, or just get hard-outclassed later. While getting ahead early and getting powerful skills as soon as possible in Wisdom Well is completly valid, it is important to know that getting skills fast come at a high price. Skills roll into the game gradually: first in S1 via Wisdom Well, Cinder Shop, and KvK; then Season 2 adds more to those same places; and Conquest opens the floodgates even further (plus day-chain bundles).

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-30-1024x507.png)

In this guide we are going to look at season 2 and which skills are available to players and where to obtain these. This guide is part of a series on skill stone availability, please review the guide on **[Conquest](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/tower-of-knowledge-passives/ability-stones-availability-season-1-2-and-conquest/complete-guide-on-all-skill-stones-available-in-conquest-and-how-to-get-them/)**skills when you are planning your spending.

So the mindset is simple: if you’re chasing a **temporary season spike**, go ahead and spend in S1/S2. If you’re **efficiency-focused** or F2P/low-spend, plan for Conquest and keep your currency flexible.

---

## How Skills Unlock Over Time (big picture)

- **Season 1:** You see the first batch in **Wisdom Well**, **Cinder Shop**, and **KvK**. Prices are high and skills will be replaced late game.
- **Season 2:** New lineup drops in those same channels, and some things become easier to get or just less premium.
- **Conquest:** Even more skills show up across **Wisdom Well**, **Cinder Shop**, **KvK**, and **day-chain bundles**. This is where patient players looking for maximum efficiency on every dollar spent will truely begin collecting skills.

If you only remember one rule: **the later the season, the better your cost-to-power on most skills.**

---

## Season 2 – What’s Actually Available

### Full list of skills in season 2, more details below the table

| Skill | Wisdom Well | Cinder Shop | KvK Shop | KvK Chests |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Siren’s Gaze | YES | NO | NO | YES |
| Weakness Protection | YES | NO | NO | NO |
| Berserker | YES | NO | NO | NO |
| Wind Rage | YES | NO | NO | NO |
| Overpower | YES | NO | NO | NO |
| Smite | YES | NO | NO | NO |
| Spring of Life | YES | NO | NO | NO |
| Battle Stance | YES | NO | NO | NO |
| Fear of Domination | YES | NO | NO | NO |
| Desire of Life | YES | NO | NO | NO |
| Weakening Curse | YES | NO | NO | NO |
| Unyielding | YES | NO | NO | NO |
| Storm Strike | YES | NO | NO | NO |
| Armageddon | YES | NO | NO | NO |
| Implosion | YES | NO | NO | NO |
| Energy Shield | YES | NO | NO | NO |
| Toxin Barrier | NO | YES | NO | NO |
| Blade Vortex | NO | YES | NO | NO |
| Full Coverage | NO | YES | NO | YES |
| Victorious Pursuit | NO | YES | NO | NO |
| Snipe | NO | YES | YES | YES |
| Stormeye | NO | YES | YES | YES |

| Purification | NO | YES | NO | NO |
| Jade Barrier | NO | YES | NO | NO |
| Spear Impale | NO | YES | NO | NO |
| Void Realm | NO | YES | NO | NO |
| Demonic Contract | NO | YES | NO | NO |

Okay, that's the overall picture. Lets dive into some more detail on each column and skill. In the following we go over each place you obtian skill stones one by one, further event details can be found in seperate guides for each event under the **[Events](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/events/)**section of the website.

---

## Wisdom Well (S2)

[Embedded media](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Screenrecorder-2025-10-04-13-14-30-406.mp4)

Season 2 updates the Wisdom Well pool and also sets a new **jackpot**: there’s a **2% chance** to pull **4× stones** of one listed skill in a single hit. That jackpot is how some players spike a build for the season without buying stones outright.

**Available in S2 Wisdom Well:**
Siren’s Gaze, Weakness Protection, Berserker, Wind Rage, Overpower, Smite, Spring of Life, Battle Stance, Fear of Domination, Desire of Life, Weakening Curse, Unyielding, Storm Strike, Armageddon, Implosion, Energy Shield.

What this means in practice: if you’re rolling the Well in S2, you’ve got access to a much healthier spread than S1. But if you’re long-term minded, you can still wait—Conquest improves the menu and the value.

---

## Wish Shop, aka Cinder Shop (S2)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-31-1024x601.png)

**In season 2, these stones are in the Cinder Shop at **17 Cinders per stone**::**
Toxin Barrier, Blade Vortex, Full Coverage, Victorious Pursuit, Snipe, Stormeye, Spell Disintegrator, Guard, Vitality Touch, Purification, Jade Barrier, Spear Impale, Void Realm, Demonic Contract.

All skill stones you roll or earn can be turned into **Cinders**, and then you buy exactly what you need.

If there’s something that’s directly core to your main march, grabbing it here is fine. Otherwise, don’t force purchases—these lineups keep evolving each season.

---

## KvK (S2)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-32-1024x594.png)

Using **Cold Coins** (earned during the season), you can buy stones for **800 Cold Coins per stone**. Current Conquest KvK stone lineup you can purchase:

- **KvK Shop (S2):** Snipe, Stormeye.
- **KvK Chests (S2):** Full Coverage, Siren’s Gaze, Stormeye, Snipe.

Here’s the thing: **I don’t recommend heavy spending here in S2.** These are decent stones, but they get replaced fast. **Full Coverage** can be cute if you’re running a **super niche high-regen build** and you only care about **this season**, but Conquest gives you better tools in both the **KvK Shop** and **Cinder Shop**. For almost everyone, the efficient move is to **bank Cold Coins** in S1/S2 for Conquest.

If you’re desperate to pivot mid-season, consider the **Cinder angle** (next section) instead of sinking a lot into direct KvK buys.

---

## The Cinder Trick (And Why It Matters)

All skill stones can be **sold for Cinders**. So you can:

1. Pick up a stone from **KvK** using **Cold Coins**,
2. **Sell** that stone for **Cinders**,
3. **Buy** something else from the **Cinder Shop** instead.

The **ratio** you get here is **1:1** between “KvK skill stone → Cinder Shop skill stone.” That’s huge for flexibility. If KvK is offering something you don’t actually want to run, you can still turn it into a Cinder Shop pick that you *do* need. This is how budget and F2P players quietly fix holes in a march without swiping.

---

## How I’d Plan It (By Spend Level)

## F2P / Low-Spend

- **Bank Cold Coins** in S1 and S2. Don’t chase every “nice to have.”
- Use the **1:1 sell-for-Cinders** trick when a Cinder Shop skill is crucial to your main march *right now*.
- If you can tolerate being a patch behind in raw power, **wait for Conquest** to splash the Wisdom Well and do the bulk of your shopping.

## Mid-Spend

- Decide if **this season** matters (e.g., competitive KvK or server politics). If yes, it’s fine to grab **one or two** cornerstone skills from Cinder Shop or take a few shots at the Wisdom Well **jackpot**.
- Don’t overcommit to **KvK Shop stones** unless they directly slot into your top march *now*. Use **sell→Cinders** to stay flexible.

## High-Spend / Season-Spike

- If you want the **immediate** edge, Season 2’s Wisdom Well list is serviceable, and the **2% 4× jackpot** can swing a build fast.
- Just accept you’ll **replace or devalue** some of these picks in Conquest. That’s the price of staying ahead in-season.

---

## Player Perspective (What I’d Actually Do)

When I am being asked about skill stone purchases by players in S1 heading into S2, I say: pick your **one main march**, identify **one or two** skills that are true **core pieces** from the S2 lists, and only buy those if they unlock a real spike. Otherwise, **sit on your currencies** and use KvK purchases as **Cinder fuel** when the Cinder Shop has something you actually need. And consider if you want to pay the premium is takes to unlock this skill in season 1 or even season 2 instead of waiting for conquest.

---

title: Complete Guide to Conquest Skill Stones and How to Obtain Them
summary: Conquest is where Infinity Kingdom’s skill system really opens up. More skills become available through the Wisdom Well, the Cinder Shop continues to expand, Legion of Frostborne adds another group of Ability Stones and…
categoryPath: Ability Stones Availability - season 1, 2 and Conquest
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-210-1024x576.png)

Conquest is where Infinity Kingdom’s skill system really opens up. More skills become available through the Wisdom Well, the Cinder Shop continues to expand, Legion of Frostborne adds another group of Ability Stones and paid recharge chains offer several additional selection chests.

The difficulty is no longer finding skills. It is understanding which currency belongs to which shop, what can be obtained for free and which skills are worth targeting first. Patch 2.9.9 has made this slightly more confusing by moving several skills between seasons, so this guide provides an updated overview of what is currently available during Conquest.

## What Changed in Patch 2.9.9?

Patch 2.9.9 changed the season in which four Wisdom Well skills are released:

- **Arcane Hunter** now becomes available in Conquest instead of Legendary Season.
- **Divine Blessing** now becomes available in Conquest instead of Legendary Season.
- **Eternal Battlelust** now becomes available in Conquest instead of Legendary Season.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-207.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-208.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-209.png)

On a related note, while not directly relevant to conquest players, its worth noting that **Energy Master**y now becomes available in Season 2 instead of Conquest. Moving Energy Master to Season 2 does not mean it disappears when a server enters Conquest. It simply becomes available earlier and remains part of the available skill progression afterward.

Likewise, it deserves to be quickly noted, that the Patch 2.9.9 skill, **Psychic Vortex** is released through the Wish Shop during **Legendary Season**, meaning it is **not**available to ordinary Conquest servers.

## Skill Sources Available in Conquest

There are five main sources of seasonal Ability Stones during Conquest:

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-211.png)

Several skills appear in more than one source. That overlap is important because it gives players alternative ways to finish a skill without relying entirely on Wisdom Well luck or paid bundles.

## Wisdom Well Legendary Skills in Conquest

Following the Patch 2.9.9 release changes, the legendary skills available by Conquest include:

- Arcane Hunter
- Attack & Defense
- Battle Frenzy
- Divine Blessing
- Drastic Action
- Energy Master
- Eternal Battlelust
- Fountain of Life
- Infinite Firepower
- Knife Through Butter
- Last Stand
- Life Protection

A legendary skill requires **60 stones to unlock**, while further upgrades require additional stones. Fully developing one is therefore a much larger project than simply obtaining the first few drops.

[Read more about upgrading legendary skills here.](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/tower-of-knowledge-passives/tok-basics/chaos-tok-skills-legendary-and-pricing-to-upgrade-and-max-2-8-5/)

The most important Patch 2.9.9 addition for the current meta is arguably **Eternal Battlelust**. It was previously held back until Legendary Season, but Conquest players can now begin building it much earlier. This is particularly relevant for Immortals such as Medusa, whose repeated passive-damage activations can make excellent use of the skill.

Arcane Hunter and Divine Blessing also expand the number of Conquest options, while Energy Master becoming available in Season 2 allows developing servers to start working on one of the game’s strongest energy-support skills before they reach Conquest.

## The Conquest Cinder Shop

The Cinder Shop is where older premium skills gradually become accessible without having to chase their original release event. It is particularly important for free-to-play and low-spending players because Cinders can be accumulated over time through Wisdom Well wishes and by recycling unwanted Ability Stones.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-214-1024x554.png)

The current Conquest Cinder Shop includes:

- Ambush
- Armageddon
- Battle Stance
- Berserker
- Blade Vortex
- Demonic Contract
- Desire of Life
- Energy Shield
- Executioner
- Fear of Domination
- Full Coverage
- Guard
- Heavy Lifter
- Implosion
- Jade Barrier
- Memory Defense
- No Escape
- Overpower
- Purification
- Siren’s Gaze
- Smite
- Snipe
- Spear Impale
- Spell Disintegrator
- Spring of Life
- Storm Strike
- Stormeye
- Toxin Barrier
- Unyielding
- Victorious Pursuit
- Vitality Touch
- Void Realm
- Weakening Curse
- Weakness Protection
- Wind Rage

Each stone costs **17 Cinders**, meaning that unlocking a skill from zero requires:

### 60 stones × 17 Cinders = 1,020 Cinders

Unwanted Ability Stones can be sold for Cinders, but this is not a direct one-for-one exchange into another Ability Stone. Selling one unwanted stone gives one Cinder, while purchasing one target stone costs 17 Cinders. Recycling remains useful, but it should be understood as slow account progression rather than a free skill swap.

This is why Cinders should be concentrated on important skills. Weakening Curse, Wind Rage, Full Coverage, Siren’s Gaze and other established options may be worth building, but the correct priority depends entirely on your marches.

## Legion of Frostborne Ability Stones

The Legion’s Vender allows players to purchase Ability Stones using Cold Silver earned during KvK. Each stone costs **800 Cold Silver**, and a full 60-stone unlock therefore costs: **60 × 800 = 48,000 Cold Silver**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-213-1024x529.png)

The Conquest KvK selection includes:

- Abundant Spirit
- Assembly Charge
- Berserker
- Full Coverage
- Siren’s Gaze
- Snipe
- Spell Disintegrator
- Stormeye
- Unforeseen Attack
- Victorious Pursuit
- Weakness Protection
- Wind Rage

For most developing accounts, these skills should take priority over ordinary resources, speedups and artifact materials sold in the same shop. **Wind Rage, Assembly Charge and Abundant Spirit** are especially important skills to secure as early as possible.

If you do not need one of the available KvK skills, its stones can still be purchased and sold for Cinders. This gives veteran players another way to make slow progress toward Cinder Shop skills, although the 17-Cinder purchase price means the conversion is expensive and should not be mistaken for an equal exchange.

Ancient Remnant chests should not be included as a Conquest Ability Stone source. In the current version, these chests focus on Holy and Shadow Immortal fragments and artifact-related rewards rather than the old selection of KvK skill stones.

## Recharge Chain Selection Chest VII

Conquest recharge chains can provide **Ability Stone Selection Chest VII**. The usual seven-day structure awards five chests on purchased days, with an additional 25-chest reward after completing five qualifying days.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-212-1024x556.png)

Selection Chest VII contains:

- Blade Dodge
- Blood Frenzy
- Chaos Storm
- Heart of Arcana
- Iron Curtain
- Lightning Strike
- Master’s Aegis
- Psionic Tide
- Soul Synergy
- Time to Shine

This is a paid shortcut rather than a free progression source, but it offers much more control than gambling for a specific Wisdom Well drop. Players who already spend regularly can use these chains to finish a targeted skill, particularly when they are only missing a small number of stones.

As always, inspect the active chest before purchasing. Selection chest contents can change as new skills are introduced, and the in-game reward preview should be treated as the final authority.

## How to Plan Your Skill Progression

Free-to-play and very low-spending players should focus on reliable sources. Complete the most important KvK skills with Cold Silver, collect Cinders gradually and avoid dividing resources between too many unfinished skills. A completed good skill is far more useful than having 20 stones for five different skills.

Moderate spenders can combine targeted Wisdom Well participation with the Cinder Shop and occasional recharge chains. The main advantage of spending in Conquest is access to legendary skills alongside Selection Chest I, so Wisdom Well Coins generally have more long-term potential here than they do during earlier seasons.

High spenders can push the legendary pool more aggressively, but even then it is worth planning around complete builds rather than collecting every new skill automatically. Eternal Battlelust may be exceptional for a Medusa composition, for example, but that does not make it equally valuable for every march.

## Should You Buy Skills Before Conquest?

Buying a skill during Season 1 or Season 2 is often a question of timing rather than permanent exclusivity. Some skills that are expensive or difficult to obtain early become available through the Cinder Shop or other sources later.

If obtaining a skill now allows you to win important fights, improve your arena position or carry your alliance through a competitive season, paying for early access can be worthwhile. If you are not competing heavily, waiting until Conquest will often be considerably more efficient.

Patch 2.9.9 reinforces this point. Energy Master now arrives in Season 2, while Arcane Hunter, Divine Blessing and Eternal Battlelust arrive in Conquest instead of forcing players to wait for Legendary Season. Skill availability is not static, and paying a premium for early access always carries the possibility that the same skill becomes easier to obtain later.

## Summary

Conquest gives players access to a much wider Ability Stone economy through the Wisdom Well, Selection Chest I, Cinder Shop, Legion’s Vender and recharge selection chests. Patch 2.9.9 expands that economy by bringing **Arcane Hunter, Divine Blessing and Eternal Battlelust** forward from Legendary Season, while **Energy Master** now begins appearing as early as Season 2.

The best approach is to choose skills based on the marches you actually use, finish one target at a time and avoid assuming that every early premium skill will remain exclusive forever. Players who plan across several seasons will almost always obtain more useful skills for the same amount of money, Cold Silver and Cinders.
