markdown:
### The William Myth Debunked: How Infinity Kingdom’s Skill Terminology Created Confusion Around William

Community testing and developer clarification have resolved a quite surprising but also VERY persistent misunderstanding or myth amongst many players. Having gone over this multiple times with newer players, VictorSeven has been kind enough to help shine a light on the misunderstanding and helping me correct is here once in for all!

For a long time, many players have been believing that William’s ultimate skill only increased the critical chance of troop attack animations, rather than increasing the crit rate relevant to Immortal damage. This interpretation usually came from the word “troops” in William’s skill description. **That assumption is incorrect.**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-64.png)

Troop attack animations should not be understood as separate damage sources that independently deal meaningful damage to opposing troops. In battle reports, damage is attributed to Immortals because Infinity Kingdom’s combat model works through Immortals commanding a number of troops under them.

Those troops still matter, but not as separate attackers in the way many players imagine. Their per-troop attributes are included in the damage equation behind the Immortal’s output. In practical terms, troop attributes contribute to the damage numbers produced by an Immortal’s normal attacks, skills, and ultimate ability.

This means William’s ultimate is not simply increasing the crit chance of some separate background troop animation. The relevant point is that the troop-based attributes under an Immortal are part of the Immortal’s actual combat calculation.

Special credit goes to community player VictorSeven, who originally investigated the issue, compared the game’s terminology across multiple systems, and shared the developer clarification that helped settle the discussion.

---

## The Terminology Problem

Recently, while reviewing Tower of Knowledge skills, we noticed something interesting. Several universally accepted buffs also use the word “troops” in their descriptions — despite clearly affecting Immortals.

For example:

- Resist
- War Blessing
- Afterimage
- Defense Blessing
- Demon Body
- Speed Blessing
- Energy Suppression

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-65.png)

That last one is what made me stop and reconsider the entire William discussion. Energy Suppression explicitly affects energy mechanics, but wait - troops do not have energy. Only Immortals do.

And you can visibly see the effect apply to Immortals during battle. So if Energy Suppression says “troops,” yet clearly affects Immortals, then the wording itself obviously cannot be treated as a strict mechanical distinction. At that point, the most likely explanation became pretty obvious: Infinity Kingdom’s English localization is inconsistent. Different translators and writers appear to use different terminology interchangeably.

---

## Confirmation From the Developers

To verify it, I contacted the developers directly.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-66-1024x358.png)

The response itself actually reinforced the heart of this issue... Instead of using the word “Immortals,” the support response referred to them as “Heroic Spirits,” which is another example of inconsistent terminology across the game’s translation pipeline.

But the important part was the clarification:

> Skills that affect troops also affect Immortals.

That includes William’s ultimate. So yes — William’s crit rate increase does apply to your Immortals.

This is not just a tooltip technicality. It directly changes how you evaluate e.g. William and fire compositions.

---

## What This Means for Fire Teams

The standard progression most players recommend looks something like this:

- Empress Wu
- Emperor Qin or Matilda
- Hippolyta
- William

Then eventually:

- Remove William
- Add Trajan

The logic behind the the William-to-Trajan swap was never entirely about damage.

A major reason many experienced players eventually remove William is his regeneration value. Compared to other late-game options, William’s sustain scaling is relatively weak, especially in longer PvP fights where survivability and recovery heavily influence march performance. That part of the community assessment is still reasonable.

The problem is that many players also believed William’s crit support did not meaningfully affect Immortal damage because his skill description referred to “troops.” Once that assumption is removed, William’s offensive contribution becomes much stronger than people originally gave him credit for.

If that assumption is wrong, the calculus changes. William suddenly becomes much more valuable in sustained PvP setups because his crit support directly benefits your Immortals’ skill damage and chase output. And that matters quite a bit for Wu.

Most optimized Wu builds already lean heavily into Chase and crit scaling. Additional crit rate has real value there, especially in extended fights where consistent skill pressure matters more than raw burst.

However, even with the clarification around William’s ultimate, Trajan is still probably the stronger overall choice in most mature Fire PvP builds. On paper, William’s skill is exceptionally strong. Once you account for the fact that his crit support genuinely affects Immortal damage — especially alongside his unique artifact — his offensive ceiling becomes much higher than many players originally assumed. In pure damage terms, there are situations where William can look better than Trajan.

The issue is regeneration. William’s regen value is simply too low compared to what Trajan brings in extended PvP fights. In practice, this means William often takes a long time before his impact is fully felt, particularly against durable late-game marches where sustain and tempo matter more than short bursts of pressure.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-67.png)

Trajan contributes much earlier and much more consistently because of his superior regeneration profile. That reliability is a major reason why most experienced players still prefer him in competitive Fire setups.

So while the old explanation for replacing William turns out to be incorrect, the end result often stays the same: Trajan is usually the more practical PvP choice.

Still, the potential is clearly there for William. A properly optimized regeneration-focused William build could eventually shift that evaluation. The offensive foundation is strong enough that it would not be surprising to see someone develop a version capable of competing with standard Trajan variants.

---

title: Default Holy Setup for Season 1 whales
summary: Holy immortals have long been seen as the go-to counter for shadow teams in Infinity Kingdom, but recent updates and the rise of Tutankhamun have made shadow the clear meta leader in Season 1. Once upon a time, Holy…
markdown:
Holy immortals have long been seen as the go-to counter for shadow teams in *Infinity Kingdom*, but recent updates and the rise of Tutankhamun have made shadow the clear meta leader in Season 1. Once upon a time, Holy offered a clean 25% damage boost and reduction against shadow, which made it the best hard-counter strategy. However, developer changes have adjusted the elemental multipliers, making Holy less dominant. Even so, Holy builds remain viable, especially for high-spending players (whales) who want to run both a maxed shadow and holy team for flexibility and power. This guide outlines a powerful Holy build optimized to deliver maximum performance while leaving key skills free for your shadow team.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-106-1024x392.png)

---

## Why Holy Still Works

Despite the recent meta leaning heavily into shadow and Tutankhamun builds, Holy still brings unique strengths to the table. It is one of the best anti-control elements in the game. Theodora, a cornerstone of Holy, can cleanse status effects like Confuse and Blade Vortex, while also providing massive healing output. The ramp-up nature of Holy teams means you won't see explosive damage early in the fight, but if you survive the first 20 seconds, you gain powerful momentum and become incredibly hard to stop.

In addition to its sustainability, Holy gives you counterplay options against specific meta strategies. Confuse from Tomyris? No problem. Bleeds and DoTs from Blade Vortex? Theodora can cleanse them. Burst from Himiko? We snipe her with Nebuchadnezzar.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-107-1024x610.png)

---

## Optimal Whale Holy Setup (Paired With Max Shadow)

This specific setup is tested and built for players who already have a separate maxed-out shadow team and want to preserve key ToK skills like Fighting Master and Guard for that team. It provides ramp-up defense and output while protecting your main damage dealer, Manco.

### Theodora

- **Purify**: Removes debuffs including Blade Vortex, stuns, wounds, etc. Consider placing Purify in your shadow team if Theo’s ultimate is enough for cleansing.
- **Shelter**: Provides substantial healing over time. In extended battles, this outperforms Vitality Touch in raw healing.
- **Vitality Touch**: Boosts healing and gives a defensive buff.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-108-1024x578.png)

### Nebuchadnezzar II

- **Snipe**: Target positioning so that you snipe key enemy backliners like Himiko.
- **Malice**: Prevents high crit bursts from enemy teams.
- **Rage Blessing**: Enables faster skill cycling early. If your shadow needs Oaken Guard, this is a good alternate defensive boost.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-109-1024x587.png)

### Khubilaikhan

- **Full Coverage**: Helps defend Manco while adding support.
- **Spear Impale**: Delivers physical damage, maintaining pressure.
- **Life-Link**: Soaks damage and redirects it. Optional for synergy. Consider replacing with Physical Shield if you don’t need it in your hybrid team.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-111-1024x565.png)

### Manco

- **Void Realm**: Provides immunity for 18s—the ramp-up window you need.
- **Victorious Pursuit**: Incredible synergy with Manco’s ultimate for ramping damage.
- **Demonic Contract**: Boosts damage the longer the fight goes.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-110-1024x585.png)

This build is especially strong because it reserves Fighting Master and Guard for your shadow team. With this configuration, the Holy team still delivers devastating late-game damage and top-tier sustain.

### Performance

This Holy setup has been tested in live PvP with exceptional results. It took down multiple maxed-out marches from top whales, even eliminating all four armies in some cases. This confirms that the right skill allocation and strategy can make Holy a serious threat in the current Season 1 meta, even if it’s no longer the go-to hardcounter it used to be.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-104-1024x546.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-103-1024x554.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-105-1024x606.png)

---

## Alternatives for Holy-Only Whales

If you don’t have a strong shadow team and want to optimize Holy alone, consider shifting your skills:

### Build Variant 1 (Pure Holy)

- **Theo**: Oaken Guard/Assist, Vitality Touch, Weakness
- **Neb**: Blade Vortex, Fighting Master, Malice
- **Manco**: Void Realm, Demonic Contract, Victorious Pursuit
- **Khubilai**: Energy Burst, Spear Impale, Full Coverage

This version gives you stronger early-mid fight output and better control resistance on Neb. Blade Vortex also provides a reliable DoT pressure tool.

---

## Strategic Considerations

- **Skill Allocation Between Teams**: If you run both a shadow and a holy team, think of your ToK skills as a limited pool. Assign Guard, Fighting Master, and Oaken Guard wisely.
- **Enemy Composition**: Adapt based on opponents. Facing Tutankhamun? Snipe him with Alex or Neb. Facing Himiko? Use Fighting Master or position properly to avoid Confuse.
- **DoT Mitigation**: Purify and Theo’s ultimate are key to countering Blade Vortex.
- **Dragon Strategy**: pairing this team with Holy Dragon for added healing, or Earth if you cannot upgrade holy fully, providing good improved troop durability.

---

## Final Thoughts

Holy may no longer be the default anti-shadow answer, but in the hands of a whale with access to maxed skills and high-end immortals, it can still dominate. This build lets you extract maximum value from your Holy march while preserving crucial skills for a powerful shadow team. Whether you run it as your main or second march, Holy is very much alive and viable in Season 1—especially for those willing to play the long game.

Stay tuned for the full triple march composition guide for whales, where this Holy setup will be featured as part of a rotation alongside a shadow and hybrid build.

title: Defending against Normal Attacks
summary: In the ever-evolving world of Infinity Kingdom, the ability to defend against normal attacks is just as crucial as launching them. Understanding which skills can protect your heroes from the relentless onslaught of foes…
markdown:
### Fortify Your Defense: Skills that Shield Against Normal Attacks

In the ever-evolving world of Infinity Kingdom, the ability to defend against normal attacks is just as crucial as launching them. Understanding which skills can protect your heroes from the relentless onslaught of foes can make the difference between victory and defeat. In this guide, we'll explore skills that provide a shield against normal attacks and the heroes who can best utilize them.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/image-45.png)

### 1. Fighting Will

Fighting Will is a skill tailor-made for frontline immortals who don't rely on their HP to be effective in battle. Heroes like Richard, Bjorn, and Trajan are prime examples of characters who can embrace the power of Fighting Will. These heroes are known for their remarkable durability and battlefield prowess. What sets this skill apart is its ability to allow these heroes to drop and, if necessary, even meet their demise swiftly.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/image-46.png)

For heroes with Fighting Will, the battlefield isn't a place where they cling to life desperately; it's where they unleash their full potential, undeterred by the fear of falling in combat. This skill ensures that they can make their presence felt, even if they are the first to face the enemy's onslaught.

### 2. Toxin Barrier

Toxin Barrier is a skill that shines in the hands of heroes like Charles and Tokugawa. These heroes have a unique talent for sustaining high HP over extended periods, making them formidable forces on the battlefield. Toxin Barrier takes their already impressive durability to the next level by allowing them to endure even more damage while simultaneously protecting them from normal attacks.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/image-47.png)

In essence, heroes with Toxin Barrier can become nigh-invincible on the front lines. Their high HP ensures they can soak up immense damage, while the barrier itself acts as a shield against normal attacks. This combination makes them exceedingly difficult to defeat and allows them to deal out substantial damage in return.

### Conclusion

In the Infinity Kingdom, the ability to defend against normal attacks is paramount to your success in battles. Skills like Fighting Will and Toxin Barrier offer unique advantages to specific heroes, turning them into unyielding bastions of defense. Whether you're using heroes like Richard, Bjorn, and Trajan to embrace the swift fall of Fighting Will or entrusting Charles and Tokugawa with the power of Toxin Barrier, these skills can turn the tide of battle in your favor.

So, as you embark on your conquests in the Infinity Kingdom, remember the importance of a solid defense. These skills and the heroes who wield them can provide the protection you need to weather the storm of normal attacks and emerge victorious on the battlefield. Fortify your defenses, choose your heroes wisely, and let these skills be your shield in the ever-expanding world of Infinity Kingdom.

title: Defensive Himiko Build (earth base progressing into chaos-conquest)
summary: For endgame players in Infinity Kingdom, Conquest is where the competition gets serious. Many of the strongest teams you’ll face are built around Chaos immortals and legendary skills, making it harder to stand out…
markdown:
## 🏯 Endgame Guide: The Ramp-Up Himiko Conquest Setup

For endgame players in *Infinity Kingdom*, Conquest is where the competition gets serious. Many of the strongest teams you’ll face are built around Chaos immortals and legendary skills, making it harder to stand out without going full whale.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/image-73-1024x489.png)

This guide showcases a **highly competitive Conquest setup** that is **achievable for mid-level spenders**. You’ll need access to **two Chaos immortals** (so yes, a long grind and some money), but you won’t need to whale out on every legendary skill to make it work. The build is based on one core idea:

👉 **Defend and stall until Himiko ramps up — then let her burn everything to ashes.**

**NOTE**: This is a default build made to counter specifically a physical based meta and based on the availability for this player. Given total free roam of skills there should be slight changes.

**Premium Upgrades (Whale/High-Spender Flex)**: For players who want to push the setup to the top of the food chain, these skills are your endgame chase goals:

- **Energy Mastery (Himiko)** – Premium mage scaling, massive power increase.
- **Infinite Firepower (Himiko)** – Synergizes perfectly with Abundant Spirit for devastating bursts.
- **Corrosive Power (Himiko)** – If available, creates regen-bursty variants of the build.
- **Fighting Master (Himiko)**– If against enemy Himiko mirrors.
- **No Escape (Flexible slot)** – Replace Vitality Touch or Energy Suppression depending on enemy comps. Provides insane CC and control.

👉 These aren’t required to make the build work, but they will make your Himiko one of the most dangerous carries in Conquest. Now, lets get on with the base build for Himiko-earth in physical meta conquest.

---

## 🐉 Dragon Choice: Earth Dragon

- **Why Earth?** Earth Dragon provides the most defensive buffs and survivability tools, letting your march outlast enemy bursts. Since the build relies on Himiko coming online after about a minute, defense and sustain are the foundation of the strategy.

---

## 🔥 Core Damage Dealer: Himiko

Himiko is the centerpiece of this march. She is fragile early but absolutely devastating once Battle Stance kicks in.

### Recommended Skills:

- **Abundant Spirit** – Boosts trigger chance by 10% and adds 30% magical damage. Essential for amplifying Himiko’s nukes.
- **Battle Stance** – The engine of the build. After 20s, grants extra damage and regen, turning Himiko into a late-fight monster.
- **Poison Thorn** – Counters physical-heavy teams like Apollo or Alexander. (Can be swapped for **Heavy Lifter** or **Chaos Storm**, depending on your meta)

It is important to note, that the specific setup on Himiko can change a lot based on what you are faced with. This is a ramp-up to match other physical ramps, but you can also lean into **hyper regen if you need frontloaded burst: Then you do Energy Master, Corrosive.** You can run it **without the ramp-up if your defensive is not high enough, then you can run e.g. abundant spirit, heavy lifter, chaos storm for trigger-chance synergy.** Or you can run **Fighting Master if you are faced with enemy himikos and needs to counter a mirror build**.

Basically, the rest of the **setup stays the same more or less but himiko needs to change based on what you are pitted against in PvP combat** in your specific battlegroup and meta.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/image-74-1024x616.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/image-75-1024x626.png)

💡 **Whale Upgrade:** If you have legendary Chaos skills like **Energy Mastery** or **Infinite Firepower**, slot them in. These outperform standard options but aren’t mandatory for this build to succeed.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/image-77-1024x480.png)

---

## 🌸 Support Backline: Fu Fei (or Theodora)

Your second backliner should focus entirely on keeping the fight going until Himiko ramps up.

### Recommended Skills:

- **Energy Suppression** – Slows down enemy ultimates.
- **Spring of Life** – Core sustain skill.
- **Assist** – Protects your fragile backline.

If you don’t have Fu Fei yet, **Theodora** works very well in this slot.

---

## 🛡️ Frontline: YSS & Athena

Two tanky frontliners to anchor the march and soak pressure. Their job is to survive, protect Himiko, and slowly grind down the enemy frontline.

### Recommended Skills:

- **Weakening Curse** – Reduces enemy damage.
- **Malice** – Adds disruption and control.
- **Oaken Guard** – Extra toughness.
- **Energy Shield** – Essential against magic-heavy comps.
- **Vitality Touch** – Sustains the frontline.

**Extra Buff:** Run **Weakness** somewhere in the comp to buff Himiko’s crits — she scales incredibly hard with crit amplification.

---

## ⚠️ Important Note: No Escape

This guide is written without **No Escape** in the skill pool. If you do have it:

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/image-78-1024x446.png)

- Replace **Vitality Touch** or **Energy Suppression**, depending on your opponents.
- This adds extra control and makes the build even nastier in extended fights.

---

## 🧩 Why This Build Works

- **Super Defensive Core** – Three supports (two tanks + healer) plus sustain skills mean you can survive nearly any burst.
- **Ramp-Up Win Condition** – Once Battle Stance triggers, Himiko goes from “okay” to “terrifying.” She snowballs harder the longer the fight goes.
- **Flexibility** – You can swap Poison Thorn, Spring of Life, or Vitality Touch based on what your battlegroup is running.
- **Scales Well With Chaos/Legendary Skills** – Even if you start mid-spend, this setup keeps getting better as you add more rare skills to it.

---

## 🏆 Final Thoughts

This **Himiko Ramp-Up Build** is one of the best “spender-friendly” Conquest setups in the current meta. It doesn’t require maxing out every Chaos skill to be competitive — but it rewards patience, smart play, and careful adaptation to your battlegroup.

The philosophy is simple: **stall, protect, and ramp up Himiko.** Once she’s online, she melts teams, and with three supports backing her up, there’s very little your opponents can do to stop it.

👉 For mid-level spenders who has been playing earth during season 1 and 2 and are now looking to hit Conquest hard without going full whale, this is one of the strongest options available.

title: Detailed guide on Attributes and their relevance for immortal types
summary: Immortals are the beating heart of every army in Infinity Kingdom, and understanding their individual stats is essential to maximizing your team’s performance in both PvE and PvP. While skill builds and elemental…
markdown:
### Understanding Immortal Stats and Their Roles

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/image-127-1024x667.png)

## Introduction

Immortals are the beating heart of every army in Infinity Kingdom, and understanding their individual stats is essential to maximizing your team’s performance in both PvE and PvP. While skill builds and elemental synergies are important, the raw stats of each Immortal directly affect their combat effectiveness. This guide will break down what each stat means, how it impacts battle performance, and what types of Immortals benefit most from each stat category.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/image-129.png)

---

## Core Immortal Stats Explained

### 1. Physical Attack (PATK)

- **What it is**: This stat determines the base damage dealt by skills or basic attacks that scale with physical attack.
- **Relevance**: Crucial for melee and ranged physical damage dealers (e.g., Alexander, Hannibal Barca).
- **Synergies**: Works well with skills like Cleave, Duel Master, and Anger.

### 2. Magical Attack (MATK)

- **What it is**: This stat affects the potency of magic-based damage skills.
- **Relevance**: Key for mages and casters such as Himiko, Merlin, and Baldwin.
- **Synergies**: Boosts effectiveness of skills like Annihilation, Fireball, and Death Breath.

### 3. Physical Defense (PDEF)

- **What it is**: Reduces incoming physical damage.
- **Relevance**: Important for frontline Immortals, because they are likely to face an enemy physical damage based immortal and also because normal attacks / Auto attacks are physical, even when made by a mage or a support!
- **Synergies**: Combines well with Oaken Guard, Physical Shield, Life-Link, Toxin Barrier and Blessing of Defense.

### 4. Magical Defense (MDEF)

- **What it is**: Reduces incoming magical damage.
- **Relevance**: Vital for units regularly exposed to AoE magic attacks.
- **Synergies**: Reinforced by skills like Resist, Magic Shield, Absolute Defense, Blessing of Defense, Jade Barrier, etc.

### 5. Dodge

- **What it is**: Huge defense against physical damage. All physical damage can be dodged. If you dodge you take 0 damage from the ability or skill you are dodging. Therefore very good value if you can get the enemy to miss attacks!
- **Relevance**: Universally important. But ultimately only relevant if you can stack enough to make your enemy miss / your immortals dodge enemy attacks. See Battle Reports!
- **Synergies**: Strong synergy with other effects like Misleading and After-Image because dodge basically is based on your dodge value versus the enemies Accuracy value. If your dodge is greater = you dodge enemy attacks.

### 6. Accuracy

- **What it is**: All physical damage can be dodged. If you dodge you take 0 damage from the ability or skill you are dodging. Accuracy makes sure your attacks dont miss or get dodged!
- **Relevance**: Important to physical damage dealers, high priority to get enough of. But once you get enough the value drops to nothing. But ultimately only relevant if you can stack enough to make your enemy miss / your immortals dodge enemy attacks. See Battle Reports! Therefore, you get huge value out of all accuracy attributes as long as you are "behind" against an enemies dodge. Once you hit 100% hit rate, the value of accuracy drops to nothing at all. But getting it to 100% is extreemly important! This can be a triggy balance if you wield a physical damage centered setup.
- Note that magical attacks cannot be dodged and thus mages require 0 accuracy to hit everything.
- **Synergies**: Strong synergy with other effects like Coercion.

### 7. Resilience

- **What it is**: The higher your resilience the less chance there is to get hit by a critical strike.
- **Relevance**: Relevant to all Immortals and especially relevant fighting against Chase-based mage setups.
- **Synergies**: Malice boosts your resilience rate significantly and is an expert defense against enemy crit-based setups.

### 8. Crit Hit / Crit Damage

- **What it is**: Determines the chance and effectiveness of critical hits.
- **Relevance**: Crucial for burst-damage dealers and builds centered around Chase or Rage Blessing.
- **Synergies**: Works exceptionally with Chase setups but generally Critical Hits are a huge factor in burst setups. You can reach over 3x crit damage if you stack and getting a single crit can literally wipe the battlefield if you are playing a high crit-damage-based setup.

### 9. Energy Regen.

- **What it is**: Determines the speed at which your immortal regains energy. Upon reaching 1000 energy your immortal will cast his or her ultimate ability. Side note, **Attack Speed is directly attributed to regen speed.**
- **Relevance**: Crucial for burst-damage dealers and builds but the higher the better for all..
- **Synergies**: Works exceptionally with Blessing of Rage builds and building using No Escape, and Energy Suppression and even Fountain of Life.

### 10. Aptitute

- **What it is**: Determines your immortals ability to govern. Higher values give boosts when appointed in Castle Government. Also factor for Shield Values and for Magical Protection and Penetration.
- **Relevance**: Crucial for Charles and Tokugawa as shield values depend on Apt.

### 11. Magical Penetration / Protection

- **What it is**: Determines the effectiveness of magical damage hits.
- **Relevance**: Magical Penetration basically works as exposure percentages. If you have high Penetration your magical damage will be amplified. Enemies with high Protection means the magical damage they recieve is reduced. Think of Elemental protection in other games.

### 12. HP (Health Points) - Unofficial attribute

- **What it is**: Determines how much damage an Immortal can take before being eliminated.
- Health Points are directly linked to troop tier attributes and your immortals "health pool" is thus a direct factor of the troop count deployed by the immortal. Increased troop count = bigger health pool.
- **Relevance**: Universally important, especially important for DPS units. **Damage Dealt by skills and healing done my skills are based directly on the amount of troops alive at the time of the cast** - thus the remaining HP which equated to troop count.
- **Synergies**: Strong synergy with healing skills and leech mechanics like Spring of Life and Duel Master.

---

## Stat Priorities by Immortal Type

### 1. Tanks

- Good stats: HP, Physical Defense, Magical Defense

### 2. Physical DPS

- Good stats: Accuracy (first prio until hit-cap), Physical Attack, Crit Rate, Regen Speed (attack speed), Physical Defense for frontliners.

### 3. Magical DPS

- Good stats: Magical Attack, Regen speed, Crit Rate, magical penetration

### 4. Support / Healers

- Focus on: Regen Speed, HP, Magical Defense, Physical Defense

---

## Advanced Tip: Balancing Base Stats with Skills

An Immortal's base stats should influence how you build their skill sets. For instance, a high MATK mage should not be given physical scaling skills. Conversely, a physical damage dealer like Alexander should be built for PATK scaling skills. Understanding base stats also helps prioritize artifacts and passive bonuses from specialization trees.

---

## Conclusion

Immortal stats are the foundation upon which all powerful teams are built. Mastering how each stat functions and contributes to different Immortal roles gives you an edge in both PvE events and competitive PvP. Use this knowledge to better assign skills, choose gear, and build cohesive and lethal team compositions.

title: Diddo-Merlin Offense
summary: This guide is part of my article series on earth builds. If this build is not to your likeing, have a look at the rest of my builds on the water build page. I have multiple builds for any taste available, IB, PvE…
markdown:
This guide is part of my article series on earth builds. If this build is not to your likeing, have a look at the rest of my builds on the water build page. I have multiple builds for any taste available, IB, PvE, arena/ToS builds and F2P/cheap builds.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/image-26.png)

This article is on water with **Merlin-Dido** as the center of attention. We are running Dido in this team, because she provides a crazy amount of**physical defense** to the team (awesome especially in this phys dmg meta!) plus she boosts the **damage**output of **Merlin (50%)** significantly by chilling enemies.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/Skaermbillede-2022-04-12-165223.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/Skaermbillede-2022-04-12-165245.png)

This build is made as an allround build performing very well against any enemy. It is not specialized to counter shadow or do anything specific, **it is plain and simple a solid strong build for all content** and highly competitive in PvP combat.

This build looses out to shadow like most other builds. It also looses against holy, like most others, but actually perform decently vs holy compared to other water setups (phys defense and damage output to chew through heals). If you want to fight holy/shadow u need to look elsewhere...

It is however, an awesome build and will kill most of what you will meet. **If you are a low spender, this is the build for you!** You can unlock Attilla, Dido through free to play activities. Ramses is very cheap to get.

**This makes the build extreemly strong, as spending a few bucks makes you competitive with whales!**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/image-27.png)

## Setup

This setup is pretty simple to run. You toss on the right passives and watch Merlin melt everything!

**When you are fighting you have 1 thing to beware of:** Enemy Immortal placement. You are using Ramesses and as such you need him to be useful. He must face your opponents physical damage dealer (Alex, Siegfried, Barca, etc.). He will significantly slow down melees running cleave due to his phys shield and if the enemy run their offensive immortal behind their melee dmg dealer = you are golden as Ramssess will disarm the enemys bath/khan/gilga. Fortunately for you, your enemy will likely do just this, because people run shelter and backline-assist on the same side, leaving double dps on the other side.

If you are too lazy to check battle reports and change setup, then you should either go life link instead of Physical shield or swap into Herald with life link inplace of phys shield.

### You want to run this passive loadout:

**Dido**: Oaken Guard + Assist + Sacrifice

**Merlin**: Concentration + Annihilation + Energy Burst

**Ramessess II**: Malice + Energy Suppression + Physical Shield

**Attila**: Fighting Mater + Death Breath + Weakness

title: Difference between Legion Marks and Cold Coin
summary: Infinity Kingdom is a popular mobile strategy game that offers players the opportunity to build their kingdoms, recruit Immortals, and engage in epic battles. One of the main currencies in the game is Cold Coin, which…
markdown:
Infinity Kingdom is a popular mobile strategy game that offers players the opportunity to build their kingdoms, recruit Immortals, and engage in epic battles. One of the main currencies in the game is **Cold Coin**, which is used to purchase a variety of rewards and items in the game's shop. Another important currency in Infinity Kingdom is Legion Marks, which is used to rank players on the Legion Marks leaderboard of an Legion of Frostborne battle. While both currencies are important, they are very often misunderstood.

![Legion Marks](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/image-3.png)

*Legion Marks*

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/image-2-edited.png)

*Cold Coin*

I have had many players ask be why they are not getting the Cold Coin rewards they should be getting when they demolish a Thermal in SvS or when they siege a City or raid gnomes. Players sometimes mistakenly think that the game is bugged, while in fact they are merely mistaken two currecies that look almost the same: **Cold Coin and Legion Marks. What the heck is the difference??**

## Cold Coin

First, let's look at Cold Coin. This currency is the main currency used to buy items in the game's shop. Players can use Cold Coin to purchase a wide range of rewards, including Ability Stone Fragments to unlock new Tower of Knowledge skills, Dragon Essences for upgrading their dragon's talent tree, and various buffs and speeds.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/Skaermbillede-2023-04-04-172934-1-1024x572.png)

However, it is essential to note that players can only obtain Cold Coin through two means: **ranking in the Legion Marks leaderboard**and earning alliance rewards.

To earn Cold Coin, players must rank high on the Legion Marks leaderboard of an Legion of Frostborne battle. The Legion of Frostborne is a server versus server battle mode in which players can earn Legion Marks by attacking enemy players, donating resources to their alliance structures, constructing thermal towers, defeating gnomes, dismantling enemy Thermal Towers, and sieging checkpoints and cities. However, players can only earn Cold Coin by ranking high on the Legion Marks leaderboard. This means that players who want to maximize their Cold Coin rewards must focus on earning Honor points, which directly translate to Legion Marks.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/Skaermbillede-2023-04-04-172821-1-1024x553.png)

The second way to earn Cold Coin in Infinity Kingdom is through alliance rewards. Alliance rewards are a way for players to earn Cold Coin by participating in alliance activities. These activities can include donating resources to the alliance, attacking enemy players, and participating in alliance events. The amount of Cold Coin earned through alliance rewards can vary depending on the alliance's performance and the player's participation in alliance activities.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/image-4-1024x559.png)

## Legion Marks

Now, let's talk about Legion Marks. As previously mentioned, Legion Marks are used to rank players on the Legion Marks leaderboard of an Legion of Frostborne battle. Players earn Legion Marks by performing various activities in the game, including attacking enemy players to obtain Honor, donating resources to alliance structures, constructing thermal towers, defeating gnomes, dismantling enemy Thermal Towers, and sieging checkpoints and cities.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/Skaermbillede-2023-04-04-172740-1-1024x447.png)

However, it is essential to note that Legion Marks cannot be used to buy anything in the game's shop. Instead, Legion Marks serve as a way for players to rank themselves against other players in the Legion of Frostborne battle.**This means that players who want to earn more Cold Coin must focus on ranking high on the Legion Marks leaderboard by earning more Honor points.**

The most crucial point to understand is that Cold Coin and Legion Marks are not the same thing. Many players make the mistake of thinking that they are earning Cold Coin when they perform various activities in the game, such as dismantling a Thermal or donating to a City. However, this is incorrect. These activities only earn players Legion Marks, which are used to rank them on the Legion Marks leaderboard. To earn Cold Coin, players must focus on earning Honor points and ranking high on the Legion Marks leaderboard.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/Skaermbillede-2023-04-04-172847-1-1024x560.png)

**In conclusion**, Cold Coin and Legion Marks are two distinct currencies used in the Legion of Frostborne game mode in Infinity Kingdom. Cold Coin is used to purchase rewards, while Legion Marks are earned through various activities in the game. Players can earn Legion Marks by donating resources to their alliance structures, constructing thermal towers, defeating gnomes, dismantling enemy thermal towers, and sieging checkpoints and cities. However, the only worthwhile method to obtain Legion Marks is by earning Honor.

On the other hand, Cold Coin is the main currency used to purchase rewards such as ability stone fragments, dragon essences, and various buffs and speeds. Players can earn Cold Coin by ranking high in the Legion Marks leaderboard and through their alliance's performance.

It's important for players to understand the difference between these two currencies in the Legion of Frostborne game mode. Many players mistakenly believe that they are earning Cold Coin when they dismantle a thermal tower or donate to a city, but in reality, they are earning Legion Marks for rankings. So, always prioritize earning Honor to maximize your Legion Marks rewards and subsequently earn Cold Coin rewards.

With a good understanding of the mechanics behind Cold Coin and Legion Marks, players can better strategize their gameplay and earn valuable rewards in the Legion of Frostborne mode. So, get ready to dominate the battlefield and earn those coveted rewards!

title: Difference between Troop attributes and Immortal attributes - prioritize troops!
summary: Exploring the difference between Troop and Immortal attributes in Infinity Kingdom — their mechanics, their relevance, and which to prioritize as a player seeking to maximize combat performance.
markdown:
Exploring the **difference between Troop and Immortal attributes** in *Infinity Kingdom* — their mechanics, their relevance, and which to prioritize as a player seeking to maximize combat performance.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-48-1024x521.png)

---

## ⚔️ Infinity Kingdom Guide: Understanding Troop vs Immortal Attributes

In *Infinity Kingdom*, every march consists of two essential components: the **Immortal** who leads the army, and the **troops** who make up the body of that army. Both Immortals and troops have their own attribute stats, and understanding how these two interact is critical for mastering combat — whether you’re pushing in PvP, dominating in PvE, or gearing up for events like **IBL** or **KvK**.

This guide unpacks how troop and Immortal attributes work, why they matter, and how to optimize your build by prioritizing what counts most.

---

## 🧠 The Basics: What Are Attributes?

Let’s start with the fundamentals.

Every Immortal in Infinity Kingdom has a set of **personal attributes** — stats like **Physical Attack**, **Magic Attack**, **Defense**, **HP**, **Energy Regen**, **Crit**, and so on. These values directly influence that Immortal’s ability to cast skills, trigger ultimate abilities, and survive in combat.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-52.png)

Meanwhile, the Immortal also commands a group of **troops**, whose strength is determined by a combination of **troop count** (how many soldiers are in the unit) and **troop attributes** (Attack, Defense, etc.). These stats come from the troop tier, castle level, buffs from city bonuses, technologies, and other global modifiers such as castle skins or Honor rank.

So when your Immortal casts a skill or deals basic attack damage, the resulting output is a blend of:

- The Immortal’s base stats
- The strength and number of troops
- Any external modifiers (like buffs, skills, and artifacts)

But here’s the critical part: while Immortal stats might be large in value, they apply to one unit. **Troop stats, on the other hand, are multiplied by how many troops are in that army** — and that changes everything.

---

## 📈 Scaling: Why Troop Stats Multiply Harder

Let’s consider a real combat example.

If your Immortal has 10,000 Magic Attack and commands 15,000 troops with a certain base attack stat, the actual damage output for an ability is not just based on that 10K Magic Attack. The troop attributes — even if modest — are **amplified by the total troop count**, and that massive scaling creates an **exponential increase in damage**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-51.png)

This is why players with high troop counts deal significantly more damage than players with similar Immortal stats but fewer troops. Even a relatively small buff to **troop attack** becomes a huge boost once multiplied by tens of thousands of units. A 5% troop attack bonus from a castle skin, for example, is more powerful than it appears — especially in late game when marches push 60,000+ troops.

And this is also why *empty marches deal almost no damage*. If your Immortal is standing alone with no troops left, their skill casts feel like gentle taps — because the troop multiplier is gone.

---

## 🎯 Strategic Takeaway: Troops First, Immortals Next

This leads to an important realization: if you’re deciding between boosting **troop stats** or **Immortal stats**, troop stats almost always offer the greater overall benefit.

Yes, Immortal attributes are crucial — they differentiate builds, influence skill synergy, and power up PvP matchups. But they don't scale in the same way that troop stats do.

So your first priority should always be to **increase troop count and improve troop attributes**. This means investing in:

- Castle upgrades (which increase troop cap)
- Research and tech
- Troop tier advancements
- City bonuses and ownership
- Castle skins that add troop stat buffs (e.g. Troop ATK, Troop HP)
- Honor rank, which boosts troop stats globally

Once you’ve maximized those factors, then it’s time to turn your attention toward building Immortal attributes via gear, artifact bonuses, skill synergies, and portrait levels.

---

## 🛡️ So Are Immortal Stats Still Important?

Absolutely — just in a different way.

While troop stats carry your base power, Immortal stats allow you to **tailor** your setup. You can emphasize Crit for burst builds like Wu-Zhao or Cyrus. You can build high Defense and Resilience on supports like Hippo or Charles. You can boost Energy Regen on key utility Immortals like Trajan, Dido, or Matilda to enable faster ability rotations.

In this way, **Immortal stats shape your identity** on the battlefield. Everyone is pulling from a similar pool of troops, but **Immortal builds create the variation** that defines matchups.

So no — you shouldn't ignore Immortal stats. But in terms of raw power, troop attributes win out, especially when it comes to endgame performance.

---

## 🧮 But What’s the Actual Damage Formula?

Here’s the truth: we don’t know the full damage formula. The developers have never shared it publicly, and despite the efforts of dedicated testers and theorycrafters in the community, we’ve only been able to approximate the impact of different variables.

What we do know, through testing and observation, is that:

1. **Troop count** massively amplifies skill damage
2. **Troop stats** are multiplied by troop count in the damage equation
3. **Immortal stats** have fixed scaling based on attributes and skill coefficients
4. **Missing troops = major damage drop-off**, especially for ultimates
5. **Execution timer** meaning as the clock ticks the damage equation amplifies itself relative to troops and eventually even would be medium damage hits can one-shot. This is the executioner mechanic being introduced to the damage equation during the time-out meta where people made unkillable setups that would time-out any battle and thus always win a defense.

The takeaway? Build for **troop sustainability** and **troop stat scaling**, and let your Immortals guide the flavor and focus of your build.

---

## 🏁 Final Thoughts

In Infinity Kingdom, understanding the difference between **troop** and **Immortal** attributes can be the key to building a dominant march.

**Troop stats** give you the brute force you need to scale your damage and carry fights. **Immortal stats** fine-tune that power and allow you to specialize, control, and outmaneuver opponents.

So next time you're thinking about where to invest your resources — gear upgrades, research, buffs, skins — think first about what affects **troop performance at scale**. Maximize that, and your Immortals will deliver truly game-changing results.

title: Different skill mechanics (Triggered, Passives, Graces, Blessings, Aura)
summary: Infinity Kingdom has a variety of different skills and passives. These in turn all have unique effects and have different mechanics in the way they interact in combat scenarios. For instance, an Aura type passive work…
categoryPath: Different skill mechanics (Triggered, Passives, Graces, Blessings, Aura)
markdown:
Infinity Kingdom has a variety of different skills and passives. These in turn all have unique effects and have different mechanics in the way they interact in combat scenarios. For instance, an Aura type passive work very different to a proc-chance trigger ability/passive and entirely different too from how graces and blessings function. Moreover, damage proc’s can both occur and trigger in different ways, some are DoT (damage over time) functions where others are bursty procs. Some trigger from hits, some time, some crits.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/image-26-1024x535.png)

The large variation to how skills and passives works in Infinity Kingdom is what makes this game such an awesome experience. You can synergize skills to great effect if you understand a few fundamentals of how the mechanic’s work. This, however, also leads to confusion, since there is a decent degree of complexity in Infinity Kingdom and has given rise to a bunch of player questions regarding how skills and passives functions and interact.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/image-30.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/image-29.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/image-28.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/image-27.png)

As such, I have promised to make a guide in which I will attempt to explain the fundamental types of skills and passives and how their mechanics should be understood. I will not be going into great detail with every single passive in the game, if you want more information on a particular passive let me know and I will do a thorough Passive Review guide for that. Instead, what we are going to do today is outline classes of passives and explain how each work and how you can think about them in terms of synergizing with passives and other Immortals.

## Tower of Knowledge Passives & Immortal Skill classes

- **Triggered skills**
- **Blessings & Grace effects**
- **Auras**
- **Passives**

Brief overview of each class of skills

For a more in-depth explanation of each and recommended synergies click on the class of skills you want to know more about to read a full review.

## Triggered skills

There are a lot of skills and passives which are “triggered”. Being triggered means that a certain condition has to occur in order for the skills effect to be triggered.

Infinity Kingdom marks some skills as "Passive" and other as "Triggered" despite the fact that they are in fact both Trigger skills (for instance combo). So disregard that in the in-game text, it will only confuse you. Think of all skills that has a trigger as trigger skills!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/image-31.png)

Take this example: Using a skill like Combo, it reads that when triggered your Immortal inflicts a x% physical damage instance on the enemy Immortal being attacked. Moreover, it is indicated that the trigger condition is normal attacks. As such, when your Immortal has Combo on, there is a x% chance to trigger x% physical damage every time your Immortal performs one normal attack.

On another skill like the Chaotic Blade or one of the magic DoT effects, we have a timer as the trigger.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/image-32.png)

### There are a few different triggered skills in Infinity Kingdom. The fundamentals are all the same:

1. Trigger condition
2. Once triggered inflicts skill effect

They do however differ greatly in terms of both trigger condition and skill effects. **[Read more about the different trigger skills, their conditions and differences in trigger effects here](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/combat/different-skill-mechanics-triggered-passives-graces-blessings-aura/1-triggered-skills/)**.

## Blessings and Grace effects

Blessings and Graces are skills which function by providing a combat buff to x amount of Immortals in your march. This buff is not permanent (like with Auras) but instead temporal. They last for varying amounts of time but provide powerful buffs to your Immortals while active.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/image-38.png)

Once the buff timer runs out, these skills will no longer provide value for the remainder of the fight. Blessings and Graces are always applied at the beginning of a fight. Meaning that for the first x seconds of a fight your Immortals will have the buff active. Once it runs out or is dispelled it no longer provides value.

### Read more about the different Blessings & Graces here

## Auras

This leads nicely into Aura skills. These skills are tower of knowledge passive which provide a combat buffs and debuffs passively to Immortals.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/image-41.png)

Auras are in general all powerful skills and as such they are also limited in use. You can only equip one aura on each Immortal, simply because being able to load up three auras on a support Immortal would make hard support Immortals too powerful. As a class of skills there is not much to know about auras besides the fact that:

1. You can only equip one aura per Immortal
2. Auras passively provide their unique effect throughout the entire battle

### Read more about all the auras and their syngeries here

## Passives

Lastly, we have the passive type of Tower of Knowledge and Immortal skills. Passives are quite simple. It means that their effects are permanent and applied at all times when equipped. They need no trigger, have no duration timer, cannot be despelled. They simply provide their boon and that's it!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/image-49.png)

Examples of Passive skills are Rage, Concentration, Anger, Duel Master, Fighting Master. Some of them are very very powerful. **[Read more about passives here](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/combat/different-skill-mechanics-triggered-passives-graces-blessings-aura/passive-skills/)**

title: Discount event august 2026
summary: The GTA Store Time-Limited Sale runs from August 20–23, 2026, offering increased amounts of several currencies used for Divine Skills, Chaos Immortals, Thea’s Roulette, and Rune Factory progression.
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-90-1024x465.png)

## GTA Store Time-Limited Sale: Best Packs to Buy

The **GTA Store Time-Limited Sale runs from August 20–23, 2026**, offering increased amounts of several currencies used for Divine Skills, Chaos Immortals, Thea’s Roulette, and Rune Factory progression.

Not every pack is equally useful. The best value in this sale comes from **Rune Factory Energy Cores and Divine Coins**, while the other offers depend much more on what you are currently building.

## Divine Coins

The limited-time Divine Coin packs give more coins than their normal GTA Store versions.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-96-1024x103.png)

The **$5 pack is an easy choice for anyone still working on Red Skills**. The $10 pack is also reasonable if you have a specific skill you are trying to finish.

I would be more selective with the higher-priced packs. Like most currency offers, the value becomes less attractive as you move into the larger tiers.

For a developed account, Divine Coins are often more useful than putting the same money toward another unfinished Immortal. Taking an important Red Skill from level 7 to 8 can have a much more immediate effect on your main march.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-92-1024x316.png)

## Chaos Eyes

The sale also increases the amount of Chaos Eyes:

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-97-1024x135.png)

The value stays consistent through the $20 pack, but I would only buy these with a specific Immortal in mind. Chaos Eyes make the most sense when you are pushing something that is not conveniently available through Rune Factory or another regular seasonal events. **Ares artifacts or speeding to complete Apollo, or Medusa** are examples where buying Eyes may be worthwhile if finishing that Immortal is your current goal.

Otherwise, there is no real need to stockpile them simply because the sale is active.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-93-1024x320.png)

## Thea’s Roulette Tickets

The $5 sale pack provides **12 Roulette Tickets instead of the usual 10**.

Thea’s Roulette is more useful after its recent improvements, particularly when you are working on Dragon progression. If you need **Dragon Crystals for the Holy or Shadow Dragon**, the extra tickets make this a reasonable purchase.

I would still avoid using Roulette as my main way of developing Holy or Shadow Immortals. There are better opportunities for those through the monthly event. For me, the main reason to buy these tickets is Dragon Crystals.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-94-1024x319.png)

## Rune Factory Energy Cores

The **Rune Factory Energy Core packs are the standout offer in this sale**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-98-1024x106.png)

The normal $5 GTA Store pack gives 15 Energy Cores, so getting 18 for the same price is already a good improvement. More importantly, these packs have a **daily purchase limit**.

The $10 pack keeps exactly the same value as the $5 pack: twice the price for twice the Cores. If you are currently building **Ninetales, Anubis, or Rune Factory artifacts**, I would prioritize both of these packs before looking at most of the other offers.

The higher-priced Energy Core packs are less attractive. They can still save time if you are trying to finish something quickly, but they are no longer an automatic purchase.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-95-1024x321.png)

## Red Skills or Chaos Immortals?

If you are deciding between developing another Chaos Immortal and finishing the Red Skills on your main march, I would usually finish the march first.

Red Skills affect a team you are already using. Another Chaos Immortal does very little until it is developed enough to actually replace something in that team.

For example, if your main march is already strong but **Arcane Hunter or Divine Blessing is sitting at level 7**, putting resources into that remaining skill progression can be more useful than starting another expensive Immortal project.

There are exceptions when a new Immortal completes a specific build, but as a general rule, **finish what you are using before spreading resources into another project**.

## Final Recommendation

The **August 20–23 GTA Store sale is mainly worth looking at for Rune Factory Energy Cores and Divine Coins**.

The $5 and $10 Energy Core packs are the best offers in the current sale because of their improved Core count and daily purchase limit. Divine Coins come next for anyone still developing important Red Skills.

***[Link to event here.](https://shop.gtarcade.com/en/game?game_id=408&tab=shop&sort=&classifier=0)***

Chaos Eyes and Thea’s Roulette Tickets are more situational. Buy them when they directly support something you are already working on rather than simply because they are part of the sale.

For an established account, that is the simplest way to judge these offers: **buy the packs that finish useful progression, not every pack that happens to be discounted.**

---

title: Dominate (2.8.1)
summary: With patch 2.8.1, Infinity Kingdom introduced Dominate, a new physical damage-focused Tower of Knowledge skill that increases an Immortal’s physical attack attribute by a flat amount.
markdown:
## Dominate Skill Guide – Tower of Knowledge (Patch 2.8.1 Update)

With patch **2.8.1**, *Infinity Kingdom* introduced **Dominate**, a new **physical damage-focused** Tower of Knowledge skill that increases an Immortal’s **physical attack attribute by a flat amount**.

Much like its magic-based counterpart **Ignite**, Dominate opens up a new path to power for **early-game players**, **secondary teams**, and **physical damage dealers** with **lower base stats**. But with the presence of other core physical skills like **Onslaught**, **Anger**, and **Duel Master**, how does Dominate really hold up?

Let’s break it down and see where it fits in your build strategy.

---

## What Does Dominate Do?

> **Dominate (Level 1)**
> ➤ Increases an Immortal’s **physical attack by 1800** (flat value)

This passive provides a **consistent stat boost** to physical attack and is meant for **physical damage dealers**—especially those who haven’t yet reached high enough base stats to fully benefit from **percentage-based buffs**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-152.png)

---

## Dominate vs. Onslaught – Which Should You Use?

### 🔍 Key Comparison:

- **Onslaught**: Increases **physical attack by up to 60%**
- **Dominate**: Adds **flat 1800 physical attack**

💡 **When does Onslaught become better?**
To match or beat Dominate’s 1800 boost:

> ### 3000 physical attack × 60% = 1800

So, if your Immortal has **less than 3000 physical attack**, **Dominate is the stronger skill**. Once they cross that threshold, **Onslaught will scale better**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-153-1024x699.png)

---

## Example Case:

- **Early Game Alex (Level 32)**: Might have only **1600–2200 physical attack** Onslaught = ~960–1320 bonus
Dominate = Flat 1800 boost
✔ **Dominate wins easily**
- **Late Game Alex (Fully built with Unique Artifact)**: Has **4000+ physical attack** Onslaught = 4000 × 60% = 2400
✔ **Onslaught becomes superior**

---

## What About Anger and Duel Master?

Here’s where Dominate gets more interesting.

### 🔥 Anger

> +30% **physical damage** (not attack attribute)
> This is an **output multiplier**, like **Concentration** for magic builds. It stacks with **Onslaught or Dominate** and is usually one of the best physical DPS boosts you can get.

### 🛡️ Duel Master

> +50% **physical attack**, **plus Wound Immunity**
> This skill provides both a substantial boost AND utility (anti-Wounds), making it a **must-have** for frontliners like **Alexander**, **Attila**, or **Peter** in PvP.

💡 **Dominate stacks with Duel Master**!

- Duel Master boosts by **50%**
- Dominate adds a **flat 1800**
- **Combined**, they create a powerful scaling effect, especially in early game

---

## When Should You Use Dominate?

### ✅ Ideal Use Cases:

- **Low to mid-level physical Immortals**
- **Secondary teams** where Onslaught/Anger are needed on your main squad
- **Budget builds** where flat stats have more immediate value
- **Frontliners with Duel Master** – for bonus synergy and early survivability

💡 **Example Loadout for Beginners:**

> **Alexander (no Unique)** → **Duel Master + Combo + Dominate**
> ✔ High uptime on ultimate
> ✔ Wounds immunity
> ✔ Flat damage boost

Meanwhile, you can equip **Anger** on your **Hannibal** with **Cleave**, or save Onslaught for a higher-stat Immortal.

---

## Dominate vs. Other Physical Skills

| Skill | Type | Value | Best Used On |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dominate | Flat Attribute Boost | +1800 Physical Attack | Early physical DPS, alt teams |
| Onslaught | Percent Attribute | Up to +60% Physical Attack | High-stat Immortals, main teams |
| Anger | Physical Damage Boost | +30% Physical Damage | All core physical DPS |
| Duel Master | Percent Attribute + Utility | +50% Attack + Wounds Immunity | Must-have for physical frontliners |

---

## Summary – Final Thoughts on Dominate

**Dominate** fits into the Tower of Knowledge skill lineup as a **progression skill**. It’s **not here to replace** Onslaught or Anger in the long term, but it plays an **important transitional role**, especially for:

- **Developing accounts**
- **Early PvP compositions**
- **Secondary/third marches**

### 🔥 Verdict:

> **“Dominate is a great stepping stone skill for physical teams. It shines in early game and works well when paired with Duel Master. As your base stats grow, you'll want to eventually graduate to Onslaught and Anger—but Dominate absolutely has a place in your arsenal.”**

---

## TL;DR – Dominate Skill at a Glance

| 🔹 Category | 🔸 Rating |
| --- | --- |
| Skill Type | Physical – Flat Stat Boost |
| Best Use | Early game, alt teams |
| Strengths | Consistent, great in synergy |
| Weaknesses | Outscaled by % boosts late |
| Stack with Duel Master? | ✅ Yes – excellent synergy |
| Final Rating | ⭐⭐⭐⭐☆ (4/5 early-mid game) |

---

title: Double Tank Lightning (2.8.6)
summary: Lightning marches have always had a special place in Infinity Kingdom. For a period two years ago, Double Tank Lightning dominated the meta as one of the most consistent and versatile builds in the game. While newer…
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/image-9-1024x579.png)

Lightning marches have always had a special place in *Infinity Kingdom*. For a period two years ago, **Double Tank Lightning** dominated the meta as one of the most consistent and versatile builds in the game. While newer strategies and Chaos immortals have since overshadowed it, this build still deserves attention — especially for players who want a **spender-friendly setup** that doesn’t require Chaos immortals or heavy investment into legendary skills.

In this guide, we’ll revisit Double Tank Lightning, explain its strengths and weaknesses in today’s Conquest meta, and outline exactly how to build and run it effectively.

---

## 🔎 Introduction: Why Double Tank Lightning?

Double Tank Lightning is exactly what the name suggests: a Lightning march anchored by **two frontline tanks** that keep the backline damage dealers safe long enough to win fights.

- The tanks (Tokugawa + El Cid) bring durability, disruption, and defensive utility.
- The backline (Khan + Hammurabi) supplies a combination of physical burst and sustained magical DPS.

The result is a balanced, grindy team that can survive physical-heavy opponents and dish out dangerous counterpressure over time.

While not the absolute peak of Conquest, it remains one of the **most accessible strong spender builds** because it avoids Chaos immortals and focuses on obtainable pieces.

---

## 🏛️ Place in the Meta

### Strengths

- **Budget Friendly:** No Chaos immortals or expensive legendary skills required.
- **Tanky & Reliable:** Double tank + defensive skills buys time for your DPS to shine.
- **Flexible:** Can be adapted for crit builds, hybrid setups, or sustained ramp play.
- **Anti-Physical:** Excels versus Alex, Hannibal, and other physical burst teams.

### Weaknesses

- **Mage Weakness:** Fire and Water magic teams often overwhelm this setup.
- **Scaling Limitations:** Without Chaos skills like Energy Mastery or Infinite Firepower, damage ceiling is lower than top-tier Conquest builds.
- **Skill Dependent:** Needs careful skill selection (Berserk Aura, Weakness, Energy Shield) to stay competitive.

### Who Should Use It?

- **Mid-to-High Spenders** who want a **competitive but not whale-exclusive build**.
- Players looking to **bridge the gap into Conquest** without relying on Chaos.
- Veterans nostalgic for Lightning,
- or players progressing into**max Cao Cao** or **Fu Fei**(where Double Tank Lightning gets a new power jump).

---

## ⚔️ Core Build Breakdown

### Frontline – The Double Tanks

### Tokugawa Ieyasu

- Specialization: *Iron Will* (core tank talent).
- Skills: *Fountain of Life (big upgrade vs No escape enemies) alternatively Heart of Arcana, No Escape, Guard* or Oaken (or mix in Weakness/Malice depending on matchup).

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/image-2.png)

- Role: Primary stall tank, holding the line and disrupting enemy DPS.

### El Cid

- Specialization: *Iron Will*.
- Skills: *Physical Shield, Energy Shield, Weakening Curse*.
- Role: Anti-physical wall, especially effective vs Alex/Hannibal teams.
- Note: El Cid artifacts and fragments are now easier to farm, making him more practical.

***OBS**: While Cid is amazing in an earth-wind based meta which you are likely in in season 2. You are going to want to replace Cid with Bjorn eventually. Use those holy/shadow chests to max Bjorn on the side.*

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/image-7.png)

*After this we progress into possibly himiko instead of hammurabi while you build Fu Fei to complete the lightning build journey.*

---

### Backline – The Damage Dealers

### Genghis Khan (Secondary DPS)

- Build Options:  - **Crit Khan Build:** *Weakness Aura, Adrenaline Rush, with Flexible third slot: Blade Vortex, Death Breath or Anger*. Can also also be upgraded with *Ambush* or *Time to Shine* if available.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/image-1024x568.png)

- **Balanced Build:** *Chaos Storm* (if unlocked) to give both physical and magical damage support.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/image-3.png)

- Specialization: *Deadly Aim* (crit rate + crit damage).
- Role: Provides physical burst and wound, crit-based one-shots when lucky.

### Hammurabi (Primary DPS)

- **Core Skills:** *Corrosive Power, Psionic Tide, Infinite Firepower* (if possible).

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/image-6.png)

***Note**: If you have a maxed Himiko, she is an improvement over Hammurabi one to one. Later we will replace this slot entirely though as we move into Khan - Fu Fei, read more **[here](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/elements/conquest-season-builds/khan-based-lightning-in-conquest/)***.

*Optional: skip Himiko if you do not spend enough to unlock and max Fu Fei run Theo instead of Hammurabi once you can max her.*

- Budget Alternatives: *Annihilation, Spell Disintegrator, Concentration*.
- Specialization: Stormeye in combination with a Crit % artifact (for crit synergy).
- Role: The main carry in most games, scaling damage with mage skills and chaos-like combos.

---

## 🧩 Skill & Specialization Notes

- **Assist + Lifelink:** Older combos that helped tanks soak for the backline. Still usable, but weaker than before.
- **Physical Shield:** Still one of the best tank skills in the game — mandatory on El Cid.
- **Weakness & Malice:** Swap in depending on whether you face heavy crit or ult-reliant enemies.
- **Chaos Skills (Optional):** If you do spend, adding *Energy Mastery* or *Infinite Firepower* will massively improve Hammurabi’s carry potential.

---

## 🧪 How It Performs Today

- **Against Physical Teams (Alex, Hannibal, Wukong):** Excellent. Double tank front plus El Cid’s shields give strong survivability.
- **Against Earth (Alex + Charles + Himiko):** Performs decently, though Himiko scaling eventually pressures you.
- **Against Fire & Water Mage Teams:** Struggles. Without Chaos regen or burst skills, mages can cut through sustained defense.
- **Arena & Conquest:** Still a solid march for spenders who want reliability and flexibility without Chaos investment.

---

## 🏆 Conclusion

**Double Tank Lightning** may no longer be the undisputed king of *Infinity Kingdom*, but it remains a **strong, spender-friendly build** in Conquest.

- It’s **budget competitive**: no Chaos immortals or legendary skills required to work.
- It’s **reliable against physical-heavy metas**, with strong counters to Alex/Hannibal teams.
- It’s **flexible**, allowing for crit builds on Khan or ramp setups for Hammurabi.
- Its **main weakness** is against top-tier mage comps, but with careful play and future Lightning supports like **Xiaoxiao**, Double Tank Lightning could see a full revival.

👉 If you’re a spender looking for a **safe, flexible, and competitive setup without going full whale**, Double Tank Lightning is still one of the best options available.

title: Dragon Chest Keys in the Time Rift Shop – Which Ones Are Actually Efficient?
summary: Dragon Crystals are one of the quiet bottlenecks in Infinity Kingdom. Portrait upgrades and dragon talents consume thousands over time, and the primary way most players accumulate them is through Dragon Chests.
markdown:
### Introduction

Dragon Crystals are one of the quiet bottlenecks in *Infinity Kingdom*. Portrait upgrades and dragon talents consume thousands over time, and the primary way most players accumulate them is through **Dragon Chests**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-40-1024x509.png)

Because of that, **Dragon Chest Keys** become an important long-term resource. You receive some keys each week from events like the **Spider Boss**, but the most consistent source is the **Time Rift Breaker Shop**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-41-1024x756.png)

A few patches ago, the system changed:
**Keys can now be combined upward at a 2:1 ratio.**

- 2 Common → 1 Uncommon
- 2 Uncommon → 1 Rare
- 2 Rare → 1 Elite
- 2 Elite → 1 Epic

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-42-1024x474.png)

This change raises an important question: **which keys should you actually buy in the Rift Shop?**

Let’s walk through the numbers.

---

## Rift Shop Key Costs

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-43-1024x264.png)

Since keys combine at **2:1**, we can compare the *true cost* of creating higher tiers.

---

## Cost of Building an Epic Key

If we combine from lower tiers:

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-44-1024x263.png)

So the conclusion here is straightforward: **If you want Epic keys, buy Epic keys directly.** Every other path wastes Rift currency.

## Where the Real Efficiency Appears

The interesting efficiency shows up one tier lower.

### Rare Keys

- Buying a Rare key: **3400**
- Making one from Uncommons:  - 2 × 1600 = **3200**

**You save 200 Rift currency per Rare key** by buying Uncommons and combining them.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-46.png)

Over time this becomes significant. If you open hundreds of chests during a season, that difference compounds quickly.

## Why Blue Keys Matter So Much

From actual gameplay experience, the **real bottleneck tends to be Rare (Blue) keys**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-47.png)

Boss drops and event rewards often skew toward other tiers, which leaves many players short on blue keys when they start opening large batches of Dragon Chests. The instinct is usually to buy blue keys directly from the Rift shop. That turns out to be inefficient.

Instead: **Buy Uncommon (Green) keys and combine them into Rare.**

You effectively gain **200 Rift currency of value per Rare key**, which adds up quickly over time!

---

## Practical Buying Strategy

From a long-term efficiency perspective, the Rift shop strategy is simple:

### Buy:

- Epic (Orange) – if you want Epics
- Uncommon (Green) – if you want to build Rare keys

### Avoid buying:

- Rare (Blue)
- Elite (Purple)
- Common (Grey)

Those tiers are always less efficient compared to combining.

Because of the **2:1 key combination system**, not every key tier in the Rift shop has equal value.

The most efficient purchases are:

- **Epic keys** when you want Epics.
- **Uncommon keys** when you need Rare keys.

Avoid buying Rare, Elite, or Common keys directly, since they always cost more than combining.

Over time, consistently following this approach saves a surprising amount of Rift currency — which means more keys, more Dragon Chests, and ultimately more Dragon Crystals for progression.

---
