Anyone playing Infinity Kingdom will have seen a ton of different icons appearing during combat encounters. Like my fight below, many setups are centered around using the different buffs, debuffs, negative effects, shields, controls, DoT, Hots, and Despells correctly.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/image-110.png)

This can be quite overwhelmingly complex to understand, but fear not! I have gone over the main mechanics and I believe I have them all listed here below with a short explanation of what they are, what type and what they do.

## Combat effects

| Effects | Type | Explanation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Absorb | Shield | Absorbs damage (shielded) |
| Bleed | Debuff | Continuous Physical Damage over Time (DoT) |
| Tear | Debuff | Continuous Physical Damage over Time (DoT) |
| Burn | Debuff | Continuous Magical Damage over Time (DoT) |
| Judgement | Debuff | Continuous Magical Damage over Time (DoT) |
| Confine | Control | Cannot attack using normal attacks |
| Defense | Shield | Block all damage for 3 attacks |
| Disease | Debuff | Continuous Magical Damage over Time (DoT) |
| Disarm | Debuff | Decreases physical damage done |
| Dispel | Dispel | Dispel buffs or debuffs or control effects |
| Freeze | Control | Cannot move/attack/cast abilities/regen energy |
| Mental Decay | Debuff | When anyone takes damage inthe battlefield you take 10% of that damage |
| Gloom Remedy | Debuff | All healing converted into damage |
| Infighting | Control | Cannot attack/cast abilities |
| Mitigate | Shield | Reduces the loss of an attribute/stat |
| Poison | Debuff | Continuous Magical Damage over Time (DoT) |
| Purify | Dispel | Dispel buffs or debuffs or control effects |
| Shield | Shield | Inflict damage on attacker |
| Silence | Control | Cannot cast abilities or regen energy |
| Stun | Control | Cannot move/attack/cast abilities/regen energy |
| Suffocate | Debuff | Continuous Physical Damage over Time (DoT) |
| Transfer | Debuff | Attribute, damage or stat is transferred. |
| Wound | Debuff | Cannot recieve healing |
| Healing | Healing | Recovers HP and Troops |
| HoT | Healing | Healing over Time effect. Recovers HP and Troops continuously over time. |

## Effect types / mechanics

| Buff | Blue | Directly Increases an attribute/stat/damage/defense. E.g. an Absorb Shield or a Grace effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dispel | - | An ability that either removes buffs, debuffs or control effects |
| Healing | Green | Recovers the HP and Troop count of the target. Can be in one recovery hit or over time as a buff/hot effect |
| Control | Purple | Influcts a control effect that cause e.g. enemy to be unable to attack/cast/recover energy |
| Debuff | Purple / Red | Inflicts a negative effect or a damage effect on the target. E.g. reducing attributes/damage/energy regen or causing damage over time. Can also be unique effects such as wounds or transfer. |

title: Elemental advantage explained
summary: Elemental advantage is one of the most misunderstood combat mechanics in Infinity Kingdom. Most players are aware that elements counter each other, but far fewer understand how deeply this system affects real damage…
markdown:
### Elemental Advantages in Infinity Kingdom – A Practical Combat Guide

### Introduction

Elemental advantage is one of the most misunderstood combat mechanics in Infinity Kingdom. Most players are aware that elements counter each other, but far fewer understand how deeply this system affects real damage output, survivability, and long-term meta balance.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-56-1.png)

Every Immortal and every Dragon belongs to one of seven elements: **Water, Fire, Wind, Lightning, Earth, Shadow, and Holy**. These elements are not cosmetic. They directly modify how much damage you deal and how much damage you take. Building your setups and marches with elemental advantage in mind, quickly takes you ahead of the pack.

This guide explains how elemental strengths actually work in practice, why Shadow and Holy sit outside the normal cycle, and how much weight you should give elemental advantage.

---

## The Core Elemental Cycle (Standard Elements)

The five standard elements follow a closed advantage loop:

- **Water → Fire**
- **Fire → Wind**
- **Wind → Lightning**
- **Lightning → Earth**
- **Earth → Water**

When an Immortal attacks an enemy it counters aka holds advantage over:

- It **deals increased damage**
- It **takes reduced damage in return**

This applies universally to **all damage sources**, including ultimate abilities, tower of knowledge skills, normal attacks, but importantly **NOT**to **true-damage** dealt by dragons like the fire or lightning dragon.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-58.png)

For example:

- A Water Immortal attacking a Fire Immortal deals bonus damage.
- That same Water Immortal also takes reduced damage from Fire-based attackers.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-59.png)

This is important: **elemental advantage is both offensive and defensive**. It is not a simple damage multiplier.

---

## What “Elemental Advantage” Actually Means in Battle

Elemental advantage applies at the **damage calculation layer**, not as a flat stat bonus. This means it scales with:

- Skill multipliers
- Critical hits
- Dragon damage
- Buff stacking

In practice, this is why two teams with identical power can have wildly different outcomes depending on elemental matchups.

From direct testing and later confirmation by official sources, elemental advantage provides a **variable bonus between roughly 10% and 25%**, affecting both damage dealt and damage taken. The exact percentage is not publicly documented and may vary by element or matchup.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-60.png)

---

## Shadow and Holy – The Special Elements

Shadow and Holy do not participate in the standard elemental loop.

### Shadow

- Has elemental advantage over **all standard elements** (Water, Fire, Wind, Lightning, Earth)
- Neutral against Holy

This is why Shadow Immortals consistently overperform in mixed or unknown matchups. They gain damage and survivability against the majority of teams without needing to “guess” the opponent’s element.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-56-1.png)

A good example is **Himiko**. On paper, her raw damage is not dramatically higher than top-tier elemental mages. In fact she is lower than Merlin (with Chill) and Baldwin on average (RNG dependent). In practice, her Shadow advantage pushes her ahead in almost every standard matchup. Interestingly, Merlin with Chill maintains a damage superiority in raw output stats, but he will take increased damage from a himiko meaning that in a head to head Himiko will still come out on top from superior mitigation and troop retention. As you can see below, Himiko's damage is actually not very high without her shadow advantage, but when we assume 25% elemental advantage her damage climbs above other mages only behind a Merlin IF Merlin hits a target with Chill active (meaning you have to run Artemisia or Dido, the hit on chill is not 100% and you thus also lock yourself into spending a support-immortal slot).

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-62-1024x269.png)

### Holy

- Has elemental advantage **only over Shadow**
- Neutral against all standard elements

Originally, this created a clear counter relationship: Holy checked Shadow, Shadow checked everything else. Over time, Shadow units have scaled better through skill design and stat growth, and the Holy advantage no longer feels as decisive as it once did. This shift has never been officially detailed, but it is noticeable in high-level combat data.

---

## How Much Should Elemental Advantage Influence Team Building?

Elemental advantage is **not everything**, but it is never ignorable.

From experience:

- **Equal power + elemental disadvantage** often loses
- **Slight power deficit + elemental advantage** often wins
- **Strong skill synergy** can overcome elemental disadvantage, but only narrowly

For example, [well-built Water mage teams](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/elements/water/top-water-build-merlin-artemisia-ragnar-hippo-best-i-have-seen-in-patch-2-8-9/) can still defeat Earth-focused armies despite the disadvantage, provided their sustain, control, and burst timing are correct. Element does not override mechanics—but it absolutely amplifies them.

The mistake many players make is overcommitting to raw stats while ignoring matchup logic. Elemental advantage rewards preparation and scouting far more than brute force.

---

## Conclusion Summary

- Infinity Kingdom has **seven elements**, with five forming a closed advantage loop
- Elemental advantage affects **both damage dealt and damage taken**
- The bonus ranges roughly from **10–25%**, making it one of the strongest combat modifiers
- **Shadow** dominates standard elements; **Holy** counters Shadow but is otherwise neutral
- Elemental advantage amplifies good builds—it does not replace good mechanics

Understanding elements does not just improve your win rate. It explains *why* certain Immortals dominate the meta and why some fights feel unwinnable until you change matchups rather than stats.

If you build with element in mind, combat in Infinity Kingdom becomes far more predictable - and far more controllable.

---

title: Elemental Domain Bosses Explained – Skills, Immunities and How to Counter
summary: A boss-by-boss guide to the four Elemental Domain Overlords – Skarn,
markdown:
![Elemental Domain Bosses – Skills & Counters – IK Wiki guide](/uploads/screenshot-20261127-110728-qa2t7p.png)

Every Elemental Domain dungeon ends with the same kind of fight: a single Elemental Overlord with **301.3 million HP** and a skill set built to punish one particular kind of team. Knowing what that boss does often decides whether you stall at 50% or reach the next reward milestone.

This guide covers all four Overlords (**Skarn, Nyxara, Thalgron and Vorthar**): what each skill does, what makes each boss hard, and what your formation has to counter to kill it.

For how the rewards work and how to plan your week, read the [Elemental Domain Strategy Guide](/posts/elemental-domain-strategy-guide-how-to-maximize-weekly-boss-rewards) first.

## Quick Overview

| Boss                      | Role   | Damage   | Immune to       | Resists (−30%)   | Below 50% HP          |
| ------------------------- | ------ | -------- | --------------- | ---------------- | --------------------- |
| Skarn the Frozen Doom     | Attack | Physical | Freeze          | Water            | +80% damage           |
| Nyxara Queen of Dread     | Mage   | Magical  | Stun            | Earth            | Heals every 6 s       |
| Thalgron the Storm Reaper | Attack | Physical | Seriously Wound | Wind & Lightning | 48% Life Steal        |
| Vorthar the Devourer      | Tank   | Physical | Critical hits   | Fire             | Takes 32% less damage |

All four are level 56, 7-star, T8 +30 boss Immortals with 87,000 troops, 301.3M HP and roughly 1.04–1.08M power.

## How Every Overlord Is Built

Every boss has the same four-skill structure:

1. **An ultimate** that hits your whole team and adds a control or damage-over-time effect.
2. **An immunity** that switches off one type of effect completely.
3. **An elemental resistance** that reduces damage from one or two elements by 30%.
4. **A phase skill** that activates when the boss drops below 50% HP.

The phase skill matters most. **Every boss gets harder in the second half of the fight.** Reaching 50% doesn't mean you're halfway to a kill, because the second half is a harder fight.

Before you build a team, check two things:

* Does your damage depend on the effect the boss is immune to?
* Are your Immortals hit by its 30% resistance?

## Skarn the Frozen Doom

**Attack · Physical damage · Resists Water**

**Skills**

* **Winter's Judgement (ultimate):** Ice spikes deal Physical damage (damage rate 126% → 420%) to all your units and apply **Chill**, which reduces attack speed by 3% → 10% for 12 seconds. Chilled units have a **50% chance to be Frozen** for 3 seconds.
* **Heart of Eternal Frost:** Immune to Freeze.
* **Frost Resistance:** Water Immortals deal 30% less damage.
* **Frostbitten Rage:** Below 50% HP, Skarn enters Rage and deals **80% more damage**.

**What makes him hard**

Skarn snowballs. Each ultimate slows your team and then has a coin-flip chance to freeze every chilled unit. A frozen damage dealer loses three seconds of output, and a slowed team builds Energy more slowly. Once Skarn drops below 50%, the same ultimate hits 80% harder, so many runs that look fine at first collapse after the halfway point.

**What to counter**

* **Survive the second half.** Physical defense, damage reduction, shields and healing matter more against Skarn than against any other Overlord. Build the team to still be standing at 40% boss HP, not just for a strong opening.
* **Stop the Freeze chain.** Control immunity or cleanse protects your carries. Freeze only lands on Chilled units, so removing Chill also removes the freeze risk.
* **Delay his ultimate.** Energy suppression means fewer Winter's Judgements, so less damage and fewer freeze rolls.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261127-112825-axozp5.png)

* **Leave Freeze at home.** He's immune, so freeze effects do nothing. Stuns and other controls still work.
* **Water teams lose 30%.** When Skarn is the boss in the Water dungeon, expect lower damage than your formation's numbers suggest.

## Nyxara Queen of Dread

**Mage · Magical damage · Resists Earth**

**Skills**

* **Toxic Eruption (ultimate):** Sprays venom that **Poisons all your units**, dealing Magical damage (damage rate 54% → 180%) every 3 seconds for 12 seconds. When a unit reaches **3 Poison stacks, the venom explodes**, dealing another 168% → 560% Magical damage to all your units.
* **Heart of Steel:** Immune to Stun.
* **Earth Resistance:** Earth Immortals deal 30% less damage.
* **Absorb Life:** Below 50% HP, Nyxara **recovers HP every 6 seconds** (recovery rate 600%).

**What makes her hard**

Nyxara is the only Overlord that deals **Magical damage**, so a team built with physical defense for the other three can fall apart against her. Her Poison stacks, and the third stack sets off an explosion that hits your whole team. In the second half she heals herself every six seconds, so a team without enough steady damage can stall and never finish her.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261127-112905-mk25q0.png)

**What to counter**

* **Magic defense.** Swap physical defense for magic defense and magic damage reduction where you can.
* **Cleanse before the third stack.** Removing Poison early should stop stacks from reaching three and exploding.
* **Healing reduction works.** She isn't immune to Seriously Wound, so healing-reduction effects cut into Absorb Life.
* **Steady damage beats burst.** Burst gets her to 50% quickly, but you need consistent damage to out-damage her healing.
* **Leave Stun at home.** She's immune. Other controls and Energy suppression still apply.
* **Earth teams lose 30%** if Nyxara is in their dungeon.

## Thalgron the Storm Reaper

**Attack · Physical damage · Resists Wind and Lightning**

**Skills**

* **Swarm Storm (ultimate):** A mechanical swarm deals Physical damage (damage rate 114% → 380%) to all your units, with a 10.5% → 35% chance to **Silence** each one for 6 seconds.
* **Resilient Shell:** Immune to Seriously Wound.
* **Storm Resistance:** **Wind and Lightning** Immortals deal 30% less damage.
* **Violent Plundering:** Below 50% HP, Thalgron gains **48% Life Steal**.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261127-112947-y3zeqe.png)

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261127-112957-vmp555.png)

**What makes him hard**

Silence stops your Immortals from casting their Energy skills for six seconds. If it hits your main damage dealer just before an ultimate, you lose a big chunk of damage. Thalgron is the only Overlord that resists two elements. Below 50% he heals for almost half of the damage he deals, and because he's immune to Seriously Wound, healing reduction can't stop it.

**What to counter**

* **Protect your casters.** Cleanse or control immunity on your carries keeps their ultimates on schedule.
* **Cut his damage to cut his healing.** Life Steal is based on the damage he deals. Physical defense, damage reduction and effects that lower his damage output reduce both the pressure on your team and his healing.
* **Leave Seriously Wound at home.** He's immune.
* **Push through the second half quickly.** The longer he spends below 50%, the more Life Steal he gets.
* **Wind and Lightning teams lose 30%** if Thalgron is in their dungeon.

## Vorthar the Devourer

**Tank · Physical damage · Resists Fire**

**Skills**

* **Scorched Earth (ultimate):** Shockwaves deal Physical damage (damage rate 99% → 330%) to all your units, with a 9% → 30% chance to **Stun** each one for 3 seconds.
* **Impregnable:** Immune to critical hits.
* **Fire Resistance:** Fire Immortals deal 30% less damage.
* **Obsidian Armor:** Below 50% HP, Vorthar **takes 32% less damage**.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261127-112634-km0ky5.png)

**What makes him hard**

Vorthar hits the softest of the four, but he's the hardest to damage. Crit immunity means every point of Crit Rate and Crit Damage on your team does nothing against him. In the second half he takes 32% less damage on top of that. If a Fire team meets Vorthar below 50% HP, it deals only about half its normal damage (0.70 × 0.68 ≈ 0.48), assuming the two reductions multiply.

**What to counter**

* **Rebuild without crits.** Where you can, replace Crit Rate and Crit Damage on gear, artifacts and skills with attack, damage bonuses and defense reduction.
* **Damage amplification and defense reduction** pay off more here than anywhere else.
* **Protect against Stun.** A 30% stun chance on every ultimate adds up, so cleanse or control immunity helps.
* **Plan for a long second half.** His damage is low, so survival is rarely the problem. Sustained damage is what matters.
* **Fire teams lose 30%** if Vorthar is in their dungeon.

## Which Boss Will You Face? The Rotation Question

The in-game rules only fix which **element** each dungeon accepts on which day:

| Day               | Open dungeons                                                       |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Monday            | Water                                                               |
| Tuesday           | Fire                                                                |
| Wednesday         | Wind                                                                |
| Thursday          | Lightning (shown as "Thunder" in game)                              |
| Friday            | Earth                                                               |
| Saturday & Sunday | All eight: Water, Fire, Wind, Lightning, Earth, Holy, Shadow, Chaos |

The rules don't say **which Overlord** you'll fight.

**We don't know how the bosses are assigned.** We do know that they switch around. The same day of the week can bring a different Overlord from one week to the next, and the same Overlord can turn up in different elemental dungeons. Don't expect last week's boss to be waiting for you this week.

So before every run:

* **Check which Overlord you're facing before you set your team.** Its immunity and resistance decide which of your effects and Immortals are worth bringing.
* **Use the Simulation Challenge** to test your formation against that day's boss without using a reward attempt.

*Do you know the pattern? If you've worked out how the Overlords rotate, reach out to us on Discord and we'll update this guide.*

## Counter Cheat Sheet

| Boss     | Resists          | Useless against it      | Bring                                                                           |
| -------- | ---------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Skarn    | Water            | Freeze                  | Physical defense, sustain, cleanse/control immunity, Energy suppression         |
| Nyxara   | Earth            | Stun                    | Magic defense, cleanse, Seriously Wound, steady damage                          |
| Thalgron | Wind & Lightning | Seriously Wound         | Silence protection, physical defense, damage-reduction effects, burst below 50% |
| Vorthar  | Fire             | Crit Rate & Crit Damage | Attack and damage bonuses, defense reduction, Stun protection                   |

*Damage rates are shown as ranges (lowest → highest skill level) because the bosses' ultimate levels weren't visible in the battles we recorded. The other skills are level 8, or level 6 for the below-50% skills.*

title: Elemental Domain Strategy Guide – How to Maximize Weekly Boss Rewards
markdown:
![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-105931-3v0dwr.png)

The key is understanding how rewards scale with damage, how the weekly schedule works, and where your investments will produce the greatest improvement.

**The most effective approach is to work toward one reliable boss-killing formation while gradually improving your performance across the other elemental bosses.** But for players who aren't yet capable of defeating a boss, there is still enormous value in reaching the intermediate reward milestones.

In this guide, we'll explain how Elemental Domain rewards work, why weekends are so important, which progression strategy makes sense for your account, and how to get the most out of your Immortals and Tower of Knowledge skills.

## TL;DR – How Should You Progress Elemental Domain?

There are two main approaches, depending on how developed your account is.

**Strategy 1: Build for kill-days**

If you have access to the right Immortals, upgraded Tower of Knowledge skills, Soul Crystals, artifacts, and other progression resources, prioritize one elemental boss until you can consistently defeat it.

A full kill provides the highest rewards, and a weekday boss can be challenged on its regular weekday and again on Saturday and Sunday.

That means **six-to-nine maximum-reward attempts every week from one formation** (depending on weather you can beat both saturday and sunday).

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-113226-hi14ns.png)

**Strategy 2: Progress through multiple elemental bosses.**

If defeating a boss isn't realistically achievable yet, focus on reaching the next reward milestone across several different elements.

The important thresholds are 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100%. Each provides additional rewards, so even going from 50% to 75% is worthwhile.

However, whether an improvement is worth investing in depends on how expensive it will be to achieve.

The goal is to maximize your total weekly rewards, rather than investing enormous resources into a single formation that remains far from its next milestone.

## How Elemental Domain Works

Elemental Domain becomes available in Legendary Season for players with Castle level 55 or higher.

It contains eight elemental dungeons: Water, Fire, Wind, Earth, Lightning, Holy, Shadow, and Chaos.

Each dungeon restricts players to Immortals and Dragons belonging to the corresponding element. This means your strongest PvP march may not necessarily be available, and even if it is, it might not be particularly effective against the boss.

The event follows a weekly schedule:

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-114813-hplchu.png)



Players receive three reward-bearing attempts each day.

During weekdays, those attempts are restricted to the available element. On Saturdays and Sundays, however, you can choose between all eight elemental bosses.

This weekend flexibility is central to developing an efficient Elemental Domain farming strategy.

The event also offers Simulation Challenges, allowing players to test their formations without consuming their daily reward attempts.

Use these simulations extensively when experimenting with new Immortals, adjusting Tower of Knowledge skills, or determining whether an upgrade is likely to improve your rewards.

## Understanding Elemental Domain Rewards

Elemental Domain rewards are determined by how much damage you deal to the boss.

The in-game completion screen lists five milestones:

* 10% damage
* 25% damage
* 50% damage
* 75% damage
* 100% damage, defeating the boss

One important detail is how the rewards are presented.

The completion screen displays rewards separately for each milestone. When these milestone rewards are added cumulatively, the difference between reaching 50%, 75%, and defeating the boss becomes substantial.

### Elemental Domain Reward Table

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-120614-zp06an.png)

*These are the cumulative totals calculated from the individual rewards displayed in the in-game Completion screen. Additional random drops or reward adjustments are not included.*

This has important implications for how players should approach progression.

Reaching 75% instead of 50% provides 50% more of each listed reward. Fully defeating the boss provides another 33% improvement over 75%.

And compared with stopping at 50%, a full kill effectively **doubles your rewards**.

### Why Every Milestone Matters

The increase from 50% to 75% adds another six Forging Chests, ten Forging Hammers, and fifty Tempering Elixirs per attempt.

Exactly the same additional quantities are obtained when progressing from 75% to a full kill.

Across three daily attempts, reaching the next milestone therefore adds:

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-120625-9ubse4.png)

That is a substantial amount of additional progression material.

Consequently, players should no longer think of 50% damage as a stopping point unless reaching 75% would require disproportionately expensive investments.

The objective is to keep improving your reward milestones, but to do so efficiently.

## Strategy 1 – Prioritize One Boss Until You Can Kill It

For developed accounts, one of the best ways to improve Elemental Domain rewards is building a dedicated formation capable of consistently defeating a weekday boss.

This strategy has a significant advantage over spreading investments across multiple elements.

![](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-105759-sqkcxb.png)

Once you establish a reliable full-kill formation, you can use it repeatedly on weekends, rather than needing separate high-performing formations for Saturday and Sunday.

### Why One Full Kill Is So Valuable

Let's imagine you've developed a Fire formation that consistently defeats the Fire boss.

You can use that formation on Tuesday, Saturday, and Sunday.

Since you receive three reward attempts per day, that's nine full kills every week.

Using the cumulative reward figures above:

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-120639-m2vxm4.png)

That's a considerable amount of equipment progression material from just one properly developed formation.

For comparison, consistently reaching 50% damage on those same nine attempts would provide only 108 chests, 180 hammers, and 900 elixirs.

In other words, upgrading from a 50% formation to a full-kill formation doubles the rewards available across those three days.

**This is why getting one reliable boss-killing formation should be a major objective for developed players.**

It creates a dependable source of maximum rewards every week, allowing you to gradually improve other elements without sacrificing your strongest farming days.

### Are You Ready to Build a Boss-Killing Formation?

Not every account should immediately invest everything into achieving a full kill.

Before committing, consider whether you have the resources necessary to develop a specialized PvE formation.

The most important requirements include:

**Suitable Immortals:** You may need to upgrade characters that aren't part of your regular PvP march. Strong single-target damage dealers and Immortals with powerful control effects can be exceptionally valuable against bosses.

**Tower of Knowledge skills:** Boss-killing formations often use specific skill combinations, including control, Energy suppression, damage amplification, and long-term scaling. These skills need to be unlocked and sufficiently upgraded.

**Soul Crystals:** Fully developing the necessary Tower of Knowledge skills can be expensive, especially when several important Legendary skills are involved.

**Immortal development:** High boost levels, experience levels, and appropriate talent development are important for both damage and survivability.

**Artifacts and equipment:** Strong artifacts with the correct attributes can provide meaningful improvements to the performance of your specialized damage dealers.

**Dragon progression:** A developed elemental Dragon with relevant upgrades can make a significant difference.

If you already possess most of these components, investing in one dedicated boss-killing build may be an excellent use of your resources.

If you're missing several of them, however, the cost of reaching 100% damage could be substantial.

That's when expanding your performance across multiple elements may be more efficient.

## Strategy 2 – Improve Your Reward Milestones Across Multiple Bosses

For many players, fully defeating an Elemental Domain boss is still a long-term objective.

That doesn't mean you should ignore the event or invest everything into one element.

Instead, focus on improving the reward thresholds you can consistently reach across the week.

The most important consideration is **how much additional investment is required to reach your next milestone**.

### Step 1 – Establish a Reliable 50% Formation

Start with the element where you have the strongest existing team.

Your first major objective should be reaching 50% damage consistently.

This provides a meaningful reward level and creates a foundation for further progression.

Because weekends allow you to choose any available boss, even one 50% formation can provide useful rewards on three different days.

For example, a Fire formation reaching 50% can be used on Tuesday, Saturday, and Sunday.

That's already nine attempts at the 50% reward tier every week.

### Step 2 – Decide Whether 75% Is Realistic

Once you're consistently reaching 50%, evaluate whether pushing to 75% would require a reasonable investment.

If you're already reaching 65–70%, a few skill adjustments, better artifacts, or upgrading an important Immortal might be enough to reach the next milestone.

In that situation, pursuing 75% makes excellent sense.

It provides 50% additional rewards compared with stopping at 50%.

However, if you're barely reaching 50% and the next milestone would require multiple expensive upgrades, it may be better to improve another element first.

This is where individual account progression becomes important.

The objective isn't automatically to push the same boss as far as possible. It's to identify where your next investment will produce the greatest reward improvement.

### Step 3 – Expand Into Additional Weekdays

Once you've established a strong formation for one element, begin improving another.

For example, suppose you can consistently reach 75% on Fire but only 35% on Earth.

Improving Earth to 50% may be a much more affordable investment than attempting to push Fire from 75% to a full kill.

You would then have two reliable weekdays with good rewards, alongside the ability to use your strongest formation during weekends.

Continue applying this principle to other elements.

Eventually, your goal should be to reach meaningful reward milestones across all five weekdays while maintaining one particularly strong formation for weekend farming.

### The Most Efficient Approach Depends on Your Next Milestone

Consider two possible upgrades:

**Option A:** Improve your Fire formation from 50% to 75%.

Across Tuesday, Saturday, and Sunday, that improvement could affect nine reward attempts. Each attempt would award six additional chests, ten hammers, and fifty elixirs.

That's an additional **54 chests, 90 hammers, and 450 elixirs per week**.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-114913-bic2pd.png)

**Option B:** Improve your Earth formation from 25% to 50%.

Assuming Earth is only used on Thursday, that improvement affects three attempts, adding eighteen chests, thirty hammers, and 150 elixirs per week.

Both upgrades are useful, but the Fire improvement has three times the weekly reward impact because the formation is used on three days.

Of course, if upgrading Earth is substantially cheaper, it could still be the better investment.

This is why players should evaluate both the cost of an upgrade and the number of weekly attempts that benefit from it.

## My Own Progression – Earth and Fire

My personal Elemental Domain progression is a good example of combining these two approaches.

My primary PvP march is Earth, built around Alexander and Medusa.

Although this formation is effective in PvP, it isn't particularly optimized for boss encounters.

To improve my Earth results, I invested in Arash and developed a dedicated Earth formation using Arash and Alexander.

This improved my boss damage significantly, allowing me to consistently reach approximately 75% damage.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-114923-b09iwl.png)

That gives me a reliable source of high-tier rewards on Thursdays.

However, rather than continuing to invest heavily into Earth, I shifted my attention to Fire.

After developing and optimizing a dedicated Fire boss-killing formation, I reached the point where I can consistently defeat the Fire boss.

That now gives me maximum rewards on Tuesday, Saturday, and past 50% on Sundays despite the counter fire boss! 

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-120902-b1li9b.png)

Now that Fire is established as my reliable boss-killing formation, I can redirect resources toward improving my other elements without sacrificing the maximum rewards I've already secured.

I am now moving on to securing a kill on another day (earth) which will enable me to get four kill days. 

Eventually, the goal is to have strong performances across all weekdays, with one or more formations capable of full kills. 

## Elemental Domain Builds Are Completely Different From PvP

One of the biggest lessons from Elemental Domain is that the strongest PvP formation isn't necessarily the strongest boss-killing formation.

In ordinary PvP, you're fighting several Immortals with different abilities, roles, and synergies.

In Elemental Domain, you're facing a single boss with enormous HP and unique defensive and offensive mechanics.

This creates an entirely different environment.

Some Tower of Knowledge skills that are rarely used in competitive PvP become extremely powerful, while certain Immortals that aren't particularly popular in the current PvP meta can become essential for maximizing boss damage.

Two mechanics are especially important.

### Control Effects and Energy Suppression

Control effects can be incredibly powerful in Elemental Domain.

Depending on the boss, skills applying Silence, Root, or other disabling effects may prevent dangerous abilities from activating or interrupt mechanics that would otherwise significantly reduce your damage.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-114942-7xkxae.png)

This can make some of the older blue Tower of Knowledge skills worth using again.

Skills such as Thump, alongside appropriate Silence or Root effects, may provide far more value than their rarity suggests.

Energy suppression is another important tool.

Hippolyta is a particularly good example. Her ultimate attacks repeatedly reduce the target's Energy and Attack Speed.

Against a single boss, every hit is directed at the same target, allowing her to interfere with the boss's ability to cast ultimates.

With an effective setup, Hippolyta can help create significantly longer and safer battles.

However, every Elemental Domain boss has different mechanics and immunities. Some are resistant or immune to particular control effects, meaning the same approach won't work equally well everywhere.

This is why dedicated builds are so important.

### Long Battles Make Scaling Skills Extremely Powerful

One particularly interesting aspect of Elemental Domain is that successful control setups can extend battles considerably.

In ordinary PvP, many encounters are decided relatively quickly.

But when you're fighting a boss with enormous HP, delaying its abilities and keeping your formation alive can create much longer encounters.

This gives certain Tower of Knowledge skills time to reach their full potential.

Two notable examples are **Demonic Contract and Battle Stance**.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-115002-1kvzmb.png)

Demonic Contract initially penalizes damage but gradually increases offensive output as the battle continues, eventually providing an extremely powerful damage bonus.

Battle Stance similarly rewards formations that can survive beyond its initial period of reduced effectiveness.

These skills may be less attractive in short PvP encounters, but in prolonged boss fights they can become particularly valuable.

The key is survival.

A scaling skill doesn't help much if your formation dies before its bonuses become effective.

Successful boss-killing formations often establish control and survivability first, then use damage amplification and scaling effects to maximize their performance over time.

## Which Immortals Are Best for Elemental Domain?

While the ideal formation differs between bosses, certain Immortals are particularly interesting because their abilities work exceptionally well against single targets.

### Water – Yoshitsune

Yoshitsune is a strong option for Water boss encounters because of his concentrated single-target damage.

His ultimate can direct multiple attacks against the same target, making it particularly effective when there's only one enemy on the battlefield.

For players already developing a Water formation, Yoshitsune is an important Immortal to consider.

### Earth – Arash and Alexander

Arash is extremely valuable against bosses because of his single-target damage and offensive support.

Combined with Alexander, he can provide the foundation for a very strong Earth boss-killing formation.

This is an excellent example of why your regular PvP lineup might need adjustments.

Replacing a PvP-oriented Immortal with someone better suited to prolonged single-target damage can produce substantial improvements.

### Fire – Hippolyta With Wu Zetian or Seondeok

Fire has some particularly interesting options for Elemental Domain.

Hippolyta's Energy suppression can make an enormous difference, potentially delaying dangerous boss ultimates and allowing your damage dealers to survive longer.

Pairing her with offensive Immortals such as Wu Zetian or Seondeok creates several interesting possibilities.

However, the correct setup depends on the boss's defensive mechanics, your available Tower of Knowledge skills, and how developed your Immortals are.

These are starting points, not complete builds.

We'll cover exact formations, skill combinations, artifacts, and Dragon setups in dedicated Elemental Domain boss guides.

## How to Decide What to Upgrade Next

Once you've established several working formations, the most efficient progression method is relatively straightforward.

First, look at your current damage results against each boss.

Next, identify which formations are closest to reaching their next reward milestone.

Then evaluate how difficult it would be to achieve that improvement.

For example, if you're reaching 72% damage against Earth and believe a small artifact upgrade could push you to 75%, that's likely an attractive investment.

If you're dealing 52% against Lightning but would need to develop an entirely new Immortal to reach 75%, the investment may be considerably less efficient.

Finally, remember that your strongest weekday formation can also be used twice during the weekend.

This means improvements to that formation can provide three times as many weekly reward opportunities as an improvement to a formation used only on its weekday.

A particularly good long-term progression plan might therefore look like this:

1. Develop your strongest element to a reliable 50% or 75%.
2. Evaluate whether reaching a full kill is realistic.
3. If it is, prioritize that formation and secure three days of maximum rewards.
4. If it isn't, expand your reward coverage across additional weekdays.
5. Once your main formation is established, continue improving other elements to 50%, 75%, and eventually 100%.

The exact order will differ between accounts, but the principle remains the same: **spend resources where they provide the greatest improvement to your weekly rewards**.

## Upcoming IK-Wiki Elemental Domain Boss Builds

This article focuses on the overall Elemental Domain progression strategy.

We'll also be publishing dedicated guides for the individual elemental bosses, including recommended Immortals, Tower of Knowledge skills, Dragon talents, equipment, and artifacts.

These guides will examine how the different bosses work and which mechanics can be exploited to improve damage.

Some formations will be designed to reach the 50% or 75% reward milestones with relatively modest investment.

Others will explore more demanding boss-killing compositions capable of consistently defeating the boss.

The aim is to help players make meaningful progress without wasting valuable resources on upgrades that don't provide a worthwhile return.

## Final Thoughts – Maximize Weekly Rewards, Not Just Damage

Elemental Domain should be approached as a long-term progression activity where your objective is maximizing the total rewards you collect every week.

Every reward milestone matters.

Reaching 75% instead of 50% provides considerably more rewards, and defeating the boss increases them further.

However, the most important consideration is how much investment each improvement requires.

For players with the resources to develop a dedicated boss-killing team, focusing on one weekday element can be extremely effective. A reliable full kill provides nine maximum-reward opportunities every week thanks to the weekend schedule.

For players who aren't ready to defeat a boss, the best approach is to gradually improve several elemental formations, targeting whichever reward milestones are realistically achievable.

And remember that Elemental Domain isn't normal PvP. Control effects, Energy suppression, sustained damage, and long-term scaling can be far more important than simply fielding your strongest Immortals.

**Our recommendation: Establish one strong formation for weekend farming, work toward a reliable full kill when realistic, and use your remaining resources to improve reward milestones across the other weekdays.**

Over time, this creates a steady and increasingly valuable source of materials for Mythic equipment progression.

title: Elizabeth Bathory - how she works and damage calculations
summary: Elizabeth Bathory’s & How Her Ultimate Damage Actually Works - damage estimates included: A practical damage model for real fights
markdown:
***Elizabeth Bathory’s & How Her Ultimate Damage Actually Works - damage estimates included***: *A practical damage model for real fights*

## Introduction

Elizabeth Bathory is one of the hardest immortals in Infinity Kingdom to get a firm grasp on what to expect from. She can dish out massive damage through her ultimate ability, but it can be very hard to figure out how she compares to "normal" immortals that simply have a fixed % damage attached to their ultimates. This is not because her kit is unclear, but because her **damage does not behave like a normal nuke**. Her ultimate ramps over time, depends on previously hit targets, and is strongly dependent on having "time to ramp up" meaning energy regen and fight length.

This guide explains:

- basics of who Bathory is and what she does,
- how her DoT and explosion mechanics really interact,
- why you cannot assume “full coverage” or “double explosions every cast,”
- and what **average damage to expect over 2–3 casts**, which is how most real battles actually play out.  - All calculations below use **96 energy regen**, which is equal to a 23 boost level 55 Bathory on an account with decent technology upgrades. So nothing overly fancy.

---

## Elizabeth Bathory

Elizabeth Bathory is a Shadow-element Bowman whose strength lies in sustained damage rather than immediate burst. She performs best in longer battles where she can cast her ultimate multiple times and gradually build pressure through repeated applications of her damage-over-time effects and follow-up explosions. Evaluating her based on a single cast undersells what she is designed to do.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-48-1024x662.png)

As a Shadow immortal, Bathory benefits from elemental advantage against most of the roster. She deals increased damage to all non-Holy enemies and takes reduced damage from them, which gives her consistent performance across common matchups. Holy teams remain her weakest point, but outside of that niche she rarely feels inefficient or mismatched.

Being a Bowman shapes how Bathory should be built. Her best immortal talent is **Deadly Aim**, as critical damage scales exceptionally well with her kit. When paired with a **physical attack % artifact with Annihilation**, this setup provides the strongest damage amplification available.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-49.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-50-1024x617.png)

Both her DoT ticks and her burst explosions benefit from crit scaling, which makes crit-focused builds noticeably outperform flat attack alternatives over time.

Because her ultimate relies heavily on damage-over-time effects, Bathory is directly countered by immortals that can cleanse or suppress DoTs. Most notably, **Theodora hard-counters** **her**by removing or neutralizing DoT-based damage before it can fully ramp.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-51.png)

In matchups where Theodora is present, Bathory’s effective damage is dramatically reduced, and she often struggles to reach the point where her scaling becomes relevant.

Bathory is also one of the more accessible high-impact immortals. She can be unlocked through VIP chests or random immortal fragments, including Shadow and Shadow/Light fragments.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-52.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-55.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-56.png)

After unlocking her once, her fragments are available in the Marketplace for gems, making long-term upgrades straightforward and reliable. This combination of accessibility and scaling potential makes her an appealing option for players building toward sustained, late-fight damage rather than early burst.

Overall, Elizabeth Bathory rewards patience and proper team support. She is not a front-loaded carry, but in compositions that can survive long enough for multiple ultimate cycles, she steadily grows into a decisive damage dealer - so long as her DoTs are allowed to stay on the field that is. Anyways, enough with the basics. Let's dive into her ultimate ability "Vampiric Kiss" this is one of the most interesting ultimates in the game in my opinion but also a bit tricky to get a firm grasp on.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-57.png)

---

## The Ultimate, broken into parts

Bathory’s ultimate does two things:

1. **Applies a DoT**  - Targets: **2 random enemies** (out of 4)
- Damage: **250% ATK every 3s**
- Duration: **15s** (ticks at 3 / 6 / 9 / 12 / 15)
- Rule: **Only one Bathory DoT per enemy**  - Reapplying refreshes the timer
- It does *not* stack
2. **Triggers an explosion**  - If the target **has been attacked by Bathory’s DoT before**
- Deals **530% ATK to all 4 enemies**
- Triggers **per application**
- So a cast can trigger **0, 1, or 2 explosions**

This is the core reason her damage must be treated probabilistically rather than as a fixed number.

---

## Cast timing (why refresh matters)

At **96 regen**, Bathory casts every: 1000/96 = **10.4 seconds**

This matters because:

- The DoT lasts 15 seconds
- The *next cast happens before the last two ticks*

If a target is hit again on the very next cast, its DoT usually only ticks at: **3s, 6s, 9s**
The 12s and 15s ticks are cut off by the refresh.

But — and this is important — **not every target is refreshed**.

---

## Expected DoT damage per application

Take a single enemy that just received Bathory’s DoT.

- It **always** gets the first **3 ticks**
- It only gets the last **2 ticks** if it is **not selected again next cast**

Each cast hits 2 of 4 enemies, so the chance the same enemy is selected again next cast is **50%** likewise, the chance it is *not* refreshed is also **50%**

So the **expected number of ticks per application** is: 3+(2×0.5) = **4 ticks**

Each tick is 250%, so the expected DoT damage per application is 4×250% = **1000%**

Each cast applies the DoT to **2 enemies**, and as such the expected DoT per cast (assuming multiple alive enemy immortals...) is 2×1000% = **2000%**

This already accounts for cases like if the first cast hits enemy A and B and the second cast hits A and C. Then A refreshes early (and explodes), B is completing all the 5 ticks of the DoT and C starts a new DoT effect. Over many fights, this averages out cleanly to **2000% per cast**.

---

## Explosion damage: using A–B–C–D examples

Let's continue thinking about combat encounters where we lable our enemy immortals as: **A, B, C, D**. For examples:

### Cast 1

- Hits: A and B
- No one has been hit before
- **Explosions: 0**

### Cast 2: Now A and B are “tagged.”

If cast 2 hits:

- **C + D** → 0 explosions (this *can* happen)
- **A + C** → 1 explosion
- **A + B** → 2 explosions

All outcomes are valid.

When you average them properly:

- Expected explosions on cast 2 = **1**
- Each explosion = **530% × 4 = 2120% teamwide**

So that means that the value in damage terms, or the expected burst damage on the second cast is = 2120%

---

## Putting it together: real damage over short fights

### Per-cast expectations

So let's say we have Bathory in a sustain setup and she lives comfortably long enough to cast 2 or more ultimates on enemies that are all alive for all three casts (all four enemy immortals). We are then getting 2000% DoT damage from cast one with 0% chance of a burst proc. From the second cast we are getting another avg. 2000% DoT damage and we now on avg. get 2120% damage from burst procs for a total of 4120% damage value of the second cast. Since the Burst effect seems to be working only on enemies afflicted by the DoT effect, all subsequent casts (2+) holds a value of 4120%.

**Disclaimer**: I have watched a lot of Bathory replays to try and figure out if the burst procs are dependent on simple target history or on active DoT applications. For example, if target A had the DoT on the first cast, but by the third cast (20+ seconds) the 15s DoT has expired. **Does Immortal A count as having been "already attacked by this skill"?**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-47.png)

As far as I can tell watching repeated Bathory replays I cannot find an instance where a target previously hit by a DoT but which has expired by the time it is hit again triggers a burst. As such, I am assuming that the text is mistakenly written as attacked before and instead should read **"has an active application of Vampiric Kiss DoT effect"**. However, I could be wrong. It is quite hard to tell in replays, so if you have better eyes than me, reach out and correct me please!

---

## Closing perspective

Elizabeth Bathory is not an immortal you judge by her first ultimate. She is built around **attrition, repetition, and survival**, and her true value only becomes apparent once she has time to cycle her kit. This is also why she is most often found in earth-builds with access to strong mitigation and sustain.

Players who understand this and build teams that support longer battles with high energy regen and defensive mitigation will consistently get more out of her than players trying to force her into burst-oriented roles. If built right she can be a real monster! Personally I am having much succes with her on the battlefield. However, given the abundance of Theodora's currently, she has lost a lot of value as a main march immortal. But since those enemy players are using Theodora tend to use her in their main march, I have placed Bathory in my second march which means she will carry my second team to victory against most everything that is not an enemy main march - for that I have my own main. Works very well for me and I expect her value to increase once Fu Fei becomes more "normal" to have, i.e. in late-game where most replace Theodora with Fu Fei for control immunity.

---

title: Endless Tower Guide: What It Is, How It Works and What You Can Earn
summary: Patch 2.9.8 introduced the Endless Tower, a new PvE mode built around
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-16-1024x568.png)

Patch 2.9.8 introduced the **Endless Tower**, a new PvE mode built around fighting your way through a series of increasingly difficult floors. The name makes it sound like an infinite survival mode, but the first version is more structured than that: each run lasts 20 days and contains 100 floors, with one Sentinel formation waiting on every floor.

The general idea is simple enough. You defeat the Sentinel, collect the reward and move to the next floor. The interesting part comes from the Floor Traits, which change the conditions from one battle to the next and are meant to stop players from clearing the entire tower with one unchanged march.

For newer players, the Endless Tower is mainly a free source of Gems, speedups, resources and rare Immortal fragments. For more established players, it is also a place to experiment with different Immortals and skill setups without losing a daily attempt when a battle goes wrong.

## Endless Tower at a Glance

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-11-1024x319.png)

The first run lasts 20 days, and the event appears likely to return regularly, possibly as part of a monthly cycle. That schedule has not yet been firmly established, however, so I would not treat a monthly return as guaranteed until we have seen the event calendar repeat.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-18.png)

## How to Unlock the Endless Tower

Your Castle must be at least **Level 20**, and your server must have been open for at least **15 days**. Both requirements need to be met when the event begins. If your server reaches the required age or you reach Castle Level 20 while a run is already underway, you will have to wait for the next Endless Tower event rather than joining halfway through.

The difficulty is adjusted according to the server's season. This is important because it means a young server is not expected to fight the same Sentinel formations as an old Conquest server. Endless Tower is intended to be relevant throughout the game's seasonal progression, although we will need several runs before we can properly judge how well the scaling works.

---

## How Daily Progress Works

Players begin on Floor 1 and must defeat every Sentinel in order. There is no option to skip a difficult floor or jump ahead, and a floor cannot be challenged again after it has been cleared. Battles are automatic once they begin, so all of the actual decision-making takes place before pressing the challenge button.

You receive five attempts each day, but the wording is slightly misleading because an attempt is only used when you win. Losing against a Sentinel does **not** reduce your remaining attempts, which means you are free to change your march, move skills around and try again until you find a setup that works. Your real daily limit is therefore five successful floor clears rather than five battle entries.

Unused attempts disappear at **00:00 UTC** and cannot be carried into the following day. This makes daily participation more important than it may initially appear:

**20 event days × 5 cleared floors per day = 100 floors.**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-17-1024x372.png)

The numbers leave no spare days. Under the current rules, finishing all 100 floors requires five victories on every day of the event. Missing one day means losing five possible floors, while clearing only three or four floors before reset also leaves progress behind that cannot be recovered later. Even if you are not interested in the leaderboard, it is worth treating all five daily clears as part of your normal routine.

---

## Floor Traits and Building Your Team

Every floor contains four enemy Immortals and a Dragon. Before starting the battle, you can inspect the Sentinel formation in detail, including its Immortal levels, stars, equipped skills, skill levels and specializations, along with the Dragon's level and abilities. This gives you considerably more information than a simple Combat Power number, and it is worth looking through it whenever your usual march begins to struggle.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-19-1024x470.png)

Each floor also has a **Floor Trait** that strengthens the Sentinels or changes the rules of the fight. Examples include immunity to Physical Damage and periodic HP recovery. While some are almost pointless, many are not to be ignored! A physical march cannot simply overpower an enemy that is immune to Physical Damage (level 4), while a formation with regular healing may require better burst damage, healing reduction or Wounds to prevent the fight from dragging on.

This is where the Endless Tower has the potential to become more than another daily reward screen. A player with one very strong march may clear the early floors quickly, but later traits can reward a broader account with both physical and magical damage options. Even if your secondary Immortals are not as developed as your main team, using the correct damage type or countering the floor mechanic can be more effective than repeatedly sending the formation with the highest listed power.

For beginners, I would approach a difficult floor in the following order:

1. Read the Floor Trait carefully and identify what it is changing.
2. Inspect the enemy Immortals, skills and Dragon instead of relying only on the displayed power.
3. Decide whether the floor favors physical damage, magical damage, burst, sustain or healing reduction.
4. Move suitable skills between your existing Immortals before spending resources on permanent upgrades.
5. Run another attempt and check the battle report to see whether the change actually helped.

Because failed challenges are free, there is no reason to keep repeating the same losing setup. The tower is one of the safer places to test how different skills and formations perform against a known opponent.

---

## Clear Rewards and Stage Rewards

Endless Tower has two separate reward tracks. The first is the **Clear Reward**, which is granted automatically whenever you defeat a Sentinel. These floor rewards include useful everyday progression items such as Superior Resource Optional Chests and Building, Training and Healing Speedups. The exact reward changes as you climb, but every victory gives you something even when you have not reached the next major milestone.

The second track is made up of **Stage Rewards**, which unlock after every five floors. These rewards must normally be claimed from the event screen and include **200 Gems** together with either five random Holy/Shadow Immortal fragments or five random Chaos Immortal fragments. If you leave a Stage Reward unclaimed when the event closes, it should be delivered through in-game mail rather than disappearing.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-20-1024x260.png)

Clearing all 100 floors gives the following milestone totals:

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-10-1024x162.png)

The word **random** matters here. These are not selection chests that let you target one specific Immortal, so the fragments will not necessarily advance the exact march you are building. Even so, Chaos fragments remain difficult to obtain without spending, and a recurring free source of them has obvious long-term value. The 4,000 Gems are also substantial for an activity that does not require purchases or consume attempts when you fail.

---

## How the Leaderboard Works

Endless Tower includes a seasonal leaderboard showing the top 100 players. Ranking is determined first by the highest floor cleared. If several players have reached the same floor, the faster clear time is used to separate them, and the leaderboard updates approximately every five minutes.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-21-1024x497.png)

The daily floor limit means active players will often be tied at the same point during the early part of the event. Keeping up with all five clears ensures that you remain on the highest floor currently available, while optimizing battle time becomes relevant for players chasing the top positions. For everyone else, the valuable part of the event remains the floor and milestone rewards; there is no need to rebuild your account around shaving a few seconds from a Sentinel fight unless the ranking itself matters to you.

---

## Is Endless Tower Worth Doing?

Yes. Endless Tower is free, failed challenges do not consume attempts, and the reward pool includes materials that most players need alongside Gems and rare Immortal fragments. The main danger is not wasting resources or losing troops; it is simply falling behind because unused daily clears cannot be saved.

The longer-term question is whether the later Floor Traits create genuinely interesting mechanical puzzles or whether progress eventually comes down to account power. The foundation is promising because players can inspect the opposing formation and retry without punishment, giving them room to learn from failed battles and adapt their teams. If future versions continue adding varied traits and sensible seasonal scaling, Endless Tower could become one of Infinity Kingdom's more useful permanent PvE activities rather than another event cleared on autopilot.

For the first run, the best advice is straightforward: unlock the event, complete five floors every day and read the trait before assuming that your strongest normal march is automatically the right answer.

---

title: Energy Burst - a Deep Dive
summary: Hello and welcome to a special guide on the Passive Tower of Knowledge ability \"Energy Burst\". In this guide we will dive into what this passive is. We will also ask, Is energy burst any good? Energy burst has been…
markdown:
Hello and welcome to a special guide on the Passive Tower of Knowledge ability "Energy Burst". In this guide we will dive into what this passive is. We will also ask, Is energy burst any good? Energy burst has been nerfed before and we will look into what has happened to this passive and how the hidden mechanics work

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/2-1024x576.png)

I have been recommending energy burst for builds for a long time, but it is very important to understand when and how to use it succesfully. In this guide we will look at how it works. Explain the hidden mechanics that some players may not even realize exist! Furthermore, we will look at how to use this Passive. What NOT to do and how to set up this Passive for major impact!

## How does it work?

This skill is pretty simple to understand at first glance. But do not let that fool you! It is one of the most complex skills in the game, because of it's hidden mechanics.

What it does on the face of it, is boost your energy regen every time you land a critical hit. Well it says every time.. But it is not really every time, more like most of the time. More on that later! What is important to know for now, is that it only provides energy regen once you land a critical hit. Once you land a crit, you gain 100 energy.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/3-1024x576.png)

This means you want to equip this passive on Immortals that scale well from Energy regen. Such as Attila, Hippolyta, Khan, Gilgamesh, and so on. Also you want to make sure to use passives to synergize with Energy Burst, meaning passives which cause many damage instances per minute as possible.

Furthermore, because we only gain energy regen once we land a critical hit on our enemy, we want to have a lot of critical hit rate before being able to use this passive. You should be aware of the significant 9% Base Crit Value boost from achieving VIP rank 13. If you do not have VIP 13, you will likely not have enough critical hit rate to gain real value from this passive.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/4-1024x576.png)

Critical hits giving energy also means that we can begin to scale Critical hit rating beyond the additional damage. Critical hit has a given value for any Immortal as it boosts the damage output of set Immortal. But with Energy Burst, we can begin to scale the value of critical hit rating further. This in turn, means more value from buffs like the Combat Crit buff and from Immortals such as William and Trajan.

## Hidden Internal Cooldown Mechanic

Now that we understand how it works, we can begin to look deeper into it's hidden mechanics. Remember I said this Passive was nerfed? So back in the day when it was first release, we would get 100 energy with EVERY single critical hit. So if a Hippolyta hit with 5 attacks from her Ultimate Ability in the half second it takes her to cast it, well then she would get back 100 energy 5 times, basically getting her to cast again.

This meant, that pairing Energy Burst with Weakness, Crit Boosts and a proc ability like Death Breath, would cause any Immortal to get almost no downtime between casting skills. As you can imagine, the results was extreemly broken and had to be fixed by the development team.

The fix they came up with was applying an internal cooldown to the ability. Which honestly, is a really good fix! They just forgot to add it to the information text of the Passive description.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/7-1-1024x576.png)

## What does all this mean?

So what this means is, once you land a critical hit Energy Burst activates and gives you 100 energy. It then begins an internal cooldown timer. Once this timer is running, any critical hits you land gives no energy. Only once the Ability is off cooldown again will you get energy from another crit.

Many players have been looking into figuring out precisely what this internal cooldown is, and it seems there is an agreement in the community that Energy Burst has a 2 second internal cooldown.

## How to run it "right"

Alright then. We fully understand what this passive does and how all the aspects of it works. How do we run it right then? Is it any good?

You want to run Energy burst preferably in a fire setup because you have the added critical hit rate.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/image-2-1.png)

If you have VIP 13 and you have strong crit technology and so on, you can run it very succesfully in other setups too. But you need to have a setup that feeds consistent critical hits into Energy Burst. That means, you should always try and have Weakness in the same setup as Energy Burst.

This means having many small instances of damage is far superior to fewer large hits. If you land for instance 1 large attack every second, then you need to have every single attack be a critical hit to not have downtime in between Energy burst going off cooldown and you activating it again.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/8-1024x576.png)

If you on the other hand, land 4 or 5 hits every second, you need only one out of these hits to crit, giving you a much higher consistency and a much lower downtime on the Passive. Hence, many small attacks is allowing you to take full advantage of the Passive and the Energy regen boosts

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/9-1024x576.png)

## So is Energy Burst any good then?

It is very very very powerful if you are using it right. Having maximum uptime on it's procs enable your Immortal to regen energy extreemly quickly. Check out this Seon, she relies on Energy Burst to secure near 100% uptime on her Ultimate Ability for massive damage.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/image-1-1-1024x615.png)

**But just as powerful as it can be when done right. Just as terrible is it to do it wrong.**If you have low critical hit and fighting against someone with Malice on. You are not going to have a very good time with this Passive. Check out this poor Gilgamesh.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/image-3-1-1024x456.png)

He is trying to run Energy Burst to get off more Ultimate Casts. Which is a good idea on paper, but because the player is not running Weakness and dosen't have very high critical hit rating. The enemy puts on Malice and suddenly Gilgamesh does not land a single critical hit for the entire fight. Hence this guy get zero value what so ever from having Energy Burst. Literally any other Passive would have more impact.

title: Energy Master
summary: Energy Master is one of the most influential Legendary skills in Infinity Kingdom, and it has reshaped how backline carries function in Conquest. When you run a mage or bowman with Energy Master, you always want to pair…
markdown:
## Introduction

**Energy Master** is one of the most influential Legendary skills in *Infinity Kingdom*, and it has reshaped how backline carries function in Conquest. When you run a mage or bowman with Energy Master, you *always* want to pair that carry with a **support immortal running Battle Excitation**. This pairing is the engine behind the modern ultimate-cycling meta: the support accelerates the initial energy curve, and Energy Master ensures the backline carry never slows down once casting begins.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-85.png)

The result is a dramatic shift away from older double-healer or bruiser-carry setups. In Conquest, the defining hallmark of a competitive march is a backline damage dealer whose ultimate fires rapidly and repeatedly, supported by both talents and skills designed to maintain that cycle.

Let’s break down how Energy Master accomplishes this.

---

## 1. What Energy Master Does and Why It’s Meta-Defining

Energy Master provides:

- A **large instant energy refund** every time the immortal casts an ultimate.
- A **significant energy-skill damage increase** for several seconds after each cast.
- A cast rhythm that becomes progressively faster as the battle continues.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-87.png)

Together, these effects do far more than increase damage:
**Energy Master changes the entire pace of a fight.** It frontloads enormous burst damage while pushing cast frequency far beyond what older builds could achieve. Instead of waiting for the typical ramp-up to full energy, your carry enters a loop where ultimates are fired in rapid succession, and each cast fuels the next. This extremely compressed damage window is what has defined the meta in the Conquest era.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-68-1024x620.png)

---

## 2. Energy Master and the Ultimate-Cycling Engine

### 2.1 How the Core Loop Works

The typical structure is:

- **Backline carry (mage or archer)** → has Energy Master.
- **Backline support** → runs Battle Excitation talents to boost initial energy.
- **Frontline tanks/supports** → stabilize the fight and create time for the carry to cycle.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-88-1024x658.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-89-1024x568.png)

You can also run **Rage Blessing** on a tank or support.
Rage Blessing provides a **3/4 chance to grant your team additional energy regeneration**, and in practice, this often lands on your carry. When it does, it accelerates the cycle even further, reinforcing the Energy Master engine.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-90.png)

### 2.2 What This Looks Like in Combat

Once the carry fires the first ultimate:

- Energy Master immediately refunds a large portion of the bar.
- If you pair it with **Corrosive Power**, you add drip-feed energy on damage ticks.
- Battle Excitation and Rage Blessing smooth the regen between casts.

See the energy of Himiko on the right side, her energy is being refunded as she casts and as she deals damage in this video. **This is ult-cycling using Energy Master and Corrosive Power.**

[Embedded media](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Infinity-Kingdom-2025-12-11-16-15-00.mp4)

You no longer watch your carry drop to low energy and slowly climb back up. Instead, ultimates appear rapidly, one after another, and opponents take heavy burst damage before they’ve fully ramped themselves.

This produces **dramatically higher total damage**, but more importantly, **far more rapid damage output**, because the team avoids the slow buildup that used to define earlier seasons.

---

## 3. Comparing Energy Master to Psionic Tide and Corrosive Power

### 3.1 Psionic Tide

- Strong energy regeneration skill.
- Outclassed by Energy Master for primary carries. Energy Master (EM) provides double the energy refund. For Mages specifically, Psionic Tide does bring a strong damage buff with it affecting your Tower of Knowledge skills damage as well as your own by 15% stacking 3 times. But for ultimate-cycling, the 100% Energy skill damage buff from EM is superior as well.
- Note Psionic cannot be equipped together with Energy Master. If you are using Energy Master in your main or on a ranged-carry, Psionic can be substitute for a mage, but for mains EM is superior.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-93-1024x647.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-88-1024x658.png)

Energy Master simply drives ultimates harder and faster, and its damage window is substantially stronger.

### 3.2 Corrosive Power

- Excellent synergy skill.
- Adds ultimate damage and continuous energy gains on hit.
- Can be paired with Energy Master (or Psionic for that matter), which is currently one of the highest-performing carry combinations in the game.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-94.png)

For burst-centric carries, **Energy Master + Corrosive Power** defines the current gold-standard build.

*Note: After the most recent nerf to Seondeok, her trigger effects on her ultimate no longer counts as ultimate damage, hence you cannot get the buffs and regen from e.g. an EM+Corrosive combination that you used to. That makes Corrosive Power near useless on her specifically, but Energy Master does still work well here.*

---

## 4. Supporting Skills and Talents

### 4.1 Battle Excitation (Support Only)

Battle Excitation is exclusive to support immortals, and in the Energy Master meta it is **mandatory**. It significantly improves the opening of the fight by boosting initial energy, which allows your carry to reach the first ultimate more quickly. Without that acceleration, the Energy Master engine still works, but it loses much of its sharpness.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-95.png)

### 4.2 Rage Blessing on Tanks/Supports

Rage Blessing adds a probabilistic layer of additional energy regeneration. When its 3/4 chance lands on your carry—and it often does—it further tightens the cycle and compounds the value of Energy Master, especially in long fights. While this does NOT affect refuned energy from Energy Master (or other sources) it does provide synergy to the general concept of ultimate-cycling builds.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-96.png)

### 4.3 Owl Guardian Talents

Running an energy centric build, you should make sure to always be using the Owl Guardian Talents, providing a 5% buff to the passive energy regen of your immortals. While this does NOT affect refuned energy from Energy Master (or other sources) it does provide synergy to the general concept of ultimate-cycling builds.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-97-1024x506.png)

---

## 5. Best Immortals for Energy Master

Any primary damage dealer that **relies on ultimate damage burst hits** performs extremely well with Energy Master. It is not limited to AoE casters; single-target burst or multi-hit patterns also scale beautifully.

### 5.1 Mages

- **Himiko**
Balanced, consistent, and extremely reliable. Energy Master elevates her damage curve and ensures fast casting cycles.
- **Baldwin**
Higher theoretical output than Himiko but more RNG-dependent. With Energy Master, his peaks become devastating, though you still experience the occasional low-roll battle.
- **Merlin, Empress Wu, Hammurabi, others**
Any mage built around strong ultimate bursts benefits greatly from Energy Master + regen builds.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-88-1024x658.png)

### 5.2 Archers

- **Genghis Khan**
High crit synergy and excellent scaling with rapid ultimates. Strong Energy Master pairing.
- **Apollo**
Absolutely not a niche pick—Apollo becomes a very strong primary carry with Energy Master. His kit aligns tightly with fast-cycling builds, making him one of the more promising long-term archer carries in Conquest.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-98-1024x595.png)

---

## 6. Leveling Priority & Investment Advice

Energy Master does not require max level to outperform other skills.
However, instead of feeling powerful at level 2–4, the practical threshold where it begins clearly surpassing most alternatives is **around level 5**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-99-1024x596.png)

- **Level 5:** The energy refund becomes large enough to sustain a reliable cycle.
- **Level 6–7:** The higher the level the better, that being said, at the 6-7 range we are getting to levels that makes the skill unrivaled by anything else on many burst-immortals.
- **Level 8?:** Yes, you want to get this to level 8 if possible. That being said, due to the nature of how the required skill stones to upgrade each level increases, most players find it the most effective to end upgrading at level 7 and move on to the next legendary skill - then to return once you have the ones you need at their appropriate levels.

### Upgrade costs to Chaos/Legendary Skills:

**Unlock: 60
level 2: 5

For players investing in Legendary skills, Energy Master is typically the best first choice for any account built around a backline carry.

## Conclusion

Energy Master is not just a high-damage Legendary skill; it is the foundation of the current ultimate-cycling meta. When paired with a support that has Battle Excitation, and supported further by skills like Rage Blessing and Corrosive Power, it creates a fight rhythm defined by:
