markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-100-1024x219.png)

Legendary Season represents the largest progression jump in Infinity Kingdom. The level cap increases from 55 to 60, Mythic equipment becomes available and several new progression systems open alongside a considerably more complicated version of Legion of Frostborne.

There is plenty to learn, but you do not need to understand every calculation before entering the season. This guide provides an overview of the main changes, what you should prepare and which systems deserve their own closer look.

## Table of Contents

- Who Can Enter Legendary Season?
- Level 60 Progression
- Mythic Equipment
- Elemental Domain
- Legendary Legion of Frostborne
- How to Prepare
- Summary

---

## Who Can Enter Legendary Season?

Servers become eligible for Legendary Season after completing **Conquest Season Phase 5 or later**.

Entering the season unlocks progression beyond level 55 across most areas of the game. This includes buildings, Lords, Immortals, Dragons, equipment, troops, Technology and Tower of Knowledge Skills.

The scale of the expansion means that Legendary Season should be approached as a long-term progression stage. You will not finish everything during the first offseason, nor are you expected to.

---

## Level 60 Progression Buildings

The most obvious change is the new level-60 cap, but upgrading beyond level 55 requires more than ordinary resources and speedups.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-101-1024x540.png)

Legendary Season introduces an **Energy Core progression system** containing five tiers with three stages in each tier. These stages are developed using Azure Crystals and Stellar Crystals.

Azure Crystals can be produced by converting Food, Wood, Stone and Iron through a level-55 Forge, while Stellar Crystals are primarily obtained through events. This creates a new progression bottleneck and prevents players from reaching level 60 using saved speedups alone.

Your early priority should therefore be to upgrade the Forge, begin producing Azure Crystals and use your resources carefully.

**Read more:** [Legendary Season Building 55-60 and Energy Core Guide](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/development/buildings/legendary-season-building-55-60-and-energy-core-guide/)

---

## Mythic Equipment

Level 56 and higher Gnomes begin dropping **Legendary+ equipment**, which can be upgraded to level 60 and eventually reforged into Mythic quality.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-104-683x1024.png)

*Image credit DaBossMan (Givens) server 382*

Mythic equipment receives between one and five random attributes, allowing individual pieces to become considerably stronger than ordinary equipment. However, reforging also comes with two important consequences:

- The equipment becomes permanently bound to the Immortal wearing it.
- The equipment returns to level 0 and must be upgraded again.

This makes Mythic equipment a major commitment. Your first pieces should normally be assigned to a long-term Immortal from your primary march rather than someone you may replace in the near future.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-103-683x1024.png)

*Image credit DaBossMan (Givens) server 382*

You should also begin saving Gold, Enchant Stones and Advanced Enchant Stones before entering Legendary Season. Reforging equipment is only the beginning; upgrading it back to level 60 is where much of the real cost appears.

**Read more:** [Mythic Equipment and Reforging Guide](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/immortals/gear-equipment/mythic-equipment-for-legendary-season/)

---

## Elemental Domain

The **Elemental Domain** is the main source of materials used to reforge Mythic equipment and reroll its attributes.

It contains eight separate dungeons covering Water, Fire, Wind, Lightning, Earth, Holy, Shadow and Chaos. Each dungeon only allows Immortals and Dragons belonging to its corresponding element.

Water through Earth rotate across the weekdays, while every Elemental Domain becomes available during the weekend. Players receive three reward attempts each day, with rewards based on their performance against the boss.

This system gives secondary Immortals and Dragons considerably more value. You do not need eight perfectly developed PvP marches, but relying entirely on one main formation will limit your ability to farm materials.

Before Legendary Season, preserve useful Immortals from different elements and keep several flexible PvE skills available. Even an imperfect elemental team is more useful than having no eligible formation at all.

**Read more:** [Elemental Domain Guides](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/events/elemental-domain/)

---

## Legendary Legion of Frostborne

Legendary Season also introduces a more complicated version of Legion of Frostborne.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-105-1024x527.png)

The first major change is the **Profession Contract system**. During the preparation period, players select one of three alliance roles:

- **Master Craftsman:** Produces materials and temporary Unit Boost items.
- **Alchemist:** Uses those materials to construct and improve Altar Stones.
- **Fighting Master:** Receives combat-focused bonuses for direct warfare.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-102-1024x261.png)

*Image credit DaBossMan (Givens) server 382*

These roles support one another. Master Craftsmen supply the materials, Alchemists turn them into Altar Stones and Fighting Masters help protect the operation. Alliances should therefore assign Contracts according to their overall strategic needs rather than allowing every player to select independently.

Contracts become locked when the war period begins, so the distribution should be agreed upon during preparation.

**Read more:** [Legion of Frostborne - Profession Contracts Guide](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/legion-of-frostborne/things-you-must-know-about-legion-of-frostborne/profession-contracts-guide/)

---

### Altar Stones and Battlefield Energy Cores

Cities and checkpoints now gain a third defensive stage. Once their walls and defenders have been defeated, a battlefield **Energy Core** is exposed.

Normal marches cannot destroy this Energy Core. It must be attacked by Altar Stones constructed by your alliance’s Alchemists. If several Federation alliances participate, the objective belongs to the alliance whose Altar Stone deals the final damage to the Core.

Altar Stones can also attack enemy Altar Stones, castles and troops. This turns city capture into a coordinated logistical operation rather than a simple contest of siege strength.

This battlefield Energy Core is separate from the permanent Energy Core system used for upgrading buildings toward level 60.

**Read more:** [Legendary KvK Altar Stone and Energy Core Guide](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/legion-of-frostborne/things-you-must-know-about-legion-of-frostborne/legendary-kvk-altar-stone-and-energy-core-guide/)

---

## How to Prepare

You do not need to stop all account development months in advance, but building a reasonable reserve will make the transition much smoother.

Try to prepare the following:

- Upgrade your buildings to 55, atleast the Castle and Forge to level 55.
- Save Food, Wood, Stone and Iron for Azure Crystal production.
- Stockpile Building and Research Speedups.
- Save Gold, Enchant Stones.
- Decide which Immortal should receive your first Mythic equipment.
- Preserve useful Immortals and Dragons from several elements in preperation for Elemental Domain.
- Keep flexible PvE skills for Elemental Domain formations.

The objective is not to complete Legendary progression immediately. It is to avoid entering the season with no resources, no secondary elemental teams and no plan for your first Mythic equipment.

---

## Summary

Legendary Season expands the level cap to 60 and introduces several connected progression systems. Energy Cores control building development, Elemental Domain supplies Mythic equipment materials and Legendary+ equipment creates a new long-term reforging system.

Legion of Frostborne also becomes more dependent on alliance organisation through Professional Contracts, Altar Stones and battlefield Energy Cores.

For most players, the best approach is simple: save resources, prepare several elemental teams, choose your first Mythic Immortal carefully and coordinate with your alliance before KvK registration closes. You can then explore each new system through the dedicated guides as it becomes relevant to your account.

---

title: Exciting News: Introducing Ranked Battle Chess!
summary: Prepare yourselves for an exhilarating new game mode coming to Battle Chess! On June 7th, 2023, we are thrilled to announce the launch of Ranked Battle Chess on all servers. It's time to elevate your gaming experience…
markdown:
Prepare yourselves for an exhilarating new game mode coming to Battle Chess! On June 7th, 2023, we are thrilled to announce the launch of Ranked Battle Chess on all servers. It's time to elevate your gaming experience and delve into the world of competitive chess like never before!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/image-4-1024x550.png)

## Ranked Mode

1. Ranked Matches: **Open daily from 14:00 to 16:00 and again from 22:00 to 24:00** during each season. Engage in intense battles against opponents who are matched based on similar rankings and skill levels. Please note that ranked matches can only be played during specific restricted time slots.
2. Rewarding Progress: After each ranked match, players will earn tier points based on their performance. These points contribute to your ranking and a unique matchmaking rating (MMR), which plays a significant role in determining your seasonal standings.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/image-6-1024x117.png)

### Ranking and Tiers

Climb the ranks and reap the rewards! Battle Chess features 10 distinctive ranks for players to achieve. At the end of each season, players can claim rewards corresponding to the rank they achieved. Think of it as similar to the rewards system in the arena. Tier and ranking rewards can be claimed once per season, adding an extra layer of excitement to your competitive journey.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/image-5-1024x523.png)

### Seasons

Each season lasts for 30 days, providing ample time for players to showcase their strategic prowess. As a season concludes, participants will be rewarded based on their final ranking, and a fresh start awaits with the beginning of a new season. Get ready for a continuous cycle of thrilling competitions!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/image-7-1024x105.png)

### Eligibility

To participate in Ranked Battle Chess, servers that have completed the Chronicle - Royal Ambition are eligible. In eligible servers, Lords who have reached level 11 and above can engage in the captivating world of Battle Chess.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/image-8-1024x339.png)

Mark your calendars and set your alarms for Wednesday at 14:00, as we kick off the very first time slot for Ranked Battle Chess. Join us as we embark on this exciting journey and take chess to unprecedented heights!

I can't wait to see you on the battlefield!

title: Executioner - DoT synergy burst skill
summary: Few Tower of Knowledge skills have had a lifecycle quite like Executioner. When it was first introduced, it immediately became one of the most explosive scaling skills in the game. Properly supported, it could…
markdown:
## Introduction – A Skill That Rises and Falls With the Meta

Few Tower of Knowledge skills have had a lifecycle quite like **Executioner**. When it was first introduced, it immediately became one of the most explosive scaling skills in the game. Properly supported, it could outperform many legendary actives simply by converting continuous damage into repeated area burst. Then the meta shifted.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-142.png)

Theodora and Purification became standard. Continuous damage stopped sticking. Executioner lost its fuel source and quietly disappeared from high-level play. Now, in the current environment — where Fu Fei has largely replaced Theodora and fewer players dedicate slots to cleanse — Executioner has become relevant again.

If you are a low spender or free-to-play player looking for a way to pressure modern Himiko builds, this is one of the few Tower skills capable of punching upward.

---

## Official Skill Description

**Executioner**: After inflicting continuous damage 8 times, deal additional physical damage (350%) to all enemies and gain the execution effect, which increases the damage dealt to targets with less than 30% troops for 6 seconds.

Available in the Cinder Shop. Meaning you can obtain it for free by purchasing Legion of Frostborne skill rewards, sell the skill stones you do not need for Cinders and buy Executioner in the Cinder shop! Same goes for Blade Vortex, which most players want to use in synergy with Executioner to get the damage over time (DoT) effect applications required to trigger Executioners damage procs.

---

## How Executioner Actually Works

Executioner does not trigger from raw damage. It triggers from **continuous damage instances** also known as Damage over Time effect or DoT's for short. That distinction is very important to understand.

Each tick of damage-over-time counts toward the 8-trigger requirement. Once 8 ticks have occurred, Executioner releases a 350% physical AoE burst to all enemies. Then the counter begins again.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-130-1024x619.png)

So the real question becomes: How fast can you generate 8 continuous damage ticks?

The faster you reach that threshold, the more often Executioner detonates. Executioner is not in itself a burst skill, it is a scaling multiplier requiring synergy with skills and immortals to perform.

---

## Ideal Synergies

Executioner requires fuel. The best fuel source in the current meta is **Gilgamesh** although Bathory also applies consistent DoT effects and can also be used for an Executioner build.

His ultimate applies:

- Initial AoE physical damage
- Followed by ticking continuous damage on all enemies

When paired with **Blade Vortex** (or other DoT skills like Chaotic Blade or Garrotte), you add additional ticking damage on multiple targets.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-140.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/image-183.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-141.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/image-184.png)

Now you have:

- DoTs from ultimate
- DoTs from skills like e.g. Blade Vortex
- Multiple targets ticking simultaneously

The result is simple: Executioner triggers repeatedly.

In testing and real KvK reports, Executioner often becomes one of the top damage contributors in properly built Gilgamesh marches — sometimes even outperforming the ultimate itself.

Bathory can run a similar structure, but Gilgamesh produces more consistent ticking frequency, which accelerates Executioner more reliably.

---

## Why Executioner Fell Out of the Meta

Executioner was not nerfed into irrelevance, it was countered. When Theodora and Purification became common, continuous damage was removed before it could stack. If DoTs are cleansed, the 8-tick requirement resets. Without ticks, Executioner never reaches critical mass.

This is why Executioner collapsed during heavy cleanse metas. The skill itself was not weak — its environment became hostile.

### Why It Works Again Today

In the current Conquest meta:

- Fu Fei has largely replaced Theodora.
- Purification is no longer a staple skill slot.
- Many Earth/Himiko builds rely on sustain and attack speed rather than cleansing.

This creates a structural vulnerability: Continuous damage now sticks, and when it sticks, Executioner scales aggressively.

If the enemy is not actively removing DoTs, you are effectively running a 350% AoE burst skill that can trigger very fast and very often for massive damage pressure.

---

## What Hard Counters Executioner

As we have touched upon earlier, Executioner has a clear Achilles heel: The ability to dispel DoT effects.

If the enemy runs: Theodora and/or Purification, then the skill loses most of its value as your enemy will consistenty cleanse damage over time effects - especially Theodora with her AoE mass dispel.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-150.png)

Continuous damage gets removed = Triggers slow dramatically = Scaling collapses.

Executioner is a meta-dependent skill. It thrives when cleansing is rare and struggles when cleansing is common.

---

## Executioner in Low-Spender Strategy

One of the most important aspects of Executioner is accessibility.

It is available in the **Cinder Shop**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/image-185.png)

This means:

- It does not require premium gacha luck.
- It can be purchased through accumulated Cinders.
- It is fully viable for free-to-play players willing to reinvest skill stones.

When paired with farmable immortals like Gilgamesh and Qin, you create a setup capable of defeating significantly more expensive builds — particularly Fu Fei Himiko structures lacking purification.

---

## Practical Takeaway

Executioner is not universally powerful. It is conditionally powerful.

When the meta favors:

- Sustain over cleanse
- Fu Fei over Theodora
- Damage scaling over debuff removal

Executioner becomes one of the most efficient Tower of Knowledge skills in the game.

Built correctly, it:

- Scales aggressively
- Punishes non-cleansing metas
- Holds elemental advantage in key matchups
- Remains fully accessible to low spenders

---

title: EXP Cost and How to Level Artifacts Efficiently
summary: Artifacts are one of the most powerful tools in Infinity Kingdom. They boost your Immortals with massive stat increases, provide unique bonuses, and can make or break your march’s performance in PvP and PvE content. But…
markdown:
Artifacts are one of the most powerful tools in Infinity Kingdom. They boost your Immortals with massive stat increases, provide unique bonuses, and can make or break your march’s performance in PvP and PvE content. But beyond simply crafting them, players often underestimate the importance of **leveling** these artifacts — a process that takes time, resources, and strategic planning.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-91-1024x418.png)

In this guide, we’ll explore why artifacts matter, how artifact leveling works, the EXP requirements for each level, how to farm artifact EXP, and a strategy for leveling efficiently to maximize your power without wasting precious resources.

---

## Why Artifacts Are So Important

Artifacts provide:

- **Flat Attribute Increases:** Each level adds significant Attack, Defense, or other attributes to your Immortal.
- **Special Bonuses:** Properly crafted artifacts with the right attribute rolls (like Attack %, Crit %, and with the right bonuses) can drastically improve your Immortal’s performance.
- **Scaling Power:** Artifacts get progressively stronger as you level them, making them a core part of late-game progression.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-92-1024x643.png)

Simply put: **artifacts are one of the biggest single power spikes you can give your Immortals**. They directly impact how hard your skills hit, how durable your frontline is, and whether you can compete against top players.

---

## Artifact Leveling: How It Works

Artifacts start at **Level 0** when crafted. To improve their stats, you need **Artifact EXP**, which you gain by **dismantling other artifacts**.

Here’s the **EXP value per dismantled artifact**:

- **Green (Common):** 10 EXP
- **Blue (Rare):** 30 EXP
- **Purple (Epic):** 100 EXP
- **Orange (Legendary):** 300 EXP

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-93-1024x433.png)

You’ll get these artifacts mainly from crafting at the **Forge**, as well as events like **Mysterium**, recurring **calendar events**, and some seasonal events.

---

## Artifact Leveling Requirements

Here’s how much EXP you need per level:

| Level | EXP Required |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | 10 |
| 2 | 30 |
| 3 | 50 |
| 4 | 70 |
| 5 | 90 |
| 6 | 110 |
| 7 | 130 |
| 8 | 150 |
| 9 | 170 |
| 10 | 190 |
| 11 | 340 |
| 12 | 390 |
| 13 | 470 |
| 14 | 550 |
| 15 | 630 |

**Total EXP to Max (Level 15):** **3380 EXP**

---

## How to Farm Artifact EXP

To upgrade artifacts, you’ll need a steady source of bad artifacts to dismantle:

1. **Forge Transmutations:**  - Use resources in the Forge to craft artifacts. Most rolls will be suboptimal, so break them down for EXP.
2. **Events & Calendar:**  - Participate in recurring events like **Mysterium** and seasonal events to get artifact fragments.
3. **Treasure Stores:**  - Seasonal event shops often include artifact selection chests — always prioritize these when available.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-94-1024x451.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-95-1024x410.png)

**Tip:** If you craft an artifact with terrible rolls, don’t keep it — **dismantle it and feed it into a good artifact** for EXP.

---

## Leveling Strategy: How to Level Efficiently

Artifact leveling is expensive. You need **3380 EXP** to max a single artifact, which is a LOT of dismantled crafts. That’s why **you need to prioritize which artifacts to level first**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-99-1024x629.png)

Here’s the recommended progression:

1. **Level Damage Dealer Artifacts First**  - Your carries (e.g., Wu, Alex, Himiko) benefit most from artifact levels because their damage output directly wins fights.
2. **Reach Level 10 Quickly**  - Leveling from 0 → 10 costs just **1000 EXP**. This gives huge power for relatively cheap.
3. **Craft Artifacts for Every Immortal**  - Even bad ones — they still provide base stats. Replace later.
4. **Upgrade Your DPS to 15**  - After getting all artifacts to 10, push your main damage dealer’s artifact to Level 15.
5. **Support & Tanks Stay at Level 10 (for now)**  - Damage dealers should be maxed first. Support and tank upgrades beyond 10 are only worth it for whales.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-97-1024x361.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-98-1024x409.png)

---

## Why This Matters

Leveling artifacts **correctly** ensures that your power gains are front-loaded where they matter most — on Immortals who decide fights. Maxing out a tank artifact before your DPS is a waste of resources.

This approach ensures:

- **Maximum efficiency per EXP spent.**
- **Biggest combat impact early on.**
- **Balanced growth across all your marches.**

---

## Conclusion

Artifacts are a **long-term progression system** in Infinity Kingdom — they aren’t just about crafting, but about carefully leveling and optimizing them for your most important Immortals.

### TL;DR:

- Prioritize leveling **damage dealer artifacts first**.
- Get **all artifacts to Level 10** for efficient power gains.
- Push your main DPS artifact to **Level 15** when you can afford it.
- **Dismantle bad artifacts** for EXP — don’t let them sit idle.
- Farm Mysterium, events, and use the Forge to keep the EXP coming.

If you follow this plan, you’ll see huge improvements in PvP and PvE performance without wasting valuable resources.

title: Explaining the difference between Crit Rate, Crit Bonus and their interaction with Resilience
summary: Critical hits are one of the defining damage mechanics in Infinity Kingdom. Nearly every high-damage lineup in the current meta relies on them in some form, especially ranged carries and magic-focused backlines that can…
markdown:
## Introduction

Critical hits are one of the defining damage mechanics in *Infinity Kingdom*. Nearly every high-damage lineup in the current meta relies on them in some form, especially ranged carries and magic-focused backlines that can stack offensive stats through artifacts, talents, research, and conquest equipment.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-49.png)

The problem is that many players confuse **Crit Rate** and **Crit Bonus**, or misunderstand how **Resilience** interacts with them. The game’s wording is not always perfectly clear, and some older explanations in community discussions mixed the mechanics together.

In practice, these are three separate systems:

- **Crit Rate** determines *whether* a critical hit happens.
- **Crit Bonus** determines *how much extra damage* the critical hit deals.
- **Resilience** reduces the *chance* of receiving a critical hit.

Understanding the difference matters because optimizing crit builds is not just about stacking every offensive stat available. A lineup with high Crit Bonus but low Crit Rate will produce inconsistent damage, while a lineup facing heavy Resilience may fail to crit reliably at all.

---

## Crit Rate: The Chance to Land a Critical Hit

Crit Rate determines the probability that an attack or skill becomes a critical hit. It controls how often your immortal is able to trigger bonus damage during combat.

A critical hit is essentially an amplified version of a normal attack. When a crit occurs, the game applies additional damage based on the immortal’s Crit Bonus stat. Crit Rate itself does not increase damage directly — it only increases the likelihood of triggering those stronger hits.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-50-1024x372.png)

For example:

- 10% Crit Rate means critical hits occur infrequently and highly unreliable
- 30–40% Crit Rate creates much more reliable burst output relying on RNG to connect with the crits you need
- 60-80% Crit Rate allows carries to crit consistently enough throughout a fight and is what you are aiming for if doing a crit-centric build

This becomes especially important for ranged and magic backline immortals because they attack repeatedly over long engagements. The more often they attack, the more value they gain from reliable critical hit frequency.

---

## Sources of Crit Rate

Crit Rate can come from many systems, including e.g:

- Artifacts
- Talent specialization trees
- Mythic equipment modifiers
- Research/technology
- Skills and buffs
- Certain immortal passives

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-51.png)

Backline damage dealers benefit the most because they attack consistently and usually scale harder from burst damage.

For instance, when I tested crit-focused Wind and Lightning setups in late-season Conquest, increasing Crit Rate often produced a larger real damage increase than adding raw attack once the lineup already had decent scaling. Consistent crit frequency tends to outperform occasional oversized hits.

---

## What Crit Bonus Does - Crit Damage Scaling

Crit Bonus determines how much additional damage a critical hit deals after it successfully triggers. While Crit Rate controls the chance to crit, Crit Bonus controls the strength of the crit itself. Crit Bonus appears in legendary season on equipment and prior to that through more explicit descriptions such as on Trajan's ultimate, Williams Unique Artifact, Artifact Annihilation Bonus, etc. The wording of Crit Bonus however, appears on mythic equipment modifiers and caused a great deal of confusion.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-53-1024x529.png)

In simple terms:

- Higher Crit Rate = critical hits happen more often
- Higher Crit Bonus = critical hits hit harder

Crit Bonus only activates when a critical hit occurs. If an attack does not crit, Crit Bonus provides no benefit to that hit.

For example, an immortal with high Crit Bonus but low Crit Rate may occasionally land extremely large burst hits, but overall damage can still feel inconsistent because critical strikes are not occurring often enough. On the other hand, combining strong Crit Rate with strong Crit Bonus creates the high burst damage profiles commonly seen in late-game PvP lineups.

The game itself describes Crit Bonus as affecting:

> “The amount of damage dealt after a critical hit.”

This is important because many players confuse Crit Bonus with Crit Rate. Crit Bonus does not increase the probability of critting. It is purely a damage amplification stat tied specifically to successful critical hits.

Crit Bonus scales especially well in the late game once players gain reliable Crit Rate through artifacts, conquest equipment, talent specialization, and technology upgrades. At that stage, increasing Crit Bonus can dramatically improve burst potential, particularly for backline carries that already crit consistently.

In actual combat, this is why optimized crit builds tend to scale both stats together. Crit Rate provides consistency, while Crit Bonus converts those successful crits into meaningful kill pressure.

---

## Why Crit Bonus Needs Crit Rate

Crit Bonus has no value if the immortal rarely crits.

That is why strong crit builds usually balance both stats instead of stacking only one.

A common mistake is over-investing into Crit Bonus early while lacking enough Crit Rate to trigger reliable critical hits. In actual combat testing, this often leads to unstable damage patterns where one battle looks excellent and the next feels weak simply because crits did not occur consistently.

Generally:

- **Crit Rate = consistency**
- **Crit Bonus = burst potential**

The best late-game crit carries usually scale both together and prioritizes crit rate as to not leave yourself reliant on RNG.

---

## Resilience: The Counter to Critical Hits

Resilience is the defensive stat that counters Crit Rate in *Infinity Kingdom*. Its purpose is to reduce the enemy’s chance of landing critical hits against your immortals.

This is one of the most commonly misunderstood mechanics in the game because many players assume Resilience reduces the damage of critical hits directly. It does not.

> Resilience reduces critical hit chance, not critical hit damage.

The game compares the attacker’s Crit Rate against the defender’s Resilience to determine the final probability of a critical hit occurring. If the defender has high Resilience, the attacker will crit less frequently overall.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-54.png)

However, if a critical hit still succeeds:

- The hit deals full critical damage
- Crit Bonus still applies normally
- The crit is not weakened by Resilience itself

For example, a backline carry with very high Crit Rate may normally crit consistently throughout a fight. Against a target stacking Resilience, many of those potential crits may instead become normal hits, significantly lowering the carry’s burst consistency.

This is why Resilience becomes increasingly valuable in PvP. As players gain access to stronger artifacts, conquest equipment, technology upgrades, and optimized talent setups, crit-focused lineups become much more common. Resilience acts as a direct counter to those builds by suppressing how often dangerous burst windows occur.

Resilience is arguably one of the most underestimated attributes in *Infinity Kingdom*, largely because its impact is less visible than raw offensive stats. Many players focus entirely on increasing damage output, while overlooking how much effective damage can be prevented simply by suppressing enemy crit frequency.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-55-1024x607.png)

Even many top-tier meta lineups benefit enormously from defensive anti-crit setups, especially through sources like Malice and optimized conquest gearing. In actual high-level PvP, reducing the consistency of enemy burst windows often has a bigger impact on fight outcomes than adding more raw stats to your own carries.

---

## Conclusion Summary

Critical mechanics in *Infinity Kingdom* are built around three connected but distinct stats:

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-48.png)

The key takeaway is simple:

- **Crit Rate controls frequency**
- **Crit Bonus controls damage**
- **Resilience counters crit chance, not crit damage**

Players who understand this interaction can build far more effective carries, optimize burst setups properly, and defend against crit-heavy metas more intelligently.

---

title: F2P Fire Main or Spender Second (2.6.9)
summary: Introduction to the Fire Build: For free-to-play players or those looking to diversify their strategies, crafting a competitive Fire team setup can be a daunting task. However, the build I've discovered harnesses the…
markdown:
### Player Guide: Dominant Free-to-Play Fire Build in Infinity Kingdom

**Introduction to the Fire Build:** For free-to-play players or those looking to diversify their strategies, crafting a competitive Fire team setup can be a daunting task. However, the build I've discovered harnesses the power of freely available skills and immortals to create a surprisingly strong fire team. It's perfect for those looking for an effective secondary setup or a primary fire setup that can hold its own against spendier builds.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/image-54-1024x448.png)

**The Fire Team Composition:** This fire build utilizes the following immortals, each playing a unique and crucial role:

- **William**
- **Hippolyta**
- **Cleopatra**
- **Empress Wu**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/image-55-1024x589.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/image-57-1024x420.png)

**Dragon and Specialization:** The team is backed by the **Fire Dragon** with the **Prairie Fire** specialization, enhancing its breath damage and synergizing well with the overall damage output of the team.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/image-56-1024x358.png)

## Immortal Roles and Skill Setups:

### William (Frontline Support)

- **Rage Blessing**: Boosts energy regeneration, crucial for quick ultimate ability usage.
- **Energy Suppression**: Limits enemy energy regeneration, disrupting their ability to use ultimates effectively.
- **Malice**: Reduces the enemy's critical hit chances, offering a buffer against high-damage spikes.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/image-58-1024x610.png)

### Hippolyta (Sustain and Defense)

- **Shelter**: Provides unexpected sustain, healing millions and significantly bolstering durability.
- **Life Link**: Reflects incoming damage back to the attacker, adding a layer of retribution.
- **Physical Shield**: Protects troop count, essential for withstanding heavy hitters like Alexander.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/image-59-1024x626.png)

### Cleopatra (Damage Reduction and Support)

- **Weakness Aura**: Increases the team's critical hit capabilities, complementing William's buffs.
- **Blessing of Defense**: Further enhances the team's defensive capabilities.
- **Poison Thorn**: Useful for reducing enemy troop counts and damaging key physical attackers.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/image-60-1024x612.png)

### Empress Wu (Main Damage Dealer)

- **Chase**: Ensures sustained damage output through repeated hits.
- **Death Breath and Spell Disintegration**: Both skills provide numerous damage instances, boosting Chase's trigger consistency and wreaking havoc on enemy lines.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/image-61-1024x596.png)

**Strategic Considerations:** This fire setup excels in defensive strategies while still packing a punch with Empress Wu's damage capabilities. It's particularly effective against popular setups like Alexander + Himiko, providing a robust defense through Hippolyta and Cleopatra's abilities while slowly chipping away at the enemy with strategic hits from Wu and support from William. It functions exceptionally well as a main for free to plays or as a secondary to a mid-spender focusing on e.g. dual tank shadow hybrid or plain himiko earth, etc.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/image-62.png)

**Conclusion:** While this build may not topple the top-tier spender formations, it offers remarkable resilience and damage potential within the constraints of free-to-play resources. It's an excellent choice for players navigating an earth-dominant meta, seeking a fire team that can consistently perform well in various battle scenarios. Give this build a try, tweak it to fit your style, and watch as it holds its ground impressively in the fiery confrontations of Infinity Kingdom.

title: F2P fire with Tomyris patch 2.6.8
summary: For players on servers in Season 3 or above in Infinity Kingdom, the Galaxy event offers cheap and even free access to key immortals like Tomyris and Himiko. This guide focuses on leveraging these opportunities to build…
markdown:
### Fire-Tomyris Build for Free-to-Play Players in Infinity Kingdom

For players on servers in Season 3 or above in Infinity Kingdom, the Galaxy event offers cheap and even free access to key immortals like Tomyris and Himiko. This guide focuses on leveraging these opportunities to build a potent free-to-play fire setup centered around Tomyris.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/image-71-1024x374.png)

## The Advantages of Fire

Fire is a compelling element for several reasons:

1. **High Damage Burst**: Ensures rapid troop count reduction, crucial in making an impact against stronger foes or in rally situations.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/image-72-1024x515.png)

1. **Energy Regeneration Reduction**: Immortals like Hippolyta excel in diminishing enemy energy regen, providing a strategic edge.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/image-73-1024x550.png)

1. **Critical Chance and Damage**: Building crit chance and damage is effective in the current meta, especially as high-power opponents often neglect Malice in their setups.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/image-74-1024x289.png)

## Key Immortals for the Build

- **Trajan**: Increases crit chance and damage and serves as a durable frontline presence.
- **Hippolyta**: Known for reducing enemy energy regen and attack speed, her multiple damage instances are vital.
- **Seondeok**: Acts as the primary damage dealer with a powerful AOE nuke ability.
- **Tomyris**: Provides battlefield control with her confuse ability, significantly aiding in damage ramp-up.

## Crafting Your Fire Setup

### Trajan's Configuration

- **Basic Setup**: Weakness Aura, Blessing of Rage, and Blessing of War are essential for foundational support.
- **Advanced Options**: Include Weakening Curse for added debuffing and consider No Escape, Purify, or Energy Shield for flexibility, maintaining Weakness Aura.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/image-75-1024x610.png)

### Hippolyta’s Loadout

- **Basic Setup**: Equip Death Breath, Energy Burst, and Full Coverage for significant damage output and instance frequency.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/image-76-1024x589.png)

### Seondeok’s Arsenal

- **Basic Setup**: Utilize Anger, Adrenaline Rush, and Fighting Master or Rage for control setups or additional crits.
- **Advanced Skills**: Incorporate Blade Vortex and Executioner for heightened damage, with Corrosive enhancing her destructive capabilities.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/image-77-1024x621.png)

### Tomyris’s Toolkit

- **Basic Setup**: Malice, Assist, and Energy Suppression offer control and support.
- **Advanced Skills**: Opt for No Escape and potentially Energy Shield, with Adrenaline Rush as an option for increased control effectiveness.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/image-78-1024x628.png)

## Strategy and Adaptation

The fire-Tomyris build's success hinges on skill synergy and strategic immortal deployment. Adapting to the enemy lineup and server meta is crucial. Flexibility allows for effective counter-strategies, making skill selection and immortal pairing key to maximizing the build’s potential.

## Conclusion

A fire setup with Tomyris offers a strategic advantage for free-to-play players in Infinity Kingdom, combining the elemental strengths of fire with Tomyris’s control abilities. By tailoring your strategy based on available skills and server-specific dynamics, you can create a formidable team capable of challenging a wide array of opponents. Adjustments and testing are essential to refine your approach and achieve optimal performance.

title: F2P friendly: Water & Fire & Hybrid
summary: I get a lot of players sending me requests for march setups, lately I have been getting a lot of interest in running a F2P version of the earth-wind hybrid as a second or third team. Furthermore, many people seem to be…
markdown:
I get a lot of players sending me requests for march setups, lately I have been getting a lot of interest in running a F2P version of the earth-wind hybrid as a second or third team. Furthermore, many people seem to be running water mains where they have spent a little to get Attila and Merlin then pure free to play from there on. Other prefer fire or lightning marches but many players are writing saying they have water main since the beginning of the game, but don't know what to do with it to make it fit with a second and third march build.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/Design-uden-navn-1024x306.png)

For the purpose of this guide I shall use a real player from the community. This player reached out and asked me to setup a complete three-march-setup that fits with what he has going for him at the moment. If you are a F2P or low-spender and is looking for inspiration for how to setup your marches, this guide may just be for you!

Togeather with the community I ended up with this three-march-setup to recommend for our requesting-player: **(1) Water main (2) Fire secondary and (3) Earth/Wind Hybrid third.**

In addition to these builds and collective setup, I will include a link to future work on how these builds can improve and develop if you choose to spend to unlock new Immortals.

*Message to the trolls: Yes this is considered F2P builds. Yes, this is technically not true since u pay a couple bucks unlocking the third builder to get Merlin. No I do not care that i'm technically incorrect, I consider the third builder "the price of installing the IK app" and No that does not make anything P2W... Aight... With that out of the way, let's dive in and actually enjoy some content!*

## Current player setups

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/Screenshot_2023-02-15-10-05-31-839_com.gtarcade.ioe_.global-1024x435.jpg)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/Screenshot_2023-02-15-10-04-42-924_com.gtarcade.ioe_.global-1024x425.jpg)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/Screenshot_2023-02-15-10-05-19-866_com.gtarcade.ioe_.global-1024x437.jpg)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/Screenshot_2023-02-15-10-05-27-690_com.gtarcade.ioe_.global-1024x427.jpg)

First up, we have got four different elements going here but only want three marches fit for combat. We are going to be leaving out Lightning, simply because we do not have any solid replacements for Peter. Peter is spearman tech as our only Immortal, this is terrible simply because we want to eliminate one troop tier to make a more slim technology progression path.

While the best options would be to replace Peter with William or Hippo, we would also have multiple magic passives in reserve since we do not have access to a Hammurabi. If you have Hammurabi yourself and a high level lightning dragon, you can go Hammu-YSG-William-Richard. But since that is not the case for our player here, it is easy to eliminate lightning from our combat roster.

The second thing we need to do is figure out what we want to focus on. You always want to focus on a main, then a second then a third. Doing all three marches at the same time (upgrading dragons and ToK passives equally) is a huge disadvantage. Since this player is invested in water dragon having it at max level progressing through the dragon talents, we are going to stay the course and keep water for main. For the second and third team, we are actually for once going to be not focusing on them as either or. Instead we will be setting up builds that fit each other so well that there is no overlap between the skills you want to run and as such can consider either one of them your second. Complete player preference.

## My recommendation for all three builds

We got some pretty scattered passive combinations going on however a decent setup for water as is. What I am going to do is move around a bit making small ajustments to the water team to fit in the current meta. Moreover, we are going to make a clear goal for how our second and third are going to look once we finish building it out. This sets up a nice goal for our player to work towards, and once achieved is an excellent position to further improve on with the later game P2P immortals, if he so chooses. Either way, a solid position for a basic setup with a good division of tok skills which means you can easily change it to fit your current server meta and also means that you are not running multiple setups that all need the same passives to work.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/image-58-1.png)

I will show the builds visually from an IB-league formation. So disregard the power and lack of artifact. The images are only to visually show you the Tower of Knowledge builds. Beware that Gilga = Arash!

**We are turning the water into a standard control-centric setup with Merlin as our core dps. As for the fire, we are building full offense and maxing its burst crit potention, with a bit of luck you can take down a huge chunck of HP on even marches with much higher power with an offensive fire. Lastly our hybrid will be a standard wind-earth hyrbrid with a few modifications since we are not running it as a main. Basically this hybrid is able to get massive value out of a lot of tok skills which are terrible anywhere else. Running it in this way means that we are using top tower of knowledge skills on all three marches instead of having a third with nothing going on (as is often the case)**

**-- WATER --
Merlin**: Concentration + Annihilation + Death Breath
**Yoshi**: Assist + Malice + Absolute Defense
**Herald**: Missleading + Energy Suppression + Oaken Guard
**Attila**: Adrenaline rush + Fighting Will + Fighting Master

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/Skaermbillede-2023-02-17-153507.png)

**-- FIRE w. GILGA --**
**Gilga**: Anger + Chaotic Blade + Onslaught
**Wu**: Chase + Toxic Nova + Rage (if you have enough crit to consistently proc chase, you can go double nova over rage)
**Hippo**: Energy Burst + Sacrifice + Garrote
**William**: Weakness + Blessing of Rage + Resist

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/image-56.png)

*Arash should NOT be used. You want to run Gilgamesh. This image is just to show the ToK skill distribution*

**-- EARTH-WIND HYBRID --**
**Zeno**: Berserk + Blessing of Speed + Life-link/After Image (depends on phys. enemy vs backline nuke mages)
**Qin**: Coercion + Blessing of War + Blessing of Defense
**Hannibal Barca**: Cleave + Shelter + Heavenly Thunder
**Alexander**: Duel Master + Combo + Absorb

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/image-57.png)

*While I have not played these myself, the respons I have gotten back from the Player who sent in the request are overwhelmingly positive. The setups seem to work very very well for him. Versus other waters and fires he prefers Life Link on Zeno and is running with double nova on Wu for the best result.*

## Further development and build progression

Like I said in the beginning of this guide, this is tailored for one particular player and then made into a generalized guide for others to seek inspiration from. Your Immortals roster, willingness to spend, server PvP meta may be a lot different from this player's and as such you should as always make careful decisions that fit your situation. Use the above as inspiration!

In addition to the three-setup-builds we have gone other in this guide, I have made some progression pathways as part of a broader series on low-spender-three-march-setups: [**Read more here.**](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/elements/full-3-march-comps/concept-ideas-for-low-spender-3-march-setups/)

Fitting with this particular three-march-setup with Water main, Fire and Hybrid second/third, you may want to consider a progression path that develops and evolve into: **Water w. Bath/Himiko + Fire w Gilga/Seon + Hybrid.**

title: Farm Alliances to Max Valor Rewards - extreem rewards!
summary: CoR is a kingdom-wide event where alliances compete to collect energy cubes by gathering mysterious energy nodes across the world map. These cubes translate into Valor Marks, which you can redeem in the CoR shop for…
markdown:
## ⚔️ What Is the Contention of Relics (CoR)?

CoR is a kingdom-wide event where alliances compete to collect **energy cubes** by gathering mysterious energy nodes across the world map. These cubes translate into **Valor Marks**, which you can redeem in the CoR shop for powerful resources—chief among them, **healing speed boosts** crucial for preparing for IBL and KvK.

Without CoR Valor, players miss out on optimal healing speed, putting them at a disadvantage when wars begin.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-43-1024x569.png)

### TL;DR

- CoR lets you collect **energy cubes** for **Valor Marks**.
- Valor Marks are primarily used to **buy healing speed-ups**, essential for war readiness.
- Valor points and healing speed are non-negotiable in IBL, KvK, and server-wide PvP.

---

## 🌟 Why Valor Marks Matter

The CoR shop offers high-value items like healing speed-ups—essential for rapidly regenerating troops post-battle. When wars hit, players with fully stocked healing boosts can relaunch attacks or defenses with minimal downtime. That edge can mean the difference between winning or losing a KVK or IBL.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-45-1024x584.png)

Maxing out Valor ensures you're never caught flat-footed.

### TL;DR

- Healing speed-ups from Valor are critical in war.
- High Valor = faster healing = more fighting power.
- CoR is your best chance to stockpile these ahead of KVK/IBL.

---

## 🚀 The Swarm Strategy: Farm Alliance Mastery

> **🙏 Special thanks to Magic Mage (Server 243)** for sharing this elegant, highly efficient farm alliance strategy

Once your **main alliance** reaches **300,000 energy cubes** (max Valor), further farming yields no additional rewards. Enter the **farm alliance swarm**: setting up **multiple small alliances** to repeatedly earn the high-value **10K cube** reward tier—boosting Valor drastically.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-44-1024x551.png)

By cycling members through farm alliances just long enough to hit 10K, you can replicate this reward endlessly.

### TL;DR

- Main alliance hits cap at 300K cubes → no more Valor.
- Small alliances that hit just 10K cubes unlock **40 Valor per cube** (400K Valor per alliance).
- You can repeat this across many alliances to top your Valor stock repeatedly.

---

## 🧩 How to Execute the Farm Alliance Swarm

1. **Primary “Main” Alliance**: Use this alliance to hit 300K cubes, win CoR, and capture kingdom rewards.
2. **Many "Farm" Alliances**: Create 10–20 mini-alliances specifically to farm just **10,000 cubes** each.
3. **Cycle Members or Alts**: Move players into a farm alliance, farm 10K cubes, claim Valor in main, get kicked, then join a new farm alliance.
4. **Repeat & Scale**: Each cycle yields **400K Valor per alliance**, multiplied by the number of farm alliances and participants.
5. **Bank in Main**: After cycles, return to main alliance and redeem all Valor at once.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-47-1024x453.png)

Magic Mage’s example: **[Watch here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BceKVKd3k9I)**

> "16 participants across 12 alliances…314,831 Valor in just farm alliances, on top of core alliance rewards."

### TL;DR

- Form main alliance for initial cap.
- Spin through mini-alliances hitting 10K each.
- Claim Valor, bounce, repeat—with no cooldown penalties.
- Every 10K mission = 400K Valor per player involved.

---

## 💸 A Closer Look: Numbers & ROI

### Unbuffed Valor rates from alliance tiers:

- 300K cubes → 3.6M Valor (12/cube)
- 10K cubes → 400K Valor (40/cube)—the goldmine!

If your group runs **12 farm alliances** with **16 participants**:
Each player walks away with:

- **~316K Valor** from farms + **225K from main** = **~540K Valor** total per CoR cycle.

That’s enough to purchase multiple **healing speed packs**, fully preparing everyone for war.

### TL;DR

- 12 farm alliances × 16 players = ~316K Valor per player.
- Add main alliance Valor → ~540K total per cycle.
- Enough Valor to secure multiple healing speed-ups every CoR.

---

## 🔧 Tips for a Smooth Operation

- **Node Refresh Awareness**: Energy nodes respawn hourly—time your node farming accordingly.
- **Communication is Key**: Use Discord or alliance chat to coordinate which farm alliance is active.
- **Kick & Rejoin Smart**: Kick players immediately after Valor claim to bypass cooldowns.
- **Monitor Alliance Capacity**: 10–16 active members yield best results in mini-alliances.
- **Alt Account Use**: Add more participation capacity and stagger farming schedules.
- **Assign Leadership Roles**: Ensure someone oversees coordination and Valor distribution.

### TL;DR

- Track node resets and rotate participants.
- Clear chat & leadership structure streamline the process.
- Alt accounts increase throughput—but coordination is essential.

---

## 🔥 Why This Strategy Is a Game-Changer

- **Dramatically Increases Valor Output**: Beyond standard farming, you unlock Valor scaling by moving into farm alliances.
- **War-Readiness Multiplier**: Consistent access to healing boosts ensures you're battle-ready at all times.
- **Access for All**: Even small alliances lacking big PvP presence can farm high-value rewards.
- **Alternative to Main Alliance Limits**: Avoid diminishing returns by farming strategically.

### TL;DR

- Boost Valor supply well beyond typical limits.
- Ensure constant healing speed reserves for war.
- Empowers small or casual alliances to remain competitive.
- Works cycle after cycle for long-term gains.

---

## ✅ Final Thoughts

The farm alliance swarm is a revolutionary CoR tactic that supercharges your Valor earnings by exploiting reward tiers. With proper coordination, even a small team can generate **half a million Valor per cycle**, far exceeding what standard CoR farming offers.

Whether you use alts, real members, or a mix, this method ensures you're not just participating in CoR—but **dominating** it. Use your more consistent Valor to gear up, speed-up, and outlast your kingdom rivals.

---

title: How to Farm Federation Reputation in Legion of Frostborne
summary: Federation Reputation is one of the numbers that ultimately determines the outcome of Legion of Frostborne, commonly referred to as KvK. Most federations build their score by capturing and holding cities, particularly…
categoryPath: Things you must know about Legion of Frostborne
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-46-1024x571.png)

Federation Reputation is one of the numbers that ultimately determines the outcome of Legion of Frostborne, commonly referred to as KvK. Most federations build their score by capturing and holding cities, particularly the valuable cities found deeper within the battlefield. However, there is another repeatable source of reputation that many alliances overlook: attacking the walls of uncaptured gates without finishing them.

Gate farming does not replace territorial control, but it can add millions of reputation over the course of a KvK. In a close bracket, that additional score may genuinely affect the final result. Even when your federation is not competing for victory, the method can help your alliance reach the **12,000,000 Alliance Reputation milestone** and secure **10,000 Cold Silver for each eligible participating member**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-47-1024x535.png)

## How Reputation From Gate Sieges Works

Technically, attacking a gate does not award Federation Reputation directly. The reputation passes through several layers of the KvK scoring system:

### Gate wall damage → Personal Legion’s Marks → Alliance Reputation → Federation Reputation

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-49-1024x617.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-50-1024x586.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-51-1024x499.png)

Dismantling city and checkpoint wall durability awards Personal Legion’s Marks to the players involved. Those marks are automatically converted into Alliance Reputation, which then contributes to the federation’s combined score.

This is important because gate farming advances several objectives at once. Participating players increase their Personal Legion’s Marks, their alliance moves closer to its progression rewards and the federation gains additional reputation in the overall ranking.

## How to Farm an Uncaptured Gate

The method relies on damaging a gate without completely destroying its walls. If the gate remains uncaptured, its durability can recover and the objective can be attacked again after its Protection Barrier expires.

The basic process is:

1. Select an eligible uncaptured gate.
2. Begin an attack and send siege marches against its walls.
3. Stop all attacks before the wall durability reaches close to zero.
4. Allow the walls to recover during the Protection Barrier.
5. Attack the gate again once the approximately 30-minute barrier expires.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-52-1024x617.png)

The most important part is stopping early enough. If the wall reaches zero durability and the gate is captured, you lose it as a repeatable farming target.

In our example, the alliance used a clear instruction to **stop at 100 million durability**. This left enough room to account for marches already travelling toward the gate, simultaneous attacks and delayed recalls.

Waiting until only a few million durability remains is unnecessarily risky. When dozens of marches are involved, several attacks can land at nearly the same time and accidentally finish the gate. Alliance leadership should choose a stopping point before the siege begins and communicate it clearly throughout the attack.

## How Much Reputation Does One Gate Provide?

During our test against a **level 17 Nammu Mine gate**, the federation ranking increased from **88,746,352 to 88,922,513**. That represents an increase of **176,161 Federation Reputation**, slightly below 200,000.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-53.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-54-1024x586.png)

This should be treated as an observed result rather than a fixed reward for every gate. The final amount may depend on the gate’s wall durability, how much damage is inflicted and whether other reputation-generating activity is taking place at the same time.

Nevertheless, the example shows how quickly repeated gate sieges can add up. Even if one cycle produces approximately 175,000 reputation, seven successful cycles provide more than 1.2 million. Spread that activity across several gates and the federation can generate a meaningful amount of additional reputation every day.

## Farming Several Gates at Once

The strongest version of this strategy is not placing the entire federation on one gate. Instead, alliances can spread their available players across several eligible gates and run multiple farming cycles simultaneously.

Each alliance or assigned group can manage its own gate, with someone responsible for announcing when the Protection Barrier expires and when players must stop attacking. A basic organization might include:

- One gate assigned to each participating alliance or player group.
- A shared timer for the 30-minute Protection Barrier.
- A predetermined durability limit for stopping the siege.
- Clear retreat instructions before the gate approaches that limit.
- Siege-focused marches to deal wall damage efficiently.

This allows the federation to continue generating reputation even during quieter periods of KvK. It also gives smaller alliances a useful task when they cannot meaningfully participate in battles for the most important cities.

## Why the 12 Million Alliance Milestone Matters

Gate farming is especially valuable for alliances that are not winning the overall KvK. Federation victory may already be out of reach, but Alliance Reputation rewards can still provide a substantial amount of Cold Silver.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-55-1024x535.png)

These are progression rewards based on the highest Alliance Reputation reached during the season. Alliance members must have entered the Legion of Frostborne battlefield during the current season to qualify for distribution.

Reaching **12,000,000 Alliance Reputation** therefore gives each eligible member 10,000 Cold Silver. For an alliance otherwise struggling to earn meaningful end-of-season rewards, organized gate farming can be the difference between missing that milestone and receiving the full payout.

## Gate Farming Does Not Replace City Control

Repeated gate sieges are useful, but they should remain a secondary strategy. Capturing cities grants first-occupation points, while holding them produces continuous occupation points for the controlling alliance. High-level cities can build a major reputation advantage throughout the season and remain central to winning Legion of Frostborne.

Do not preserve a gate for farming if capturing it is necessary for expansion, blocking an opponent or securing access to important cities. The method should be used on gates that your federation can safely leave uncaptured without compromising its position.

The best approach is to combine both sources. Your main forces should fight for strategically valuable territory, while spare players and marches farm suitable gates whenever the battlefield allows it.

## Concluding remarks

Gate farming is a simple but powerful way to generate additional Federation Reputation. Attack the walls of an eligible uncaptured gate, stop before its durability reaches zero and repeat the siege once the Protection Barrier expires. Used across several gates, this can help decide a close KvK or push an alliance toward the important **12 million reputation milestone and its 10,000 Cold Silver reward**.

However, the value does not stop with the federation. Damaging gate walls first awards **Personal Legion’s Marks**, which are then converted into Alliance Reputation and added to the federation total. This means gate farming is also one of the strongest strategies for progressing your personal KvK rewards.

There is much more to consider when farming Personal Legion’s Marks efficiently, but that deserves a guide of its own. Stay tuned!

markdown:
### Infinity Kingdom 3rd Anniversary Event Guide: Mastering Sweetness Guardian

Hey, fellow lords and ladies of Infinity Kingdom! The 3rd Anniversary Event is here, bringing with it a whirlwind of excitement and the chance to bag heaps of rewards. Today, we're diving deep into the "Sweetness Guardian" tab, your golden ticket to farming Stardust and event Dice, essential for maximizing your gains during this festive period. So, grab your gear, rally your Immortals, and let's conquer this event like the legends we are!

#### Understanding the Event Mechanics

First off, "Sweetness Guardian" is all about completing missions to earn points. These points are your currency to unlock those sweet, sweet rewards. There are two types of missions:

- **Timed Missions:** Send your Immortals on a long journey, and they'll return with event points. This is highly inefficient and should only be done while you are taking a break from IK. As you see below, I am not stuck and cannot farm anything. Have to wait for the missions to complete.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-96-1024x555.png)

- **Find Traces Missions:** Here's where the fun begins. These missions involve hunting down snowman bosses, and trust me, they're the key to farming effectively.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-99-1024x460.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-100-1024x400.png)

## Strategic Farming for Stardust and Dice

Here's where strategy plays a crucial role. To maximize your rewards, follow this expertly crafted approach:

- **Timing is Everything:** Only dispatch your Immortals on timed missions when you're about to log off. Why? Because while you're actively playing, you don't want to clog your mission slots with long-wait missions.
- **Focus on Find Traces Missions:** While playing, prioritize completing all "find traces" missions. These are your golden goose, leading you to snowman bosses which can be quickly defeated and refreshed.
- **The Refresh Strategy:** After clearing the traces missions, hit that refresh button without starting any new timed missions. This increases the chances of more traces missions popping up, leading you to more snowman bosses to farm.
- **Rinse and Repeat:** Complete all traces missions, refresh, and continue this cycle. This method ensures you're farming snowman bosses efficiently, propelling you towards maxing out your event rewards.

#### Why This Strategy?

You might wonder, why all this fuss about avoiding timed missions? Here's the deal: to complete the entire event and unlock the full spectrum of rewards (we're talking about a whopping 1500 points), timed missions just don't cut it. They're slow, and their point yield isn't enough to reach the event's summit. Snowman bosses, on the other hand, are your express ticket to success, offering quick and repeatable missions that can be farmed for a consistent point influx.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-101-1024x236.png)

#### Rewards Unlocked

By mastering this strategy, you're looking at bagging 100 Stardust and 50 event Dice. And guess what? These Dice pair wonderfully with those you'll collect in the Fireworks Party, setting you up for some major reward hauls!

**Happy farming, and here's to a bountiful 3rd Anniversary Event!**

title: Legion of Frostborn Federation Reputation
summary: Federation Reputation is one of the central progression systems in the modern Legion of Frostborne battlefield. Since the Federation system replaced the older Alliance structure, coordination between alliances now…
categoryPath: Things you must know about Legion of Frostborne
markdown:
## Introduction

Federation Reputation is one of the central progression systems in the modern Legion of Frostborne battlefield. Since the Federation system replaced the older Alliance structure, coordination between alliances now matters far more than individual alliance performance alone.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-56-1024x588.png)

A Federation can contain up to five alliances from the same faction, and all participating alliances contribute toward shared battlefield progress. In practice, Federation Reputation acts as the combined measure of your coalition’s activity, battlefield control, and long-term expedition performance. Legion of Frostborne rewards organization more than raw power once the expedition enters the mid and late stages.

---

## What Is a Federation?

According to the in-game rules:

- A Federation can include up to 4 alliances.
- Only alliances from the same faction may join.
- The alliance leader who creates the Federation becomes the Federation Leader.
- The Federation Leader can invite alliances, approve applications, and disband the Federation.
- Alliances that leave a Federation must wait 8 hours before joining another one.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-57-1024x546.png)

The system effectively creates a battlefield coalition. Instead of alliances operating independently, Federations share strategic goals and contribute toward faction-wide progress.

One important detail many newer players miss is that Federation structure affects both coordination and rewards. Poorly organized Federations often lose efficiency because reputation generation becomes fragmented across disconnected objectives. Managing high Alliance Reputation and Legion Marks throughout all members of your Federation is to the benefit of all!

---

## How Federation Reputation Works

Federation Reputation is tied directly to overall battlefield contribution during the expedition.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-60-1024x356.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-62-1024x579.png)

The game evaluates performance through several connected systems:

- Personal Legion’s Marks
- Alliance Reputation
- Federation Reputation

These layers build upward from individual activity into alliance performance, then finally into Federation-wide progression.

---

## Personal Legion’s Marks

Players earn Legion’s Marks through battlefield activity, including:

- Earning Honor
- Gathering resources
- Defeating Gnomes and Gnome Bosses
- Building Thermal Towers
- Destroying enemy Thermal Towers
- Reducing enemy Territory Prosperity
- Expelling enemy territories
- Attacking cities and checkpoints
- Donating resources for repairs

In actual gameplay, active participation matters more than pure troop power. A mid-powered player constantly building towers, gathering, reinforcing, and contributing to objectives often generates more useful marks than a high-powered inactive player.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-58.png)

During several Frostborne seasons, I noticed that Federations with disciplined activity schedules climbed reputation rankings much faster than alliances relying only on whales fighting frontline battles.

---

## Alliance Reputation

Alliance Reputation is built from the collective Legion’s Marks generated by alliance members.

The game tracks:

1. Total Legion’s Marks earned by alliance members
2. Additional battlefield contribution metrics tied to expedition objectives

This creates a cumulative progression system where alliance-wide participation becomes extremely important.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-59-1024x579.png)

An alliance with 70 consistently active players will usually outperform a stronger but less organized alliance with low participation rates.

Frostborne was designed to reward sustained activity and strategic coordination over isolated combat wins.

---

## Victory Conditions and Expedition End

The expedition lasts a maximum of 32 days.

However, Humanity can achieve an early victory if an alliance occupies the Gnome King Capital for more than 24 hours.

Once the expedition ends:

- Players withdraw from the Frozen Realm
- Rewards are distributed
- Federation and Alliance Reputation determine progression payouts

Importantly, players must have entered the battlefield during the season to receive rewards.

---

## Player Perspective

From several Frostborne seasons, one pattern becomes obvious: activity density matters more than raw alliance power.

The strongest Federations are rarely the ones with the biggest individual spenders alone. They are usually the groups with:

- Consistent participation
- Reliable leadership
- Coordinated objective timing
- Clear battlefield structure

For instance, when our Federation split tower responsibilities between alliances instead of letting everyone expand randomly, overall progression speed improved noticeably. We wasted less stamina, secured cities earlier, and hit higher reputation thresholds well before the final week.

The Federation system rewards organization at every level.

---

## Conclusion Summary

Federation Reputation is the core progression system behind Legion of Frostborne coalition play. It reflects the combined battlefield contribution of all alliances within a Federation and directly determines rankings and seasonal rewards.

The system heavily rewards:

- Active participation
- Strategic expansion
- Alliance coordination
- Long-term battlefield efficiency

Players who understand how Personal Marks scale into Alliance and Federation Reputation generally perform much better across an entire Frostborne season than players focused only on combat power or kill counts.

---
