title: Harvest Festival 2026
summary: The Harvest Festival 2026 follows Infinity Kingdom's familiar seasonal-event format, with several returning activities alongside a few important changes to the rewards and progression.
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-40-1024x571.png)

## Introduction

The **Harvest Festival 2026** follows Infinity Kingdom's familiar seasonal-event format, with several returning activities alongside a few important changes to the rewards and progression.

If you played through the previous seasonal festivals, most of the event will feel familiar. **Lucky Koi, Summer Passion, Fishing Contest, Dazzling Wish, Grail Shop, Pinnacle Trial, and Glorious Challenge** all return, while **Fruit Frenzy** introduces a 2048-style minigame to the rotation.

The interesting part of Harvest Festival is not simply that these activities are back. It is how the rewards have changed.

Fishing Contest continues the progression of **Alexander the Great – Summer Passion**, while Dazzling Wish once again focuses on **Athena – Summer Passion**. Fruit Frenzy provides another source of Magic Fishing Nets and introduces its own seasonal insignia.

The biggest change, however, concerns **Eternal Grails**.

The large Grail jackpot previously found in Dazzling Wish has been removed, but it has effectively been replaced by a dedicated **Grail Wheel**. In practice, this is a very good change: considerably more Grails can now be obtained than through the old jackpot system. At the same time, the Grail Shop has received one of its most interesting updates yet, including much cheaper access to **Apollo and Medusa**, as well as their artifact progression.

Rather than listing every reward available during the festival, this guide focuses on what each event tab is for, what has changed, and where I think players should concentrate their effort.

---

## Lucky Koi

**Lucky Koi** returns in essentially the same format as previous seasonal events.

Purchasing the Koi Gift Pack provides entry into the Lucky Koi lottery alongside the resources contained in the pack. Players who participate repeatedly without winning also progress toward the guaranteed consolation reward, so there is at least some protection against walking away empty-handed after several unsuccessful draws. Note that this 5-purchase bonus reward alone is the highest efficiency Grail Item available in the game. So make sure you get it!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-43-1024x527.png)

There is also a free daily gift attached to Lucky Koi. Even if you have no intention of purchasing the paid pack, remember to open the tab and collect it each day.

---

## Summer Passion

**Summer Passion** is the main progression battlepass for Harvest Festival and acts as one of the links between the different event activities.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-44-1024x562.png)

Progressing the pass supplies resources used elsewhere during Harvest, including **Tokens of Light** for Dazzling Wish and **Magic Fishing Nets** for Fishing Contest.

It also continues the seasonal progression surrounding **Alexander the Great – Summer Passion**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-45.png)

Alexander's outfit requires 60 fragments for the initial craft, with additional fragments used afterward to increase its Glamour Level. Players who started the outfit during the previous festival can therefore continue developing it during Harvest rather than starting an entirely separate outfit progression.

Summer Passion is also connected to the **Judgment Realm** castle skin.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-46.png)

Judgment Realm provides permanent account bonuses and is significant enough that its fragment requirements and progression deserve a separate article rather than a small subsection here.

### → See our Judgment Realm Castle Skin Guide

The practical point with Summer Passion is simply to keep progressing it before making decisions elsewhere. Nets and Tokens obtained here reduce what you may need to acquire through other means later in the festival.

---

## Fishing Contest

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-47-1024x566.png)

**Fishing Contest** is once again particularly important for Alexander players.

The event uses **Magic Fishing Nets**, with Fishing Contest progression providing **Alexander the Great – Summer Passion Outfit Fragments** at its major catch milestones.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-50.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-49-1024x556.png)

There is also a **unique Harvest Festival insignia** available through Fishing Contest, giving collectors a separate reason to pay attention to the event.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-48-1024x369.png)

Fishing Contest has enough going on that it makes more sense as a standalone guide. Catch progression, milestone planning and the various ways of acquiring Nets all influence how far it is actually worth pushing. To complete the 15 level each day you need around 57K nets each (two players).

**→ See our Fishing Contest Guide for the complete progression and cost-efficiency breakdown.**

Harvest Festival offer Nets through several other activities. Fruit Frenzy, Summer Passion and the combat events all contribute toward your total. There is little reason to buy your way toward an Alexander milestone on the first day when free Nets earned later in the festival might have completed the same threshold.

---

## Fruit Frenzy

**Fruit Frenzy** is the new minigame in Harvest Festival, although the underlying game will be immediately recognizable to a lot of players. It is basically **2048 with fruit**. You combine matching fruits to create progressively higher-level fruits, while trying to keep enough usable space on the board to continue merging. If you already know how to play 2048, there is very little new to learn mechanically. If you do not, this video provides a useful explanation of the underlying strategy: [Watch this 2048 strategy guide on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kQhkkqjGkFA&utm_)

The most important habit is to keep your largest fruit toward one corner and build the board around it. Randomly chasing every available merge tends to scatter your high-level pieces, and once that happens it becomes increasingly difficult to combine them before the board fills.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-51-1024x532.png)

Prioritize **board structure over short-term merges**. Sometimes declining an attractive-looking movement pattern is better than disrupting the corner you have spent the entire game building.

Fruit Frenzy is also worth doing even if you are not particularly interested in the minigame itself. The event provides **Magic Fishing Nets**, which means Fruit Frenzy progression feeds directly into Fishing Contest and Alexander's outfit progression. There is also a **unique Harvest Festival insignia** to obtain here.

For Alexander players, that makes Fruit Frenzy effectively part of Fishing Contest progression. Every useful batch of Nets obtained here is one less batch you potentially need to purchase elsewhere.

---

## Dazzling Wish

**Dazzling Wish** returns as the main event associated with **Athena – Summer Passion**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-52-1024x538.png)

Tokens of Light collected throughout Harvest Festival can be spent here, with Athena outfit fragments forming the major long-term target.

The core event is therefore familiar, but there is one important change compared with previous seasonal versions.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-53-1024x499.png)

The big **Eternal Grail jackpot is gone from Dazzling Wish**.

Initially, I expected this to be a fairly substantial reduction in the value of the event. Eternal Grails have become increasingly useful, particularly as the Grail Shop continues to improve, so removing a large Grail payout would normally hurt.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-54-1024x573.png)

Fortunately, that is not really what happened. Instead of keeping Grail acquisition tied to a lucky Dazzling Wish result, Harvest Festival introduces a separate **Grail Wheel**. And the new system is considerably better.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-55-1024x508.png)

The dedicated Grail Wheel provides a much stronger opportunity to accumulate Eternal Grails, to the point that players can obtain **even more Grails than were available through previous versions of the festival**. I think this is an excellent change to the event structure. Dazzling Wish now has a clearer identity: **you are primarily here for Athena**. Eternal Grail progression has its own system instead of being dependent on hitting the right Dazzling Wish reward.

---

## Grail Shop

The **Grail Shop is arguably the biggest winner of Harvest Festival 2026**.

There are still plenty of familiar resources and progression materials available, but those are not what makes the current version noteworthy. The big change is access to **Apollo and Medusa**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-56-1024x528.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-57-1024x568.png)

Both are now available through extremely attractive Eternal Grail options compared with the investment historically required to develop these Immortals. For players who have wanted to build either Immortal but could never justify the previous cost, this is a significant change.

Apollo and Medusa have traditionally sat in a category where deciding to build them represented a serious investment. Harvest's Grail Shop substantially lowers that barrier quite significantly, enabling slow-build strategies by low- to mid-spenders.

The choice between Apollo and Medusa will depend on your account and where you are in progression. Apollo remains extremely strong during Conquest, while Medusa becomes a much more interesting long-term proposition once **Legendary Tower of Knowledge skills** enter the picture. **[Read more here.](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/new-player-guides/season-progression-everything-you-need-to-know-before-a-new-season/which-chaos-immortal-carry-to-get-going-from-conquest-into-legendary/)**

I would therefore make sure to buy fragment chests simply because they are cheap. Decide which Immortal actually fits your account later, and use the seasonal discount to accelerate a build you genuinely intend to finish.

The other important part of the Grail Shop update is **artifact progression**. Cheap Immortal fragments are only half the equation if the corresponding artifact remains prohibitively difficult to develop. Having artifact options alongside the Immortals makes the current shop much more useful because players can work toward a complete build rather than merely unlocking another Immortal.

For developed accounts, I would pay particularly close attention here. If you already have the Immortal progression you need, artifact fragments may provide considerably more practical combat value than adding another unfinished Immortal to the roster.

---

## Pinnacle Trial

**Pinnacle Trial** returns as one of Harvest Festival's combat activities. The basic format has not changed enough to require another lengthy explanation. Work through the available stages, collect the festival progression attached to them, and participate in the ranking component if your account is strong enough to compete for it.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-58-1024x551.png)

What matters for the wider Harvest Festival is that Pinnacle Trial contributes resources that feed into the other event systems.

---

## Glorious Challenge

**Glorious Challenge** fills a similar role. Progress through the stages, collect the available festival resources, and move into the harder content as it becomes available and your account allows.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-59-1024x557.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-60-1024x336.png)

Again, I would not overcomplicate this section. Glorious Challenge is familiar content, and the strategic decision is less about how the activity itself works and more about remembering to finish it before calculating how many Nets, Harvest Coins you require each day for the daily stock in the Challenge Shop.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-61-1024x484.png)

Free progression should always be exhausted before paid progression.

---

## Conclusion Summary

Harvest Festival 2026 keeps the familiar seasonal format, but several reward changes make this version particularly worthwhile. Fishing Contest remains the main route for **Alexander – Summer Passion**, Fruit Frenzy provides additional Fishing Nets and a seasonal insignia, while Dazzling Wish once again focuses on **Athena – Summer Passion**.

The biggest improvement is the combination of the new **Grail Wheel and updated Grail Shop**. More Eternal Grails are available, and they are considerably more valuable now that the shop offers cheap access to **Apollo and Medusa**, alongside useful artifact progression. Clear Pinnacle Trial and Glorious Challenge, collect all the free resources first, and only afterward decide which Alexander, Athena or Grail Shop milestones are worth pursuing.

---

title: Harvest Song
summary: Infinity Kingdom has a ton of cool city skins. You get skins from purchases during events, performance from in game activities such as contention of relics and/or Legion of Frostborne, Throne of the Supreeme, and so on.
markdown:
Infinity Kingdom has a ton of cool city skins. You get skins from purchases during events, performance from in game activities such as contention of relics and/or Legion of Frostborne, Throne of the Supreeme, and so on.

**Castle Skins serve two purposes:**(**1)** they provide **unique buff effects**to specific activities such as e.g. tech speed, dragon speed, combat buffs, recovery speed, resource collection rate, etc. and **(2)** they provide **unique cosmetic effects** that change the way your castle looks inside the game. The cosmetic effects work in all aspects of the game, any game mode, and provides some awesome customization to make youself more unique and your castle look.. well.. more awesome!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-96.png)

In this article we shall look to one of my personal favorite cosmetic skins in all of **Infinity Kingdom: Harvest Song**

## What does Harvest Song do?

Every castle skin has unique beneficial effects, from building speed to rss gathering and troop HP. The Harvest Song provides you a 3% increase to your Resource Gathering Speed. What this means is often misunderstood by some players, and understandable so. There are many different ways to obtain resources in Infinity Kingdom and some of them blend togeather. What this skin does is it increases the rate at which your troops harvest resources at resource nodes. As such it provides NO buff to the rate at which your farms inside your castle produce resources, instead it allows you to be faster at collecting resources around the map of Norheim and Frostborne.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-97.png)

For example a level 10 node in Legion of Frostborne provides a gathering/harvest speed of 1M/hour. Without this skin active, you will harvest at a base speed of 1M/hour (not counting other tech, see below).

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-98.png)

With this skin on, your collection rate increases by 30,000 resources per hour. What this means is, that per default it will take you 9 hours to collect all the resources in this node, but with the skin active you reduce that time to 8.7 hours.

The actual collection rate is a lot faster than the above, because you are getting strong modifiers to resource collection via Personal Technology as well as Alliance Technology. For instance, Stone gatherer provides a total of 20% increased collection rate to all Alliance members once max level.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-99.png)

Moreover Quick Mine provides you another 30% increased collection rate at max level (personal technology).

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-100.png)

All in all, not a very powerful effect and certainly not an effect that I will recommend you to go after as one of the "best"... You should only get this skin if you think that the skin cosmetic effects are just too cool to pass on - which, I kinda get if you do! It is a very cute look.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-96.png)

## How to get it?

There is only one way to obtain this skin**: (1) Harvest Festival and (2) Golden Path seasonal shop**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-101-1024x576.png)

This skin was first released with the very first version of the Harvest Festival which occur every **August**in Infinity Kingdom. During this seasonal event, players have been able to complete quests and earn the Harvest Song Casle Skin. You should beware that these seasonal events tends to change every year, and as such I cannot give any guarantees as to how or if you will be able to collect this skin from the seasonal even when May comes around again.

However, lucky for you guys there is a place where you can be sure to collect this skin - in the Golden Path seasonal shop!

## Golden Path

The Harvest Song Castle Skin can be found in the first and second rotation of the Golden Path shop.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-94.png)

This skin is available in the golden path rotation! **[Check out my article here to read more about the Castle skins offered via Golden Path as well as the full rotation](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/development/market/golden-path/)**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/image-102.png)

Published: 23-03-23

title: Healing and Training Troops
summary: Introduction: Greetings, commanders! Are you tired of burning through speedups while healing and training troops? Fear not, for this guide is tailored for alliances dedicated to efficient troop recovery and training…
markdown:
### Guide to Troop Training and Healing Optimization in Infinity Kingdom

**Introduction:**
Greetings, commanders! Are you tired of burning through speedups while healing and training troops? Fear not, for this guide is tailored for alliances dedicated to efficient troop recovery and training strategies. Brace yourselves for a journey that will save you countless speedups in the long run.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-135-1024x553.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-137-1024x547.png)

**Overview:**
Scattered across Norheim are cities that offer Seriously Wounded Healing Speed and Troop Training Speed buffs to controlling alliances. This presents a golden opportunity for players to conserve speedups during troop recovery. One alliance manages healing cities, while another oversees training cities. The current King can also assign positions granting a 10% increase in healing and training speed, complementing the mayor buffs that offer 3%.

**Healing Cities:**
Nine cities, including Managarmr and Anahita, provide a combined 63% Seriously Wounded Healing Speed. Various castle decorations, skins, and technologies enhance healing speed, with Quick Relief II research offering a 10% speedup. Military Commanders contribute an additional 20-25%, although some percentages are not additive.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-138.png)

**Training Cities:**
Ten cities, including Egeria and Gaviel, contribute a total of 50% Troop Training Speed. Few castle decorations offer training speed buffs, and exclusive skins like Frozen Fortress and Phantom Glory provide additional benefits. Mayor buffs and technology nodes further increase training speed by 30%, with Military Commanders adding 20-25%. Similar to healing, some percentages are not additive.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-139.png)

**Calculations:**
Assuming maxed healing and training technology nodes, and excluding castle skins and mayor buffs, training 9,750 troops can be reduced from 14 hours and 40 minutes to about 11 hours, saving over three hours of speedups. Healing 77,000 troops can be shortened from 24 hours to approximately 15 hours. Recovering a full training ground of 850,000 troops results in savings of about 260 hours of speedups.

**Summary:**
Nineteen cities distribute increased Seriously Wounded Healing Speed or Troop Training Speed. With alliances capable of holding up to 15 territories, strategic planning can maximize speedup savings. One alliance controlling all cities of one type and some of the other, or two alliances managing one type each, are viable approaches. The latter, though slightly more tedious, offers greater savings. Removing your character from alliances after completion accelerates the process. While not suitable during battle, this method significantly conserves speedups, allowing you to outlast opponents in events like Legion of Frostborne. Save on speedups here to invest in other critical events, such as Illusion Battlefield, where this tactic is not applicable. Optimize your troop management and dominate the realms of Infinity Kingdom!

title: Heart of Arcana (aura)
summary: Heart of Arcana is one of the strongest offensive aura skills added to Infinity Kingdom in recent patches, and it has already reshaped how mage-centric teams are built at high level play. The skill is straightforward on…
markdown:
## Introduction

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-113-1024x589.png)

Heart of Arcana is one of the strongest offensive aura skills added to *Infinity Kingdom* in recent patches, and it has already reshaped how mage-centric teams are built at high level play. The skill is straightforward on paper, but its impact in actual combat is enormous because it amplifies the exact damage type most burst compositions rely on.

The official description reads:

> “After the battle starts, increases magical damage of all allied units by 35%.”

A flat 35% magical damage increase across the entire team is an exceptionally large modifier in Infinity Kingdom’s combat system. For any composition relying on a primary mage carry, Heart of Arcana is effectively mandatory. The tradeoff is that it occupies the highly contested aura slot, forcing players to make real decisions about sustain, mitigation, or offensive scaling.

---

## Skill Breakdown

### What Heart of Arcana Actually Does

Heart of Arcana increases all magical damage dealt by allied units by 35% immediately after battle begins. The effect is active for the entire fight and applies teamwide.

Because the buff is multiplicative with many existing scaling sources, the actual battlefield impact often feels larger than “just” 35% as not only your ultimate skills but also all tower of knowledge skills are affected.

In practical terms, fights that would previously end with enemy frontline surviving on low HP often become clean kills once Arcana is equipped.

---

## Why the Aura Slot Matters

The balancing factor is simple: Heart of Arcana is an aura.

Every immortal can only equip one aura skill, and aura slots are already among the most valuable skill slots in the game. Choosing Arcana means giving up other powerful utility or sustain options.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-114.png)

As the skill pool expands, builds become less about “best skill overall” and more about opportunity cost.

---

## Best Use Cases

### Mage-Carry Compositions

Heart of Arcana is strongest when your team is built around one primary magical damage dealer carrying the fight.

These setups benefit the most because the 35% amplification concentrates into a single highly optimized damage source.

Typical examples include:

#### Water Merlin Carry

Merlin remains one of the clearest examples.

In solo-carry water formations, Merlin often contributes the overwhelming majority of total team damage. Arcana directly multiplies the value of every cast, especially in burst windows after crowd control chains.

From actual testing, the difference becomes very noticeable in PvP against sustain-heavy teams. Without Arcana, enemy backlines sometimes stabilize after the first rotation. With Arcana active, Merlin frequently secures kills before recovery skills can cycle.

---

#### Fire Wu Carry

Empress Wu fire setups also benefit heavily.

Wu scales extremely well with raw magical amplification because her burst profile already pressures both frontline and backline simultaneously. Arcana pushes those thresholds much higher.

In aggressive fire teams, the skill often changes matchups from attrition fights into fast snowball victories.

---

#### Earth Himiko Tank Core

Himiko compositions with double frontline tanks are another strong Arcana environment.

When running durable frontliners whose purpose is simply to buy time for Himiko damage scaling, maximizing magical output becomes the optimal approach. Arcana fits naturally because the team structure already commits heavily into magical carry value.

This is especially effective in prolonged fights where Himiko repeatedly cycles abilities while protected by layered mitigation.

---

## The Defensive Counter: Aegis

The release of Heart of Arcana also increased the value of anti-magic defensive setups.

Aegis has become one of the most important responses to mage-heavy metas because magical burst damage is now reaching extremely high levels.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-115.png)

Aegis does not completely neutralize Arcana, but it significantly reduces the pressure created by mage-carry teams.

That interaction is important strategically:

- Mage teams want Arcana active whenever possible
- Anti-mage teams increasingly prioritize Aegis
- Team building becomes a direct offensive-versus-defensive skill trade

This is one of the healthier evolutions in the current meta because offensive scaling finally has meaningful counterplay rather than simply stacking damage unchecked.

---

## Situations Where Arcana Is Not Optimal

Despite how strong the skill is, there are still compositions where Heart of Arcana is difficult to justify.

### Mixed Damage Teams

If your team splits damage between physical and magical sources, Arcana loses efficiency.

You are effectively dedicating an entire aura slot to only part of your total output, which can become inefficient compared to utility or mitigation auras.

Some formations simply cannot afford to give up survivability.

A good example is Earth with Himiko and Alexander. In these builds, Spring of Life often occupies the only realistic aura slot because sustain provides more total combat value than additional magical scaling.

I have seen many players try forcing Arcana into defensive earth variants only to discover the team collapses before the extra damage matters. In practice, surviving long enough for Himiko to cycle repeatedly is usually the higher priority.

---

## Conclusion Summary

Heart of Arcana is currently one of the premier offensive aura skills in *Infinity Kingdom* and a defining tool for mage-carry compositions.

Key takeaways:

- Grants a massive 35% magical damage increase to all allies
- Best-in-slot for dedicated mage-carry setups
- Exceptional with Merlin, Wu, and Himiko-focused teams
- Strongly influences current PvP meta dynamics
- Countered partially by Aegis and defensive anti-magic setups
- Not always optimal in sustain-heavy or mixed-damage formations due to aura slot competition

For players building around magical burst damage, Heart of Arcana is very close to mandatory. The value is simply too high to ignore when your entire win condition depends on mage output.

---

title: Heavenly Thunder (for Physical Imortals!)
summary: Did you know that Heavenly Thunder (magic) performs INSANELY well on ALEXANDER and other physical Immortals?
markdown:
Did you know that Heavenly Thunder (magic) performs INSANELY well on ALEXANDER and other physical Immortals?

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/image-38-1024x349.png)

## Using Heavenly Thunder Passive on Physical Immortals for SURPRISING damage!

Heavenly Thunder is a Tower of Knowledge Passive that has been overlooked ever since we began playing Infinity Kingdom back almost two years ago – it’s description offers magical damage procs on Normal Attack hits, which just has never really proved viable to use. Since the mages of Norheim have pretty low attack speed and dosen’t really benefit from boosting set attack speed, most players like myself has left Heavenly Thunder rightfully where it belongs – on the bench – while we took full advantage of the many strong magic damage passives that the Tower of Knowledge has to offer.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/image-24-1024x622.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/image-25-1024x553.png)

But did you that on Alexander or Barca in an attack-speed based build, Heavenly Thunder despite having no physical damage actually deals a surprisingly high amount of damage! Moreover, and maybe even more importantly, it deals damage to random enemies offering us a rare opportunity to have our Alexander frontline deal solid damage to the enemy backline!

## How does Heavenly Thunder work?

When your Immortal lands a normal attack Heavenly Thunder has a 30% deals 150% magical damage to 2 random enemies.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/image-37.png)

This means, that the more attack speed we get, the more procs we are also getting on Heavenly Thunder – same as with Cleave and Combo. What is different is the fact that this on the face of it, really shouldn’t be any significant damage since Heavenly Thunder deals magical damage and we are trying to use it in a physical damage Immortal? Well, we were wrong!

## How does it perform in combat?

I have been running Heavenly Thunder on my Alexander and my Hannibal Barca lately to test out what kind of damage we are getting on this thing. I must admit, it is quite a bit more than I expected! We are getting near the same damage as many of the best physical damage passives and on rare occasions I see Heavenly Thunder doing MORE damage than Death Breath (a notoriously strong passive).

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/image-33-1024x615.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/image-34-1024x618.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/image-35-1024x616.png)

While it is true that it CAN even perform better than some of the best physical damage passives, I will not go as far as to say it is indeed better. Usually I see results of between 10-20% of total damage dealt, which is very very solid. Though I do see both combo and cleave provide significantly more, the fact that we are damaging backline Immortals adds further value to this passive!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/image-27-1024x617.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/image-28-1024x622.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/image-29-1024x615.png)

Does Heavenly Thunder work on any physical Immortal? No. You need to have a very high attack-speed for this passive to work well, meaning it can be run with success on Alexander the Great and on Hannibal Barca (in the right build). In addition, you can run it on Julius Caesar if you are doing the meme-build where you run him as a mage (since he has abnormally high magical attack attributes). But I do not recommend you using this Passive unless you are running either Alexander or Hannibal Barca (and even on Barca you want it to be in an attack-speed centric build like earth-wind hybrid with the attack-speed boost from Qin and Zeno with unique artifact).

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/image-36-1024x618.png)

But if you are running Alexander especially in an AOE-build with either Genghis Khan or Elizabeth Bathory in the backline, then the value of the damage dealt is a lot higher than e.g. combo, since we turn our Alex into additional pressure on the enemy’s backline. Between an Alex with Heavenly Thunder and a Genghis Khan or Elizabeth with Anger and Death Breath, you can really melt backline Immortals at a very rapid pace.

## Conclusion

The overall verdict from me is that this is a passive that anyone running Earth as a main has to look into! For me personally, I see huge potential in this Passive for my future march composition, especially because I will be running Alexander in either a wind-hybrid attack speed build (scaling well with Heavenly Thunder) or in an Earth-Khan lineup!

title: Heavy Lifter (written in 2.9.8)
summary: Heavy Lifter is one of those skills that spent years sitting on the sidelines. It was never a bad skill on paper, but there simply wasn't a realistic opportunity to use it because every competitive mage build demanded…
markdown:
## Introduction

Heavy Lifter is one of those skills that spent years sitting on the sidelines. It was never a bad skill on paper, but there simply wasn't a realistic opportunity to use it because every competitive mage build demanded the same premium setup. Corrosive Power, Energy Mastery and Fighting Master occupied the available skill slots, leaving Heavy Lifter as the odd one out regardless of how much damage it could potentially produce.

What's interesting is that Heavy Lifter hasn't changed at all. The skill works exactly as it always has, yet it has quietly become much more attractive because the meta surrounding it has shifted. As fewer players rely on hyper-regeneration mage mains and more primary marches are built around physical carries, those premium energy skills are no longer permanently tied to a single team. That opens the door for secondary and third marches to use combinations that simply weren't practical before, and Heavy Lifter is one of the biggest beneficiaries of that change.

I've been running exactly that kind of setup myself. After replacing my long-time Baldwin main march with an Alexander-focused physical team, Corrosive Power and Energy Mastery suddenly became available again. Instead of letting those skills gather dust, I moved them onto my Wu march together with Heavy Lifter, and the results have been much stronger than I expected. With Wu sitting at around 122 Energy Regeneration before any in-combat effects are taken into account, she already casts frequently enough to make Heavy Lifter highly competitive, while Corrosive Power and Energy Mastery only accelerate those rotations even further once the battle gets going.

---

## What Heavy Lifter Does

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-12.png)

At level 8, Heavy Lifter provides:

- **70% chance** to trigger whenever the immortal casts an Ultimate Skill.
- Deals **350% magic damage** to all enemies.
- Reduces the Attack Speed of the two highest Physical Attack enemies by **30% for 12 seconds**.

The attack speed reduction is a nice bonus against physical teams, but it is not why players equip the skill.

Heavy Lifter is all about converting **energy regeneration into repeated AoE damage.**

Every ultimate cast is another opportunity to proc Heavy Lifter, meaning the faster an immortal cycles ultimates, the more valuable the skill becomes.

---

## Why Heavy Lifter Was Rarely Worth Using

Heavy Lifter didn't spend years on the sidelines because it was weak; it simply never won the battle for a premium skill slot. If you were building a competitive mage team, there was a combination that almost everyone ended up with: Corrosive Power, Energy Mastery and Fighting Master. Together they provided the energy generation needed to keep ultimate rotations flowing while also ensuring your main damage dealer wasn't constantly shut down by crowd control.

That became even more important once Fu Fei and Knife Through Butter started appearing in almost every serious matchup. Relying on Fu Fei's control immunity was no longer enough, which pushed Fighting Master from a strong option to an almost mandatory one. Once those three skills were locked in, Heavy Lifter was left without a place, regardless of how much potential damage it could produce.

---

## Why It Makes Sense Again

The interesting part is that Heavy Lifter hasn't changed at all. What has changed is the way players build their main marches. As more players move away from hyper-regeneration mage teams and towards physical carries or hybrid compositions, premium mage skills are no longer tied to a single lineup for every battle.

That's exactly what happened for me after replacing my long-time Baldwin main march with an Alexander-focused physical team. Corrosive Power and Energy Mastery suddenly became available again, and instead of leaving them unused I built a second march around Wu, Baldwin, Himiko and Merlin. With those energy skills now supporting a secondary mage team instead of the main march, Heavy Lifter finally has the room to do what it was always designed to do.

A year ago, that simply wasn't a realistic option because your strongest mage needed those premium slots. Today, many players have the flexibility to build an entirely separate energy-focused composition without making compromises elsewhere.

---

## Heavy Lifter Is All About Energy Regeneration

Heavy Lifter isn't a skill you judge by reading the tooltip. Its real value comes from how often it has the opportunity to activate, which means energy regeneration matters far more than the listed damage percentage.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-11.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-9.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-10.png)

Every ultimate cast gives Heavy Lifter another chance to trigger, so the faster your immortal cycles through ultimates, the more damage the skill produces over the course of a battle. At level 8, each proc has a 70% chance of dealing 350% magic damage to every enemy, giving an average expected value of roughly 245% magic damage every time an ultimate is cast.

You can think of its damage as:

### Expected DPS = (Damage × Trigger Chance) ÷ Time Between Ultimate Casts

The exact numbers are less important than the principle behind them. A mage casting every six or eight seconds will trigger Heavy Lifter dramatically more often than one casting every fifteen or twenty seconds, and because the skill has no internal cooldown, there is nothing limiting that scaling beyond your ability to generate energy.

---

## Why Wu Is Still the Best Choice

Despite the growing number of energy-focused immortals, Wu is still the benchmark for Heavy Lifter. She naturally reaches ultimate casts much faster than most other mages, which gives her considerably more opportunities to trigger the skill over the duration of a fight.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-13-1024x750.png)

My own Wu currently sits at around 122 Energy Regeneration before any additional energy starts flowing from Corrosive Power or Energy Mastery. That's already enough to make Heavy Lifter perform exceptionally well, and once those skills begin feeding even more energy after each ultimate, the entire rotation accelerates. Every cast helps generate the next one, which means Heavy Lifter continues finding opportunities to activate throughout the battle instead of waiting on a fixed cooldown like most offensive skills.

---

## Comparing Heavy Lifter to Other Magic Skills

Heavy Lifter often looks unimpressive if you compare nothing more than the damage percentage written on the skill. That comparison misses the most important part of how the skill actually works.

Traditional damage skills are limited by their cooldowns, so their damage output remains relatively predictable throughout a fight. Heavy Lifter behaves differently because its damage scales directly with ultimate frequency. The more energy your immortal generates, the more often the skill has a chance to activate, and the further it pulls ahead of conventional damage skills.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-14-1024x257.png)

The comparison chart below illustrates that relationship by showing how much Energy Regeneration is needed for Heavy Lifter to match or outperform other Tower of Knowledge damage skills. Some require extremely high regeneration before Heavy Lifter catches them, while others are overtaken surprisingly early. Either way, the chart makes one thing clear: investing in energy regeneration doesn't just improve Heavy Lifter—it is what determines whether the skill is average or exceptional.

---

## Team Synergy

Heavy Lifter naturally performs best in teams built around rapid ultimate rotations, making any source of additional energy generation particularly valuable. Corrosive Power and Energy Mastery remain its strongest partners because both help shorten the time between ultimate casts, allowing Heavy Lifter to trigger more frequently over the course of a battle.

That is also why Wu stands out as the ideal user. Her naturally high energy generation means she doesn't need an extreme amount of support before Heavy Lifter starts producing consistent value. On slower mages, however, the skill becomes much harder to justify because there simply aren't enough ultimate casts during a typical fight for Heavy Lifter to reach its full potential.

---

## Is Heavy Lifter Worth Investing In?

Whether Heavy Lifter is worth the investment depends far more on your account progression than on the skill itself. If you're still short on Cinder Wishes, your priority should always be your primary march. Legendary Tower of Knowledge skills are expensive, and investing heavily into a second or third team before your main lineup is complete will usually slow your overall progress.

The picture changes once you've reached the point where you're regularly collecting enough Cinders to purchase multiple legendary skills. At that stage, many players already have their main march finished, which means premium skills like Corrosive Power and Energy Mastery can be moved onto secondary teams without weakening their primary lineup. That's exactly where Heavy Lifter becomes an excellent investment.

If you already have a fast-casting immortal such as Wu ready for a second or third march, Heavy Lifter makes very good use of those freed-up energy skills and provides consistent team-wide damage throughout a fight. I still wouldn't recommend it as a universal skill for every mage, but for established accounts building multiple competitive marches, it has become one of the more attractive premium Tower of Knowledge options available.

---

## How to Obtain Heavy Lifter

Heavy Lifter is a **Legendary Tower of Knowledge** skill that can be purchased from the **Wisdom Well (Triss's Cinder Wish Shop)** once it becomes available in the rotation. Like all legendary Tower of Knowledge skills, it requires **Cinder Wishes** to obtain, making it a long-term investment rather than a skill most players will unlock early in their account progression.

Because Cinder Wishes are relatively limited for newer players, it's generally recommended to prioritize legendary skills for your primary march before investing in secondary teams. Once your core march is complete and Cinders become more plentiful, Heavy Lifter becomes a much more compelling purchase for energy-focused second and third marches.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-15-1024x522.png)

---

## Conclusion

Heavy Lifter is one of the best examples of how a shifting meta can completely change the value of an older skill without a single balance adjustment. For years it was squeezed out by stronger priorities on every competitive mage team, yet those priorities have gradually moved elsewhere as more players transition towards physical main marches.

That has created an opportunity for energy-focused secondary teams built around immortals like Wu, where Heavy Lifter can finally be paired with the premium energy skills it always wanted. If your Wu is already sitting around the 120 Energy Regeneration mark, you'll likely find that Heavy Lifter contributes far more than its tooltip suggests, making it one of the more rewarding premium Tower of Knowledge skills to revisit in the current meta.

title: Himiko Earth meta build - Vader's setup from patch 2.8.9
summary: King Vader’s Himiko Earth Meta Build — A Veteran Analysis on his top tier meta build
markdown:
***King Vader’s Himiko Earth Meta Build — A Veteran Analysis on his top tier meta build***

## Introduction

Across multiple seasons, Earth–Himiko has settled into one of the most reliable endgame archetypes in Infinity Kingdom. What separates average versions from top-tier variants, however, is the discipline to allocate spending and skillstones efficiently while understanding the mechanics that make the composition resilient.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-69-1024x424.png)

King Vader’s (s344) build represents the “finished” form of this lineup: a configuration polished through testing against mirror Earth teams, high-spender Shadow variants, and even Fu Fei–anchored control cores. After speaking with him at length, the strengths of his approach became clear. It is a measured, sustain-oriented Earth base whose entire structure exists to give Himiko the sustain she needs to carry the victory home, clean windows to crit, and maximum troop preservation.

Below is a detailed breakdown of his setup and why it consistently outperforms even into difficult matchups. Before going over the details, you can also watch this short video to see more details on performance and how Vader is able to beat whales at a disadvantage both in terms of Legendary Immortals, Legendary Skills and simple raw STP. Enjoy!

[Embedded media](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Infinity-Kingdom-2025-12-09-10-12-43.mp4)

---

## Immortal Lineup

## Theodora — Sustain Engine and DOT Cleanser

Theodora remains the most practical choice for players not committed to the extreme expenditure required to finish a Fu Fei talent tree. While Fu Fei technically edges her out at absolute peak investment, Vader’s results reinforce a simple truth: *most players get far more value directing money into skillstones and artifacts instead of forcing Fu Fei early.*

Her value in this lineup comes from:

- **Frequent, stable healing** that complements the long fight durations the of Earth cores that assist her in sustaining this team so well.
- **DOT removal**, which is crucial in matchups against Shadow (Blade Vortex), lightning compositions, and any setup built around stacking DoT effects (damage over time).

**Artifact:**
A **Surge** artifact for increased regeneration rate. This improves both healing consistency and given increased regen rate you will clear DoT effects more consistently as well as trigger Spring of Life more frequently as surge is allowing her to cycle heals faster.

### Talent:

- **Battle Excitation** — mandatory for initial energy on our Himiko as well as for the damage amp it contributes to Himiko, overall a significant tempo gain.

---

## Himiko — Primary Damage and Backline Control

Himiko is the centerpiece. Beyond her raw damage, her targeting logic—always landing her control on the enemy backliner with the highest HP—allows her to directly pressure sustain teams and punish compositions relying on a single protected carry if they neglect to run Fighting Master.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-72.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-68-1024x620.png)

What elevates her here is the synergy between:

- **Shadow elemental advantage** (beating every element except Holy),
- **High crit scaling** as a mage, and
- **Massive AoE pressure**, avoiding any risk of not hitting your desired enemy target (compared to e.g. Empress Wu where you can get unlucky and not hit the enemy's carry with multiple ultimates)

### Artifact:

- **Crit% main stat**
- **Annihilation bonus**
This combination is the highest-value damage profile available to her. For secondary attributes, if you can get more crit % that is a big advantage, that being said, crit value and magical damage is also very helpful.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-70.png)

### Talent:

- **Stormeye** — essential for amplifying her overall damage through raw damage modifier and its boost to crit chance.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-71-1024x340.png)

---

## Yi Sun-Shin (YSS) — Damage Reduction and Tempo Control

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-73.png)

YSS performs two jobs exceptionally well in this team:

1. He protects the team from collapse via his huge 30% damage taken reduction and provides a significant 30% healing buff while under his effect.
2. He disrupts opposing Alex lines by simply being placed in front of them, because we are running **Fearless Stance** to reduce damage taken, turning him into a durable brick wall.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-75.png)

### Artifact:

- **Physical Defense %** as the top attribute
- **Growth** as the bonus
Growth gives value into both physical and magical matchups, making it the most efficient single artifact choice for the long term. If you are able to craft two artifacts maxed with physical defense % top, then you can have a Guard bonus artifact in your inventory and equip this when fighting into physical damage enemies - especially when using YSS to tank an enemy Alex or other high physical damage dealers.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-74.png)

This contribution is one reason the build holds up so well against other top builds. YSS provides invaluable mitigation effects and ensures the rest of our sustain setup has time to do its job.

---

## Bjorn — Resilience Boons and Damage amp

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-76.png)

Bjorn is an incredible choice for the second tank in this Earth–Himiko. He provides:

- A debuff increasing the **damage taken by the enemy by 20%**
- A **resilience**buff of 30% defending our frontlines against critical hits.
- And his shadow affinity also gives him an advantage as he takes reduced damage from all other elements than holy.

### Talent:

- **Sturdy Barrier**, which supplies shields across the lineup—an important layer in a sustain-based structure and given the sustain focus and high mitigation of this setup, you will actually see very high shield-values from an upgraded Sturdy Barrier talent - unlike on many other more squishy setups where damage is taken too quickly for Study to have a real impact.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-77.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-78-1024x366.png)

### Artifact:

- **Physical Defense %** with **Growth**bonus
Against magic-heavy enemies, **Growth** outperforms Guard, and late-game players generally maintain both options for matchup flexibility. Vader currently has a Guard artifact, but a slight improvement would be to have a Growth one and change between the two as needed.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-79.png)

---

## Skill Setup

## Bjorn

- **Purification**: Cleanses debuffs and triggers small heals, which in turn activate *Spring of Life*'s 15% reduced damage taken buff.
- **Energy Shield**: Core mitigation; prevents unnecessary troop loss across the board through powerful shield effects. Mitigation/sustain through shielding is superior to raw healing, simply because there is no loss of troop count. When you take damage from an enemy you loose troops, healing will revive these troops, but in the interim you are left with reduced troop counts. For example, a Himiko taking damage: If she has shields up to absorb the damage, she loses no troops at all. If she does not, she loses troops which reduces her damage until she is healed back up. So even at identical values, shielding is technically superior to healing.
- **Weakness Aura**: Simple, cuts down on enemy resilience, reinforcing Himiko's crit reliability.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-80-1024x597.png)

**Temporary options:**
If you lack skillstones and are looking for alternatives as you progress into the skill setup above. I suggest using skills such as: *Blessing of Rage*, *Blessing of Defense*, or *Oaken Guard*.

---

## Yi Sun-Shin

- **Energy Suppression**: Reduces enemy energy gain, slowing down the energy regen of your enemies is a powerful method of mitigating damage.
- **Weakening Curse**: Disarms physical damage dealers, extremely valuable versus physical damage dealers, e.g. Alexanders.
- **Master’s Aegis**: Major magical mitigation; this is one of the core reasons why the build is so stable in a mage-heavy meta.  - If you are fighting into a physical damage enemy or meta in general, then you should not run Master's Aegis but instead opt for a Heart of Arcana for your aura slot here.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-81-1024x606.png)

**Budget alternative:**
Run **Oaken Guard** or **Resist**in place of Weakening Curse / Aegis, until your Wisdom Well/Cinder skills are completed.

---

## Theodora

- **Vitality Touch**: Core source of healing and a reliable trigger for *Spring of Life* and a nice mitigation effect.
- **Spring of Life**: Increases all healing effects and provides a strong mitigation buff once immortals are healed. Raises overall survivability and strengthens your heals.
- **Assist**: Essential for preserving Himiko’s troop count, which directly affects her damage output. Absolutely mandatory in all builds that rely on a carry-backline damage dealer.

**Temporary substitutes:**
*Rage Blessing*, *Blessing of Defense*/*Oaken Guard/Resist*, and *Malice Aura* can fill gaps during early construction, depending on what you are fighting against.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-83-1024x605.png)

### Fighting into No Escape

**Important notes for fighting into No Escape setups:** If you are fighting into enemies that rely on No Escape, Fountain of Life becomes a must have legendary skill. Having it at level 1 is perfectly fine, but you need it to counter No Escape. That being said, on many servers and in many KvKs you will find that many are not using No Escape on their main march simply because of how common Fountain of Life has become. If you do face No Escape enemies, you need to equip Fountain of Life on Theodora, move Spring of Life to YSS in place of Energy Suppression which you move to Bjorn and give up Purification.

For this feature on Vader's build, he is not fighting into No Escape builds often and hence do not use Fountain of Life by default. Note that upgrading fountain of life to higher levels will also provide enough healing output that you should baseline it into the setup. But as money is not infinite, keeping a level 1 on the sidelines to swap in while you prioritize other skills is a good strategy.

---

## Himiko

- **Annihilation**: While Infinite Firepower is best-in-slot for raw damage, short of being able to afford multiple high level legendary skills, Vader is using Annihilation until he completes Infinite Firepower.
- **Energy Master**: Top-tier for both damage and energy cycling; expensive, but the improvement is immediate as this skill enables fast ultimate-cycling. Later can be paired with Corrosive Power when you are able to get it (amongst the most expensive skill in the game).  - **Spell Disintegration** works well as a placeholder until Energy Master reaches level 5.
- **Fighting Master** — mandatory unless you run Fu Fei. Control immunity is non-negotiable for your primary carry.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-82-1024x600.png)

---

## Dragon setup

Vader is running this build with the Earth Dragon Dementer and using the Collapse dragon specialization talent tree. The earth dragon provides unrivaled mitigation effects in its Sandstorm Breath and with Collapse we max out on the mitigation effect which works perfect in synergy with our core setup here. Collapse increases both the chance of the mitigation buff taking effect (to 98% from 90% base) and provides increased duration of the effect (16.8 seconds from 12 seconds base).

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-84-1024x504.png)

As an added advantage to simply being perfect for this build, the earth dragon is also a free-to-play dragon meaning you can upgrade its talents with Dragon Crystals from elemental bosses without having to spend on events like with the Shadow dragon.

Talking to Vader, his take is that if he did want to spend on a paywalled dragon (holy / shadow) he would opt for the holy dragon for its healing and mitigation effects. That being said, he does not think this would be a real benefit to the build as the mitigation from Dementer is simply amazing! And for the record, I personally agree with that statement.

---

## Player Perspective — Why Vader’s Version Works

What impressed me most in testing variants of this structure is its remarkable **matchup stability**. Earth–Himiko traditionally wins long fights, but it often struggles to maintain troop advantage when pressured early by optimized Shadow or by other burst-heavy builds. Vader’s version seem to consistently be able to sustain and take advantage of superior troop counts.

In practice, this lets Himiko maintain effective DPS deep into the fight, even against enemy carries with higher level legendary skills and Fu Fei support. I am very impressed with the performance - and consistent performance - of Vader's build here. Hence I am very happy that he has taken the time to talk it through so I can publish it here on the wiki for many others to read and learn from. Thank you King Vader for your contribution to the community!

---

## Conclusion

Vader’s Himiko Earth build represents a very well engineered conquest setup. While progress is yet to be made towards the final endgame form of the composition (legendary progress for skills and Fu Fei eventually) this build is a prime example of a sustain- and mitigation-heavy shell enabling a crit-focused, high-pressure Himiko. What makes it extreemly interesting for me to see and share, is that Vader prooves it doesn’t demand early Fu Fei investment; instead, by channeling his spending into the skills and artifacts he is able to actually deliver matchup wins against others who on the face of it should have the advantage (check the video in the top if you have not yet).

For players building toward a long-term Earth-Himiko lineup, this is in my opinion the most reliable blueprint currently available as of time of writing. Huge thank you to King Vader of server 344 for sharing this awesome build with us all!

---

title: Himiko (shadow) Immortal Guide
summary: Himiko is a sustained magical damage carry built around repeated Ultimate casts rather than single burst windows. She fits naturally into full Shadow as well as mixed-element formations and can function either as a…
markdown:
## Introduction

Himiko is a sustained magical damage carry built around repeated Ultimate casts rather than single burst windows. She fits naturally into full Shadow as well as mixed-element formations and can function either as a primary carry or as a secondary source of sustained AoE pressure depending on the structure of the setup.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-76-1024x559.png)

Her effectiveness depends heavily on taking advantage of shadow's elemental advantage in builds that rely on control, energy support, and strong mitigation. The longer she remains active, the more her value compounds.

Himiko fragments can be obtained through Thea’s Roulette, random Shadow Immortal shards, Legion of Frostborne Chests and Legendary Battlepass.

---

### Ultimate Skill – Demon Ambush

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-77.png)

### Core Mechanics

- Deals magical damage to **all enemies**
- 450% damage rate at max level
- If more than two targets are present:  - Control effect: Pulls the back-row enemy with the highest troop count into the void for 6 seconds
- The target cannot attack, cast, or be targeted

With her exclusive artifact, Demon Ambush gains **+30% total damage**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-78.png)

The skill performs two functions:

1. Massive AoE magical burst
2. Temporary removal of a key backline unit (control)

The void effect is often countered by Fighting Master, but even when countered it forces structural decisions in enemy builds. Because each Immortal only has three skill slots, compelling an opponent to dedicate one to Fighting Master instead of a damage amplifier or energy tool is a meaningful advantage in high-level play.

---

## Team Fit and Synergy

Himiko thrives in compositions that protect her casting rhythm. Since nearly all her damage comes from repeated Ultimate Ability activations. Where I see her performing the best, is in builds with earth dragons and either:

(1) runs a dual tank frontline of e.g. Bjorn/Charles and YSS for maximum defensive advantage (mitigation combined with shadow advantage) where you rely on Himiko to solo carry the damage through sheer refusal to take damage while unleashing devestating AoE burst.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-80-1024x616.png)

Or (2) in a more offensive setup where you combine her with an Alexander in the frontline with Knife Through Butter for regen control and increased frontloaded damage pressure.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-81-1024x618.png)

## Support

In terms of backline support, she needs a support for the key Battle Excitation specialization buffs. There are four supports I will highlight as pairing well with Himiko in the current meta. Let's quickly go over each, more details in seperate build guides. This is mostly to get your understanding of what how to think of pairing her.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-82.png)

### Qin Emperor

Qin is one of the most practical and accessible partners for Himiko. He is perhaps the cheapest and easiest support to max talents on and provides the extremely valuable wounds effect.

He provides:

- Full-team Serious Wound
- Attack speed increase

Himiko applies repeated AoE pressure over time. Qin prevents healing from reversing that pressure. Because Qin fragments are more accessible than many premium supports, players often push his specialisation levels higher, making him a stable long-term pairing.

In extended fights, this combination steadily erodes sustain-based compositions.

### Zenobia

Zenobia offers focused sustain:

- Heals the two units taking the heaviest losses
- Provides continued healing via normal attack triggers

She is cheap and easy and does well in Himiko plus Alex builds enabling elemental buff as well as her added attack speed buff through unique artifact. For players looking to maintain long-fight uptime without heavy investment, she is a practical choice.

### Theodora

Theodora provides:

- Full-team healing
- Cleansing of continuous damage effects
- Stronger burst healing below half HP

She is more expensive to build but significantly increases backline stability. In long-duration fights, she ensures Himiko survives long enough to fully leverage her Ultimate cycle.

### Fu Fei

For Chaos-oriented or high-investment teams:

- Full-team healing
- Control removal
- Temporary control immunity (extended with artifact)

Because Himiko depends on uninterrupted casting, control removal has high strategic value. Fu Fei is especially effective in structured marches that aim for long engagements. **She is the best support for Himiko, but also expensive to get to immortal talent 8.**

---

## Skill Build Philosophy

Himiko’s build direction is straightforward: **Increase Ultimate cast frequency and increase Ultimate / Magical damage.**

Older long-ramp builds relied on Battle Stance and Demonic Contract. These skills scale over time but are poorly suited to the current tempo of the game. Battle Stance delays energy gain for 20 seconds, and Demonic Contract ramps too slowly to influence mid-length fights. Modern builds however prioritise immediate impact through skills that synergize for rapid energy regen.

**Core Modern Skills**:

### Energy Mastery

- Restores 240 energy after each Ultimate
- Significantly increases next Ultimate damage

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-83.png)

Because Demon Ambush defines her entire kit, Energy Mastery directly amplifies both frequency and impact. It is one of her strongest upgrades.

### Infinite Firepower

- Periodic magical AoE trigger
- Temporary energy regeneration boost

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-85.png)

The energy regeneration effect is the primary value. It accelerates her cycle and strengthens her sustained rhythm.

### Corrosive Power

After three Ultimate hits:

- Restores 200 energy
- Boosts subsequent Ultimate damage

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-84.png)

Himiko naturally triggers this during standard play, making it a strong synergy option.

### Fighting Master (Defensive Stability)

- Control immunity
- Damage reduction

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-86.png)

While not an offensive increase, it prevents lost tempo due to stuns or burst focus. In control-heavy environments, it can be necessary if you do not have Fu Fei and are fighting into enemy earths or Himiko's. Ideally you have Fu Fei to support Himiko, meaning you run the three skills above.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-89.png)

---

## Specialisation Choice

**Stormeye****(Recommended)**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-87.png)

- Increased critical rate
- Increased magical damage at battle start

Both stats directly scale Demon Ambush. The benefits apply immediately and enhance every cast.

---

## Artifact

For your artifact, you want to craft until you get one with crit % as the main attribute, preferably one crit % secondary roll and magical attack attribute. You want Annihilation as the bonus roll.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-88.png)

---

## Damage Comparison and Affinity Scaling

With exclusive artifact active and assuming a 25% Shadow elemental affinity bonus, Himiko’s performance shifts significantly.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-90-1024x125.png)

Assuming Shadow affinity is indeed 25% (consistent with historical balancing adjustments), Himiko reaches the highest average sustained damage among these carries.

Note: She does not provide built-in Serious Wound when comparing to Khan. She has no Random luck required as compared to Baldwin, who's average damage is slightly higher but consistency no where near the same. Baldwin can cast multiple times without hitting the enemy carry if unlucky. Himiko will always strike the enemy carry as the has full AoE damage.

Her raw numbers are strong. Her strategic value depends on matchup and tempo.

### What really makes her so insanely strong tho!

It is important to understand how damage works in Infinity Kingdom. The damage output is based on skills and passive, but players must remember that troop count at the precise time of cast is also a **HUGE**factor for the output damage numbers. That means, that while the shadow elemental advantage of Himiko does means more damage dealt, **it also means less damage taken**.

That is huge in a battle as troop retention is the key to big damage numbers. Taking a real combat scenario into account Himiko will outperform all others on the list above, but on paper output but because she retains troops better so her second wave of damage will be a lot higher than the others given the same damage taken during the window between casts.

---

## Meta Position and Practical Limitations – Current Competitive Reality

Himiko’s decline in popularity is not the result of weak damage numbers. On paper, especially with full Shadow affinity scaling, her sustained output remains among the highest in the game. The shift happened because the surrounding systems evolved in ways that directly target regen-based burst structures.

### Knife Through Himiko's Butter

The most important change was the introduction of Knife Through Butter on Alexander. This skill reduces enemy energy significantly, and that single mechanic directly interferes with the foundation of Himiko builds. Her entire identity is built around repeated Ultimate cycles. She does not win through a single explosive cast; she wins by reaching Demon Ambush consistently and repeatedly.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-91.png)

When Alexander suppresses energy, that rhythm breaks. Corrosive Power triggers later. Energy Mastery loops slow down. Instead of cycling smoothly, she stalls between casts. Meanwhile, Alexander applies pressure immediately and does not rely on long ramp windows. In practical Conquest fights, this difference in energy timing becomes obvious after the first suppression cycle. Regen-based burst builds lose momentum, and once they lose tempo, they struggle to recover it.

### Players have gotten used to defending against magical damage by default

At the same time, defensive structures have shifted toward layered magic mitigation. Master’s Aegis reduces magical damage taken for the entire team, and when paired with Resist, the reduction becomes substantial.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-92.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-93.png)

Himiko deals exclusively magical damage. Every Demon Ambush is directly reduced by these layers. In contrast, physical carries bypass Master’s Aegis entirely. Because magical damage dominated the meta for so long, players naturally adapted by stacking anti-mage tools. The unintended consequence is that physical cores are now regaining value simply by attacking through less-contested defensive layers.

Malice is also returning in relevance. Many high-investment builds rely on large critical burst windows, and Himiko needs to lean into maximise crit scaling in order to land the big bursts she needs to solo-carry. Malice punishes crit-reliant damage spikes by reducing their reliability and effective pressure. In practical terms, this makes large Demon Ambush crit chains less decisive in certain matchups. When crit-based builds meet Malice-supported teams, damage thresholds become less predictable and finishing pressure weakens.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-94.png)

**What does that mean for Himiko then?**

However, this does not mean Himiko is obsolete. It means she functions differently. In the current Conquest environment, one of the stronger-performing structures combines Himiko with Alexander rather than opposing him. A composition such as Himiko, Fu Fei, YSS, and Alexander works because it controls tempo on both sides. The build is no longer purely about letting Himiko scale over time; it is about controlling when both sides are allowed to scale. This is why in my opinion based on what I am seeing right now, most Himiko players that remain absolute top are beginning to lean more into Alex-Himiko builds over the traditional meta solo carry Himiko with great succes.

The key point is that Himiko did not lose her damage. The meta gained direct counters to energy cycling and layered magic mitigation. In response, successful Himiko builds now incorporate tempo control rather than relying purely on sustained regen loops. In structured compositions that account for energy suppression and defensive stacking, she remains highly competitive.

## Conclusion

Himiko remains the strongest consistent magical damage dealer in *Infinity Kingdom* when fully supported and placed in the right structure. With full Shadow affinity scaling, her average damage is among the highest in the game, and her repeated Demon Ambush cycle can overwhelm opponents in longer, controlled fights.

What changed is not her output, but the environment around her. Energy suppression from Alexander, layered magic mitigation through Master’s Aegis and Resist, and the resurgence of Malice have all made pure regen-based mage builds harder to execute. At the same time, physical carries have benefited from defensive overinvestment into anti-mage tools.

In the current meta, Himiko performs best in tempo-aware hybrid compositions, often alongside Alexander, rather than as a standalone long-ramp carry. When properly structured, she is still highly competitive. When forced into uncontrolled, fast-paced engagements without support, she struggles to reach her ceiling.

She is no longer the default choice for most players—but in the right hands and the right march, she remains a powerful and relevant option.

---

title: Hippolyta - one of the absolute best Immortals in Infinity Kingdom
summary: Hippolyta is one of the absolute best Immortals in Infinity Kingdom and a personal favorite of mine. She isn't just a must-have for fire setups; she also shines in other elements like water and lightning. Her unique…
markdown:
### Hippolyta (Hippo) Guide - Infinity Kingdom

Hippolyta is one of the absolute best Immortals in Infinity Kingdom and a personal favorite of mine. She isn't just a must-have for fire setups; she also shines in other elements like water and lightning. Her unique ability to control enemy energy while dealing strong damage makes her an incredibly versatile and valuable asset in multiple lineups.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/image-5.png)

---

### Hippolyta's Ultimate Ability - Flaming Smite

Her ultimate ability, **Flaming Smite**, strikes enemies five times per cast, dealing 120% damage per hit. Once you acquire her unique artifact, **Goddess' Waist Belt**, this increases to seven smites per cast. In addition to dealing damage, each smite removes **100 energy** from the target. Moreover, each smite causes a 10% attack speed debuff on the target, stackable and with a 6s duration.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/image-4-1024x546.png)

While her raw damage output is solid, **the true power of Hippolyta comes from her energy reduction effect**. This ability enables her to disrupt enemy ultimates, giving her team a significant advantage in both PvP and PvE scenarios.

---

## Hippolyta in Different Setups

### Fire Setup (Her Most Common Role)

Hippolyta is an **essential** part of any Fire team. Since Fire thrives on **frequent critical hits**, her multiple attack instances make her an ideal pair with **Seondeok**, whose **ultimate damage scales with crit activations**. To enhance this synergy:

- Consider using **Energy Suppression** to further prevent enemy ultimates.
- If you're running a lower-level Fire build, **Rage** can be equipped on Hippolyta to increase her **crit rate**, further maximizing Seondeok’s damage output.
- She provides excellent control and helps sustain Fire’s high-pressure playstyle.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/image-8.png)

### Lightning Setup (Control and Buff Synergy)

Hippolyta also fits **extremely well in Lightning compositions** due to her debuff application. In Lightning teams, applying **debuffs increases overall team damage** (due to the Lightning Dragon’s passive effect). Her **attack speed slow** on enemies contributes to this, making her an indirect damage amplifier.

A great **Lightning composition** featuring Hippolyta would be:

- **Richard** (frontline tank, stun control)
- **Hippolyta** (energy control, attack speed debuffs)
- **Hammurabi/Himiko** (Hammurabi's ultimate boosted by debuffs)
- **Genghis Khan** (high burst damage)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/image-10-1024x310.png)

This setup excels in both **control and burst damage**, making it a deadly combination.

### Water Setup (Energy Control Focus)

Water teams benefit from **strong CC (crowd control) and energy denial**. A control-based Water setup including Hippolyta can prevent opponents from launching their ultimates, creating a **huge energy advantage**. Skills such as **Energy Suppression** and **Weakness** work well here.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/image-9-1024x553.png)

Ideal Water control setup with Hippolyta:

- **Attila** (control and energy drain synergy through silence)
- **Hippolyta** (energy control, attack speed slow)
- **Merlin** (primary damage dealer)
- **Yoshitsune** (consistent DPS and execute) – can be swapped out if you have e.g. a Bathory or a Mathilda available.

While not as common as Fire, a **Water-control setup** with Hippolyta can be incredibly powerful.

---

## Hippolyta for Spiders & Bosses

Hippolyta is one of the **strongest immortals for Spider and PvE Boss fights**. Her **ultimate deals all seven smites to a single target** when there is only one enemy, making her function as a **pseudo-single-target nuker**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/image-6-1024x603.png)

Even more importantly, **her energy drain can prevent bosses from using their ultimate abilities entirely**. By stacking **Energy Regen** skills (such as those from the Tower of Knowledge), she can repeatedly remove the boss’s energy, massively reducing incoming damage.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/image-7-1024x547.png)

This makes her a **top-tier pick for PvE content**, significantly improving survivability and damage output over prolonged fights.

---

## Final Thoughts

Hippolyta is an amazing immortal, not just for her strong damage but for her unique ability to **control enemy energy and slow their attack speed**. Whether she is placed in a **Fire, Lightning, or Water** team, she provides massive utility and helps shape the battlefield to your advantage.

### Key Takeaways:

- **Energy Denial**: Her ultimate removes 100 energy per hit (7x per cast with artifact).
- **Fire Team Synergy**: Works exceptionally well with Seondeok by maximizing crit activations.
- **Lightning Team Utility**: Provides **debuffs** that increase Lightning team damage.
- **Water Team Control**: Combos well with other **energy suppression** and CC units.
- **PvE Dominance**: Can prevent bosses from using ultimates, making her a **top-tier PvE immortal**.

Hippolyta is one of the most versatile and impactful Immortals in the game. If you manage to obtain and build her, she will be an absolute game-changer in any lineup!

---

**Myth Busting: Does Her Attack Speed Debuff Count as Chill?**

There has been some speculation that **Hippolyta’s attack speed slow might count as a Chill effect**, potentially boosting Merlin and other Water Immortal’s ultimates. While an **IK support employee initially claimed this was true**, it has been **proven false**. Her ability does **NOT**count as Chill, so don’t build around that assumption!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/image-11.png)

---

That wraps up the guide! If you have any questions, feel free to ask. Otherwise, start building your **Hippo** and enjoy watching your enemies struggle to cast their ultimates! 🚀
