title: Holy element in Preperation and season 1 (much different from later in the game)
summary: Welcome to a new guide on Theia’s Roulette, an event that appears on preparation servers just before Season 1, coinciding with the release of Holy immortals. If you’ve been dominating early-game with Shadow—or seeing…
markdown:
Welcome to a new guide on **Theia’s Roulette**, an event that appears on preparation servers just before Season 1, coinciding with the release of Holy immortals. If you’ve been dominating early-game with Shadow—or seeing others do so—Theia’s Roulette might seem like the natural next step for those who want to jump straight into the power of Holy.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/image-145-1024x473.png)

In this guide, I’ll walk you through how the event works in the early seasons, compare costs and spin efficiency, and share my opinion on whether it’s really worth investing heavily in Holy from the start.

## Theia’s Roulette and the Arrival of Holy

When Holy immortals become available, whales on a new server typically scramble to switch from Shadow to Holy. Although Shadow can put up a fight, Holy is considered a hard counter to Shadow, thanks to the inherent damage reductions and damage buffs Holy immortals gain against Shadow.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/image-146-1024x412.png)

On top of that, key Holy immortals like Theodora and Manco directly undermine the strengths of Shadow teams. For instance, Theodora can dispel continuous damage (a big part of Tutankhamun’s kit), while Manco provides control immunity for the Holy team.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/image-147-1024x572.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/image-148-1024x576.png)

The catch is that unlocking and maxing Holy immortals during preparation or early-season servers is extremely expensive. Although it’s possible to piece together a Holy lineup relatively quickly through Theia’s Roulette, you should know that those same Holy fragments will be available **far more cheaply** in late-game events. Whether you decide to spend big now or wait largely depends on how competitive you want to be right away.

## How Theia’s Roulette Works

On new servers, Theia’s Roulette offers a chance to spin for Holy Immortal Fragments and Holy Dragon Fragments. Each spin costs 1,000 gems, or you can purchase special bundles for spin tickets. The main bundles in the in-game store range from $5 to $100. Notably, the **$5, $10, and $20 bundles** each give exactly 1 spin per dollar, which is the best rate. The **$50 and $100 bundles** offer more spins in total but at a slightly worse spin-per-dollar ratio.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/image-149-1024x473.png)

Every spin has a 3% chance to drop x10 Immortal Fragments for your chosen Holy immortal, and an 8% chance to drop x100 Holy Dragon Fragments. While 100 dragon fragments may not seem like much, you’ll need a lot of them later, so picking them up early can still be worthwhile if you have the budget.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/image-150-1024x473.png)

## Bonus Bar and Spin Efficiency

Unlike older versions of the wheel—where you might get a guaranteed immortal after 25 spins—this new iteration has a **“bonus bar”** that rewards you with extra fragments at certain spin milestones (50, 100, 200, 350, 500, 700, and 900). The best value tiers are 50, 100, and 200 spins; 900 is also decent because it grants 60 bonus fragments at once. However, the mid-range tiers (350, 500, 700) have poor spin-per-fragment ratios.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/image-151-1024x473.png)

**Pricing** **estimates**

**For example**, if you do 200 spins, you get about 60 Immortal Fragments in total: around 30 from the bonus bar plus an estimated 30 from the spins themselves. At that rate, you’d need roughly eleven or twelve events (each lasting three days) to collect enough fragments (1,020 total) to max a single Holy immortal. That’s a lengthy process, and if you’re willing to wait that long, you might as well hold off until Holy immortals become cheaper in later events.

Doing 900 spins per event means you buy 3x 5, 3x 10, 3x20, 3x50 you get just 240 spins in total for the event. Thus you are going to need the 99$ bundles adding up from there. You need 10x 100$ bundles to get a total of 940 spins at a cost of 1255$ which on average will yield you: 120 from the bonus bar plus 282 fragments from spin rewards, i.e. roughly 402 immortal fragments in total. Over three events you can thus max out one immortal and begin working on the next.

Assuming you want to speed it up (if not, just wait for later game events) you will be spending an average of**3184$** maxing a single holy immortal. That is quite expensive and the same price range as the original servers spent getting these. For comparison, know that holy fragments are actually available for free in the harbour in Conquest and at extremely cheap prices and for gems in Galaxy events later in the game.

If you then bank for 900 you come in a slightly higher total cost but **FAR**greater speed.

### Combining In-Game Store and GTArcade

Using the Gtarcade store in addition to the in-game store: The above is assuming you are only using the in-game store. With Gtarcade you have access to spin tickets at: 6 tickets for 5$, 12 tickets for 10$, 22 tickets for 20$ and 48 tickets for 50$. These are all available with a 5 times weekly limit.

This changes the maths somewhat. These are all very efficient at 0.83$ to 1.04$ per ticket. Thus, buying out all five a week in all tiers, you only need 3.15 purchases of the inefficient in-game 100$ bundle in order to reach the 900 tickets you need for fast maxed holy immortals while still taking advantage of the bonus bar somewhat (3.15 means that you buy 4 the first event then not for the later ones while you have excess).

This means you spend a total of 955$ per event for the 402 fragments i.e. this **takes you price to reach 1020 fragments down to: 2423$**. A significant saving of 761$ per immortal you complete. Ultimately however, holy immortals quickly will be very expensive and you should consider if you can wait till later in the game.

| In--game store |  |  | 900,5 | 995 |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Buys | Bundle Price | Tickets | USD/Ticket | Spins bought | total cost |
| 3 | 5 | 5 | 1,00 | 15 | 15 |
| 3 | 10 | 10 | 1,00 | 30 | 30 |
| 3 | 20 | 20 | 1,00 | 60 | 60 |
| 3 | 50 | 45 | 1,11 | 135 | 150 |
| 3,15 | 100 | 70 | 1,43 | 220,5 | 315 |
| Gtarcade Store |  |  |  |  |  |
| 5 | 5 | 6 | 0,83 | 30 | 25 |
| 5 | 10 | 12 | 0,83 | 60 | 50 |
| 5 | 20 | 22 | 0,91 | 110 | 100 |
| 5 | 50 | 48 | 1,04 | 240 | 250 |
|  |  |  |  | 0 | 0 |

## Opinion: Spend Now or Wait?

In my view, there are two main reasons you’d want to dump resources into Theia’s Roulette during the prep or early seasons:

1. **You want immediate dominance.** If you’re set on leading the server as a top whale, you’ll want Holy as soon as possible, regardless of cost.
2. **You have a long-term goal to max Holy eventually and don’t mind an early start.** You might accept paying more now so you can have the advantage right away.

For everyone else—especially low to mid spenders—**waiting is usually better**. Once your server reaches Conquest, you’ll see Holy fragments in events like **Galaxy** and free sources like the **Harbor**, at a fraction of the early-game cost. If you aren’t determined to be the absolute top player during the first few seasons, patience will save you an enormous amount of money.

Ultimately, holy is obtainable going into season 1 and during season 1, but it is extremely expensive to get and is only something you should be doing if you want to be the absolute biggest whale during early game seasons. If you do not need to be that, wait till later to get your holy immortals online!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/image-152-1024x493.png)

*This is GreatScott from a preperation stage server 8 weeks old.*

**Summary**
Theia’s Roulette brings Holy immortals to early-game servers, triggering a rush to assemble new lineups or counter unstoppable Shadow whales. While Holy is indeed powerful and counters Shadow effectively, unlocking and maxing your Holy team through Theia’s Roulette can be prohibitively expensive. For players who want immediate top-tier power, that might be a worthwhile price. However, if you’re more budget-conscious or simply willing to wait, you can acquire the same Holy fragments much more cheaply in late-game events. Keep an eye on your spending, explore bundle options both in-game and through GTArcade, and decide whether racing into Holy is worth the premium—or if you’d rather bide your time and transition more affordably later on. Good luck spinning, and may your Holy army shine bright when the time is right!

title: Holy & Shadow Dragon Crystals Guide – Where to Get Them, Costs & Best
markdown:
![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-095012-o2riwk.png)

Fortunately, recent updates have introduced better alternatives. With the changes to Rune Factory and especially Theia's Roulette in August 2026, players now have more opportunities to collect these valuable crystals without relying entirely on expensive bundles.

But where should you collect them, how many do you actually need, and which options offer the best value?

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-095119-rnt6vy.png)

## TL;DR – The Best Ways to Obtain Holy & Shadow Crystals

For most players actively developing Lucasta or Melanthios, **Theia's Roulette and Rune Factory should be the main events to watch**. Both offer recurring opportunities to obtain crystals, either through Gems or real-money purchases.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-094938-f76hio.png)

**Important**: These are expected costs, not guaranteed returns. Purchase limits mean players cannot necessarily buy thousands of crystals at the cheapest rate. That's why a complete heavy-spender comparison should consider the marginal cost of successive purchases, not just the best advertised bundle.



## How Many Holy or Shadow Dragon Crystals Do You Need?

Dragon Crystals are required for three different progression systems: upgrading your Dragon's basic skills, developing its Talent Tree, and upgrading its Dragon Portrait.

The costs quickly become enormous.

Using the Holy Dragon, Lucasta, as our example, the current estimates are:

That means developing Lucasta's full Talent Tree and Portrait alone requires approximately **300,000 Holy Dragon Crystals**, without including the crystals consumed by the three basic Dragon Skills.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-094540-qkpgf6.png)

The Shadow Dragon faces similarly expensive progression, although the exact current full Talent Tree total should be verified separately. Both dragons share the same Portrait upgrade costs.

These numbers also explain why selecting one dragon and focusing your resources is so important. Splitting your crystals between multiple expensive dragon projects can leave both underdeveloped for a very long time.

For more information, see our [Dragon Portrait Upgrade Costs Guide](https://ik-wiki.com/posts/upgrade-costs-of-dragon-portraits).

## Theia's Roulette – A Major Improvement in August 2026

Theia's Roulette has become one of the most interesting recurring sources of Holy and Shadow Dragon Crystals since Patch 2.9.8.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-094823-lrl7eu.png)

Players can now select either **350 Holy Dragon Crystals or 350 Shadow Dragon Crystals** as their featured reward.

The wheel also contains smaller crystal rewards, meaning you can obtain crystals without necessarily hitting the jackpot.

The important mechanics are:

* The 350-crystal jackpot has a natural 3% drop chance.
* The jackpot is guaranteed by the 25th spin if it hasn't appeared earlier.
* Five additional crystal rewards provide 45 crystals each, with a combined 5.2% chance.
* The jackpot counter resets whenever the grand prize is obtained.

Taking the jackpot guarantee and smaller crystal rewards into account, the expected return is approximately **22 Dragon Crystals per spin**.

This is a considerable improvement over earlier versions of the event.

### What Can You Expect?

These are long-run statistical averages. Individual results will vary, particularly during smaller sessions.

The event also awards milestone chests at certain spin thresholds. These are valuable additional rewards, although they shouldn't be counted as extra Dragon Crystals.

For players purchasing tickets with Gems, each ticket costs 1,000 Gems. This means approximately **4,540 Gems per 100 expected Dragon Crystals**.

Theia's Roulette also has one free spin each event day, making it worth visiting even when you aren't planning to spend.

For the complete odds, pity calculations, and milestone analysis, see our [Theia's Roulette Guide](https://ik-wiki.com/posts/theias-roulette---pricing-chance-calculations-and-more/).

## Rune Factory – The Other Major Recurring Source

Rune Factory replaced the older Sparks of Galaxy event and remains an important source of Holy and Shadow Dragon Crystals.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-094908-4f7c15.png)

Players use Energy Cores to make draws and obtain Rune Insignias, which can then be exchanged for rewards in the Factory Shop.

The relevant exchange rate is straightforward:

**20 Rune Insignias = 100 Holy or Shadow Dragon Crystals.**

After the Rune Factory rework, the published reward probabilities became:

This produces an average of approximately **1.31 Rune Insignias per Energy Core**, equivalent to 6.55 Dragon Crystals per draw when exchanging all Insignias for crystals.

Rune Factory still has a pity mechanic, but because the counter resets whenever you receive any Rune Insignias, reaching the full guarantee is extraordinarily unlikely.

### Buying Crystals with Gems

Rune Factory also provides three Energy Cores for 1,000 Gems.

At the published average drop rate, this means approximately 19.65 Dragon Crystals per 1,000 Gems, or roughly 5,090 Gems per 100 expected crystals.

That is slightly less efficient for Dragon Crystals alone than the current Theia's Roulette calculation.

However, Rune Factory remains attractive because its shop contains other valuable rewards, including Dragon Essences, Holy and Shadow Immortal progression materials, and other rare items.

Players who need several different progression materials may therefore find Rune Factory particularly useful.

For details, see our [Updated Rune Factory Guide](https://ik-wiki.com/posts/updated-using-rune-factory-to-buy-shadow-and-holy-immortals/).

## VIP Shops, GTArcade Rewards & Dragon Bundles

Outside recurring events, there are several additional opportunities to collect premium Dragon Crystals.

**VIP Points Shop:** Holy Dragon Crystals have historically been available at VIP 15, with 20 crystals costing 3,000 VIP Points. This can be useful for players with accumulated VIP Points, although the opportunity cost is substantial.

**Mystery Pearl Shop:** Shadow Dragon Crystals have historically been available for 15 Mystery Pearls per 50 crystals, subject to the relevant account requirements. Mystery Pearls are valuable, so this isn't necessarily an efficient purchase.

**GTArcade Rewards:** Certain monthly rewards and Points Gift Packs have offered batches of 500 Holy or Shadow Crystals. These are worth checking, particularly for players who already participate in GTArcade reward programs. Availability and eligibility may vary.

**Dragon Knight and Light & Shadow Bundles:** Both provide direct crystal purchases. The Light & Shadow bundles have also included Dragon Essences, which can improve their overall value for players developing their Talent Trees.

These sources are useful for supplementing progression, but their prices, stock limits, and availability should be checked against the current shop before purchasing.

## Can You Collect Holy and Shadow Crystals for Free?

Yes, although free progression is extremely slow compared with the quantities needed for complete upgrades.

The most reliable recurring opportunities are the free spins in Theia's Roulette, free Rune Factory entries, and purchasing additional attempts using Gems earned through ordinary gameplay.

If both events continue on their published weekly schedules, three free Roulette spins provide approximately 66 Dragon Crystals per week on average. Three free Rune Factory draws add an expected equivalent of about 20 more crystals, assuming the Rune Insignias are exchanged for crystals.

That works out to approximately **86 Dragon Crystals per week from free event entries**, before Gem spending, promotions, or other rewards.

These averages assume that the event schedules, free-entry quantities, and reward tables remain unchanged.

Over time, that adds up. But compared with a requirement approaching 300,000 crystals, it becomes obvious why completing a premium dragon solely through free entries is an extremely long-term project.

For F2P players, the most practical strategy is to combine free entries with carefully planned Gem spending, while taking advantage of any additional crystal rewards that become available.

## Which Event Offers the Best Value for Spenders?

This is where things become particularly interesting.

Historically, Rune Factory was considered one of the most efficient ways to purchase Holy and Shadow Dragon Crystals. However, the August 2026 update significantly improved Theia's Roulette.

Using the published drop rates and efficient small-pack prices, the comparison currently looks like this:

Theia's estimate uses tickets purchased at approximately $0.50 each, while Rune Factory assumes Energy Cores costing around $0.33 each.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-094647-7shh8v.png)

These prices represent modeled efficiency under the published small-pack offers, not guaranteed current purchasing prices. Purchase limits, regional pricing, discounts, and additional rewards can all affect the result.

Theia's Roulette appears to provide better direct crystal value under these assumptions, but Rune Factory retains an important advantage in flexibility. Players can exchange its currency for other progression materials when Dragon Crystals are no longer their priority.

We will cover the complete cost comparison, purchase limits, direct bundles, and best spending routes in a separate, dedicated IK-Wiki value guide.

## Which Dragon Should You Prioritize?

The choice between Holy and Shadow should depend primarily on the march you're developing.

**Lucasta, the Holy Dragon**, offers healing, defensive support, and additional utility that can work well in a broad range of formations.

**Melanthios, the Shadow Dragon**, provides offensive pressure and disruption, including its distinctive Shadow mechanics, making it particularly interesting for certain PvP compositions.

Both can be powerful, but neither is a good investment simply because you happen to have some spare crystals.

Because upgrades require such enormous quantities, players should decide which dragon contributes most to their main march before investing heavily.

When spending your crystals, develop the important basic skills first, then balance Talent Tree progression against affordable Portrait upgrades. Early Portrait levels can be cost-efficient, while key Talent nodes may offer more impactful combat bonuses.

## Final Thoughts – Make Every Crystal Count

Holy and Shadow Dragon Crystals remain among Infinity Kingdom's most difficult progression materials to collect.

Fully developing a premium dragon requires hundreds of thousands of crystals, so completing one is a major long-term investment even for regular spenders.

Fortunately, the acquisition options have improved considerably.

Theia's Roulette now provides a direct route with an expected return of around 22 crystals per spin, while Rune Factory offers regular access to crystals through Rune Insignias and a flexible selection of alternative rewards.

For ordinary players, the best approach is to claim all available free entries, save Gems for efficient event opportunities, and avoid spending scarce currencies on crystals that won't support their primary march.

For spenders, **start with the most efficient recurring event purchases before considering expensive direct bundles**, but always check the current prices and purchase limits.

Above all, remember that these dragons are long-term investments. You don't need to max every skill, talent, and Portrait level immediately to gain meaningful combat benefits.

Choose your dragon, prioritize the upgrades that matter most, and make every crystal count.



### Further Reading

* [Theia's Roulette – Pricing and Probability Guide](https://ik-wiki.com/posts/theias-roulette---pricing-chance-calculations-and-more/)
* [Rune Factory – Updated Mechanics and Value](https://ik-wiki.com/posts/updated-using-rune-factory-to-buy-shadow-and-holy-immortals/)
* [Dragon Portrait Upgrade Costs](https://ik-wiki.com/posts/upgrade-costs-of-dragon-portraits/)

title: Holy w. Bathony & Charles
summary: This guide is part of my article series on holy builds. If this build is not to your likeing, have a look at the rest of my builds on the lightning build page. I have multiple builds for any taste available, IB, PvE…
markdown:
This guide is part of my article series on holy builds. If this build is not to your likeing, have a look at the rest of my builds on the lightning build page. I have multiple builds for any taste available, IB, PvE, arena/ToS builds and F2P/cheap builds.

**This article is on holy as an off-march (2nd or 3rd)**

**Why not run holy main?? Because we are taking advantage of how natively strong the holy Immortals and Bathony is. With a minimum of ToK passives, we are able to create a powerful setup. Holy Immortals and Bath do scale like every other Immortal, but no where near as much! I.e. improving ToK passives on an earth march makes a much bigger difference than on holy. Thus, when we need a 3rd for Arena or Throne, this march enables us to have 3 extreemly strong teams instead of 2.**

***This is an example of this build in action: Holy-bath-Charles build which will wreck any other second or third march. It even kills some mains at equal power!***

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/image-1024x473.png)

## How does it work?

This setup is pretty simple, we use whatever ToK skills we have left after building our first and second teams and watch these powerhouses of Immortals beat the living **** out of even solid main march armies.

We abuse **Manco**, **Bath**and **Gilga's**superior ultimate abilities to deal massive damage. Moreover, we use **Charles**here, because **his shield is the strongest healing spell in the game.** It is impossible to counter, as wounds dosen't work and Peter is waaaaaaaay too slow.

## ToK passive setup (3rd march)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/Skaermbillede-2022-08-01-204758-1.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/unknown-1.png)

**You want to run this passive loadout:** Remember that this is what I have left, what you have left will do fine too! Remember that the green passives are surprisingly strong. Also blues like **silence**and **rage**also perform well.

Above you see two examples of how to run this build. It all depend on the ToK passives you have left after filling main and second march. The great thing about holy tho, is that because of Manco, you can stack dodge like no other march and actually make very good use of dodge grace and misleading aura (passives not of highest value anywhere else).

This is just what I have left, you can pretty much run this team with anything and it will perform!

title: Honor Ranking Buffs 101
summary: In Infinity Kingdom, honor buffs play a crucial role in enhancing your gameplay by providing significant advantages through the honor ranking system. Each of the three kingdoms of Norheim has its own set of honor ranks…
markdown:
In Infinity Kingdom, honor buffs play a crucial role in enhancing your gameplay by providing significant advantages through the honor ranking system. Each of the three kingdoms of Norheim has its own set of honor ranks, meaning there are three positions in total per server for each rank, making the competition for these spots fierce.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-21-1024x570.png)

### Understanding Honor Buffs

Honor buffs are obtained as you climb the honor rankings within your kingdom. These rankings are not only a measure of prestige but also a source of powerful buffs that can increase your troop count, strength, intelligence, agility, physique, and aptitude by a percentage. The higher you are on the ranking, the more substantial the buffs you receive, which can significantly impact your power and performance in the game.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-22-1024x558.png)

### Competition and Strategy

The competition for honor rankings is intense, as each rank has a limited number of spots. For instance, there can only be one Prince, one Archduke, and one Duke, with the number of spots increasing as you go lower in the ranking list. Achieving a higher rank requires not just accumulating honor but also outmaneuvering other players who are vying for the same positions.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-23-1024x435.png)

### Maximizing Honor Buffs

To maximize the benefits of honor buffs, players should adopt strategic approaches, such as allocating their strongest fighters across the honor ladders of different kingdoms. This strategy ensures access to a broader range of buffs, providing strategic advantages in battles and wars. Key steps include evaluating your alliance's strengths, planning for kingdom allocation, and securing and maintaining honor rankings through active participation in kingdom activities.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-24-1024x532.png)

The power of honor ranking buffs lies in their ability to make your armies more resilient and versatile. Achieving high honor rankings and strategically utilizing the buffs can tilt closely contested battles in your favor, making your force a formidable opponent on the battlefield.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-26.png)

For detailed strategies on maximizing honor ranking buffs and understanding the intricate mechanics behind the honor system in "Infinity Kingdom," consider exploring resources and guides available on platforms like ik-wiki.com, which offer comprehensive insights into leveraging these buffs for individual and alliance-wide success​​​​.

By carefully positioning your most critical fighters within the honor ladders of various kingdoms and harnessing the power of honor ranking buffs, you can significantly enhance your competitive edge in "Infinity Kingdom." This nuanced strategy not only maximizes individual prowess but also strengthens your alliance's collective might, paving the way for dominance in the world of Norheim.

title: How does Initial Occupation Rewards work?
summary: Understanding one of the most misunderstood reward systems in Legion of Frostborne
markdown:
*Understanding one of the most misunderstood reward systems in Legion of Frostborne*

If you’ve ever participated in **Legion of Frostborne** (KvK) or other large-scale server events, you’ve seen the **“Initial Occupation Reward”** pop up when cities, citadels, or gates are captured. But here’s the thing — many players, especially on younger servers, are still unclear about how these rewards actually work.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-81.png)

Do you have to be in the **top 10 contributors** to earn them? Do you need to be in the **winning alliance**? Or do you just need to **tag the city once**?

Let’s break it down clearly because these rewards are **massive** — and understanding them will make you rethink how you approach city sieges.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-82-1024x625.png)

---

## What Are Initial Occupation Rewards?

Whenever your alliance captures a **city, citadel, or gate** for the first time in Legion of Frostborne, the game grants **Initial Occupation Rewards**.

These rewards typically include:

- **Millions of resources** (scaled by city level)
- **Gold**
- **Gems**
- **Occasionally, speedups or other special items**

For example, **capturing a Level 13 City** in Frostborne rewards each participant:

- **22M mixed resources**
- **1.3M gold**
- **200 gems**

That’s for **every single player who contributed — not just the top 10**.

---

## Who Gets the Rewards?

Here’s where the confusion comes in.

**Do you need to be in the top 10?**
**No.**

**Do you need to do a ton of damage?**
**No.**

**Do you need to be in the winning alliance?**
**Yes — but only during the siege.**

**So how do you qualify?**
**Anyone who sends at least one march to hit the city while it’s being captured gets the reward.**

That’s it.

If your alliance successfully takes the city, and you sent **even a single march**, you’ll receive the full Initial Occupation Reward.

---

## Why This Is a Big Deal

The beauty of this system is that **small players, free-to-play users, and even alts can benefit enormously**.

- **F2P Growth Boost:** For a low-level castle, getting **22M resources + 1.3M gold + 200 gems** just for tagging a city is huge.
- **Alt Farming:** Many players use their alt accounts to tag cities for easy resources, helping them keep up with main-account growth.
- **Alliance-Wide Value:** It encourages every member to participate in city sieges, making teamwork more rewarding.

---

## How to Maximize These Rewards

1. **Always Tag the City**
Even if you can’t do much damage, **send at least one march** to every city your alliance is capturing. Don’t sit idle.
2. **Join All Major Sieges**
Make a habit of joining sieges for **gates, citadels, and high-level cities** — the bigger the city, the bigger the reward.
3. **Use Your Alts**
If you have alt accounts in the same alliance or kingdom, **send their marches too**. It’s free resources and gems for accounts that need them most.
4. **Coordinate with Alliance Leadership**
Ask your R4/R5 when sieges are happening so you don’t miss out.

---

## TL;DR – The Quick Version

- **Initial Occupation Rewards** go to **any player who sends at least one march** to help capture a city.
- **It’s not just for the top 10 contributors.**
- **Huge for small players and alts:** A Level 13 city gives **22M resources, 1.3M gold, and 200 gems** each.
- **Always tag cities** during sieges — it’s free, easy, and worth it.

---

## Final Thoughts

This is one of the **most efficient ways to farm resources and gems** in Infinity Kingdom, especially in Legion of Frostborne. Whether you’re a top-tier spender or a F2P grinder, there’s **no excuse not to tag every city your alliance goes for.**

It’s free growth — don’t leave it on the table.

title: How Forced Impeachment works
summary: A practical guide to understanding activity status, voting requirements, and why many impeachment attempts fail.
markdown:
## Introduction

*A practical guide to understanding activity status, voting requirements, and why many impeachment attempts fail.*

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-34-1024x596.png)

Forced impeachment is one of the least understood alliance systems in *Infinity Kingdom*. The game does provide instructions in the alliance interface, but the wording leaves several important mechanics unclear—particularly how the game defines **“active members”** and which players actually count toward the vote.

Most failed impeachment attempts happen because alliances calculate the numbers incorrectly. Players often assume the vote is based on **total alliance size**, when the game actually calculates participation using **activity status categories**.

This guide explains the system clearly, focusing on the most confusing points:

- What counts as an **active member**
- Which members **can vote**
- How the **80% participation rule** works
- How **winning votes are calculated**

The explanations are based on in-game text and observed behavior tested by alliances.

---

## Who Can Start a Forced Impeachment

Only alliance members with the following ranks can initiate a forced impeachment:

- **R4 (Officer)**
- **R5 (Alliance Leader)**

Without an R4 or R5 initiating the process, the impeachment vote cannot begin.

---

## Activity Status — The Most Important Mechanic

Every player in an alliance is automatically assigned an **activity status** based on their recent login behavior.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-35-1024x573.png)

The game uses four activity categories:

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-36-1024x245.png)

### Key Rule

**Only Silent members are excluded from the impeachment system.** All other statuses count as **active members**.

This means the impeachment system calculates participation using: **Hyper + Active + Present**

Silent accounts are completely ignored.

---

## How the 80% Voting Requirement Works

For impeachment to succeed, **at least 80% of active members must vote**.

Active members are defined as:

```
Hyper + Active + Present
```

Silent members do not count toward the total.

### Example

Alliance size: 100 members

Status distribution:

- Hyper: 20
- Active: 30
- Present: 25
- Silent: 25

Active member pool:

```
20 + 30 + 25 = 75 active members
```

Required voters:

```
75 × 0.80 = 60 votes required
```

If fewer than **60 players vote**, the impeachment automatically fails.

---

## Why “Present” Players Cause Confusion

Many community explanations incorrectly claim that **only Hyper and Active players count**. Testing and in-game behavior show this is incorrect.

**Present members do count as active members and can vote.**

This has two important consequences:

1. Present players **increase the total active member count**
2. They **raise the 80% voting requirement**

For example: If many players are “Present,” the alliance must gather **more votes** to reach the 80% threshold.

---

## Winning the Vote — The 50% Rule

After the participation requirement is satisfied, the game checks the **majority condition**.

The candidate must receive: **More than 50% of the votes cast.**

Example: Votes cast: 60

Winning threshold: More than 30 votes

A candidate must receive **31 votes or more** to become the new leader.

---

## What Happens If Conditions Are Not Met

The system checks three failure conditions when the voting period ends.

Impeachment fails if:

### 1. Less Than 80% Participation

If fewer than **80% of active members vote**, the impeachment is invalidated.

The current leader remains in position.

---

### 2. No Candidate Reaches 50%

If both candidates receive **less than 50% of the votes**, the leader stays unchanged.

---

### 3. Tie Vote

If both candidates receive the **same number of votes**, the current leader remains.

---

## When the Vote Ends

The voting process ends when **one of two things happens**:

1. **All eligible members vote**
2. **The voting timer expires**

If everyone votes early, the result is calculated immediately.

---

## Player Strategy and Practical Observations

From a practical alliance management perspective, the impeachment system is less about raw alliance size and more about **controlling the active member pool**.

Experienced alliances often pay attention to:

- The number of **Silent members**
- The number of **Present members**
- Coordinating voting to reach the **80% threshold**

Because Silent members are excluded from calculations, alliances sometimes remove or relocate inactive players before starting impeachment.

Similarly, alliances that control many **active accounts** can reliably meet the participation requirement and control the vote outcome.

---

## The Core Formula

When calculating whether impeachment will succeed, alliances only need two numbers.

### Active Member Pool

```
Hyper + Active + Present
```

### Required Votes

```
Active Members × 0.80
```

### Winning Votes

```
More than 50% of votes cast
```

---

## Conclusion

Forced impeachment in *Infinity Kingdom* follows a straightforward system once the activity rules are understood.

The most important detail is how the game defines **active members**.

Active members include:

- **Hyper**
- **Active**
- **Present**

Only **Silent members are excluded**.

From this active pool:

- **80% must participate in the vote**
- The winner must receive **more than 50% of the votes**

Understanding these mechanics allows alliances to correctly calculate their voting requirements and avoid failed impeachment attempts caused by incorrect assumptions about alliance size or activity status.

---

title: How Legion of Frostborne Evolved into a More Competitive Battlefield in 2026
summary: Legion of Frostborne has changed considerably since its early Conquest seasons. Some improvements, such as the Federation system and revised matchmaking criteria, were introduced through official updates. Others have…
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-84-1024x519.png)

## Introduction

Legion of Frostborne has changed considerably since its early Conquest seasons. Some improvements, such as the Federation system and revised matchmaking criteria, were introduced through official updates. Others have happened more quietly, without much explanation from the developers.

One of the biggest changes has been the gradual shift toward fewer, but much more populated, KvK worlds.

While this adjustment was never prominently documented, veteran players quickly noticed the difference. Modern Legion of Frostborne seasons consistently place more active alliances into the same battlefield, creating wars that feel larger, more competitive, and far less predictable than they did a few years ago.

Looking back, it's one of the best changes the mode has received.

---

## The Early Days of Legion of Frostborne

Older Legion of Frostborne seasons were spread across a much larger number of separate KvK worlds.

Instead of concentrating servers into a handful of competitive battles, the matchmaking system created many individual worlds running simultaneously. Although this allowed more KvKs to take place at once, it also spread active alliances much more thinly.

Most battlefields followed a familiar pattern.

One alliance—or occasionally two—stood well above everyone else in terms of activity, organisation, and spending. Once those alliances established control of the map, the outcome often became predictable.

Many cities were captured with little resistance, major objectives were secured early, and large parts of the map became relatively quiet as the season progressed.

There were certainly memorable wars during this period, but they were the exception rather than the rule.

---

## A Quiet Change to Matchmaking

At some point, the matchmaking landscape began to change.

Without any major announcement, the number of active Legion of Frostborne worlds appeared to decrease. Instead of creating many smaller KvKs, the game began grouping more active servers into fewer battlefields.

Whether this was a direct adjustment to matchmaking or part of broader improvements behind the scenes, the result was immediately noticeable.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-83-1024x483.png)

Every KvK suddenly felt busier.

Instead of encountering one dominant alliance supported by several weaker ones, it became increasingly common to see multiple established alliances competing within the same world.

For players who enjoy large-scale warfare, this completely changed the character of Legion of Frostborne.

---

## More Powerhouses, Fewer Easy Victories

Perhaps the biggest difference is the quality of competition.

In the past, a dominant alliance could often dictate the pace of an entire season. Once they secured the central objectives, there were relatively few opponents capable of mounting a serious challenge.

Today's KvKs rarely feel that straightforward.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-85-1024x540.png)

A single battlefield can now contain several highly organised alliances spread across multiple factions. Each of those alliances brings experienced leadership, active members, and enough strength to influence the outcome of the war.

Winning no longer comes from simply having the strongest alliance.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-86-1024x567.png)

Success depends on outperforming several strong opponents over the course of an entire season.

---

## Every Stage of the War Feels Active

One of the biggest improvements is the overall pace of Legion of Frostborne.

Because more active alliances share the same battlefield, there is much less downtime. Border conflicts continue throughout the season. Cities remain contested. Major objectives attract genuine competition instead of becoming routine captures.

Even after the initial expansion phase, there are usually multiple fronts where meaningful battles are taking place. From my experience, modern KvKs simply feel alive for much longer than they did under the older format.

---

## Diplomacy Has Become More Important

The increased level of competition has naturally placed greater emphasis on diplomacy.

When every faction contains several capable alliances, coordination becomes just as valuable as military strength. Strong alliances still need to work together, agree on city ownership, and coordinate attacks against rival factions. Internal disagreements are much more costly when every opponent is capable of exploiting them.

The most successful servers are rarely the ones with the highest power alone. More often, they're the ones that organise effectively before the map even opens.

---

## A Healthier Competitive Environment

The modern format has also given more alliances meaningful roles throughout the season.

Older KvKs often revolved around a single dominant alliance while everyone else played a supporting role. Today, multiple alliances contribute to capturing cities, defending territory, reinforcing allies, and contesting key objectives. Success is spread across a larger part of the server rather than resting on one group of players.

That makes Legion of Frostborne feel less like a showcase for a few powerhouse alliances and more like a genuine server-wide war.

---

## Looking Back

No matchmaking system will ever produce perfectly balanced KvKs, and some worlds will always be stronger than others.

Even so, the gradual shift toward fewer, larger Legion of Frostborne battlefields has been one of the most positive developments the game has seen.

More active alliances now compete within each world, creating longer campaigns, more meaningful diplomacy, and far more opportunities for large-scale PvP. Instead of spending weeks waiting for the next major battle, players are far more likely to find action throughout the season.

The developers may never have officially highlighted this change, but its impact is difficult to miss. Legion of Frostborne has become a more engaging, more competitive, and ultimately more rewarding experience because of it.

---

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-129-1024x497.png)

#### Understanding the Event Mechanics

In this thrilling event, players use dice to navigate around a special board, collecting points to unlock rewards. The main prizes to eye are the Chaos Selection Chests and Fu Fei fragments, requiring 1500 and 3500 points, respectively.

### Points Accumulation:

- **Flag Points:** Each purple-marked flag you pass grants you 10 points.
- **Start Bonus:** Circling back to the start nets you an additional 20 points.

**To reach the 1500-point milestone** for all Chaos Selection Chests:

- You'll need an**estimated 184 dice**, calculated as 1500 points divided by 70 points per round, then multiplied by 8.6 dice per round.

**Aiming for the full 3500 points** to claim all Fu Fei fragments:

Securing 220 dice for a mere $20 not only propels you towards achieving the 80 Chaos Selection Chests but also demonstrates the unparalleled value offered by this event. This approach is highly recommended for players looking to significantly enhance their strategic options without breaking the bank.

The 3rd Anniversary Dice Event in Infinity Kingdom offers a blend of strategy, luck, and potential for significant gameplay advancements. Whether you're a dedicated F2P player or willing to invest a bit for exponential gains, this event is your golden ticket to unlocking powerful rewards. So, roll wisely, strategize smartly, and may the dice fall in your favor!

title: How Owl Guardian actually works - scaling off of base stats
summary: Owl Guardian is one of those talents that most experienced players default to, especially in builds centered around ultimate skill damage. The talent choice is on the same line as attack speed, so for some players this…
markdown:
### Introduction

Owl Guardian is one of those talents that most experienced players default to, especially in builds centered around ultimate skill damage. The talent choice is on the same line as attack speed, so for some players this will be entirely irrelevant.. however for the many out there relying on energy regen understanding precisely how Owl Guardian works is important! Most players already lean toward energy regen because it benefits every immortal, while attack speed only shines in specific normal-attack builds.

**However, the real value of Owl Guardian is often misunderstood because the tooltip is inaccurate.** What it actually scales from is not your *current* Energy Regen stat, but something more fundamental. That is what this article will be all about!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-39-1024x463.png)

---

## The Core Mechanic: Base Energy Regen Scaling

After testing and comparing multiple immortals across different stat ranges, the pattern becomes clear: **Owl Guardian increases Energy Regen by 5% of the immortal’s *base* Energy Regen — not their total stat after bonuses.** Personally this came as a surprise for me, given how for example boost levels I would think where cooked in as flat value increases. I know that is surprising to many, so lets take a bit of a closer look at preciesly what scaling off of base energy regen means.

### What “Base Energy Regen” Means

Each immortal has a default, built-in Energy Regen value before:

- Tech bonuses
- Lord talents
- Boost levels
- Equipment
- etc.

Owl Guardian ignores all of those modifiers and only applies its bonus to this base value.

---

## Verified Examples

### Low Base Regen Immortal (Baldwin)

- Base Energy Regen: **66**
- 5% of 66 = **3.3**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-33-1024x754.png)

My Baldwin with boost levels and tech, etc. has 78.5 with Owl Guardian that gets to → 81.8. Not a 5%, instead a gain of **+3.3** **equal to 5% of his base energy regen** before any modifiers or boosts (66 x 0.05 = 3.3).

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-38-1024x799.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-37-1024x811.png)

The increases line up perfectly once you calculate from base instead of total.

---

### High Base Regen Immortals (e.g. Hippolyta, Empress Wu, Qin)

These immortals share a key trait:

- Base Energy Regen: **100**
- 5% of 100 = **5**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-34-1024x717.png)

Despite my Empress Wu being at 115 without Owl Guardian she only gets to 120 when the talent is active. Again this lines up with 5% of her default base energy regen value of 100.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-35-1024x744.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-36-1024x749.png)

---

## Why the Tooltip Feels Misleading

The game shows Energy Regen as a final, combined stat, but Owl Guardian does not use that value in its calculation.

So when players see: “Energy Regen +5%”, they naturally assume the **current energy regen attribute shown on immortal page** **× 1.05**

But the real formula is: **Base Regen × 1.05 → then added to your total** through other modifiers and increases.

That difference is what causes lower-than-expected gains on upgraded immortals.

---

## Conclusion Summary

Owl Guardian does not scale from your total Energy Regen stat.

**It scales from base Energy Regen only.**

- Low-base immortals gain ~3–4 Energy Regen
- High-base immortals (100 base) gain exactly +5
- Buffs, tech, and gear do not increase the talent’s value

While the tooltip suggests a universal 5% increase, the actual behavior is **+5% of base Energy Regen, added on top of your total stat**

Even with this limitation, Owl Guardian remains the most reliable and widely applicable choice for most builds, because faster ultimate access consistently outweighs the niche benefits of attack speed.

---

markdown:
### Legion of Frostborne KvK Rewards: avoid getting stuck without rewards

The Legion of Frostborne KvK (Kingdom vs. Kingdom) rewards have significantly evolved with the recent patch, introducing a pivotal change that allows players to convert Skill Stones into Cinders. This currency exchange is monumental, especially for free-to-play (F2P) gamers, as it unlocks the potential to acquire powerful Triss skills by purchasing Legion of Frostborne skill stones. However, navigating this newfound opportunity requires strategy to avoid pitfalls that could hinder your progress.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/image-14-1024x475.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/image-15-1024x530.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/image-10-1024x347.png)

**The Currency Exchange Mechanism:** The option to sell Skill Stones for Cinders has revolutionized the way players approach the game's economy. By participating in Legion of Frostborne events and using Cold Coin in the shop or gems in the KvK chests, players can now invest in skill stones. These stones, once deemed surplus or unnecessary, can be sold for Cinders, granting access to a range of potent Triss skills previously out of reach for many F2P players.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/image-11-1024x530.png)

**A Crucial Caution:** While the mechanism to sell Skill Stones is a game-changer, a legacy mechanic from before this update presents a significant challenge. Once a skill is fully unlocked, its corresponding Skill Stones become inaccessible for purchase or acquisition. This means that completing all Legion of Frostborne skills can effectively block your ability to generate more Cinders through Skill Stone sales, leaving you in a potentially stagnant position without the means to acquire new Triss skills.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/image-12-1024x592.png)

**Strategic Spending:** To circumvent this obstacle, it is essential to adopt a strategic approach to managing your Skill Stones:

1. **Reserve at Least One Skill:** Always keep at least one of the Legion of Frostborne skills from reaching completion. This approach ensures a continuous flow of Skill Stones that can be sold for Cinders. "Stormeye" is recommended as the skill to hold back due to its relatively lower utility compared to other skills available in the Legion of Frostborne roster. However, player preferences and strategic needs might vary, so choose the skill that best suits your long-term goals while having the least immediate impact on your gameplay effectiveness.
2. **Sell, Don't Use, Selected Skill Stones:** For the skill you've chosen to never fully unlock, consistently sell the Skill Stones associated with it. This tactic is vital for maintaining an ongoing source of Cinders.
3. **Evaluate and Adapt:** Player needs and game dynamics can change. Regularly assess whether the skill you've chosen to withhold aligns with your evolving strategy and the broader game environment. Flexibility and adaptability are key to maximizing the benefits of this approach.

**Conclusion:** The recent updates to Infinity Kingdom offer groundbreaking opportunities for players to enhance their arsenals with powerful skills, significantly leveling the playing field for F2P participants. By carefully managing Legion of Frostborne Skill Stones and employing a strategic approach to spending Cold Coin and gems, players can avoid common pitfalls and fully leverage the rewards available through KvK participation. Remember, strategic foresight and judicious resource management are your best tools in navigating the evolving landscape of Infinity Kingdom.

title: How to beat Amplify

markdown:
### Mastering the Challenge: A Guide to Dominating the Time Rift Breaker Boss - Amplify

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-84-1024x572.png)

Greetings, valiant commanders! In our relentless pursuit through the Time Rift, today's focus is on the fearsome adversary known as Amplify. Unlike the previous boss, Venom, who showered us with continuous magical damage, Amplify opts for a different approach—delivering colossal physical blows in a few decisive strikes. In this guide, we'll unravel the intricacies of Amplify's tactics, weaknesses, and share strategies to maximize your damage potential.

## Amplify's Mechanics:

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-85-1024x265.png)

Amplify specializes in dealing massive physical damage, primarily targeting your front-left tanking Immortal. His energy skill, Furious Bite, inflicts substantial damage, but the real threat lies in its 20% damage increase per active buff, potentially doubling the damage output. Furthermore, Furious Bite may trigger Crush, an immensely powerful ability activated after specific conditions are met, posing a severe threat to your Immortals.

## Weakness Exploitation:

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-86.png)

Amplify is susceptible to Fire, Water, and Earth damage, offering a 25% damage boost when exploiting weaknesses. While weaknesses play a crucial role, the deciding factor for success lies in adapting your strategy to counter the boss's mechanics effectively. Fire builds are particularly advantageous against Amplify, making Alexander Khubilai and Hippolytta a potent combination.

## Control Tactics:

In a surprising turn of events, control strategies are rendered ineffective against Amplify. The boss seems entirely immune to control effects, making Loki builds less effective this week. Remove instigation, root, and similar effects from your builds, and focus on alternative strategies.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-87-1024x559.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-88-1024x580.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-89-1024x611.png)

## Proven Strategies for Amplify Showdown:

1. **High Energy Regeneration:** Equip Immortals like Hippolytta and Khubilai Khan with high energy regeneration to enhance offensive capabilities.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-90-1024x443.png)

1. **Utilize Single Target Damage Skills:** Optimize your physical damage-dealing frontliners with combo and other single-target damage skills for maximum impact.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-95-1024x603.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-94-1024x600.png)

1. **Exploit Weakness Crits:** Always leverage weakness to gain a consistent high crit rate, amplifying the effectiveness of each hit.

title: How to beat Vampirism
summary: In this guide, we will examine the Rift Breaker Boss named Vampirism, exploring his abilities and strategies for achieving the most significant hits possible. In our previous guides, we delved into Venom and Amplify –…
markdown:
### Conquering Vampirism: A Comprehensive Player Guide

In this guide, we will examine the Rift Breaker Boss named Vampirism, exploring his abilities and strategies for achieving the most significant hits possible. In our previous guides, we delved into Venom and Amplify – two bosses that are complete opposites.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-1024x463.png)

With Vampirism, we encounter a unique boss that balances continuous damage and high burst damage, without being immune to control but not particularly weak to it either. Unfortunately, defeating this boss requires a considerable investment in pay-to-play skills and setups, along with very high power to outscale the damage output. Personally, it is my least favorite of the three bosses.

## Firstly, let's cover the basics

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-1.png)

Vampirism possesses an active skill and two passive skills to engage in battle. Its active skill, 'Super Spiderweb,' inflicts massive Magical Damage to enemies while absorbing health equal to 50% of the damage dealt. Despite my attempts to test wounds against this effect, I did not observe any healing negation. However, wounds debuffs are worth further investigation for future encounters with Vampirism. Please try this out yourself and share your results!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-3-1024x608.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-2-1024x590.png)

In addition to the active burst skill, the boss has a passive skill called 'Counterattack.' This ability poses a significant threat as it counters the high damage output required for a boss-killing build. The boss cannot regenerate passive energy, but every time it takes damage, it gains energy.

Once it reaches 300 energy, it uses Torment, inflicting additional damage on your team.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-4-1024x549.png)

Consequently, setups like Alexander Berserk, Wind Rage, Combo, and Wind Rage + Adrenaline Rush regen builds are not effective due to the high frequency of damage instances, causing setups to rapidly self-destruct. To counter this, focus on building more damage into attacks rather than increasing attack speed. For example, on Alexander, consider using Anger or even Duel Master over some attack speed-boosting skills.

**Weaknesses: Shadow, Lightning, Wind**
While exploiting weaknesses for an added 25% damage is beneficial, it is not the sole determinant of what works best. The weakness to lightning can be advantageous if wounds prove effective, but using lightning requires a Charles to avoid quick demise. Although a leech shadow team might work, I have not witnessed any build achieving sustained power high enough to combat Vampirism as effectively as Holy Energy Shield builds.

## Control strategies

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-5-1024x302.png)

Control strategies can be effective against Vampirism. Stuns, roots, and confusion effects can mitigate incoming damage. However, achieving awe-inspiring results with control builds is challenging, and luck plays a significant role, especially with perfect confusion procs around important skill triggers. Loki holies are top-tier for this boss. While I experimented with Instigation builds, I found the value to be lacking compared to running other defensive or offensive buffs on my support Immortals.

## What you should be doing:

There are numerous spider-killing builds, and my setup is continually evolving. However, some fundamentals remain consistent:

- Running high energy regen on Immortals like Hippolytta and Khubilaikhan provides substantial offensive capability. Note that Wind-Rage regen builds are weaker on this boss than on others, but you may still want to use them for the additional damage. Be aware that you will need to enhance offensive capacity with more sustain due to triggering more regen effects with increased damage instances to the boss.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-7-1024x590.png)

- Utilize combo and other single-target damage skills on your physical damage-dealing frontliners. While Combo still yields good results, consider running it in combination with Anger instead of Wind Rage to maximize damage per hit.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-6-1024x240.png)

- Always apply Weakness. Bosses have relatively low resistance, and with weakness, you gain a consistently high crit rate, crucial for maximizing damage.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-8.png)

- Incorporate defensive strategies. Against Vampirism, shield effects are essential due to continuous damage. Charles is an MVP Immortal for this boss fight. Additionally, tower of knowledge skills like Energy Shield and Jade Barrier are potent against Vampirism.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-9-1024x407.png)

- Regarding Life-Link + Absolute Defense combos, this is recommended against Vampirism. While it yields better results than against Venom, it has less impact than against Amplify. The boss deals considerable damage to your tank Immortal, but the main threat is the AOE damage. This combo is strong enough to be recommended, and I achieved varying results in battles. I also experimented with an Assist + Absolute Defense + Life-Link combination on my tank, which worked well, but the usefulness of Assist depends on your build and backline reliance.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-11-1024x384.png)

- This week, prioritize defensive ToK skills such as Resist over control slots. This allows for more damage boons instead of control, but also necessitates prioritizing defense and sustain over some offensive capacities used in Amplify builds.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-13.png)

- **The best defenses against Vampirism include:**  - Charles, the Earth tank Immortal, due to powerful shields.
- Life-Link + Absolute Defense on your tank.
- Resist, a powerful effect against Magical Damage.

Note that dodge rate and attack speed reductions are almost worthless for this boss. Additionally, Hippolytta is ineffective for Vampirism, as her ability to remove energy is useless against this boss.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-12.png)

## Here are my notable builds for Vampirism

- Khubilaikhan – Alexander – Qin – Zeno builds still top my list with 97.6M damage. However, they are noticeably weaker due to the high attack speed of the build, making it challenging to sustain the damage being dealt back.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-14.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-15-1024x590.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-16-1024x591.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-17-1024x590.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-18-1024x598.png)

- I experimented with a holy pure build, achieving decent results with 79.7M damage. However, this setup required removing Khubilaikhan from the earth team. I then changed it to a Himiko-Alexander-Charles-Zeno earth team, which performed well with Charles's exceptional sustain, achieving 78.4M damage.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-23.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-19-1024x591.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-20-1024x596.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-21-1024x584.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-22-1024x570.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-24.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-25-1024x582.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-16-1024x591.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-27-1024x569.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-18-1024x598.png)

- My fire build performed poorly, as expected, with 35.9M damage hits. Fire lacks sustain, leading to troop losses and reduced damage output. If fire or lightning is your main in PvP combat, it's advisable to use them for bosses as well, running Charles and considering swapping out Hippolytta this week for better sustain.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-29.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-30-1024x589.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-33-1024x573.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-34-1024x587.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-32-1024x569.png)

- None of my attempts came close to the whale holy setups. A holy team achieved top ranking on my server with 188M damage, showcasing the boss's reliance on raw power and healing capability. With a maxed Theo, energy shield, Vitality Touch, and Spring of Life, these builds can sustain high troop counts for extended periods, allowing low single-target builds to still deal significant total damage.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-35-1024x382.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-36-1024x580.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-37-1024x576.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-38-1024x572.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-39-1024x571.png)

I can only imagine what the biggest holy whales can achieve on this boss if they tried hard for it. Definitely not a F2P or light spender friendly boss.

### Infinity Kingdom Guide: Conquering the Time Rift Breaker Boss - Venom

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-63-1024x564.png)

## Understanding Venom's Tactics:

Venom, the Time Rift Breaker Boss, poses a significant threat with frequent Magical Damage to all enemies. Additionally, his Dark Harvest ability inflicts massive damage once your Immortal accumulates 2 stacks of Venom.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-64-1024x227.png)

To maximize your success against Venom, you must carefully plan your strategy and capitalize on his weaknesses.

## Exploiting Weaknesses:

Venom is particularly vulnerable to Holy, Lightning, and Fire damage. While Holy and Lightning perform admirably, Fire can lack sustain and succumb quickly to continuous damage.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-66-1024x401.png)

If opting for a Fire-based strategy, ensure sustainability to withstand Venom's onslaught. Remember, exploiting weaknesses is beneficial, but a robust overall build is crucial for success.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-65-1024x516.png)

## Optimal Team Compositions:

While exploiting weaknesses is advantageous, certain builds prioritize immense single-target damage over weaknesses.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-68-1024x266.png)

Consider a lineup like Khubilai-Alex-Qin-Zeno for exceptional results, relying on Alex's potent single-target damage.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-67-1024x485.png)

## Incorporating Control Strategies:

Controlling Venom is paramount for achieving high scores. Stuns and confusion are particularly effective.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-70-1024x513.png)

Utilize Immortals with Instigation or Loki (for advanced players) for powerful control. Stuns grant additional fighting time and interrupt abilities, while confusion prevents the boss from hitting your Immortals, reducing damage to zero.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-69-1024x455.png)

## Essential Tips for Venom Showdown:

1. **High Energy Regeneration:** Equip Immortals like Hippolytta and Khubilai Khan with high energy regen to enhance offensive capabilities.
2. **Strategic Skill Usage:** Employ combo and single-target damage skills on physical damage-dealing frontliners for maximum impact.
3. **Defensive Maneuvers:** Prioritize defensive skills like Berserk, Resist, and healing abilities to maintain troop count and stabilize damage output.
4. **Utilize Instigation:** Incorporate Instigation for crucial confuse procs, significantly impacting the damage dealt to Venom.
5. **Embrace Weakness:** Always exploit Venom's weakness. Use Weakness for a consistent high crit rate, enhancing each hit's value. Blessing of War is essential for maximizing initial damage when troop counts are high.

Here are my most recent builds. Like I said, I am always changing these and I will likely not use Blessing of Defense on my next run at Venom, since it seems low value against a boss that deals continuous damage like Venom. However, most of what I have going here seems to work pretty well.
