markdown:
## Introduction

The Hunting Festival has returned to Norheim for May 2026, bringing another seasonal event built around Token of Light progression, Eternal Grails, and cooperative milestone rewards. Structurally, the event is very similar to previous seasonal festivals, though this version introduces the new **Throne of Blood** castle skin and a cooperative progression system through the **Hunting Feast** tab.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-69-1024x543.png)

For experienced players, the event is mainly about efficient grail acquisition and long-term Chaos immortal progression. For newer or mid-game accounts, the value comes from maximizing free Token of Light income, coordinating feast participation properly, and avoiding inefficient spending traps.

The event includes eight primary tabs:

1. Lucky Koi
2. Throne of Blood
3. Ingredient Hunt
4. Hunting Feast
5. Dazzling Wish
6. Grail Shop
7. Glorious Challenge
8. Pinnacle Trial

Below is a full breakdown of each section, including where the real value sits and which areas deserve priority.

---

## 1. Lucky Koi

The Lucky Koi tab works almost identically to previous festival versions. Purchasing a **Koi Gift Pack** enters you into the recurring lottery for a large Eternal Grail jackpot every two days.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-70-1024x554.png)

### Koi Gift Pack Rewards

Each purchase includes:

- 5 Tokens of Light
- Gems
- VIP Points
- Participation in the 4,250 Eternal Grail lottery

In addition, purchasing five Koi packs during the event grants an extra **850 Eternal Grails**.

From a pure efficiency perspective, the Koi pack remains one of the strongest direct grail-value purchases in the game. If your account is actively progressing Chaos immortals, especially expensive immortals like Tengu or future artifact upgrades, the grail-per-dollar efficiency is difficult to beat.

Players also receive one free Token of Light daily from this tab. It is minor individually, but over the full event duration it contributes meaningfully toward additional Dazzling Wish spins.

---

## 2. Throne of Blood

This is the event battle pass section.

Like previous festivals, there is both a free reward track and a premium reward track.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-71-1024x528.png)

## Free Track Rewards

The free track mainly provides:

- 30 Tokens of Light
- Standard progression resources

## Premium Track Rewards

The premium pass includes:

- 120 additional Tokens of Light
- Gems
- Large quantities of Gem Meat
- The Throne of Blood castle skin

The important detail here is the amount of Gem Meat included. Compared to earlier seasonal passes, the raw Token of Light count may look similar, but the Hunting Feast system dramatically**increases the total effective value.**

If your feast group contributes evenly, the extra Gem Meat effectively converts into significantly more Tokens of Light, Soul Crystal Chests, and Philosopher’s Offer Chests.

## Throne of Blood Castle Skin Analysis

The new skin provides:

- 5% Troop Attack
- 5% Technology Speed

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-72.png)

The troop attack bonus immediately places this among the strongest combat-oriented castle skins currently available.

In practice, troop attack scales better than immortal stats because it scales off of troop count to much greater values.

### Comparison to Abyssal Throne

Many late-game players will compare this skin directly with Abyssal Throne.

- **Abyssal Throne** offers troop attack plus reduced death rate.
- **Throne of Blood** offers troop attack plus technology speed.

From actual gameplay experience, Abyssal Throne still has slightly better wartime sustainability because reduced death rate saves resources during prolonged fighting.

However, the 5% technology speed bonus on Throne of Blood is extremely relevant because technology tends to remain one of the final long-term progression bottlenecks even for highly developed accounts.

For players still heavily progressing research, this skin has real long-term value beyond appearance alone.

## Battle Pass Progression

Progression is handled through standard daily quests.

Quests include:

- Troop training
- Arena battles
- Well of Time
- Market purchases
- Pinnacle Trial
- Glorious Challenge
- Gnome bosses

You can afford to miss a small number of tasks, but consistent daily completion is strongly recommended if you want full value from the pass.

---

## 3. Ingredient Hunt

Ingredient Hunt is the event’s 2048-style minigame.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-73-1024x542.png)

Mechanically, it works almost identically to previous puzzle events. Players merge ingredients into higher-tier dishes while progressing through increasingly valuable reward tiers.

## Main Rewards

The most important rewards are:

- Gem Meat
- Festival Insignia progression
- Small amounts of Eternal Grails at higher tiers

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-74-1024x520.png)

The real value here is the Gem Meat. Because Hunting Feast rewards scale so well, every free piece of Gem Meat matters. Even fully free-to-play players can accumulate meaningful feast progression simply by maximizing their Ingredient Hunt attempts.

The Eternal Grail rewards at the highest tiers are useful, but noticeably less generous compared to some earlier 2048 event versions.

## Should You Buy Extra Attempts?

In most cases, no.

If you are exceptionally good at this game, you can max it without and if you are not, you are most likely not going to see the big lobster rewards anyway.

For most players, the better approach is:

1. Use all free attempts
2. Maximize Gem Meat income
3. Convert that value through Hunting Feast progression

If you play the mode consistently every day, the cumulative rewards become surprisingly solid even without spending.

---

## 4. Hunting Feast

Hunting Feast is the most important tab of the entire event.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-75-1024x530.png)

Players invite two partners and collectively spend Gem Meat to progress through shared milestone rewards.

## Major Rewards

The reward pool includes:

- Large quantities of Tokens of Light
- Soul Crystal Chests
- Philosopher’s Offer Chests
- Speedups
- Additional progression resources

The overall value here is extremely high.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-76.png)

## Coordination Matters

This event heavily rewards balanced participation.

The best setup is usually:

- Three players with similar spending levels
- Similar activity levels
- Shared expectations before starting

One of the biggest mistakes players make is joining random feast groups where contribution expectations are unclear.

## Spending Strategy

Buying Gem Meat can be relatively efficient compared to directly purchasing Tokens of Light, but only if:

- Your group is active
- Both parties contributes
- You actually reach meaningful milestone tiers

Note that for some, you may have a whale friend who does not mind carrying you. In that case, you naturally do not need to buy anything but instead thank the kind person for carrying your feast! Efficiency of bundles assume equal participation...

This is the event section I would prioritize above almost everything else during the event.

Even lower-spending accounts can gain substantial value simply by coordinating properly with alliance members. In previous cooperative seasonal events, the players who planned participation ahead of time consistently gained far more value than players spending impulsively.

---

## 5. Dazzling Wish

Dazzling Wish remains the standard Token of Light spin system.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-77-1024x545.png)

Players spend Tokens of Light for chances at Eternal Grails.

## Grail Drop Rates

- 0.45% → 300 Grails
- 1.55% → 50 Grails
- 3.5% → 25 Grails
- 12% → 5 Grails
- 82.5% → 1 Grail

## Expected Value

Over large sample sizes, the average value remains approximately: **1 Token of Light ≈ 4.2–4.3 Eternal Grails**

---

## 6. Grail Shop

The Grail Shop is where event currencies convert into permanent account progression.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-78-1024x524.png)

## Eternal Grail Costs

### Immortals

- Tengu → 750 Grails
- Fu Fei → 450 Grails
- Athena / Wukong / Loki / Poseidon → 250 Grails

### Artifacts

- Tengu Artifact → 1050 Grails
- Most Chaos Artifacts → 1000 Grails
- Fu Fei Artifact → 600 Grails

## General Priority Advice

Since there is no major new immortal release pressure this event, most accounts should focus on efficient long-term Chaos development.

### Mid-Spender Perspective

For many mid-spenders:

- Daily 250-grail immortals
- Fu Fei purchases

...often provide the best long-term efficiency.

Moving into the 750-grail tier is a larger commitment because those immortals generally require continued investment through future events and artifact progression.

## Challenge Shop

The Challenge Shop uses Feathers earned through Glorious Challenge.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-79-1024x547.png)

Important purchases include:

- Stardust
- Unique Artifacts
- Tokens of Light

## Smart Feather Management

Do not spend all gem-ticket resources immediately.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-80.png)

Hard Mode unlocks later during the event, and many players regret exhausting their ticket economy too early.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-81.png)

## Player Perspective

Personally, I almost always prioritize Stardust because opportunities to accumulate meaningful quantities remain relatively limited.

After that, remaining currency usually goes toward Tokens of Light for additional grail progression.

---

## 7. Glorious Challenge

Glorious Challenge consists of:

- Normal Mode
- Hard Mode

Normal Mode opens immediately, while Hard Mode unlocks later during the event.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-82-1024x556.png)

## Rewards

Players earn:

- Feathers
- Gem Meat
- Gems
- Tokens of Light

This mode is simple mechanically, but skipping daily clears significantly hurts event efficiency (you get 5 daily free tickets that cannot carry over into other days).

Raiding gives smaller returns than first clears, but you will need to raid a few Normal camps to make sure you use the daily stock in the feather-shop for the items you most desire based on current account progression (e.g. artifacts vs stardust vs tokens).

Again, careful management of gem-ticket purchases matters if you want enough currency available for Hard Mode progression.

---

## 8. Pinnacle Trial

Pinnacle Trial features stronger enemies with one-time daily attempts.

## Main Rewards

- Random Chaos immortal fragments
- Tokens of Light
- Gem Meat
- Festival Insignia progression

## Do Not Miss Daily Attempts

Missing days here is one of the easiest ways to lose free event value.

Even accounts that cannot fully clear every stage should attempt progression daily.

## Difficulty Advice

Some later stages can become surprisingly difficult depending on account development.

If you struggle:

- Adjust skill compositions
- Experiment with march positioning
- Ask alliance or Discord communities like the ik-wiki community for tested setups

Often small composition adjustments matter more than raw power.

---

## Conclusion Summary

The May 2026 Hunting Festival is one of the stronger seasonal events we have seen recently because multiple systems overlap efficiently.

The combination of:

- High-value cooperative rewards
- Strong Token of Light generation
- A genuinely useful castle skin
- Consistent Chaos progression

...makes this an event worth taking seriously even for players who normally spend conservatively.

For free-to-play players, the key is maximizing daily participation and finding reliable feast partners.

For spenders, the best value comes from combining Koi efficiency, battle pass rewards, and coordinated Hunting Feast progression.

Most importantly, avoid wasting resources early in the event without planning around Hard Mode unlocks and cooperative milestones. Good coordination matters just as much as spending during this festival.

---

title: Hybrid Water featuring Qin and Alex (v2.8.3)
summary: In the ever-evolving Infinity Kingdom meta, seasoned players continue to discover unconventional builds that challenge expectations. One such unique composition comes courtesy of player Bunga, brought to our attention…
markdown:
In the ever-evolving Infinity Kingdom meta, seasoned players continue to discover unconventional builds that challenge expectations. One such unique composition comes courtesy of player Bunga, brought to our attention by the always insightful Batman. This hybrid Water setup drops the traditional Artemisia/Dido + Bjorn/Attila core and instead incorporates Emperor Qin and Alexander, creating a two-damage-dealer strategy that has shown great promise in Conquest Season.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-94-1024x498.png)

This build is something player **Batman**was kind enough to direct my attention to, and I have only ever seen player **Bunga**running this setup. In this guide we are going to look at Bungas results and build and make some recommendations as to how to improve it even further.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-93-1024x498.png)

Let’s break down the reasoning, structure, and optimizations behind this build—and explain why it might just be the most efficient and underrated water hybrid team available today.

---

## Overview of the Build

The team lineup:

- **Merlin** (Core AoE magic burst)
- **Emperor Qin** (Support, wounds debuff, early energy/damage via talents)
- **Ragnar** (Debuff tank and essential ToK skill carrier)
- **Alexander** (Secondary physical DPS)

This build differs from standard water compositions in two big ways:

1. **Qin** replaces Artemisia/Dido as the support backliner. Why? Because Qin is far easier to max in talents giving early access to support buffs at much lower cost. He also brings **wounds** and **attack speed**, which synergizes with Alexander’s burst potential.
2. **Alexander** joins the water march not for elemental synergy, but to rapidly reduce enemy frontliner troop count. This is especially useful against high-impact single-target damage dealers like Tutankhamun, who rely on surviving long enough to ramp damage.

The classic water core of **Merlin + Ragnar** remains untouched, as their roles in burst damage and damage mitigation are irreplaceable.

---

## Why This Build Works

- **Qin's Talents and Utility**: Maxing out Emperor Qin is surprisingly cheap, yet he delivers top-tier support buffs from the Immortal Talent Tree. His wounds effect cripples healing-based teams and his unique artifact boosts attack speed for the team, helping Alex reach very high damage outputs right out of the gate without needing any ramp-up.
- **Alexander as Physical Burst DPS**: Alex is a top-tier early game physical damage dealer, and thanks to Ragnar's artifact change (adding a physical damage debuff), Alex's effectiveness rises even higher. In this hybrid setup, he acts as a flanker and burst tool to eliminate dangerous frontliners.

- **Double Damage Dealer Pressure**: Many setups aim to protect and amplify one star damage dealer. This build splits the burden between Merlin and Alex, creating a less predictable march and making enemy targeting and defense harder to manage.
- **Cost-Effective Progression**: Artemisia and Bjorn are expensive to max. This setup uses easier-to-access immortals and still achieves impressive performance metrics.

---

## Recommended Tower of Knowledge Skill Setup

### Original Bunga Setup:

- Merlin: Spell Disintegration, Poison Thorn, Annihilation
- Qin: Berserk, Vitality Touch, Oaken Guard
- Ragnar: No Escape, Weakening Curse, Weakness
- Alexander: Cleave, Assist, Combo

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-89-1024x498.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-90-1024x498.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-91-1024x498.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-92-1024x498.png)

### Recommended Optimization:

- **Merlin**: Annihilation, Spell Disintegration, Fighting Master  - *Why*: Annihilation is amazing damage and Spell Disintegration stack magic debuffs. Fighting Master is essential for control immunity, especially when Qin’s talent boost puts Merlin at highest troop count making him get hit 100% of the time by enemy Himiko's controls.
- **Qin**: Berserk, Oaken Guard, Assist  - *Why*: Berserk synergizes well with Alexanders attack speed based damage output. Assist protects Merlin and ensures he stays alive to cast multiple ultimates. Oaken Guard gives team durability.
- **Ragnar**: No Escape, Weakening Curse, Weakness  - *Why*: The classic water-support tank setup. All skills chosen for utility and debuffing.
- **Alexander**: Cleave, Death Breath, Combo  - *Why*: Death Breath adds AoE support in combination with Cleave while Combo gives him strong single-target output. Control immunity from his unique artifact keeps his DPS consistent.

*Check out my other water guides for more details on tower of knowledge skill interactions in water builds:*

[Season 2 Water Build (v2.8.3) - Wiki & Tools | Infinity Kingdom](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/elements/water/season-2-water-build-v2-8-3/)
[Water build for Conquest Season (v2.8.3) - Wiki & Tools | Infinity Kingdom](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/elements/water/water-build-for-conquest-season-v2-8-3/)

---

## Strategic Considerations

- **Fighting Master** vs. Concentration: If you're facing shadow teams or other control-heavy marches, Fighting Master is mandatory. Merlin becomes the top troop count due to Qin’s support talents, making him vulnerable.
- **Weakness**: Essential for amplifying crit rate, particularly important for Merlin’s burst capabilities. Skipping this weakens the overall build.
- **Malice**: Still a strong option if you're facing high-crit teams, though not needed in every match.
- **Misleading**: Can be added if you're up against hybrid or physical burst teams and can stack enough dodge to make it effective.

---

## Summary

This Emperor Qin + Alexander Water Hybrid build is one of the most refreshing and cost-efficient Conquest meta teams we’ve seen to date. Offering dual-damage output, powerful utility, and strong defensive synergy, it's an especially appealing build for mid-spenders or players seeking more from their water march without unlocking or maxing expensive immortals like Bjorn or Artemisia.

Thanks again to player Batman for the tip and to Bunga for the innovative strategy. With the right ToK setup and immortal talents, this hybrid water comp can outperform many more "meta" compositions—at a fraction of the cost.

title: Ignite (2.8.1)
summary: Absolutely! Here's a polished and structured blog-style guide for the new Tower of Knowledge skill Ignite, introduced in Infinity Kingdom patch 2.8.1.
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-147-1024x452.png)

Absolutely! Here's a polished and structured **blog-style guide** for the new *Tower of Knowledge* skill **Ignite**, introduced in **Infinity Kingdom patch 2.8.1**.

---

## Ignite Skill Guide – Tower of Knowledge (Patch 2.8.1 Update)

## Introduction

Patch **2.8.1** brought us several new Tower of Knowledge skills, and in this guide, we’ll take a closer look at **Ignite** — a **magic-based passive** that boosts an Immortal’s **magical attack attribute** by a **flat amount** rather than by a percentage.

While this might not sound groundbreaking at first, Ignite introduces **a new way to scale your damage**, and depending on the build, level, and Immortal, **it can outperform older skills like Wisdom**—especially on **lower-level or secondary magic users**.

---

## What Does Ignite Do?

> **Ignite (Level 1)**
> ➤ Increases an Immortal's **magical attack by 1800** (flat value)

- Unlike **Wisdom**, which increases **magical attack by up to 60%**, Ignite adds a **fixed 1800** to the magical attack stat.
- This may sound simple, but it opens up **new optimization paths**, especially for **lower-level mages**, **secondary teams**, and **players in early to mid seasons**.

---

## Ignite vs. Wisdom – Which is Better?

### 🔍 Key Comparison:

- **Wisdom**: Increases magical attack by **up to 60%**
- **Ignite**: Adds a **flat 1800** magical attack

💡 **When does Wisdom overtake Ignite?**
To break even with Ignite’s 1800 boost, an Immortal would need:

> ### 3000 magical attack × 60% = 1800

So, if your Immortal has **more than 3000 base magical attack**, **Wisdom will outperform Ignite**. If they have less than 3000, **Ignite is more effective**.

---

## Real Game Example:

- **Level 40 Season 1 Mage (e.g. Wu)**: Usually **well over 3000 magical attack**, so **Wisdom (or Concentration)** is preferred.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-148-1024x565.png)

- **Level 32 Medb**: Has only **1579 magical attack**, so: Wisdom: 1579 × 60% = **947** Ignite: Flat **1800**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-150-1024x707.png)

In this case, **Ignite is nearly twice as strong as Wisdom**!

---

## How Does Ignite Stack with Wisdom?

At the time of writing, it's **unclear whether Ignite and Wisdom stack fully or overwrite each other**, but initial observations suggest **they do stack**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-151.png)

🧪 **Testing is ongoing**, and if you’ve confirmed it one way or the other, feel free to comment or reach out—**community input is always appreciated**.

---

## When Should You Use Ignite?

### ✅ Ideal Use Cases:

- **Early game mages** before they reach high magical attack values
- **Secondary or tertiary teams** with lower-level Immortals
- **Flexible builds** that lack access to percentage scaling skills like **Concentration**
- **Budget builds** where you're saving purple crystals or slotting affordable passives

---

### ⚠️ When to Avoid:

- On **maxed-out or well-geared mages** where **Wisdom or Concentration** offers greater value
- In **late game builds** where every percentage of scaling matters
- If you already have **two or more strong damage-boosting passives** in place

---

## Ignite vs. Other Magic Skills

| Skill | Type | Value | Best Used On |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ignite | Flat stat | +1800 Magic Attack | Early/low-level mages |
| Wisdom | Percent-based | Up to +60% Magic Attack | Mages with 3000+ base magic atk |
| Concentration | Percent-based | +30% Magic Damage Output | Best-in-slot for main mages |

Note that Concentration most always wins, as pure damage modifier is superior to attribute value which is only part of the equation. **[See more here.](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/tower-of-knowledge-passives/all-passives/concentration-versus-wisdom-magic/)**

---

## Final Thoughts & Verdict

**Ignite** may not be revolutionary, but it **fills an important niche** in the current Tower of Knowledge lineup:

- **Early game-friendly**: Raw stat boosts are often more impactful early when base attributes are still low
- **Budget-friendly**: Easy to use on side teams or less optimized marches
- **Flexible**: Can be used temporarily until better scaling skills become available

### 🔥 Verdict:

> **“Ignite is a valuable skill for newer or low-attribute Immortals. It shines in early game and supports second/third teams. However, it gets outclassed by percentage-based skills in the late game.”**

---

## TL;DR – Ignite Skill at a Glance

| 🔹 Category | 🔸 Rating |
| --- | --- |
| Skill Type | Magic – Flat Attribute Boost |
| Best Use | Early game, alt teams |
| Strengths | Consistent, strong early output |
| Weaknesses | Falls off late game vs % scaling |
| Stack with Wisdom? | Possibly – still testing |
| Final Rating | ⭐⭐⭐⭐☆ (4/5 for early game) |

---

title: Illusion Battlefield Beginners Strategy Guide: Relocations, Tower
markdown:
![](/uploads/illusion-battlefield-strategy-guide.png)

## Plan Your Opening Around Positioning

Before the battle begins, decide which objectives your alliance intends to contest and assign responsibility for each area. Every player should know their opening destination, their relocation marker and the commander they follow.

Then consider starting positions. Players with favourable spawns can secure important spaces before the enemy arrives. Use those advantages when assigning the frontline around a tower, rather than distributing players purely by power or sending everyone wherever numbers appear lowest.

Your strongest attacker may be valuable in several areas. A player who can win a critical relocation race has an immediate job that someone starting farther away may be unable to perform.

[More on relocation here.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Wtqq975VxP4)

### Place Precise Relocation Markers

Markers should identify an exact position, allowing players to follow the plan with minimal adjustment. Align them with the bottom-left corner of the intended relocation footprint and check that friendly relocations do not overlap.

Prioritize positions close enough to support the objective and one another. A castle established next to a tower can help reinforce it, challenge nearby enemies and deny space to incoming relocations. An isolated castle farther away may struggle to contribute before its teammates come under pressure.

Prepare a fallback assignment as well. Players whose opening relocation fails should report the situation and receive a useful next move quickly.

## Treat Relocation Denial as a Core Job

Blocking or destroying an enemy relocation prevents that player from establishing their intended position. It can remove an attacker, delay reinforcements or stop the opponent from surrounding your tower.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261020-152154-6fppzi.png)

Assign players to watch incoming relocations while others organize rallies and prepare the objective fight. If everyone focuses on attacking the nearest enemy castle, important arrivals can go unchallenged.

The immediate goal is to create a local numbers advantage. Six players who successfully establish themselves can control an area against a larger group whose arrivals are repeatedly blocked or destroyed.

Once an enemy foothold is removed, occupy the useful positions it leaves behind. Otherwise, the opponent may return to the same area and rebuild its presence.

## Use the Central Tower to Support Your Wider Strategy

The Central Tower combines high scoring value with a location that supports movement toward other objectives. Controlling it provides points and a useful base for reinforcing battles elsewhere.

This matters when players need to replace teammates who have been forced out. A group established near the center can often respond more efficiently than players committed to a distant outer tower.

Your center allocation should fit the wider plan. Decide how many players are needed to establish control, who will remain to defend and who can rotate once another objective needs help.

If you concede the center, you need a realistic scoring alternative. That usually means securing enough other objectives quickly and preventing the opponent from using its central position to challenge them. A plan that depends on several captures must account for the time needed to achieve all of them.

### Release Players From Secure Objectives

An uncontested tower rarely needs the same commitment as a tower under sustained pressure. Once an objective is secure, reassess who needs to remain and who can contribute elsewhere.

Keep suitable coverage and make sure you surround your objectives before giving specific players new responsonsibilities. 

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261020-152300-fy32mi.png)

Avoid leaving a large group waiting at a safe objective while another group loses a contested position.

The same principle applies at the center. Its usefulness as a staging area depends on players being ready to move when needed.

## Defend the Tower and the Castles Around It

A tower defense depends on the players supporting the garrison. If the enemy removes your nearby castles, reinforcement becomes harder and the opponent gains better access to the objective.

Maintain positions that allow teammates to reinforce one another, challenge incoming relocations and organize rallies. Protect the players doing that supporting work, including those carrying useful capture skills.

### Replace Weakened Frontline Players

Watch Prosperity before a frontline castle is close to being forced out. A weakened player who moves behind teammates can continue helping with rallies and garrisons, while a healthier player takes the exposed position.

Coordinate the swap. The replacement needs a clear destination, and both players must avoid obstructing friendly relocations. Waiting until the frontline player is removed gives the enemy a better chance to occupy the space first.

Keeping players established around the objective preserves your options. A defender who remains nearby can contribute to the next exchange instead of spending time returning from elsewhere.

### Create an Opening Before Repeating a Capture Attempt

If both alliances can continually interrupt occupation, sending more marches into the same situation may produce little progress. Identify the enemy positions that allow those interruptions and coordinate pressure against them.

Controlling an additional side of the tower improves access and can make it harder for defenders to respond quickly enough. Coordinate the push so newly arriving players have support rather than leaving isolated castles around the objective.

Once a workable opening exists, call the capture attempt clearly. Troop arrivals and support skills such as **Quick Occupy** should be coordinated around the same attempt.

## Attack the Enemy’s Supporting Positions

A defended tower is harder to take when the opposing backline can organize rallies and reinforce teammates without coming under pressure.

Identify which castles sustain that defense. Depending on the situation, removing a support player or cutting off an arrival route can create more progress than repeatedly attacking the tower from one direction.

Approaching from additional sides can force defenders to divide their attention, but the arriving players need enough support to survive. Surrounding the objective with isolated, vulnerable castles gives the enemy opportunities to remove them individually.

Each group should understand its immediate job: establish a position, block arrivals, remove a particular castle or support the capture. That gives commanders a way to judge whether the attack is progressing.

## Know When to Reinforce and When to Withdraw

A failed opening does not justify abandoning an objective automatically. It does require a new assessment before committing more players.

Identify what reinforcements would change. Can they secure a position, remove an exposed enemy or help complete the occupation? If they are likely to repeat the same failed approach, use them where they can contribute sooner.

Withdrawing can preserve players for a more useful fight or allow a coordinated return later. Communicate the new assignment so the group moves together instead of returning individually to the lost position.

### Defending to Buy Time

An objective can remain worth defending even when eventually losing it is likely. If holding it delays a larger enemy force while your alliance scores elsewhere, the defense may still contribute to victory.

Make that purpose clear. Players assigned to delay should understand how long they need to hold and when they should leave. Their success is measured by the time and points gained for the alliance.

## Organize Rotations and Home Defense

A rotation is the reassignment of players from one area to another. The receiving commander should know where they can arrive and what they are expected to do.

Specify the number needed, the destination and the immediate task. Leave named players responsible for the objective being vacated.

Short calls are easier to follow during a fight:

* “Tower 1 is secure. Four players follow the center markers.”
* “Stop relocating to Tower 4. Reinforce center.”
* “Block the incoming relocation south of the tower.”
* “Home tower needs two defenders. Others hold position.”

### Keep Home Defense Responsive

Assign enough coverage to spot an invasion and contest its first arrivals. The number required depends on the threat, your defenders and how quickly help can reach them.

A small guard preserves players for contested objectives only when it is actively monitoring the area and has a realistic reinforcement plan. Report incoming relocations before the enemy establishes several castles nearby.

You can also keep a few players available for changing assignments. Give them useful work near positions from which they can respond, and avoid committing every available player to a distant fight at the same time.

## Let the Scoreboard Guide Your Decisions

As the match develops, review the score difference, current scoring rates and remaining time. Capturing a tower helps only if its rewards can still affect the result.

If your current holdings are sufficient to win, consider the risk before moving defenders away to pursue another objective. If you are behind, identify which change in control would close the gap and concentrate on making that change possible.

A late capture can come after the opportunity to recover has already passed. Equally, a tower held for most of the match may have done its job even if the enemy eventually takes it.

Reassess after every major capture, lost objective or rotation. Tell each group whether its current task is to capture, defend or delay, and keep that instruction tied to the score.

## Common Mistakes to Avoid

## A Practical Plan for Alliance Leadership

**Before the battle**, confirm attendance, assign commanders and prepare opening markers. Coordinate strategy skills and give each group a fallback assignment.

**During the opening**, check who actually establishes a position. Adjust allocations around successful arrivals rather than assuming every assigned player reached their destination.

**As objective fights develop**, protect supporting castles, replace weakened frontline players and coordinate capture attempts. Release players from secure objectives when another area offers a more useful job.

**In the final phase**, make the scoring plan explicit. Every group should understand what it needs to hold, capture or delay for the alliance to win.

## Final Thoughts

Good Illusion Battlefield leadership keeps players useful throughout the match. That means securing positions, preventing enemy arrivals and moving reinforcements while they can still change the outcome.

The most practical improvements are habits your alliance can repeat: precise markers, clear local command, earlier replacement calls and a willingness to change assignments when a position collapses. Build those into your preparation, then review which decisions cost you time after each match.

## Recommended guides for further reading

* [Basic Positioning in Illusion Battlefield](https://forum.gtarcade.com/topic/177361)
* [Illusion Battlefield Battle Strategy Skills](https://forum.gtarcade.com/topic/176526)
* [ARC versus SJ: Match Analysis](https://forum.gtarcade.com/topic/262399)
* [BUNS versus HOT: Match Analysis](https://forum.gtarcade.com/topic/262432)

title: Illusion Battlefield Talents Guide – Best Skills, Builds & Alliance Strategy
markdown:
![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261020-174141-tu72hc.png)

## How Do Illusion Battlefield Talents Work?

Before entering an IB match, every player selects one of three Battle Strategy talent trees:

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261020-172547-qpixds.png)

* **Offensive:** Focuses on combat, rallies, and rapid repositioning.
* **Defensive:** Focuses on survival, healing, and defending important positions.
* **Support:** Focuses on capturing towers, disrupting enemy occupation, and relocation speed.

Each tree contains four abilities powered by Energy, which regenerates automatically and accumulates faster when actively participating in combat.

Importantly, **you cannot change your selected talent tree once you enter the battlefield**. Alliance leaders should therefore coordinate their players' selections before the match begins.

## Offensive Talents – Attack and Reposition

Offensive talents are designed for players who need to fight aggressively, lead attacks, or relocate quickly between objectives.

### Which Offensive Skills Matter Most?

**Teleport is the standout ability.** It gives players the flexibility to relocate to another objective without paying the normal teleport cost.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261020-172558-e885mv.png)

This is particularly valuable when your alliance needs to reinforce a distant tower, organize an unexpected attack, or recover from a failed opening.

**Hold Fast** is another useful option, particularly for strong players involved in sustained fighting. Its 10% damage reduction can make a meaningful difference when defending against powerful opponents.

Comrades and Grievous Wound are more situational. Although additional rally damage and wounded troops can be useful, spending Energy on them may delay access to Teleport.

**Our recommendation:** Offensive players should generally prioritize saving Energy for Teleport, using Hold Fast when immediate survival is more important than another relocation.

Offensive talents are particularly suitable for strong, mobile players who can lead attacks and respond quickly to changing battlefield conditions.

## Defensive Talents – Survive and Hold Towers

Defensive talents focus on keeping players alive, reducing healing costs, and buying time for reinforcements.

For many alliances, these are the most universally useful talents.

### Why Defensive Talents Are So Valuable

The biggest advantage of Defensive talents is their ability to keep players fighting for longer.

In Illusion Battlefield, being eliminated from an important tower position can be much more damaging than simply losing troops. An alliance that loses its surrounding castle positions may struggle to reinforce or defend the objective.

**Resurrection** is particularly powerful because it can prevent a player from being removed when their Prosperity reaches zero, provided the ability is active.

This creates opportunities to delay enemy advances until reinforcements arrive.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261020-172614-6f86sj.png)

**Healing** is another excellent skill, especially for players who expect heavy combat. Restoring wounded troops directly reduces the need for healing speedups.

**Sturdy** provides additional Prosperity recovery, while Undying offers temporary protection.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261020-172624-b4jxfk.png)

One interesting mechanic is that garrisoning a tower does not remove the **Undying** barrier. This makes it especially useful when a player needs to remain at a critical defensive position.

**Our recommendation:** Defensive is the safest general-purpose choice for most players, especially frontline defenders, players with limited healing speedups, and anyone responsible for holding important positions.

## Support Talents – Capture Towers and Control Objectives

Support talents are perhaps the most strategically interesting tree because they directly influence how quickly alliances capture objectives. 

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261020-172810-4syn1u.png)

Personally I prefer to play Support Talents because you can make huge impact plays with these talents - Especially Ambush from a stealth-alter and Quick Occupy.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261020-172832-5wbiu8.png)

While Offensive and Defensive talents focus primarily on combat and survival, Support abilities can determine who actually controls the tower.

### Quick Occupy – The Key to Capturing Towers

Quick Occupy is arguably the most important Support ability.

It increases occupation speed, allowing alliances to capture objectives faster.

Even more importantly, **Quick Occupy effects can stack**, meaning multiple Support players activating the ability together can significantly improve occupation speed.

This is why organized alliances assign dedicated Support players to specific towers rather than simply allowing everyone to select talents independently.

When your alliance is ready to capture a tower, Support players should coordinate their marches and activate Quick Occupy at the appropriate moment.

### Sudden Assault – Disrupt Enemy Captures

Sudden Assault provides a chance to reduce the enemy's occupation progress when attacking their troops inside a tower.

Interestingly, the effect can trigger regardless of whether your attack wins or loses.

The original guide suggests using very small marches to repeatedly attack enemy troops while Sudden Assault is active, minimizing the troops risked.

This can be especially useful when you need to delay an enemy capture long enough for reinforcements to arrive.

### Ambush – Faster Relocations

Ambush allows players to relocate much faster, reducing relocation construction time to just one second.

This creates opportunities for surprise attacks or rapid reinforcements.

However, the relocation can still be blocked by enemy players. Its speed does not guarantee that the target position will remain available.

**Our recommendation:** Support players should generally prioritize Quick Occupy when their alliance is actively contesting objectives. Ambush is valuable for coordinated relocations, while Sudden Assault provides another way to delay enemy captures.

## Which Talent Should You Choose?

There isn't one universally correct talent for every player.

The best choice depends on your role within the alliance and the objectives you're assigned to defend or attack. The key is recognizing that talents serve different strategic purposes.

A team consisting entirely of Defensive players may be difficult to eliminate but lack the occupation advantages provided by Support.

An alliance with too many Support players may capture quickly but struggle to survive prolonged fighting.

Meanwhile, excessive Offensive selections can leave important tower positions vulnerable.

## How Should Alliance Leaders Distribute Talents?

Veteran IBL strategy players will all recommend building teams around **a majority of Defensive players, one or two Support players per contested tower, and a smaller number of Offensive players**. This provides a useful starting point for alliance planning. 

For example, a hypothetical 30-player roster might use the following distribution:

This is an illustrative allocation rather than a universal optimal setup. The correct distribution depends on attendance, player strength, objectives, and expected opposition.

The most important part is assigning Support players to the actual towers they are expected to help capture.

If all your Support players are stationed at the same objective, their abilities may be wasted elsewhere.

Likewise, Offensive players should understand when the commander expects them to relocate rather than independently using Teleport whenever available.

### Coordinate Energy Usage

One common mistake is using abilities immediately whenever enough Energy becomes available.

Because more powerful abilities require substantial Energy, spending it on smaller skills can prevent players from activating a strategically important ability later.

For example, an Offensive player who repeatedly uses Comrades may not have enough Energy to activate Teleport when the alliance suddenly needs reinforcements elsewhere.

Similarly, a Support player should avoid spending all their Energy just before the alliance begins a major tower capture.

Good alliance leadership means communicating not only where players should go, but also **when they should activate their talents**.

## Final Thoughts – The Right Talent Mix Wins Matches

Illusion Battlefield talents aren't simply individual combat bonuses. They are strategic tools that should support your alliance's overall battle plan.

Defensive abilities help players survive and maintain control of important positions. Support abilities help capture towers and disrupt enemy occupation. Offensive abilities provide mobility and additional combat advantages when attacking or reinforcing objectives.

For most players, Defensive is the most reliable general-purpose choice.

However, alliance leaders should ensure that every important objective has enough Support coverage and that some players retain the ability to reposition quickly.

**The best alliance isn't necessarily the one with the strongest individual talents. It's the one that coordinates those talents at the right moment.**

Before your next match, discuss talent assignments with your team, identify your dedicated Support players, and make sure everyone understands when their abilities will be needed.

Combined with good positioning, relocation control, and coordinated rotations, proper talent management can make a meaningful difference in competitive Illusion Battlefield.

title: Immortal: Artemisia (Water)
summary: Hey there, fellow Infinity Kingdom player! Today, I want to talk about a new Water-elemental support Immortal named Artemisia. She’s designed to provide both Chill effects and a physical defense debuff on enemies, which…
markdown:
Hey there, fellow Infinity Kingdom player! Today, I want to talk about a new Water-elemental support Immortal named **Artemisia**. She’s designed to provide both **Chill effects** and a **physical defense debuff** on enemies, which makes her a very interesting option for Water teams. In this guide, I’ll explain how her ultimate ability works, how she synergizes with popular Water Immortals like **Merlin** and especially well with **Margaret**. Moreover, we will see how she stacks up against the older Water support, **Dido**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-15.png)

---

### Artemisia’s Ultimate Ability and Synergy

Artemisia’s ultimate ability, **Arctic Storm**, creates a storm in the enemy area that reduces their **physical defense by 30%** and applies a **Chill** effect for 9 seconds. The Chill effect lowers the enemy’s attack speed by 10%. This is important for two reasons:

1. **Reliable Chill Setup**: Water damage dealers like **Merlin** and **Margaret** get massive bonus damage if they strike enemies who are under a Chill effect when they cast their own ultimates. Since Arctic Storm guarantees Chill on all enemies for 9 seconds, you can ensure that Margaret’s or Merlin’s ultimate hits chilled targets—if you time it right.
2. **Physical Defense Debuff**: The 30% physical defense reduction amplifies the damage of any physical-damage Immortal, most notably **Margaret**. Merlin’s damage is magical, so he won’t directly benefit from the defense debuff, but Margaret and your frontline physical fighters certainly will.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-16-1024x419.png)

Artemisia’s **base energy regen of 100** is another key factor. This high regeneration rate helps her cast Arctic Storm quickly and more consistently, making it easier to set up combos with Margaret’s ultimate.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-17.png)

If you use skills like **Adrenaline Rush** to adjust cast timings, you can almost guarantee that Arctic Storm lands right before Margaret unleashes her ultimate.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-18-1024x552.png)

---

### Comparing Artemisia to Dido

Before Artemisia arrived, **Dido** was a go-to support Immortal for Water teams. Dido’s ultimate, **Frost Armor**, lasts for 9 seconds and provides a substantial physical defense boost (2000% of the target’s level), while also granting a **35% chance** to inflict Chill on attackers for 6 seconds.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-20.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-19.png)

1. **Offense vs. Defense**: If you need a sturdy frontline or you’re running a more defensive setup with Immortals like **Ramses**, Dido’s physical defense boost can be a lifesaver. Artemisia, on the other hand, offers an offensive edge by lowering the enemy’s physical defense, letting you rack up more damage from both Margaret in the backline but also e.g. Attila and Herald in the frontline.
2. **Chill Duration**: Dido’s Chill has a lower chance to activate (35%) and only lasts 6 seconds per proc, but because Frost Armor stays active for 9 seconds, you can potentially get multiple procs in a short period. Sometimes the Chill might refresh, stacking your Chill uptime closer to 14–15 seconds total. Artemisia’s Chill is guaranteed for 9 seconds, but once those 9 seconds are over, there’s no immediate chance to reapply it until she can cast again.
3. **Synergy and Timing**: While Dido may provide a more defensive approach and potentially higher total Chill uptime, Artemisia’s guaranteed Chill and physical defense debuff can be far more impactful if timed to match **Margaret’s** or **Merlin’s** casts. If you’re focusing on strong offense and building synergy around Margaret’s physical attacks, **Artemisia** is generally the better pick.

---

### My Opinions and Recommendations

I find **Artemisia** to be an excellent addition to Water teams that focus on damage and control. If you’re running **Margaret** as one of your primary damage dealers, the physical defense debuff will boost her DPS significantly. Meanwhile, the guaranteed Chill effect ensures your Water team’s synergy remains intact, allowing Merlin or Margaret to hit chilled targets for massive burst damage.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-21-1024x564.png)

However, if your Water lineup leans heavily on defensive Immortals and you want more team survivability, **Dido** might still be the better choice. Her Frost Armor can soak up a lot of incoming physical damage, which can be a lifesaver in tougher matchups.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-22.png)

Another factor to keep in mind is **energy regen and timing**. Artemisia’s higher base energy regen (100 vs. Dido’s 83) means she’ll often cast sooner, which can be great if you plan your combos well. Skills that manipulate energy—like Adrenaline Rush—can help you line up Arctic Storm to occur just before Margaret casts. If your Margaret casts first, you’ll lose the Chill synergy for that round.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-23.png)

Lastly, it’s important to note that **Merlin** deals magic damage, so he won’t benefit from Artemisia’s physical defense debuff, but he will benefit from the Chill effect. This makes Artemisia particularly potent in a lineup built more around **Margaret**. If your Water team is Merlin-centric, you can still gain a lot from Dido’s defense and Chill uptime.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-24-1024x601.png)

---

### Summary

Artemisia is a strong offensive support for Water teams, offering a **guaranteed 9-second Chill** and a **30% physical defense reduction** on all enemies. She pairs brilliantly with **Margaret**, enhancing her physical damage, and can also help Merlin land his ultimate on chilled targets. Compared to **Dido**, Artemisia leans more toward offense, while Dido offers a stronger defensive approach with physical defense buffs. Dido can achieve higher overall Chill uptime if her Frost Armor procs repeatedly, but Artemisia’s steady energy regen and guaranteed Chill make her more reliable for **precision combo setups**.

If your Water lineup relies on heavy offense and you’re aiming to maximize Margaret’s damage potential, **Artemisia** is likely the better choice. If you’d prefer a sturdier defense with occasional Chill procs, **Dido** might serve you well. Ultimately, it comes down to how you want your team to perform on the battlefield—whether you prioritize **offense**, **defense**, or a balance of both. Whichever path you choose, both Water supports can shine under the right circumstances, so experiment and see which style fits your playstyle best.

### Immortal Boost Levels – Costs, Milestones, and Smart Priorities

Boost Levels are basically your Immortal’s gym membership: pure stats and combat juice, paid for in gold. And yeah—upgrading them gets **expensive fast**. From level 1 to 30, the costs snowball, so you want to pace it, hit the right milestones, and line things up with your actual marches instead of chasing pretty numbers.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/image-56-1024x525.png)

The good news: you can shave up to **20% off** the gold costs through **Immortal Technology**. The trick is knowing **where to stop**, **who to push first**, and **how to keep alt teams from falling so far behind that they become dead weight**.

---

## Important to know: Boost Levels and the 20% Discount

- Every Immortal can be boosted from **Level 1 → 30**.
- Costs climb hard as you go up.
- **Immortal Technology** can reduce gold costs by **up to 20%**.
- The table below shows **Base Cost** and **Cost w/ Tech (-20%)**, plus the **stat/buff** you unlock at each level.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/image-58-1024x426.png)

### Total Gold (levels 1→30)

- **Base total:** 572,948,663
- **With -20% Tech:** 458,358,930
That’s why planning matters.

---

## Full Cost & Buff Table

| 29 | 75,000,000 | 60,000,000 | +5.0% Resilience, +10 Initial Energy, +2.0% Energy Regen |

| 5 | 3,100 | 2,480 | +300 Troop Number |

| 3 | 1,700 | 1,360 | +3.0% Crit Rate |
| 2 | 1,000 | 800 | +3.0% Dodge |
| 1 | 300 | 240 | +3.0% Accuracy |

## Milestones You Should Care About

While all boost levels provide solid buffs, some are naturally better than others depending on the immortal you’re using. For instance, Crit and Energy are great for mages, while Physical Attack and Accuracy are naturally better for physical damage dealers. However, there are milestone upgrades that make natural stopping points: boost levels 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, and 30 each grant **+300 troops**.

When upgrading your immortals, I’d follow a few rules of thumb. First, prioritize your **main march**. Getting one strong march is super important, and within that march you should prioritize your main damage dealer(s) first, then move on to secondaries. That said, you shouldn’t end up with a main team at boost level 30 while everyone else sits at 0. You do need to prioritize your main, but you should also make sure the rest aren’t falling too far behind. This balance can be tricky.

What works well for me is upgrading in increments based on the troop-count milestones (these are the most impactful level upgrades). For example, as I pushed my main to boost level 30 in Season 2, I kept my second team at 20 and my third and fourth at 15. After finishing 30 on my main, I upgraded all teams I rely on for combat (Arena, Throne, etc.) to level 20. Then I began taking key immortals outside my main up to 30.

### Cumulative Gold to Hit Each Milestone (1 → X)

- **Lvl 5:** 8,500 base | **6,800** w/ Tech
- **Lvl 10:** 258,663 base | **206,930** w/ Tech
- **Lvl 15:** 2,948,663 base | **2,358,930** w/ Tech
- **Lvl 20:** 52,948,663 base | **42,358,930** w/ Tech
- **Lvl 25:** 227,948,663 base | **182,358,930** w/ Tech
- **Lvl 30:** 572,948,663 base | **458,358,930** w/ Tech

So yeah—**20 and 25** are huge commitments. Plan your season around these jumps if you’re aiming for serious PvP benchmarks.

---

## Flex Picks vs. Raw DPS: Choose Your Path

Once you’re figuring out what to upgrade after completing your main immortals, there are generally two ways to approach it. Either upgrade your secondary team’s strongest damage dealers first, **or** upgrade key immortals you might want to swap into your main when you need to counter specific enemies. For example, I’m maxing **Qin** even though he isn’t in my main right now, because having access to **Wounds** to counter a heal-sustain (Holy) player is extremely powerful. Once I finish that, I’ll move on to the damage dealers from my secondary and third marches.

---

## Conclusion Summary

- Boost Levels are **powerful but pricey**—the **-20% Immortal Tech** discount is huge, so unlock it early if you can.
- **Troop milestones (5/10/15/20/25/30)** are the best **stopping points** and make planning way easier.
- **Match stats to roles**: Energy/Crit for mages, Accuracy/Physical% for physical DPS, Resilience/Dodge/DR for tanks.
- **Don’t neglect alt teams**—hit milestones so they remain useful in Arena/Throne/KvK instead of becoming dead weight.
- Use a **mixed plan**: main carry to 30 over time, bring other teams to 15→20, then sprinkle 25/30 where it actually swings fights.

**Bottom line:** Push your main, milestone your backups, and always keep one counter-immortal climbing. That’s how you stay strong now without trashing your long-term gold economy.

title: Immortal Combat Simulation Feature
summary: Patch 2.9.9 introduced a new Immortal Demonstration feature that allows players to watch selected Immortals fight as part of a complete formation.
markdown:
Patch 2.9.9 introduced a new **Immortal Demonstration** feature that allows players to watch selected Immortals fight as part of a complete formation.

At first glance, this is clearly a marketing feature. The game places the newest Immortal inside a carefully selected march and demonstrates that formation defeating an older meta setup. The purpose is not difficult to understand: show players the new Immortal winning, create excitement around the release, and encourage people to obtain it.

That does not make the feature useless, however. Holy, Shadow and especially Chaos Immortals can be extremely expensive to unlock and develop. Being able to watch them perform in a proper battle before investing provides information that a skill description alone cannot offer.

## How to Access the Battle Simulation

Open the Immortal interface and select an Immortal that supports the new demonstration feature. Patch 2.9.9 initially introduced it alongside newer Immortals such as Horus, although more Immortals may receive demonstrations later.

In the bottom-left corner of the Immortal screen, you will see a new **Simulation Combat** icon. Select it to open the demonstration lineup.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-35-1024x549.png)

The game will display the two formations, their Immortals, Dragons and total power before allowing you to begin the **Simulation Challenge**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-36-1024x499.png)

Once the battle begins, it plays like a normal combat replay. This lets you observe the new Immortal’s Ultimate, skill timing, targeting, survivability and interaction with the rest of the formation.

## Why the Feature Is Useful

Immortal descriptions tell us what an ability is supposed to do, but they do not always communicate how that ability feels in a complete battle.

This is particularly relevant for Horus. His passive prevents any individual instance of incoming damage from exceeding a percentage of his maximum HP, while his active skill damages all enemies and can apply Punishment. On paper, this suggests an unusually durable back-row mage that is difficult to remove with concentrated burst damage.

The simulation allows players to see that durability in practice. You can watch how long Horus survives, how frequently he casts, how his damage develops and how his abilities interact with the recommended supporting Immortals and skills.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-32-1024x560.png)

It also gives players an opportunity to inspect a complete suggested formation. Even if you do not intend to copy it exactly, it may reveal useful combinations or help explain what role the developers expect the new Immortal to perform.

That is valuable when developing a premium Immortal can cost hundreds or even thousands of dollars. A demonstration cannot replace genuine player testing, but it is considerably better than making that investment based entirely on a written skill description.

## This Is Mostly Marketing, but It Is Still Useful

The demonstration should not be mistaken for independent balance testing.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-33-1024x465.png)

The new Immortal is placed inside a formation selected by the developers and matched against a specific opposing team. Differences in skills, positioning, Dragon development, attributes and formation power can all influence the outcome. There is also an important matchup issue hidden inside the first demonstration.

In my opinion, this initial preview battle is probably more a case of **Great Tengu countering Ares** than definitive proof that **Horus outperforms Medusa**. The new formation changes more than one Immortal, so we cannot isolate Horus and attribute the entire result to him.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-34-1024x564.png)

Anyway, that is a discussion for another guide entirely!

The wider point is that one demonstration battle cannot establish a new meta. It shows that the promoted formation can defeat the particular opponent selected for the preview. It does not tell us how either march will perform against every other popular composition.

Strong Medusa and Ares formations should still be perfectly capable of competing with Horus teams. Medusa remains an exceptionally powerful damage dealer, and a developed player formation may use different skills, artifacts, specializations and supporting Immortals from those shown in the simulation.

## What the Simulation Cannot Tell Us

The demonstration does not replace testing in Arena, Legion of Frostborne, Illusion Battlefield or real server combat.

It cannot fully answer questions such as:

- How does the formation perform against several different meta teams?
- Does Horus remain effective when the opponent uses anti-healing or sustained damage?
- How dependent is the result on Great Tengu?
- How does Horus compare with an equally developed Medusa?
- Which Tower of Knowledge skills produce the best results?
- Does the recommended formation remain strong when both sides use optimized artifacts and specializations?

Those answers require battle reports and repeated testing against multiple formations. A single favourable result should therefore be treated as a preview, not as proof that the previous meta has become obsolete.

## Final Thoughts

The Immortal Demonstration feature is promotional, but it is a welcome addition.

Players should remain sceptical of any simulation designed specifically to showcase a newly released Immortal. The formation, opponent and conditions have all been selected to present that Immortal favourably. Winning the demonstration does not automatically make the new hero mandatory or prove that the featured lineup is the strongest march in the game.

Even so, the feature lets us watch expensive Immortals interact with a complete team before deciding whether to build them. We can examine their animations, ability timing, survivability and intended synergies without first making a major financial commitment.

Use the simulation as an introduction to the Immortal, not as a final verdict on the meta. It is a useful preview and a clever piece of marketing, but the real test will always begin when players start placing Horus into their own formations.

***Immortal Price Classification Guide - How to Understand, Plan, and Spend Wisely on Immortals***

---

## 1. Why Immortal Price Tags Matter

When you start in *Infinity Kingdom*, it’s easy to assume that the most expensive immortals are automatically the strongest. While there’s some truth to that—many pay-walled immortals are powerful—the reality is more nuanced:

- **Some of the best immortals are completely free** (🆓) and obtainable with only time and effort.
- **Some expensive immortals are underwhelming** in practice, especially outside their niche.
- Price tags are heavily influenced by *availability* rather than pure *combat strength*.

Understanding the cost classification of immortals helps you:

- **Plan your builds** around what you can realistically obtain.
- **Avoid wasting resources** on overpriced or short-lived options.
- **Maximize your investment** in Golden Path, seasonal events, and lucky draws.
- **Stay competitive** without overspending.

Example: In **Fire**, Empress Wu (🆓) is one of the strongest DPS immortals in the game and costs nothing. But for an optimal build, she shines brightest alongside **Trajan** (❄️), who can be much harder to get.

---

## 2. Immortal Price Symbol Key
