---

## 4. Price ≠ Power: Understanding the Difference

Not all costly immortals are top-tier, and not all free immortals are weak.

### Examples:

- **Empress Wu (🆓)** – One of the best AoE DPS immortals in the entire game, no spending required.
- **Trajan (❄️)** – Mandatory for many high-end Fire builds but locked behind KVK.
- **Himiko (💰)** – Pricey and powerful, but niche outside of Shadow setups.
- **Cao Cao (💰👑)** – Can be costly early, later cheap but paywalled. Only support for Lightning, and all substitutes are equally or more expensive.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/image-27-1024x544.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/image-32-1024x575.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/image-28-1024x510.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/image-31-1024x611.png)

**Why this matters:** You don’t have to chase *every* high-cost immortal. Many teams can be competitive with a strong core of free immortals supplemented by one or two targeted purchases.

---

## 5. How Price Tags Change Through the Seasons

Immortal pricing isn’t static. Seasonal progression changes accessibility:

- **Season 1:** Shadow and Holy are the most expensive elements; their key immortals are mostly locked in *Roulette* events. Chaos is unavailable.
- **Season 2:** Costs for older expensive immortals drop as new acquisition paths open (e.g., **Galaxy** and **Harbor**). Shadow/Holy become easier to obtain, freeing resources for other priorities.
- **Conquest Season:** Many once-expensive immortals become nearly free through events and market offers. But *newly released immortals* take their place as the premium chase units—like Chaos immortals in Conquest (🐳 tier).

**Key takeaway:** If you can wait, some of the most expensive immortals become accessible for free or much cheaper in later seasons. But in competitive servers, early access still has value.

---

## 6. Spending Strategy: Golden Path & Events

If you plan to spend:

- **Golden Path:** Great for guaranteed shards of targeted immortals; use it for those in your endgame build.
- **Roulette Events:** High risk, high reward. Only spin heavily for immortals you *must* have immediately.
- **Market Purchases (📜):** Gem-only immortals are reliable long-term goals; buy consistently when they appear.
- **KVK Exclusives (❄️):** Save KVK coins and plan early; missing them can block entire builds.

If you’re **F2P or low spender**:

- Focus on the strongest 🆓 immortals in your element first.
- Use events for shard boosts but avoid burning all resources on early hype.
- Time your efforts with seasonal price drops.

---

## 7. Building Around Price and Availability

- **Mix Free & Paid Wisely:** Example: Fire build → Wu (🆓) + Hippolyta (🆓) + Frederick I (🆓) + Trajan (❄️).
- **Plan for KVK Gates:** Don’t commit to a build where *multiple* key immortals are ❄️-locked unless you’re sure you can get them.
- **Prioritize Core Units:** Get the immortals that define your team’s playstyle first, even if that means delaying secondary supports.

---

## 8. Final Advice

Knowing immortal price classifications is not just about “who’s expensive.” It’s about:

- **Planning your growth path.**
- **Avoiding wasted investment.**
- **Getting the most powerful teams for your budget.**
- **Adjusting to seasonal price shifts.**

The strongest players—F2P and whales alike—are the ones who combine *timing, planning, and smart spending* with a deep understanding of the immortal economy.

title: Immortal Darius: A new meta for lightning?
summary: Unleashing the Power of Immortal Darius: A Comprehensive Guide The latest update in Infinity Kingdom has introduced a new powerhouse, Immortal Darius, who is now available as a reward in the Legion of Frostborne…
markdown:
***Unleashing the Power of Immortal Darius: A Comprehensive Guide***
The latest update in Infinity Kingdom has introduced a new powerhouse, Immortal Darius, who is now available as a reward in the Legion of Frostborne Season's Conquest P5. In this guide, we'll delve into the remarkable abilities of Darius and provide insights on how to make the most of his incredible powers on the battlefield.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-78.png)

**On Paper: Unveiling the Potential**
On paper, Darius is an exceptionally powerful immortal with a set of abilities that make him a formidable force. His ultimate ability deals 360% physical damage to all enemies in a full area of effect, making him one of the few immortals capable of such widespread devastation. Additionally, his ultimate has a 30% chance to reduce the physical damage dealt by enemies by 30% for 6 seconds.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-79.png)

Darius's first skill cast is equally impressive, as it doubles down on his utility by reducing the enemy's physical attack by a whopping 60%. This attribute makes him particularly potent against the current meta, which is predominantly dominated by physical attack damage from Earth-Wind hybrid builds and Holy builds. His abilities synergize seamlessly with the concept of Lightning elemental builds, as Darius is of the Lightning element and deals additional damage to Earth immortals. This combination, along with his ability to carry Khan with wounds, provides players with a variety of tools to combat physical damage-oriented builds.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-84.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-90.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-90.png)

**In Testing: A Force to be Reckoned With**
In practice, Darius lives up to the hype. He performs exceptionally well on the battlefield and aligns with the expectations set by his on-paper capabilities. Darius can deal staggering amounts of damage to enemies while his damage reduction debuff effectively counters physical damage-based opponents, particularly those who aim to deal damage at the outset of the battle, such as hybrid builds.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-89.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-79.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-81.png)

However, it's important to note that Darius appears to be somewhat fragile and can be taken down quickly. To mitigate this vulnerability, players should focus on building his defenses. There are two main approaches to consider: equipping single-immortal defense skills on Darius for greater durability or creating a balanced build by incorporating defense from other support immortals and emphasizing damage skills on Darius himself.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-84.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-82.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-88.png)

### Building for Success: Strategies and Synergies

1. **Defense-Centric Build:** To maximize Darius's survivability, equip him with single-immortal defense skills. These skills significantly enhance his ability to withstand enemy attacks, making him a formidable presence on the battlefield.
2. **Balanced Build:** Alternatively, you can adopt a balanced approach by leveraging Darius's high damage output. Pair him with other support immortals who can boost his defenses and focus on his damage-dealing skills. Running skills like Anger, Toxin Barrier, Desire of Life, and energy regeneration can be incredibly effective in this setup.
3. **Synergies:** Darius synergizes particularly well with the shadow immortal, Bjorn. Bjorn provides additional damage buffs and enhances Darius's defensive capabilities, creating a dynamic duo. Consider investing in builds that guarantee Guard will activate on Darius 100% of the time, especially if you have access to immortals like Bjorn or Tokugawa. This combination has the potential to become a top-tier build in the current meta.

Immortal Darius is a game-changer in Infinity Kingdom, offering players the opportunity to harness unmatched area-of-effect damage and crowd control. When used strategically and in the right team compositions, he can be an invaluable asset on the battlefield. Experiment with different build approaches and synergies to unlock the full potential of this electrifying new immortal. Darius has arrived, and he's here to make a thunderous impact!

title: Immortal EXP Farming Through Solo Gnome Camps
summary: A veteran breakdown of how EXP distribution really works in Infinity Kingdom
markdown:
## Introduction

*A veteran breakdown of how EXP distribution really works in* **Infinity Kingdom**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-194-1024x287.png)

Immortal leveling is one of those systems that looks straightforward on the surface, but once you understand how EXP is actually distributed, your farming efficiency can change dramatically. Over the years, I’ve seen many players slow their own progression simply by running full marches out of habit.

This guide focuses specifically on **Immortal Experience Point (EXP) farming via solo or reduced-immortal gnome hits**, explaining why it works, when it doesn’t, and how to push the system even further using Immortal Rebirth.

---

## How Gnome Camp EXP Distribution Works

Every gnome camp has a **fixed EXP value**. That EXP is **split evenly among all immortals participating in the fight**.

There is **no catch-up mechanic**. Lower-level immortals do not receive a larger share, and higher-level immortals do not receive less. The game simply divides the total EXP by the number of immortals present.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-195.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-196.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-197.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-198.png)

Using **Level 45 gnome camps** as a clean example:

- **4 immortals** → 4 × **156,681 EXP**
- **3 immortals** → 3 × **208,908 EXP**
- **2 immortals** → 2 × **313,362 EXP**
- **1 immortal** → 1 × **626,724 EXP**

The implication is obvious once you see the numbers clearly:

> **If a single immortal can solo a camp, they level four times faster than in a full march** given same gnome level

---

## Dragons and EXP: A Common Misunderstanding

Removing the dragon **does nothing** for EXP optimization.

- Dragons **do not gain EXP**
- Dragons **do not consume EXP**
- EXP distribution is **only affected by the number of immortals**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-200.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-199-1024x513.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-202.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-201-1024x576.png)

Whether you bring a dragon or not has **zero impact** on how EXP is split. Bring a dragon if you need the combat power; remove it if you don’t. From an EXP standpoint, it’s irrelevant.

---

## Why Max-Level Immortals Actively Hurt EXP Farming

A very common mistake is trying to “cheese” the system by filling a march with max-level immortals and one immortal you actually want to level.

Unfortunately, the game doesn’t care. The EXP is still split evenly, and any portion assigned to a max-level immortal is **simply deleted**.

Example, again using Level 45 gnome camps:

- 3 max-level immortals + 1 leveling immortal
→ Your target immortal still only receives **156,681 EXP**

The other three shares are wasted. There is no overflow, no redistribution, and no conversion.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-203.png)

**If an immortal doesn’t need EXP, they should not be in the march.**

---

## Solo vs Carry: Choosing the Right Gnome Level

Ideally, you want your target immortal to **solo the highest possible gnome camp** they can reliably clear.

If soloing is not possible, you have two options:

1) **Lower the gnome camp level**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-204-1024x426.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-205-1024x426.png)

2) **Add a second immortal as a carry**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-206-1024x340.png)

### Practical Example

Let’s say **Seon** cannot solo Level 50 gnomes.

- Level 50 gnome, 2 immortals → **406,821 EXP** for Seon (see above)
- Level 45 gnome, solo → **626,724 EXP** for Seon (see below)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-205-1024x426.png)

Even though the camp is weaker, the solo hit produces **significantly more EXP**. This would suggest that you should always solo the highest possible gnome camp - that however is not entirely true. We are forgetting about Immortal Rebirth!

---

## EXP Soaking via Immortal Rebirth

Through Rebirth tricks we can find the most high-efficiency EXP farming setups/method. The **Alchemy Lab** allows you to **Rebirth immortals**, converting their stored EXP into **EXP scrolls** that can be reassigned freely.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-208.png)

Assuming you are not constantly constrained by the rebirth cooldown because you are changing up your battle formations, then the optimal setup becomes: **Always farm gnome camps with two immortals below max level.**

### How This Works in Practice

- Immortal A: your **priority immortal**
- Immortal B: a **temporary EXP sponge**

You farm the **highest gnome level the pair can reliably clear**, even if Immortal A cannot solo it. Both immortals receive half the EXP per fight.

Once Immortal B approaches max level, you **rebirth them**, converting their accumulated EXP into scrolls, and then feed those scrolls back into Immortal A.

### Why This Beats Soloing Lower Camps

Returning to the earlier example:

- Seon cannot solo Level 50 gnomes
- Two-immortal clear at Level 50 gives Seon **406,821 EXP**
- Rebirthing the second immortal returns **another 406,821 EXP per camp** as scrolls

Effectively, Seon gains **full 813.642** **EXP from Level 50 camps**, despite not being able to solo them.

This method strictly outperforms soloing lower-level camps as long as:

- You can clear the higher camp with two immortals
- You can afford the rebirth cooldown

---

## Conclusion Summary

- Gnome camp EXP is **always split evenly**
- Soloing gives **up to 4× faster progression**
- Dragons have **no effect** on EXP
- Max-level immortals **waste EXP**
- Lower gnome levels often outperform adding carries
- Two-immortal farming + rebirth is the **most efficient method overall**

If your goal is to level a specific immortal as quickly as possible, the game rewards precision, not brute force. Reduce the number of immortals, choose your gnome levels carefully, and let the EXP system work for you instead of against you.

---

title: Immortal Margaret l (Water)
summary: Margaret I is a Water backline Immortal built around physical area damage and control synergy. Unlike the traditional magic-focused Water setup, Margaret fits into a physical Water march, where Freeze/Chill and Physical…
markdown:
**Margaret I** is a Water backline Immortal built around physical area damage and control synergy. Unlike the traditional magic-focused Water setup, Margaret fits into a **physical Water march**, where Freeze/Chill and Physical Defense reduction are used to amplify her ultimate.

Her main attraction is **Winter Passage**. At maximum level it deals 500% Physical Damage in a fan-shaped area, with another 300% damage against affected targets when its control condition is met. That gives Margaret considerable burst potential, but also makes her dependent on the rest of the march.

She works best when you build around that condition rather than treating her as a standalone damage dealer.

## Margaret I – General Information

- **Element:** Water
- **Position:** Backline
- **Damage Type:** Physical
- **Role:** AoE damage dealer
- **Ultimate:** Winter Passage
- **Main Synergies:** Freeze/Chill, Silence and Physical Defense reduction

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/image-71.png)

Margaret l

**Ultimate skill: Winter Passage**
Inflict physical damage to the enemy team in the fan-shaped area in front (damage rate x%), if the target is affected by the Chill effect, the skill will deal and additional physical damage (damage rate y%), if the target is affected by the silence effect, the physical damage they deal is reduced by z% for 6 seconds.

**Damage**:
Damage rate x - 150% / 200% / 250% / 300% / 350% / 400% / 450% / 500%

**Additional Damage**:
Damage rate y - 90% / 120% / 150% / 180% / 210% / 240% / 270% / 300%

**Reduced Damage Dealt**:
Damage rate z - 6% / 8% / 10% / 12% / 14% / 16% / 18% / 20%

Margaret is particularly interesting because physical backline damage dealers are relatively unusual in Water. Instead of supporting Merlin's Magic Damage, a Margaret march can concentrate on weakening enemy Physical Defense and setting up her ultimate.

---

## Ultimate Skill: Winter Passage

**Winter Passage** deals Physical Damage to enemies in a fan-shaped area in front of Margaret.

Its three effects scale as follows:

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/image-13-1024x293.png)

At maximum level, the basic hit is already a respectable **500% Physical Damage**. When Margaret hits a target affected by the required control effect, Winter Passage deals another **300% Physical Damage**, bringing the combined damage rate against that target to **800%**.

There is also a defensive component. If the target is affected by **Silence**, the Physical Damage they deal is reduced by **20% for 6 seconds**.

This makes Winter Passage more than a simple damage ultimate. Margaret wants the rest of the march to prepare targets before she casts.

---

## Why Freeze/Chill Matters

The difference between a normal Winter Passage and a fully enabled one is substantial:

### 500% → 800% Physical Damage

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/image-15-1024x587.png)

That additional 300% is a major part of Margaret's damage potential, so reliable control application is one of the first things to consider when building around her.

**Dido** early game and later **Artemisia**are particularly useful for this reason. They provide the Chill interaction Margaret needs, allowing the march to trigger the additional portion of Winter Passage much more consistently.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/image-16.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/image-14.png)

The important part is timing. It is not enough for the march to apply the relevant effect at some point during battle; ideally it needs to be present **when Margaret casts Winter Passage**.

That leads directly into Margaret's main weakness.

---

## Margaret's Energy Generation

Margaret's biggest weakness is her slow energy regeneration. Winter Passage can hit extremely hard, but she takes longer than most damage dealers to actually get the skill off.

This is especially important because so much of her damage depends on the enemy already being affected by the right control effects. If Margaret casts too late and those effects have expired, you lose the additional damage that makes Winter Passage so strong in the first place.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/image-17-1024x812.png)

Because of that, I generally prefer giving her some help with energy rather than simply stacking as much Physical Damage as possible. A slightly weaker Winter Passage that casts at the right time can perform much better than a stronger one that constantly misses the window.

Keep an eye on your battle reports when testing her. If Margaret regularly casts while the enemy is properly debuffed, the setup is working. If she keeps missing those windows, I would work on her energy generation before adding more damage.

---

## Using Margaret in a Physical Water Build

Margaret makes the most sense when you commit to a **physical Water setup** rather than trying to fit her into a traditional Merlin march. Her damage is entirely physical, so you want the rest of the team helping her in two ways: keeping the enemy under the control effects needed for Winter Passage and reducing their Physical Defense before she casts.

A good starting point is **Harald and Attila in the frontline with Margaret and Dido in the backline**. Dido is particularly important because she helps provide the control Margaret needs for the additional damage on Winter Passage, while Harald and Attila fit naturally into the physical side of the build through Physical Defense reduction. When everything lines up, Margaret is not just landing her 500% base hit; she can get the additional 300% against affected targets while hitting enemies whose Physical Defense has already been reduced.

I would build Margaret around that interaction rather than simply loading her with every Physical Damage skill available. Her energy generation is on the slow side, so skills that help her get Winter Passage out at the right time can be just as valuable as another damage increase. **Onslaught, Anger and Chaotic Blade** are reasonable options while developing her, with **Death Breath** available later. Once you have access to SvS and Triss skills, options such as **Blade Vortex, Spell Disintegrator, Demonic Contract, Energy Mastery, Corrosive Power and Eternal Battlelust** give you considerably more room to tune the build. Adrenaline is also worth considering if her ultimate timing is the main problem.

There is no single three-skill setup I would recommend for every Margaret march. Watch the battle reports. If Winter Passage is landing at the right time but the damage is lacking, you can lean further into offense. If she keeps casting after the relevant control effects have disappeared, work on her energy cycle first. Margaret is one of those Immortals where getting the sequence right matters more than having the prettiest skill list on paper.

Her **Silence interaction** is also worth remembering. A Silenced enemy hit by Winter Passage can have its Physical Damage reduced by up to **20% for 6 seconds**, so Margaret provides a little protection for the frontline while doing her main job. Her exclusive artifact, **Seal of the Alliance**, extends that effect to **9 seconds**, making it much more noticeable against physical teams IF it lands.

Overall, I would recommend Margaret mainly to players who actually want to build **physical Water**. She needs more support than a straightforward damage dealer, and I would not invest heavily in her without having the Immortals and skills to make the setup work. If you already have Dido and a frontline capable of supporting physical damage, however, Margaret becomes much more interesting. The goal is simple: **set up the control, lower Physical Defense, and have Winter Passage land while both advantages are still in play.**

---

## Conclusion

Margaret I gives Water something quite different from its traditional magic-focused compositions: a genuine **backline physical AoE damage dealer**.

At maximum level, Winter Passage provides **500% Physical Damage with up to 300% additional conditional damage**, while its Silence interaction can reduce enemy Physical Damage by 20%. With Seal of the Alliance, that reduction can last for 9 seconds.

The best way to use her is not to chase the 800% figure in isolation. Build the conditions that allow her to reach it consistently.

With reliable control, Physical Defense reduction, and sensible management of her energy cycle, **Margaret can become the centerpiece of a dedicated physical Water march rather than simply another Water backliner.**

---

title: Immortal Outfit Develop Costs – Fragments & Gold for Levels 1–8
summary: Full cost table for developing Immortal Outfits from level 1 to 8:
markdown:
![Immortal Outfit Develop Costs – IK Wiki guide](/uploads/screenshot-20261127-101236-5lgrot.png)

Immortal Outfits do more than change how your Immortal looks. Once an outfit is unlocked, you can **develop** it up to level 8, and every level adds a percentage bonus to all five of the Immortal's attributes. The develop screen only ever shows you the cost of the *next* level, though, so it is hard to plan how many fragments you actually need.

This guide lists the full cost of every outfit level, fragments and gold, and shows which levels are worth paying for. If you are new to outfits, start with [Basics: Everything You Need to Know About the New Outfit System](/posts/basics-everything-you-need-to-know-about-the-new-outfit-system).

## How Outfit Levels Work

* **Unlocking** an outfit costs **60 outfit fragments**. The outfit becomes permanently available for that Immortal.
* An unlocked outfit starts at **level 1 with +0% to all attributes**. Unlocking alone gives you the look and the skill effect, but no stats.
* You then **develop** the outfit with more fragments plus gold. There are 7 stars, so 7 develop steps take the outfit from level 1 to the **maximum, level 8**.
* Every level raises **Strength, Agility, Intelligence, Physique and Aptitude** by the same percentage, up to **+15% each at level 8**.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261127-101403-jb7l2x.png)

## Cost of Every Level

| Level            | Fragments | Gold        | Bonus to all 5 attributes |
| ---------------- | --------- | ----------- | ------------------------- |
| Unlock (level 1) | 60        | –           | +0.0%                     |
| 1 → 2            | 30        | 15,000,000  | +6.0%                     |
| 2 → 3            | 60        | 30,000,000  | +7.5%                     |
| 3 → 4            | 90        | 45,000,000  | +9.0%                     |
| 4 → 5            | 120       | 60,000,000  | +10.5%                    |
| 5 → 6            | 150       | 75,000,000  | +12.0%                    |
| 6 → 7            | 180       | 90,000,000  | +13.5%                    |
| 7 → 8            | 210       | 105,000,000 | +15.0%                    |

The pattern is simple: every level costs **30 more fragments and 15M more gold** than the one before, and adds **+1.5%** to every attribute. The only exception is the jump from level 1 to level 2, which gives a big +6% on its own.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261127-101412-dbzrab.png)

We checked the unlock, level 1 → 2, level 2 → 3 (Louis IX – Night of Terror) and level 7 → 8 (Alexander the Great) in-game. All four match the pattern exactly, so the levels in between follow the same steps.

## Running Totals

| Reach level  | Total fragments | Total gold | Bonus      |
| ------------ | --------------- | ---------- | ---------- |
| 1 (unlocked) | 60              | –          | +0.0%      |
| 2            | 90              | 15M        | +6.0%      |
| 3            | 150             | 45M        | +7.5%      |
| 4            | 240             | 90M        | +9.0%      |
| 5            | 360             | 150M       | +10.5%     |
| 6            | 510             | 225M       | +12.0%     |
| 7            | 690             | 315M       | +13.5%     |
| 8 (max)      | **900**         | **420M**   | **+15.0%** |

A fully maxed outfit costs **900 fragments and 420 million gold**.

## Which Levels Are Worth It?

Fragments are the real bottleneck, so the question is how much bonus each fragment buys:

| Step  | Fragments | Bonus gained | Bonus per 100 fragments |
| ----- | --------- | ------------ | ----------------------- |
| 1 → 2 | 30        | +6.0%        | 20.0%                   |
| 2 → 3 | 60        | +1.5%        | 2.5%                    |
| 3 → 4 | 90        | +1.5%        | 1.7%                    |
| 4 → 5 | 120       | +1.5%        | 1.3%                    |
| 5 → 6 | 150       | +1.5%        | 1.0%                    |
| 6 → 7 | 180       | +1.5%        | 0.8%                    |
| 7 → 8 | 210       | +1.5%        | 0.7%                    |

* **Level 2 is a must.** Just 30 fragments after unlocking gives +6% to everything, which is 40% of the outfit's total bonus for 3% of its total cost.
* **Unlock + level 2 = 90 fragments.** Treat that as the real "price" of an outfit.
* **Levels 3–8 get steadily worse.** The last 810 fragments only add the remaining +9%. Push them on your main Immortals, where every percent counts, and stop at level 2 on everyone else.

## Gold

Gold is rarely the limiting factor late in the game, but it adds up: 420M for a single maxed outfit. If you plan to max several outfits at once, keep an eye on your gold before an outfit event.

## Quick Summary

* Unlock = 60 fragments, no stats.
* Level 2 = +30 fragments for +6% to all attributes. Always do it.
* Each level after that costs 30 more fragments and 15M more gold than the last, for +1.5%.
* Max (level 8) = 900 fragments and 420M gold in total for +15% to all five attributes.

Have you developed an outfit with different costs, for example Fu Fei or Athena? Send us a screenshot and we will add it.

title: Immortal Yi Sun-Shin
summary: Back when Yi Sun-Shin (YSS) was released he was largely disregarded by players in favor of other immortals such as Charles, etc. But YSS isn’t “underrated” anymore. He’s firmly in the spotlight now, mostly because his…
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/image-186.png)

Back when Yi Sun-Shin (YSS) was released he was largely disregarded by players in favor of other immortals such as Charles, etc. But YSS isn’t “underrated” anymore. He’s firmly in the spotlight now, mostly because his kit stacks insanely well with modern healing/mitigation comps, as he turns your whole team into a pain sponge that just won’t die. If you’re running Himiko meta or any sustain-heavy earth core, YSS is not just optional — he’s the key.

---

## Profile (Quick Facts)

- **Element:** Earth
- **Role:** Frontline Tank
- **Troop:** Cavalry
- **Ultimate:** **Guard of Devotion** — reduces damage taken by **all allied immortals** by **30% for 6s**.
- **With Unique Artifact:** Guard of Devotion also **increases healing received by affected allies by 30%** for the same duration.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/image-171.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/image-172.png)

**What that means in real fights:** he’s a mitigation anchor that turns on a team‑wide wall for six seconds, and the artifact turns that wall into a massive sustain window. You’ll see it most when your healers ramp or your defensive procs overlap.

---

## How to Use Him (the short version)

YSS shines when you stack **multiple sources of damage reduction** and **time your heals** to land inside his ultimate window.

- **Stacks nicely with**: Oaken Guard, Resist, Weakening Curse, other flat or % DR sources, and **Earth Dragon’s Sandstorm Breath**. These are all separate lanes of '*take less damage,*' and multiplicative stacking here is what makes your march feel immortal.
- **Heals love him**: the **+30% healing received** from the **artifact**supercharges **Theodora** and **Fu Fei**. You’ll notice Vitality Touch and similar skills pushing bars back up way harder when YSS ult is up. **[Read more about his artifact here.](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/immortals/artifacts/unique-artifacts/yi-sun-shin-and-the-spear-ship/)**

Practical note: you get the most value when your team is under burst. If you see enemy alts cycling (Himiko/Tomyris/Matilda spikes), YSS’s window is the difference between surviving the volley or folding.

---

## Immortal talents (s2 and onwards)

Generally speaking Fearless Stance will be your go-to as you stack damage mitigation to turn enemy damage skills into wet noodles. However, there are some players who swear to Sturdy Barrier, I am not one of them and as far as I have seen you will always get superior results running Fearless Stance.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/image-187-1024x478.png)

---

## Team Compositions where YSS is S‑tier

Honestly, he’s mostly a Himiko meta piece right now, but he’s flexible.

### Earth Himiko cores (spend level changes who heals, not whether YSS is there):

- **Fu Fei / Himiko / YSS / Bjorn**
- **Theodora / Himiko / YSS / Bjorn**
- **Theodora / Himiko / YSS / Charles**
- **Zenobia / Himiko / YSS / Charles**

**[Read more here.](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/elements/season-2-builds/earth-himiko-build-for-season-2-a-top-meta-build-short-of-chaos/)**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/image-185.png)

> All of these are variations of the same idea: Himiko handles pressure/DPS, YSS covers the damage mitigation, and you pack a premium healer.

### Earth–Wind hybrid (dev path):

- **Zenobia / Qin / YSS / Alexander**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/image-184-1024x486.png)

While I am sure there are many more builds he can work in, these are some of the best ones I’ve seen so far. The main takeaway here is that he has a top place in the current meta and can be used in most comps past season 1. For example you could run a **Water** with **Ragnar / YSS / Merlin / (Matilda | Fu Fei | Artemisia | Theodora)**. Not meta‑standard, but if your water artifacts are ahead, YSS can still carry the defensive core.

**Why he fits:** YSS doesn’t care who’s doing damage; he cares about creating safe windows. Any comp relying on sustained heals or mid‑fight ramp loves that.

---

## How to Obtain

### Fragments

- **Mysterious Pearl Shop (from Season 2):** **1 Pearl per fragment**, **daily limit 30 fragments**. Reliable drip if you log in daily.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/image-173.png)

- **Elemental Bonds** event: available in that pool as well.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/image-174.png)

- **Golden Path (monthly/seasonal):** **300 fragments per season** at **200 Golden Path coins per 60 fragments** (**total 1,200 coins** if you buy all five stacks).

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/image-178.png)

---

## Practical Synergy Notes (what you’ll feel in battles)

- **Earth Dragon timing**: If Sandstorm Breath lands during YSS ult, you get that comfy “we just don’t die” stretch. The more the enemy tries to spike, the better it feels.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/image-182-1024x373.png)

**[Read more about skills and builds here and in other build guides.](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/elements/season-2-builds/earth-himiko-build-for-season-2-a-top-meta-build-short-of-chaos/)**

---

## Conclusion Summary

YSS is meta for a reason: **team‑wide 30% DR** on demand, and with his artifact, **team‑wide +30% healing received** for the same six seconds. Stack that with Earth dragon and standard DR skills and you get a comp that sails through burst windows while your DPS keeps working.

**Bottom line:** if you’re building Himiko meta or any heal‑centric earth shell, **get YSS + his artifact effect online**. The rest is just optimization.

---

title: Impeachment vs Forced Impeachment in Infinity Kingdom
summary: Alliance leadership in Infinity Kingdom can change through two different systems: Impeachment and Forced Impeachment. Although both mechanics ultimately allow members to replace the alliance leader, they exist for…
markdown:
## Introduction

Alliance leadership in *Infinity Kingdom* can change through two different systems: **Impeachment** and **Forced Impeachment**. Although both mechanics ultimately allow members to replace the alliance leader, they exist for different situations and follow very different procedures.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-37-1024x563.png)

The regular **Impeachment** system is designed as a structured leadership replacement when the leader becomes inactive. **Forced Impeachment**, by contrast, is a player-driven vote used when the inactivity conditions are not met but members still want to challenge the current leader.

Understanding the difference between the two systems is important because the voting rules, candidates, and outcomes are not the same.

---

## Impeachment

Impeachment is an automatic leadership replacement mechanism that becomes available when the alliance leader has been inactive for a specific period of time. The system checks the leader’s login activity and allows impeachment if the inactivity thresholds are met. During the first three days after a server opens, the leader must be absent for **24 consecutive hours** to trigger impeachment eligibility. After the initial three days, the requirement increases to **72 consecutive hours without login**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-38-1024x617.png)

Once these conditions are satisfied, any **alliance member with rank R2 or higher** can start the impeachment process. At this point the system opens a leadership election rather than a direct replacement.

During a regular impeachment, **all alliance members are eligible to both vote and stand as candidates**. Players who wish to become leader must actively sign up as candidates. Members then vote among the registered candidates, and the player who receives the most support becomes the new alliance leader.

This process functions more like a **leadership election** than a direct removal. The outcome is not predetermined by who started the impeachment; instead, the alliance collectively selects a new leader from the pool of volunteers.

Players who join the alliance **after the impeachment process has started** cannot participate in the vote.

---

## Forced Impeachment

Forced impeachment exists for situations where the leader is still considered active by the game but alliance members want to replace them anyway. Because the inactivity conditions for normal impeachment are not met, the system instead uses a direct challenge vote between two players.

Only **R3 members or higher** can initiate a forced impeachment. When the process begins, the vote is immediately structured as a contest between **the current leader and the initiating player**. Unlike regular impeachment, there is no candidate registration phase and no additional candidates can join the race.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-39-edited.png)

All alliance members are allowed to vote between these two options. During the forced impeachment period, the leader temporarily loses several administrative authorities, including the ability to transfer leadership, remove all alliance members, or dissolve the alliance. These permissions return once the impeachment process ends.

The outcome depends on participation and majority rules. If the vote succeeds, the **player who initiated the forced impeachment automatically becomes the new leader**. If the conditions for a successful vote are not met, the current leader remains in power.

There is also a **seven-day cooldown between forced impeachment attempts**, which prevents alliances from repeatedly triggering the system in quick succession.

As with regular impeachment, players who join the alliance after the process begins cannot participate in the vote.

---

## Conclusion Summary

Although both systems replace the alliance leader, their purpose and structure are different.

Regular **Impeachment** occurs when the leader is inactive and functions as a leadership election where members vote among multiple candidates. Any R2 member can start the process once the inactivity requirement is met.

**Forced Impeachment** is a direct leadership challenge used when the leader is still active. It can only be initiated by R3 members or higher, and the vote is strictly between the current leader and the player who started the impeachment. If the vote succeeds, the initiating player immediately becomes the new alliance leader.

Understanding which system applies—and why—prevents confusion and helps alliances navigate leadership changes more effectively.

---

title: Talent builds
summary: Infinity Kingdom offers many ways in which you can develop your kingdom and your Lord. Talents is one of the ways you can get unique skills to accelerate your development and improve your efficiency. Choosing the right…
markdown:
Infinity Kingdom offers many ways in which you can develop your kingdom and your Lord. Talents is one of the ways you can get unique skills to accelerate your development and improve your efficiency. Choosing the right talents will have a big impact on your development, and you can also customize your talent tree to maximize your chances of winning events or accelerate your growth in a specific area.

In this article we will look into the best talents to accelerate your growth, and in which situations each talent is best.

In your talent tree you can spend a limit of five points per line, so you need to decide wisely which talent to focus on. Once you reach 5 points, a line with three options will be unlocked and you can only choose one talent for that line.

There are two distinct talent trees: Development and Military. The most beneficial talents for growth are in the development tree, but it is important to know that the Military tree also has very good options that will significantly support your growth. The best strategy is usually a hybrid of the two.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-84-1024x565.png)

### Talents

## Talent builds

I will not go through all the same talents here, since you are going to want different talen builds based on the activity you are doing. Therefore, I have curated an array of articles on different talent builds. You can read them here:

- **[Gold talents](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/lord-lady/talents/gold-talents/)**
- **[Dragon talents](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/lord-lady/talents/dragon-talent-builds/)**
- **[Leveling & Raid talents](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/lord-lady/talents/leveling-raid-talent-builds/)**
- **[Building & Resource talents](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/lord-lady/talents/building-resource-talents-build/)**
- **[Illusion Battle (IB) talents](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/lord-lady/talents/ib-talents-illusion-battle/)**
- **[Combat (general PvP) talents](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/lord-lady/talents/combat-talent-builds/)**

It costs 200 gems to reset / switch between talent builds. 200 gems is not nothing, so you have to use it wisely, but it is almost always worth swapping talents as you go about different stages and game activities. Remember to use the 3 talent loadout pages! **These are very useful, I personally keep them as:** (1) Gold and Tech hybrid with Rank Advancement. My base talent build I can use for most everything. (2) Dragon upgrading, I switch into these talents whenever I am beginning a new dragon upgrade. (3) IB-talents.

There are many interesting talents which are not part of a greater build, but are handy tools to solve the problems you might have. Because they are more or less standablone talents, I have no guide for them. They should however still be noted, since they definetly have their value.

## Standalone important talents

##### AP preservation

Divine Walker allow you to safe a lot of AP, no matter what activies you are doing. I personally have this talent in every single build I use.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-97.png)

##### Honor farming

Rank Advancement is a great talent to boost your honor gain. [Especially if you are using alts to farm honor.](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/lord-lady/nobility-honor/using-alts-to-farm-honor/)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-99.png)

##### Anti Outlaw talent

If your server is plagued by one or more outlaws, you want to run **Divine Protection** and/or **Tactical Retreat**when you send our gatheres and log off for the night.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-100.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Skaermbillede-2022-03-28-133753.png)

##### Boosting Immortal Star level in a hurry

Perhaps the most niche talent of all, is: Prosperous Trading. This talent lets you refresh the market 20 more times, useful if you are spamming the reset button looking for those last few fragments for an Immortal.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-101.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/image-29-1024x1024.png)

The Infernal Assault event not only encompasses team-based gameplay but also includes individual challenges that allow players to test their skills and prowess on their own. While these missions are intended for solo completion, players are not alone in their journey, as they can seek assistance from alliance friends and other players. In this article, we aim to provide recommendations to help players navigate the Individual Challenge of the Infernal Assault, maximizing their chances of obtaining the highest prizes while minimizing troop losses.

One crucial aspect to consider when undertaking the Individual Challenge is the strength of the troops players should deploy. To assist in making informed decisions, we have provided troop power recommendations based on specific levels. It is our hope that these recommendations will aid players in completing the Infernal Assault with maximum rewards while minimizing the loss of troops.

### The troop power recommendations for farming are as follows:

- X - 40,000: Recommended for Under Level 4
- 40,000 - 80,000: Recommended for Level 4
- 80,000 - 100,000: Recommended for Level 6
- 100,000 - 130,000: Recommended for Level 8
- 130,000 - 150,000: Recommended for Level 10
- 150,000 - 200,000: Recommended for Level 15
- 200,000 - 300,000: Recommended for Level 20
- 300,000 - 400,000: Recommenden for Level 30
- Above 400,000: Push to max level and farm **ONLY**small outer camps. Leave the Core alone and farm gold on minors when they respawn.

These power recommendations correspond to the strength of your strongest troops, taking into account the minimum number of death troops. By aligning your troop power with the recommended levels, you can optimize your performance and increase your chances of success.

You might wonder why there are no power recommendations for levels such as Level 7 or Level 18. The reason for this omission is the significant disparity in troop losses between certain levels. Specifically, there is a notable difference in the number of death troops between Level 6 and Level 5, as well as between Level 19 and Level 20. As a result, we advise players to adhere to the power recommendations outlined in the table above, unless they are willing to surpass those limits in pursuit of additional rewards.

For instance, let's consider an example. Suppose you have already reached Level 20 but desire to obtain the extra reward offered at Level 21. In order to accomplish this, you must successfully clear the next stage and overcome the challenges it presents.

By following these recommendations and carefully strategizing your troops' deployment, you can enhance your performance in the Individual Challenge of the Infernal Assault event. Remember to leverage the assistance of your alliance and other players, as teamwork and coordination can significantly contribute to your success. May this guide assist you in your quest to conquer the Infernal Assault and secure the maximum rewards while minimizing troop losses.

title: Infernal Assault 101
summary: The Infernal Assault event in the popular online game Infinity Kingdom is driven by an intriguing background story that captivates players and sets the stage for an exhilarating gaming experience. The narrative unfolds…
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/image-29-1024x1024.png)

### Background Story of Infernal Assault

The Infernal Assault event in the popular online game Infinity Kingdom is driven by an intriguing background story that captivates players and sets the stage for an exhilarating gaming experience. The narrative unfolds in a fantastical world where the mischievous Gnomes, notorious for their disruptive behavior, once posed a significant threat. However, following the momentous fall of Harold's Ice Wall, a pivotal event in the game's lore, a noticeable decline in Gnome activity was observed.

Yet, the resilient Gnomes refused to be easily deterred. Adapting their tactics in response to previous failures, these cunning creatures showcased newfound intelligence and resourcefulness. No longer content with their traditional approach of heading north for supplies, the Gnomes displayed a remarkable shift in behavior. They began venturing to the front lines, constructing weaponry on-site to further their wicked agenda.

This strategic evolution resulted in the creation of Core Furnaces, instrumental in the Gnomes' nefarious endeavors. It is imperative to thwart the Gnomes' progress and put an end to their infernal assault. The fate of the realm hangs in the balance, and players must rise to the challenge, uniting their forces to counter the relentless onslaught of these resilient adversaries.

*Special thank you to player Tea who has been kind enough to share much of the information used for this article!*

## Infernal Assault in General

The Infernal Assault event, available in the immersive world of Infinity Kingdom, offers players an opportunity to engage in a thrilling in-game experience. To participate in the Infernal Assault, players must have been on the server for a minimum of three weeks, unlocking access to this challenging event. Spanning three days, the Infernal Assault demands strategy, teamwork, and skill to emerge victorious.

Once unlocked, the event progresses in a specific order, with players required to complete each round sequentially. The Infernal Assault presents players with a distinct set of defenses, specifically designed for this event, presenting a fresh and exciting challenge. Successful completion of the Infernal Assault rewards players with varying quantities of valuable in-game items, enhancing their progress and providing new opportunities for growth.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/image-28-1024x593.png)

Upon conclusion of the event, players have the chance to participate in subsequent iterations of the Infernal Assault on a cyclical basis. By completing the final stage of the event each month, players can continue engaging in this action-packed experience, further refining their skills and reaping greater rewards.

The Infernal Assault is a team-based event that encourages players to coordinate and mobilize their troops to launch an assault on the Gnome camps. The size of the player's team directly affects the bonuses received, making it advantageous to recruit as many teammates as possible. Having a full team significantly reduces troop losses during the assault, increasing the chances of success. It's worth noting that individual attacks contribute to the overall progress of the team, but to earn credit for a level, players must reach the last node, known as the furnace.

Advancing through higher-level camps unlocks additional squad slots, allowing players to optimize their benefits by increasing their squad size up to five slots. This strategic choice enhances their chances of success and maximizes the rewards obtained.

To ensure effective coordination, it is recommended that teammates remain in close proximity. This proximity facilitates collaborative attacks, allowing players to assist each other and conserve valuable Action Points (AP). Even if all marches are engaged in resource gathering, players can still contribute by "joining" the team, providing buffs and support. The Infernal Assault does not require every player to initiate individual attacks; as long as the level criteria are met, all players can participate in the rally and contribute to the alliance's progress.

The Infernal Assault event presents an immersive and cooperative gaming experience, where players must strategize, coordinate, and support each other to overcome the relentless Gnome assault. By triumphing in this epic battle, players not only safeguard their world from chaos but also earn rich rewards.

## Event Rewards

The Infernal Assault event offers rewards to both individuals and alliances, further incentivizing players to participate and excel in this challenging endeavor. There are three categories of rewards available:

1. **Gold Farming**: This event is the single best method and the only event where you are able to consistently farm gold resource. This makes is an extreemly valuable event and one that you want to prioritize until you have all Immortals and Dragons at max level and rank.
2. **Alliance Rewards:** These rewards are distributed based on the accumulation of points earned collectively by the alliance. The more points earned, the greater the rewards bestowed upon the alliance as a whole.
3. **Individual Rewards:** To be eligible for individual rewards, players must meet specific requirements. These rewards are tailored to each player and can include valuable items such as philosopher stones, a coveted resource within the game.
4. **Destroying Core Rewards:** Destroying the core within the Infernal Assault yields additional rewards. The quality and quantity of these rewards are determined by the level of the Infernal Assault. Higher-level events offer superior rewards, incentivizing players to strive for greater challenges and achievements.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/image-31.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/image-30-1024x581.png)

By successfully navigating the Infernal Assault, players have the opportunity to reap substantial rewards, both individually and as part of their alliance. The event not only tests their skills and strategic prowess but also provides a pathway to acquire coveted resources and enhance their progress within the game.

## Further readings
