title: Infinity Kingdom Insignia Workshop: Design an Insignia for the Game
markdown:
![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261004-200250-3lgghg.png)

## 💠How Does the Insignia Workshop Work?

There is no fixed monthly theme. Players are free to create an original insignia inspired by Infinity Kingdom, its Immortals, elements, dragons, events, factions or wider game world.

At the end of each month, the official team reviews the qualified submissions. Outstanding designs can receive additional rewards, while selected insignias may be adapted and released in-game.

If a design is officially adopted:

* The insignia may be added to Infinity Kingdom.
* Its creator receives priority access after release.
* The creator’s name will appear in the insignia’s in-game description.
* The developers determine its final attributes and acquisition method.

This makes the workshop more than an ordinary fan-art competition. Players can make a lasting contribution to the game and receive visible credit for their work.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261004-200106-n5yf4m.png)

## 💠How to Submit an Insignia

Entries must be submitted through the designated **Insignia Workshop event channel** in the official Infinity Kingdom Discord.

Every submission must use the following format:

**Insignia Name:**
**Design Description:**
**Attached Work Image:**

The image itself must meet these requirements:

* PNG format
* Transparent background
* Exactly 100 × 100 pixels
* Only the central insignia pattern
* No insignia frame or background
* Original player-created artwork
* Based on Infinity Kingdom elements and compatible with the game’s visual style

You may submit original designs throughout the month. However, do not submit the same design more than once, as duplicate submissions are considered invalid.

**[PARTICIPATION HERE](https://discord.gg/EQsHnBks)**

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261004-200303-ajkxvk.png)

## 💠Monthly Participation Rewards

Every player who submits a qualified entry receives:

* 500 Gems
* 5 Superior Resource Packages
* 5 Superior Speedup Chests

These rewards make the workshop worth joining even if your design is not selected as one of the month’s outstanding entries.

## 💠Excellence Award

The official team will also select outstanding monthly submissions. Excellence Award winners receive:

* 1,500 Gems
* 9 Philosopher’s Stones
* 15 Superior Resource Packages
* 15 Superior Speedup Chests
* 30 Market Orders

The greatest reward, however, is the possibility of seeing your own insignia added to Infinity Kingdom.

## 💠Important Rules

All submitted work must be original. Plagiarism or reposting someone else’s artwork results in disqualification from the current workshop and the following three months.

Designs must not contain violent, pornographic or politically sensitive material. Entries that do not fit Infinity Kingdom’s style or comply with the event rules may be removed.

By submitting, players allow the official team to modify and use their work. Creators retain authorship rights and must be credited whenever the design is used officially.

Monthly rewards are distributed within 72 hours after the results are announced. The final appearance, attributes and availability of any adopted insignia remain at the discretion of the Infinity Kingdom team.

## 💠Why Players Should Participate

The Insignia Workshop is a genuinely interesting form of community-driven development. Instead of merely voting on content created by the developers, players can design something that may become a permanent part of Infinity Kingdom.

The workshop is now entering another monthly round, so there should be repeated opportunities to participate. Whether you are an experienced artist, enjoy casual graphic design or simply have a good concept for an insignia, this is a chance to contribute to the game, earn useful rewards and potentially have your name recorded inside Infinity Kingdom.

Head to the official Infinity Kingdom Discord, visit the Insignia Workshop event channel and take a look at what the community is creating. Even if you do not submit an entry this month, the designs themselves are well worth following.

title: Infinity Kingdom Launches Jadwiga Creator Event – Oct. 2026
markdown:
![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261029-105358-s4khne.png)

## What Is the Jadwiga Creation Design Event?

The event challenges players to create original content inspired by Jadwiga, the recently introduced Immortal.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261029-104351-ph7xbc.png)

There are very few restrictions on what you can create. The organizers explicitly welcome different creative formats, including:

* **Artwork and illustrations:** Draw or digitally design your own interpretation of Jadwiga.
* **Wallpapers and posters:** Create beautiful or dramatic artwork featuring the new Immortal.
* **Immortal skins and outfits:** Design your own outfit concept for Jadwiga.
* **Stories and lore:** Write an original story inspired by Jadwiga and the world of Infinity Kingdom.
* **Creative character concepts:** Explore Jadwiga's personality, emotions, or alternative appearances.

Hand-drawn artwork, Photoshop creations, and **AI-assisted designs are all allowed**, provided submissions are original, comply with the rules, and remain recognizable as Jadwiga.

The organizers also encourage participants to include design notes explaining their creative decisions, such as color choices, inspiration, and character details.

## Free Rewards for Everyone for consistent participation!

Simply participating with an eligible submission earns a reward package.

That's a nice collection of resources for creating something fun and sharing it with the community.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261029-104324-7y59g9.png)

### Additional Rewards for the Top 10

The Infinity Kingdom team will select **10 outstanding submissions**, whose creators will receive additional rewards:

These are additional to the standard participation rewards, giving selected creators a total of 2,000 Gems, 12 Philosopher's Stones, and other useful items.

## Exclusive Creator Avatar Frame

There's also a special reward for players who regularly participate in these community events.

Players who have participated in **three Creator Theme Events in total** will receive an exclusive Creator Avatar Frame.

So even if you're not particularly interested in competitive art contests, participating now can help you work toward this collectible cosmetic reward.

## How to Participate

To enter, simply create your Jadwiga-inspired submission and post it in the designated[ **\#creator-event・jadwiga-creation-design**](https://discord.gg/QhMVhAzduC) channel on the official Infinity Kingdom Discord server.

Make sure your work is original, clearly connected to Jadwiga, and follows the event's design requirements.

**Submission deadline: November 8, 2026.**

## Our Take – Give It a Try!

Community creation events are a great opportunity to do something different in Infinity Kingdom.

We spend plenty of time optimizing Immortal builds, calculating event probabilities, and fighting over territory. Sometimes it's nice to celebrate the artwork, characters, and stories that make the game interesting in the first place.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261029-104408-k70c8u.png)

With AI-assisted artwork explicitly permitted, you don't necessarily need to be an experienced illustrator to participate. You can experiment with creative concepts, design a custom outfit, or even write your own short story.

**Let your imagination loose, show the Infinity Kingdom community your version of Jadwiga, and don't forget to submit before November 8!**

title: Infinity Kingdom Lore Series – Chapter 10: In the Name of Salvation
markdown: ## 💠 The First Stone and Its Three Fragments The episode opens with a flashback to an ancient catastrophe. ![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261015-223839-rtjyty.png) A temple burns as people fight over a powerful artifact known as the **First Stone**. To prevent further disaster, its keeper divides the stone into three fragments and sends them to distant lands. The keeper believes that separating the fragments will prevent anyone from reuniting them and unleashing another catastrophe. ![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261015-223821-tfl93f.png) However, we learn that the final fragment was entrusted to the palace of Vitas. This is a significant revelation. Throughout the series, we've encountered references to mysterious stones, ancient powers, and the Council's attempts to manipulate forces beyond ordinary human understanding. Now we know that at least one important artifact was deliberately divided to keep its power out of anyone's hands. Naturally, that raises an obvious question: what happens if someone manages to bring all three fragments together again? ## 💠 A Dangerous Return to Vitas We then follow Kael and a mysterious older man wearing a monocle as they prepare to enter the royal palace. Kael is carrying a small chest containing two glowing red fragments. These appear to be the same ancient stones introduced in the opening sequence. Meanwhile, Vitas is facing a serious military threat. ![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261015-223910-53p9hy.png) An army of dwarves has gathered outside the city, deploying enormous cannons and preparing to attack its defenses. The situation inside the palace is understandably tense. When Kael and his companions enter the throne room, they are greeted by the king and a mysterious woman carrying a staff. The woman clearly knows Kael and remarks that he has finally returned. There is an immediate sense that these characters share a history we haven't yet been told about. ## 💠 The King's Desperate Plan During the confrontation, the king reveals that the royal family has been safeguarding the final fragment of the First Stone. With Kael bringing the other two fragments to Vitas, all three are now within reach. The king is desperate. The dwarven army is approaching, and the city may soon fall. He asks the mysterious woman to help save Vitas. At first glance, this sounds like a reasonable request from a ruler trying to protect his people. But given everything we've learned about ancient stones and dangerous experiments throughout the series, bringing together three fragments that were deliberately separated to prevent catastrophe seems like a remarkably bad idea. And things are about to become even more suspicious. ## 💠 The Worldheart and a Terrifying Revelation The man with the monocle reveals that he was responsible for writing a binding spell. However, when the ancient fragments are brought together, he realizes something is wrong. Rather than simply saving Vitas, the ritual appears connected to a much larger and more dangerous plan. He reveals that the King's sorcerer is in fact **draining the Worldheart to summon heroes**. ![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261015-224205-ipcghq.png) This is perhaps the most fascinating revelation in the chapter. In Infinity Kingdom, Immortals are legendary heroes summoned to fight alongside players. Until now, the animated lore series has largely focused on the consequences of alchemical experimentation and the manipulation of souls. The mention of summoning heroes through the Worldheart potentially connects those mysteries to one of the fundamental mechanics of Infinity Kingdom itself. Could the power required to summon Immortals come at a terrible cost to the world? And could the Alchemical Council's experiments be connected to this process? These are still theories, but the implications are fascinating. ## 💠 Salvation at Any Cost? As the ritual begins, glowing red energy spreads through the city. The mysterious woman channels the power of the fragments, and figures begin to materialize around her. ![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261015-224101-iy6v3o.png) What initially appears to be an attempt to protect Vitas takes on a much darker appearance. The woman believes that she is acting in the name of salvation, but the monocled man's warning suggests that the ritual may sacrifice far more than anyone realizes. It's an interesting continuation of one of the series' recurring themes: the pursuit of extraordinary power by people who believe they are serving a greater good. We've seen similar justifications surrounding the Alchemical Council's experiments, and now the same ideology appears to have reached the heart of Vitas itself. ## 💠 Brynhild Confronts Kael The episode ends with a dramatic confrontation. As the mysterious woman commands those around her to kneel, Brynhild draws her sword and turns toward Kael. ![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261015-224340-d867ru.png) And with that, the chapter ends. It's a rather excellent cliffhanger. For much of the series, Brynhild and our Hangover Knight have been traveling together, uncovering the Council's secrets and investigating the mysterious stones. Now, however, we have to wonder whether Kael has been telling us everything. He clearly has connections to powerful people in Vitas, and his arrival with two fragments has helped make this dangerous ritual possible. Was he aware of what would happen? Has he been manipulated? Or is there something more complicated going on? Whatever the answer, Brynhild certainly doesn't appear willing to stand quietly by. ## 💠 My Take – Are We Finally Learning How Immortals Are Summoned? Chapter 10 might be one of the most important episodes of *Resonance of the Sacred Emblem* so far. The revelations about the First Stone and its three fragments give us a much clearer understanding of the ancient power everyone seems to be pursuing. But what really caught my attention was the reference to the Worldheart. The possibility that summoning legendary heroes requires draining an ancient source of power opens up some interesting questions about Infinity Kingdom's wider mythology. We've already seen the Alchemical Council experimenting with warrior souls, attempting to create enhanced soldiers, and pursuing the power to forge a false god. Could all these experiments ultimately be different approaches to controlling the same source of power? I'm also very interested in Kael. After following the Hangover Knight for so many chapters, we're finally learning more about his identity and his connections to Vitas. He may turn out to be considerably more important than his occasionally ridiculous behavior has suggested. And then there's Brynhild, who once again finds herself standing against forces that seem willing to sacrifice others in pursuit of power. The chapter leaves us with plenty of questions, but one thing seems increasingly clear: **the greatest threat to Norheim may not be the armies fighting its wars, but the people claiming they can save it.** ## 💠 Follow the Story *Resonance of the Sacred Emblem* continues to expand Infinity Kingdom's lore, introducing new mysteries surrounding the Immortals, ancient artifacts, and the Alchemical Council. We'll continue following Brynhild and Kael as the story unfolds, particularly now that their journey has brought them face to face with the powers controlling Vitas. *IK-Wiki is a fan-run, community-supported resource for Infinity Kingdom players.*

title: Infinity Kingdom Lore Series – Chapter 9: Ruslan
markdown: **[Watch Chapter 9 – Ruslan on Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/reel/1066171459131883)** ## 💠 The Alchemical Council's Experiments The episode opens with a rather disturbing look inside an alchemical laboratory. We learn that the empire's desire for military strength and resources led to experiments involving human DNA. Through alchemy, researchers began modifying living bodies, reinforcing bones, strengthening muscles, and even incorporating steel into their creations. The result is an army of monstrous, artificially enhanced soldiers. ![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261015-222507-nqoj3o.png) This is particularly interesting when we consider what we already know about the Council. Earlier chapters revealed that it was harvesting the souls of fallen warriors to power its experiments, supposedly as part of an effort to forge a false god. Now we're seeing another side of that experimentation: the creation of living weapons. Whether these experiments are directly connected to the false god remains unclear, but the Council is certainly becoming one of the most dangerous forces in Norheim. ## 💠 Welcome to Ruslan Meanwhile, Brynhild and our Hangover Knight arrive in Ruslan, hoping to pass through the region without attracting too much attention. That plan doesn't last particularly long. The landscape is devastated by war, with ruined fortifications and the remains of battles scattered across the desert. Our travelers are soon confronted by armored soldiers who mistake them for merchants from Vitas. ![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261015-222619-nkctg0.png) The encounter gives us another interesting glimpse into Norheim's political situation. Ruslan appears to be caught in a prolonged conflict, and the region's soldiers are clearly suspicious of outsiders. Our Hangover Knight manages to talk his way through the confrontation, although not without a little improvisation. I've grown rather fond of this character. He continues to approach dangerous situations with an almost ridiculous level of confidence, which provides some welcome humor in an increasingly dark story. ## 💠 A Mysterious Survivor and the Council's Plans After the encounter, our travelers discover an injured man among the remains of the fighting. Before dying, the stranger makes a cryptic statement about the alchemists, describing them as new gods sent to save the world. It's another indication that the Council's work may have developed into something resembling a religious or ideological movement. At least some people appear to believe that the alchemists are humanity's salvation rather than a threat. The man is also carrying a mysterious document covered in ancient symbols. ![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261015-222642-dfzbrg.png) When our Hangover Knight examines it, he recognizes its significance but cannot decipher the writing. According to him, **only a Valkyrie's Sight can unravel the runes**. Given that Brynhild is a Valkyrie, this is a particularly interesting development. Her importance to the story may extend far beyond her fighting abilities. Perhaps the Valkyries possess knowledge or supernatural abilities that are essential to understanding the Council's plans. The episode doesn't explain exactly what Valkyrie's Sight involves, but it certainly gives us another reason to pay attention to Brynhild's mythological background. ## 💠 The Sorcerer's Stone Returns The chapter ends with another intriguing development. A mysterious man wearing a monocle approaches our travelers. He appears to know something about the ancient document and the Council's activities. More importantly, he reveals that they are looking for information about the Sorcerer's Stone. This brings us straight back to one of the biggest mysteries of the series. In earlier chapters, the Philosopher's Stone appeared to be connected to the Council's experiments and its efforts to manipulate the souls of fallen warriors. We also learned about an ancient covenant between humanity and the Goddess, suggesting that the stone might have a much deeper significance within Norheim's history. The English subtitles again use the term Sorcerer's Stone, which appears to refer to the same mysterious object. If this new character understands the stone, he might finally be able to explain what the Council wants with it and why Brynhild and the Hangover Knight have become involved. Of course, whether he can be trusted is another matter entirely. ## 💠 My Take – The Council's Influence Is Growing Chapter 9 continues building the larger mystery surrounding the Alchemical Council, but what I find most interesting is how its influence appears to extend across Norheim. We began this story with a mysterious emblem discovered in the black market of Vitas. Since then, we've encountered underground laboratories, stolen warrior souls, experiments involving artificial divinity, and now alchemically enhanced soldiers in the middle of a war. The Council is clearly involved in much more than a single secret experiment. I'm also particularly interested in the reference to Valkyrie's Sight. Brynhild's connection to Valhalla was already important when we discovered the imprisoned warrior souls, and now her Valkyrie heritage may hold the key to deciphering ancient texts. I really like seeing the writers incorporate these mythological details into the story rather than treating Immortals as ordinary fantasy soldiers. And then there's our Hangover Knight, whose identity remains one of the series' longest-running mysteries. For now, the biggest questions are whether the Council is deliberately fueling the conflict in Ruslan, what the ancient document reveals, and how these new alchemical soldiers connect to the attempt to forge a false god. Most importantly, what does the mysterious stranger know about the Philosopher's Stone? Hopefully, Chapter 10 will bring us a little closer to finding out. ## 💠 Follow the Journey *Resonance of the Sacred Emblem* continues to explore the history, mythology, and mysteries behind the world of Infinity Kingdom. You can follow the previous chapters and our ongoing lore analysis here on IK-Wiki as we uncover more about Brynhild, the Hangover Knight, and the Alchemical Council.

title: Infinity Kingdom New Player Talent Guide
summary: Starting on a new server in Infinity Kingdom can be exciting and challenging. To ensure smooth growth and progression, this guide focuses on how to allocate your talent points efficiently as a beginner. Talents are…
markdown:
Starting on a new server in Infinity Kingdom can be exciting and challenging. To ensure smooth growth and progression, this guide focuses on how to allocate your talent points efficiently as a beginner. Talents are unlocked at level 5, and as a new player, prioritizing the **Development** talent tree is key to rapid growth.

---

## Talent System Overview

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/image-102-1024x551.png)

### Talent Trees

Infinity Kingdom offers two talent trees:

1. **Development**: Focused on growth and economic boosts, ideal for new players.
2. **Military**: Geared towards troop and battle enhancements, essential for mid-to-late game PvE and PvP content.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/image-103-1024x564.png)

### Talent Pages

You have access to three "Talent Pages," allowing you to preset different talent configurations. These are particularly useful as you unlock more talent points and need to switch between setups for specific tasks such as dragon upgrades or PvP encounters.

- **Page 1**: Development (Primary for beginners)
- **Page 2**: Dragon Upgrade (Unlocked at level 21)
- **Page 3**: Military (For later stages of the game)

For advanced talent builds beyond level 40, refer to specific guides.

---

## Beginner Talenting Strategy

### Why Development First?

As a beginner, focus exclusively on the **Development** tree. Military bonuses are negligible at early levels due to low stats, and rapid economic growth is crucial. The Development tree provides significant boosts to your resource generation, building speed, and technology upgrades.

### Step-by-Step Talent Allocation

#### Levels 5-20: Early Growth

1. **Building Speed** (1 point): Your first talent point should go here to accelerate construction.
2. **Massive Construction** (5 points): Increases building speed further, essential for faster castle upgrades.
3. **Experienced** (1 point): Grants bonus experience to your immortals, helping them level up quickly.
4. **Plentiful Gold** (5 points): Gold is a critical resource, and this talent boosts its production.
5. **Divine Walker** (1 point): Provides free marches every 8 hours, saving precious Action Points (AP).
6. **Leaps and Bounds** (5 points): Boosts technology upgrade speed by 10%.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/image-106-1024x507.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/image-107-1024x350.png)

By the time you reach level 20, you should have a balanced setup optimized for construction and technology upgrades.

#### Level 21+: Advanced Development Setup

At level 21, you must split your Development focus into two distinct talent trees:

1. **Technology Speed Tree**:  - Use this setup most of the time, as research is a key aspect of growth.
2. **Dragon Upgrade Tree**:  - Switch to this setup right before initiating a dragon upgrade, then revert to the Technology Speed Tree.

### Talent Allocation for Level 21+

### Technology Speed Focus:

- **Massive Construction** (5 points): Maintains building speed boost.
- **Experienced** (1 point): Retains immortal XP bonus.
- **Plentiful Gold** (5 points): Continues to enhance gold production.
- **Divine Walker** (1 point): Keeps free marches active.
- **Leaps and Bounds** (5 points): Maximizes technology upgrade speed.

**Dragon Upgrade Focus:** Follow specific guides for dragon-focused talent setups to maximize dragon growth efficiency.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/image-108-1024x445.png)

---

## Tips for Efficient Talent Use

1. **Preserve AP**: Avoid unnecessary marches and save AP for critical activities.
2. **Resource Management**: Use talents like Plentiful Gold to address early resource shortages.
3. **Switch Wisely**: Use your free resets strategically, especially as you transition to dragon upgrades and Military talents later in the game. It costs gems to swap, so make sure you plan your progress and swaps between technology and dragon talents.
4. **Plan Ahead**: Monitor your castle and research upgrade timelines to optimize talent usage.

By following this guide, you’ll establish a solid foundation for growth, ensuring you’re well-prepared for the challenges ahead. Good luck in Norheim!

title: Infinity Kingdom Patch 3.0.1: Alliance Rewards, Judge and the Changing
summary: Patch 3.0.1 brings two important developments to Infinity Kingdom: a
markdown:
![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261121-153248-uadcec.png)

Alliance War Points create another route to Chaos, Holy and Shadow Immortal fragments, while Operation Frontline gives alliances convoy escorts and interceptions to organize. On the battlefield, Judge introduces a new source of repeated magical damage, Horus becomes harder to counter through dispels, Charles gains faster energy regeneration, and Yi Sun-Shin trades some damage reduction for additional Defense.

The result is a patch with potential benefits for everyday progression and some significant questions for established formations. Here is what changes, why it matters and what to consider before adjusting your builds.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261121-153241-v2xy31.png)

## Alliance War Points: A New Route to Valuable Rewards

Alliance War Points can be earned directly through alliance events or distributed by alliance leadership from event rewards. They are spent in the Alliance Shop, whose announced rewards include **Chaos Immortal fragments, Holy and Shadow Immortal fragments, and Ability Stones**.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261121-153329-7s3di9.png)

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261121-153356-mr5ad8.png)

That is an important addition for players developing expensive Immortals over time. Another acquisition route can make progress less dependent on individual spending events, provided the amount earned and the shop’s prices make the rewards realistically accessible.

However, the presence of Chaos fragments in a shop does not establish how quickly players can develop an Immortal. Before judging its value, check the live prices, purchase limits, available selections and your own War Point income. A small regular supply can still be worthwhile, but it should be evaluated as part of a longer development plan.

The distribution system also gives alliance leadership more responsibility. Clear expectations about participation and reward allocation will help members understand what they can earn and how to contribute.

## Operation Frontline: Escorts, Interceptions and Alliance Coordination

Operation Frontline is the new convoy event accessed through the alliance interface. Alliances dispatch transports and defend their supplies, while other alliances can organize interception rallies.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261121-153316-738bef.png)

Participation requires **Alliance Level 2 and Castle Level 10**. Only R5 and R6 members can create convoys, making scheduling an alliance responsibility.

### Guardians and Transporters Have Different Roles

Guardians take the combat role and can be challenged by interception squads. Their rewards depend on convoy type and the supplies remaining, with the relevant War Points distributed by alliance leadership.

Transporters participate without being challenged in combat and receive a smaller amount of War Points upon successful delivery. This gives players a way to participate without taking the same defensive role as the alliance’s stronger accounts.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261121-153027-5dibj8.png)

Successful interceptions award War Points to participating members. Failed interceptions provide no reward, so use your daily attempt on a target your group has a realistic chance of defeating.

### Make Participation Work for Your Alliance

The practical challenge is giving members a reasonable opportunity to join while protecting valuable deliveries. Publish convoy times, account for different time zones and explain how Guardian rewards will be distributed.

Strong defenders can protect the convoy, while Transporter opportunities give less-developed accounts a useful participation route. Repeatedly filling every lineup with the same small group limits the wider benefit of the system.

For individual players, learn your alliance’s schedule and use the participation opportunities available to you. For leadership, treat the event as a recurring progression activity that needs organization, rather than assuming the daily convoy allowance will manage itself.

## Judge: A New Legendary Magical Damage Skill

Judge is a Legendary passive obtained through the **Legendary Season Wish Shop**. It deals magical damage to all enemies every six seconds, with **50% increased damage against targets affected by Punishment**.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261121-153429-zdbwf6.png)

At maximum level, its base damage rate is 500%. The Punishment bonus raises that coefficient to an effective 750% against affected targets, before other damage modifiers and defenses are considered.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261121-153049-c59320.png)

This makes Horus an obvious partner because his ultimate applies Punishment. However, **Judge does not require Horus to be its bearer**. Its bonus checks the enemy’s status, so another magical attacker in a formation containing Horus can also be considered.

The important decision is which Immortal makes the best use of the skill and what they must give up to equip it. Putting Judge on Horus consumes one of his slots; assigning it elsewhere may preserve his existing setup while adding another source of damage.

Also consider timing. Judge attacks on a six-second interval, while Punishment lasts six seconds after being applied. Its bonus depends on which targets are affected when each hit occurs. Strong synergy on paper still needs to translate into useful damage during the actual battle.

## Horus: Less Damage Amplification, More Reliable Punishment

Horus’s Punishment can no longer be dispelled. In exchange, its maximum damage-taken increase falls from **15% to 10%**. His passive damage cap and ultimate’s base damage are unchanged in these notes.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261121-153059-h0a7nq.png)

Against opponents who previously removed Punishment, this improves the reliability of Horus’s contribution. The effect can remain for its duration, helping both the formation’s damage and Judge’s conditional bonus.

Against opponents who were not removing it, the lower amplification is a genuine reduction. Whether the overall change benefits Horus therefore depends partly on the opponents he faces.

**Undispellable also does not mean permanently active.** Punishment still has a 60% application chance and a limited duration. Horus needs to cast, successfully apply it and maintain useful coverage through the battle.

## Yi Sun-Shin: Damage Reduction and Defense Are Different

Yi Sun-Shin’s Guard of Devotion receives the patch’s most important defensive tradeoff. At maximum level, its damage reduction falls from **30% to 20%**, while the skill adds **20% Physical and Magical Defense** during its protection window.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261121-153114-khbvzb.png)

The new percentages cannot simply be added together. Defense and damage reduction affect combat differently, so 20% Defense does not automatically replace the lost 10 percentage points of damage reduction.

### How Large Is the Damage-Reduction Loss?

Looking only at that component, an incoming damage amount of 100 becomes 70 under the old 30% reduction and 80 under the new 20% reduction. That is approximately **14.3% more damage received before accounting for the newly added Defense**.

For the new Defense to offset that difference in this simplified comparison, it would need to reduce the incoming amount before this damage-reduction step by 12.5%.

This calculation illustrates the tradeoff; it is not a prediction of the final battle result. The actual outcome depends on the damage source, attack and defense interactions, and other active effects.

For players already using YSS, the sensible response is to evaluate familiar matchups before replacing him. Check whether the formation survives the same pressure, how well the protection window covers important enemy attacks, and whether another defensive Immortal produces better results.

## Charles the Great: A Meaningful Energy Regeneration Buff

Charles’s base Energy Regen increases from **64 to 80 points per second**, a 25% improvement. That gives him a stronger foundation for reaching his ultimate and reapplying Terra Shield.

Looking at regeneration alone, the time needed to accumulate a fixed amount of energy falls by 20%. Actual casting intervals will also reflect other energy sources, energy reduction and control effects.

The value of the buff depends on whether earlier shields arrive at useful moments. A shield before a major enemy burst can change the result, while shields that are quickly stripped or overwhelmed may provide less benefit.

Charles is therefore worth revisiting if you already have him developed, particularly alongside the changes to YSS. The patch does not establish that he becomes the better choice in every formation.

## Activity Gifts and Additional Alliance Rewards

Alliance Gifts now include **Activity Gifts** alongside the recharge-based gifts, which are renamed **Golden Gifts**. Activity Gifts can come from Daily Missions, Infernal Assault and Alliance Supply Convoys.

Infernal Assault also adds Alliance War Points and Alliance Activity Chests to its rewards. Together, these changes give regular alliance participation more progression value and make consistent activity relevant to the rewards shared within the group.

Gilded Club receives new Active Quests, with Chaos Immortal Selection Chests among the Fortune Wheel rewards mentioned in the notes. Their presence alone does not establish good value; check the actual milestones and coin requirements before planning around them.

## Quality-of-Life Improvements

Several smaller changes reduce repetitive actions and simplify event management.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261121-153130-f49kp5.png)



When managing Illusion Battlefield participants, remember that using Select All again overrides manual deselections. Complete the bulk selection first, then make individual changes.

## Skill Description Corrections Are Not Additional Balance Changes

The developers also clarified that the revised English skill descriptions are **text-only corrections**. They do not change skill effects, values or battle behavior.

Those corrections include clarifications about whose damage triggers an effect, which types of skills receive a trigger-probability bonus, and how certain defensive effects are described.

Keep these separate from the explicit YSS, Horus and Charles adjustments. A clearer tooltip may change how we understand an existing mechanic without changing what happens in battle.

## What Should Players Focus On?

For developing accounts, the alliance systems are the most useful starting point. Learn the convoy schedule, participate in events that award War Points and compare the shop’s options with your long-term Immortal plans.

For players using YSS or Charles, revisit the defensive performance of your current formation before committing resources to a replacement. The patch changes their relative strengths, but the right choice still depends on the team and opponents.

For Legendary Season players considering Judge, identify its intended bearer and the skill it would replace. Judge’s interaction with Punishment is clear, while its best placement and practical advantage over an existing setup require comparison.

## Final Thoughts

Patch 3.0.1 gives alliances a more direct role in player progression while changing several important combat decisions. War Points and convoy rewards create opportunities for steady development, provided members can participate and the shop economy supports meaningful progress.

The combat changes reward a closer look at individual formations. Horus gains more reliable Punishment, Judge adds a new damage option, Charles reaches his shields faster, and YSS exchanges part of his damage reduction for Defense.

Use those confirmed changes to decide what to test. They provide good reasons to revisit builds, without making every early verdict or proposed replacement an established upgrade.

## Sources and Further Reading

*   [Official v3.0.1 Patch Notes](https://infinitykingdom.gtarcade.com/en/news/7025357.html?utm_)


*   [Official Skill Description Corrections](https://infinitykingdom.gtarcade.com/en/news/7025373.html?utm)

title: Infinity Kingdom Troop Tiers Guide – T1 to T9 Stats, Power Differences &
markdown:
![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-103246-h2t1t2.png)

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-103527-p37p3g.png)

With Legendary Season introducing **Tier 9 troops at Barracks level 60**, it's time to look at how all nine tiers compare, how much stronger each upgrade makes your troops, and why troop attributes become increasingly important as your account develops.

All the statistics in this guide have been collected directly from the in-game Barracks menus in November 2026.

## TL;DR – How Much Stronger Are Higher-Tier Troops?

Moving to a new troop tier increases the base attributes of every soldier of that type.

The early tiers offer particularly large percentage improvements, often increasing Attack and Defense by approximately 50% per upgrade. From T5 onward, progression becomes more gradual, but the bonuses remain substantial.

The latest T8-to-T9 upgrade provides approximately:

* **+19% base Troop Attack**
* **+19% base Troop Defense**
* **+11% base Troop HP**
* **+28% Troop Load**

These are increases to the troops' base attributes, not guaranteed increases to final combat damage or total march power.

By T9, individual soldiers have roughly ten times the base Attack and Defense of their T1 counterparts, while HP has increased by more than four times.

## All Nine Troop Tiers and Unlock Requirements

Infinity Kingdom currently has nine troop tiers, unlocked by upgrading the Barracks responsible for training each troop type.

Each of the four troop types has its own Barracks, allowing players to upgrade their Shieldmen, Spearmen, Cavalry, and Bowmen independently.

When a Barracks reaches the next tier threshold, the existing troops of that type are automatically upgraded. You don't need to retrain your entire army from scratch.

This is why players should generally fill their Training Grounds before completing a major Barracks upgrade. Converting an existing stockpile of soldiers can save substantial resources compared with training large numbers of higher-tier troops afterward.

## Complete Troop Attack Comparison – T1 to T9

Attack is the most obvious offensive attribute. Higher Attack increases the offensive potential of soldiers, although final battle damage depends on several additional mechanics.

The following table shows the base Attack attributes of every troop type.

An interesting observation is that Spearmen have the highest base Attack across every tier, followed by Cavalry. Shieldmen and Bowmen have identical base Attack values.

This doesn't automatically mean Spearmen deal the most total damage in every situation. Attack frequency, targeting, troop counters, Immortal skills, and the combat damage formula all influence the actual result.

Nevertheless, the numerical progression demonstrates how dramatically troop Attack improves as new tiers become available.

For example, T9 Shieldmen have 225 base Attack compared with just 22 at T1. That's more than ten times the starting value.

Even compared with T8, the difference is substantial: 189 Attack increases to 225, a gain of approximately 19%.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-103039-fxzfvf.png)

## Complete Troop Defense Comparison – T1 to T9

Defense improves the ability of troops to withstand incoming attacks.

As expected, Shieldmen have the highest base Defense, while Bowmen have the lowest.

The Defense improvements follow almost exactly the same percentage pattern as Attack.

At T9, Shieldmen reach 213 base Defense, compared with 179 at T8. That represents another approximately 19% increase.

This is particularly important for frontline Immortals, whose troops must withstand enemy attacks throughout the battle.

However, Bowmen also benefit considerably from higher Defense. Although they normally fight from the back row, additional survivability becomes valuable against area attacks, targeting effects, and abilities that threaten the backline.

## Complete Troop HP Comparison – T1 to T9

HP determines the health available to individual soldiers.

Unlike Attack and Defense, HP scales somewhat differently between tiers, especially after T5.

Cavalry have the highest base HP, reaching 525 at T9. Shieldmen follow with 500, while Spearmen and Bowmen have 465 and 430 respectively.

The difference between T8 and T9 is approximately 11% for most troop types, slightly lower for Bowmen.

HP has grown much less rapidly than Attack and Defense over the complete progression from T1 to T9.

This is an important distinction. Higher-tier soldiers aren't simply scaled-up versions of earlier troops with every attribute increasing by the same percentage.

Attack and Defense have increased roughly tenfold, while HP has increased approximately fourfold.

The relative balance between these attributes therefore changes considerably as players advance through the game.

## How Much Power Does Each New Troop Tier Add?

Looking at individual attributes is useful, but the most interesting question is how much stronger your soldiers become whenever you unlock a new tier.

The following table calculates the average percentage increases across all four troop types.

These are changes in base troop attributes. They shouldn't be interpreted as direct percentage increases in overall march damage, durability, or victory probability.

### Early Tiers – Enormous Relative Gains

The most dramatic percentage increases occur between T1 and T5.

For example, moving from T3 to T4 increases Attack and Defense by approximately 50%, while HP increases by 25%.

These upgrades can make an enormous difference for developing accounts, especially when fighting other players who have not yet reached the same troop tier.

This also explains why reaching an important Barracks milestone can be more impactful than several smaller upgrades to other parts of your account.

### T5 to T8 – More Gradual Progression

Once players reach T5, the relative increases become smaller.

Moving from T5 to T6 provides approximately 24% additional Attack and Defense, while T6 to T7 provides around 20%.

The increase from T7 to T8 is slightly smaller again, at approximately 17%.

However, it's important not to underestimate these improvements.

By this stage, players are commanding much larger armies, and the base attributes of individual troops are already considerably higher.

Even a relatively modest percentage increase can therefore represent a substantial amount of additional raw troop strength.

### T8 to T9 – A Significant Legendary Upgrade

Interestingly, T9 breaks the gradual decline in percentage improvements.

Instead of continuing toward a smaller bonus, the upgrade from T8 to T9 provides approximately 19% additional Attack and Defense, compared with the 17% received when moving from T7 to T8.

The HP improvement is also greater than the previous two tier upgrades.

This makes T9 particularly interesting for players entering Legendary Season.

Reaching Barracks level 60 isn't simply a small additional increase in combat power. It provides a meaningful upgrade to the underlying attributes of every soldier of that troop type.

## T8 vs. T9 – The Exact Differences

Since T9 is the newest troop tier, it's worth looking more closely at its attributes compared with T8.

The percentages are remarkably consistent between the four troop types, with almost identical Attack and Defense improvements.

For practical purposes, players can regard T9 as offering approximately **19% stronger base offensive and defensive attributes** than T8, alongside roughly 11% more base HP.

The upgrade also increases Troop Load from 180 to 230, an improvement of 27.8%. Load helps with resource transport and gathering but isn't itself a combat attribute.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-103105-lm6g3m.png)

## Which Barracks Should You Upgrade First?

Although every troop tier provides substantial bonuses, upgrading all four Barracks simultaneously isn't always the best use of resources.

This becomes particularly important during Legendary Season, where building upgrades beyond level 55 require Energy Core charging in addition to ordinary resources and speedups.

For most players, the best approach is to prioritize the troop types used in their main march.

Bowmen are often an especially important consideration because both back-row Immortals command Bowmen. This means every standard full march uses two Bowman units, making Bowmen relevant across a wide variety of teams.

However, if your main march relies heavily on powerful frontline damage dealers, upgrading the Barracks associated with those Immortals may be equally important.

The goal should be improving the march you actually use for competitive combat rather than spreading resources across troop types you rarely deploy.

Players preparing for T9 should also remember that reaching Castle level 60 doesn't automatically upgrade every troop type. Each relevant Barracks must reach level 60 to unlock its T9 soldiers.

## Why Troop Percentage Bonuses Are So Powerful

One of the most important lessons from troop progression is how valuable percentage-based Troop attributes become in the late game.

Troop Attack, Defense, and HP bonuses affect the soldiers commanded by your Immortals. As the base attributes of these soldiers increase through higher tiers, the raw attribute increase provided by a percentage bonus grows as well.

Consider a simple example.

A T9 Bowman has 225 base Attack. A 5% Troop Attack bonus adds 11.25 Attack per soldier, before considering the wider combat calculation.

For a hypothetical combined backline of 40,000 Bowmen, that represents an additional 450,000 points in the aggregate base Attack pool.

This illustrates how percentage bonuses scale across a large troop stack. But do remember, they are not literal predictions of actual damage inflicted during a battle, which also depends on defensive attributes, existing bonuses, skill effects, and many other combat mechanics and variables.

Nevertheless, they demonstrate why Troop Attack bonuses are so highly valued.

This is also the reason that the **Abyssal Temple castle skin**, sometimes referred to as Abyssal Throne in community discussions, is considered one of the strongest offensive castle skins in Infinity Kingdom.

Its upgradeable Troop Attack bonus ranges from +5% to +15%, applying a powerful percentage modifier to an increasingly large base of troop attributes. The skin also provides a reduction in soldier death rate.

By comparison, modifiers that improve only an Immortal's personal attributes affect a different part of the combat calculation and may provide less overall benefit when troop-derived attributes dominate.

This doesn't mean that every Troop percentage modifier is automatically better than every Immortal modifier in every situation. Their relative effectiveness depends on the attribute, current bonuses, and the formation involved.

However, for late-game combat, percentage-based Troop Attack bonuses are among the most attractive general-purpose offensive improvements available.

We'll explore this relationship in more detail in our upcoming guide comparing the best castle skins for combat, including Abyssal Temple and its alternatives.

## Final Thoughts – How Important Are Troop Tiers?

Troop tiers remain one of the most important progression milestones in Infinity Kingdom.

From T1 to T9, the base Attack and Defense attributes of soldiers increase by approximately ten times, while HP grows by more than four times.

More importantly, these improvements affect the soldiers you actually bring into battle, providing a larger base for your other Troop attributes and percentage bonuses.

For players progressing through the early seasons, reaching each new troop tier should remain a major development objective.

For experienced Conquest players entering Legendary Season, upgrading from T8 to T9 offers an especially attractive improvement: approximately 19% additional base Attack and Defense, alongside around 11% more HP.

And as troop counts increase, the value of powerful Troop percentage bonuses becomes even more apparent.

**My recommendation:** Prioritize the Barracks used by your main march, prepare sufficient troops before completing major tier upgrades, and don't underestimate the combined effect of higher troop tiers and percentage-based Troop buffs.

title: 🛡️ Iron Curtain: Part of the Recent Revival of Earth–Wind Hybrid
summary: A brand-new skill is coming to Infinity Kingdom, and it has the potential to shake up the meta in a big way. It’s called Iron Curtain, and while it’s not available just yet, early previews already have competitive…
markdown:
A brand-new skill is coming to *Infinity Kingdom*, and it has the potential to shake up the meta in a big way. It’s called **Iron Curtain**, and while it’s not available just yet, early previews already have competitive players buzzing.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/image-79-1024x428.png)

At first glance, it may not look like a game-changer — but if you dig deeper, you’ll see why it could **reshape defensive strategies** and potentially **bring back the Earth–Wind hybrid**, one of the classic march archetypes that has fallen out of the spotlight.

---

## ⚔️ What Iron Curtain Does

Iron Curtain is a **passive skill** designed specifically for **physical carries** like Alexander, Poseidon, or Wukong. It has two distinct parts:

1. **Damage Reduction:** When your troop count is above 70%, reduce damage taken by 35%.  - This effectively makes your frontline much harder to burst down in the opening phase of a fight.
- In today’s **burst-heavy meta**, surviving the first ultimate cycle often decides the match. Iron Curtain gives your frontliners a massive cushion, buying critical time.
2. **Barrier Weakening:** When your normal attacks hit, there’s a 60% chance to weaken barriers on all enemies by 30% for 30 seconds.  - The exact mechanics are still being clarified, while it is safe to assume it applies to shield like Charles' ultimate and Energy Shield, we are still finding out if YSS shield effect for example are also part of this. If true, this could finally introduce a **direct counter to YSS based meta teams**.

---

## 🧩 Why This Matters

### Part 1: The Early Damage Reduction

This is where the skill really shines.

- With Iron Curtain, your physical carries take **35% less damage** right at the start, which often means surviving with enough HP to keep swinging.
- Survive longer = more attacks = more lifesteal/healing procs = higher total damage.

It can also be used for **ramp-up strategies** (like Battle Stance or Demonic Contract), which need time before hitting full power.

---

### Part 2: Barrier Weakening

This is trickier. Shielding isn’t dominant in the current meta, so this effect won’t always be relevant. However:

- If Iron Curtain counts *all shielding effects* (YSS’s protection, Charles’ shields, Energy Shield, Fu Fei, etc.), it becomes a flexible soft-counter.
- Against Charles-heavy or tanky hybrid teams, reducing shield strength by 30% can absolutely matter.
- Even if it’s niche right now, it future-proofs physical teams against any shift back toward shield-heavy metas.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/image-80-1024x551.png)

---

## 🌪️ Why This Could Revive Earth–Wind Hybrid

For a long time, Earth–Wind hybrids were feared for their balance of tankiness and strong physical DPS. Then the burst meta pushed them out.

Iron Curtain changes the equation:

- Add in the recent rise of **auto-attack synergies** (new normal attack procs, “Knife Through Butter” style skills), and suddenly **Earth-Wind Hybrids are beginning to look viable again**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/image-81.png)

---

## 🏆 Who Should Use Iron Curtain?

- **Alexander** –Gains survivability for one-on-one fights + benefits from high rate of auto-attacks for procs/triggers.
- **Poseidon** – Becomes harder to delete early, possibly giving him time to ramp his AoE.
- **Any physical-heavy frontline** looking to fight back against shield-setups.

---

## 🔮 Final Thoughts

Iron Curtain may not look flashy at first glance, but its **35% opening damage reduction** alone is decent in today’s meta. Add in the potential of barrier weakening, and its adding up to be a nice skill. I do not think this will be overpowered in any way, and I dont see this as a default skill for every setup. But it is very good to hace an improved physical shield for alex that also counters charles-energy-shield builds. Very good, and a step towards brining back hybrids? Possibly!

👉 Expect to see **Earth–Wind hybrids with Alexander and other physical carries re-enter the Conquest scene** once Iron Curtain goes live. It’s not just a defensive skill — it’s a skill that could mark the start of a new meta cycle.

title: Jadwiga Guide: Skills, Artifact and Team Building
summary: Jadwiga, the Polish Queen, joins Infinity Kingdom as an Epic Earth
markdown:
**That targeting is confirmed through repeated testing across multiple attacks using test marches without interfering skills. Every cast in those tests applied both buffs to two allies.** This gives Jadwiga a particularly interesting role in formations combining physical and magical damage dealers. Her competitive verdict remains open, however. We still need comparisons using a fully developed Jadwiga before declaring her an upgrade over established supports such as Zenobia or Qin. ![](/uploads/screenshot-20261017-233323-h1g2a0.png) ## Jadwiga at a Glance Jadwiga is an offensive support. Twin Crowns strengthens your attackers rather than providing healing or protection, so the rest of the formation needs to supply enough durability to make use of her buffs. ## Twin Crowns Explained Twin Crowns makes two target selections: * The allied Immortal with the **highest Physical Attack**. * The allied Immortal with the **highest Magical Attack**. **Both recipients receive the Attack Speed increase and the damage dealt bonus** for six seconds. The effect cannot stack. ![](/uploads/screenshot-20261017-232713-976emk.png) At maximum level, each selected ally gains **25% increased Attack Speed and 60% increased damage dealt**. Attack Speed increases the frequency of normal attacks, while the damage bonus strengthens damage dealt during the buff window. The bonuses are not divided between the two targets. The physical attacker does not receive only Attack Speed while the magical attacker receives only damage amplification. **Both receive both effects.** ![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261018-193251-rmbcjh.png) ### Targeting Confirmed Through Testing The skill’s wording has caused understandable confusion. The phrase referring to the allied unit with the highest Physical Attack and Magical Attack could be read as selecting one Immortal based on their combined attack stats. Repeated testing resolves that question: Twin Crowns separately selects the highest Physical Attack ally and the highest Magical Attack ally. In our tests, every cast applied the Attack Speed and damage buffs to both recipients. The recording below shows the buffs active on two allies at the same time. Watch Alexander and Loki’s status rows: both display the timed Attack Speed and damage buffs together. ### Video: Twin Crowns Targeting Test
This confirms the targeting behaviour observed in the repeated tests. The battle result itself is not a benchmark for a finished Jadwiga formation. ### Why This Matters for Team Building Jadwiga can support two damage dealers simultaneously, which makes physical-and-magical combinations especially interesting. Alexander can receive the Physical Attack selection while a mage receives the Magical Attack selection, allowing both to benefit from the same cast. However, dealing a particular damage type does not automatically mean an Immortal has the highest corresponding attack stat. Check the actual values in your formation, especially when using unusual builds or Immortals whose damage mechanics involve stat conversion. If your highest Magical Attack belongs to a support with limited damage output, the second selection still occurs, but the formation may gain less from it than a team with a dedicated magical damage dealer. ## Energy Regeneration and Exclusive Artifact Jadwiga’s displayed **83.0 Energy Regen** is solid for a support whose contribution depends on repeatedly casting her ultimate. ![](/uploads/screenshot-20261017-232728-wpydvn.png) Her Exclusive Artifact extends Twin Crowns by three seconds, taking its duration from **six to nine seconds**. That is a **50% increase in duration per application**, giving both selected allies more time to deal damage with the buffs active. It makes the artifact an important part of assessing a developed Jadwiga. Longer duration does not automatically establish permanent coverage. Actual uptime still depends on her casting intervals, survival, control effects and energy disruption. Her Energy Regen stat is encouraging, but replays are needed to judge uptime in competitive battles. ## Potential Team Combinations With the targeting confirmed, the most interesting starting points are formations that give both selections a valuable damage dealer to support. These remain team concepts for testing rather than established best builds. ![]() ![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261018-193713-w4xf7x.png) ### Alexander + Himiko or Loki Combining Alexander with a magical carry such as Himiko or Loki is a natural direction to explore. Alexander can receive the Physical Attack selection, while the magical carry receives the Magical Attack selection. A formation combining **Alexander, Himiko or Loki, Jadwiga and Zenobia** would retain healing while adding offensive amplification for both attackers, provided they hold the relevant highest attack stats. This gives us a reason to revisit Alexander hybrids. Whether Jadwiga adds enough pressure to improve their competitive position still needs testing against comparable opponents. ### Alexander + Louis IX Alexander + Louis is also worth exploring because Twin Crowns can support both of them, provided Alexander has the highest Physical Attack and you somehow are able to get Louis to have the highest Magical Attack. I am not sure if this it possible, but IF it is this could be a new hybrid build in the making! That last condition matters. **Louis dealing magical damage does not automatically establish that his Magical Attack exceeds the supports in the formation.** Check his actual stats, try to boost his magical attack through gems, etc. and confirm the recipients in replays. If the selections line up, this could allow two frontline attackers to benefit from Jadwiga while leaving the remaining backline slot available for another support. Neither version is proven. The first tests whether healing can sustain the attackers through their buff windows; the second tests whether greater offensive pressure justifies giving up Zenobia’s healing. ### Louis + YSS Louis + YSS with Jadwiga and Qin remains another formation to investigate. Louis can be the intended magical recipient, with the physical recipient determined by the actual attack stats of the team. The relevant question for this team is how much value each recipient gains, and whether the formation performs better with Jadwiga than with an alternative support. ![](/uploads/screenshot-20261017-232953-9vogmb.png) ## Does Jadwiga Replace Zenobia or Qin? **TBD.** We still lack enough comparative testing with a fully developed Jadwiga to establish a reliable verdict. Keeping Zenobia preserves healing, while keeping Qin explores a different balance of offensive support. Jadwiga needs to contribute enough additional damage through Twin Crowns to justify what the replaced Immortal brings to the formation. The targeting tests answer how her skill works. They do not yet establish which support pairing wins more battles. That requires comparisons across several fights against comparable opponents, looking at damage, survival and buff uptime. ## Tower of Knowledge Skills Choose Jadwiga’s support skills around the needs of your overall build. She does not need a specific Tower of Knowledge combination to make Twin Crowns function. Healing, protection, energy support and other utility can be distributed according to the formation and the skills already assigned to its other Immortals. The priority is making the whole march work together. ## How to Obtain Jadwiga Jadwiga is obtained through **Elemental Bond**. Select her as your target and collect fragments through the card-matching event using Soulglass Crests. She requires **60 fragments to summon**, with further fragments needed for development. ![](/uploads/screenshot-20261017-232749-ao1roc.png) For the event mechanics and spending approach, see our dedicated [Elemental Bond guide](https://ik-wiki.com/posts/should-you-spend-on-the-elemental-bond-event/). Unlocking her and developing a competitive replacement are separate investment decisions. Her skill progression and Exclusive Artifact both matter when assessing the version you intend to use. ## Final Thoughts Repeated testing confirms the important mechanic: **Twin Crowns selects the ally with the highest Physical Attack and the ally with the highest Magical Attack, giving both recipients both the Attack Speed and damage buffs.** That makes Alexander with Himiko or Loki, and potentially Alexander with Louis, interesting combinations to explore. Solid energy regeneration and an artifact that extends the buff to nine seconds add to her appeal. Her place in the meta remains TBD. The next step is establishing whether that offensive contribution outperforms the healing or utility of the support she replaces in a fully developed formation.
