markdown:
### Introduction

Today we are going to have a look at the perhaps most common question I get during KvK seasons: *"Can I leave my alliance and come back to the KvK??"*. With the updated Legion of Frostborne registration rules, many players are cautious about leaving their alliance once a season approaches. That concern is understandable: registration now matters, and being in the wrong place at the wrong time can lock you out.

However, once registration is complete and Frost begins, **temporary alliance movement is not only allowed—it is often strategically useful**. Understanding *why* experienced players do this helps remove the fear and turns the mechanic into a tool rather than a risk.

---

### Registration vs. Participation: A Quick Reminder

Before getting into reasons, it’s worth restating the core rule clearly:

- You **must** be in the alliance that registers for Frost
- Once registration is finished and the season begins, your Frost eligibility is tied to that alliance
- You may leave and later rejoin **the same alliance** without losing access

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-22-1024x501.png)

Everything below assumes registration has already completed.

---

### Helping Other Alliances in Norheim

The most common and legitimate reason players temporarily leave is to **support allied alliances in Norheim**.

In practice, this happens when:

- A secondary alliance is holding an important zone but lacks enough high-power players
- A sister alliance needs temporary reinforcement for defense or structure pushes
- Leadership wants experienced players embedded elsewhere for coordination

By leaving briefly and joining another alliance, you can:

- Rally and reinforce under their banner
- Contribute honor and pressure where it’s most needed
- Help stabilize fronts without permanently restructuring alliances

Once the objective is complete, you simply return to your registered alliance and continue Frost as normal.

---

### Temporary Support During KvK Itself

Although less common, the same logic can apply **inside Frost**:

- Filling rally slots during critical pushes
- Assisting with timed objectives
- Acting as a bridge between allied groups

As long as you return to the alliance that registered you, your Frost status remains intact.

This flexibility is especially useful on competitive servers where coordination across multiple alliances matters more than rigid structure.

---

### Changing Alliance Color for Honor Buffs

This is the question many players have been hesitant to test, and it’s now confirmed through direct testing:

**You can leave, change alliance color, and rejoin your registered alliance to gain better honor buffs—and it works.**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-23-1024x536.png)

Some players leave briefly to:

- Join a Kingdom where the honor ladder is more favorable to you
- Gain access to stronger honor buffs

And yes. You can re-join alliances and KvK even after changing Kingdom. I have tested directly on alternate accounts and verified to function correctly before being done on mains. As long as the alliance you return to is the one that registered you, Frost participation is unaffected.

---

### Administrative or Structural Adjustments

Occasionally, alliance leadership needs to:

- Reorganize rosters
- Shuffle members between main and secondary alliances
- Resolve temporary capacity issues

In these cases, players may step out briefly while changes are made. Again, timing matters—but once Frost has begun, this can be done safely if handled carefully.

---

### The “Keep Your Members Safe” Kick Trick

Another practical reason to understand alliance leaving and rejoining is **member protection**, especially for offline or inattentive players.

In Frost and Norheim, it’s still common to see situations where:

- An enemy alliance ports aggressively into a cluster
- A member is offline, unshielded, or slow to react
- Leadership needs a fast way to prevent unnecessary losses

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-24.png)

In these cases, **officers can remove a member from the alliance** to force their city out of danger and back to Norheim where the player can re-join the alliance and the KvK when back online.

A few important clarifications:

- This **no longer works on players who are in rage**  - It *used* to, but that interaction was extremely broken and heavily abused
- The developers corrected this, and rage-state players cannot be kicked anymore
- It **does still work** on players who are:  - Offline
- Forgetful
- Sitting in unsafe zones without a bubble

For many alliances, this has become a quiet but effective safety tool—especially during off-hours.

---

### Player Perspective

This is one of the most common questions I am getting asked during KvK seasons. Essentially the system is intentionally designed to **lock registration, not movement**. The developers want to prevent last-minute alliance hopping for KvK advantages, but they also allow flexibility for coordination, support, and optimization once the season is underway.

I’ve personally left and rejoined during Frost seasons for coordination and testing purposes without losing access, rank, or rewards. The only consistent failures I’ve seen come from players leaving *before* registration finalized.

### Conclusion Summary

- Stay in your alliance until Frost registration is complete
- Once the season begins, you may leave and rejoin the same alliance freely
- Temporary moves can help with Norheim support, Frost coordination, and honor optimization
- Changing alliance color for better honor buffs **does work**, when done correctly
- Just remember: registration locks eligibility, not your movement afterward

Used properly, this mechanic gives experienced players flexibility without risk. The key is understanding *when* movement is safe—and why you’re doing it in the first place.

---

title: Legendary Battle Pass (holy/shadow)
summary: Once you hit castle level 40 and you are in season 2, you unlock the Legendary Battle Pass. This article will give you the details you need to understand and plan how to best take advantage of this pass relative to your…
markdown:
Once you hit castle level 40 and you are in season 2, you unlock the Legendary Battle Pass. This article will give you the details you need to understand and plan how to best take advantage of this pass relative to your goals and objectives.

Legendary Battle Pass is the steady, predictable way to build out **Holy** and **Shadow** rosters without relying on lucky pulls. There are two tracks per pass — **Silver Medallion** (free) and **Golden Medallion** (paid, $29.99) — and you level them by doing normal daily stuff like hunting gnomes and collecting resources. There will also be special daily quests that relate to current calendar events, like honor for KE days or Rebels killed for Rebel Event days.
A full cycle runs on your server timeline; if you migrate while it’s active, don’t stress — your progress stays. When a pass ends, the next one syncs to the server’s schedule.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-50-1024x497.png)

---

## How the Two Medallions Work

### Silver Medallion (free):

- **Rewards across level 1–100:**  - 60 × Random Immortal Fragments
- 30 × Random Holy/Shadow Immortal Fragments
- 10 × 30-min Universal Speedups
- 5 × 30-min Training Speedups
- 5 × 30-min Healing Speedups
- 250,000 of each basic resource (no gold)
- Good baseline for F2P or alts. The random Holy/Shadow frags are nice trickle progress.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-49-1024x525.png)

### Golden Medallion ($29.99):

- **Additional rewards on top of Silver:**  - 60 × **Shadow and Light Selection Chest II**
- 60 × Random Holy/Shadow Immortal Fragments
- 1,900 Gems
- **930 Inferno Insignias** (the currency you spend in the BP shop)
- If you’re actively building Holy/Shadow, Golden basically turns steady grind into targeted progress via the shop + selection chests.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-51-1024x617.png)

**Level cap:** Silver medallions go up to **level 50 and Gold continues rewarding Insignias until 100**. You cannot repeat level 100 for additional insignias in the same way as you can repeat the last level of the Golden Pass.

---

## Leveling the Pass (EXP Math You Can Actually Use)

Daily there are **6–7 tasks**, each worth **150 pass EXP**.

- Min-case (6 tasks): **900 EXP/day**
- Often (7 tasks): **1,050 EXP/day**

**Cost per pass level:** 250 EXP
**Total EXP to max to level 100:** **24,750 EXP** (that’s 99 level-ups × 250)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-52-1024x504.png)

### 28-day season floor math:

- Min-case missions: **6 × 28 = 168**
- EXP from those: **168 × 150 = 25,200**
- That’s **more than enough** to hit level 100 without grinding anything extra. You can even miss a few tasks and still cap. Bare in mind, that some days hold 7 daily quests, allowing you to catch up slightly if you missed some tasks during the season.

**Skip option:** If you fall behind, you can buy levels at **600 Gems per level**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-53.png)

**Migration note:** Moving servers during the season **does not** reset your progress.

---

## The Legendary Battle Pass Shop (Holy/Shadow)

This is where the pass really pays out.

- **Inventory:** All **Holy** and **Shadow** Immortals **and their artifacts**.
- **Currency:** **Inferno Insignias** (same currency used later in Peak BP; more on that below).
- **Prices & limits:**  - **60 Immortal Fragments** = **450 insignias** *(limit 4 purchases per cycle)*
- **Artifact** = **600 insignias** *(limit 2 purchases per cycle)*

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-54-1024x484.png)

Quick value gut-check: The Golden track gives **930 insignias**, which is worth **just over two 60-frag packs** (930 ÷ 450 ≈ 2.06 → ~124 frags), or **1 artifact + leftover**. Combine this with the selection chests and you can make a noticeable dent in a Holy/Shadow project every season.

**Tip:** If you are close to castle level 50. You need to know that the currency Insignias are used in both the Legendary and the Peak Battle Pass where you can redeem for Chaos immortals and artifacts. Read below.

---

## Peak Battle Pass (Heads-Up for Castle 50+)

Once you hit **Castle level 50**, there’s also the **Peak Battle Pass** (**[separate guide here](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/development/battle-passes/peak-battle-pass-chaos-immortals-and-artifacts/)**), focused on **Chaos** immortals and artifacts.
The important thing here: **both passes use the same insignia currency**. That means you can **bank insignias across seasons** and spend them in **either** shop.

**So what should you do?**

- **Below C50 and far from it:** It’s totally fine to spend on Holy/Shadow now — you’ll feel the power spike earlier. Not all players have the spending level required to ever complete Chaos Immortals with artifacts and talents requireing a lot of investment. If that is you, going for key shadow or holy immortals and artifacts is perfectly valid!
- **Close to C50 or planning Chaos soon:** Consider **banking insignias** so that, when Peak BP unlocks, you can grab **Chaos** fragments/artifacts. It’s a long grind if you’re going pure Battle Pass, but banking makes the first Peak cycle hit way harder. If you do go for Chaos Immortals remember you need 4750 immortal fragments to upgrade talents after completing the star ranks. **[More on that here](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/immortals/immortal-talent-specializations/upgrading-immortal-talents-and-well-of-time-elite/)**.
- If you plan to **spend real money** specifically for Chaos, banking before C50 is usually the smarter play.

---

## Conclusion Summary

- **Two tracks:** Silver (free) and Golden ($29.99).
- **Leveling is easy:** 6–7 × 150 EXP dailies; you need **24,750 EXP** total; **28 days** at minimum tasks is **25,200 EXP**, so you can cap without sweat.
- **Rewards worth noting:** Golden adds **1,900 Gems**, **930 insignias**, **60 Selection Chest II**, and **60 random Holy/Shadow frags**.
- **Shop:** **450 insignias = 60 frags (limit 4)**, **600 insignias = 1 artifact (limit 2)**. Plan purchases ahead.
- **Think ahead:** Same insignia currency is used in **Peak BP** (C50+ Chaos). If Chaos is your endgame, **bank now** and cash out later.

**Bottom line:** If you’re actively building Holy or Shadow or Chaos later, Golden Medallion is a good value. If Chaos is your target and C50 is close, bank the insignias and go big when Peak unlocks.

---

title: Legendary KvK Explained – What's New in Legion of Frostborne?
summary: Reaching the Legendary Season in Infinity Kingdom introduces one of the
markdown:
![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261029-095930-9l8cvz.png)

While Conquest KvK largely revolves around alliance coordination, PvP strength, thermal towers, and capturing objectives, **Legendary KvK adds new mechanics that make production, specialized professions, and logistical planning essential to winning wars**.

The most important changes are the introduction of three new professions, a completely new Altar Stone system, and Energy Cores that must be destroyed before cities and gates can be captured.

Just like in Conquest, kvk lasts **32 days!** With the addition of altars and roles, you have a **massive time crunch/quota** as a result. Less freedom but more certainty. 

Let's take a look at what changes and what players should expect when entering their first Legendary KvK. 

## From Conquest to Legendary – What Changes?

The familiar foundation of Legion of Frostborne remains. Alliances still compete for territory, fight opposing armies, and attempt to capture strategically important cities and checkpoints.

However, Legendary KvK introduces several new systems that fundamentally change how these objectives are captured.

The result is a more complicated battlefield where even the strongest alliance need to ajust gameplay and strategy accordingly.

## Three New Professions – Everyone Has a Job

The biggest new mechanic is the **Lord Contract System**, which requires players to select one of three professions before the war begins.

* The reason you need people to manually choose contracts/jobs to do is because 

  **any unassigned lords in the alliance will default to Fighting  Master**

  !
* If there is a lack of alchemists and craftsman, you will have a terrible time. These two are essential to play kvk.
* Caps of 90 Fighting Master, 60 Craftsman, 30 alchemists. These are the caps so far. When you have unassigned players not choosing a contract, the game prioritizing FM to max is what will get you, this can be an issue since you need to cap both alchemists and craftsmen in order to keep up with production of materials and alter stones (see later).



![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261030-144525-w4bw6p.png)

Each profession has its own skill tree, objectives, and responsibilities.

### Master Craftsman – The Alliance's Supply Chain

Master Craftsmen form the backbone of the new production system.

Their main responsibility is producing materials that Alchemists need to manufacture Altar Stones. They can also produce temporary Unit Boost items that provide additional combat bonuses to alliance members.

This makes Craftsman an excellent profession for players who may not have the strongest marches but still want to make an important contribution to their alliance.

Without sufficient Craftsmen producing materials, the alliance's Alchemists cannot maintain an effective supply of Altar Stones.

### Alchemist – The Key to Capturing Cities

Alchemists are arguably the most strategically important new profession.

They take the materials produced by Craftsmen and use them to manufacture Altar Stones, which alliance officers can then deploy across the battlefield.

Altar Stones are essential because **they are the only structures capable of destroying the new Energy Cores defending cities and checkpoints**.

Alchemists also have specialized skills that improve Altar Stone production, attack range, and damage.

This profession is particularly suited to active players who can coordinate closely with alliance leadership and keep production running when major battles are approaching.

### Fighting Master – The Frontline Specialists

Fighting Masters are the combat-focused profession.

Rather than managing the production chain, they concentrate on improving their fighting capabilities through specialized combat bonuses.

This profession is naturally suited to powerful and active PvP players who expect to spend much of their KvK fighting other alliances.

However, selecting another profession doesn't prevent you from fighting. Craftsmen and Alchemists can still participate in PvP, defend objectives, and join alliance operations.

The profession simply determines your additional responsibilities and available bonuses.

## Altar Stones and Energy Cores – A New Way to Capture Cities

Perhaps the most significant battlefield change is the introduction of **Energy Cores**.

Previously, capturing cities and gates largely involved defeating defenders and destroying their remaining fortifications.

In Legendary KvK, that is no longer enough.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261030-145153-p5qqq0.png)

When the defenders have been defeated and the walls reduced to zero, a new Energy Core becomes exposed.

This Energy Core cannot be damaged by ordinary armies.

Instead, the alliance must deploy Altar Stones to destroy it.

### How a Legendary KvK Capture Works (Alter Stones)

Capturing a city or checkpoint in Legendary KvK involves four main steps:

1. **Defeat the defending armies and destroy the walls.** Clear the objective's conventional defenses.
2. **Expose the Energy Core.** Once the defenses are eliminated, the Energy Core becomes vulnerable.
3. **Deploy Altar Stones within range.** Alliance officers place Altar Stones produced by Alchemists to attack the core.
4. **Destroy the Energy Core.** The alliance whose Altar Stone delivers the final blow captures the city or checkpoint.

Altar Stones function as automated defensive and offensive structures. They can attack Energy Cores, enemy Altar Stones, castles, and marching troops.

They also introduce a new tactical challenge because ordinary troops cannot destroy enemy Altar Stones. Alliances must use their own Altar Stones to eliminate opposing structures.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261030-144336-lcsfe3.png)

Even more importantly, when several allied alliances attack the same objective, **the alliance whose Altar Stone delivers the final hit to the Energy Core receives control of the city or checkpoint**.

This makes positioning, timing, and Altar Stone management essential parts of Legendary KvK strategy.

## Contract Skills – Progression Matters

Each profession has its own talent tree that players develop throughout the KvK season.

Progression is tied to profession-specific achievements and Contract Crystals, with talents unlocking additional abilities and improving existing ones.

For example, Craftsmen can improve their production efficiency, Alchemists can strengthen their Altar Stones, and Fighting Masters can unlock additional combat advantages.

Developing these skills requires resources, including substantial amounts of Gold.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261030-144440-d94i3a.png)

Based on player experience, fully developing a profession can require tens of millions of Gold, so preparing a healthy reserve before KvK is strongly recommended.

Unlike conventional combat progression, these new talent trees reward players for actively performing the responsibilities associated with their profession.

This makes activity and participation important even for players who aren't among the alliance's strongest fighters.

## Choosing Your Profession Before KvK

Profession selection takes place during the preparation period after alliance registration.

Players can change their selection during preparation, but **contracts become locked once the war period begins**.

There are also limits to how many players can select each profession within an alliance. Players who fail to choose a contract are automatically assigned Fighting Master.

This means alliance leaders should coordinate profession assignments before the war begins.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261029-100348-4lpkwm.png)

A good alliance needs a balanced mixture of Craftsmen, Alchemists, and Fighting Masters. Too many fighters and the alliance may struggle to produce enough Altar Stones. Too few fighters and it may lack the military strength necessary to protect those structures.

The ideal distribution will depend on the alliance's roster, activity levels, and overall strategy.

## Why Legendary KvK Requires More Organization

The biggest difference between Conquest and Legendary KvK is the increased importance of teamwork outside of combat.

In Conquest, an alliance with excellent communication, strong players, and good battlefield leadership could accomplish most of its objectives through coordinated military operations.

Those things remain essential in Legendary KvK, but alliances must now also organize a production chain.

Craftsmen need to supply materials, Alchemists need to manufacture Altar Stones, and alliance officers must coordinate their placement and use.

This creates new opportunities for less powerful players to contribute meaningfully to their alliance's success.

A highly active Craftsman or Alchemist may become just as important to a successful city siege as the strongest rally leader.

Conversely, poor organization can prevent even a very powerful alliance from capturing objectives efficiently.

## Final Thoughts – A New Kind of KvK

Legendary KvK represents a major change in how Infinity Kingdom approaches large-scale alliance warfare.

The familiar battles, territory competition, and alliance politics remain, but the introduction of professions, Altar Stones, and Energy Cores means that military strength alone is no longer sufficient.

Alliances must now plan their production, develop specialized players, and coordinate logistics alongside their battlefield operations.

For players entering Legendary KvK for the first time, the most important thing is understanding that **everyone has a role, and those roles depend on one another**.

You don't need to master every new mechanic immediately. Start by understanding the three professions, how Altar Stones are produced, and why Energy Cores change the way cities are captured.

We'll explore these systems in more detail in upcoming IK-Wiki guides, including profession selection, contract talents, Altar Stone mechanics, and practical strategies for alliance leadership.

*For more information, see the [official Legendary Season patch notes](https://infinitykingdom.gtarcade.com/m/en/news/7023649.html) and our [guide to preparing for Legendary Season](https://ik-wiki.com/posts/everything-you-need-to-know-going-into-legendary-season/).*

title: Legendary KvK Fighting Master Guide – Talents, Buffs, Upgrade Costs &
markdown:
![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-090646-s9yv7k.png)

For players who enjoy PvP, Fighting Master is the most straightforward profession. Its talent tree provides powerful bonuses to Troop Attack, Troop Defense, Marching Speed, and survivability, along with additional bonuses for Immortal damage and rallies.

However, upgrading these talents is expensive, and not all of them are equally valuable. In this guide, we'll go through what Fighting Masters do, how the talent tree works, the costs of upgrading it, and which bonuses are most useful.

## TL;DR – Is Fighting Master Worth Choosing?

Fighting Master is designed for active combat players who want to maximize their effectiveness during Legendary KvK.

* **Best for:** Strong, active PvP players and alliance rally leaders.
* **Main advantage:** Up to +10% Troop Attack, +10% Troop Defense, +10% Marching Speed, and additional combat bonuses.
* **Upgrade cost:** 3 million Gold per talent point, with five points available in each of seven talents.
* **Maximum theoretical cost:** 105 million Gold to fully upgrade all 35 talent points.
* **Our recommendation:** Prioritize Troop Attack and Troop Defense for general PvP performance, while considering survivability and specialized bonuses depending on your battlefield role.

Importantly, Fighting Master doesn't unlock exclusive combat activities. Craftsmen and Alchemists can still fight normally. The difference is that Fighting Masters gain additional bonuses that make them more effective in battle.

## What Does a Fighting Master Actually Do?

Fighting Master is the combat-focused profession in Legendary KvK. Unlike the other two professions, Fighting Masters don't have any production responsibilities. Instead, their specialization is designed around fighting enemy armies, attacking objectives, defending territory, and participating in alliance operations.

Their most important contribution is helping the alliance win the battles that allow Altar Stones to be deployed and protected.

Even though Altar Stones are needed to destroy the new Energy Cores, ordinary armies remain essential for defeating defending garrisons, destroying walls, fighting other players, and protecting strategic positions.

In practice, Fighting Masters are especially useful for powerful players who regularly participate in these activities.

For alliance leadership, however, it's important to remember that Fighting Master isn't automatically the best choice for everyone. An alliance with too many Fighting Masters and insufficient Craftsmen or Alchemists may struggle with the production needed to capture cities.

## The Fighting Master Talent Tree

Fighting Masters have seven talents, each with five upgrade levels. Every talent provides a different combat bonus, and developing the full tree requires a substantial investment.

The talent tree follows a progression system in which players must invest points to unlock additional talents.

Here are all seven talents and their maximum bonuses.

These are the maximum bonuses displayed in the current Fighting Master talent tree, based on in-game screenshots.

### 1. Superhuman Speed – Up to +10% Marching Speed

Superhuman Speed is the first talent in the Fighting Master tree and provides additional marching speed.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-090702-noag1e.png)

Each upgrade increases Marching Speed by 2%, reaching a maximum of 10% at five points.

While this doesn't directly improve combat damage, mobility is incredibly important during KvK. Faster marches allow players to reinforce threatened positions, move between objectives, and respond more quickly to changing battlefield conditions.

This is also the starting talent, meaning players must develop it to progress further through the tree.

### 2. Mighty Forces – Up to +10% Troop Attack

Mighty Forces increases Troop Attack when entering battle.

Each point provides 2% Troop Attack, reaching a maximum bonus of 10%.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-090710-7g4fv5.png)

This is arguably the strongest general-purpose talent available to Fighting Masters.

Troop Attack is valuable across virtually every march composition and directly improves offensive combat performance, making it particularly attractive for players who regularly attack other Lords or participate in contested sieges.

Unlike specialized bonuses that only benefit certain situations, Troop Attack is relevant to every single battle and is the single best modifier to obtain in terms of damage scaling. That makes this talent node particularly important and players want to try and complete enough achievements to unlock 5/5 Mighty Forces BEFORE the gates open and PvP begin.

**In essence:** One of the highest-priority talents for Fighting Masters. Once unlocked, maximizing Mighty Forces should be a major objective for offensive PvP players.

### 3. Rock Steady – Up to +10% Troop Defense

Rock Steady provides additional Troop Defense when entering battle.

Like Mighty Forces, it increases by 2% per point, reaching +10% at maximum level.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-090718-xtzk74.png)

Troop Defense improves survivability and can be particularly valuable during long engagements, defending objectives, or fighting opponents with stronger marches.

For competitive players, defensive bonuses can also help preserve troops and reduce the frequency with which armies need to be replenished.

The in-game talent tree shows that Rock Steady requires a total investment of 10 talent points before it becomes available.

**In Essence**: Another extremely valuable talent, particularly for frontline fighters and players responsible for defending important objectives. Together with Mighty Forces, this forms the core of a strong Fighting Master build.

### 4. Shelter – Up to −5% Soldier Death Rate

Shelter reduces soldier casualties, with each point providing a 1% reduction in Death Rate. At maximum level, the bonus reaches −5%.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-090725-e6few0.png)

This is an interesting talent because it doesn't necessarily make your march stronger during an individual battle. Instead, it helps reduce permanent troop losses.

During Legendary KvK, where players may spend weeks fighting over territory and participating in repeated battles, reducing deaths can have considerable long-term value.

For players who fight constantly, even a relatively modest reduction in casualties may help preserve troop reserves and reduce rebuilding costs.

### 5. Gladiator – Up to −5% Critical Damage Received

Gladiator reduces the critical damage received by all Immortals.

Each upgrade provides a 1% reduction, reaching −5% at maximum level.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-090732-jky4pz.png)

Unlike Rock Steady, which increases Troop Defense, Gladiator specifically targets critical damage dealt against Immortals. This is a super important node to reach, as crit damage is extreemly powerful in Infinity Kingdom and most top tier builds center around consistent critical strike chance and high critical strike damage.

Against teams that rely heavily on critical damage, the effect may be useful. Against opponents with limited critical damage, its value will naturally be lower.

### 6. Wild Nature – Up to +5% Immortal Damage

Wild Nature increases damage dealt by Immortals.

The bonus starts at +1% and increases to +5% when fully upgraded.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-090741-l09bh8.png)

This provides an offensive improvement that is separate from Mighty Forces' Troop Attack bonus.

For marches relying heavily on powerful damage-dealing Immortals, additional Immortal damage can be useful, particularly when combined with other offensive buffs.

This is the single strongest talent in the tree giving raw damage output. However it is also quite far to reach and requires you to be consistently and actively engaged in the season in order to complete enough achievements to unlock 5/5 here. 

When in a highly competitive season, you want to help your main key strongest players to complete their achievements in order to unlock Wild Nature before fighting for zone 3.

### 7. Team Worker – Up to +5% Rally Damage

Team Worker is the final specialized talent, increasing damage dealt when attacking through a rally.

Each upgrade provides +1% damage, reaching +5% at maximum level.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-090748-vmrfer.png)

There is one important restriction: **the bonus does not activate if the rally contains only one player**.

This makes Team Worker particularly interesting for alliance rally leaders and players who regularly participate in coordinated attacks.

However, players who primarily fight through individual marches will receive considerably less value from this talent.

An attractive specialization for dedicated rally players, but lower priority for players who spend most of their KvK fighting independently.

## How Much Does It Cost to Upgrade Fighting Master?

Every Fighting Master talent has five upgrade levels.

Each point costs **3 million ordinary Gold**, alongside one Contract Crystal earned through Legendary KvK achievements or other available sources.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261104-090759-db5qbz.png)

This means fully upgrading a single talent costs 15 million Gold.

Fully upgrading all seven talents therefore requires a theoretical total of **105 million Gold and 35 Contract Crystals**, assuming every upgrade costs one Crystal and 3 million Gold as shown in the current tree.

However, having enough Gold isn't the only requirement.

Players must also unlock talents progressively by investing points in earlier parts of the tree. Contract Crystals must be earned through the relevant achievements, and some talents require a minimum number of points to be invested before becoming available.

For example, Rock Steady requires 10 total invested points.

This means players cannot simply choose to maximize the strongest late-tree talents immediately.

The exact unlock requirements for every later talent should be checked in-game as the tree progresses.

## How to Progress Your Talents Efficiently

Fighting Master talents are developed using Contract Crystals obtained through Legendary KvK achievements.

For example, the Legion Achievements menu includes objectives such as constructing Thermal Towers, destroying enemy Thermal Towers, damaging city walls, and defeating gnome garrisons.

Some of the demonstrated achievements award two Contract Crystals upon completion.

Players looking to maximize their Fighting Master talents should therefore pay attention to these achievements throughout the season.

An important practical point is that progressing your talent tree isn't simply a matter of spending Gold.

You also need to actively participate in the tasks that reward the required Contract Crystals.

If you're planning to maximize your Fighting Master talents, preparing 105 million Gold is useful, but you'll also need to complete enough achievements to unlock all the required upgrades.

For active players, the best approach is to review your available achievements early and incorporate them into your normal KvK activities instead of leaving them until the final days.

## How to Use Fighting Master Effectively in Legendary KvK

The biggest advantage of Fighting Master is that its bonuses improve activities players are already performing.

Strong PvP players benefit from additional Troop Attack and Defense, frontline fighters can reduce casualties, and rally participants can gain additional offensive power.

However, Legendary KvK introduces an important strategic consideration.

Capturing cities now requires destroying an Energy Core using Altar Stones produced by Alchemists. Fighting Masters cannot replace this requirement, regardless of their combat strength.

Fighting Masters should focus on clearing defending enemies, contesting enemy positions, protecting friendly Altar Stones, and preventing opponents from interfering with important sieges.

For alliance leadership, selecting Fighting Masters should make sure to include the strongest and most active fighters you have. 


## Final Thoughts – Is Fighting Master the Best Contract?

Fighting Master is undoubtedly the strongest of the three Legendary KvK professions when considering direct personal combat bonuses.

Fully developed, the talent tree provides +10% Troop Attack, +10% Troop Defense, +10% Marching Speed, reduced soldier deaths, additional Immortal damage, and specialized defensive and rally bonuses.

That's a substantial collection of improvements for players who spend much of their time fighting.

However, Fighting Master isn't necessarily the most valuable profession for every alliance member.

Craftsmen and Alchemists are essential to producing and deploying Altar Stones, and without these structures an alliance cannot capture Legendary KvK objectives.

For strong, active PvP players, Fighting Master is an excellent choice. For players who are less active in combat, another profession may offer considerably more value to the alliance.

**My recommendation:** Choose Fighting Master if you expect to spend much of your Legendary KvK fighting, reinforcing, or participating in alliance attacks. Develop the universal combat bonuses first where the talent prerequisites allow, and invest in the more specialized talents according to your battlefield role.

In order to keep up with Alter Stone production, you need a lot of actives to NOT be Fighting Masters. However at the same time you want your most powerful fighters to BE Fighting Masters. Hence, alliance leadership must figure out enough active players to fill Craftsman and Alchemist roles first, then filling the rest info Fighting Master. 

While that is true they must ALSO make sure that the most powerful fighters ARE Fighting Master no matter what.

And remember to prepare your Gold. With a potential 105 million Gold required to maximize the tree, Fighting Master is not a cheap profession to develop.

title: Legendary Season Building 55-60 Requirements and Energy Core Guide
summary: Legendary Season raises the building cap from level 55 to 60, but it
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-109-1024x584.png)

Legendary Season raises the building cap from level 55 to 60, but it also changes how upgrades work. From this point onward, having enough resources and speedups is no longer sufficient. Buildings must first have their **Energy Core charged** before their normal upgrade can begin.

For players entering Legendary Season, the main priorities are understanding Energy Cores, keeping the Forge producing Azure Crystals and preparing the correct building requirements for each new Castle level.

---

## Castle 56-60 Requirements

Every Castle upgrade requires the Wall and two additional buildings to reach a specific level. Planning these requirements in advance is the fastest way to avoid unnecessary delays.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-111.png)

The Wall is required at every stage and should always be upgraded shortly after the Castle. The other requirements rotate between Barracks and important progression buildings.

For example, once Castle 57 begins, you already know that Wall 57, Cavalry Barracks 57 and Warehouse 57 will be needed for Castle 58. Their Energy Cores and ordinary upgrades can therefore be prepared while continuing to produce Azure Crystals.

## Planning Your Progression

If your only objective is reaching Castle 60 as quickly as possible, follow the prerequisite table closely and avoid spending Energy Cores on unrelated buildings until the next Castle requirements are ready.

However, the shortest Castle route is not always the strongest account route.

Personally, I recommend prioritising the **Academy** whenever a new level becomes available.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-112-1024x528.png)

Legendary Season introduces new Technology nodes, and research takes a significant amount of time. Starting this research early gives your account permanent combat improvements while you continue preparing the next Castle and Barracks upgrades.

My preferred progression is therefore:

1. Reach the next Castle level.
2. Upgrade the Academy and begin new Legendary Technology.
3. Upgrade the Wall and buildings required for the next Castle.
4. Upgrade the relevant Barracks and troop ranks.
5. Continue toward the next Castle level.

This may be slightly slower than a pure Castle rush, but it avoids reaching a high Castle level with the Academy and research several steps behind.

Players should also avoid leaving the Forge and Tower of Knowledge at level 55 for too long. Both must reach level 59 before Castle 60 can begin, so delaying them creates a large progression barrier near the end.

---

## Energy Core Basics Explained

Buildings above level 55 require Energy Core progression. There are five Energy Core tiers, matching the five new building levels from 56 to 60, with three stages in each tier.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-108-1024x712.png)

Energy is added by consuming:

- **Azure Crystals**, produced in the Forge
- **[Stellar Crystals](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/development/buildings/energy-core-and-stellar-crystals/)**, obtained primarily through events

The first Energy Core requires **7,500 Energy** and contains three reward thresholds:

| Stage | Total Energy |
| --- | --- |
| Stage 1 | 2,475 |
| Stage 2 | 4,950 |
| Stage 3 | 7,500 |

Completing these stages provides rewards such as resources and Building Speedups. Once the Core is full, you can begin the ordinary building upgrade if its resource and prerequisite requirements are also satisfied.

Energy Cores are attached to individual building upgrades. Charging one building does not unlock every other building at that level, and excess Energy does not carry into the next Core.

## Producing Azure Crystals

Azure Crystals become available after entering Legendary Season with a level-55 Forge. They are manufactured by converting all four ordinary resources.

The largest production batch creates **999 Azure Crystals** in just under ten hours:

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-110-1024x781.png)

Without any double-Energy activations, producing 7,500 Azure Crystals would require 60 million Food and 37.5 million each of Wood, Stone and Iron. It would also take 75 hours of continuous Forge production.

Keeping the Forge active is therefore one of the most important parts of Legendary building progression. Even players with large resource reserves can be delayed if they have not produced enough Azure Crystals.

### Charging the Energy Core

Each Azure Crystal normally provides one Energy, but charging has a chance to trigger a double result and provide two Energy instead.

The exact probability is not officially displayed. Based on early observations, it appears to be around **10%**. If this rate is accurate, filling a 7,500-Energy Core would require approximately 6,818 Azure Crystals on average rather than the full 7,500.

Auto-Charge can be used to speed up the process. However, because excess Energy does not carry over, players who want to conserve every possible crystal can complete the final few charges manually.

## Summary

Legendary Season building progression is controlled by both ordinary upgrade requirements and the new Energy Core system. Azure Crystals are produced in the Forge using Food, Wood, Stone and Iron, then consumed to unlock individual building upgrades beyond level 55.

To progress efficiently:

- Keep producing Azure Crystals.
- Maintain reserves of all four resources.
- Follow the Castle prerequisite table.
- Keep the Wall moving alongside the Castle.
- Prepare future requirements before they become blockers.
- Prioritise the Academy if you want to begin Legendary Technology early.
- Do not leave the Forge and Tower of Knowledge until the final Castle upgrade.

The route to Castle 60 is ultimately a balance between Energy production, building requirements and research. Planning all three together will make the transition through Legendary Season considerably smoother.

---

title: Legendary Season & Energy Crystals
markdown:
![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261029-102158-ljb2p4.png)



## What Are Stellar Core Crystals?

Stellar Core Crystals are a premium alternative to the ordinary Azure Crystals produced through the Coin Forge.

Both crystals contribute Energy toward upgrading level 55–59 buildings, but their values are very different.

In other words, **one Stellar Core Crystal is equivalent to 100 Azure Crystals**, before accounting for any critical hits that may occur when charging with Azure Crystals.

The biggest advantage is that Stellar Core Crystals don't require you to spend hours producing Azure Crystals in the Coin Forge.

Instead, you can purchase them using Eternal Grails and immediately inject the Energy into your buildings.

## How Much Do Stellar Core Crystals Cost?

During the October 2026 Ghost Fiesta, Stellar Core Crystals are available in the Grail Shop.

The price is **30 Eternal Grails for 10 Stellar Core Crystals**, with a permanent purchase limit of 30 bundles during the event.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261029-102405-v20xsk.png)

That gives us the following breakdown:

Assuming the same offer continues appearing in future monthly seasonal events, players can purchase up to **30,000 Energy per month for 900 Eternal Grails**.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261029-102405-v20xsk.png)

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261029-102421-6j4fjs.png)

This is a substantial amount of Energy, particularly when we consider how long producing it normally takes.

## How Much Forge Time Can You Save?

The Coin Forge takes approximately **36 seconds to produce one Azure Crystal**, meaning players can produce around 100 Azure Crystals per hour when maintaining continuous production.

Since each Azure Crystal provides one Energy, the baseline production rate is approximately 100 Energy per hour.

Purchasing the maximum 300 Stellar Core Crystals therefore saves the equivalent of **300 hours, or 12.5 days, of continuous Azure Crystal production**.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261029-102429-1g4x9t.png)

That's almost two weeks of forging skipped through a single seasonal purchase.

These figures use the normal 36-second forging time and don't account for critical hits during charging, which can increase the Energy gained from ordinary Azure Crystals.

## How Much Energy Do Legendary Buildings Need?

The reason Stellar Core Crystals are so valuable is the enormous amount of Energy required for Legendary building upgrades.

For example, upgrading the Castle to level 58 requires **13,500 Energy**.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261029-102439-6mcnvw.png)

That's equivalent to 13,500 ordinary Azure Crystals, requiring 135 hours of continuous production at the normal forging rate.

Alternatively, players could purchase 135 Stellar Core Crystals, providing the same amount of Energy immediately.

The important thing to remember is that this represents the Castle's Energy requirement alone.

Before reaching Castle 58, players must also upgrade prerequisite buildings, many of which require thousands of additional Energy.

Consequently, progressing through Legendary building levels requires an enormous amount of production time.

Even the maximum 30,000 Energy available from seasonal Stellar Core Crystal purchases will cover only part of the total Energy required for continued progression.

## You Also Save Hundreds of Millions of Resources

The production time isn't the only thing players save by purchasing Stellar Core Crystals.

Forging ordinary Azure Crystals also consumes resources.

Based on player calculations shared within the Infinity Kingdom community, producing 300 Azure Crystals requires approximately:

* 80 million Food
* 50 million Wood
* 50 million Stone
* 50 million Iron

Scaling those figures to 30,000 Azure Crystals gives us:

These estimates are based on the resource costs reported by players and should be treated as illustrative rather than universal, particularly if forging costs differ depending on progression.

Nevertheless, the resource savings can be significant.

For players who are already struggling to maintain the resources required for Legendary building upgrades, skipping production can provide additional benefits beyond simply saving time.

That said, the extremely long forging times often mean that active players can gather additional resources faster than they can convert them into Azure Crystals.

For many accounts, production time remains the bigger bottleneck.

## Is Spending 900 Eternal Grails Actually Worth It?

This is where the decision becomes interesting.

At the maximum purchase limit, you're effectively spending **900 Eternal Grails to skip 300 hours of forging**, alongside the resources that would otherwise have been consumed.

That's equivalent to:

**3 Eternal Grails per hour of forging time saved.**

For players trying to reach higher building levels quickly, that may sound extremely attractive.

But Eternal Grails are also one of Infinity Kingdom's most valuable premium currencies.

They can be used to purchase Immortal fragments, exclusive artifact schematics, Chaos Immortal selection chests, and other highly valuable progression materials.

For example, the October festival offers an 80-fragment Fate of Chaos Selection Chest for just 250 Eternal Grails, while a 60-fragment Chaos Artifact Schematic Selection Chest costs 330.

Spending 900 Eternal Grails on Stellar Core Crystals means giving up the opportunity to purchase several of these rewards.

And unlike Immortal fragments and artifacts, **Energy is something players can eventually obtain entirely for free**.

That distinction is important.

### Long-Term Efficiency vs. Short-Term Progression

If your priority is maximizing long-term account value, spending Eternal Grails on Energy generally isn't the most efficient choice.

The Coin Forge will continue producing Azure Crystals, and eventually you'll accumulate enough Energy to complete your upgrades without spending premium currency.

Every Eternal Grail spent on Energy is one that cannot be invested into Immortals or other premium rewards.

However, if your priority is reaching higher building levels as quickly as possible, Stellar Core Crystals can offer tremendous value.

For example, reaching a new building milestone ahead of your opponents may unlock better research, higher troop tiers, or other progression advantages that improve your performance in PvP.

In that situation, saving almost two weeks of forging could be worth substantially more than the Eternal Grails you spend.

The key is recognizing that **Stellar Core Crystals are a purchase for progression speed, not necessarily long-term resource efficiency**.

## Should You Buy Stellar Core Crystals?

My recommendation depends on what kind of player you are.

**For F2P and low-spending players:** Generally skip Stellar Core Crystals. Eternal Grails are too valuable to spend on something that can eventually be produced for free. Prioritize Immortal development, artifact progression, and efficient selection chests instead.

**For moderate spenders:** Consider them if you're approaching an important building milestone and the saved production time will make a meaningful difference. You don't necessarily need to purchase the full 300-crystal allowance.

**For competitive players and heavy spenders:** Stellar Core Crystals can be an excellent way to accelerate Legendary progression. Saving up to 300 hours of forging every seasonal event is a substantial advantage, particularly when racing toward higher troop tiers and important research milestones.

## Final Thoughts – Buying Time Rather Than Power

Stellar Core Crystals are an interesting addition to Infinity Kingdom's seasonal shops because they offer something different from the usual Immortal and artifact rewards.

They don't directly strengthen your marches or unlock new Immortals. Instead, they allow you to accelerate one of the slowest parts of Legendary progression.

For **900 Eternal Grails**, players can obtain 30,000 Energy and skip the equivalent of 300 hours of continuous Azure Crystal production, alongside substantial resource consumption.

That's a very meaningful acceleration.

However, it's important to remember that the Energy Core system is ultimately a time gate. Given sufficient time, players can progress through it without purchasing Stellar Core Crystals.

For most players, Eternal Grails are better invested in permanent combat progression, especially Immortal fragments and artifact schematics.

But for players who prioritize speed over long-term spending efficiency, Stellar Core Crystals offer a straightforward way to turn premium currency into faster Legendary building upgrades.

**Our recommendation:** Don't purchase Stellar Core Crystals simply because they're available. Purchase them when the time saved allows you to reach a meaningful progression milestone sooner than you otherwise could.

Sometimes the best investment is permanent power. Other times, getting there two weeks earlier is exactly what you need.

*For more information about Legendary progression and Azure Crystal production, see our earlier [Legendary Season preparation guide](https://ik-wiki.com/posts/everything-you-need-to-know-going-into-legendary-season/).*

title: Legendary Season: What to Do in Your First Days
categoryPath: Things you must know about Legion of Frostborne
markdown:
![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20260930-155425-jldygz.png)

## 💠Prepare Before Legendary Season Begins

If you are reading this before entering Legendary Season, begin saving **AP and SP** now. A large reserve allows you to take full advantage of the opening events and immediately begin farming the materials needed for Legendary progression.



You will use far more Enchantment Stones, experience and equipment materials than before. Arriving with a healthy supply of potions lets you farm heavily without immediately becoming limited by daily recovery.

## 💠Farm the Rebel Double Rewards Event

One of the first things you should look for after entering Legendary Season is a **Rebel Double Rewards event**. If one is active, use it.

Legendary progression requires an enormous amount of additional farming. Your Immortals need more experience, your existing equipment still needs Enchantment Stones and later Mythic upgrades introduce the new **Advanced Enchantment Stones**. You will also need to collect and develop the stronger equipment that becomes available in Legendary Season.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20260930-155450-zxzqpn.png)

The double-reward event is therefore an excellent opportunity to turn your saved AP into:

* Immortal experience
* Enchantment Stones
* Advanced Enchantment Stones
* New equipment
* Equipment development materials

Progressing into higher-level Gnomes and Gnome Bosses also improves the experience and loot earned from your AP. However, efficiency is not only about attacking the highest level available. If every fight causes severe losses, you will quickly convert your AP reserve into wounded troops and healing costs.

Push upwards when your marches can farm reliably, but do not destroy your army for a marginal increase in rewards. Consistent farming is more valuable than forcing a level your account cannot yet clear efficiently.

## 💠Keep Azure Crystal Production Running

Azure Crystals are one of the central progression materials introduced for Legendary building upgrades. You will need a very large number of them, which makes production uptime more important than trying to recover from a shortage later.

Azure Crystals can be queued in batches of up to **999**, with a full batch taking approximately ten hours. You do not need to wait for the entire batch to finish before collecting it. Completed Crystals can be collected while the remaining production is still underway.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20260930-155510-in3rjb.png)

The most practical routine is:

1. Queue the maximum batch of 999 Azure Crystals.
2. Collect completed Crystals whenever you log in.
3. Before going to bed, collect what has finished, stop the current production and immediately begin a fresh batch of 999.
4. Repeat the process before leaving for work and again when you return home.

The point is not to wait for every batch to finish perfectly. The goal is to ensure that the Forge always has enough queued production to continue running while you are offline. With a morning, afternoon and evening routine, you can keep Azure Crystal production running close to 24 hours per day.

Do not neglect this during the opening days because you are busy farming or fighting. Building upgrades consume a tremendous number of Azure Crystals, and lost production time cannot easily be recovered.

## 💠Upgrade the Castle, Then the Academy

The natural temptation is to rush directly towards the Barracks and unlock the next troop tier. That should not be your first priority.

Begin by progressing the **Castle**, then push the **Academy to Level 56** as quickly as your requirements allow. Use speedups where necessary, even if you cannot immediately begin the next building upgrade afterwards.

Temporary downtime in your building queue is not the real problem. Falling behind on Legendary technology is.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20260930-155321-wk11hy.png)

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20260930-155338-3cas0o.png)

Reaching Academy Level 56 opens the first new Legendary technology nodes and allows your research queue to begin working while you continue upgrading the rest of your city. Research takes time, so every day spent without access to those technologies delays your long-term Immortal and troop progression.

Your initial route should therefore be:

**Castle progression → Academy Level 56 → Legendary research → Barracks and troop-tier requirements**

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20260930-155409-ia1ev7.png)

After reaching Academy Level 56, continue raising the Academy whenever necessary to keep useful troop and Immortal technologies available. From there, you can work through the buildings required for higher Barracks levels and the next troop tier without leaving your research queue behind.

## 💠Building Requirements for Legendary Troops



The building path shown above is important because Barracks cannot simply be upgraded in isolation. Each level is tied to Castle progression and supporting-building requirements, meaning that Azure Crystals spent on the wrong buildings can delay your next meaningful unlock.

Use the requirement chart to work backwards from your next Barracks level. Identify every prerequisite in advance and avoid spending your first Azure Crystals on optional buildings that do not advance either the Academy or your troop-tier route.

The Academy should remain ahead far enough to provide new research, while the remaining building progress should gradually move towards the Barracks requirements. This keeps both major progression timers working simultaneously: research continues in the Academy while your builders prepare the route towards stronger troops.

## 💠First-Days Checklist

During your opening days in Legendary Season, focus on the following:

* Spend saved AP during the Rebel Double Rewards event.
* Farm experience, equipment and both normal and Advanced Enchantment Stones.
* Increase Gnome and Gnome Boss levels when your marches can do so efficiently.
* Avoid excessive troop losses that interrupt farming.
* Maintain close to 100% Azure Crystal production uptime.
* Progress the Castle first.
* Reach Academy Level 56 before rushing directly towards higher troop tiers.
* Keep new Legendary troop and Immortal technologies available for research.
* Plan later building upgrades around the exact Barracks requirements.

## 💠Summary

A strong start in Legendary Season is less about unlocking the next troop tier immediately and more about establishing continuous progression.

Farm the opening double-reward event while your saved AP and SP provide the greatest return, keep Azure Crystal production running around the clock and prioritise Castle and Academy progression until Legendary research is underway. Once your Academy is working through the new technologies, you can begin completing the building chain towards stronger Barracks and the next troop tier.

Players who establish these routines during the first few days will avoid the most common Legendary Season bottlenecks later.

title: Legion Achievements and Battle Pass
summary: The Expedition Battle Pass is a limited progression track tied specifically to Legion of Frostborne during Conquest Seasons. It does not appear outside this event cycle, which makes it easy to miss if you are not…
markdown:
### Introduction

The **Expedition Battle Pass** is a limited progression track tied specifically to **Legion of Frostborne** during **Conquest Seasons**. It does not appear outside this event cycle, which makes it easy to miss if you are not actively checking Legion content (like in a non-kvk-competitive alliance). You can find it under the **Legion → Achievements** tab once the season is active.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-5-1024x511.png)

From a design standpoint, this Battle Pass is not about daily grinding or alliance coordination. It is entirely built around **personal achievements**, which significantly affects how quickly and reliably you can complete it.

---

### Battle Pass Structure and Progression

The Expedition Battle Pass consists of **30 levels**, split into **free** and **premium** reward tracks. The premium version costs **$50**.

Progression is straightforward:

- Each level requires **100 experience points**
- Total experience required to reach level 30 is **3,000 points**
- Experience is earned only through **personal Legion achievements**
- **Alliance achievements do not count**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-6-1024x471.png)

Each completed personal achievement grants **150 experience points**, which means:

- You need **20 achievements** to fully max the Battle Pass
- There are **26 total achievements** available
- Several of them are trivial for any active Conquest player

In practice, this makes the Expedition BP one of the least restrictive passes in the game. You are not racing timers or relying on alliance performance; you are simply completing objectives you would likely finish anyway during Legion of Frostborne.

If you find yourself in a server where you are not big on Legion of Frostborne, talk to your leadership about signing up anyway. Even playing KvK as part of a losing faction, players can complete the 20 achievements required for a skill unlock on the paid tier, but you need to work with your faction.

---

### Free vs Premium Rewards

#### Free Track

The free rewards are functional but unremarkable:

- Speedups
- Resources
- One random Immortal

They offer relatively low value but free rewards are always better than nothing!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-7-1024x437.png)

#### Premium Track

The premium rewards are where the Battle Pass becomes strategically relevant:

- **6,500 Gems**
- **60 Artifact Schematic Selection Chests**
- **1 random Light or Shadow Immortal**
- **1 full Legion of Frostborne skill (selection from the Legion skill pool)**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-8.png)

Note that while you may not need any of these skills, you can simply sell the skill stones and use them to purchase one of the top tier skills from the Cinder Wish Shop - like No Escape!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-9-1024x604.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-10.png)

---

### Skill Value and the KvK Comparison

At first glance, spending $50 for something you can technically obtain through **KvK Cold Coins** may seem unnecessary. However, the key detail is availability.

- The KvK Legion skills in the KvK Shop are **one-time purchases**
- Once bought, they are no longer available for repeat acquisition

This creates a bottleneck for players who are still missing Legion skills but do not want to rely entirely on long-term RNG or extreme spending, as you will eventually run out of skills to purchase in order to sell for Cinder Wish generation.

The Expedition BP gives you flexibility:

- You can directly select Legion skills faster using the BP rewards
- Or convert unused rewards into **Cinders of Wish** and buy exactly what you need in the Wish Shop

In raw value terms, the conversion is significant. The $50 Expedition BP effectively replaces the need for approximately **510 Wisdom Well draws**, which translates to roughly **$300–$400** worth of spending to reach the same amount of cinders through normal means.

Heavy spenders will naturally accumulate cinders through legendary skill chasing. For them, the BP is optional.
For **low to mid spenders**, however, this is one of the most efficient shortcuts in the game for closing skill gaps and obtaining those key Cinder skills.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-9-1024x604.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-8.png)

### Conclusion Summary

- Expedition BP is **only available during Legion of Frostborne**
- Progression is fast and based solely on **personal achievements**
- **20 achievements** are enough to fully complete it
- Free rewards are minor; **premium rewards are skill-focused**
- For low and mid spenders, it offers **exceptional value compared to Wisdom Well spending**

If Legion skills matter to your long-term account plan, the Expedition Battle Pass is not just reasonable—it is efficient.
