title: Legion of Frostborne Shop Beginners
summary: Legion’s Vender is one of the most important long-term shops in Infinity Kingdom, but it is also one of the easiest places for a new player to make an expensive mistake. The shop uses Cold Silver, often simply called…
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-3-1024x517.png)

## Legion’s Vender for Beginners: Which Ability Stones Should You Buy?

Legion’s Vender is one of the most important long-term shops in Infinity Kingdom, but it is also one of the easiest places for a new player to make an expensive mistake. The shop uses Cold Silver, often simply called Cold Coins by players, and contains exclusive Ability Stones that can unlock some of the strongest Tower of Knowledge skills in the game.

The mistake many beginners make is treating Legion’s Vender like a normal event shop. They earn some Cold Silver, see a skill available and begin buying stones because they assume the currency should be spent before the shop closes. What the game does not explain very clearly is that the selection expands as your server progresses. This continues throughout Conquest, which is divided into five phases, and the complete shop is not available until Conquest P5.

Cold Silver can be carried forward. If none of the currently available skills belongs in your planned march, you can simply keep the currency and use it during a later season.

For newer players, that may be the most important thing to understand about the entire shop.

## How Much Does a Complete Skill Cost?

Every skill requires 60 Ability Stones to unlock, and each stone costs 800 Cold Silver.

### 60 Ability Stones × 800 Cold Silver = 48,000 Cold Silver

A player who reaches the highest contribution milestones and receives strong alliance and objective rewards can potentially earn enough for approximately one complete skill from a very successful KvK. Many beginners will earn less and need to combine their Cold Silver from two or more seasons.

This means Ability Stones are not small purchases. Buying 20 stones costs 16,000 Cold Silver, while buying 40 costs 32,000. If those stones belong to a skill you never use, you may have delayed a genuinely important skill by an entire KvK season.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-4-1024x529.png)

Keeping Cold Silver in its original form gives you complete flexibility. Once it has been converted into a particular Ability Stone, it is tied to that skill unless you later use the dismantling and Cinder system.

## Legion’s Vender Expands with Your Server

The shop you see during your first Legion of Frostborne is not the final version. New Ability Stones are added as your server moves through Season 1, Season 2 and the five Conquest phases.

Patch 2.8.3 merged the old Seasons 2 and 3, so modern servers now move through the following structure:

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-1.png)

The important point is that entering Conquest does not immediately unlock everything. Conquest itself contains five phases, and the shop continues developing as you progress through them. By P5, the full Ability Stone selection is available:

- Assembly Charge
- Abundant Spirit
- Snipe
- Unforeseen Attack
- Stormeye
- Spell Disintegrator
- Wind Rage
- Berserker
- Weakness Protection
- Victorious Pursuit
- Siren’s Gaze
- Full Coverage

Unlocking all twelve would cost a total of:

### 12 skills × 48,000 Cold Silver = 576,000 Cold Silver

Even with maximum or near-maximum KvK rewards, that represents roughly eleven complete payouts. Under normal conditions, most players are looking at twelve or more strong KvK seasons before the collection is finished.

You therefore cannot treat every skill as equally urgent. Eventually, it is worth collecting the full shop, but your first purchases should be the skills that provide the greatest lasting improvement to your account.

## The Three Skills You Should Plan Around

Among the complete selection, three skills stand out as top-tier long-term targets: **Wind Rage, Assembly Charge and Abundant Spirit**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-5.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-6.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-7.png)

They do not all belong in the same type of march, but between them they cover the two most important offensive directions: physical normal-attack builds and triggered magic builds. A newer player should know about these skills well before they actually become available, because they can change whether spending Cold Silver early is sensible.

### Wind Rage

Wind Rage gives every normal attack a chance to trigger an additional normal attack. That makes it far more than a basic attack-speed skill, because each extra attack can interact with other normal-attack mechanics.

It works particularly well with physical carries such as Alexander and Hannibal, as well as skills including Combo, Cleave and Assembly Charge. The extra attacks increase direct damage while giving the Immortal more opportunities to activate other triggered effects.

For an Alexander player, Wind Rage is normally a much more important long-term purchase than Snipe or Stormeye. If it is not available in your current shop, banking Cold Silver until the appropriate Conquest phase is often the correct decision.

Wind Rage is one of the safest physical investments in Legion’s Vender because its mechanic remains useful anywhere normal attacks form a significant part of the march’s damage.

### Assembly Charge

Assembly Charge is another top-tier physical skill, especially for fast-attacking Immortals. Every normal attack has a chance to deal physical damage to the target and two nearby enemies while also increasing the user’s Physical Damage.

The skill becomes increasingly reliable as the Immortal attacks more frequently. A slow attacker receives fewer opportunities to trigger it, while an Alexander build using attack-speed effects and Wind Rage can activate it repeatedly throughout the battle.

This is why Wind Rage and Assembly Charge form such a natural pairing. Wind Rage produces additional normal attacks, and every additional attack creates another opportunity for Assembly Charge to trigger. One skill feeds directly into the other.

If you are planning a physical normal-attack carry, these two skills should sit near the top of your long-term Cold Silver plan. Earlier skills may still be worth unlocking, but you should avoid reaching the later Conquest phases without enough currency to secure these when they become available.

### Abundant Spirit

Abundant Spirit is the corresponding top-tier target for mage builds. It increases Magic Damage while also improving the trigger chance of triggered Tower of Knowledge skills.

That makes it especially valuable on mages using several triggered damage skills. Spell Disintegrator, Annihilation, Fire Nova and similar effects become more consistent, while the permanent Magic Damage increase also improves the rest of the Immortal’s magic-based output.

Abundant Spirit works so well because it improves more than one part of the build at once. It strengthens magic damage directly and makes the triggered skills around it activate more often. On Immortals such as Wu, Himiko, Baldwin and other serious mage carries, it can become one of the strongest offensive skills available.

Mage players should still consider Spell Disintegrator before Abundant Spirit becomes available. The two are not competing for the same role and work extremely well together. Spell Disintegrator provides repeated area damage and Magic Defense reduction, while Abundant Spirit increases Magic Damage and helps Spell Disintegrator trigger more consistently.

## How I Would Prioritise Skills by Build

A useful priority list must begin with the march rather than the shop. Wind Rage may be top tier, but that does not mean it should be the first purchase for a Merlin main. Abundant Spirit may be one of the strongest magic skills in the game, but Alexander has no reason to equip it.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-2.png)

This is why a universal ranking can be misleading. Wind Rage, Assembly Charge and Abundant Spirit are the standout long-term skills, but they support different types of damage dealer.

For most physical normal-attack accounts, Wind Rage and Assembly Charge are the main project. For mage accounts, Spell Disintegrator and Abundant Spirit form the corresponding core.

## What About the Other Skills?

The remaining Legion’s Vender skills are not necessarily bad. They are simply more dependent on a particular Immortal, mechanic or team structure.

**Snipe** can be a very good early skill for physical backline carries. It targets the enemy positioned furthest away, which gives physical marches a way to apply pressure directly to the opposing backline. If you use a carry such as Khan, Yoshitsune or Gilgamesh and expect Snipe to remain in the build, it can be worth completing before the later Conquest skills arrive.

**Spell Disintegrator** remains one of the strongest general magic purchases. It deals repeated area magic damage and reduces enemy Magic Defense, allowing the rest of your magic damage to hit harder. Mage players should not skip it simply because Abundant Spirit becomes available later; the two skills complement one another.

**Stormeye** deals magic damage and gains additional value against Rooted enemies. It can perform well in the correct setup, but part of its potential is tied to a condition. For a new mage player without reliable Root, Spell Disintegrator and Abundant Spirit are generally simply much better and safer investments.

**Unforeseen Attack** provides another form of pressure against the enemy backline. Its value depends on whether your build actually wants focused backline targeting, so it should be purchased as part of a deliberate setup rather than because it appears later in Conquest.

**Berserker** can be powerful in attack-speed builds, particularly when its drawbacks do not interfere with the Immortal’s ults (i.e. Alexander and Hannibal). It is useful in the right setup but is not as universally safe as Wind Rage or Assembly Charge.

**Victorious Pursuit** requires a build capable of producing enough damage instances to stack its effect efficiently. It can become very strong, but most beginners will not yet have the skills and Immortals needed to exploit it properly. Excellent for Manco-builds.

**Siren’s Gaze** provides control through its Taunt and Silence interactions. It belongs in specialized tank and disruption builds rather than being a standard first purchase. A skill I personally like early to mid game for its ability to setup control builds well. That being said, it will never be top tier.

**Full Coverage**, can be excellent specifically for Fire builds on Hippolyta.

**Weakness Protection** is a defensive mitigation skill that has never really found its place in the meta.

Many of the above skills are only mostly interesting as you begin building secondary and third marches. They should normally come after the skills that directly establish your main march’s damage engine.

## Why Banking Cold Silver Matters So Much

Imagine that you are building Alexander and finish Season 1 with 22,000 Cold Silver. Snipe is available, but you do not have a permanent use for it. Buying 27 Snipe stones would give the feeling of progress, but those stones would not improve your active march.

If you keep the 22,000 instead and earn another 24,000 during the next KvK, you enter the following shop with 46,000 Cold Silver. A small amount from a later reward is then enough to complete a full 48,000-cost skill.

The same logic continues inside Conquest. Perhaps you already have Spell Disintegrator and none of the current P2 or P3 additions matters to your main march. There is no reason to spend the balance on a weaker option when Assembly Charge or Abundant Spirit will appear during a later phase.

This is what makes Cold Silver different from many ordinary event currencies. Its value is not tied only to the current shop. It can be carried forward until the skill you actually need is added.

For a physical player, that may mean holding enough to buy Wind Rage and then immediately beginning the next 48,000 reserve for Assembly Charge. For a mage player, it may mean completing Spell Disintegrator during an earlier season and then refusing every unnecessary purchase until Abundant Spirit becomes available.

## Is It Safe to Buy Partial Stones?

There is nothing wrong with buying a skill gradually when you are certain that you want it. Purchasing 25 Wind Rage stones now and the remaining 35 during the next KvK gives the same final skill as saving enough to buy all 60 at once.

The problem arises when players buy partial stones without having made a long-term decision. Owning 20 Snipe stones, 15 Stormeye stones and 18 Berserker stones leaves you with three unfinished skills and no usable upgrade.

Raw Cold Silver can still become any skill offered during a future phase. Partial Ability Stones are less flexible, even though the dismantling and Cinder systems provide ways to repurpose them later.

My general rule is simple: if you know you will complete the skill, buying partial stones is fine. If you are still comparing options, keep the Cold Silver.

The permanent purchase limit is 60 stones for each skill. Screenshots may show a lower remaining limit or display a skill as sold out when stones have already been purchased, but the full initial allowance is enough to unlock the complete skill.

## Using Unwanted Stones for Cinders

Ability Stones can be dismantled into Cinders, which can then be used to acquire other skills through the Wisdom Well Cinder Shop. This gives KvK stones value even after you have obtained the most important skills from Legion’s Vender.

There is also a Buyback Shop for Ability Stones previously purchased and dismantled. This protects players who recycle a skill and later decide that they need it after all, although the account-wide repurchase limits still need to be respected.

For beginners, this should be treated as a later layer of the system. Do not buy a poor-fitting skill simply because you might recycle it one day. Secure Wind Rage, Assembly Charge, Abundant Spirit and whichever other skills directly support your marches first. Once your important Legion’s Vender collection is in place, Cold Silver can become another route into the wider Cinder economy.

## Final Recommendation

Legion’s Vender is a progression shop, not a one-season shopping list. The selection expands through Season 1, Season 2 and all five phases of Conquest, with the complete 12-skill selection available at P5.

New players should plan for that complete shop from the beginning. If you are building a physical normal-attack carry, make sure you can obtain Wind Rage and Assembly Charge as soon as they become available. If you are building around a mage, Spell Disintegrator is an excellent earlier purchase, while Abundant Spirit should become a major target later in the progression.

Skills such as Snipe, Stormeye and Unforeseen Attack can still be good purchases when they serve a specific build. What you should avoid is buying them automatically because they happen to be available before the skill you really want.

Cold Silver does not become less valuable while sitting in your inventory. In many cases, the patient player who spends nothing during an early shop will reach Conquest with a much stronger skill collection than the player who bought a little of everything.

## TL;DR

- One complete skill costs **48,000 Cold Silver**: 60 stones at 800 each.
- Conquest contains **five phases**, and the shop continues expanding throughout them.
- The complete **12-skill selection** becomes available at **Conquest P5**.
- Unlocking all twelve costs **576,000 Cold Silver**, so purchases must be prioritised.
- **Wind Rage** and **Assembly Charge** are top-tier targets for physical normal-attack builds.
- **Abundant Spirit** is a top-tier target for serious mage and triggered-skill builds.
- **Spell Disintegrator** remains an excellent earlier purchase for mage players.
- Cold Silver can be banked across seasons and Conquest phases.
- Partial stones are fine when you are committed to completing the skill.
- When you are uncertain, keep the Cold Silver and wait for the later shop.

title: Legion of Frostborne Shop Veteran Players
summary: The Legion’s Vender is one of the most important long-term progression shops in Infinity Kingdom. Cold Silver arrives in a fairly large bundle at the end of a successful KvK, but the numbers are deceptive: unlocking a…
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-3-1024x517.png)

## Legion’s Vender Guide: The Best Ways to Spend Cold Silver

The **Legion’s Vender** is one of the most important long-term progression shops in Infinity Kingdom. Cold Silver arrives in a fairly large bundle at the end of a successful KvK, but the numbers are deceptive: unlocking a single Ability Stone skill requires 60 stones at 800 Cold Silver each, bringing the total cost to **48,000 Cold Silver**. Once you begin buying complete skills, even a strong season’s earnings disappear very quickly.

This is why Cold Silver should be planned across several KvK seasons rather than treated like an ordinary event currency. For most players, the vendor is first and foremost a way to expand their skill collection, both through the Ability Stones sold directly in the shop and through unwanted stones that can be recycled into Cinders for use in the Cinder Shop. Later, once the important skills are covered, the same currency becomes one of the best ways to work on harder-to-obtain account upgrades such as the Wind Dragon.

There are resources, speedups, artifact materials and cosmetics in the shop as well, but availability does not necessarily make something a good purchase. Cold Silver accumulates too slowly to spend without a plan, and every ordinary item bought today delays an exclusive skill or a meaningful amount of Wind Dragon progression later. The purpose of this guide is therefore not simply to list what the vendor contains, but to establish a sensible purchase order for both developing accounts and veterans who have already collected most of what they need.

## Ability Stones Should Be Your First Priority

For newer players, the first priority is straightforward: work towards unlocking all the skills available in Legion’s Vender. A complete skill requires 60 Ability Stones, with each stone costing 800 Cold Silver. That brings the total cost of one skill to: **60 Ability Stones × 800 Cold Silver = 48,000 Cold Silver**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-4-1024x529.png)

At the upper end of KvK rewards, a highly active player in a successful faction can earn enough to unlock approximately one complete skill per season. Reaching that amount is not guaranteed simply because your faction wins, however. Your personal contribution, alliance reputation, ranking and control of important objectives all affect the final amount.

With the current number of skills available, completing the entire collection represents roughly twelve excellent KvK seasons. For most players, it will take longer, which is why these skills should be treated as a long-term project rather than something you expect to finish quickly.

You do not necessarily need to buy the skills in a fixed order. Start with whichever skill offers the greatest improvement to your main march, then continue working through the remaining options. The important point is that you should not interrupt this progression to buy resources or consumables that can easily be obtained elsewhere.

Ability Stone skills provide permanent account value. Speed-ups and resources disappear as soon as they are used, while a skill can remain relevant across different marches and metas for years. That difference is what makes the skills considerably more valuable than almost everything else in the shop.

## What Should Veteran Players Buy?

Once you have unlocked all the KvK Ability Stone skills, the shop becomes much more flexible. At that stage, the best remaining progression purchases are generally **Wind Dragon Crystals** and **Dragon Essence**.

Wind Dragon Crystals are the obvious choice if you are still developing the Wind Dragon or expect to use it in one of your marches. Dragon Essence is a broader investment in dragon progression and remains useful for accounts that still have dragons or dragon talents left to develop.

Both options provide lasting account progression and are relatively difficult to accumulate in large quantities. That makes them considerably better uses of Cold Silver than ordinary resources, speed-ups or other items you can farm through regular gameplay.

A simple priority order looks like this:

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-8.png)

## Wind Dragon Crystals: The Best Long-Term Purchase After Skills

Once the important skills have been secured, **Wind Dragon Crystals should become one of your main priorities in the Legion’s Vender**. The Wind Dragon is not simply a niche alternative for players running a traditional Wind march. It is one of the strongest high-end dragons to have available, with excellent base attributes and powerful specializations that can significantly increase the Ultimate Damage of the march using it.

There are also far more places to use the Wind Dragon than may initially be obvious. An Alexander–Hannibal formation is one good example, particularly when Alexander is not being used in your primary march. Many developed accounts now run a dual-tank frontline with the Earth Dragon on their main team, leaving the Wind Dragon available for an aggressive physical or hybrid secondary march. The extra offensive attributes and Ultimate Damage can produce excellent results in those formations, especially when the Immortals already have enough protection from their own skills and supports.

Hybrid marches open up even more possibilities because the Wind Dragon does not need to be restricted to four Wind Immortals. I am currently working on a Holy hybrid that uses some interesting interactions involving Dodge and Ultimate Damage, and this is only one of several directions in which the dragon can be taken. Its combination of superior attributes and offensive specializations makes it useful across a wide range of physical, hybrid and secondary formations. Even if you do not have an immediate place for it, developing the Wind Dragon gives you another genuinely strong option as your marches and the wider meta continue to change.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-4-1024x529.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-9-1024x540.png)

The problem is availability. Wind Dragon Crystals are extremely difficult to accumulate through normal gameplay, particularly in the quantities required to develop the dragon’s talents and complete its later progression. The KvK shop is one of the few places where you can collect a meaningful number of crystals every season, which makes them considerably more valuable than ordinary resources, speedups or artifact materials.

That does not mean newer players should immediately spend all their Cold Silver on the Wind Dragon. **Skills still come first**, including both the Ability Stones sold directly in the KvK shop and important skills from the Cinder Shop. KvK Ability Stones can be recycled into Cinders, allowing Cold Silver to help you obtain skills that are not directly available from the Legion’s Vender. If you do not need a skill such as Snipe, for example, you can buy its stones, sell them for Cinders and use those Cinders toward another skill that your marches actually need.

This makes the correct priority slightly broader than simply buying every KvK skill. First secure the useful skills available directly from the vendor, then consider whether unwanted KvK stones can help you complete your Cinder Shop collection. Only when your important skill needs are covered should Wind Dragon Crystals become the main target for your Cold Silver. Skills will normally have the largest immediate effect on your account, but once that stage is finished, the Wind Dragon offers one of the best long-term investments available in the entire shop.

## What Should You Avoid Buying?

There are several items I would almost never recommend purchasing with Cold Silver:

- Philosopher’s Stones
- Teleports
- Artifact materials
- Speed-ups
- Resources

None of these items are useless. The problem is that Infinity Kingdom already gives us many other ways to obtain them through events, shops, bundles, daily activities and ordinary farming. Cold Silver, by comparison, is earned through a limited seasonal event and accumulates very slowly.

Using Cold Silver to buy resources or speed-ups is effectively exchanging months of permanent skill progression for a small amount of temporary convenience. It may help you finish something today, but it will delay an exclusive skill that could strengthen your account permanently.

Artifact materials are slightly more tempting because artifact development can be painfully slow. Even so, the quantities available do not normally justify sacrificing progress towards Ability Stones or dragon materials. Unless your account has already exhausted every better option, I would leave them alone.

Cosmetics belong in a different category. Chat boxes, frames and nameplates do not provide meaningful combat value, but efficiency is not the only reason people play the game. If you find a design you genuinely like and would enjoy using, there is nothing wrong with buying it. Just understand that you are choosing appearance over progression and make the decision accordingly.

## What If You Already Have Everything?

Older accounts may eventually reach a point where all the KvK skills are unlocked, the relevant dragons are finished and none of the remaining shop items provide a meaningful upgrade. If that describes your account, there is no reason to spend Cold Silver simply because it is available.

You can keep the currency for future shop additions or reserve it for the chests available around the end of KvK. Those chests can provide access to far more interesting rewards, including valuable Holy and Shadow Immortal fragments, and Cold Silver can be used in place of Gems when opening them.

This is one of the few situations in Infinity Kingdom where refusing to buy anything may be the most efficient choice. Spending a rare currency on items you do not need does not improve your account; it only removes your ability to take advantage of something better later.

## Final Recommendation

For most players, Legion’s Vender should be viewed as an Ability Stone shop first and everything else second. Buy the skill that benefits your main march, complete it, and then begin working towards the next one. Continue until the entire KvK skill collection is unlocked, even if that process takes many seasons.

Once the skills are finished, move on to Wind Dragon Crystals or Dragon Essence according to your account’s needs. Cosmetics are perfectly reasonable if you enjoy them, but common resources, teleports, speed-ups, Philosopher’s Stones and artifact materials offer poor value for such a limited currency.

Cold Silver rewards patience. The players who gain the most from it are rarely the ones who spend it fastest, but the ones who consistently direct it towards progression that will still matter several KvK seasons from now.

title: Legion of Frostborne Weather System Guide
summary: Weather is one of the more overlooked mechanics in Legion of Frostborne, largely because most players only pay attention to it when a Blizzard appears before a major fight. In reality, the weather system influences…
markdown:
## Introduction

Weather is one of the more overlooked mechanics in Legion of Frostborne, largely because most players only pay attention to it when a Blizzard appears before a major fight. In reality, the weather system influences several aspects of the season, from gathering efficiency and territory management to Thermal Tower expansion and combat performance.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-16-1024x625.png)

Every province in the Frozen Realm has its own weather conditions, which means two neighboring regions can be experiencing completely different effects at the same time. Fortunately, the game provides both current conditions and a forecast for the following day, giving alliances an opportunity to plan ahead rather than simply reacting when penalties appear.

While weather alone will not decide a season, alliances that consistently use forecasts to guide expansion, gathering, and military operations often gain small advantages that accumulate over time.

---

## Understanding Weather in the Frozen Realm

The weather panel can be accessed directly from the Frozen Realm interface and shows both the current weather and the forecast for the next day in every province.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-19.png)

Weather is divided into three categories:

- Normal Weather
- Abnormal Weather
- Disaster Weather

Normal weather has no impact on gameplay and serves primarily as a neutral state. Abnormal weather introduces moderate bonuses or penalties that affect gathering and Thermal Towers, while Disaster Weather creates much stronger effects that can influence alliance strategy on a larger scale.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-17-1024x568.png)

One important detail is that weather is regional rather than global. A province experiencing favorable conditions may sit directly beside another suffering from severe penalties. Because of this, experienced alliances often monitor weather forecasts when planning expansion routes or scheduling important operations.

---

## Normal Weather

Normal weather includes both Cloudy and Overcast conditions. These weather types do not provide any bonuses or penalties and can generally be ignored from a strategic perspective.

When a province is under normal weather, gathering speeds, combat effectiveness, and Thermal Tower performance all function exactly as expected. Most players consider these conditions the baseline against which all other weather effects are measured.

---

## Abnormal Weather

Abnormal weather introduces manageable but noticeable effects. These conditions rarely force an alliance to change its plans completely, but they can make certain provinces more or less attractive depending on your objectives.

### Light Snow

Light Snow reduces resource gathering speed by 10%.

The penalty is relatively minor, and most players will not move gathering marches solely because of Light Snow. However, over the course of a long Frostborne season, even small reductions add up. If multiple gathering locations are available, it often makes sense to prioritize provinces with better weather conditions.

For alliances trying to maximize every bit of resource income, Light Snow is worth paying attention to, even if it is not a major concern.

### Moderate Snow

Moderate Snow reduces resource gathering speed by 20%.

At this point the effect becomes much more noticeable. Gathering marches spend significantly longer collecting resources, which can slow development and tower construction if an alliance relies heavily on local gathering.

In several Frostborne seasons I have seen alliances overlook Moderate Snow and continue gathering as normal, only to realize later that their resource production lagged behind neighboring groups. The penalty is not devastating, but it is large enough to justify relocating gatherers whenever practical.

### Fog

Fog reduces the effective range of Thermal Towers by 25%.

This is one of the most strategically important weather effects in the entire system.

Thermal Towers determine how efficiently an alliance can expand across the map. Losing a quarter of their range can create unexpected gaps between territories, increase the number of towers required to reach objectives, and complicate carefully planned expansion routes.

Fog becomes particularly problematic near choke points or when pushing toward important strategic targets. A route that appears viable under normal conditions may suddenly require additional towers and resources to maintain.

### Sunny

Sunny weather increases Thermal Tower range by 25%.

If Fog is the most frustrating weather condition for expansion, Sunny is arguably the most useful.

The additional range allows alliances to cover more territory with fewer towers, making expansion faster and more resource-efficient. In some situations, Sunny weather can even open routes that would otherwise be impractical.

Whenever I have been involved in alliance leadership during Frostborne, Sunny forecasts were often treated as opportunities. Expansion projects that might normally require extensive tower chains suddenly became much easier to execute.

---

## Disaster Weather

Disaster Weather represents the most severe category of weather effects. These events can have a direct impact on gathering, combat, and territorial stability.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-18-edited.png)

According to the in-game rules, provinces experiencing abnormal weather have a chance to develop into disaster weather conditions. While forecasts provide some warning, these events are designed to be less predictable than standard weather changes.

### Freezing Rain

Freezing Rain reduces the total amount of resources gathered by 20%.

Unlike snow, which slows gathering speed, Freezing Rain directly reduces gathering output. Even if a march completes its gathering cycle normally, the final amount collected is reduced.

For players focused on maximizing resources, this is generally one of the least desirable conditions in which to gather.

### Blizzard

Blizzard reduces damage dealt by Immortals by 20%.

This weather has a direct impact on combat and can dramatically alter battle outcomes.

Because Immortals account for the majority of damage in most engagements, a 20% reduction is substantial. Battles tend to last longer, offensive momentum slows, and the value of defensive positions increases.

In practice, Blizzard is one of the few weather conditions that alliance leaders regularly consider when planning major attacks. Launching an offensive into a province under Blizzard conditions often produces very different results than the same battle fought under normal weather.

### Sleet

Sleet causes territories outside a Thermal Zone to lose Prosperity 50% faster. Territories protected by a Protection Barrier are not affected.

This weather is less visible than Blizzard but can be extremely disruptive for alliances with large or fragmented territory networks.

Remote provinces become harder to maintain, disconnected territory loses value more quickly, and weak expansion routes become increasingly vulnerable. Alliances with strong Thermal Tower coverage are generally able to manage Sleet without major issues, while alliances stretched across the map often feel the effects much more heavily.

---

## Using Weather Forecasts Effectively

Many players treat the forecast window as informational rather than strategic, but the strongest Frostborne alliances usually do the opposite.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-15.png)

Before sending gathering marches, it is worth checking whether nearby provinces are affected by snow or Freezing Rain. Before beginning a major expansion project, look at the forecast for Fog or Sunny weather. Before launching large-scale military operations, check whether Blizzard conditions could reduce combat effectiveness.

None of these decisions will win a season by themselves, but Frostborne is often decided by dozens of small advantages rather than a single decisive factor.

The alliances that consistently pay attention to weather are usually the same alliances that waste fewer resources, expand more efficiently, and avoid fighting battles under unfavorable conditions.

---

## Final Thoughts

The Weather System adds another layer of strategy to Legion of Frostborne by forcing players to adapt to changing regional conditions throughout the season.

Most weather effects are manageable, but a few deserve special attention. Sunny and Fog can significantly influence Thermal Tower expansion, while Blizzard can directly affect combat performance during critical battles. Meanwhile, Freezing Rain and snow conditions primarily impact resource efficiency and long-term development.

markdown:
### Gnome Equipment Drop Rates (Levels 51–55): What the Numbers Actually Say

## Introduction

Equipment farming from gnomes becomes strategically important once you enter **Conquest levels 51–55**. These tiers are the first where **legendary equipment** enters the drop pool in meaningful volume, including **normal**, **plus**, and **elemental** variants.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-2-1024x464.png)

There is a persistent misconception that any legendary drop automatically outclasses lower-rarity gear. In practice, the data tells a more nuanced story. When elemental bonuses are factored in, **Epic+ elemental gear actually outperforms normal legendary**, and sometimes even rivals legendary plus pieces depending on stat alignment. Anyway, players want to get the best possible equipment - that means legendary elemental equipment! Let's look at the drop rates and figure out if you should farm level 55's only as most players think?

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-1-1024x357.png)

This article breaks down actual drop-rate data from levels **51 through 55**, explains what those percentages mean in real farming terms, and outlines how experienced players should interpret the results.

---

## Dataset Overview

The following data was collected from several thousand gnome camps cleared across conquest levels 51–55. Each row represents total clears at that level and the observed drops.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image.png)

---

## Legendary Drops: Rarity vs. Reality

### Legendary Normal

Legendary normal gear makes up the largest share of legendary drops at every level. At level 55, you are seeing it in **roughly 1 out of every 4 camps**.

In practice, most legendary normal pieces are fuel for your enchanted stone stores, as it is outperformed by legendary plus, legendary elemental AND Epic + elemental.

### Legendary Plus

Legendary plus is significantly rarer, stabilizing between **4–6%** across all five levels. This rarity reflects its intended role: a decent upgrade for players as they enter Conquest. The advantage of these are that they can be used across all immortal regardless of elemental affinity.

### Legendary Elemental

Legendary elemental drops sit very close to legendary plus in frequency, generally **5–6%** across the range.

What makes legendary elemental special is not raw stats, but **elemental synergy**. On the right immortal setup, a legendary elemental piece outperforms a legendary plus.

### The Quiet Standout: Epic+ Elemental

This is where many players underestimate the data. Epic+ elemental gear drops at **16–21%**, depending on level. That is **three to four times more frequent** than legendary plus or legendary elemental.

From real usage:

- Epic+ elemental **consistently outperforms legendary normal**
- With the correct element, it can compete surprisingly well with legendary plus
- It is far easier to refine, replace, and optimize due to volume

---

## So… What Level Gnomes Should You Farm for Legendary Elemental Gear?

This is the question I get most often, and the honest answer is one many players don’t expect:

**It largely doesn’t matter.**

Looking at the drop-rate data from gnome levels **51 through 55**, there is no clear upward trend in **legendary elemental** frequency, while there seem to be a bit higher drop rate at 55, it is not as significant as I would have thought and I think it is most likely down to the sample size that we see real differences. That being said, if you take little to no losses on 55's farm them just in case! The percentages fluctuate slightly from level to level, but those variations are small enough that they are almost certainly the result of **sample size and random variance**, not a meaningful difference in underlying drop tables.

If we were to grind **tens of thousands of camps at each level**, I am confident those curves would flatten further. In other words, level 55 does not meaningfully “unlock” a better legendary elemental rate compared to 53 or 54. The game simply doesn’t reward higher gnome levels with a noticeably higher chance for that specific outcome.

---

## Why Pushing Higher Can Be a Mistake

Because the legendary elemental drop rate remains effectively stable, **pushing into higher gnome levels only makes sense if the cost stays reasonable**.

If moving from level 53 to 55 means:

- Significantly higher troop losses
- Slower clears
- More healing downtime
- Increased reliance on reinforcements

Then the efficiency equation breaks down.

You are not being compensated with better odds. You are simply paying more for the same lottery ticket.

From practical experience, players who insist on farming the highest possible gnome level often progress **slower**, not faster, because stamina efficiency and troop sustainability matter far more than marginal level differences.

markdown:
### Best Talent Setup for Efficient EXP Farming

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-142-1024x532.png)

## Introduction

Immortal EXP is one of the quiet bottlenecks in Infinity Kingdom. Every level gained increases both stats and troop capacity, meaning combat power scales far more sharply with levels than many newer players expect. This becomes recurringly relevant as you move between seasons—Season 1 to Season 2, into Conquest, and eventually Legendary—because each transition raises the immortal level cap again.

In practice, this creates two overlapping goals:

1. **Max your main march as quickly as possible** to push PvE content and stay competitive in PvP.
2. **Gradually raise a wide immortal roster** across all four marches, plus several benched immortals for situational or niche setups.

Both goals demand a large and steady supply of EXP. Since Action Points (AP) are a limited resource—and compete with PvP, Infernal Assault gold farming, and event participation—the only sustainable approach is to extract as much EXP as possible from every AP spent.

This guide focuses on the **most efficient talent setup for manual EXP farming**, specifically targeting gnome camps.

---

## Core Principle: Daily Talent Swaps for Maximum Value

All of the talents discussed below share one thing in common: **charges with cooldowns**. That means you do not need to stay in this talent setup permanently. Instead, the optimal approach is to:

- Swap into your EXP farming talent page **once per day**
- Spend all available charges efficiently
- Swap back to your normal build afterward

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-143.png)

This mirrors how experienced players already manage talents for gold farming, honor farming, or dragon and technology progression. Unfortunately we can only have three talent pages, so combining some of the uses may also be useful. In this guide we are only looking at most efficient EXP gnome farming, but if you are not incurring big losses farming gnomes, you can opt to combine EXP farming talents with the **[Technology](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/lord-lady/talents/technology-development-talent-build/)** or **[Dragon upgrade talents](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/lord-lady/talents/dragon-talent-builds/)**, more on those in their own guides here on site.

While the EXP-relevant Development talents are being secured, you have two you should consider combining these with either **[Technology Development](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/lord-lady/talents/technology-development-talent-build/)talents** or **[Dragon Development talents](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/lord-lady/talents/dragon-talent-builds/).**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-113.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-162.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-161.png)

---

## Development Tree Talent Build for EXP Farming

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-144.png)

### Experienced (Level 15)

- **Effect:** 100% bonus EXP from one gnome camp
- **Charges:** 4
- **Cooldown:** 6 hours

This is the single most important EXP talent in the game. Doubling EXP on four gnome camps every day dramatically accelerates immortal leveling, especially at higher levels where EXP requirements spike.

In practice, you should always plan your daily farming route around consuming all four charges. Because of the cooldown structure, this naturally fits into a once-per-day talent swap without waste.

---

### Safe and Sound vs Divine Walker (Level 21)

This choice depends entirely on your current progression and troop situation.

#### Safe and Sound

- **Effect:** Prevents troop deaths entirely
- **Charges:** 6
- **Cooldown:** 4 hours

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-145.png)

Safe and Sound shines when you are **pushing into higher-level gnome camps** where troop losses start to spike. In early new seasons or right after a level cap increase, this talent can be the difference between continuing your EXP grind or being forced to stop because you ran out of troops.

If you are still stabilizing your marches or notice heavy losses, this is the safer and often more practical option.

#### Divine Walker

- **Effect:** Removes AP cost for one attack per charge
- **Charges:** 3
- **Cooldown:** 8 hours

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-146.png)

Once you can comfortably clear the highest gnome camps available to you with minimal losses, Divine Walker becomes the more efficient long-term choice. AP is arguably the most constrained resource in the game—needed for PvP, Infernal Assault gold farming, and event participation—so any daily AP savings compound over time.

For established accounts, Divine Walker is usually the correct pick.

---

### Side Note: Pleasant Surprise (Level 27)

- **Effect:** Doubles Enchanted Stones from gnome camps
- **Charges:** 4
- **Cooldown:** 6 hours

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-148.png)

While this talent does not affect EXP directly, it deserves mention because it fits perfectly into the same daily routine. Enchanted Stones are consistently in short supply, especially as equipment upgrades ramp up in later seasons.

If you are already swapping talents daily for EXP farming, it makes sense to consume these charges as well.

At this stage you can opt to stop in the Development Tree and move into Military talents to reduce troop losses while fighting gnomes. However, there are still the talent node **Marathon Runner** available in the end of the tree, giving you a 10% reduction to AP costs while fighting gnomes.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-160.png)

This is technically the most efficient talent for this gnome-daily routine setup, BUT it does require you to go through 18 points that does not provide value for gnome fighting (beyond Effortless for gnomes bosses if you do those daily too) and then 5 points more to get the 10% reduction of Marathon Runner. This is a choice you have to make based on your needs: AP efficiency versus troop preservation efficiency. Read more below.

---

## If you are struggling with high troop losses

So to get all of the efficiency talents in the development tree, we are spending the vast majority of our talent points (based on your level maybe even all of them) getting these. If you are experiencing large troop losses as you kill gnomes and you wish to reduce on the AP-efficiency in favour of more combat strength and reduced troop losses. You can opt to stop with the Development Talents after getting e.g. Pleasant Surprise. **In that case, you want to move into the Military talents**instead of continuing through Marathon Runner in Development.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-150.png)

For pure gnome farming, the Military Tree offers tangible benefits.

### If you go into Military Talents for Gnome Farming

### Clutch Shot

- Increases Crit Value
Crits dramatically improve kill speed against gnomes, which directly reduces incoming damage and troop losses.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-151.png)

### Pack Light vs Riding Fast

- **Pack Light:** 5% AP cost reduction
- **Riding Fast:** 50% marching speed

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-152.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-153.png)

Pack Light is technically more efficient from a resource perspective. Riding Fast, however, significantly shortens your daily routine. Personally, I use Riding Fast because time efficiency matters in practice, but players focused on strict optimization should take Pack Light.

---

### Survival Methods

- Reduces troop losses by 10%
This talent has a noticeable impact when farming higher-level camps repeatedly.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-154.png)

### Domination

- Reduces enemy physical and magical defense by 5%
Lower defense means faster kills, fewer hits taken, and better troop conservation.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-155.png)

---

### Guardian Choice: Owl vs Meerkat

- **Owl Guardian:** 5% Energy Regen
- **Meerkat Guardian:** 6% Attack Speed

This depends on your march composition:

- **Normal attack-focused builds** (for example, Earth–Wind hybrids) benefit more from attack speed.
- **Most other builds** gain more consistency from energy regeneration.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-156.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-157.png)

---

### Strong Will

- Increases Resilience
Reducing incoming crits is a subtle but meaningful form of troop protection during extended farming sessions.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-158.png)

---

## Talent Row Note: Rank Advancement

After Survival Methods, there is a talent row that does not meaningfully affect gnome farming. In that row, **Rank Advancement** is the most practical pick—not because it helps with EXP, but because it aligns with the same daily routine.

- **Effect:** Double Honor gains
- **Charges:** 3
- **Cooldown:** 6 hours

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-159.png)

Since you are already swapping talents daily, it makes sense to also consume Rank Advancement charges during your routine. This is standard practice among experienced players and keeps honor income consistent over time.

---

## Conclusion Summary

Efficient EXP farming in Infinity Kingdom is less about grinding endlessly and more about **intentional daily optimization**:

- Use **Experienced** every day without fail.
- Choose **Safe and Sound or Divine Walker** based on troop stability and season progression.
- Fold **Pleasant Surprise** into your routine for long-term equipment progress.
- Invest remaining points into **Military talents** that improve kill speed, reduce losses, and conserve AP.
- Treat this entire setup as a **once-per-day talent swap**, not a permanent build.

Handled correctly, this approach ensures you keep pace with rising level caps while preserving AP and troops for the parts of the game that truly demand them.

---

title: Leveraging Kingdom Changes for Buffs in Infinity Kingdom
summary: In the ever-evolving world of Infinity Kingdom, a groundbreaking update has introduced the ability for players to switch kingdoms for strategic buffs, while maintaining their allegiance to their chosen alliance. This…
markdown:
In the ever-evolving world of Infinity Kingdom, a groundbreaking update has introduced the ability for players to switch kingdoms for strategic buffs, while maintaining their allegiance to their chosen alliance. This new feature from patch 2.6.6 fundamentally alters gameplay dynamics, enabling players to tailor their strategies more closely to their playstyle. Here's your comprehensive guide on how to take full advantage of this game-changing update.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-4-1024x565.png)

## Understanding the Change

Previously, players were bound to the alliances within their own kingdoms, limiting their access to specific kingdom buffs. Now, players can freely change their kingdom affiliation to access different buffs, and then rejoin their original or desired alliance, even if it's based in another kingdom.

### Why It Matters

This flexibility allows players to:

- Optimize their army compositions with the most suitable buffs.
- Enhance their overall strength for both personal growth and competitive events.
- Collaborate more effectively with their alliances by maximizing the strategic benefits of kingdom buffs.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-7-1024x570.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-5-1024x568.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-6-1024x560.png)

## How to Change Kingdoms for Buffs

Changing your kingdom for buffs, while staying in your preferred alliance, involves a few key steps. Follow this guide to ensure a smooth transition:

### Step 1: Leave Your Current Alliance

- **Before changing kingdoms,** you must leave your current alliance. This is a temporary measure to allow for the kingdom switch.

### Step 2: Change Your Kingdom

- **Navigate to the kingdom selection screen** within the game. Here, you'll choose the kingdom that offers the buff best suited to your current strategy and army composition.
- **Complete the kingdom change process.** Depending on the game's specific requirements, this might involve using in-game items or meeting certain criteria.

### Step 3: Rejoin Your Alliance

- **After successfully changing kingdoms,** you can now reapply to your original alliance or another alliance of your choice in your new kingdom.
- **Coordinate with your alliance leaders** to ensure a smooth re-entry. This might involve prior communication about your plans and the strategic benefits of your kingdom change.

### When planning your kingdom change, consider the following to maximize the benefits:

- **Buff Alignment:** Choose a kingdom whose buffs align closely with your army's composition and your overall gameplay strategy. For example, if you primarily use cavalry, seek a kingdom with buffs that enhance cavalry strength.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-7-1024x570.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-8-1024x551.png)

- **Alliance Strategy:** Discuss your plans with your alliance leaders and members. Your switch could be part of a larger strategic plan, benefiting not just you but your alliance as a whole.
- **Timing:** Plan your kingdom change around major game events or battles. Maximizing the benefits of your new buffs at critical moments can be a game-changer in competitive play.

## Benefits of Strategic Kingdom Changes

- **Enhanced Combat Efficiency:** Tailoring kingdom buffs to your army's composition can significantly boost your effectiveness in battle.
- **Flexibility in Gameplay:** You're no longer locked into a kingdom's buffs based on your alliance. This opens up new strategies and ways to play the game.
- **Alliance Strength:** By optimizing buffs among alliance members, your alliance can become more formidable in events and wars, leveraging diverse buffs from various kingdoms.

In conclusion, the ability to change kingdoms for strategic buffs while maintaining your alliance membership opens up a plethora of strategic possibilities in Infinity Kingdom. By carefully selecting your kingdom based on the buffs that best suit your playstyle, and by coordinating with your alliance, you can significantly enhance your effectiveness and enjoyment of the game. Embrace this new flexibility to become a more formidable player and alliance member in the quest to conquer Norheim.

title: Life Link - How does it actually work?
summary: The Life Link Tower of Knowledge Passive is a powerful ability featured in various fantasy role-playing games and is notably known for its defensive and offensive capabilities. This passive ability allows the user to…
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/image-38-1024x512.png)

The Life Link Tower of Knowledge Passive is a powerful ability featured in various fantasy role-playing games and is notably known for its defensive and offensive capabilities. This passive ability allows the user to establish a Life Link with two enemy units every six seconds after the battle begins, providing a unique and strategic advantage during combat. In this article we explore precisely how this works. Is damage shared? Or do we reduce the damage we take when we run Life Link? I asked the development team to make sure.

**Official Description**: The official description of the Life Link Tower of Knowledge Passive states that, once activated, *there is a 50% chance of creating a Life Link with two enemy units. This Life Link enables the sharing of received damage, specifically 50%, between the user and the linked enemies. The Life Link remains active for a duration of 6 seconds*.

## Defensive and Offensive Mechanisms

The Life Link Tower of Knowledge Passive skill serves a dual purpose, both as a defensive mechanism and as an offensive tool. Many players often question whether it functions as damage mitigation or a thorns mechanic.**However, the true nature of this ability lies in its unique damage transfer mechanism.**

When an Immortal character possesses the Life Link Tower of Knowledge Passive, they are able to mitigate incoming damage, resulting in a reduced overall impact. T**he portion of damage mitigated by Life Link on our own Immortal is then transferred to the linked enemies, transforming it into offensive damage against them**. This innovative mechanic allows the user to capitalize on the damage they would have otherwise sustained, turning it into an opportunity to harm their adversaries.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/image-37-1024x573.png)

## Strength and Importance

Undoubtedly, the Life Link Tower of Knowledge Passive skill is considered exceptionally powerful due to its versatile nature and the strategic advantages it provides during combat. With the ability to significantly reduce the damage taken while simultaneously retaliating against enemies, it offers a distinct edge in battles, making the Immortal wielding this skill a formidable force on the battlefield.

**Especially in situations where you are faced with a prolongued fight with consistent damage. Life Link has a pretty high uptime making for an amazing mitigation and offensive capacity against e.g. holy setups or on a tank facing an enemy Alexander.**

The strength of the Life Link Tower of Knowledge Passive lies in its ability to turn defense into offense, creating a symbiotic relationship between damage reduction and counterattacks. This makes it a highly sought-after skill among players and a crucial asset for those seeking to excel in combat scenarios.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/image-36-1024x547.png)

In conclusion, the Life Link Tower of Knowledge Passive is a remarkable ability that enhances the defensive and offensive capabilities of Immortal characters in fantasy role-playing games. With its unique damage transfer mechanism, it provides a means to mitigate incoming damage while simultaneously dealing a blow to adversaries. Its strength and versatility make it an invaluable asset, cementing its reputation as a potent and highly sought-after skill in the gaming world.

title: Lifesaving Skills: The Art of Healing
summary: In the tumultuous battles of Infinity Kingdom, the ability to mend wounds and keep your immortals in the fight can make all the difference between victory and defeat. Understanding the skills that revolve around healing…
markdown:
### Lifesaving Skills: The Art of Healing in Infinity Kingdom

In the tumultuous battles of Infinity Kingdom, the ability to mend wounds and keep your immortals in the fight can make all the difference between victory and defeat. Understanding the skills that revolve around healing is essential for building a resilient and formidable army.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-28-1024x535.png)

In this guide, we'll explore the skills designed for healing and the heroes who can master these abilities to become invaluable support on the battlefield.

### 1. Vitality Touch

Vitality Touch is a skill that truly shines when equipped on heroes like Theodora, Zenobia, or defense-oriented immortals who can reliably maintain high troop counts, such as Charles or Tokugawa. This skill provides a significant healing effect to your troops, ensuring that they remain in fighting shape throughout the battle.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-29.png)

What makes Vitality Touch especially potent is its synergy with other healing skills like Nebuchadnezzar, Spring of Life, and Purification. When combined with these abilities, the healing potential of Vitality Touch is magnified, turning your immortals into nearly indestructible forces on the battlefield.

### 2. Purification

Purification is a skill that finds its place with heroes like Theodora and Zenobia. This skill has the unique ability to remove the Wound status, which can be a game-changing effect in battles. By eliminating Wound, Purification ensures that your immortals remain at their full combat effectiveness, ready to deliver their devastating blows.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-26.png)

Purification becomes especially effective when used in conjunction with healing skills like Vitality Touch and Spring of Life. The combination of these skills ensures that your immortals not only recover from Wound but also receive continuous healing, making them formidable assets on the battlefield.

### 3. Wine & Dine

Wine and Dine is a very special skill, I have included it in this guide because it only works through healing. It is a very powerful skill that increases the damage dealt by an Immortal being healed. For instance Wine and Dine equipped on a Zenobia has a chance to increase the damage output of e.g. Alexander when Alexander is healed by Zenobia's ultimate or skills.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-27.png)

Please make note that I write ultimate OR SKILLS. While is has not been confirmed if aura's can proc the effect, it has been confirmed by players that Wine and Dine can be activated with skills like Vitality Touch and Purification.

### 4. Spring of Life

While spring of Life is an aura effect and as such could fit into the aura section of these guide collections, it has no value outside of healing setups.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-30.png)

In healer based sustain setups this is a very powerful skill which both increases the amount of healing recieved by friendly Immortals and provides a strong buff effect reducing incoming damage quite significantly every time they are healed. Despite the low duration, the fact that it is a 100% proc on all healing taken means that this skill has very high uptime and is an incredibly powerful tool for anyone running a powerful healer in their build.

**In conclusion**, the art of healing in Infinity Kingdom is a vital aspect of your strategy. Understanding the skills that can mend your immortals' wounds and keep them in fighting shape is crucial for achieving victory. Whether you're deploying the restorative powers of Vitality Touch or removing the debilitating effects of Wound with Purification, these skills can turn your heroes into resilient and unstoppable forces on the battlefield.

So, embrace the power of healing, refine your tactics, and watch as your immortals become the champions who lead your army to victory in the world of Infinity Kingdom.

title: Lightning Dragon - Tanaris

markdown:
## Infinity Kingdom Guide: Taranis, the Lightning Dragon

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/image-61-1024x526.png)

Among all the elemental dragons in *Infinity Kingdom*, **Taranis** (the Lightning Dragon) stands out not only for his striking design — easily one of the best-looking in the game — but also for his consistent usefulness. Even before dragon skills were introduced, Taranis was already considered one of the strongest elemental dragons.

In this guide, we’ll break down his skills, how they really work, and which ones are worth using. We’ll also look at why he still ranks among the **top 3 dragons in the game** and how to best integrate him into your Lightning marches.

---

## Why Taranis Matters

- **Core Element Dragon**: Lightning remains one of the most popular elements in Infinity Kingdom because of its fast-paced, crit-heavy playstyle. Taranis fuels that with dragon buffs that amplify burst damage.
- **Scales With Meta**: With the rise of talents, crit-Khan builds, and support backlines, Lightning marches have become even more dangerous — and Taranis’ dragon skills synergize perfectly with this evolution.
- **Long-Term Investment**: Even if you eventually diversify into Earth or Shadow, Taranis stays relevant as a secondary dragon because of how well his skills fit high-burst teams.

---

## Dragon Skills Overview

Taranis has three possible dragon skills. On paper, they all look useful, but in practice, some are much stronger than others. Let’s go through them:

### 1. Lightning Shriek

- **Effect**: Increases true damage by 6%. Damage doubles if the target is stunned.
- **Reality Check**: Sounds great, but it’s inconsistent. Unless you have reliable stuns in your march, the bonus damage rarely triggers at full potential. When it does, it’s nice — but overall too situational for most Lightning setups.
- **Verdict**: *Fun, but not reliable*.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/image-62-1024x552.png)

---

### 2. Lightning Cage

- **Effect**: 90% chance to reduce damage dealt by 3 random enemy immortals by for 12s.
- **Possible Bug Note**: The in-game tooltip mentions normal attack damage, but testing seems to indicate that this may not be true. There are reports which points towards this reducing a**ll damage**, not just basic auto-attacks. If this is true, this only further improves Tanaris and cements him as one of the absolute strongest dragons.
- **Reality Check**: This is actually a very powerful defensive option. Shutting down three enemy DPS units for 12 seconds can swing battles — especially in Conquest where fights drag out.
- **Verdict**: *Excellent vs. strong AoE and burst teams*.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/image-63-1024x524.png)

---

### 3. Ghostly Drumming (passive)

One of Taranis’ most underrated strengths is his **passive skill**, which increases all damage dealt to the enemy by **3% for each debuff applied**, stacking up to **5 times** for a maximum of **15% bonus damage**. This might not sound like much at first glance, but in practice it’s extremely powerful for Lightning teams, which naturally layer debuffs through immortals and skills. Since Lightning marches thrive on burst damage windows, this passive turns every well-timed debuff into a damage amplifier, letting your big hitters like Khan and Hammurabi land devastating ultimates. In high-end matches where debuff management is critical, this passive can easily tip the scales in Lightning’s favor.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/image-64-1024x358.png)

## Talents: Thunder Cry (Recommended)

- **Effect**: Increases ultimate skill damage dealt, and reduces physical damage taken by your team for 12s.
- **Reality Check**: This is **the bread and butter skill for Lightning**. It directly amplifies Khan and Hammurabi’s ultimates (and even Peter’s if you run him). On top of that, it reduces incoming physical damage, giving your fragile backline some survivability against heavy hitters like Wukong or Apollo.
- **Verdict**: *Best overall skill — synergizes with Lightning’s high-crit, ultimate-burst playstyle*.

---

## Best Setup: Thunder Cry All the Way

After years of testing, most Lightning mains agree: **Thunder Cry is the go-to dragon skill for Taranis**.

- Boosts Khan’s crit-ultimate bursts.
- Supercharges Hammurabi’s mage damage.
- Adds survival value against physical comps.
- Works across multiple Lightning march variations, from spender builds (Qin + Hammurabi) to more consistent F2P builds (Theodora + Khan).

Pair this with strong debuff skills like **Energy Mastery, Corrosive Power, or Psionic Tide**, and your Lightning march becomes a burst monster.

---

## Ranking the Dragon Skills

1. **Thunder Cry – Best choice**
2. **Lightning Cage – Niche but powerful**
3. **Lightning Shriek – Situational**
4. **Overload – Avoid**

---

## Final Thoughts: Where Taranis Ranks

Even as new dragons and content arrive, **Taranis remains in the top 3 dragons of Infinity Kingdom** (only Shadow and sometimes Earth rank higher). His synergy with the Lightning element, his ability to amplify burst damage, and his versatility in both spender and free-to-play builds keep him relevant across all seasons.

If you’re a Lightning main, Taranis is non-negotiable. If you’re dabbling in multiple elements, he’s still one of the best dragons you can invest in long term.

⚡ Verdict: **Third-best dragon overall, and an absolute must for Lightning players.**

title: Lightning Immortals
summary: Lightning element is the counter to earth. This is primarily what drives the strenght of the element. It is not very strong in PVE content, so you should go earth/water for gnome farming and fire/water for boss killing.
markdown:
Lightning element is the counter to earth. This is primarily what drives the strenght of the element. It is not very strong in PVE content, so you should go earth/water for gnome farming and fire/water for boss killing.

**What it does extreemly well however, is counter earth teams.**Most servers see a ton of water mains in the beginning, then moving into more and more earth mains. This is because earth is the third cheapest march to build out (first being water and fire) and because many people build earth mains to counter all the water teams.

Lightning is a PVP element. As stated, it has elemental bonuses when fighting earth, but it also performs very well versus other teams and is one of (if not THE) strongest setup versus holy, provided you unlock Genghis Khan.

- Genghis Khan provides **wounds**debuff to the enemy, which means the enemy team **cannot recieve any healing**. This is extreemly powerful and hard counters water dragon and holy dragon as well as all healers such as e.g. Zenobia and Theodora.
- Peter the Great is **one of the best physical damage** dealers in the game, putting his front line opponent under heavy dmg pressure. Additionally, his **despell**ability provides insane value in **PVP**encounters, when playing against teams with shields and/or buffs.

**YSG**is decent **IF**you choose to build towards the **assist-meta**, because he has strong defenses from his skill. This means that he can be running assist passive to protect Genghis Khan (Genghis Khan is squichy and dies quickly).

**Richard**and **Cid**are the only other epic front line immortals for lightning. However, none of them are particularly good right now.
In the future, Richards new artifact may make him viable to use. Likewise, IF you are playing lightning to counter physical damage setups (in a physical damage meta) Cid could potentially be strong, also given artifact. **At the moment of writing however, I prefer to run an out-side-element immortal as the 4th spot in lightning. Strong candidates for the spot are: Bjorn, Attila and Hippolyta**.

## Highlighted Lightning Immortals

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/genghiskhan-1024x1024.png)

Genghis Khan

**Ultimate skill: Arrow Storm**
Inflicts Physical Damage (damage rate 440%) to all enemies, and couses Would-enemies cannot be healed for 10 seconds.

Damage rate - 132% / 176% / 220% / 264% / 308% / 352% / 396% / 440%

Peter the Great

**Ultimate skill: Mighty Thunder**
Purifies the enemy targets directly ahead, despelling all buffs and inflicting Physical Damage (damage rate 550%).

**Scaling**:
Damage rate - 165% / 220% / 275% / 330% / 385% / 440% / 495% / 550%

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/richard-1024x1024.png)

Richard I

**Ultimate skill: Heaven's Wrath**
Inflicts Physical Damage on enemy targets within a certain range (Damage Rate 170%) and has a 40% chance of Stunning them so that they cannot move or recover Energy for 4s.

**Scaling**:
Damage rate - 51% / 68% / 85% / 102% / 119% / 136% / 153% / 170%
Silence Rate - 12% / 16% / 20% / 24% / 28% / 32% / 36% / 40%

*Speculation: Reportedly, a "certain range" means 3/4 immortals with the diagonal enemy being "out of range".* Please contact me if*you prove/disprove this!*

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/elcid-1024x1024.png)

El Cid

**Ultimate skill: Conquest**
Reduces the physical damage inflicted on your front row teoops by 9%, and when they are targeted by normal attacks, there's a 65% chance of inflicting physical damage on the enemy (damage rate 30%) for 12s.

**Scaling**:

**Recieved damage reduction**:
