markdown:
In this guide we are going to have a look at all of the Magic Immortals that populate Infinity Kingdoms vast battlegrounds. Moreover, we are going to look at each and every single Immortal’s Unique Artifact to let you know where and how you can obtain it!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/image-116-1024x533.png)

## Unique Artifacts – how to obtain

| Immortal | Unique Artifact | How to obtain Artifact Fragments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Loki | Inferno Crown | Triss Event |
| Hammurabi | The Totem of Order | Triss Event |
| Himiko | The Golden Seal | Triss Event + Sparks of Galaxy |
| Empress Wu | Locana Buddha | Triss Event |
| Baldwin | The Silver Mask of Baldwin | Triss Event |
| Merlin | Dragon's Prophecy | Triss Event |
| Cleopatra | The Eternal Serpent | Throne of the Supreme Shop |

## These UA-Events explained

We have a few different events in play here. Mainly we are getting drops from **Triss Event** but also from the **Throne of the Supreme**, the **Sparks of Galaxy** and from the **Chaos Roulette**. Let's dive on in a learn a bit about these events.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/image-72.png)

## Blessings of Triss Event

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/image-73-1024x580.png)

Blessings of Triss is perhaps the purest whale-event of all in Infinity Kingdom. It is a huge gamle making wishes with relative poor chance for useful rewards spending wish coins only available through spender shop. However, it is an important event for Infinity Kingdom, since it is where most of the unique artifacts are available.

You will get one free wish per day over the three day event period. With each event there will be 6x different Unique Artifacts available, you obtain 30 fragments at a time when you get lucky on a wish.

The chance to get Fragments on a free spin is precisely 6%. Per default you have a 1% chance to obtain each fragment jackpot (hence 6x1% = 6%).

You can exclude rewards you do not need to significantly increase the drop chance of items you do need. However, the amount of wishes required also grow. If you are farming for Unique Artifacts, you should always exclude all Unique Artifacts you do not want.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/image-74-1024x643.png)

There is no Free-to-Play way to compete in Triss. You have to spend to get a chance at the Unique Artifacts here.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/image-76-1024x540.png)

Every wish also rewards you one **Cinder of Wish**currency, to be exchanged at the Triss Shop. Here you can buy Unique Artfacts but DON'T! You need the cinders to buy ToK stones.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/image-75-1024x526.png)

## Throne of the Supreme

Throne of the Supreme is an Arena-styled Cross Realm PvP event. What this means is that you are setting your three march setups just like we do in Arena, and we fight other players in the same way as we do in arena. However, the participating players are not only from your server, but from your entire battlegroup. This means multiple realms/servers fighting. Moreover, it is not a simple ranking scheme, but instead a tournament layout in which we (1) compete for rankings to qualify for (2) the play off stages with standard bracket-styled tournament PvP.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/image-78-1024x269.png)

The entire event has a **betting mini-game** to is, which is the main method of obtaining the **Event currency** which you can exchange for rewards. These rewards include **Unique Artifacts** and hence relevant for this article.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/image-77-1024x539.png)

## Sparks of Galaxy

This event is quite special and in my opinion an awesome event because it offers rewards which has previously been very expensive, for mid-spenders! Yes, you heard correct. In this first itteration we are looking at shadow Immortals and Unique Artifacts available for gems and low-cost bundles!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/image-50.png)

This means that more players will be able to afford and access (heck, even slow grind) shadow Immortals and their **unique artifacts**via this event. You do not have to participate in the expensive Triss Roulette and Theia's Roulette anymore!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/image-79.png)

There are a few limitations on this event though! Unlike most other events, big spenders are not able to spend on a ton of expensive and low-efficiency 99$ bundles to quickly empty the event. Instead, we have an event shop where the stock limits are quite strict.

### Over the course of this 3-day event you can purchase each day:

20 x 5 Frosty Orbs at a cost of = 20,000 gems
1 x 5 Frosty Orbs at a cost of = 0.99$
1 x 10 Frosty Orbs at a cost of = 1.99$
1 x 18 Frosty Orbs at a cost of = 4.99$
1 x 24 Frosty Orbs at a cost of = 9.99$
5 x 32 Frosty Orbs at a cost of = 19.99$

**In total per day =**317 Orbs at a cost of 118$ and 20,000 gems.

**Sparks of Galaxy event is a very efficient way to obtain the Unique Artifact, since you spend only 9,685 gems per unique artifact crafted. Extreemly cheap, especially compared to Triss which is the only alternative options for these artifacts.**

## Chaos Roulette

The latest artifact generating event of Infinity Kingdom. Chaos Roulette is unit specific to the Chaos Immortals. As such, this is where you earn both Immortal Fragments and Artifact Schematic Fragments for the Chaos Immortals, e.g. Loki, Wukong.

The event itself is much akin to that of Theia’s Roulette but with Unique Artifact fragments in stead of dragon shards basically.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/image-103-1024x542.png)

title: Main Guide to Farm Gold
summary: Farming Gold in Infinity Kingdom 2.6.6.
markdown:
Farming Gold in Infinity Kingdom 2.6.6.

In the realm of Infinity Kingdom gold is a most precious commodity. Our Immortal require immense amounts of gold to reach their full potential at boost level 30 and our Dragons are ever more hungry for gold tressure. As such, gold is arguably the most sought after resource in the game and one that players struggle to keep up with.

For information on total costs of upgrading Immortals to boost level 30 and the costs of Dragon levels 1-55 check the links here.

In this guide we are going to have a look at how best to farm gold. Enjoy!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/image-63-1024x573.png)

## Ways of obtaining Gold

### Dwellings

Dwellings are the easiest way to obtain gold and they are a constant stream of gold production for your Castle Kingdom. Upgrading your Dwellings to level 55 should be a priority for anyone struggling to keep up with the mounting gold costs. The production boost increases are quite significant. Personally, I prioritize upgrading all my dwellings every time I unlock a new Castle level.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/image-64.png)

Furthermore, you should remember to buff your gold production. Using the in-game buff items you can maintain a constant 50% boost to gold production, which makes Dwelling income go through the roof. This is arguably the single best use of gems (500 gems per 24 hour boost). I personally always maintain the buff as it is the most growth-value per gem spent until Immortals and Dragons are maxed (and even at this point, I will continue because we know we will need more for levels 60 once that is released).

For more information on **[Dwellings and Gold income check out the link here](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/resources/gold-farming-guides/main-guide-to-farm-gold/dwellings/)**.

### Mysterium

With patch 2.6 we got an onerhaul to the Mysterium. Rewards are difficulties were increased significantly. On a regular Mysterium run you will net a total of 5 to 5.5 million gold. This can be done every two days, making Mysterium a very good method of obtaining gold at a steady pace.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/image-70-1024x350.png)

In addition to the increased gold rewards, the new Mysterium also have other significant rewards for players, namely speed-ups, artifact fragments and even unique artifact fragments.**[For more information see the link.](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/resources/gold-farming-guides/main-guide-to-farm-gold/earn-gold/)**

### Infernals

The calendar event Infernal Assault can for some players be the single best method of obtaining gold. It is not as easy or cheap to come by as in the Mysterium and with simple Dwelling production, but it can yield insane amounts of gold for players who have the time, AP and troops to farm it for the three-day period the event lasts. The event is a recurring event that comes around every month or so.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/image-69.png)

During a single event I was able to farm 1 billion gold recently, a quite massive pile of much needed gold for my development and growth. There are a few different ways of farming gold in the Infernal event. For detailed information on multiple methods of farming gold during the Infernal event check out the comprehensive **[guide here](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/resources/gold-farming-guides/main-guide-to-farm-gold/infernal-event-gold-farming/)** where we go over (1) AP-intensive farming, (2) level climbing as well as (3) how to get passive gold from other players’ kills.

title: Malena's Ambition - Beginners Guide (preperation friendly)
summary: Here's a comprehensive guide to Malena's Ambition, structured in an engaging and informative way for both new and experienced players. It explains event mechanics, strategies, power level recommendations, and rewards…
markdown:
Here's a comprehensive guide to **Malena's Ambition**, structured in an engaging and informative way for both new and experienced players. It explains **event mechanics, strategies, power level recommendations, and rewards**, along with **critical tips for maximizing success** in the event.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-39-1024x570.png)

---

## Comprehensive Guide to Malena's Ambition

**Malena’s Ambition** is a **PvE-based event** in **Infinity Kingdom** where alliances **defend cities from waves of Gnome armies**. It’s an excellent opportunity to earn **personal and alliance rewards** while testing your **troop strength and coordination**.

This guide will cover:
✔️ **How the event works**
✔️ **How to participate effectively**
✔️ **Key strategies for new and veteran players**
✔️ **Optimal troop placement and defense tactics**
✔️ **Reward breakdown and power recommendations**

If this is your **first time participating**, don’t worry! By the end of this guide, you’ll know exactly what to do to **maximize rewards and contribute effectively** to your alliance’s defense efforts.

---

## How Malena’s Ambition Works

### 1. The Basics of the Event

- Your alliance **selects a city to defend** against **waves of attacking Gnomes**.
- The Gnome waves **increase in difficulty** as the event progresses.
- **If the city walls fall**, you can **still continue fighting** by defending the **garrison pillars inside the city**.
- The **event rewards personal contributions and alliance-wide performance**, so both individual and teamwork efforts matter.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-48-1024x574.png)

Complete challenges to gain bonus power against the Gnome invaders as well as a bit of extra rewards.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-49-1024x470.png)

💡 **Tip:** The **Gnome difficulty scales** based on the city’s **base level** (not the upgraded level). You can check a city's **base level** by **clicking on it on the map**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-50-1024x567.png)

---

## How to Participate Effectively

### 1. Entering the Event & Positioning Yourself

- You **must move either close to or into the event area** to participate.
- If your castle is **inside the event area**, **it will be attacked** by the Gnome waves.
- **Lower power players should stay outside the siege circle** and **send their army to garrison the city walls** instead.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-47-1024x562.png)

💡 **Tip:** If you **can defeat the incoming Gnomes** with at least **two of your marches**, you can **safely stay inside the event area** and repeatedly garrison the city walls. Otherwise, it’s safer to remain outside and just send reinforcements.

---

### 2. Garrisoning & Reinforcing Defenses

- **If you are outside the siege zone:** Send troops to **garrison** the **city walls** to help repel Gnome waves.
- **If you are inside the siege zone:** You can repeatedly **garrison** the **city walls** to strengthen defenses and earn extra points. ALWAYS garrison yourself when inside.
- **If the walls fall:**  - Your alliance **has NOT lost yet**!
- You can **continue defending from the garrison pillars inside the city**.
- If needed, **stack everything into one pillar** for maximum resistance.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-51-1024x482.png)

💡 **Tip:** Even if your city’s **outer walls collapse**, you still have a chance to **earn rewards and hold back Gnome forces** from completely overwhelming the city.

---

## Strategic Tips for Maximizing Success

### 1. Role Assignments Based on Power Levels

- **High-Power Players (Strongest Troops & Marches):**
✔️ Should be **inside the siege zone** to **garrison city walls** and **defeat Gnome waves directly**.
✔️ If the **walls fall**, they should **hold the garrison pillars**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-46-1024x543.png)

- **Mid-Power Players (Moderate Strength & Good Formations):**
✔️ Can **stay outside the siege zone** and **reinforce the city walls** consistently.
✔️ If they can **beat Gnome waves with atleast two marches**, they should consider **being inside the area**.
- **Low-Power Players (Weaker Armies & Troops):**
✔️ **Do NOT move inside the siege zone**—this will **get your castle attacked**.
✔️ Instead, they should **send their armies from outside the siege zone** to reinforce the city walls.
✔️ Focus on **supporting stronger players** with constant reinforcements.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-44.png)

💡 **Tip:** **If your alliance is struggling**, prioritize **reinforcing ONE garrison pillar** rather than spreading defenses too thin.

---

### 2. Prioritizing Targets & Maximizing Damage

✔️ **Coordinate with your alliance**—keep checking each square of the wall, ping your alliance to reinforce if one section is weak.
✔️ **Save your strongest marches for garrisoning walls and use a march that wins despite larger losses on your own garrison (or stay outside the area).**
✔️ Note that there will be gnome bosses in a few major waves, make sure to secure the area with strong marches when you see a boss moving towards the wall section

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-45-1024x611.png)

💡 **Tip:** If your alliance is **losing ground**, focus on **defending garrison pillars** to maximize points and prolong survival.

---

## Rewards & Recommended Power Levels

### 1. Personal & Alliance Rewards

- Rewards are given based on **individual contribution (damage dealt, troops sent, etc.)** and **alliance-wide performance**.
- Higher-tier cities **give better rewards**, but **are also more difficult to defend**.

**Main rewards include:**
✔️ **Alliance Coins (main reward)**
✔️ **Speed-Ups**
✔️ **Gems**
✔️ **Philosopher stones**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-42-1024x407.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-43-1024x388.png)

💡 **Tip:** Even if your alliance **doesn’t fully defend the city**, you’ll still **earn valuable rewards**, so participation is always worth it. Note alliance coins rewards are based on the amount of gnomes you kill, being the last to garrison a section of the wall means the first to fight incoming gnomes.

---

### 2. Power Level Recommendations

These differ greatly based on server progression and city level! In preperation for example: a **Level 4 Cities** (Low Difficulty) – Recommended **39K+ power per march. **Base Level 7 Cities (Moderate Difficulty) – Recommended **72K+ power per march. However, these recommendations are not entirely honest since they assume you do not have a well-created army. If you have strong builds you can go quite far above the recommended power. Note that Capitals are more dangerous but certainly not impossible if you alliances larger players participate.**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-41-1024x364.png)

The event is easier than most players think in preperation servers and season one. So I would recommend you try one of your higher level cities to begin with. If that is easy for your alliance, move on to your capital. If it is hard and you maybe barely defend in the last pilar, move to a lower level city. But dont go too low, the difficulty drops fast and so does the reward points!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-39-1024x570.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-40-1024x597.png)

💡 **Tip:** Check the **level of the city** before selecting a siege target. You can do this by **clicking on the city on the map** to see its base stats.

---

## Summary

✔️ **Malena’s Ambition is a city defense event where alliances must repel waves of Gnome attackers.**
✔️ **Lower-power players should stay outside the siege zone and send reinforcements, while stronger players should garrison inside.**
✔️ **If the city walls fall, you can still fight from the garrison pillars inside the city.**
✔️ **Rewards are based on personal contributions and alliance performance—so always participate!**
✔️ **The difficulty scales with the base city level, so check the map before choosing a target.**

💡 **Final Tip:** **Always communicate with your alliance** to assign roles, coordinate reinforcements, and maximize success.

🔥 **Now you’re ready to dominate Malena’s Ambition and earn top rewards!** Good luck, and may your defenses hold strong! 🏰⚔️

**Here's a link to an older video I made about this event. The concept remains the same.**

    https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rMGMzczDk2c

title: Coutering: Magical Damage
summary: In the ever-shifting landscape of Infinity Kingdom, battles are often a showcase of immense power and varied abilities, including the formidable domain of magical damage. To emerge victorious in the face of these…
categoryPath: Countering Tower of Knowledge Skills: A PvP Guide Series
markdown:
### Introduction: Mastering the Art of Countering Magical Damage in Infinity Kingdom

In the ever-shifting landscape of Infinity Kingdom, battles are often a showcase of immense power and varied abilities, including the formidable domain of magical damage. To emerge victorious in the face of these mystical onslaughts, understanding the art of countering magical damage is an absolute necessity. It is incredibly important that players are aware of the difference between magical and physical damage and are able to defend against them properly. Hence this guide and another seperate guide here on the wiki for defending against physical damage.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-106-1024x369.png)

Players should understand:

- The difference between **magical** and **physical** damage scaling.
- How mage teams generate burst through energy acceleration.
- Which defensive skills actually change outcomes in practice.

Every serious account should maintain:

- **One formation built to counter magical damage**
- **One formation built to counter physical damage**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-110.png)

This guide focuses specifically on magical damage mitigation, updated for the current skill pool and meta trends as of 2.9.2. Let's take a look at defending against magical damage!

---

## Understanding Magical Damage in the Current Meta

Magical damage primarily scales from **INT** and interacts with:

- Magical Crit
- Magical Penetration
- Energy regeneration cycles
- Skill multipliers and Magical damage buffs

Common magical damage skills and effects in the current environment include a wide range of skills like: **Chase**, **Toxic Nova / Fire Nova**, **Annihilation**, **Poison Thorn**, **Concentration**, **Death Breath**, **Spell Disintegration**, **Infinite Firepower, Chaos Storm**.

In the current meta you will likely see two main strategies deployed by enemies leaning into magic for damage output:

1. **Hyper-regeneration burst builds**
For example, Himiko builds running skills like Energy Mastery + Corrosive Power and are able to cycle ultimates extremely quickly.
2. **Crit-focused mage cores using Chase builds or even Infinite Firepower**
This build punishes teams that rely only on raw HP or standard tanking. Without magical mitigation, even well-built frontline immortals collapse quickly.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-107-1024x626.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-108-1024x651.png)

The takeaway: magical fights are often decided early. Your defensive structure must address that timing.

---

## Counter Strategies

### Core Defensive Skills Against Magical Damage

### 1. Master’s Aegis – Consistent Aura Mitigation

**Type:** Aura
**Effect:** ~25% reduced magical damage taken (full duration)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-111.png)

Master’s Aegis remains one of the most reliable anti-mage tools available.

- Applies to the entire formation
- Active for the full battle duration
- Does not rely on timing windows

The tradeoff is the Aura slot. You sacrifice offensive scaling, but against mage-heavy servers, that trade is often correct.

---

### 2. Resist – High Impact, Short Window

**Effect:** ~50% magical damage reduction
**Targets:** 3 immortals
**Duration:** 18 seconds

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-113.png)

Resist is one of the most powerful situational defensive skills in the game.

The 18-second window aligns almost perfectly with how modern mage builds operate. Most burst compositions aim to win before or shortly after that mark.

---

### 3. No Escape – Preemptive Energy Control

**Effect:** Silence at start of battle (6 seconds)
**Counters:** Early ultimate cycling
**Hard countered by:** Fountain of Life

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-112.png)

No Escape is extremely strong — when used correctly. It disrupts:

- Early Energy Mastery loops
- Immediate mage ultimates

However, many players use **Fountain of Life** precisely to counter No Escape. If Fountain is present, No Escape loses almost all value.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-114.png)

### Rule of thumb:

- If enemy does NOT run Fountain of Life → equip No Escape.
- If they DO → remove it immediately.

This is one of the few skills in the game that requires active scouting before locking your formation.

---

## Secondary but Viable Mitigation Options

While the three above are core anti-mage tools, several additional skills can complement your build.

### Jade Barrier

- Provides shield + magical reduction.
- Flexible and effective in mixed damage environments, especially valuable against mages with many counts of damage instances per second.

### Blessing of Defense

- General damage reduction.
- Less specialized, and short timer.

### Energy Shield

- Generic shielding effects like Energy Shield provides a buffer, however not specifically shielding from magical damage, Shields at 3s and 6s intervals can help a lot defending against magical damage skills at similar trigger timers.
- Better as supplementary protection rather than primary defense.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-109.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-71.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-75.png)

---

## Other means of controling mages ability to deal magical damage:

### Control and Silencing: The Power of Restraint

Control is a potent way to counter magical damage, especially against immortals who rely on casting their spells. Utilize the following skills to silence and control your magical adversaries:

- **Silence**: Prevents enemies from casting ultimate skills and energy regeneration.
- **Siren's Gaze**: Like No Escape this skills silence control provide effective ways to disrupt enemy mages and casters.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-72.png)

---

### Malice Aura: Shield Against Critical Hits

Magical damage often comes in potent bursts, and you don't want to face a critical hit.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-73.png)

Use skills like **Malice** to protect against critical hits, which can be particularly powerful against magical damage given how all mages need to build into crit to secure quick massive bursts to win.

---

### Transferance and Tanking: Shifting the Burden

Mitigating magical damage can also involve transferance and tanking immortals. These strategies help divert and distribute damage more effectively:

- **Guard and Assist**: Skills that transfer incoming damage to specific tank immortals.
- **Absolute Defense and Void Realm**: Skills that bolster the ability of tanking immortals to absorb and mitigate damage.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-74.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-76.png)

---

### Universal Mitigation: Healing Effects

Healing effects, while primarily seen as sources of health regeneration, also function as universal damage mitigations. They keep your immortals healthier and better able to withstand the barrage of magical damage.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-77.png)

As you venture into the world of Infinity Kingdom, these skills and strategies will serve as your shield against the formidable magical damage from your adversaries. Master the art of countering magical damage, and watch your immortals thrive amidst the mystical storm.

---

## Conclusion Summary

To counter magical damage effectively:

1. **Always maintain a dedicated anti-mage formation.**
2. Prioritize:  - **Master’s Aegis** (consistent reduction)
- **Resist** (high-value timing window)
- **No Escape** (situational energy denial)
3. Use control to delay ultimates.
4. Reduce crit impact where possible.
5. Combine mitigation with sustain to outlast burst windows.

Magical damage in the current meta is fast, crit-focused, and energy-driven. Surviving it requires preparation, not reaction.

Players who treat magical defense as a deliberate build choice — rather than an afterthought — consistently perform better in competitive environments.

---

title: Legion of Frostborn Matchmaking Guide (2026)
summary: Matchmaking is one of the least transparent systems in Legion of Frostborne. The developers have never revealed the exact formula, but they have explained the factors used to build each Conquest season. Understanding…
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/image-19-1024x559.png)

## Introduction

Matchmaking is one of the least transparent systems in Legion of Frostborne. The developers have never revealed the exact formula, but they have explained the factors used to build each Conquest season. Understanding those basics makes it much easier to prepare your alliance before KvK begins.

Over the years, the system has also evolved. Older Legion of Frostborne seasons often produced uneven matchups or worlds with very little activity. The current matchmaking system aims to create more competitive wars by considering more than just alliance power.

This guide covers the core mechanics of matchmaking, faction assignment, and Federations as they work today.

---

## How Matchmaking Works

Legion of Frostborne matchmaking is used during the **Conquest Season**.

Instead of grouping servers using a single statistic, the game evaluates several factors before creating each KvK world. According to the developers, these include:

- Lord Power
- Historical battle performance
- Player activity
- Previous participation in Legion of Frostborne

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/image-20-1024x571.png)

The exact weighting of these factors has never been published, so nobody outside the development team can calculate matchmaking in advance. From experience, however, active servers with a history of strong KvK performance generally face opponents of similar strength.

The goal is to create worlds where every faction has a realistic chance to compete, rather than matching highly active servers against inactive ones.

---

## Faction Assignment

Once matchmaking is complete, each KvK world is divided into **four factions**.

The eight strongest alliances, based on Alliance Power, are automatically assigned to those factions. Every remaining alliance has a 48-hour window to choose which faction it wants to join.

If an alliance does not make a selection before the deadline, the game assigns one automatically.

One important restriction begins at this stage: once faction selection opens, server migration is locked until the Legion of Frostborne season ends.

---

## Understanding Federations

One of the biggest changes to Legion of Frostborne was the introduction of the **Federation** system.

A Federation replaces much of the old alliance-only cooperation by allowing up to four alliances from the same faction to work together almost as a single group.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/image-21-1024x563.png)

Any alliance leader can create a Federation by spending Gems, and leadership can later be transferred if needed.

In practice, Federations have become the foundation of alliance coordination throughout KvK.

---

## What Federations Can Do

Alliances inside the same Federation gain access to several forms of shared gameplay.

They can:

- Launch rallies together.
- Garrison cities, checkpoints, and Thermal Towers together.
- Donate troops to shared garrisons.
- Reinforce players from other Federation alliances.
- Defend each other during battles.
- Attack enemy Federations as a coordinated force.

Friendly fire is also disabled between Federation members. You cannot attack players or Thermal Towers belonging to another alliance within your Federation.

This level of cooperation makes Federations far more effective than individual alliances operating independently.

---

## City Ownership and Rewards

Although Federations fight together, city ownership still follows alliance rules.

If multiple Federation alliances participate in a siege, the city belongs to whichever alliance defeats the final defending garrison.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/image-22-1024x651.png)

Rewards are divided differently depending on the objective.

**First Occupation Points** are shared between participating alliances based on the percentage of damage each alliance contributed during the capture.

**Continuous Occupation Points** belong only to the alliance that officially owns the city.

Federation members also share city specialties and city benefits, allowing every participating alliance to benefit from successful expansion.

---

## Why Planning Matters

One detail catches many servers by surprise.

The top eight alliances are assigned to factions automatically. Because of this, two allied alliances from the same server can occasionally end up in different factions before anyone has a chance to create a Federation.

If that happens, they cannot join the same Federation during that Legion of Frostborne season.

From my experience, this makes communication before matchmaking incredibly important. Server leadership should already have a rough plan for alliance organisation before faction assignments appear. Once the assignments are locked in, there is very little room to fix mistakes.

---

## Veteran Tips

A few habits consistently make Legion of Frostborne preparation much smoother.

- Keep your alliance active throughout the season. Activity appears to be one of the factors considered during matchmaking.
- Plan Federation leadership before KvK starts instead of deciding after factions are assigned.
- Coordinate city ownership early so alliances know which objectives they are responsible for.
- Remember that a Federation is much more than a diplomatic agreement. Use its shared rallies, garrisons, and reinforcements to their full potential.

I've found that the strongest servers aren't always the ones with the biggest spenders. More often, they're the servers that organise well before the map even opens.

---

## Final Thoughts

While the exact matchmaking formula remains unknown, the overall system is much easier to understand than many players think. The game evaluates several indicators of server strength before creating each Conquest season, then divides those worlds into four factions supported by the Federation system.

For most players, success starts long before the first battle. Understanding how factions are formed, how Federations operate, and how city rewards are distributed allows your server to prepare properly instead of reacting once the war has already begun.

No matchmaking system is perfect, but knowing how the current one works gives your alliance the best chance to enter Legion of Frostborne organised and ready to compete.

---

title: Matilda damage buff timers, advanced guide
summary: Matilda’s ultimate, Elegant and Magnificent, gives two buffs:
markdown:
### Matilda’s Damage Buff Timing Guide – How to Check if Your Immortals Benefit

## Introduction – Why This Even Matters

Matilda’s ultimate, **Elegant and Magnificent**, gives two buffs:

1. A 20% energy regen boost for 9 seconds (12 with her artifact).
2. A 20% *damage buff* for 1.5 seconds each time an immortal deals ultimate damage, stacking up to 3 times.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-34.png)

Most players understand the first part — it’s straightforward and valuable.
But that **1.5-second damage buff**? That’s the hidden power — and it’s also where 90% of players get no real value because they never check if their immortals actually align with it. Note that the skill was most likely "intended" to work well on ultimates with staggered damage instances, like Saladin, Hippo, and Wu/Baldwin if they trigger their chain. But there is more power to it if you like it up right and make it buff up your tower of knowledge skills. Imagine a Himiko with 60% damage buff active the second her IF ToK skill triggers - absolute destruction.

Problem is, the timing on this is super slim. This short buff window matters ***if***your immortal’s *Tower of Knowledge (ToK) skills* or other abilities activate **within that 1.5-second window** after their ultimate lands. If not, the buff fades before anything meaningful happens.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-135.png)

So, the question becomes:
👉 *How do you check whether your immortals’ timing lines up to benefit from Matilda’s buff?*

Let’s go through it step by step.

---

## Step 1: Understand What Triggers the Buff

When your immortal casts their ultimate, Matilda’s damage buff activates for 1.5 seconds.

That window starts **at the moment the ultimate’s damage instance lands** (not when it begins casting). During that short 1.5s, any damage dealt by Tower of Knowledge skills like *Annihilation, Toxin Nova*, *Garrote*, *Death Breath*, *Blade Vortex and many many more skills* will be amplified.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-35.png)

These ToK skills don’t fire constantly — they have cooldown timers or proc intervals. Most are on a 6 second timer, with some on a 3s timer and most all fire around 6, 12, 18 with some in between too. So if your immortal’s ultimates naturally happen around 11 seconds apart, you can overlap the buff window with those ToK activations by having an ultimate land at second 11 to gain the damage buff lasting through second 12 where ToK skills trigger.

---

## Step 2: Check Your Immortal’s Energy Regen Speed

You can see this number in-game:

- Tap your immortal → Power Info → scroll down to **Energy Regen**.

That number tells you how much energy they regenerate per second.
You need **1000 energy** to cast an ultimate, so the formula is simple:

> ### 1000 ÷ Energy Regen = Time (seconds) per ultimate

Example:
If your immortal has 92 Energy Regen:
1000 ÷ 92 = **10.8 seconds per ultimate**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-36-676x1024.png)

That means, on average, they’ll cast their ultimate every 10.8 seconds.

---

## Step 3: Account for Starting Energy

Here’s where most testing goes wrong — immortals don’t all start from 0.

Through **technology**, **talents**, and **boost levels**, most immortals begin with several hundred energy. For example:

- *Outstanding Talent* (tech)
- *Battle Excitement* (Support talent)
- *Boost level bonuses*

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-37.png)

If you’ve got those active, your immortals might start the fight with around **470 energy** already charged (for a backline DPS).

That means they only need **530 more** energy to cast the first ultimate. So, instead of waiting the full 10.8 seconds, they’ll often fire their first ultimate in around **4–5 seconds** — depending on regen rate.

This is why you can’t just do math on regen alone — the first ultimate comes much sooner because of starting energy, but *Matilda’s buff won’t be active yet* at that point.

---

## Step 4: Calculate When the Second Ultimate Lands

Now, the real testing point is the **second ultimate cast**, because that’s when Matilda’s buff is likely active and synced into the battle flow.

Let’s take my Empress Wu example:

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-38.png)

- Base Energy Regen: 122
- Starting energy: 470
- Energy needed for first cast: 530
→ 530 ÷ 122 = **4.3 seconds to first ultimate**. Because energy cannot overcap, **we cast at second 5.**

After casting, energy resets to 0, and she starts regaining energy again:

- 1000 ÷ 122 = **8.2 seconds to recharge** **--> 9s cast 2nd time.**

So, the **second ultimate lands at around 14 seconds** total battle time.

Third will land at 14 + 9 = 23 seconds.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/output-1024x610.png)

---

## Step 5: See if That Lines Up With Tower of Knowledge Skill Timers

Now we check what happens at those timestamps.

- **Toxin Nova:** every 6 seconds, and DoT 3s.
- **Death Breath:** every 6 seconds
- **Spell Disintegration:** 3 seconds
- **Annihilation**: 6 seconds

So, if your immortal’s second ultimate lands around 14 seconds, the 1.5s buff window *overlaps perfectly* with the ToK activation window at second 15. Here we will see Nova Dots and Spell Disintegration. But we will **not**see the main Nova hit nor DB or Annihilation.

That means the skill damage during that activation will be boosted by 20–60% (depending on stack count).

The very first cast at 5 second does actually line up to boost all the best skills that trigger at s6. But problem is, that our Wu has a lot more starting energy than Matilda will have due to Battle Excitation, so we will not get the buff within 5 seconds to activate. At the 12s window for ToK skills, we have not yet cast the second ultimate and at the 18s window is again out of sync with the third ultimate landing at second 23. All in all, Matilda's damage buff will NOT line up well for this Empress Wu's energy regen. Sadly!

That being said, we can still gain a lot of value from Matilda, and I still like Matilda in fire builds, simply because that one Wu ultimate that activates a chain effect will chain with the added damage and because we get the regen, which is huge value in itself (although outside the scope of this article).

---

## Step 6: Testing In Practice

You can test your timings easily:

1. Go to **Battle Replay**.
2. Tap the **buff icons** on the right side of the screen.
3. Watch when your immortal’s ultimate lands, and check the 1.5s Matilda buff window.
4. See which ToK skills activate during that same second.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-134.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-135.png)

If you see Toxin Nova or Death Breath firing while the buff icon is visible, you’re golden — your immortal is syncing with Matilda perfectly.

If not, they’re missing out on the damage window entirely.

---

## Conclusion – The Bottom Line

Matilda’s 1.5-second damage buff is one of those tiny windows that makes a huge difference if you actually line it up. For most immortals, it just comes and goes unnoticed — but if your energy regen cycles put your ultimates near that **11 second mark** and/or the **17 second mark**, your Tower of Knowledge skills can hit while the buff is active and deal noticeably more damage.

**Bottom line:**
If you want to know whether Matilda’s damage buff really helps your team — don’t guess.
Check your regen speed, test your timings, and watch your replays. If those ToK skill activations happen during the buff window, you’re getting the real value she offers. If not, she’s just giving you energy regen — which is good, but nowhere near her full potential.

title: Immortal: Matilda of Flanders (wind)
summary: Matilda might be technically as a support, but honestly, she plays like an engine. Her kit doesn’t heal or shield — instead, it supercharges your team’s energy regen and turns your immortals into ultimate-spamming…
markdown:
### Matilda Guide – The Energy Queen of Infinity Kingdom

Matilda might be technically as a *support*, but honestly, she plays like an *engine*. Her kit doesn’t heal or shield — instead, it supercharges your team’s **energy regen** and turns your immortals into ultimate-spamming machines.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-127.png)

She belongs to the **Wind element**, but don’t let that lock you in. The best part about Matilda is that she fits into almost any setup that relies on frequent ultimate casts — Fire, Wind, even odd cross-elemental hybrid control comps. I’ve used her with Hippo, Wu, and in Baldwin setups, and she performs incredibly well in the right synergy because her buff directly amplifies what makes most top-tier immortals strong: their ultimates.

---

## How to Get Matilda

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-128-1024x536.png)

Matilda first appears as a **KvK reward** in Season 2. But for most players, the real way to build her is through the **Golden Path Battlepass**:

- You can get her fragments directly
- Or from the random Wind elemental fragment

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-129-1024x417.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-130.png)

She also has a **small chance** to appear in:

- Random epic immortal fragments
- Advanced Summons in the Hall of Immortals

**Important:** She does **not** appear in the Marketplace, so the Battlepass is by far the most reliable route for progression.

---

## Skill Breakdown – “Elegant and Magnificent”

Matilda’s ultimate skill is the reason you pick her, period.

### Elegant and Magnificent:

- Increases **energy regen speed by 20%** for all allies for **9 seconds**.
- Every time an immortal deals *damage with their ultimate* during this 9-second window, that immortal gains a **20% damage increase** for 1.5 seconds, stacking up to 3 times.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-133.png)

So, theoretically that’s +60% damage, but — and here’s the catch — that buff window is very short (1.5 seconds). It’s not a 9-second blanket buff; it spikes for brief moments during staggered ultimate damage hits.

You can confirm this in combat replays by checking the **buff tab** — you’ll see the stacks appearing and falling off quickly as ultimates tick.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-134.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-135.png)

---

## Artifact – Bayeux Tapestry

This is what turns Matilda from “good” into “crazy.” Obtained via the Golden Path, Daily Pearls Shop (in s2) or through Stellar Compass event.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-132-1024x606.png)

### Bayeux Tapestry:

- Extends her buff duration from **9 seconds to 12 seconds.**

That extra 3 seconds doesn’t sound like much, but in reality, it closes the loop on her energy cycle. With high enough regen, you can reach **near-100% uptime** on her buff. Let’s break that down, read more below.

---

## Matilda’s Energy Regen and Uptime

Her default base **energy regen is 71.0**, meaning she takes about **14 seconds** to reach 1000 energy and cast. Her ultimate lasts 9 seconds, so normally she’d have a **5-second gap** between buffs.

But once you invest in her and build properly, that gap disappears.

### At Boost Level 25 + Energy Surge Tech (no surge artifact, no talents):

- 83.1 energy regen → 12.03 seconds. But since we cannot overcap on energy she casts at the **13 second marker.**

### With Bayeux Tapestry:

- Buff lasts **12 seconds**
- Cast cycle 13 seconds
- → **1 second of downtime!**

### Hitting the 100% Uptime Threshold

If you add *either* of the following, you exceed the **critical 83.4 regen threshold**needed for perfect rotation: 1000 energy divided by 83.4 regen = time to max energy of 11.9 seconds meaning you cast at the 12s marker.

### At Boost Level 25 + Energy Surge Tech + Owl Guardian Military talent (no surge artifact):

- **Owl Guardian Talent (+5%)** AND **Surge Tech (+5%)**

With those, you’re looking at around **86.6 energy regen**, which maintains full uptime.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-141-1024x798.png)

---

## How It Actually Plays Out

Matilda’s ultimate works best on immortals that:

- Deal *multiple* damage instances in one ultimate but with staggered timing on each damage instance (e.g. **Hippolyta**, or given procs **Wu**, **Baldwin** and others).
- Given the very short window, you will **NOT**be able to chain multiple cast sequences.

Take Hippo, for example. Her ultimate hits 7 times. Each hit refreshes the damage buff, and by the 4th–7th tick she’s doing up to 60% more damage.

Wu and Baldwin also benefit because they sometimes re-cast their ultimates rapidly. Every extra proc can trigger another burst of boosted damage.

Now besides the simple "can I get a damage buff for my ultimate", players are also asking me how to figure out if they can get the damage buffs on their tower of knowledge skills. Tower of knowledge skills are a very large part of an immortal's damage output. To figure out if you can get a juicy Matilda damage buff for your tower of knowledge skills, you have to carefully review your immortal's energy regen, starting energy and then count out the time to casts and see if they line up with the timer of tower of knowledge skills. For example, if an energy regen and starting energy means that an immortal casts his or her ultimate at second 11 (assuming no interruptions from silences and other control effects), then you are going to have the Matilda damage buff active at the 12th second where most tower of knowledge skills have a trigger timer. To read more about this pretty nerdy thing, **[check out this guide](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/immortals/specific-immortal-deepdives/matilda-of-flanders-wind/matilda-damage-buff-timers-advanced-guide/)**.

---

## The Real Power: Energy Regen Buff

Getting value from the damage buff can be hard and sometimes impossible, but fear not, the real value here is that **+20% energy regen** for 9 (12) seconds.

That’s massive, especially for immortals who already have solid base regen or rely heavily on fast cycling. Think of it like a global Adrenaline Rush for your whole team.

---

## Best Pairings

If you want to get real value from Matilda, pair her with immortals that either:

1. Have **multi-hit ultimates**, or
2. Depend heavily on **fast energy cycling**.

Here are some top combos I’ve tested and liked:

- **Fire:** Hippo + Wu + Trajan + Matilda → nonstop ultimates and good scaling.
- **Wind:** Baldwin + Saladin + Matilda → great regen uptime and Baldwin gets full damage buff chains.
- **Hybrid Defense:** Charles + Hippo + Baldwin + Matilda → strong sustain and ultimate frequency.

She’s flexible — just avoid slotting her where no one benefits from the regen or short damage buff.

---

## Conclusion – The Bottom Line

Matilda isn’t about flashy plays or top-line damage; she’s about **flow**. She controls your team’s tempo like a metronome, letting your main carries fire off ultimates faster and harder.

If you invest in her artifact and a make sure you have some combination of the regen bonuses, you can reach **permanent uptime** on one of the strongest buffs in the game.

---

title: Max Bounty Gem Farming Guide – Better Than Gnome Bosses?
markdown:
![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261018-195919-ofao1q.png)

## How Max Bounty Gem Farming Works

Max Bounty features six combat missions, ranging from one to six stars. Each mission rewards **5 Gems per star**, meaning the six-star mission provides 30 Gems.

| Difficulty        | Gem Reward   |
| ----------------- | ------------ |
| 1 Star            | 5            |
| 2 Stars           | 10           |
| 3 Stars           | 15           |
| 4 Stars           | 20           |
| 5 Stars           | 25           |
| 6 Stars           | 30           |
| **Full Rotation** | **105 Gems** |

Completing all six missions provides 105 Gems, and a new set becomes available every hour.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261018-195826-uyndo5.png)

Importantly, completing the final milestone at 260 points doesn't stop the activity. Players can continue earning Gems from missions throughout the event, even after collecting all milestone rewards.

## Max Bounty vs. Gnome Bosses – Gem Efficiency

To determine whether Max Bounty is worthwhile, we compared it with farming Level 20 Gnome Bosses, which consistently provide **5 Gems per successful attack**.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261018-195808-ng2fgc.png)

Based on our testing, the average AP cost is approximately 77 per Max Bounty mission and 83 per Level 20 Gnome Boss attack.

| Metric                 | Max Bounty | Level 20 Gnome Boss |
| ---------------------- | ---------- | ------------------- |
| Gems per attack        | 5–30       | 5                   |
| AP per attack          | ~77        | 83                  |
| Gems per 100 AP        | **22.7**   | **6.0**             |
| AP needed for 100 Gems | ~440       | ~1,660              |

This means that Max Bounty provides approximately **3.8 times more Gems per AP** than regular Level 20 Gnome Bosses.

For example, spending 1,000 AP on Max Bounty would theoretically yield around 227 Gems, compared with just 60 Gems from regular boss farming.

That's a significant difference, particularly for players with large AP reserves.



## How to Improve Your Farming Efficiency

One useful trick is to **activate AP-reduction talents before starting Max Bounty missions**.

Testing has confirmed that these talents work on Max Bounty encounters, reducing the AP cost of individual battles.

Players can also rally with alliance members to tackle difficult missions, potentially reducing the burden on weaker formations.

Remember that you don't necessarily need to complete every mission each hour. If particular encounters cause excessive casualties, it may be better to focus on easier missions rather than repeatedly losing troops for a few additional Gems.

## Is Max Bounty Worth Farming?

**Yes, particularly for players who can defeat the missions without suffering excessive troop losses.**

Based purely on AP efficiency, Max Bounty is an excellent source of Gems, providing approximately 3.8 times the Gem rewards of Level 20 Gnome Boss farming.

However, that advantage must be weighed against the potentially higher troop casualties, especially for players with weaker marches.

For stronger players, the ability to earn 105 Gems every hour makes Max Bounty one of the more interesting repeatable farming opportunities introduced with Tycoon's Club.

**Our recommendation:** Complete the 260-point milestone track first, then continue farming Max Bounty if your AP reserves and troop losses make it worthwhile. With significantly better Gem returns per AP than regular Gnome Bosses, there's good reason to keep participating even after collecting the final milestone reward.

title: Max Resource to EXP efficiency for artifact leveling
summary: Artifacts are one of the most impactful progression systems in Infinity Kingdom. While they may appear secondary compared to buildings, technology, or immortal ascension, artifacts contribute a significant portion of an…
markdown:
## Artifact Leveling and EXP Efficiency in Infinity Kingdom

Artifacts are one of the most impactful progression systems in Infinity Kingdom. While they may appear secondary compared to buildings, technology, or immortal ascension, artifacts contribute a significant portion of an immortal’s effective combat power. They scale core stats that influence damage thresholds, survivability breakpoints, and consistency in prolonged fights.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-93-1024x433.png)

In modern Infinity Kingdom, city progression is fast. Buildings and technology advance quickly, especially compared to earlier versions of the game. Artifact leveling, however, does not scale at the same pace. As a result, many players reach mid and late game with strong cities and well-built immortals, but underleveled artifacts across their primary marches.

Reaching artifact level 15 is especially demanding. While the level cap itself does not look extreme, the cumulative EXP requirement becomes a major bottleneck when multiplied across multiple immortals and multiple marches. This pressure is felt most acutely at the same time players are heavily investing resources into city development and technology.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-139-1024x502.png)

Understanding **EXP efficiency**,**i.e. how many resources you spend per point of artifact EXP**, is therefore critical.

To further understand artifact upgrading and efficient use of EXP, **[read this guide too.](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/immortals/artifacts/artifact-upgrade-costs/exp-cost-and-how-to-level-artifacts-efficiently/)**

---

## How Artifact EXP Is Actually Generated

Artifact EXP primarily comes from **feeding artifacts into other artifacts**. While fragments are earned from many sources, including events and rewards, the consistent and free-to-play source of long-term artifact fragments is **Mysterium**. These fragments are non-unique and are well suited for EXP purposes.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-95-1024x410.png)

This guide does not focus on fragment acquisition strategies. The assumption is simple: keep farming Mysterium consistently. The real challenge lies in what happens next—**forging artifacts and converting them into EXP efficiently**.

---

## Artifact Forging Basics

All artifacts, regardless of tier, follow the same basic forging structure.

Each artifact requires **two types of forging materials**, with **six of each**, for a total of **twelve materials per artifact**. While the individual resource composition may vary (some materials cost more wood, others more iron or food), the **total resource cost per material tier is fixed**. For efficiency analysis, it is therefore correct to treat all costs as total resources.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-140-1024x512.png)

This allows us to compare tiers directly.

---

## Resource Cost to Forge One Artifact

The following values represent the **total resource cost** to forge a single artifact of each tier:

- **Normal (Green)**: 132,000 resources per material → 1,584,000 resources per artifact
- **Rare (Blue)**: 800,000 resources per material → 9,600,000 resources per artifact
- **Elite (Purple)**: 2,000,000 resources per material → 24,000,000 resources per artifact
- **Epic (Orange)**: 4,800,000 resources per material → 57,600,000 resources per artifact

Legendary artifacts are excluded from this guide. Using them for EXP is never efficient under any realistic scenario.

---

## Artifact EXP Values by Tier

When forged artifacts are consumed as EXP fodder, they provide the following amounts:

- **Green**: 10 EXP
- **Blue**: 30 EXP
- **Purple**: 100 EXP
- **Orange**: 300 EXP

Unique artifacts provide no EXP advantage over non-unique ones. From a pure EXP standpoint, uniqueness is irrelevant.

The total EXP required to reach **artifact level 15** is **3,380 EXP**.

---

## Core Metric: Resources per 1 EXP

The most important efficiency metric is **how many resources are required to generate one point of EXP**.

- **Green**: 158,400 resources per EXP
- **Blue**: 320,000 resources per EXP
- **Purple**: 240,000 resources per EXP
- **Orange**: 192,000 resources per EXP

### Efficiency Ranking (Best to Worst)

1. Green
2. Orange
3. Purple
4. Blue

This ranking is consistent and unforgiving. From a purely mathematical standpoint, **Blue artifacts are the least efficient EXP source in the game**.

---

## Total Resource Cost to Max an Artifact (Level 15)

To put the efficiency into practical terms, here is what it costs to generate 3,380 EXP using each tier.

### Ideal Cost (No Wasted EXP)

- **Green**: 535,392,000 resources
- **Blue**: 1,081,600,000 resources
- **Purple**: 811,200,000 resources
- **Orange**: 648,960,000 resources

### Practical Cost (Whole Artifacts Only)

Because artifacts can only be consumed whole, slight overproduction is unavoidable.

- **Green**: 338 artifacts → 535,392,000 resources
- **Blue**: 113 artifacts → 1,084,800,000 resources
- **Purple**: 34 artifacts → 816,000,000 resources
- **Orange**: 12 artifacts → 691,200,000 resources

The takeaway is clear: **Blue artifacts cost roughly twice as much as Green to reach the same result**, and significantly more than both Purple and Orange.

---

## EXP Return per Million Resources

Another useful way to view efficiency is EXP gained per 1,000,000 resources spent:

- **Green**: 6.31 EXP per million
- **Orange**: 5.21 EXP per million
- **Purple**: 4.17 EXP per million
- **Blue**: 3.13 EXP per million

This perspective reinforces the same conclusion: Green artifacts convert resources into EXP better than any other tier.

---

## Practical Strategy for Most Players

For players managing limited resources while upgrading multiple marches, the optimal EXP strategy follows a clear hierarchy.

**Green artifacts are the most resource-efficient EXP source** and should form the backbone of long-term artifact leveling plans. They are slow in volume but unmatched in value.

**Orange artifacts offer the best balance between efficiency and speed**. While slightly less efficient than Green, they drastically reduce the number of artifacts required and are often preferred when pushing key artifacts to level 15 quickly.

**Purple artifacts sit in an inefficient middle ground**. They are acceptable if already available, but rarely worth forging specifically for EXP.

**Blue artifacts should generally be avoided as EXP fodder**. Their cost-to-EXP ratio is the worst in the system, and they consume resources that could be used far more effectively elsewhere.

---

## Final Thoughts: Why Efficiency Matters Long-Term

Artifact leveling is not a one-time task. As you build more marches, unlock more immortals, and refine your competitive setups, EXP demand grows continuously. Because artifact transmutation directly competes with city and technology development, inefficient EXP choices can quietly delay overall progression.

Understanding resource-to-EXP efficiency allows you to level artifacts deliberately rather than reactively. Over time, this translates into stronger marches, smoother progression, and fewer moments where artifact leveling becomes a bottleneck rather than a power spike.

For players who want sustained strength rather than short-term gains, **artifact EXP efficiency is not optional—it is foundational**.

---

markdown:
### Mastering the Art of Skill Stone Farming in the Blessings of Triss Event

Welcome, commanders, to the Blessings of Triss event—a realm of wishes, artifacts, and the elusive skill stones. In this guide, we will unravel the strategic approach to maximize your chances of acquiring skill stones efficiently, saving resources and ensuring success in your endeavors.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-206-1024x546.png)

### 1. Event Overview:

The Blessings of Triss event offers commanders the opportunity to purchase wishes, which can be used to obtain various rewards, including artifact fragments, unique artifacts, and the highly sought-after skill stones. With 151 drops available in a single clear, understanding how to farm skill stones efficiently is paramount.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-209-1024x580.png)

### 2. Resetting the Board:

After obtaining the desired rewards, commanders have the option to reset the Triss event, refreshing the board and cycling through artifacts and skill stones. This allows for targeted farming, enabling players to focus on specific artifacts or skill stones they need for their Immortals.

### 3. Farming Artifact Fragments:

While farming artifact fragments, commanders can strategically eliminate unwanted artifacts, increasing the drop rate for the desired ones. However, this approach comes at the cost of additional wishes. It is crucial to evaluate the trade-off between increased drop rates and efficient wish usage.

### 4. Skill Stone Drop Rates:

Unlike artifact drop rates, the drop chance for skill stones remains constant regardless of the number of wishes used. Whether a commander opts for a 1-wish draw or a 6-wish draw, the chance of obtaining a skill stone remains the same.

### 5. Efficient Skill Stone Farming Strategy:

To maximize efficiency in acquiring skill stones, commanders are advised to follow these steps:

1. **One-Wish Draws:** Initiate one-wish draws until you obtain a skill stone. The drop chance remains consistent, making this the most resource-efficient method.
2. **Reset and Repeat:** Once a skill stone is acquired, reset the board, and repeat the process. This ensures commanders focus on finishing one skill before moving on to the next.
3. **Wish Banking:** To avoid inefficient wish usage, maintain an adequate reserve of wishes. Unlucky streaks may require multiple draws, and having enough wishes to complete a round even with bad luck is crucial.
4. **Estimated Cost:** On average, commanders may spend around 55-60 wishes per skill stone. Considering the cost of wishes, approximately $137-$150 per skill stone draw can be expected.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-208-1024x576.png)

### 6. Note on Drop Chance:

While the official drop chance for a skill stone is 1%, it's essential to understand that the probability changes with each wish. The initial draw has a 1% chance, but subsequent draws see a slightly higher chance as the pool of unwanted items decreases.

### 7. Conclusion:

Mastering the art of skill stone farming in the Blessings of Triss event requires a strategic and resource-conscious approach. By adopting efficient wish usage, resetting the board judiciously, and maintaining a wish reserve, commanders can navigate the event with precision. May your wishes be granted, and your Immortals strengthened with the coveted skill stones. Best of luck, commanders!

title: Maximizing Honor Ranking Buffs in Infinity Kingdom

markdown:
Navigating the intricate world of Infinity Kingdom, where alliances and kingdoms vie for supremacy, the strategic allocation of your most influential fighters across the honor rankings of all kingdoms stands as a pivotal gameplay element. This guide delves into the art of leveraging honor ranking buffs, a cornerstone for individual and alliance-wide success.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-1024x360.png)

## The Power of Honor Ranking Buffs

Honor ranking buffs are among the most coveted enhancements in Infinity Kingdom. Attained through achieving high ranks within a kingdom's honor ladder, these buffs confer significant advantages, including troop enhancements and substantial buffs to immortals. Understanding and exploiting these buffs can elevate your gameplay, making your forces a formidable opponent on the battlefield.

### Key Benefits

- **Troop Strength:** Certain honor titles grant additional troops, bolstering your army's size and resilience.
- **Enhanced Immortal Performance:** High percentage buffs to immortals can dramatically increase your effectiveness in combat.
- **Strategic Advantage:** Possessing these buffs can tilt the balance in closely contested battles, making your army more versatile and powerful.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-1-1024x348.png)

## Strategic Allocation Across Kingdoms

To maximize the impact of honor ranking buffs, a strategic approach to their allocation is essential. This involves positioning your alliance's most vital active fighters within the honor ladders of different kingdoms to ensure access to a broader range of buffs.

### Step-by-Step Strategy

#### Step 1: Evaluate Your Alliance and server Strengths

- **Assess the Composition:** Determine the primary strengths and compositions of your players who are the leading fighters. Understanding each member's strategic value is crucial for optimal placement.
- **Identify Key Buffs:** Pinpoint which buffs will most benefit your alliance's overall strategy and which members are best suited to pursue these buffs.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-2-1024x541.png)

#### Step 2: Plan for Kingdom Allocation

- **Distribute Strategically:** Allocate your top fighters across the kingdoms based on the buffs that align with their strengths and your alliance's needs. This strategic distribution ensures access to a diverse set of buffs, enhancing your collective fighting capability.
- **Coordinate Moves:** Organize the transition of members to target kingdoms, ensuring they can achieve the necessary honor rankings for the desired buffs.

#### Step 3: Secure and Maintain Honor Rankings

- **Pursue Rankings:** Once positioned in the target kingdom, your fighters must actively participate in events and battles to climb the honor ladder.
- **Maintain Activity:** Keeping high-ranking positions requires consistent participation and success in kingdom activities, demanding ongoing commitment from your key members.

### Maximizing Buff Benefits

- **Leverage Buff Synergies:** Utilize the combination of different buffs across your alliance to create synergistic effects, enhancing your strategic options in wars and events.
- **Adapt and Evolve:** As your alliance grows and the game dynamics change, continually reassess your buff strategy to maintain optimal alignment with your goals.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-3-1024x433.png)

## Conclusion

The strategic allocation of honor ranking buffs across different kingdoms represents a game-changing approach in Infinity Kingdom. By carefully positioning your most critical fighters within the honor ladders of various kingdoms, your alliance can harness a powerful array of buffs, significantly enhancing your competitive edge. This strategy not only maximizes individual prowess but also strengthens your alliance's collective might, paving the way for dominance in Norheim. Embrace this nuanced strategy, and lead your alliance to glory through the strategic use of honor ranking buffs.

title: Medusa (chaos)
summary: So, Medusa just dropped, and honestly she’s already looking like one of the spiciest Immortals IK has pushed out in a long while - while we do not know yet being released literally today as I write this - I do believe…
markdown:
So, Medusa just dropped, and honestly she’s already looking like one of the spiciest Immortals IK has pushed out in a long while - while we do not know yet being released literally today as I write this - I do believe she will redefine the meta along with the new 2.8.9 ToK skills (read more under ToK skill guides or patch notes).

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-46-1024x518.png)

In this guide, I’ll run through what we actually know from her in-game description, how her stats translate into real gameplay, and some early thoughts on team setups and skill builds. Think of this as a veteran player reacting in real time while also trying to make sense of where she fits into the meta.

---

## Medusa’s Stats – Why Her Energy Regen Is a Big Deal

The real headline with Medusa isn’t her damage or her CC. It’s that *base* Energy Regen of **122.1**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-47-1024x739.png)

To put that in context:

- I was expecting maybe 90–100.
- She came in way above that.
- Maxed with boosts, she’s realistically landing somewhere around **135–145 Energy Regen**.

That’s nuts...!

What that means in actual battles is:

- **She isn’t getting stopped by anti-regen effects** like Knife Through Butter.
- **She’s firing her skills constantly**, no matter what.
- In burst teams, that fast cycling is basically a win condition by itself.

---

## Medusa’s Kit — Overtuned? Perhaps

Let’s break down the two main parts of her kit, based on what’s shown in-game.

### 1. Passive Damage: Up to 600%

Patch notes originally listed **500%**, but IK literally wrote “you cannot refer to this” and told players to trust in-game text. And in-game? It clearly says **600%**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-48-1024x555.png)

600% passive damage with her Energy Regen means:

- She hits harder *and* more often than e.g. Genghis.
- She becomes a consistent source of pressure instead of the usual “big moment, long wait.”
- This scales insanely well in full-burst teams like Fire.

### 2. Active Skill: Cleanse + 70% Petrify

Her active skill:

- **Removes ALL debuffs from herself**
- **Fires a Petrification beam with up to 70% chance**

The cleanse alone is already incredibly strong. But that **70% CC chance** is quite massive!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-49.png)

For comparison:

- Ares’ Fright is **50%**, and that still decides fights.

Honestly, this is the part that scares me the most. At 70%, she’s going to lock marches down constantly unless something counters her directly and given her speed I dont see much to actually stop her, especially paired with.. yes you guessed it: Ares for Fright. Maybe we will see those two being at the heart of the new meta.

### Artifact (Case of Silence)

The artifact adds:

- **Extra duration to the petrification effect (around +3 seconds)**
- Which makes the CC even more oppressive when it lands.

If you pull her artifact early, she’s going to become a monster in CC-centric burst builds.

---

## Skill Suggestions – Not Final, but Looking Strong

This is still early, but based on her design:

### Top skill picks so far

These are the ones you mentioned and they logically make sense:

- **Energy Mastery** – Perfect synergy with her regen.
- **Blade Dodge** – Helps her survive burst focus when she becomes the enemy’s #1 target.
- **Time to Shine** – One of the best offensive boosters for fast-rotation Immortals.
- **Demonic Contract** – Works if your march can keep her alive long enough to output.

Because she fires so often, anything that feeds more casts or keeps her alive between casts is basically gold.

---

## Conclusion Summary

Medusa looks extremely strong right out of the gate, mainly because of:

- **Insane Energy Regen**
- **600% passive damage**
- **70% petrify chance with a cleanse**
- **Artifact that extends CC even further**

Fire teams are the best fit for her so far, but she might splash into other lineups once players get hands-on time.

**Bottom line:**
If she plays even half as well as her numbers suggest, Medusa is likely going to reshape burst meta teams immediately. That being said, she released today, so these are naturally all just my ideas as to how the meta will change and how she will perform. Only time will tell if I am right!

**Mercantile Path**, The latest update patch in the Infinity Kingdom 2.2 patch release. This new event has a unique playstyle unlike any other in Norheim history. Let's dive into what is up and down here.
