title: Mercantile Path incl. Rewards scaling across seasons
summary: The Mercantile Path is one of the more quietly important recurring
markdown:
## Mercantile Path Event Guide (Free-to-Play Focus)

### Introduction

The **Mercantile Path** is one of the more quietly important recurring events in **Infinity Kingdom**. It appears every week, costs no gems, and steadily feeds one of the most constrained progression resources in the game: **Unique Artifact fragments**. Because artifacts scale slowly and demand huge fragment counts, Mercantile Path ends up mattering far more than its simple mechanics suggest—especially for free-to-play and low-spender players.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-160.png)

At a glance, the event is straightforward: summon a caravan, escort it through waves of gnome attackers, and deliver it safely to the bazaar. Underneath that simplicity, however, are a few efficiency considerations that decide whether the event is—all but background noise—or one of your most reliable long-term power sources.

---

### Event Basics: How Mercantile Path Works

Mercantile Path revolves around escorting a single caravan instance from start to finish.

- You **summon a caravan** and choose its difficulty.
- The caravan moves along a fixed route toward the bazaar.
- **Gnome raiders periodically attack**, attempting to steal supplies.
- If you successfully defeat the gnomes before they reach the caravan, you preserve your reward.
- You are limited to **5 escorts per day**, so each run matters.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-162.png)

There are **three difficulty levels**, each with a recommended power value. Unlike many Infinity Kingdom hints, these recommendations are surprisingly accurate. Max difficulty is not trivial, but it *is* soloable for a large portion of mid- to late-game players, and easily manageable with alliance reinforcement if needed.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-163.png)

You can escort alone or group up. Functionally, the caravan behaves like a rally: multiple marches can defend it, and reinforcements help cover weaker setups. That flexibility is what keeps the event accessible even if your anti-gnome efficiency isn’t optimized.

---

### Difficulty Selection and Why Max Difficulty Matters

If you are unable to complete Caravans at the highest level you should adjust difficulty accordingly. While it sucks to be short on artifact fragments, getting as many as you can is always the priority. Never give up, push your limit and farm!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-165.png)

If you are able to clear it consistently - either solo or with help - you should always do so. Over weeks and months, running lower tiers translates directly into fewer completed artifacts.

If max difficulty feels unstable:

- Bring alliance reinforcements.
- Run your strongest, most consistent march rather than experimental builds.
- Prioritize survival and control over raw damage if gnomes are slipping through.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-166.png)

Specialized anti-gnome builds do exist and can trivialize the event, but those optimizations are optional. Raw march quality and sensible immortal pairing are enough for most players.

---

### Rewards Breakdown (By Season)

This is where Mercantile Path earns its reputation.

You are capped at **5 escorts per day**, and you should treat that cap as mandatory participation rather than optional content.

- **Season 1 & 2 Servers**  - Each max-difficulty escort grants **5× elemental Unique Artifact selection chests**
- Standard elements only: *Water, Fire, Earth, Lightning, Wind*

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-167.png)

- **Conquest & Legendary Servers**  - Each max-difficulty escort grants **7 Unique Artifact fragment chests**
- That’s **35 fragments per day**, **105 per week**, from a single event meaning one maxed artifact takes just 9 weeks completly for free!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-161.png)

These rewards are guaranteed on successful completion, not tied to RNG drops or rankings. That reliability is exactly why Mercantile Path scales so well over time.

---

### Alliance Ranking Rewards: Small Numbers, Long-Term Value

Beyond the per-run rewards, **Mercantile Path** also includes an **alliance-based ranking system**. Every alliance on the server competes collectively, with rankings determined by overall event participation and performance. The rewards are not flashy—typically a modest bundle of items—but they do include **Philosopher’s Stones**, which makes them worth caring about.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-164.png)

On their own, a few stones don’t feel impactful. Over time, however, they add up, especially once you start converting them into **purple Soul Crystals** for **Tower of Knowledge** upgrades. Those upgrades scale slowly and demand a steady trickle of resources rather than sudden bursts, which is exactly where these ranking rewards fit in.

The important point is that **individual consistency feeds alliance-wide progress**. Every escort you complete contributes toward your alliance’s standing. Even if you personally don’t feel the immediate benefit, skipping attempts actively weakens your alliance’s long-term resource flow.

So if nothing else, treat your **5 daily escorts** as a contribution obligation. You’re not just escorting a caravan - you’re helping secure incremental, alliance-wide growth for your friends, and in Infinity Kingdom, those small efficiencies compound faster than most players expect.

---

### Why You Should Never Skip Your 5 Daily Escorts

Artifact progression is slow by design. To fully max **one** Unique Artifact, you need:

- **15 fragments per craft**
- **60 crafts** to reach max rank
- That’s **900 fragments minimum**, *before* accounting for:  - Bad attribute rolls
- Poor bonus effects
- Recrafting to fix undesirable stats

Seen through that lens, Mercantile Path stops being “just another weekly event” and starts looking like infrastructure. It quietly funds your long-term power curve.

There’s also a secondary incentive: **battle pass progression**. Mercantile Path escorts frequently appear as required tasks in paid and free passes alike. Even if you don’t care about the pass itself, skipping escorts usually means leaving value unclaimed.

---

### Player Perspective: Practical Takeaways

From experience, Mercantile Path rewards consistency more than optimization.

I’ve run it with fully tuned anti-gnome marches, and I’ve run it with generic PvE setups. The difference is comfort, not outcome. As long as you clear max difficulty reliably, the event does its job.

The real mistake players make is **treating Mercantile Path as optional**. Five escorts a day feels repetitive, especially when caravan travel time stretches out, but over a few months the fragment gap between consistent players and skippers becomes enormous.

---

### Conclusion Summary

Mercantile Path is one of Infinity Kingdom’s best free-to-play events:

- Weekly, predictable, and low-stress
- Guaranteed Unique Artifact fragments
- Scales extremely well over time
- Accessible solo or with alliance support

If you can clear max difficulty, **do all five escorts, every time**. Unique Artifacts are too central to late-game performance to ignore one of the few steady sources available. Mercantile Path may not be flashy, but it quietly carries long-term accounts forward—one caravan at a time.

---

---
***Meteorain: A Pre-Castle 50 Earth/Wind Hybrid Counter*** --- ***A practical guide to VictorSeven’s Season 2 counter-build***

Season 2 of *Infinity Kingdom* has been defined by one thing more than any other: the widespread abuse of Earth/Wind Hybrid. High attack speed, cleave scaling, and relentless normal-attack pressure allow these teams to overwhelm most midgame defenses long before players gain access to true hard counters.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-157-1024x619.png)

VictorSeven’s **Meteorain** build exists specifically to answer that problem. As he puts it:

> *“I dunno about you, but I am sick to death of that awful Earth Wind Hybrid everyone seems to be abusing in Season 2. So I came up with a low spend (not free, sadly) counter comp that has some mid spend options to maximize it.
> I call it Meteorain. Why? We'll get to that. Just know that, at 230k STP, this comp was taking out Earth Wind Hybrids that were around 311k STP.”*

This guide breaks down Meteorain and how VictorSeven is using game mechanics to turn the tables on earth-wind-hybrids in season 2 where players do not easily have access to the tools we usually rely upon to counter hybrids. Through its sustain loop, he flips enemy strengths into liabilities, and why it remains effective even with modest gear, artifacts, and specialization levels.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-156-1024x620.png)

This build is the work of **VictorSeven**, and it reflects a level of testing and mechanical understanding that only comes from spending countless hours in real fights. Meteorain wasn’t discovered by accident—it was refined through repeated theorycrafting, iteration, and careful observation of how hybrid comps actually function in practice.

I’m personally very grateful to VictorSeven for taking the time to discuss the build in depth, explain his reasoning, and share both the strengths and limits of the setup. His willingness to openly share his thought process is what makes this guide possible, and it’s why Meteorain deserves recognition as a genuinely original contribution to the IK community.

---

## Design Goal: Beating Hybrid Before Weakening Curse

The entire foundation of Meteorain revolves around a single constraint: **most players fighting Earth/Wind Hybrid do not have access to Weakening Curse**.

That matters because Weakening Curse is the cleanest, most direct answer to hybrid comps. It cripples their normal attack damage and removes the core of their scaling. Unfortunately, it’s gated behind both spending and Castle level.

VictorSeven summarizes the problem succinctly:

> *“How does this comp counter Earth Wind Hybrid? Well, you may have seen Myrahk's article on hard countering Earth Wind Hybrid. It's simple. You just need Weakening Curse. Boom. Hybrid gutted.
> Except Weakening Curse is a paid skill.
> And you have to be Castle level 50 to fuggin use it.
> And let's face it... if you're reading this article because you hate Earth Wind Hybrid as much as I do, you're probably nowhere near Castle level 50.”*

Meteorain solves this by **reproducing the *effect* of Weakening Curse** rather than the skill itself. It does so by stacking percentage-based damage reduction, he then further adds conditional healing, and healing amplification achieving a counter stronger than WC itself turning the tables on hybrids by making normal attacks no longer function as damage sources at all. In fact, they become triggers for sustain.

---

## The Meteorain Lineup (Baseline)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-151.png)

### Immortals

- **Yi Sun-Shin**: Best mitigation and heal amp around
- **Manco:** High damage after ramping
- **Himiko**: High damage and effective control
- **Cao Cao**: Sustain scaling off of amount of damage instances taken

### Dragon

- **Lightning Dragon**, specifically needed for *Lightning Cage*

This composition is intentionally compact. Every immortal serves a mechanical purpose, and none are included simply for raw STP. When piloted correctly, Meteorain routinely defeats higher-power hybrid teams because its defensive engine scales *against* the opponent’s aggression.

---

## Versatility Beyond PvP

While Meteorain is designed first and foremost as a PvP counter, it is not locked to that role. It is worth mentioning here, that it performs perfectly well against PvE content like gnomes, Well of Time and even bosses with slight modifications. For PvP outside of fighting Hybrids, it performs excellent too, having good mitigation and very good damage and control, it is a surprisingly versatile build despite being crafted as a project to hard-counter one build.

> *“Meteorain is a fairly complete PvP setup that also does well against gnomes, Well of Time, and bosses if you swap Hippolyta in. Even better if you swap Hippolyta and Cyrus in. With Resist, it also handles those Water Crit comps [and other mage based builds] where Merlin nukes your entire team before you get your first ult. ”*

This flexibility matters because it allows players to consolidate investment. You are not building a niche counter that only works in one matchup—you are building a defensive framework that adapts through skill and immortal swaps.

---

## The True Core: Lightning Dragon and Lightning Cage

If Meteorain has a single non-negotiable priority, it is **Lightning Dragon’s second skill: Lightning Cage**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-152.png)

This ability applies a **70% normal attack damage reduction** to three random enemy units for 12 seconds. Against Earth/Wind Hybrid, this is catastrophic.

> *“Level this puppy up ASAP. It has a percentage chance to decrease the normal attack damage of 3 random enemy units by 70%. What do Alex and Barca rely on? NORMAL ATTACKS. If this hits them both, their damage is GUTTED for 12 seconds. As you can see, mine’s not even maxed. Nothing in this comp is maxed yet. My current iteration is only at 285k STP.”* *- VictorSeven*

Lightning Cage is the first layer of the Weakening Curse simulation. It does not need to hit the entire enemy team - just the primary normal-attack carriers. Once their output is reduced, every other mechanic in Meteorain begins compounding the effect.

---

## Sustain Engine: Cao Cao and Yi Sun-Shin

Meteorain does not merely reduce damage; it **converts damage into healing**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-154.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-153.png)

Cao Cao’s *Hearts United* is the backbone of this process, providing:

- Flat damage mitigation reducing enemy damage dealt by a blanket 20%
- Healing when the frontrow is struck by normal attacks

Yi Sun-Shin amplifies this loop through:

- Additional damage mitigation of 30%
- Healing amplification (30%) once artifacted

Neither immortal requires high artifact investment to function. Even base artifacts activate their core interactions, allowing the comp to come online far earlier than most late-game defensive builds. Hearts United and Shelter both do the same thing, but since they're separate abilities, they BOTH trigger, and BOTH benefit from YSS ult and Spring of Life (later on).

---

## Skill Setup and Layered Mitigation

Once skills are assigned, the system becomes clear.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-155.png)

- **Cao Cao**  - **Absolute Defense** to keep Cao Cao alive through mage crit ultimates, or **Assist** to keep Himiko’s troop count high.
- **Shelter** for the complete inversion of the enemy’s damage.
- **Resist** to protect Manco while he’s channeling and to counter Water crit burst from Merlin or Wu’s first ultimate.
*(Against purely physical setups, this can be swapped out for something like **Rage Blessing** to speed up ramp-up.)*
- **Himiko**  - **Annihilation**
- **Concentration**
- **Fighting Master** so she can’t be CC’d (crowd-controlled).
- **Manco Capac**  - **Anger** for a damage boost.
- **Duel Master** for additional damage and immunity to Wound (because Qin and Khan can go to hell), ensuring Manco can never be stopped from healing.
- The third slot can run **Energy Suppression** versus ultimate-based setups, or **Berserk** for more attack speed and even more healing.
- **Yi Sun-Shin**  - **Defense Blessing**, which protects Manco while he’s channeling his ultimate and guards the entire team against the first round of enemy ultimates.
- **Sacrifice** — if this lands on both Himiko and Manco, the damage amp is significant.
*(This skill needs to be higher level; Victor reborned it for soul crystals when transitioning into new paid Wisdom Well skills after recording the video below)*
- **Oaken Guard**, which protects Manco during channeling and guards against Hippolyta ultimate spam if she’s built for damage.

Let’s break this down: **Defense Blessing**, **Oaken Guard**, and **Resist** are all mitigating damage alongside **Lightning Cage**, **Hearts United** (Cao Cao), and **Guard of Devotion** (Yi Sun-Shin). Stacking all of this together with **Shelter**, which heals you when you take a normal attack, and **Hearts United**, which heals you when you take damage—combined with Yi Sun-Shin’s healing amplification—means that if **Lightning Cage** lands on Alex and he’s doing the insane attack-speed routine he’s known for, he will **heal Manco or Yi Sun-Shin every time he connects**, because his damage is so low and the healing amplification is so high.

This is the moment Meteorain fully reveals itself. **Alex’s greatest strength - attack speed - becomes a liability**. Each hit triggers healing faster than he can deal damage. Against cleave commonly used as a ToK skill on hybrids (and active by default from Qin's ultimate on Hannibal), the effect is even more pronounced.

> *“And if they go Cleave? BAHAHAHAHAHA
> Don’t believe me? Look at myyyyyy resume. This is Meteorain at 230k STP cleaning up Earth Wind Hybrid at 311k STP BEFORE the immortals hitting level 50. Barely any Specializations. Crap artifacts. Gear at level 40 at best. This was a couple weeks ago. Just… just watch Manco’s health. Just watch it. I can’t stop laughing. Alex is HEALING MANCO. And now you see why I call it Meteorain.
> Do you believe yet? ‘Cause you’re gonna.”*

[Embedded media](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/13.12.2025_06.25.36_REC.mp4)

This is why the build works. It does not out-burst hybrid - it **invalidates** it and then it rains down meteors of doom once it has had its time to ramp up.

---

## Specializations

Specializations reinforce Meteorain’s defensive philosophy rather than redefining it. Even low levels provide meaningful returns, particularly on:

- Cao Cao (Battle Excitation)
- Himiko (Stormeye Spell)
- Yi Sun-Shin (Fearless Stance or Sturdy Barrier)
- Manco Capac (Destroyer Stance)

---

## Scaling Meteorain into a Mid-Spend, Late–Season Build

Once the low-spend foundation of Meteorain is in place, the next step is not a redesign but a **measured escalation**. The core idea remains unchanged—layered mitigation, sustain conversion, and normal-attack denial—but additional investment allows the comp to scale more cleanly into late Season 2 and eventually Conquest. As VictorSeven puts it:

> *“This changes the comp from low spend to mid spend, here’s how you absolutely ruin people with this comp… Just because you can’t HEAR the evil laughter doesn’t mean I’m not doing it. I am absolutely cackling right now.”*

This version of Meteorain cleared **Elite Well of Time up to 13-1 at 285k STP**, and more importantly, it begins to resemble a true Conquest-ready framework rather than a midgame counterpick. The shift to mid-spend largely revolves around selective Wisdom Well skills that enhance ramp speed, healing scaling, and damage efficiency—while still respecting the original defensive engine.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-159.png)

On **Cao Cao**, the first slot remains flexible. Absolute Defense and Assist both remain valid depending on matchup and comfort, while **Rage Blessing** becomes the go-to adjustment when facing Energy Suppression. The goal here is not to reinvent Cao Cao’s role, but to ensure the team reaches its first ultimate cycle reliably under pressure.

**Himiko** benefits the most offensively from mid-spend investment. Replacing Concentration with **Spell Disintegrator** dramatically increases the lethality of both her ultimate and Annihilation. At this stage of progression, fights are no longer decided solely by survival - Himiko begins to actively punish teams that fail to break through Meteorain’s sustain loop.

For **Manco Capac**, one upgrade is non-negotiable: **Demonic Contract**. This skill aligns perfectly with his natural ramp. Manco spends the opening seconds gaining energy and channeling; by the time his first major hit lands, the initial damage penalty from Demonic Contract has already expired, and his damage is accelerating rapidly. From that point forward, the only requirement is keeping him alive - something Meteorain is already designed to do exceptionally well. Add to that a Victorious Pursuit (in later conquest we can even do Blade Dodge) and we are really stacking damage amps for his constant meteorain.

**Yi Sun-Shin** sees the most transformative upgrade, but also the most restrictive one. Swapping Sacrifice for **Spring of Life** requires Castle level 46, making it the hardest change to implement, but one you should get done before Conquest if possible or as you enter conquest as a priority (available in wish shop for cheap/free in conquest). The payoff, however, is enormous. Every instance of healing now grants additional damage resistance. With Shelter triggering on normal attacks and Hearts United healing on damage taken, the team begins stacking resist continuously. At this point, Meteorain doesn’t just stabilize, it compounds.

For players willing to push even further, **Guard** can replace Oaken Guard, providing more frequent protection for Manco. This comes with risk, as the rest of the team becomes more exposed to early Alex and Barca cleave damage, but in controlled matchups it can further optimize Manco’s uptime.

Taken together, these upgrades do not change what Meteorain *is* - they simply allow it to scale harder, stabilize faster, and punish mistakes more decisively. What starts as a clever pre–Castle 50 hybrid counter gradually evolves into a legitimate Conquest-capable build, retaining its identity while expanding its ceiling. I look forward to talking to VictorSeven in the future and keeping tabs on how this build performs as he goes through Conquest season next.

---

## Known Weaknesses and Practical Limits

Meteorain is not a universal answer.

- Early silence effects (No Escape) are going to be dangerous (short of having Fountain of Life)
- Heavy Energy Suppression can delay critical ultimates
- Shield-heavy enemies require Shatter adaptation, on that note, VictorSeven reports succes using Shatter on Cao Cao to break key shielding. Quite interesting in itself and something that needs exploring in its own guide.
- Extreme spender setups (Alex + Chaos) remain oppressive

These limitations do not invalidate the build; they define its intended operating window. Meteorain is a **mid-level execution comp**, designed to dominate the space between early hybrid abuse and late-game Castle 50 skill access. That being said, I can see it scale well into conquest. Time will tell!

---

title: Part 2 - Farming low-level alts easily and efficiently
summary: Farming resources for your main is crucially important for any player in Infinity Kingdom. However, not everyone has the time to spend a few hours every day sending army after army to kill dead castles with all our many…
markdown:
Farming resources for your main is crucially important for any player in Infinity Kingdom. However, not everyone has the time to spend a few hours every day sending army after army to kill dead castles with all our many alts. Instead, what you can choose to set up passive-alts.

If you do not have the time to spend AP on alts attacking castles all over Norheim, then you may want to simply create a farmvile group of alts where you only do the bare minimum and still achieve quite solid resource income (almost) without moving a finger.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/image-84.png)

## Method 2

We left off with how to grow your alts into powerful production capacities each producing millions of resources for your main every day. However I also want to share with you another concept for how to build resource farms with barely any effort.

This is particularly attractive for players with access to solid computing hardware. Since the more instances you are able to run at the same time the more efficient this method is. While method 1 is far superior for players who can only play a few instances at a time, this method 2 is extreemly efficient if you are able to boot say 10-20 instances at a time.

This is because you need to make A TON of castles at the same time and get them to level 6 where you can join an alliance. Once you joined an alliance you gain access to the passive tax-income from the cities held by the alliance. You login once per day and collect, that's it. If you can boot 10 instances at a time without your computer melting down, you can do this in a couple minutes and have earned millions of resources on every single alt.

## Resources per day

I will not assume that you have a max level alt alliance with a full set of cities at your disposal. I think it is rare for any one player to be able to take up 20, 30 maybe even 40 spots in a max level alliance with cities (unless of course your are in a not very active server).

However, let us say you are in a decent level alliance with maybe 10-11 cities (a standard alt / academy alliance in most servers). You will be collecting taxing resources at a rate of around 400k / hour (combined). **That nets each of your alts 9.6 million resources per day**, a not insignificant amount of resources earned by spending literally 10 seconds clicking "Claim" once a day.

Using this method you do not have to send out marches to nodes, you don't need to find dead castles to kill, you do not need to upgrade any buildings or technology. No. All you need to do is make it to level 6 and join the alliance.

## Every day at the same time you simply

### (1) boot up all your instances with auto-login

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/image-89.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/image-88.png)

### (2) Collect alliance Territorial taxes

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/image-90-1024x104.png)

### (3) Use the same instances to swap between all three low level alts on the account

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/image-91-1024x210.png)

### (2) Collect more alliance taxes

**DONE**! Congratulations, if you can run even 5 instances at a time, you just earned a 150 million resources!

**If you are a true monster and run a 35 instance rotation, you earn a massive 1 billion resource per day.**

*Note that it is important you login every day at the same time, since alliance territory taxes accumulate for 24 hours and then stop.*

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/image-87.png)

title: Midsummer Festival 2025
summary: Infinity Kingdom’s annual summer celebration is back—and this time, it’s bringing waves of power, Poseidon-themed aesthetics, and serious value for both collectors and competitive players. Launching right after the July…
markdown:
## ☀️ Midsummer Festival 2025 – What You Need to Know

Infinity Kingdom’s annual summer celebration is back—and this time, it’s bringing waves of power, Poseidon-themed aesthetics, and serious value for both collectors and competitive players. Launching right after the July patch, the **Midsummer Festival 2025** builds upon the formula from past seasonal events like Spring Fiesta and Children’s Day, but adds a few key improvements that make it well worth your attention.

Whether you're chasing Chaos Immortal fragments, looking to snipe jackpots from the Treasure Hunter wheel, or simply want one of the best-looking castle skins ever added to the game, this event has something for you. In this guide, we’ll walk through all the components of the event, explain what’s new, what’s valuable, and how to make the most of your time during this 10-day festival.

### Midsummer Festival 2025 – Your Complete Guide to the Seasonal Event

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-23-1024x576.png)

---

## ☀️ A Sunny Season with Familiar Shadows

Running from **July 11 to July 20**, the **Midsummer Festival 2025** marks the return of Infinity Kingdom's full-format seasonal celebration. Following in the footsteps of recent events like Spring Fiesta and Children’s Day, this festival keeps the same structure while offering new cosmetics, rewards, and chaos progression opportunities.

This event looks bright and breezy on the surface—open fields, summery themes—but underneath, it’s a strategic event with meaningful long-term implications. With PvE trials, premium reward tiers, chaos immortal fragments, and an **upgradeable castle skin**, this is a high-stakes, high-value event worth digging into.

---

## 📝 Sign-In Rewards – Simple, Solid, Worth the Tap

Each day you log in, you get **2 Resonance Crystals**. Over the event's duration, that’s a guaranteed **20 free Crystals**. No strings attached, no tasks to complete. Just log in, tap, and bank progress.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-24-1024x544.png)

---

## 🏰 Celebration Pass – New Skin, Familiar Strategy

The Celebration Pass follows the same 30-level structure as before. You complete up to 7 daily missions to earn **EXP**. You’ll need **7,000 EXP** in total to finish the pass, which is easily achievable in 6–7 days.

### Free Track:

- 60 Resonance Crystals

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-25-1024x429.png)

### Premium Track ($49.99):

- 145 Resonance Crystals
- 6,000 Gems
- 60 Random Holy/Shadow Immortal Fragments
- **New Skin: Abyssal Temple** (Upgradeable Castle Skin)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-26-1024x434.png)

#### Abyssal Temple Skin:

- Base effect: **+5% Troop ATK**, **-3% Death Rate**
- Max upgrade (Level 10): **+15% ATK**, **-6% Death Rate**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-27-1024x436.png)

This skin is a Poseidon-themed upgradeable castle skin—expected to replace or surpass the previous **Children’s Day skin** with better combat stats and an oceanic visual overhaul.

> 🧠 If you’re missing an upgradable castle skin or a +Troop ATK bonus, this one is a must. Compared to the **Skyriver Palace** (which increases Physical and Magical ATK), the universal **Troop ATK** on Abyssal Temple is more versatile and impactful across all compositions.

---

## ⚔️ Glorious Challenge – Smart Timing, Solid Coins

This PvE challenge gives you **5 tickets daily**. The rewards are **Radiance Marks**, the primary event currency.

- **Normal Mode** is available from Day 1
- **Hard Mode** unlocks on Day 3 i.e. the 14th of july 2025.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-28-1024x510.png)

> 🧠 Don’t spend gems on tickets until Hard Mode unlocks. Maximize your returns.

---

## 🧱 Pinnacle Trial – One Daily Try, Always Worth It

Each day, you get **one free challenge attempt**. Win and you unlock:

- 18 Resonance Crystals
- Holy/Shadow Immortal Fragments
- Random Immortal Fragments
- A PvE node to farm for 24h

No entry cost. No risk.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-30-1024x489.png)

> 🧠 Free value with scaling rewards. Try every day. The top PvE setups benefit most, but everyone wins.

---

## 💎 Treasure Hunter – Ares, Skins, and the Spending Dilemma

This gacha-style Crystal draw event lets you:

- Spend Crystals to open chests
- Compete in daily leaderboards
- Snipe rewards like Immortal fragments and skin shards

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-31-1024x546.png)

### Major Rewards:

- **Ares Chaos Immortal** Fragments
- **Abyssal Temple Skin Fragments**
- **Epic Immortal Selection Chests**

Pools refresh every 2 hours unless a top-tier reward is drawn.

### Leaderboard Rewards:

- 1st: 60 Abyssal Temple Fragments
- 2nd: 36 Fragments
- 3rd: 24 Fragments
- 4th–10th: 12 Fragments each

This system mirrors past events but adds wider access to skin shards. Still, the cost of maxing the skin remains extremely high—requiring top-3 placements multiple days in a row.

> 🧠 Casual players should avoid this unless sniping a low day late in the event. This feature remains whale territory.

---

## 🛒 Celebration Store – Pick Power Over Shine

Your Radiance Marks are best spent on power. Prioritize:

- **500 Stardust**
- **Artifact Selection Chests (x3)**
- **90 Resonance Crystals**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-32-1024x401.png)

### Optional:

- Cosmetic items
- Crystal bundles (unless focused on Chaos)

> 🧠 Same strategy as always—Stardust and Artifacts have long-term value. Avoid cosmetics unless you're already maxed out elsewhere.

---

## 💰 Bundles & Spending – Small Buys, Big Wins

- $2.99 / $4.99: Excellent value
- $9.99–$19.99: Diminishing returns
- $49.99: Worth it only for skin collectors or high-end players

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/image-33-1024x414.png)

> 🧠 if you're spending, go for the Pass and 1–2 cheap bundles. Skip mid-tier packs unless you’re all-in.

---

## 🧠 Final Take – Seasonal Event, Strategic Impact

The **Midsummer Festival 2025** sticks to the proven formula but continues layering premium power behind upgradable cosmetics and Chaos progression. It’s effective, rewarding, and increasingly demanding.

### 🟢 Free-to-Play:

- Log in daily
- Clear PvE modes
- Max the pass
- Spend Marks on Stardust and Artifacts

### 🟡 Light Spenders:

- Buy the Celebration Pass
- Add a $3–$5 bundle
- Save Crystals, try Treasure Hunter on a quiet day

### 🔴 Whales:

- Everything’s here: Chaos, Cosmetics, Castle Skins
- Compete for Ares, max the Abyssal Temple, dominate the rankings

This event is generous, strategic, and polished—but also reminds us how steep the curve is getting for full progression. For most players, the best gains come from planning, not spending.

title: Midsummer Festival 2026 (july)
summary: The 2026 Midsummer Festival follows the familiar structure used by recent Infinity Kingdom seasonal events. Players complete challenges, collect Tokens of Light, exchange event currencies, progress through a battle…
markdown:
## Introduction

The 2026 Midsummer Festival follows the familiar structure used by recent Infinity Kingdom seasonal events. Players complete challenges, collect Tokens of Light, exchange event currencies, progress through a battle pass, and spend Eternal Grails in the seasonal shop.

The underlying structure has not changed dramatically. What has changed is the purpose of several major reward tracks.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-45-1024x461.png)

Previous festivals primarily converted participation into broad account resources such as Eternal Grails, Philosopher’s Stones, Soul Crystals, speedups, and castle skins. The Midsummer Festival redirects much of that value toward the new Immortal Outfit system. Athena replaces the traditional Dazzling Wish jackpot, while Alexander fragments is available in addition to the large resource rewards previously found in similar event tabs, e.g. Candy Defenders.

As a result, the event is much more account-specific than earlier festivals. Players using Alexander or Athena may see considerable value. Players using neither immortal lose some of the flexibility that made earlier seasonal events broadly rewarding.

The event accompanies Version 2.9.7, which officially introduced Immortal Outfits and new time-limited activities.

---

## Event Structure

The main festival tabs are:

- Koi Gift Pack
- Summer Passion Battle Pass
- Fishing Contest
- Dazzling Wish
- Challenge Shop
- Grail Shop
- Glorious Challenge
- Pinnacle Trial

Most of these are returning seasonal systems with adjusted rewards. The Fishing Contest is the main themed activity introduced for Midsummer.

---

## Koi Gift Pack

## Structure

The Koi Gift Pack retains the usual low-cost seasonal bundle structure.

The first bundle costs approximately $5 and contains:

- Lucky Koi participation
- Tokens of Light
- Magic Fishing Nets
- Access toward the recurring Koi consolation and grand-prize system

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-47-1024x461.png)

After purchasing the initial bundle, players can unlock an additional bundle costing $10. This provides more Tokens of Light and Magic Fishing Nets.

## What Changed

Previous festivals generally limited players to the standard daily Koi purchase. Midsummer allows additional bundle purchases.

Mechanically, this does not improve the original bundle. It simply increases the amount of event currency available for purchase.

The important point is that buying the additional bundle is not required to qualify for the normal Koi reward structure. Purchasing the regular $5 bundle on the five required days still provides the usual consolation-prize progression and the top grail efficiency purchase available anywhere.

## Player Perspective

For most players, very little has changed.

The initial bundle remains one of the more efficient seasonal purchases for players who already buy it. The extra bundles mainly provide additional stock for heavy spenders who intend to clear the Fishing Contest, make large numbers of Dazzling Wish pulls, or empty substantial portions of the Grail Shop.

Light and medium spenders should not interpret the additional bundles as mandatory event progression. They are simply another way to buy more currency.

---

## Summer Passion Battle Pass

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-46-1024x461.png)

## Structure

The seasonal battle pass returns with the usual combination of free and paid rewards.

Expected contents include:

- Tokens of Light
- Magic Fishing Nets
- Gems
- Event resources
- Alexander Outfit Fragments

The paid track awards 60 Alexander Outfit Fragments at Level 30.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-59-1024x629.png)

## What Changed

Previous festival passes usually awarded a castle skin or an evolution copy of an existing castle skin.

Midsummer replaces that castle reward with a complete first-stage Alexander outfit unlock.

This is one of the most meaningful changes in the event.

## Player Perspective

For an account using Alexander, the paid pass offers unusually strong value. Players who would normally buy the seasonal pass receive the regular Tokens, Gems, and event resources while also obtaining enough fragments to unlock the outfit directly.

That is considerably more useful than receiving an unwanted castle skin or a minor evolution increase on a skin that rarely sees use.

For players who do not use Alexander, the pass remains a normal event bundle with good currency value, but its headline reward is much less important.

For free-to-play players, the change is less favourable. A castle skin could provide account-wide attributes or collection progress regardless of march composition. Alexander fragments have little immediate value unless the player is actively building him.

---

## Fishing Contest

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-48-1024x461.png)

## Overview

Fishing Contest is the main Midsummer activity.

Mechanically, it resembles Candy Defenders and similar paired seasonal systems. The presentation has changed from attacking candy creatures or seasonal bosses to catching fish, but the underlying progression loop remains familiar.

Players spend Magic Fishing Nets to participate and may pair with another player. Pairing must be renewed daily, so players should verify that they have an active partner before committing large amounts of currency. That being said, partnering up is not as important as in past events. While getting the Token rewards from the 15 daily levels is great, the main reward here is the personal "Smiley-sharks" cought progression found under My Catch - this awards Alexanders outfit fragments and is the real prize here.

The activity contains two separate reward tracks:

1. Daily fishing-level progression
2. Cumulative My Catch milestones

Understanding the difference between them is important.

---

## Fishing-Level Progression

The daily portion contains 15 levels.

Players spend Magic Fishing Nets to progress through the levels, with rewards improving as they advance. The activity appears to reset daily, including its Token of Light rewards, while cumulative catch progression remains for the duration of the event.

Reaching Level 15 awards only a small number of Alexander Outfit Fragments—reported as three fragments per complete clear.

Clearing all 15 levels each day may still provide Tokens of Light and other useful rewards, but the final level itself is not the main source of Alexander fragments.

---

## My Catch

The real outfit progression sits under **My Catch**.

Fishing produces different catches, including Smiley Sharks. Catching large quantities of the required fish advances cumulative milestones containing substantially more Alexander Outfit Fragments.

This is the equivalent of the deeper reward track seen in previous Candy Defenders iterations. Rather than receiving most of the value from individual attacks, players gradually progress through a larger event-wide milestone ladder.

The difficulty is volume. Players need a very large number of Smiley Sharks, and the outcome is partly affected by fishing results rather than only by a fixed currency threshold.

## What Changed from Candy Defenders

Previous versions of this event type rewarded large quantities of broadly useful resources, including:

- Philosopher’s Stones
- Soul Crystals
- Speedups
- Resource boxes
- General development materials

Midsummer shifts the premium milestones toward Alexander Outfit Fragments.

This makes the reward track narrower but potentially more valuable for the correct account.

A player relying on Alexander may prefer permanent outfit progression over another pile of expendable resources. A player who does not use Alexander will generally find the fishing rewards less compelling than the old Philosopher’s Stone and Soul Crystal packages.

---

## Fishing Strategy

Players should not judge the activity only by the three fragments shown at Level 15.

The main questions are:

- How many Smiley Sharks are obtained per amount of Fishing Nets?
- How far can the account progress through My Catch?
- How many fragments are available at reachable milestones?
- Does the player intend to use Alexander long-term?

For mid-spenders running Alexander, concentrated investment can make sense because the outfit is a permanent combat upgrade. The seasonal pass also supplies the first 60 fragments, allowing fishing progress to build on an outfit that is already unlocked.

For free-to-play players, converting large quantities of Eternal Grails into Fishing Nets is much harder to justify. Grails remain one of the primary routes toward Chaos Immortals and artifacts, while Fishing Nets provide uncertain progress toward one specific immortal.

Until the complete catch rates and milestone requirements are documented, players should avoid assuming that a partial fishing push will reach a meaningful Alexander threshold.

---

## Dazzling Wish

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-49-1024x461.png)

## Structure

Dazzling Wish still consumes Tokens of Light.

Players make individual draws and receive smaller Eternal Grail rewards, while a pity counter guarantees the featured final reward after enough attempts.

However, both the jackpot and pity structure have changed.

---

## Removal of the 300-Grail Jackpot

Previous seasonal events included a chance to obtain a 300 Eternal Grail jackpot from an individual draw.

That jackpot is no longer part of the standard Midsummer reward table.

The final pity reward has also changed from general Grail value to Athena Outfit Fragments.

This sharply reduces the flexibility of Tokens of Light. Previously, almost every account benefited from converting Tokens into Grails because Grails could be spent on multiple Chaos Immortals, artifacts, and seasonal resources. Athena fragments only benefit players investing in Athena.

---

## New Pity Requirement

The pity threshold has reportedly increased from 300 to 700 draws.

At 700 pulls, players receive 20 Athena Outfit Fragments.

This is a much heavier commitment than previous Dazzling Wish systems. Players should not begin chasing the pity reward unless they understand how many Tokens they can obtain and whether unfinished progress carries into a future event.

---

## Mystery Bonus

Dazzling Wish also includes a new mystery or special reward.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-50.png)

Reported options include:

- A refund of one Token of Light
- A reward of two Tokens of Light
- A Cleopatra crying emoji
- Access to a discounted Token of Light bundle that still requires payment

In practical terms, the mystery reward is extremely weak.

A special draw should normally provide additional progression value. Here, several outcomes either return a negligible amount of currency, award a cosmetic emoji, or merely unlock another purchase opportunity.

The Cleopatra crying emoji is unintentionally appropriate, because it accurately reflects the value of receiving the “special” reward.

---

## Player Perspective

For Athena users, Dazzling Wish now has a clear long-term purpose. The outfit fragments are scarce, and the outfit itself provides meaningful progression.

For everyone else, Dazzling Wish has become substantially worse.

The removal of the 300-Grail jackpot reduces average excitement and broad account value. The increased pity threshold requires far more stored currency, and the featured reward is tied to one immortal.

Players who do not use Athena should strongly consider preserving Tokens of Light for a later seasonal event. Future versions may feature a different immortal, introduce selectable outfit fragments, or restore a more flexible Grail-based reward structure.

Tokens of Light should no longer be spent automatically simply because Dazzling Wish is available.

---

## Challenge Shop

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-53-1024x461.png)

## Structure

The Challenge Shop follows the established seasonal format.

Players use currency earned from Glorious Challenge to purchase daily and limited-stock rewards.

Important purchases usually include:

- Tokens of Light
- Stardust
- Progression resources
- Event-specific materials

## Strategy

Tokens of Light and Stardust remain the safest general purchases for most accounts.

Beware the shop is on daily stock meaning you need to make sure you buy the items you most need, e.g. Tokens or Stardust or Artifacts each day and make sure you have enough currency to do so. Early days it is worth it buying additional gem-hits on Glorious Challenge to take full advantage of the daily stock resets.

Hard Mode becomes available later in the event and improves the amount of currency that can be earned.

---

## Grail Shop

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-55-1024x441.png)

## Structure

The Grail Shop remains the primary destination for Eternal Grails.

Its established rewards include:

- Chaos Immortal fragments
- Chaos Immortal artifact fragments
- Triss or Token Skill-related progression
- Seasonal materials
- Magic Fishing Nets

The exact Immortal selection depends on server progression and seasonal availability.

## New Fishing Net Exchange

The relevant Midsummer addition is the ability to exchange Eternal Grails for Magic Fishing Nets.

A reported exchange offers:

- 5,000 Magic Fishing Nets
- Cost: 200 Eternal Grails

This connects the traditional Grail economy directly to Fishing Contest progression.

## Opportunity Cost

The exchange is not automatically good or bad. Its value depends on the account.

Buying Fishing Nets means giving up progress toward:

- Chaos Immortal fragments
- Chaos artifacts
- Future discounted Chaos chests
- Other limited Grail Shop rewards

For a committed Alexander player who is close to an important My Catch milestone, purchasing Nets may be reasonable. For a developing account still missing important Chaos Immortals, spending hundreds of Grails on uncertain fishing outcomes is much harder to defend.

The correct comparison is not “Are more Fishing Nets useful?” They obviously are. The correct comparison is whether the expected Alexander fragments are more valuable than the Chaos progression sacrificed to obtain them.

---

## Glorious Challenge

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-51-1024x461.png)

## Structure

Glorious Challenge remains one of the main sources of seasonal shop currency.

The usual progression pattern is expected:

- Complete rotating objectives
- Earn event currency
- Unlock later difficulty stages
- Spend currency in the Challenge Shop

Hard Mode traditionally becomes available around Day 4 and is the main breakpoint for efficient progression.

## Strategy

During the early days:

- Complete objectives normally
- Buy important daily stock
- Avoid unnecessary spending merely to force low-value tasks
- Preserve resources for Hard Mode requirements

Once Hard Mode opens, players can commit more heavily because later objectives generally provide better event progression.

Unlike the Original Festival and Children’s Day versions, Glorious Challenge is no longer primarily feeding a huge Candy resource engine. Its importance remains substantial, but the broader event value is now more concentrated in Fishing Nets, Tokens of Light, and outfit progression.

---

## Pinnacle Trial

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-52-1024x461.png)

## Structure

Pinnacle Trial returns as the festival’s staged combat challenge.

Rewards generally include:

- Immortal fragments
- Tokens of Light
- Event resources
- Additional seasonal progression materials

Difficulty increases through successive stages, making march depth and formation quality increasingly important.

## Player Perspective

Pinnacle Trial remains worth pushing as far as the account can manage without wasting large quantities of premium resources.

Tokens of Light are particularly important during Midsummer because they are more difficult to value correctly. Athena players may want every available Token, while non-Athena players can stockpile them for future events.

Even players skipping Dazzling Wish should complete Pinnacle Trial. Saving the Tokens does not make them less valuable.

---

## Main Changes from Previous Festivals

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-56-1024x680.png)

## Dazzling Wish

Previous events:

- Included a 300-Grail jackpot
- Converted Tokens of Light into broadly useful Grail progression
- Used a much lower 300-draw pity structure

Midsummer:

- Removes the 300-Grail jackpot
- Features Athena Outfit Fragments
- Raises pity to 700 draws
- Adds a poor-value mystery reward

This is the largest negative change for general account progression.

---

## Seasonal Side Activity

Previous events:

- Used Candy Defenders or similar themes
- Awarded large quantities of Stones, Soul Crystals, speedups, and resources

Midsummer:

- Uses Fishing Contest
- Requires Magic Fishing Nets
- Focuses cumulative milestones on Smiley Sharks
- Awards Alexander Outfit Fragments as the premium reward

This is a major improvement for Alexander accounts but a reduction in universal resource value.

---

## Battle Pass

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-57-1024x532.png)

Previous events:

- Awarded a castle skin or skin evolution copy

Midsummer:

- Awards 60 Alexander Outfit Fragments
- Provides a complete initial outfit unlock

For players using Alexander, this is arguably the strongest improvement in the event.

---

## Koi Gift Pack

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-58-1024x561.png)

Previous events:

- Offered the standard limited Koi bundle

Midsummer:

- Retains the original bundle
- Unlocks additional bundles after purchase
- Provides more Tokens and Fishing Nets for players willing to spend further

For ordinary spenders, the practical value is unchanged. Whales simply have more stock available.

---

## Spending Perspectives

## Free-to-Play

The event is less generous in broadly usable progression materials than earlier festivals.

Best priorities:

- Complete Glorious Challenge
- Push Pinnacle Trial
- Collect free Tokens of Light
- Buy important daily Challenge Shop stock
- Participate in Fishing Contest with free Nets
- Avoid chasing Athena pity without a realistic Token reserve
- Be cautious about exchanging Grails for Fishing Nets

Free-to-play Alexander users can collect fragments gradually, but should not sacrifice core Chaos progression without knowing that a meaningful outfit milestone is reachable.

---

## Light Spenders

The regular Koi Gift Pack remains efficient if it was already part of the player’s seasonal spending.

The paid battle pass becomes highly attractive for Alexander users because the 60-fragment reward provides an immediate unlock.

Additional Koi bundles are optional. They should not be treated as necessary simply because they are available.

---

## Mid-Spenders

Mid-spenders running Alexander are the clearest winners.

The battle pass gives the first outfit level, while Fishing Contest offers a path toward further development. Spending on Nets can be worthwhile when it secures a known My Catch fragment milestone.

Athena users should calculate Dazzling Wish carefully. A 700-draw pity is too large to approach casually, even for a moderate spender.

---

## Heavy Spenders

Heavy spenders can purchase the additional Koi stock, clear daily fishing progression, push My Catch deeply, and pursue Athena fragments through Dazzling Wish.

For these accounts, Midsummer offers a large amount of permanent combat progression.

However, the event does not necessarily provide better general value than previous festivals. It simply provides more purchasable stock and more character-specific progression.

---

## Player Perspective

The Midsummer Festival looks familiar when viewed from the main event screen, but its reward philosophy has changed considerably.

The Original Festival was memorable because Candy Defenders produced enormous piles of resources that helped almost every account. Children’s Day made the same system more expensive, but Stones, Soul Crystals, and speedups still had universal value.

Midsummer replaces much of that flexible progression with Alexander and Athena fragments.

For an Alexander player, the trade can be excellent. The battle pass alone provides a far more meaningful headline reward than many previous castle skins, and Fishing Contest gives mid-spenders a realistic reason to invest beyond the pass.

For an account using neither featured immortal, the event is notably weaker. Dazzling Wish has lost its 300-Grail jackpot, the new mystery reward is poor, and Fishing Contest no longer showers the account with the same quantity of universal development materials.

The event is therefore not simply better or worse than previous festivals. It is more specialized.

---

## Conclusion Summary

The 2026 Midsummer Festival retains the standard seasonal framework but redirects its most valuable rewards toward Immortal Outfits.

The key points are:

- Koi Gift Pack now offers additional purchasable stock, mainly benefiting heavy spenders.
- Summer Passion replaces the usual castle skin with 60 Alexander Outfit Fragments.
- Fishing Contest functions like Candy Defenders with a fishing theme.
- Smiley Shark milestones are the main source of Alexander fragments.
- The daily Level 15 fishing reward is much less important than My Catch progression.
- Dazzling Wish no longer contains the 300-Grail jackpot.
- Athena fragments replace the old flexible jackpot progression.
- The pity requirement has increased from 300 to 700.
- The new mystery bonus offers extremely poor value.
- Eternal Grails can be exchanged for Fishing Nets, creating a direct choice between Alexander and Chaos progression.
- Glorious Challenge, Pinnacle Trial, Challenge Shop, and the usual Token economy remain important.

For Alexander users, particularly mid-spenders, this can be one of the more valuable seasonal passes and side events released so far. For players without Alexander or Athena, the correct approach is more conservative: collect the general rewards, preserve flexible currencies, and avoid being pulled into expensive outfit tracks that do not support the account’s actual marches.

title: Milestones and Costs upgrading dragon talents (a season 2 guide)
summary: Season 2 is when dragons finally start to come alive. You unlock their Talent Trees, giving each dragon powerful upgrades that directly impact your marches. If you’re still in Season 1, this guide is worth bookmarking —…
markdown:
Season 2 is when dragons finally start to *come alive*. You unlock their **Talent Trees**, giving each dragon powerful upgrades that directly impact your marches. If you’re still in Season 1, this guide is worth bookmarking — because Season 2 progression can eat up crystals *fast*.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-118-1024x572.png)

The short version? **Start saving crystals now**. You’ll need a lot of them once dragon talents open up.

This guide covers:

- Dragon node types and upgrade costs
- Key milestones to hit in Season 2
- Smart pathing choices depending on your build
- How to avoid wasting crystals on low-value nodes

---

## Understanding Dragon Talent Trees

Each dragon’s talent tree is split into **two sides**, with **unique nodes**, **minor nodes**, and **major nodes**. You’ll have to work through the tree, unlocking and upgrading nodes as you go. Here’s what each one does and costs.

### 🔹 Minor Nodes

These are your bread and butter — small stat boosts like:

- Resilience
- Accuracy
- Physical Attack / Magical Attack
- Physical Defense / Magical Defense

Each **minor node** has **3 levels**, giving **+30 attribute points per level** (so 90 total when maxed).

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-119.png)

Costs per level:

- Level 1 → **150 crystals**
- Level 2 → **300 crystals**
- Level 3 → **450 crystals**

That’s **900 crystals total** to max one minor node.

---

### 🔸 Unique Nodes

Unique nodes are checkpoints in your tree — they’re the key to unlocking your dragon’s special abilities and next sections of the tree.

Each **unique node** costs:

- **30 Dragon Essences**
- **3000 crystals**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-120.png)

They’re expensive, but you can’t skip them if you want to progress or upgrade your dragon’s signature skills.

---

### 🔺 Major Nodes

These are the big hitters. Major nodes offer percentage-based boosts like:

- **Claw** → +% Damage Dealt
- **Armor** → -% Damage Taken
- **Accuracy** and **Resilience** (later in the tree)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/image-70.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/Skaermbillede-2022-08-18-161218.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/Skaermbillede-2022-08-18-161208.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/Skaermbillede-2022-08-18-161202.png)

Each major node has **5 levels**, scaling like this:

- 600 → 1200 → 1800 → 2400 → 3000 crystals
- That’s **9000 crystals** to max one major node.

---

## Key Milestones and Crystal Costs

Here’s the practical roadmap most players follow when building their dragon in Season 2. We’ll break it down step-by-step so you can plan your crystal budget ahead of time.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-121-1024x542.png)

---

### 🥇 Milestone 1: Unlocking Your First Major Node (Claw or Armor)

You’ll need to push through **7 minor nodes** and **1 unique node** before you can unlock your first major.

### Cost:

- 7 × 150 = 1050 - 3000 (unique)   - 600 (Claw unlock)
= **4650 crystals total**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-122-1024x642.png)

You’ll repeat this on the opposite side to unlock **Armor** for another 4650, bringing you to **9300 crystals total** to unlock both Claw and Armor.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-123-1024x499.png)

💡 *Tip:* If you’re using a magic-heavy march (like Fire with Wu or Himiko), you can skip Accuracy nodes — they don’t help you at all.

---

### 🥈 Milestone 2: Upgrading Claw & Armor to Level 3

Once unlocked, getting both Claw and Armor to level 3 gives a strong early boost for relatively low cost:

- Each: 600 + 1200 + 1800 = 3600
- Both: 7200 total
- But since the first 600 was already spent unlocking, you’re actually only spending **6000 more** to hit Level 3.

✅ **Result:** +2% damage and +2% damage reduction — a massive early jump in performance.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-124-1024x393.png)

---

### 🥉 Milestone 3: Unlocking Your Dragon’s Primary Unique Talent (Level 5)

After you’ve got Claw and Armor to a solid level, it’s time to push deeper into your dragon’s tree toward its **main unique ability**.

#### The Straight Path (Rushing to Level 5)

- 8 minor nodes × 150 = 1,200
- 3 unique nodes × 3,000 = 9,000
➡️ **10,200 crystals total**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-125-1024x465.png)

#### The Smarter Path (With Maxed Core Minors)

Along the way, pick up the best minor for you (magical attack for example) and **upgrade your best minor nodes to level 3**.
For example, I max **Magical Attack** and **Magical Defense** minors on my Fire Dragon.

Each of the 4 key minors adds:
4 × (300 + 450) = **3,000 extra crystals**

➡️ **13,200 crystals total**, but way more value gained.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-126-1024x601.png)

✅ **Result:**

- Level 5 main unique ability unlocked
- Core stat minors maxed out

---

### 🏅 Milestone 4 & 5: Your Path Splits Here

Now it depends on your dragon and your build:

1. **If both unique abilities are strong**
→ Do the same process on the other side and unlock the second unique talent to level 5.
(Expect another 10,200 - 13,200 crystals)
2. **If the second talent isn’t useful for your setup**
→ Skip it and instead max your Claw and Armor nodes to level 5.

**Cost to max Claw + Armor to 5:**
(2400 + 3000) × 2 = 10,800 crystals total.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-127-1024x581.png)

👉 Example:
For Fire Dragon, I skip **Flaming Breath** because it only reduces *physical* damage dealt by enemies, which is useless against mage teams. Instead, I max my Claw and Armor and invest in all **magical attack** and **magical defense** minors.

If you choose to do the unique first then finish armor and claw after, if you do armor and claw level 5 first, finish your unique after.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-128-1024x550.png)

Upgrade minors that are best for you along the way, then finish the tree with the last majors as the completionist you are and begin banking crystals for later when the rest of the tree is unlocked and you do it all over again!

title: Misleading
summary: \"Misleading\" is a Tower of Knowledge skill in Infinity Kingdom that offers significant defensive potential but requires careful consideration and strategic deployment to be effective. It's a skill that either defines a…
markdown:
### Player Guide: Harnessing the Power of "Misleading" in Infinity Kingdom

"Misleading" is a Tower of Knowledge skill in Infinity Kingdom that offers significant defensive potential but requires careful consideration and strategic deployment to be effective. It's a skill that either defines a battle or becomes a wasted slot, depending on the context and enemy builds. This guide explores how to maximize the effectiveness of "Misleading" and integrate it into your battle strategy.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/image-19-1024x229.png)

## Skill Mechanics

### Core Functionality

- **Effect**: "Misleading" is an aura skill that reduces the Accuracy Rate of all enemy units by 20% for the duration of the fight.
- **Impact**: A reduced accuracy rate increases the likelihood that enemy attacks will miss your units, effectively making "Misleading" one of the strongest defensive measures available—when it works.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/image-20.png)

## Strategic Application

### Understanding Accuracy and Dodge

- **Dodge vs. Accuracy**: Battles in Infinity Kingdom are influenced by two opposing attributes—Dodge rate and Accuracy. While Dodge increases your chances of evading an attack, Accuracy is designed to counteract this and ensure hits land.
- **Balancing Act**: The effectiveness of "Misleading" hinges on having a higher Dodge rate than the enemy's Accuracy. If successful, it forces the enemy to miss attacks, which means zero damage dealt during those instances.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/image-21.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/image-22.png)

### Ideal Use Cases

- **High Dodge Builds**: "Misleading" excels in builds that naturally have high Dodge rates or are enhanced through other skills and artifacts that boost evasion, such as "After-Image" or Manco's unique artifact.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/image-23.png)

- **Enemy Build Analysis**: Before deploying "Misleading," it’s crucial to analyze the likely builds of your opponents. If they invest heavily in Accuracy through their immortals' attributes, dragon talents, or skills like "Coercion," the effectiveness of "Misleading" diminishes.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/image-24.png)

## Tactical Considerations

### When to Use Misleading

- **Effective Scenarios**: Use "Misleading" when you know your opponents have lower Accuracy investments. This is often more feasible in controlled environments or where you have good intelligence on enemy setups.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/image-28.png)

- **Risky Deployments**: Avoid using "Misleading" in high-stakes battles without prior knowledge of the enemy's build, as it could potentially waste a valuable skill slot if the enemy has high Accuracy.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/image-26.png)

### Building Around Misleading

- **Complementary Skills and Gear**: Enhance the effectiveness of "Misleading" by equipping your immortals with gear and skills that increase Dodge rates. This synergistic approach maximizes the chances of enemy attacks missing, leveraging the full defensive potential of "Misleading."

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/image-27.png)

- **Strategic Immortal Placement**: Consider placing immortals with "Misleading" in positions where they can affect the maximum number of enemies, especially against high-damage dealers whose impact you want to mitigate.

## Conclusion

"Misleading" offers a powerful defensive capability in Infinity Kingdom, potentially turning the tide of battle by causing enemy attacks to miss. However, its effectiveness is highly contingent on the relative Dodge and Accuracy attributes of engaged forces. Properly utilized, it can render your army nearly untouchable, but it requires careful preparation and a deep understanding of both your and your enemy's builds. As with any strategy, the key to success with "Misleading" lies in adaptability and informed decision-making, ensuring that each slot in your Tower of Knowledge is optimized for maximum impact on the battlefield.

title: Mont Saint Michel
summary: Greetings, lords and ladies! Today, we embark on a journey to explore the all-new Castle skin, \"Mont Saint Michel.\" This majestic skin promises not only a visually stunning upgrade for your stronghold but also valuable…
markdown:
### Player Guide: Mont Saint Michel Castle Skin

Greetings, lords and ladies! Today, we embark on a journey to explore the all-new Castle skin, "Mont Saint Michel." This majestic skin promises not only a visually stunning upgrade for your stronghold but also valuable buffs to aid you in your conquests. Let's delve into the details of how to obtain it, its cost, appearance, and the benefits it brings.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-205.png)

### Obtaining the Mont Saint Michel Skin:

To adorn your castle with the Mont Saint Michel skin, you'll need to navigate through the three-step bundles available in the in-game shop. Each bundle provides distinct rewards:

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-209-1024x529.png)

- **First Bundle (5$):** Unlocks a unique profile picture frame.
- **Second Bundle (10$):** Grants you an exclusive chatbox skin.
- **Third Bundle (100$):** The grand prize! This bundle includes the Mont Saint Michel castle skin along with a castle name decoration to truly personalize your stronghold.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-206-1024x525.png)

![](blob:https://ik-wiki.com/edc0c84f-0618-48b6-bb6b-8b3dd55684ba)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-208-1024x522.png)

### Appearance and Aesthetics:

The Mont Saint Michel Castle skin boasts a visually striking design that is sure to catch the eyes of fellow players.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-205.png)

Though personal opinions may vary, many players appreciate the intricate details and unique charm of this skin. It's worth noting that the skin looks particularly impressive in the Red faction, but it still adds a touch of elegance to your castle in Green.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-210.png)

Additionally, the Mont Saint Michel skin includes a troop cosmetic skin that enhances the overall appearance of your army. Prepare to lead your forces with style!

### Functionality and Buffs:

Beyond its aesthetic appeal, the Mont Saint Michel skin provides tangible benefits to aid you in your conquests:

- **Resource Production Bonus:** Enjoy a 5% boost to all resource production, excluding gold.
- **Troop Training Speed Bonus:** Experience a 5% acceleration in troop training speed.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/image-211-1024x523.png)

While these buffs might not revolutionize your gameplay, they contribute to the overall efficiency of your kingdom. The troop training speed bonus is especially valuable for those who may not have the Fire Dragon skin.

In conclusion, the Mont Saint Michel Castle skin is a worthy addition to your collection, combining visual elegance with practical benefits. Whether you seek to showcase your status or optimize your resource management, this skin offers a well-rounded package for lords and ladies ready to elevate their kingdom to new heights. Best of luck on your quest!

title: More tips to blocking areas
summary: Introduction: Legion of Frostborne in Infinity Kingdom introduces a colossal player versus player environment where servers are pitted against each other in a massive battleground. Beyond the battles themselves…
markdown:
### Securing Strategic Areas in Legion of Frostborne PvP Season in Infinity Kingdom

**Introduction:**
Legion of Frostborne in Infinity Kingdom introduces a colossal player versus player environment where servers are pitted against each other in a massive battleground. Beyond the battles themselves, strategic gameplay becomes crucial as servers vie for control over cities and, most importantly, gates connecting different sections of the map. Securing these gates is paramount for success in Legion of Frostborne, and one effective strategy involves blocking access points to these vital structures.

**The Hive Formation:**
The Hive Formation is a key tactic for blocking important strategic areas around gates. Follow these steps to create an effective hive around a gate:

1. **Coordinate Castle Placement:**

- Players should strategically position their castles with one space between them to cover as much area as possible.
- Consider the gate's surroundings and place castles to maximize coverage while leaving no gaps for opponents to exploit.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-92.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-94.png)

1. **Utilize Shields:**

- Once castles are in position, activate shields to protect your forces from enemy attacks.
- Ensure that the shields cover as much of the area around the gate as possible.

1. **Leverage the Yellow Area:**

- Recognize the yellow area near the gates where players cannot shield.
- Place powerful players or critical defensive units in this space to deter and repel enemy forces.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-96.png)

1. **Deploy Thermal Towers:**

- To block off the yellow area entirely, fill it with Thermal Towers.
- Thermal Towers can provide both defensive capabilities and obstruct enemy movements.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-95.png)

**Advanced Blocking Strategies:**
While the basic Hive Formation is effective, employing additional strategies can enhance your blocking capabilities:

1. **Spawn Gnome Camps:**

- Temporarily block large areas by strategically spawning Gnome Camps.
- Gnomes can create obstacles for enemy forces, disrupting their movements and buying precious time.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-99.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-100.png)
