title: Patch 2.9.0 - Zuma Towers, Throne Rework, Chaos Immortal buffs, and more
summary: Patch 2.9.0 is not a content-heavy update in the traditional sense, but it is a structurally important one. Rather than introducing a new system layered on top of existing mechanics, this patch focuses on reworking…
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-105-1024x576.png)

## Introduction

Patch 2.9.0 is not a content-heavy update in the traditional sense, but it is a structurally important one. Rather than introducing a new system layered on top of existing mechanics, this patch focuses on reworking competitive formats, adjusting long-standing activities, and reshaping several underperforming or awkwardly positioned Immortals. As such, its real impact will be felt over time, not on day one.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-106-1024x316.png)

This article analyses the announced changes before the patch goes live, focusing on *why* these changes were made, what problems they attempt to solve, and where they may fall short. The goal is not to predict a perfect outcome, but to outline likely player experiences across free-to-play, mid-spender, and late-game competitive brackets.

---

## Revamped Throne of the Supreme

The headline feature of Patch 2.9.0 is the return of Throne of the Supreme in a revamped form. On paper, the format is clearer, more structured, and significantly faster-paced than the old version. In practice, the success of this rework will hinge almost entirely on one design decision: the expansion of the matchmaking pool to *Same-Season Regions*.

### Tournament Structure Overview

Each Throne season now runs on a fixed 37-day cycle:

| Stage | Duration | Format | Advancement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qualifying Round | 14 days | Point-based arena challenges | Top 128 players |
| Group Elimination | 8 days | 16 groups of 8, round-robin BO3 | Top 4 per group (64 total) |
| Grand Final | 7 days | 64 split into 4 brackets of 16, BO5 | 1st–3rd place |

The Grand Final explicitly takes the 64 remaining players and divides them into four parallel elimination brackets of 16, eventually producing the final podium. This is a clean structure and avoids the awkward pacing issues the previous Throne suffered from.

Combat itself remains familiar: auto-mode only, fixed four-team lineups used for both attack and defense, and arena-style rules. There is nothing experimental here, which is appropriate for a flagship competitive mode.

### Same-Season Region Matchmaking: The Core Problem

The controversial change is the matchmaking pool. As written, *Same-Season Region* appears to mean that **all servers within a given season**—entire Conquest seasons, entire Legendary seasons, and earlier seasonal brackets—are merged into a single competitive pool.

This directly undermines the stated goal of the Throne rework.

The original problem with Throne of the Supreme was not that it lacked prestige. It was that participation felt pointless for the majority of players. The same small group advanced every cycle, while everyone else served as ladder filler. Expanding the initial qualification to 128 players *sounds* inclusive, but if those 128 slots are drawn from an enormous seasonal population, the end result is even more static than before.

In such a system:

- The Top 128 will stabilize quickly.
- Movement into that group will require extreme spending or attrition from existing top players.
- Most participants will effectively play 14 days of qualifiers, then spectate the same matchups every season.

Larger pools only work if there are **parallel paths to meaningful competition**.

### A Missed (But Easily Fixable) Opportunity

The solution here is straightforward and already proven in other competitive games: **tiered brackets**.

After the qualifying round, instead of funneling everyone into a single elimination path, players could be divided into multiple playoff tiers:

- **Tier S Bracket**: Top-end competitors fighting for prestige titles and maximum rewards.
- **Tier A Bracket**: Strong mid-to-high spenders with meaningful competitive stakes.
- **Tier B Bracket**: Competitive but accessible brackets for developing accounts.

This approach preserves elite competition while giving thousands of players a reason to care beyond Day 14. Importantly, it scales naturally with seasonal population size.

As it stands, the revamped Throne improves structure and pacing, but risks becoming *more restrictive* than the version it replaces. Whether this is adjusted quickly will determine if Throne becomes a flagship mode again or another spectator event.

---

## Zuma Tower – A New Stardust Economy Lever

Zuma Tower replaces the old Primal Pinball event as the primary activity tied to Stardust and Crimson Moonlight acquisition. Conceptually, it is a high-risk, high-reward climbing mode with a clear gambling-style progression loop.

*The video below is from the test servers. Therefore, this is an indication of how the event is supposed to work, but remain subject to changes before coming live on servers. So beware! We have seen changes from test-server to live-server implementation before.*

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/20251211-144757-1.gif)

### How Zuma Tower Works

Each attempt consumes **Pearl of Finding**, currently obtainable through Daily Deals. Every attempt has a probability to:

- Move up 1–2 floors
- Stay on the same floor
- Drop 1–2 floors

At any point, the player may choose to stop and claim rewards based on their *current floor*. Claiming resets the run back to the base level.

An example run:

- +1 floor → +2 floors → -1 floor → +2 floors
- Player stops at net +4
- Rewards are granted for Floor 4, then the run resets

The tower caps at Floor 7, which grants a special currency used toward high-end rewards such as castle skins.

### Risk, Protection, and Cost Uncertainty

Pre-release footage shows a temporary buff that prevents players from dropping floors. It is currently unclear whether:

- This is a test-only safeguard
- A purchasable buff
- A limited-time event modifier

This distinction matters enormously. With protection, climbing becomes relatively efficient. Without it, pushing for Floor 7 could become prohibitively expensive very quickly.

### Expected Value and Player Impact

While concrete pricing is unknown, the intent appears clear: **increase Stardust and Crimson Moonlight accessibility**, particularly Stardust, which has long been one of the tightest progression bottlenecks.

Early indications suggest:

- Better money-efficiency than previous events
- Meaningful rewards for mid-spenders
- Limited value for true free-to-play players

Zuma Tower also introduces an upgradable Shadow Fortress variant, though details remain scarce. This suggests the mode may become a long-term progression feature rather than a simple event replacement.

Overall, Zuma Tower has strong potential, but its reception will depend almost entirely on Pearl pricing and drop protection mechanics.

---

## Activity and System Optimizations

Patch 2.9.0 includes a broad set of smaller adjustments that, while not individually dramatic, collectively improve pacing and fairness.

### Alliance Supremacy Matchmaking

Alliance Supremacy (Alliance Championship) matchmaking is now restricted to **within the same season**. This directly addresses a major fairness issue where Conquest alliances were previously matched against Legendary-season opponents. This is an unequivocally positive change.

### Arena Team Unlock Timing

Arena multi-team deployment is now tied to server age rather than progression speed:

| Team | Unlock Timing |
| --- | --- |
| Team 2 | Day 14 |
| Team 3 | Day 31 |
| Team 4 | Day 45 |

This standardizes pacing across spend levels. Free-to-play players gain access faster, while heavy spenders lose the ability to brute-force early unlocks. In practice, this is a minor change, as one dominant march still decides most outcomes.

### Infernal Assault Rewards Scaling

Gold rewards have been **significantly increased,** with diminishing returns applied per activity cycle:

We do unfortunately not know precisely what "significantly" means, but on the face of it. Increasing the rewards by a lot in exchange for a diminishing return effect on rewards, means that most players are able to reap the same rewards as with the current event faster and for less AP. That being said, the few players that are actually doing 4-500 infernals per event (true grinders) will see this as a nerf given the massive reduction post 200.

| Attempts | Reward Rate |
| --- | --- |
| 1–100 | 100% |
| 101–200 | 60% |
| 201–300 | 30% |
| 300+ | 10% |

All in all though, I think this is a big quality of life improvement for most players who do not want to farm infernals for 36 hours but do need the gold.

This incentivizes moderate engagement without encouraging unhealthy grinding patterns.

---

## Immortal Balance Adjustments

This patch focuses exclusively on Chaos Immortals, and importantly, all changes are buffs rather than nerfs.

### Apollo – Energy Tempo Restoration

Apollo’s base energy regeneration increases from 66 to 80 points per second. This is a substantial buff and helps him remain competitive following Medusa’s release. While Medusa still outclasses him in most late-game contexts, this adjustment keeps Apollo relevant rather than obsolete. 80 energy regen may not sound like a lot, but remember that this is base stats. With simple decent tech (not even fully upgraded) on my castle he baselines 72 before the patch going live (given my global modifiers).

Upgrade him, technology, etc. fully and you will see a final energy regen far larger and honestly quite high compared to others. Actually, this buff brings him to precisely the same base energy regen stat as Loki, that is not too bad!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-110-1024x678.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-111-1024x684.png)

*Calculations for comparison: Apollo 66 baseline + 10% in culumative modifiers = 72.6. After patch, 80 baseline + 10% modifiers for comparison = 88. This is precisely the same as a baseline Loki.*

### Ares – Control Immunity and Momentum

Ares receives baked-in control immunity and a stronger Frighten effect trigger chance (up to 70% which is very good and should provide good consistency this is possibly (for some hopefully) make the Frighten effect actually worth building control setups around. Moreover, a buff to the barrier weakening effects (50%, up from 30%). This is a transformative change and I think it makes Ares highly valued both as the "better Alex" he is clearly intended to be (but has not been so far) and more interestingly, as someone to build control builds around.

Here is Ares BEFORE the update for comparison:

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-109-1024x506.png)

Control immunity ensures uptime, allowing Ares to function as intended in momentum-driven builds such as Fully Prepared, Warpath Rage, and KTB compositions. This places him much closer to Alexander in practical strength and reliability.

### Nine Tails – Backline Amplifier

Nine Tails gains a new passive that **increases backline damage by up to 30%** while also boosting trigger-skill activation.

Here she is BEFORE the update for comparison:

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-107-1024x597.png)

She remains compared naturally to Fu Fei, the dominant Chaos support, but this buff narrows the gap significantly. In certain backline-centric builds, Nine Tails may now be a legitimate better than Fu Fei, or atleast a real alternative rather than a niche counter pick to Poseidon.

---

## Conclusion Summary

Patch 2.9.0 is a patch about *direction*, not spectacle.

- Throne of the Supreme is structurally improved but risks failing its inclus imagined purpose due to over-expanded matchmaking pools.
- Zuma Tower replaces Primal Pinball with a more engaging, potentially more generous Stardust system—assuming costs remain reasonable.
- System optimizations clean up long-standing fairness and pacing issues.
- Chaos Immortal buffs meaningfully refresh underused options without destabilizing the meta.

If developers are willing to iterate quickly—particularly on Throne bracket structure—this patch could mark a meaningful step toward healthier long-term competition. If not, it risks reinforcing the very problems it set out to solve.

---

title: Patch 2.9.1 - Factory Event (new), Galaxy retired, new skill currency for legendary skills, etc.
summary: Patch v2.9.1 is a systems-focused update for Infinity Kingdom. Rather than introducing new immortals or combat mechanics, this patch adjusts how several core events, seasonal systems, and interfaces work. The goal is…
markdown:
### Patch v2.9.1 – First Look at What’s Changing and What It Means

### Introduction

[Patch **v2.9.1** is a systems-focused update for **Infinity Kingdom**](https://infinitykingdom.gtarcade.com/en/news/7023887.html). Rather than introducing new immortals or combat mechanics, this patch adjusts how several core events, seasonal systems, and interfaces work. The goal is clearer progression, more predictable rewards, and fewer confusing or underused mechanics.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-76-1024x258.png)

Below, I’ll go through the patch notes **section by section**, explaining what each change does and what it practically means for players.

---

## New Features

### 1. Manufacturing Factory Event

### What’s in the patch notes

- A brand-new recurring event called *Manufacturing Factory*
- Active every **Sunday, Monday, and Tuesday**
- Unlocks once a server is **75 days old**
- Uses a new interaction with **Energy Cores**:  - Each Energy Core used gives a random reward and fills an energy bar
- When energy reaches 100%, you receive a **Rune Insignia**
- Energy then resets, allowing the process to repeat
- Rune Insignias can be exchanged for rare rewards
- The old **Sparks of Galaxy** event is removed
- **Frosty Orbs** can be exchanged for Energy Cores at a **3:1 ratio**

### What this means

This event replaces Sparks of Galaxy entirely. Instead of a single-event currency with a fixed reward structure, progress is now tied to filling an energy meter repeatedly. The system is designed to reward ongoing participation rather than one-time spending. How precisely this event will impact players grinding e.g. shadow immortal fragments via the Galaxy event, is unknown. Will it be cheaper than Galaxy? We just do not know yet, but if it is anything like the re-work that introduces Zuma towers we can expect a cost increase in exchange for new reward possibilities.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-80-1024x683.png)

The Frosty Orb exchange ensures older resources don’t become useless, but at a reduced conversion rate. Players should expect this event to become part of regular weekly activity rather than a skippable side event.

If we are able to get a sneak peek at this event, I will make sure to drop a news article while event is yet pre-released. Stay tuned for news here on site.

---

### 2. VIP Privilege Expansion

### What’s in the patch notes

- New summon options unlocked at higher VIP levels:  - **VIP 10:** 10-pull summons
- **VIP 15:** 20-pull summons
- These apply to:  - Theia’s Roulette
- Sparks of Galaxy / Manufacturing Factory
- Wisdom Well

### What this means

This is a convenience upgrade for higher-VIP players. Instead of performing many single summons, players can now bundle pulls together. This does not change odds or rewards, but it reduces time spent interacting with these events and makes large summon sessions easier to manage.

---

## Optimizations

### 1. Wisdom Well Adjustments

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-77-1024x572.png)

### What’s in the patch notes

- The **ban function** has been removed
- Acquisition methods adjusted for:  - Ability Stones
- Unique Artifact Schematic Fragments
- New item added: **Wisdom Elixir**
- **Wish Shop updates**:  - Wisdom Elixir can be used to buy **Epic and Legendary Skills**
- Cinder of Wishes remains usable for Epic Skills, Schematics, and Alchemy Stones
- Skill availability rules clarified:  - Epic Skills available starting **Season 0**
- Legendary Skills available starting **Season 1**
- Epic Skills rotate into the Point Shop the following season

### What this means

Wisdom Well is being simplified and made more structured. Removing the ban function eliminates an option most players didn’t use. Adding Wisdom Elixir another direct connection between Wisdom Well participation and skill acquisition through the Wish Shop. This is perhaps one of the biggest items in the 2.9.1 patch, as we are going to see legendary skills becoming easier to obtain (still expensive and pay-walled entirely, but cheaper). This is very good news and something I am looking very much forward to. I am going to be skipping a round of Wisdom Well myself to bank Divine Coins in anticipation of the 2.9.1 patch change.

---

### 2. Zuma Tower Event Adjustments

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-78-1024x575.png)

### What’s in the patch notes

- Items in the Zuma Shop now have **daily purchase limits**
- **Colosseum skin fragments** added to the shop  - The skin can be upgraded visually

### What this means

Daily limits prevent players from buying large quantities of shop items in a single event. Skin fragments add another long-term cosmetic upgrade path.

### 3. Battle Pass Opening Time Optimization

### What’s in the patch notes

- **Peak Battle Pass** now unlocks **90 days after server launch**

### What this means

Battle Pass access is super important to player growth, making this a simple but very good change for newer players.

---

## Legion of Frostborne Optimizations

### 1. Legendary Season Changes

### What’s in the patch notes

- Middle Ring entry requirement reduced:  - From **3,600,000** to **2,800,000 Faction Points**
- Legion Personal Achievements now vary by **Lord Contract**
- Some achievements:  - Require specific zones
- Require investing talent points to activate contract talents

### What this means

Entering the Middle Ring becomes easier for legions, reducing progression bottlenecks. Personal achievements are now tied to a player’s chosen contract, meaning different roles within a legion are evaluated differently.

---

### 2. Altar Stone Optimizations

### What’s in the patch notes

- Altar Stone and Thermal Tower ranges now displayed using tiles
- New **View Range** button in Legendary Season
- Attack ranges show different colors for allies vs enemies
- When exposed, all inner city tiles become attackable
- **Core Durability** now shown in City Info

### What this means

These are interface clarity improvements. Players can more easily see ranges, understand targeting, and assess city durability without guessing or opening multiple screens.

---

### 3. Season 1 & 2 Off-Season Changes

### What’s in the patch notes

- Once server requirements are met:  - A unified **5-day wait** before matchmaking begins
- A visible **matchmaking countdown** is added in the Preparation Zone
- **Corrosive Power** unlock level adjusted to **Tower of Knowledge level 40** (season 0): The Corrosive Power adjustment makes that skill available earlier, smoothing progression through Tower of Knowledge - that being said, it is still technically the most expensive skill in the game only available through the low % skill stone chests from Wisdom Well.

### What this means

Off-season timing becomes clearer and more predictable. Players and legions can see exactly when matchmaking will begin instead of waiting without clear indicators.

---

### 4. Season Interface Server List Optimization

### What’s in the patch notes

- Server lists now show **round numbers** in Conquest and Legendary Seasons

### What this means

At a glance, players can see which round a server is in, making it easier to understand progression and matchups across seasons.

---

## Conclusion

Patch **v2.9.1** focuses on clarity, structure, and long-term usability. Events are streamlined, seasonal systems are easier to read, and underused mechanics are removed or replaced. Rather than changing how battles are fought, this update changes how players interact with the game’s systems—making progression more transparent and easier to plan around as Infinity Kingdom moves forward into 2026.

---

title: Patch 2.9.2 - Great Tengu, 5th Anniversary Event, Divine Protection buff, and more
summary: Patch 2.9.2 is scheduled to go live on February 5, aligning with the fifth anniversary of Infinity Kingdom. It’s a restrained update by design: one new immortal, an anniversary decoration, and a set of targeted…
markdown:
### Patch 2.9.2 Overview – Practical Notes from a Veteran Perspective

Patch **2.9.2** is scheduled to go live on **February 5**, aligning with the fifth anniversary of **Infinity Kingdom**. It’s a restrained update by design: one new immortal, an anniversary decoration, and a set of targeted adjustments to competitive modes and long-standing systems.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-3-1024x373.png)

Nothing here rewrites the meta overnight, but several changes are worth understanding properly—especially if you participate in Throne, Infernal Assault, or plan to invest in the anniversary content.

---

## New Immortal: Great Tengu

### Role and Positioning

Great Tengu is a **Chaos**, **Defense-position**, **Shieldman** immortal. That alone tells us most of what we need to know: he’s designed for the frontline, built to absorb pressure (especially to counter Ares and Alexander builds). His kit reinforces that identity almost entirely.

### Skill: Unbreakable Pact

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/image-4-1024x169.png)

**Passive effect**
Each time Great Tengu is hit by a *normal attack*, he gains a stacking Physical Damage increase. At max stacks (20), this becomes a meaningful damage contribution, but only in prolonged engagements. This is not a ramp-up you feel in quick skirmishes or against spell-heavy comps but it will quickly build to max versus Alexanders and Ares'.

From experience, passives like this only shine when the frontline survives long enough to benefit—think sustained Throne fights or drawn-out arena mirrors rather than quick Open Arena clears.

**Active effect**
The active skill does three things, depending on conditions:

1. **Cleanses all debuffs from allies**
2. **If no debuffs are present**, it triggers a heal (scaling with skill level)
3. **Grants front-row immortals a counterattack buff** for 6 seconds, dealing Physical Damage back to attackers when hit by normal attacks

On paper, this positions Great Tengu as a **direct answer to normal-attack carries**. Immortals like Ares or Alexander rely on frequent basic attacks to function. Against them, Tengu:

- Gains damage from being hit
- Reflects damage back through counterattacks
- Punishes extended trades rather than burst windows

The fact that Tengu also cleanses all debuffs is incredibly powerful on paper, though it will be very interesting to see precisely what "debuffs" will encompass. We have previously seen dispel effects that work only on specific debuffs and not negative effects or wounds effects for example. If I where to venture a guess, I would think things like Wounds will not be dispelled by this - alas, time will tell. Tengu is looking like a very good counter to high attack speed builds, will he be top meta pick though? I think that will depend on how this active dispel will work in practice. Stay tuned for Tengu to come live!

### The Key Uncertainty

The wording also leaves another critical question unresolved: **Is the counterattack tied to the “no debuffs” condition, or only the heal?**

If the counterattack only triggers when no debuffs are present, its reliability drops sharply. In real combat, frontliners almost always carry at least one debuff—burns, slows, defense breaks, or control effects. In that case, this part of his kit would rarely activate outside of very specific matchups.

If, however, the cleanse → heal check is separate and the counterattack always applies, Great Tengu becomes much more consistent and far more relevant in sustained PvP.

This is something battle reports will clarify quickly once the patch goes live.

### Exclusive Artifact: Tengu Mask

The artifact extends the counterattack duration by **3 seconds**. Its value depends entirely on how often that counterattack is active in real combat. If the buff is conditional and rare, the artifact is marginal. If it’s reliable, this becomes a meaningful extension in long frontline trades.

### Availability

- Obtained through the **5th Anniversary Celebration**
- Server age requirement: **178 days**

This keeps him firmly out of early-server balance considerations.

---

## Anniversary Castle Decoration: Hall of Divine Might

This is a straightforward but valuable stat stick:

- **Base:** +5% Troop Attack, +5% Troop Load
- **Max:** +15% Troop Attack, +10% Troop Load

There’s no trick here. Troop Attack is universally strong, and Load has obvious utility for PvE, rallies, and logistics-focused playstyles.

Unlock condition is modest (server age ≥14 days), so nearly all active servers will have access.

---

## Throne of the Supreme – Structural Tightening

At first glance, the Throne changes look generous: **256 players** now advance from qualifiers instead of 128. The reality is more nuanced.

- 256 players are split into **32 groups of 8**
- Only **Top 2** from each group advance (down from Top 4)

In practice:

- More players reach the group stage
- Advancement becomes significantly more competitive once there

If you’re used to cruising through group stages on consistency alone, this change raises the bar. Placement matters more than volume, and bad matchups inside your group are harder to offset.

---

## Zuma Tower & Rune Factory – More Attempts, Same Systems

### Zuma Tower

- Each round now grants **5 free Vision of Zuma packs**
- Packs can be saved for future events

This doesn’t reduce risk or alter mechanics, but it does increase long-term attempt volume without spending. Over time, that adds up—especially for players who already understand optimal stopping points.

### Rune Factory

- New gem pack: **3 Energy Cores per purchase**, up to 20 daily
- Added **$0.99** and **$1.99** packs

As with Zuma, this increases throughput rather than changing gameplay. Progression pacing remains the same; spending options simply become more granular.

---

## Infernal Assault – Clear Daily Limits

Gold reward decay now **resets daily**, with defined brackets:

- 1–60 runs: 100%
- 61–100: 60%
- 101–150: 30%
- 151+: 10%

This formalizes what many players already optimized around. The key difference is clarity and predictability. You now know exactly when further runs stop being efficient on a given day.

---

## Smaller but Relevant Adjustments

- **Open Arena:** Level 60 troop templates now available in Legendary Season
- **Battle Reports:** Kingdom buffs are now visible in statistics
- **Troop Balance:**  - Archer HP increased at levels 6–8
- All troop types gain HP at level 9
- **Dragon Skill – Divine Protection:**  - Damage reduction scaling increased, improving late-level survivability

None of these shift metas dramatically, but they smooth progression gaps and improve transparency.

---

## Final Thoughts

Patch 2.9.2 is intentionally modest. Outside of **Great Tengu**, most changes refine existing systems rather than introduce new ones. The Throne adjustments tighten competition, Infernal Assault becomes more predictable, and anniversary content adds some universally useful stats.

Whether Great Tengu ends up being impactful depends almost entirely on how his counterattack condition works in practice. If it’s reliable, he’ll find a niche against normal-attack-heavy comps. If not, he’s likely to remain a situational pick rather than a staple.

Overall, this is an anniversary patch that focuses on polish and accessibility rather than upheaval. Useful, measured, and unlikely to disrupt day-to-day play—but still worth understanding before it lands.

---

title: Patch 2.9.3 – Dragon Talent Rebalance, Atalanta Rework, and Rune Factory Rewards
summary: Patch 2.9.3 focuses on three areas:
markdown:
## Introduction

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-10-1024x304.png)

Patch **2.9.3** focuses on three areas:

- Event and system optimizations
- Quality-of-life improvements for alliances and map interaction
- A substantial **dragon talent rebalance**, alongside a **rework for Atalanta**

While some of the optimizations are largely interface improvements, several changes have practical strategic implications—especially the dragon adjustments, which may shift the current **burst-heavy meta toward longer sustain fights**.

Below is a breakdown of each official patch section with practical interpretation and player commentary. [Please see the full patch notes here.](https://infinitykingdom.gtarcade.com/en/news/7024067.html)

---

## Optimizations

## Rune Factory Reward Pool

### Official Change

- Added **Chaos (red) tier Immortals**
- Added **Chaos Exclusive Artifacts**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-30-1024x530.png)

This is potentially one of the more important event changes in the patch.

The main uncertainty is **how these rewards will be distributed**, but reading the notes I assume that they will be available in the shop.

For now, treat this as a **potential value increase for Rune Factory**, but wait for confirmation of how the reward pricing actually works out compared to e.g. Roulette.

---

## Immortal Specialization Unlock Rules

### Official Change

- Specialization levels will not be displayed until unlock conditions are met.

Purely a **UI clarity improvement**. It prevents confusion for newer players seeing locked specialization levels without understanding the requirements. No gameplay impact.

---

## Returning Player Event Rules

### Official Change

- Each character can trigger the returning player event **only once**.

This closes a loophole where some players attempted to repeatedly trigger returning bonuses through inactivity cycles. For normal gameplay, this change has **minimal strategic impact**.

---

## Legion of Frostborne Map Optimization

### Official Changes

1. Added **Federation markers** managed by alliance leaders
2. Leaders automatically join Federation chat groups
3. **Alliance Thermal Towers now display server identifiers**

### Comments:

The **server identifier on Thermal Towers** is the key improvement here. Previously in Legion of Frostborne it was sometimes difficult to determine:

- Which alliance controlled a tower
- Which **server** that alliance came from

This information matters when evaluating **enemy strength and diplomacy decisions**. Knowing the server origin immediately helps alliances estimate potential resistance or alliances behind a structure.

This is a **small but genuinely useful improvement** for cross-server events. However, mostly a quality of life thing..

---

## Chat Features

### Official Change

- Chat channels now support secondary tabs.

Primarily organizational. No gameplay implications.

---

## City Declaration of War

### Official Change

- After declaring war on a city, attacks must begin **within 10 minutes** or the declaration resets.

This change mostly targets **war coordination discipline**. Previously, alliances could declare war and delay the attack indefinitely.

Now:

- The attacking alliance must **mobilize immediately**
- Leadership must ensure players are **ready before declaring**

It removes some of the flexibility previously used for **timing manipulation**. You are no longer able to keep as many options for pressure points open at a time and thus it becomes easier for defenders to recognize where they are about to be attacked.

For casual alliances or farmers, this may occasionally cause missed declarations.

---

## Alliance Level After Server Merge

### Official Change

- After server merges, **Alliance Level and Technology remain unchanged**

This is arguably something that should have existed from the start.

Previously, merges could severely disrupt alliances because technology progression might reset or change. Keeping alliance progression intact protects:

- alliance investment
- long-term technology planning
- established competitive balance

For veteran alliances, this change removes a major frustration from server merges.

---

## Balance Adjustments

The patch also introduces a bunch of different balance adjustments for Atalanta and for dragon talents!

---

## Atalanta Skill Rework

### New Skill – Focused Sniper

- Fires a crossbow bolt dealing **Physical Damage (240% + 80%/level)** to one random enemy
- Grants normal attacks a **piercing chance (30% + 10%/level)** for 10 seconds
- Pierced attacks hit the enemy behind the target

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-11.png)

### Artifact Effect

- Focused Sniper damage **+30%**

Atalanta has historically struggled to remain relevant in the **Wind meta**. Many players experimented with her but eventually moved away due to inconsistent performance.

However, until testing confirms the interaction frequency of the pierce mechanic, her true value remains uncertain.

In practice, most veteran players will likely **wait for battle testing** before rebuilding Wind compositions around her.

---

## Dragon Talent Adjustments

This is the most impactful section of the patch.

The adjustments strongly suggest a **meta shift toward sustain-oriented combat**, rather than the burst-damage environment that has dominated for over a year.

---

## Holy Dragon

### Changes

- Healing increased from **6% → 10% per level**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-12-1024x468.png)

- Protect now scales **Attack & Defense from 75 + 15/level**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-13-1024x445.png)

- Concentration healing increased
- Judgment Roar increased true damage when enemy troops remain high

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-15-1024x475.png)

Holy Dragon appears to receive the **largest buff in this patch**.

Early analysis suggests it may once again become **one of the strongest dragons in the game**, potentially surpassing Earth Dragon in popularity.

Historically, Holy Dragon and Shadow Dragon were intended to be the **top-tier dragons**, but Earth Dragon dominated the meta for a long period due to its durability.

These changes may finally restore Holy Dragon to its intended role as a **high-impact sustain and scaling dragon**.

---

## Shadow Dragon

### Changes

- Silhouette: Dark Breath true damage increased **10% → 15% per level**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-16-1024x468.png)

A simple **damage increase**.

Shadow Dragon remains strong in offensive compositions, but many players hoped for more mechanical improvements. The buff is welcome, though it likely **won’t dramatically change its current position**.

---

## Wind Dragon

### Changes

- Turmoil Breath: True damage scaling increased

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-17.png)

- Stormy Breath: Healing scaling increased

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-18.png)

The buffs are decent but may not be enough to revive Wind Dragon usage across the meta.

Players who already invested in Wind Dragon will appreciate the improvement, but it may still struggle against stronger sustain dragons.

---

## Earth Dragon

### Changes

- Collapse damage increased from 30,000 to 50,000

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-19-1024x435.png)

- Fissure now:  - Reduces damage by **25%**
- Provides stronger healing or true damage on attacks

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-20-1024x457.png)

Interestingly, Earth Dragon did not necessarily need more damage.

These changes appear focused on **increasing sustain across the board**, reinforcing the idea that the developers are pushing combat toward **longer battles rather than burst kills**.

Even with these changes, Earth Dragon was already extremely strong. It will likely remain a **top defensive option**.

---

## Lightning Dragon

### Changes

- Shock spec: Damage increased from 6%/level to 10%/level

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-22-1024x461.png)

- Overload spec: Increases damage dealt gets buffed from 25% to 35% + 5%/level for every stunned target on the battlefield

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-23-1024x482.png)

The rework improves scaling but probably **won’t dramatically elevate Lightning Dragon**.

The main limitation remains its reliance on **stun-heavy compositions**, which are not always reliable in competitive environments.

---

## Water Dragon

### Changes

- Frigid spec: Healing increased **6% → 10%**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-25-1024x461.png)

- Coalesce spec: Converted to stronger **continuous healing** (from 10%/level to 12%/level, duration extended by 12s)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-26-1024x456.png)

- Buff for ALL specs: Ice Breath freeze chance increased from 24.75% + 2.25%/level to 27.5% + 2.5%/level. At max level from 45% to 47.25% at baseline

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-24.png)

These improvements are long overdue.

However, Water Dragon still suffers from **hard counters in the immortal roster**, such as compositions that disrupt healing mechanics.

Currently, many Water Dragon teams rely heavily on **Athena-based builds** to remain viable as well as ones focused around energy regen (no change). The buff helps, but it may not be enough to bring Water Dragon fully back more options for sustain water in the meta.

---

## Fire Dragon

### Changes

- Burning damage increased for Prairie Fire. Damage increased from 6%/level to 10%/level.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-28-1024x452.png)

- Wildfire spec: Critical strikes now increase **Attack and Defense**. Changed from 30 + 5/level to 75 + 15/level for 30s when it lands a Crit. At max that means instead of 120 attack and defense you now get 210 attack and defense for every crit.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/image-29-1024x446.png)

This is one of the more interesting changes in the patch. Critical strikes now converts crits into **stat boosts**, potentially enabling stronger sustained DPS setups. This is something I am very keen to be testing out once the patch lands, as I have hopes for more mitigation enabled setups with the fire dragon.

Testing will determine whether this becomes a meaningful buff or just a minor adjustment.

---

## Player Perspective – Meta Direction

From a veteran standpoint, the overall patch direction suggests a clear goal:

**Reduce the dominance of burst-nuke teams and encourage sustain-based combat.**

Signs pointing toward this shift include:

- Multiple dragons receiving **healing improvements**
- Defense scaling increases
- Sustained damage mechanics replacing burst amplification

If this trend continues, we may see:

- Longer battles
- Greater value in healing and mitigation
- More diverse team compositions

However, the real impact will only become clear after **battle testing in Arena and PvP events**.

---

## Conclusion Summary

Patch **2.9.3** introduces meaningful adjustments, especially to dragons.

The key takeaways:

- **Rune Factory rewards may become significantly more valuable**
- **Holy Dragon likely receives the biggest buff**
- Many dragon changes favor **sustain and longer fights**
- **Atalanta receives a potentially important rework**, though her viability remains to be tested
- Several quality-of-life improvements help alliance coordination and cross-server clarity

Overall, this patch feels like the **first step in a broader meta adjustment**, rather than a complete balance overhaul.

Veteran players should watch closely how Holy Dragon and sustain-based teams perform once the update goes live.

---

title: Patch 2.9.4 - Quality of Life, New Arcane Hunter skill, Athena changes and more
summary: Patch 2.9.4 is, on the surface, a quality-of-life update. Most of the changes improve clarity and usability rather than raw power. However, underneath that, there are two adjustments that point clearly toward ongoing…
markdown:
## Introduction

Patch 2.9.4 is, on the surface, a quality-of-life update. Most of the changes improve clarity and usability rather than raw power. However, underneath that, there are two adjustments that point clearly toward ongoing developer intent: a continued push away from magic-dominated compositions and toward physical damage setups.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-25-1024x572.png)

This direction isn’t new. It started around the release of Apollo, accelerated significantly with Medusa, and has continued through skill design. With Arcane Hunter and the Athena adjustment, we’re seeing that trend reinforced again—this time through both offensive scaling and defensive counterplay.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-17-1024x368.png)

### Full patch notes available here

---

## Resource and Speed-Up Tracking

This change is purely quality of life, but it’s one that has been overdue for a long time.

For years, players have had to manually track their speed-ups and resources, especially when planning KvK participation or long upgrade cycles. The lack of visibility often led to inefficient usage—burning universals too early, misjudging healing capacity, or simply not knowing what was available without digging through the inventory.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-18-1024x466.png)

To give some context, tools were created outside the game to solve this. I built a resource and speed-up calculator for the wiki some time ago because there was consistent demand from players trying to plan more accurately.

With this update, that process is now built into the game. You can quickly see your totals and make decisions accordingly.

In practice, this won’t make you stronger, but it will make your progression smoother. It’s especially valuable during KvK, where proper allocation of speed-ups directly determines how long you can stay active in fights.

---

## Zuma Tower Transparency Update

The Zuma Tower change is minor. The event was already functional and reasonably transparent, but this adds another layer of clarity by showing reward claims directly.

While I haven’t seen a full Zuma cycle post-patch yet, the intention is clear: reduce guesswork and make progress easier to track.

In reality, this doesn’t change how you play Zuma. It just makes it easier to judge whether continuing to invest is worth it. These kinds of changes tend to reduce wasted resources over time, even if the immediate impact feels small.

More transparency is always a positive, especially in events where efficiency matters.

---

## Arcane Hunter and the Ongoing Meta Shift

Arcane Hunter is the most important addition in this patch, not just because of what it does, but because of what it represents.

At a base level, the skill provides three things: reduced magical damage taken, periodic AoE physical damage every six seconds, and a conditional 30% critical rate bonus when Light Blessing is active.

The numbers themselves are solid. At max level, you’re looking at roughly 300% damage every six seconds, which is consistent pressure rather than burst. The magic damage reduction, around 20% at scale, is also highly relevant in a meta that still leans heavily on magic-based damage.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-19.png)

But the real significance is how this fits into the broader direction of the game.

This shift away from magic started when Apollo was introduced, though at the time he struggled to find a place. It accelerated with Medusa, who effectively defined the modern physical damage meta—especially when paired with skills like Eternal Battlelust. Since then, we’ve seen multiple skill releases that favor physical scaling and reward sustained damage output.

Arcane Hunter continues that trend.

At the same time, it feels like a corrective measure. Apollo has largely fallen out of favor in high-end play, especially compared to Medusa-based setups. This skill gives him a clear avenue back into relevance. While any physical damage dealer can use Arcane Hunter effectively, Apollo benefits the most due to his access to Light Blessing.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-20.png)

That additional 30% crit rate is significant. It turns the skill from steady pressure into something that can consistently spike damage during longer fights. In practice, this could bring Apollo back into contention for optimized builds, particularly in setups designed around sustained engagements.

That said, in top-end whale environments, Medusa is still likely to remain the preferred option. Her scaling and synergy with existing skills are simply more established. But Arcane Hunter does close the gap slightly and broadens viable options.

---

## Athena Adjustment and Wound Counterplay

Athena’s change is subtle in design but important in context.

Her passive no longer provides 200 initial energy and instead grants immunity to Seriously Wound effects to all allies. This is a direct response to how strong wound mechanics have become, particularly outside of full whale compositions.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-21-1024x636.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-22.png)

Wounds remain one of the most effective ways to shut down sustain. We continue to see immortals like Qin performing well across standard elemental setups largely because of how impactful healing denial is. Even when raw damage isn’t overwhelming, preventing recovery creates consistent advantages over time.

The developers have already tried to address this. In the previous patch, Nine Tails was adjusted to remove wound effects more effectively. However, that change didn’t meaningfully shift her into a dominant healer role.

Athena appears to be the next attempt at solving the same problem.

From a gameplay perspective, this change shifts her role rather than strictly buffing her. Losing the 200 starting energy hurts her early tempo, which was already one of her weaker points. However, the wound immunity introduces a very specific and valuable niche.

In high-end whale fights, this likely won’t change much. Those setups typically don’t rely on wound mechanics in the first place. But in mid to high spender environments—where players mix elemental cores with one or two Chaos immortals—this becomes much more relevant.

We’ve already seen the return of Genghis Khan in many of these setups. Against those builds, Athena can now enable sustain-based compositions that were previously difficult to maintain. By removing wound pressure entirely, she allows healing and mitigation strategies to function as intended.

For players struggling against Khan-based marches, this could open up new defensive options that weren’t viable before.

---

## Conclusion Summary

Patch 2.9.4 is primarily a quality-of-life update, but it carries clear signals about where the game is heading.

Resource tracking and Zuma improvements reduce friction and improve efficiency, particularly in long events like KvK. Arcane Hunter reinforces the ongoing shift toward physical damage and sustained combat, while also giving Apollo a path back into relevance. Athena’s adjustment addresses the continued strength of wound mechanics, offering a targeted counter that will matter most in mid- to high-tier play.

Individually, these changes are modest. Together, they continue to shape a meta that favors durability, consistency, and careful matchup planning over raw burst or single-strategy dominance.

If you approach the patch with that in mind, the value becomes much clearer.

---

title: Patch 2.9.5 - Immortal Affinity, Asteria changes and adjusted preperation times for kvk
summary: The introduces several long-term progression systems at once, while also reviving older content that many veteran players have not seen in years. Some of these additions look promising immediately, while others still…
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-40-1024x437.png)

The introduces several long-term progression systems at once, while also reviving older content that many veteran players have not seen in years. Some of these additions look promising immediately, while others still raise important questions that the official notes do not fully answer yet.

The official patch notes confirm three major additions: the Immortal Affinity system, the new Insignia system, and the return of Battle of Asteria. On top of that, the preparation phase for Conquest and Legendary Seasons has finally been shortened, which is likely the most impactful quality-of-life change for active competitive alliances.

You can read the full official notes on the [Infinity Kingdom Official Forum](https://infinitykingdom.gtarcade.com/en/news/7024309.html).

---

## Immortal Affinity – A New Long-Term Progression System

The new Immortal Affinity feature allows players to send gifts to specific immortals in order to increase affinity levels. According to the official notes, reaching certain milestones unlocks rewards and additional story content, while affinity level 30 grants rare insignia rewards.

At the moment, the largest uncertainty is whether this system is purely narrative and cosmetic, or whether it has direct gameplay implications beyond the confirmed insignia rewards.

For now, the official answer from the development team on press officer requests for more information is: "Please wait for us to organize the content and I will get back to you all". Once they do, I will make sure to keep you all updated!

From experience with previous Infinity Kingdom systems, there are a few possibilities here:

- Pure lore and story progression
- Cosmetic profile rewards (which would be quite cool)
- Permanent account combat bonuses
- Immortal-specific stat increases
- Unlockable new combat features/effects tied to affinity levels

The wording in the patch notes strongly suggests there is more attached to this than simple flavor text. The mention of “rare insignia rewards” seems to indicate to me that there will either be some tie into the existing Insignia systems and shops, perhaps adding insignia rewards upon completion of Immortal Affinity levels which can be used in the shops for new immortal fragments or artifacts? I hope so! Or an entirely new Insignia type specifically for the new rewards tied to affinity levels (most probably in my humble opinion).

What remains unclear is whether:

- affinity progression is time-gated,
- gifts are farmable or premium-limited,
- rewards reset seasonally,
- or certain immortals provide better progression value than others.

---

## The Insignia System – Cosmetic Collection or Another Power Layer?

The Insignia System is probably the feature generating the most discussion right now.

Officially, insignias are obtained through:

- Immortal Affinity
- Appearance Collection
- Festival Events
- Gameplay events

The important line from the patch notes is this:

> “Activating insignias grants additional attribute bonuses. Collecting the specified number of each insignia type provides total attribute bonuses that affect all Immortals.”

That wording matters. It strongly suggests stat scaling rather than temporary event buffs, most likely additional attribute bonuses tied to specific immortals upon completing affinity levels with that immortal? I would think so, let's see..

If that interpretation is correct, insignias could function similarly to the boost levels where we completed lore and story content to earn currency/materials to activate new boost levels for buffs. Sounds like we are getting a new layer of something kind of similar but with a lot more to it than pure combat buffs as they also mention various cosmetic features.

---

## Battle of Asteria Returns

Older players will immediately recognize Battle of Asteria.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-42-1024x403.png)

This event existed during the earlier years of Infinity Kingdom before eventually disappearing from rotation. At the time, it had interesting concepts but eventually became outdated because the rewards no longer matched the pace of account progression.

The new version appears significantly expanded.

According to the patch notes:

- the event will now be server-wide,
- difficulty scales with season progression,
- both solo and alliance participation exist,
- and there are multiple challenge types including rally content.

The addition of:

- Single Squad Challenges,
- Multi-Squad Challenges,
- and Rally Challenges

suggests the developers are trying to modernize the event structure around current account diversity and alliance coordination.

The most important factor will ultimately be rewards.

The official notes already confirm:

- event currency,
- resource chests,
- and Immortal Affinity items.

If reward scaling is competitive with current seasonal progression, Battle of Asteria could become meaningful weekly or periodic content again. If rewards remain tuned like the older version, players may treat it as optional filler content instead.

From a veteran perspective, bringing back older content is generally positive when it is modernized properly. Infinity Kingdom has accumulated many systems over the years, and rotating older events back into relevance is healthier than endlessly stacking entirely new modes on top of existing ones.

---

## Season Preparation Time Reduction – Quietly the Most Important Change

For many active alliances, this may actually be the best part of the patch.

The preparation phase changes are straightforward:

- Off-season reduced from 14 days to 7 days
- Announcement phase reduced from 5 days to 2 days
- Cold Night duration remains unchanged

This significantly improves pacing for competitive kingdoms and active alliance leadership.

Long preparation downtime has been a recurring frustration for high-activity servers because momentum tends to collapse during extended waiting periods. Shortening dead time keeps:

- recruitment active,
- alliance organization tighter,
- and player engagement more stable between seasons.

For R5 and R6 players especially, this reduces a lot of unnecessary idle management.

It is also one of the few recent changes that benefits nearly every type of player equally, regardless of spending level.

---

## Smaller Optimizations That Still Matter

Two smaller quality-of-life updates are also included:

### Alliance Statistics Mail

The addition of 24-hour and 48-hour filters is a simple but genuinely useful improvement for alliance management, especially during:

- IB registration,
- migration prep,
- inactivity tracking,
- and event participation reviews.

### Forge Interface Improvements

The Forge coin conversion interface now displays material types more clearly. Not a game-changing update, but interface cleanup for older systems has been overdue for a while.

---

## Conclusion Summary

v2.9.5 introduces several systems that could significantly affect long-term account progression, especially through the new Insignia mechanics and Affinity rewards. However, the current patch notes still leave many important questions unanswered regarding scaling, accessibility, and permanent stat impact.

The return of Battle of Asteria is a welcome surprise for older players, particularly if rewards are modernized properly, while the reduced preparation time for Conquest and Legendary Seasons is likely the most universally appreciated change in the patch.

We will publish updated guides and deeper system breakdowns once the development team responds to the press officer requests for additional clarification, or once the patch is fully live and tested in-game.

---

title: Patch 2.9.6 - Deepsea Venture, new legendary skill, Asteria ajustments, Tengu buffs and more
summary: The v2.9.6 patch is now live, bringing a new event, several quality-of-life improvements, changes to Battle of Asteria, and a surprisingly interesting buff to Great Tengu. While this isn't a major content update on the…
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-1024x390.png)

The v2.9.6 patch is now live, bringing a new event, several quality-of-life improvements, changes to Battle of Asteria, and a surprisingly interesting buff to Great Tengu. While this isn't a major content update on the level of a new season or immortal release, there are a few changes that could have a noticeable impact on progression and endgame team building.

Let's go through the patch notes one section at a time and look at what they actually mean for players.

## Deepsea Venture Event

The headline feature of this patch is the new **Deepsea Venture** event. Unfortunately, the patch notes don't tell us much beyond the fact that it has been added.

From the event interface, we can already see a new currency called **Colorful Scales** and a **Mermaid Shop** containing rewards related to Oley and Shadow progression. Based on what is currently visible, my first impression is that this looks more like a spending event than a standard participation event.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-1-1024x583.png)

The important question isn't whether the rewards are good. It's whether they are better than the alternatives. Will this be a free-to-play friendly way to progress holy and shadow? Will is be more cost-efficient that e.g. Rune Factory? Time will tell and we will make sure to keep you updated here on site when the event is live.

Until we see the reward structure and bundles, it's too early to judge. This is definitely the section of the patch that deserves a follow-up once the event actually goes live.

---

## New Daily Mission: Affinity Gifting

This is a small change, but it's one that most players will benefit from immediately.

Daily missions now include gifting one affinity item. For active players, this is a very minor thing. Since the daily stock for the Otherworldly shop is well.. daily, you are most likely buying these every day anyway.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-2-1024x321.png)

---

## Norheim Survival Guide Improvements

The Survival Guide now includes more detailed explanations for immortal attributes and how they work.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-3-1024x566.png)

Veteran players probably won't spend much time here, but newer players should. One of the biggest learning curves in Infinity Kingdom is understanding stats, scaling, and progression systems. Having better explanations inside the game is always a positive change.

A lot of information currently comes from community guides, so seeing the game itself provide more detail is long overdue.

---

## Squad Survival Tournament

The Squad Survival Tournament is now being divided between Season 1 and Season 2 servers.

The rules themselves aren't changing, but the separation should create more balanced competition.

This feels like a matchmaking improvement rather than a gameplay change. Players competing against others at a similar stage of progression should make the tournament more enjoyable and more competitive overall.

---

## New Legendary Skill: Thorn Armor

The new legendary skill introduced in this patch is **Thorn Armor**.

At a basic level, the skill reduces incoming physical damage for the entire team. That's already useful, but the more interesting part is the interaction with Counterattack effects.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-4-1024x504.png)

When Counterattack is active, Thorn Armor also reflects damage back to attackers. 20% physical damage reduction does not look like anything huge, but given the thorn reflect damage (requires counterattack from e.g. Tengu) this looks a lot like another attempt at making a whale counter for Alexander builds. And this one might work quite well I suspect!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-5.png)

On its own, Thorn Armor looks like a situational defensive skill. Combined with the Great Tengu changes (and him applying Counterattack), however, it starts to make a lot more sense.

---

## Great Tengu Gets a Significant Buff

The biggest balance change in the patch is the adjustment to Great Tengu's skill, **Unbreakable Pact**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-6-1024x484.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-7.png)

The new version still provides cleansing and debuff immunity, but now also grants Counterattack to front-row immortals. Looking at this alongside Thorn Armor, it feels clear that the developers are trying to expand Counterattack into a real team archetype rather than a niche mechanic. Does this suddenly make Tengu a must-have immortal? I don't think so.

Tengu is still an expensive Chaos immortal and most players will likely prioritize immortals such as Fu Fei or Medusa first. However, players who already own Tengu have gained a lot of additional utility.

He now brings:

- Cleansing
- Debuff immunity
- Healing
- Counterattack support

That's a much more complete package than before.

---

## Battle of Asteria Rework

For the average player, this may actually be the most important part of the patch.

After the update, everyone starts back at Difficulty 1 and must progress through the stages again. At first glance this looks like a reset, but I think it's mostly a positive change. The new system is much easier to understand, progression is more structured, and players will earn rewards while climbing back through the difficulties. More importantly, many players will collect additional Otherworld Crystals during the process.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image-8-1024x524.png)

That means:

- More purchases in the Otherworld Shop
- More affinity items
- More progression resources

Yes, you'll spend some AP and troops while climbing again, but the extra rewards should offset that for most active players.

---

## Quality-of-Life Changes

The remaining changes are fairly minor but still welcome.

Affinity levels are now visible directly on immortal information screens, saving players from jumping through multiple menus just to check progress.

The Alliance Championship result changes appear to be mostly an interface adjustment. We'll probably need to see a few championship cycles before knowing whether there is any meaningful impact beyond presentation.

---

## Final Thoughts

The biggest unknown remains Deepsea Venture. Until players can actually participate, it's impossible to know whether it will become a valuable progression event or simply another premium activity competing for resources.

Outside of that, the standout changes are the Battle of Asteria rework and the new Counterattack synergy between Thorn Armor and Great Tengu. Neither change is likely to completely reshape the meta overnight, but both have the potential to become more important as future content arrives.

---

title: Patch 2.9.7 - New Outfit System and more!
summary: Version 2.9.7 isn't one of the game's largest updates, but it introduces something that could become one of the most important long-term progression systems we've seen in quite a while: Immortal Outfits.
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-1024x316.png)

## Immortal Outfits Arrive – Plus Quality-of-Life Improvements

Version **2.9.7** isn't one of the game's largest updates, but it introduces something that could become one of the most important long-term progression systems we've seen in quite a while: **Immortal Outfits**.

Alongside that, Lilith has added a new Decoration Shop and several welcome quality-of-life improvements across Asteria, Legion of Frostborne, Arena, and the Ruins interface.

Let's go through everything that changed and what it actually means for players.

---

## New Immortal Outfit System

The headline feature of this patch is the brand-new **Immortal Outfit** system.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-1-1024x547.png)

The first two Immortals receiving outfits are:

- Alexander
- Athena

These are called the **Summer Passion Outfits**, and they're much more than simple cosmetic skins.

## How to Unlock Outfits

Outfits are obtained by collecting **Outfit Fragments** during **Festival Events.**

Once you've collected enough fragments, the outfit becomes permanently unlocked for that specific Immortal.

A few important things to know:

- Outfits are permanently bound to their Immortal.
- Rebirthing an Immortal does **not** remove the outfit.
- Unlocking an outfit also activates a unique **Outfit Insignia**.
- Different outfits can modify that Immortal's Ultimate Skill.

The permanent binding works similarly to Mythic Equipment. Once you've unlocked an outfit, you don't need to worry about losing it during rebirths or rebuilding your Immortal.

---

## The Big Feature: Ultimate Skill Changes

This is easily the most interesting part of the entire update.

Changing an outfit doesn't simply change your Immortal's appearance—it also changes their **Ultimate Skill**.

That means these outfits are effectively a brand-new progression system rather than a cosmetic feature.

Exactly how much each Ultimate changes will vary by outfit, but the important takeaway is that these aren't visual upgrades—they can directly affect combat performance.

For now, only Alexander and Athena have alternate Ultimate Skills.

As more outfits are released, this system has the potential to completely reshape how certain Immortals are built and played.

---

## What Does This Mean?

It's still very early, but a few things already seem likely.

### 1. This is another long-term progression system

Like Artifacts, Mythic Equipment, Affinity, and Candy Defenders before it, outfits appear to be another layer of account progression.

If future outfits continue to provide new Ultimate Skills, collecting them could become a major part of strengthening your account.

---

### 2. Alexander Gets Even More Attention

Many players were surprised that Alexander was chosen as one of the first Outfit recipients.

Alexander has already been one of the strongest Immortals in the game for a long time.

If his alternate Ultimate ends up being stronger—or even just better in certain situations—it could make him an even more valuable investment.

Of course, we'll need testing before drawing conclusions, but it's definitely something worth watching.

---

### 3. We Don't Yet Know How Accessible They'll Be

Outfit Fragments come from Festival Events.

The big question is how generous those events will be.

If fragments are obtainable through normal gameplay, this could become another enjoyable progression system.

If they're heavily tied to spending, however, outfits could become another gap between free-to-play players and heavy spenders.

For now, it's simply too early to know.

---

## New Decoration Shop

The patch also introduces a brand-new **Decoration Shop**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-2-1024x570.png)

### Unlock Requirement

- Lord Level 6

Players can purchase **exclusive Collection Outfits** here.

At the moment, the shop appears to focus primarily on cosmetic collections rather than gameplay progression, although we'll likely see more items added over time.

For newer players, unlocking it is straightforward, and it provides another place to browse and collect account cosmetics.

---

## Optimizations

While the new Outfit system steals the spotlight, the patch also includes several welcome quality-of-life improvements.

## Battle of Asteria Adjustments

Alliance difficulty and Boss HP have both been adjusted.

The exact numbers weren't provided, but the goal appears to be improving overall balance and making progression smoother for alliances.

---

## Ruins Exploration Button Moved

The Ruins button has been relocated next to the Mail button.

It's a small change, but one that makes Ruins much easier to access during daily gameplay.

---

## Legion of Frostborne Alliance Log

The Alliance Log now records:

- Legion registration
- Registration cancellations

This gives alliance leaders much better visibility into who's signing up—and who isn't.

It's a small improvement that should make organizing Legions a little easier.

---

## Improved Battle Reports

Arena, Open Arena, and Throne of the Supreme now display battle reports more consistently.

Previously, HP values shown during wheel battles could be confusing.

Now, the HP displayed throughout the report matches the HP values present when combat actually began, making it much easier to follow what happened during a fight.

---

## Final Thoughts

Version 2.9.7 is relatively small in terms of content, but the **Immortal Outfit system** has the potential to become one of the game's biggest progression mechanics over the coming months.

Right now, we only have two outfits, so it's far too early to judge how impactful—or how accessible—the system will be. The real test will come as more Immortals receive outfits and we begin to see whether these alternate Ultimate Skills create meaningful new strategies or simply become another source of raw power.

The rest of the update is mostly quality-of-life focused, with cleaner interfaces, better battle reports, and a few welcome improvements for Asteria and Legion of Frostborne.

Overall, this feels less like a major content patch and more like the foundation for a feature that Lilith plans to expand over time. Whether it becomes a fun layer of customization or another mandatory progression system will depend entirely on how future outfits are released and balanced. For now, it's definitely the feature to keep an eye on.

---

title: Patch 2.9.8 - Endless Tower and Alliance Sparring Take Center Stage
summary: Update 2.9.8 isn't a massive content expansion filled with new immortals or balance changes, but it introduces two features that could have a lasting impact on how Infinity Kingdom is played. Alongside a brand-new PvE…
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-129-1024x444.png)

Update **2.9.8** isn't a massive content expansion filled with new immortals or balance changes, but it introduces two features that could have a lasting impact on how *Infinity Kingdom* is played. Alongside a brand-new PvE mode, the long-requested Alliance Sparring system finally gives players a way to enjoy meaningful PvP outside of Kingdom vs Kingdom.

The remainder of the update focuses largely on progression improvements and quality-of-life features, including changes to Artifacts, Dragon Souls, the Zuma Shop and several interface improvements. None of these are game-changing on their own, but together they make progression a little smoother, particularly for newer players.

Let's take a closer look at what Update 2.9.8 brings.

---

## Alliance Sparring Finally Fills a Long-Standing Gap

For many servers, meaningful PvP has been limited for years. Outside of Legion of Frostborne and Kingdom vs Kingdom, there often isn't much opportunity to fight.

On one-alliance servers, there simply isn't another alliance of similar strength to compete against. Even on servers with two or three large alliances, Norheim usually settles into an unofficial peace because everyone wants to focus on growth rather than constant troop losses. The result is that many players only experience large-scale PvP during KvK.

The new Sparring System looks set to change that.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-130-1024x491.png)

From the patch notes, it appears alliances will be able to divide into two teams and fight one another during dedicated sparring sessions. Assuming that's how it works in practice, this could become one of the most valuable additions the game has received in years. It gives alliances a way to organise PvP training, test marches and rally compositions, practise coordination, and even earn Honor without asking players to leave the alliance to create temporary enemies.

The fact that Sparring still causes troop losses and triggers Bloody Rage also suggests it is intended to feel like genuine world-map combat rather than a simplified duel mode. That should make it a much better environment for testing real marches before taking them into KvK.

It's a feature the community has been asking for since the early days of the game, and it's great to finally see it become a reality.

---

## Endless Tower Looks Promising

The second major addition is **Endless Tower**, a new PvE progression mode unlocked after 15 days on a server once players reach Castle Level 20.

The mode follows a familiar formula, with players climbing increasingly difficult floors while adapting to unique Floor Traits that change the challenge from one level to the next. Five attempts are available each day, rewarding players with progression materials and fragments for Holy, Shadow and even Chaos immortals.

Whether Endless Tower becomes a favourite will probably depend on what kind of player you are.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-132-1024x104.png)

Players who enjoy solving PvE encounters and experimenting with different teams will likely appreciate another challenge mode, especially if Floor Traits encourage creative team building rather than simply rewarding higher Combat Power. Players who already feel there are enough daily PvE activities may be less enthusiastic about another mode to complete every day.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-131-1024x172.png)

Personally, I hope the difficulty comes from mechanics rather than raw statistics. If success depends on choosing the right immortals, adapting your skills and responding to each floor's traits, Endless Tower could become one of the more engaging PvE modes in the game. If progression simply comes down to increasing your Combat Power, it risks becoming another routine grind.

The rewards are what make Endless Tower particularly interesting. A new source of **Holy, Shadow and Chaos Immortal fragments** has the potential to improve long-term progression, especially for low and mid-spending players building around Holy and Shadow marches instead of full Chaos teams. Making those immortals more accessible should encourage greater variety in team building across the game.

Chaos fragments are also listed as rewards, although I wouldn't expect them to be especially generous. Much like the Harbour, they will likely provide slow, steady progress rather than replacing the existing premium acquisition methods.

---

## Other Notable Changes

Although Endless Tower and Alliance Sparring are clearly the headline features, the remainder of the patch contains several welcome improvements.

**Artifact progression** has become much more accessible. Removing the Chronicle requirement means every new server can begin using Artifacts immediately instead of waiting for progression milestones. At the same time, Artifact Potential has been adjusted so Season 0 players can reach Silver quality while Season 1 players can progress to Gold. It's a sensible change that allows newer servers to engage with the Artifact system much earlier.

**Theia's Roulette** has also been updated with selectable Holy and Shadow Dragon Soul rewards. We still need to see exactly how these rewards are distributed, but giving players more control over Dragon Soul progression is certainly a positive step.

The **Zuma Shop** receives a smaller update, adding new Rare Fragments while removing the option to exchange Pearl of Findings for Energy Cores. Depending on what fragments become available, this may change purchasing priorities for players who regularly use the shop.

Several quality-of-life improvements round out the patch. Immortal Outfits can now be previewed immediately, the Appointment interface has been simplified with static portraits, Insignias now use clearer colour coding based on rarity, and chat finally gains the ability to quote messages. None of these changes transform the game, but they make the overall experience a little cleaner and easier to navigate.

---

## Final Thoughts

Update 2.9.8 may not introduce flashy new immortals or sweeping balance changes, but it addresses several areas that have needed attention for a long time.

The **Alliance Sparring System** has the potential to give players meaningful PvP outside of Kingdom vs Kingdom, solving a problem that has existed on many servers since the game launched. If it works as advertised, it could become one of the most useful social features ever added to *Infinity Kingdom*.

Meanwhile, **Endless Tower** adds another avenue for long-term progression while introducing a valuable new source of Holy and Shadow Immortal fragments. Whether it becomes an engaging strategy mode or simply another daily activity will depend largely on how challenging and varied its Floor Traits prove to be.

Overall, this feels less like a major expansion and more like a quality-of-life update that strengthens the game's core systems. It may not be the most spectacular patch on paper, but if these new features deliver on their potential, Update 2.9.8 could have a lasting impact on how players spend their time in *Infinity Kingdom*.

---

title: Patch 2.9.9 - Horus Could Break the Burst Meta
summary: Infinity Kingdom's v2.9.9 update contains a long list of quality-of-life improvements, but its real strategic importance is concentrated in three changes: the arrival of Horus, the release of Psychic Vortex, and the…
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-12-1024x405.png)

Infinity Kingdom's v2.9.9 update contains a long list of quality-of-life improvements, but its real strategic importance is concentrated in three changes: the arrival of Horus, the release of Psychic Vortex, and the decision to make several important Wish Shop skills available earlier in seasonal progression.

The smaller improvements are welcome. Automatic building upgrades will help developing accounts, Lord Talent trees will become easier to adjust, and formation copying should make Elemental Domain less tedious. None of those changes, however, are likely to reshape the strongest marches in the game. Horus might.

Horus is a new back-row Chaos magic Immortal whose passive limits the damage he can receive from any single instance. That mechanic directly challenges the high-burst approach that has defined a large part of the Infinity Kingdom meta in recent years. When combined with Psychic Vortex and an energy-regeneration build, he has the potential to become an extremely difficult carry to burst down while steadily scaling into overwhelming magical damage.

At the same time, Eternal Battlelust is moving from Legendary Season to Conquest. This removes one of the main reasons Medusa previously had to wait until Legendary before reaching her full potential.
