title: Preperation - Talents and Troop allocation
summary: Illusion Battlefield (IB) is a cornerstone in Infinity Kingdom PvP and my personal favorite activity. It has a high skill cap and because gemming prosperity and shielding for hours is disables and replaced with zone…
markdown:
Illusion Battlefield (IB) is a cornerstone in Infinity Kingdom PvP and my personal favorite activity. It has a high skill cap and because gemming prosperity and shielding for hours is disables and replaced with zone specific talent skills, it allowes for fun PvP battles where alliances can overcome a stronger foe by playing well and being coordinated.

This article we go through the preperation phase of IB. This article goes through:

1. Buffs
2. Talents
3. Troop allocations
4. IB specialization

If you already know all the basics and want to head deep into strategy - and get a few tips n tricks - skip ahead and read the article **[Illusion Battlefield/Combat/How-to-win](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/pvp/illusion-battlefield-ib/combat-strategies-tips-n-tricks-to-win/)**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/image-3-1024x478.png)

## Buffs

An important note some people seem to confuse - **YES city buffs and alliance buffs count in IB**. For a short periode of time, these were disabled, but were quickly set back on.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/image-10-1024x95.png)

In addition, you should always use personal buffs as well as secure yourself an appropriate city-position, e.g. +5% Damage dealt by Cavalry as the Governor of Baldr.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Skaermbillede-2022-02-23-214801.png)

Personal buffs can be used within IB so you don't waste precious time by buffing ahead of entering. You can thus rely on the cheap 1 hour buffs.

## Talents

You want to swap into your combat talent set for Illusion Battlefield matches.

There are two very important talents you must make sure you have on for any IB match: **Riding Fast + Working Hard.**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Skaermbillede-2022-02-23-215028.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/Skaermbillede-2022-02-23-215010.png)

You want both of these because you want to quickly move around the map, speed is extreemly important both for your attacks and for your relocations. Moreover, with Working Hard you can strategize your first relocation and [cancel enemy relos right out of the gates!](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/pvp/illusion-battlefield-ib/combat-strategies-tips-n-tricks-to-win/)

## Troop Allocation

You must allocate the number of troops you want to bring into IB. It is very important that you are efficient in your allocation. By this I mean, you will be loosing way more archers than anything else - therefore you should bring around 50-60% of your troops as archers. The remaining troops should be distributed relatively equal, but you can slack a little on shieldmen as you will tend to loose proportionally fewer of these (because of their generically tanky Immortals).

You should have 1 or 2 marchers that are strong enough to be used as battle marches inside the IB match. Make sure you match these to your troop allocations. Your third march is a buffer march to be used for [relo denials](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/pvp/illusion-battlefield-ib/combat-strategies-tips-n-tricks-to-win/) and your fourth should be turned into a [1 unit confusion march](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/pvp/illusion-battlefield-ib/combat-strategies-tips-n-tricks-to-win/). As such, just make sure you have troops for the marches you actually fight with.

IMAGE

## IB Specializations

There are three specializations to choose from when preparing to enter IB.

1. **Defense**
2. **Offense**
3. **Support**

For a detailed guide, please see: **[IB Specialization deep dive](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/pvp/illusion-battlefield-ib/specialization-deep-dive/)**

You need to pick one that is best suited for your playstyle and your role in the battle to come. Most of the time you want to be **Defense**, especially if you do not have a lot of speedups to heal troops with. This is simply because Defense has nice defensive abilities like shielding and healing troops.

If you are in an offensive role or perhaps take part of a strike-team style group of players. You want to go **Offensive**for the famous teleport. This can realistically only be used once per battle (long CD) but is still extreemly powerful to backstab enemy towers.

**Support**roles are important, despite having no high impact combat abilities, their ability to speedup occupation speed is very powerful if your team is able to use it whilst your offense roles stack a lot of marches with Hold Fast into the structure at the same time. **[Read more in the strategy guide](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/pvp/illusion-battlefield-ib/combat-strategies-tips-n-tricks-to-win/)**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Support-1024x257.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/defensive-1024x295.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/offensive-1024x311.png)

title: Price comparison Chaos Roulette vs Serpent's Gaze (chaos immortal and artifacts only)
summary: Chaos development is one of the biggest long-term investments in Infinity Kingdom. Two events allow players to directly acquire Chaos immortal fragments and Chaos artifact materials:
markdown:
### Cost of Chaos Immortals and Artifacts in Serpent’s Gaze vs Chaos Roulette

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/image-188-1024x550.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-51-1024x519.png)

---

## Introduction

Chaos development is one of the biggest long-term investments in Infinity Kingdom.
Two events allow players to directly acquire Chaos immortal fragments and Chaos artifact materials:

1. **Chaos Roulette** – weekly event → Eyes of Chaos → spins → fragments
2. **Serpent’s Gaze** – seasonal event → Tokens → Grails → immortal fragments and artifacts

Both events reward Chaos progress, but their **cost efficiency is drastically different**.
This guide compares the exact value of each system so whales and high spenders can decide where their money is best spent.

---

## Quick Recap: What We Know About Chaos Roulette (For Comparison)

Before comparing Serpent’s Gaze and Chaos Roulette, here are the core numbers from the Chaos Roulette guide — just the essentials you need to understand the value difference.

### Expected immortal fragments per spin:

- **≈ 0.434 fragments per spin**
(This already includes 4% jackpot, 25-spin pity, and the two 3% immortal slots.)

### Expected artifact fragments per spin:

- **0.09 per spin**
(Bonus bar does not add artifact fragments.)

### Bonus bar efficiency:

- Best value at **50**, **100**, and **200** spins
- Worst at **350–700**
- 900 spins gives decent value because of the final 60-frag chest
- If you care about value → stay ≤200
- If you care about speed → go 900

### Cost of a full Chaos immortal (1,640 fragments)

### 200-spin weekly route (value path):

- ~14 weeks
- Costs **≈ $1,400 total**
- **≈ $0.85 per fragment**

### 900-spin weekly route (speed path, corrected):

- 3 × 900-spin weeks + 1 × 200-spin week
- Costs **≈ $1,630 total**
- **≈ $0.99 per fragment**

This gives us the real comparison baseline:

**Chaos Roulette immortal fragments cost between ~$0.85 and ~$0.99 each.**

### Chaos Roulette artifact cost

- Requires about **667 spins** per artifact
- Costs **$333–$378** depending on whether you follow 200 or 900-spin pacing
- Much slower overall because you need ~10,000 spins for 15 artifacts
- Causes heavy immortal-fragment overflow (5,600–6,100 frags gained in the process)

These numbers are what make Roulette excellent for immortals but inefficient for artifacts.

For the full deep-dive math, drop rates, cycle modeling, and bundle analysis, **[see the full guide here.](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/events/wheels-roulette/chaos-roulette-2-6-9/)**

---

## Serpent’s Gaze – Detailed Cost Breakdown

Serpent’s Gaze gives Chaos progress through the **Grail Shop**:

### Immortals

- **Medusa:** 850 grails → 80 frags
- **Others:** 750 grails → 80 frags

### Artifacts

- **Medusa artifact:** 1100 grails → full artifact (60 frags)
- **Other Chaos artifacts:** 1000 grails → full artifact (60 frags)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-43-1024x513.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-39-1024x513.png)

### Grail Wheel Expected Value

Spin probability → expected grails per spin:

| Reward | Chance | Grails |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1000 | 0.1% | 1.0 |
| 500 | 0.15% | 0.75 |
| 100 | 0.8% | 0.8 |
| 50 | 1.5% | 0.75 |
| 5 | 10% | 0.5 |

Total estimated value (EV): 1+0.75+0.8+0.75+0.5=3.81.

## Expected grails per spin = 3.8

---

## Token Cost — Using Only $3, $5, $10 Packs First

- $3 → 3 tokens → **$1/token**
- $5 → 5 tokens → **$1/token**
- $10 → 8 tokens → **$1.25/token**

Let's begin with only using the most efficient bundles, the 3 and 5 dollar ones at 1 dollar per token. Thus we have: 1 token = 3.8 grails and **1 grail costs** = $1÷3.8=0.263$

---

## Serpent’s Gaze – Cost to Buy 1640 Immortal Frags

### Non-Medusa Immortals (750 grails → 80 frags)

- Grails per fragment:
750 / 80 = **9.375**
- Cost per fragment:
9.375 × 0.263 = **$2.47**

That gets us 1,640 fragments * $2.47 = **$4,041** for a full 1640 fragments this way.

### Medusa (850 grails → 80 frags)

- Grails per fragment:
10.625
- Cost per fragment:
10.625 × 0.263 = **$2.80**

1,640×2.80= $**4,592** for max star Medusa.

---

## Serpent’s Gaze Immortal Cost Summary

| Immortal | Cost per 1640 fragments |
| --- | --- |
| Non-Medusa | ≈ $4,040 |
| Medusa | ≈ $4,590 |

For comparison, we are doing only the cheap bundles so far in the Serpents Gaze event, but we are much much less cost efficient comparing to Chaos Roulette (200–900 spin paths) which was **$1,400–$1,630**, meaning: **Serpent’s Gaze costs 2.5x to 3x more than Chaos Roulette for immortal fragments.**

---

## Serpent’s Gaze – Artifact Cost

Artifacts in the Grail Shop:

- 1,000 grails (most artifacts)
- 1,100 grails (Medusa)

### Cost at $0.263/grail:

- **1,000 grails → $263**
- **1,100 grails → $289**

### Comparing to Roulette ($333–$378):

## Serpent’s Gaze artifacts are cheaper than Chaos Roulette artifacts.

---

## Final Comparison Table

| Category | Chaos Roulette | Serpent’s Gaze | Winner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1640 Immortal Fragment Cost | $1,400–$1,630 | $4,040–$4,590 | Chaos Roulette |
| Immortal Cost per Frag | $0.85–$0.99 | $2.47–$2.80 | Chaos Roulette |
| 1x Complete Artifact Cost | $333–$378 | $263–$289 | Serpent’s Gaze |

---

## Conclusion

When you put everything side-by-side, the pattern is actually really clear:
**Chaos Roulette is the superior place to buy Chaos immortal fragments**, but **Serpent’s Gaze quietly becomes the best place in the entire game to buy Chaos artifacts.**

Roulette gives you far better value on immortal fragments because of the pity system, the new 1-fragment drops, and the weekly bonus bar. Even the fast 900-spin route, corrected to three full weeks plus one 200-spin week, comes out around **$1,630** for a full 1,640-fragment Chaos immortal. That’s miles cheaper than Serpent’s Gaze’s ~$4k price tag for the same number of fragments.

But here’s the interesting twist—for artifacts, the math completely flips.
In Chaos Roulette you need **11–12 full weeks of 900 spins (≈10,000 spins avg. total)** to secure the **15 unique artifacts** required for a max bonus artifact. That run gives you **around 5,600-6,100 immortal fragments**, which massively over-caps your Chaos immortals even if you max every talent node (4,750 fragments needed). You basically drown in immortal fragments long before you finish the artifacts.

Serpent’s Gaze doesn’t have that problem at all.
Everything is converted into **Grails**, and you spend those Grails in a shop where you choose exactly what to buy. That means whales can **target only the Chaos artifacts they want**, pay **less per artifact** than in Roulette, and avoid the painful over-capping of immortal fragments entirely. For high spenders optimizing Chaos development, that flexibility is huge.

So the ideal whale strategy looks like this:

- **Do Chaos Roulette for immortal fragments** — it’s the best value by far.
- **Do Serpent’s Gaze for artifacts** — it’s cheaper, faster, and doesn’t force you into excess immortal fragments you don’t need.

And while Serpent’s Gaze is a limited-time seasonal right now, there’s some indication (IKVIP whispers, not confirmed) that versions of the Grail Shop may return in future seasonals. If that happens, this becomes one of the best recurring artifact paths in the game for whales.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-50.png)

Bottom line:
**Whales should build their immortals in Roulette and finish their artifacts in Serpent’s Gaze.**
It’s cheaper overall, it’s cleaner, and it avoids the big inefficiencies built into Roulette’s artifact progression.

---

title: Primal Pinball
summary: The Primal Pinball event in Infinity Kingdom is an exclusive
markdown:
### Navigating the Primal Pinball Event in Infinity Kingdom

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-42-1024x561.png)

The Primal Pinball event in Infinity Kingdom is an exclusive opportunity for players, especially big spenders, to accumulate valuable resources for upgrading portrait levels on Chaos Immortals. This guide aims to provide an overview of the event mechanics, the significance of Crimson Moonlights and Stardust, and strategic advice on maximizing your returns from the event.

## Event Overview

To participate in the Primal Pinball event, players need Pearls of Finding, which are purchasable in the game shop. The primary rewards from this event are Crimson Moonlights and Stardust, essential for upgrading portrait levels and enhancing the power and appearance of your Chaos Immortals.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-43-1024x321.png)

### Crimson Moonlights and Stardust

- **Crimson Moonlights**: These are premium items used specifically for upgrading portrait levels on Chaos Immortals, increasing their stats and overall effectiveness in battles.
- **Stardust**: This resource is also used for enhancing portrait levels, although it might serve a more general purpose across different types of immortals or in-game enhancements.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-44-1024x484.png)

## Event Mechanics and Chances

The Primal Pinball event offers a variety of rewards with different probabilities:

- **Yellow Tier 4 Rewards**: There's a 5% chance to land on this tier, rewarding players with 4x Crimson Moonlights. Given this probability, on average, you would need 500 Pearls to obtain 100 Crimson Moonlights.
- **Stardust Fields**: These have a slightly higher chance of 6.8% for players to land on, providing another avenue to gather essential resources.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-45-1024x499.png)

## Strategic Spending for Maximum Efficiency

Given the structure of bundle prices and the probabilities for obtaining rewards, strategic investment is crucial:

- The $5 bundle provides exceptional value, offering 3.6 Pearls per dollar, making it the most cost-efficient option.
- The value decreases with higher-priced bundles, with the $15 bundle yielding 2 Pearls per dollar, and further diminishing returns for the $30 bundle and beyond.

For those playing the long game and focusing on efficiency, combining the $5 and $15 bundles for a total of $30 provides 48 Pearls, equating to roughly 10 Crimson Moonlights.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-48-1024x652.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/image-50-1024x579.png)

## Conclusion

The Primal Pinball event is a long and potentially expensive endeavor tailored towards players willing to invest significantly to enhance their Chaos Immortals. The key to maximizing your investment lies in strategic spending, focusing on the more cost-effective bundles to gather Pearls of Finding. While the event offers a path to obtaining valuable Crimson Moonlights and Stardust, players should approach with a plan for resource allocation to ensure the best return on their investment in upgrading portrait levels. Remember, patience and strategic planning are essential in navigating the cost-intensive landscape of the Primal Pinball event.

title: Prosperity Explained – Production Penalty, Bonus Tiers, Recovery and When
summary: Prosperity decides how much your territory produces and how close you
markdown:
![Prosperity Explained – IK Wiki guide](/uploads/screenshot-20261126-213408-6d5ksu.png)

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261127-091934-81cbz6.png)

Prosperity is one of those systems most players ignore until the day their castle suddenly flies across the map. It sits quietly in your Territory Info, but it controls how much your territory produces, how close you are to being zeroed, and how many gems you will burn if you panic-restore it in the middle of a fight.

This guide puts everything about Prosperity in one place: where to find it, what it actually does, how you lose it, how it comes back, and when gemming it is worth it.

## Where to Find Your Prosperity

Tap your Castle and open **Territory Info**. At the top you will see your kingdom's unique ability (on my kingdom Ruslan that is *Cavalry HP +5%*), and below it the Prosperity panel. The panel shows three things:

* **Current Territorial Resource Production Speed** – how much of your normal production you are actually getting
* **Current / Max Prosperity** – your Prosperity bar
* **Recovering Speed** – how much Prosperity you regain per hour

The blue **+** next to the bar is the gem restore button. More on that further down.

![Territory Info showing Prosperity at 1 / 60,690 and production speed at 43%](/uploads/screenshot-20261126-214721-7ffhrj.webp)

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261127-091943-v21uvo.png)

## The Rules

The game's own details page lists five rules. In plain words:

1. **Your Castle level sets your maximum Prosperity.** The higher the Castle, the higher the cap.
2. **You lose Prosperity when your territory is attacked and your defense fails.**
3. **At 0 Prosperity you are relocated to a random location**, and a Protection Barrier opens automatically for a while.
4. **Low Prosperity cuts your territory's resource production**, but Gold production from Dwellings is not affected.
5. **Gemming Prosperity back to full gets more expensive each time you do it.** The cost resets daily at UTC 0:00.

## Prosperity Bonus Tiers

High Prosperity does not just protect you, it also boosts your resource production:

| Prosperity | Resource Production Increase |
| ---------- | ---------------------------- |
| 5,000      | +2%                          |
| 15,000     | +4%                          |
| 30,000     | +6%                          |
| 40,000     | +8%                          |
| 50,000     | +10%                         |
| 60,000     | +12%                         |

My Castle 57 caps at **60,690 Prosperity**, just above the 60,000 threshold for the final +12% tier. Lower castles have lower caps, so check which tier your own cap actually reaches before you assume you get the full bonus.

![In-game Prosperity details and bonus tier table](/uploads/screenshot-20261126-214312-rw6v9s.webp)

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261127-091948-g8b44o.png)

## The Production Penalty

This is the part most people miss. Here is my castle at the time of writing, sitting at **1 / 60,690 Prosperity**:

* Current Territorial Resource Production Speed: **43% (100% − 57%)**

In other words, near zero Prosperity my territory produces less than half of what it normally would. Food, Wood, Stone and Iron all take the hit. Gold from Dwellings does not.

Swing that around and you get the real value of Prosperity for a farmer: the gap between a castle at the bottom and a castle at full Prosperity is the difference between 43% production and 100% production **plus** a 12% bonus on top.

If you bank hundreds of millions of resources and mostly fight, this barely matters. If you rely on your territory and gathering to fund upgrades, it matters a lot.

## How You Lose Prosperity

**Failed defenses.** Every lost fight at your walls costs Prosperity. The amount depends on how badly you lose: a loss to a much stronger army with many troops dead costs more than a narrow loss. There is a cap on how much you can lose in a single attack, and that cap depends on your Walls level.

**Legion of Frostborne.** Castles sitting in the snow outside a Thermal Zone lose Prosperity over time. During **Sleet** weather, territories outside a Thermal Zone lose Prosperity 50% faster. A Protection Barrier stops the Sleet drain. My castle is parked in the snow on the Legion map right now, which is exactly why it reads 1 Prosperity and **0/hour** recovery.

![Castle sitting in the snow on the Legion of Frostborne map](/uploads/screenshot-20261126-215116-yiwpfa.webp)

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261127-091952-m2mto4.png)

**Last Stand.** The Last Stand talent adds a strong damage boost to your army, but it comes at a Prosperity cost. Great in a close fight, risky if you are already low.

**Sparring and Squad Survival.** Alliance Sparring uses normal combat rules, so Prosperity loss still applies (territory resources are never lost, though). In Squad Survival, standing in lava drains Prosperity fast, and you cannot gem it back there.

## What Happens at Zero

When Prosperity hits 0:

* A short timer starts, and when it ends your castle flies to a random location.
* A Protection Barrier opens automatically.
* **Second Wind** triggers, and you receive a resource package based mostly on the troops you lost since your last zeroing.

Being zeroed is not always a disaster. Some players deliberately let Prosperity fall to 1 and then get zeroed on purpose to cash in Second Wind. See [Understanding Second Wind](/posts/understanding-second-wind) for how that works.

## How Prosperity Comes Back

Outside of combat zones, Prosperity recovers on its own at the rate shown under **Recovering Speed**. You can speed that up with:

* **"King of the Supreme" Territory Decoration** – increases Prosperity recovery speed
* **Paradeisos Castle Skin** – +5% Prosperity Recovery Speed
* **Capital cabinet position** – a Governor can appoint a position worth +30% Prosperity regeneration speed
* **Sturdy** (Legion of Frostborne skill) – extra Prosperity recovery during Legion

## Gemming Prosperity: When It's Worth It

Tap the **+** on the Prosperity bar and the game offers a full restore for gems. My quote at 1 / 60,690 was **1,097 gems** to go all the way back to max. Since patch 2.8.6 the price climbs with every restore you do on the same day and only resets at UTC 0:00, so the old trick of gemming back to full again and again during a fight gets very expensive very fast.

![Gem restore prompt: 1,097 gems to recover to max Prosperity](/uploads/screenshot-20261126-214101-lzg0o7.webp)

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261127-091956-2pwlqb.png)

**Gem it when:**

* You are holding an important position (a frontline castle in Legion, a garrison next to an objective) and getting zeroed would remove you from the fight.
* You need your territory production back for a long farming stretch and you are not planning to fight in the next day or two.

**Don't gem it when:**

* You are about to be hit again by a much stronger player. You will just pay to lose it twice.
* You want to be zeroed for Second Wind.
* You are playing a low-Prosperity raiding style where being ported to new hunting grounds is the point.
* You are in Illusion Battlefield, where gemming Prosperity is disabled anyway.

A better habit than gemming in a panic: if you are frontline and dropping low, swap position with a healthier teammate. A weakened player behind the lines can still help with rallies and garrisons.

## Quick Summary

* Check Prosperity in Castle → Territory Info.
* Bonus tiers go from +2% at 5,000 up to +12% at 60,000.
* Near zero, my production dropped to 43%. Gold from Dwellings is never affected.
* You lose it from failed defenses (capped per attack by Walls level), Legion snow and Sleet, and Last Stand.
* At zero you relocate, get a barrier and trigger Second Wind.
* Gem restores get more expensive with each use and reset at UTC 0:00, so save gems for moments where staying in place actually matters.

Related guides:

* [Understanding Second Wind](/posts/understanding-second-wind)
* [How to Protect Troops and Resources from Defeats](/posts/how-to-protect-troops-and-resources-from-defeats)
* [Legion of Frostborne Weather System Guide](/posts/legion-of-frostborne-weather-system-guide)
* [Patch 2.8.6 – New Skills, Putting an End to Endless Whale-Gemming and More](/posts/patch-2-8-6---new-skills-putting-an-end-to-endless-whale-gemming-and-more)

title: Psionic Vortex
markdown:
![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261001-181503-50u6zt.png)

## 💠Table of Contents

* Psionic Vortex Skill Effect
* Damage Scaling by Level
* How the Stacks Work
* Why Horus Is the Natural Carrier
* Other Potential Carriers
* Skill Synergies
* Limitations and Unconfirmed Interactions
* How to Unlock and Upgrade Psionic Vortex
* Is Psionic Vortex Worth Building?
* Summary

## 💠TL;DR

Psionic Vortex increases the carrier’s Magical Damage whenever their HP decreases by 10% or an Ultimate Skill is cast. At Level 8, each stack grants 30% Magical Damage and the five-stack maximum reaches 150%.

Horus appears specifically designed to use it. His high Energy Regeneration helps him cast frequently, while Royal Sarcophagus prevents individual attacks from bursting him down before Psionic Vortex has time to scale. The likely high-end setup is **Energy Mastery, Infinite Firepower and Psionic Vortex**, creating a durable magical carry whose damage continues rising throughout the battle.

The skill is unlocked through the Legendary Season Wisdom Well using Wisdom Elixirs. It costs **300 Elixirs to unlock** and **1,200 Elixirs to reach Level 8**.

## 💠Psionic Vortex Skill Effect

Psionic Vortex is a passive Legendary Tower of Knowledge skill with the following effect:

> When your HP decreases by 10% or an Ultimate Skill is cast, increase your Magical Damage by 9%, stacking up to five times.

The percentage increases by three points with each skill level, eventually reaching 30% per stack at Level 8. The current in-game card also displays a ranged-position restriction and recommends Horus and Cleopatra as potential carriers.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261001-181524-e3kljt.png)

Unlike skills that increase only Ultimate Skill Damage, Psionic Vortex increases **Magical Damage**. This is much broader because it can strengthen the carrier’s magical output from their Ultimate as well as magical damage produced by their equipped Tower of Knowledge skills.

It begins the battle without any bonus, however. The carrier must actively generate stacks before receiving the full benefit.

## 💠Damage Scaling by Level

This progression is important when deciding whether Psionic Vortex must be completely maxed before it becomes useful. Even at Level 4, three stacks provide 54% Magical Damage and the completed effect reaches 90%. At Level 6, only two stacks are required to reach a 48% increase.

The skill therefore does not suddenly become useful at the fifth stack. Every stage of the buildup matters.



A useful comparison is **Concentration**, which provides a permanent 30% Magical Damage increase at Level 8. A maxed Psionic Vortex reaches the same bonus with its first stack, doubles it with the second and can eventually reach five times the amplification. Concentration remains more reliable at the opening of a battle, but Psionic Vortex has a vastly higher ceiling.

## 💠How Does Psionic Vortex Build Stacks?

Psionic Vortex has two separate triggering conditions:

1. The carrier’s HP decreases by 10%.
2. An Ultimate Skill is cast.

This gives the skill two possible sources of momentum. A fast-casting Immortal can generate stacks through Ultimate cycles, while an Immortal under pressure can build additional stacks through HP loss.

In practice, the two mechanics should work together. The carrier may lose 10% HP, gain a stack, cast an Ultimate for another stack and continue building from both conditions as the battle develops. This potentially allows Psionic Vortex to reach its maximum considerably faster than a skill relying exclusively on repeated Ultimate casts.

There are still some details that require proper battle testing. The English description says “an Ultimate Skill is cast” rather than explicitly stating “when you cast your Ultimate Skill.” Current analysis assumes that this refers to the equipped Immortal, but the wording leaves room for testing.

We also need to confirm exactly how the HP condition tracks damage. The most likely interpretation is that the skill counts cumulative reductions equal to 10% of maximum HP, but healing and repeated HP loss could affect how quickly those thresholds are reached. These interactions will be particularly important in sustain formations.

## 💠Why Horus Appears Designed for Psionic Vortex

Horus is the most obvious carrier and appears almost purpose-built for the skill.

His unusually high native Energy Regeneration, reportedly around **153**, should allow him to reach his Ultimate quickly and continue casting regularly during longer battles. Every completed cycle contributes another Psionic Vortex stack while also applying his Magical Damage and Punishment effect.

The other half of the interaction comes from **Royal Sarcophagus**. Horus limits how much HP he can lose from an individual instance of damage, protecting him against the enormous burst attacks that have defined much of the recent meta.

Psionic Vortex wants its carrier to experience HP loss, but it also needs that carrier to survive. Horus can take repeated damage and build toward the HP trigger without being removed by one enormous hit. This gives him time to accumulate stacks through both damage received and Ultimate casts.

Once the effect is developed, Horus becomes an increasingly difficult problem. He is hard to burst, continues applying Punishment across the enemy formation and gains more Magical Damage as the fight progresses.

The most aggressive version of this build is likely:

* **Energy Mastery**
* **Infinite Firepower**
* **Psionic Vortex**

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261001-181658-hsl574.png)

Energy Mastery helps Horus reach his Ultimate more quickly, Infinite Firepower adds further scaling and Psionic Vortex rewards every additional cycle. In a sustain-heavy formation capable of protecting and healing him, this creates the possibility of an extremely durable magical carry whose damage continues climbing rather than declining during a long battle.

## 💠Other Potential Carriers

The in-game recommendations currently show **Horus and Cleopatra**. Cleopatra provides an accessible magical carrier and naturally benefits from any effect that increases her total Magical Damage, but the real question is how quickly she can generate stacks compared with Horus.

Medusa may be another extremely interesting candidate. Her Ultimate already possesses exceptional damage scaling, and Psionic Vortex could make later casts considerably stronger once the first stacks have been established. The main uncertainty is whether giving her Psionic Vortex produces more value than the established skill combinations supporting her current meta build.

Other ranged magical carries may also use the skill effectively, particularly if they combine strong Energy Regeneration with enough survivability to remain active throughout longer battles. However, Psionic Vortex should not automatically be placed on whichever Immortal has the highest Magical Attack. Stack generation and survival matter just as much as the carrier’s initial attributes.

An Immortal reaching four stacks consistently may use the skill better than a more explosive carrier who dies after reaching only one or two.

## 💠Skill and Formation Synergies

Psionic Vortex naturally works with three broader mechanics: energy generation, magical amplification and sustain.

**Energy Mastery** helps the carrier cast more frequently, potentially accelerating both stack generation and Ultimate damage. **Infinite Firepower** provides additional offensive scaling for builds designed around repeated Ultimate cycles, while **Corrosive Power** can contribute damage and improve pressure against the enemy formation.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261001-181847-2cyhbl.png)

**Heart of Arcana**, when carried elsewhere in the march, can provide another layer of Magical Damage amplification without occupying one of the Psionic Vortex carrier’s own skill slots.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261001-181910-sa4q92.png)

Healing, shields and damage mitigation are equally important. Psionic Vortex benefits from HP loss, but losing HP only creates value if the carrier remains alive long enough to use the resulting stacks. Hyper-sustain formations may therefore be the best environment for the skill, especially when built around Horus.

## 💠The Limitations Behind the 150% Number

Psionic Vortex should not be described as a permanent 150% Magical Damage increase. That is its maximum potential after five successful triggers.

In a short battle, the carrier may reach only one or two stacks before the result has already been decided. In that situation, an immediate damage skill or an always-active effect may provide more practical value.

The fifth stack can also arrive too late. Reaching 150% Magical Damage during the final seconds of a battle is very different from reaching it while several Ultimate cycles remain.

There is also an opportunity cost. Psionic Vortex occupies one of only three Tower of Knowledge skill slots. Even if the skill produces an enormous personal damage increase, players must compare that output with alternative damage, control, energy or survival skills that could occupy the same position.

Horus is likely to reduce several of these weaknesses because he combines rapid Energy generation with exceptional anti-burst protection. For other Immortals, the ramp-up period may be much more noticeable.

## 💠How to Unlock Psionic Vortex

Psionic Vortex is a Legendary Season Chaos skill obtained through the **Wisdom Well**. Unlike Epic or Cinder Shop skills, its Ability Stones are purchased using **Wisdom Elixirs**.

Each Psionic Vortex Ability Stone costs **5 Wisdom Elixirs**.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261001-181942-7bdd8a.png)

Unlocking the skill requires 60 stones:

**60 stones × 5 Elixirs = 300 Wisdom Elixirs**

Legendary skills have eight levels, with the following stone requirements:

Fully upgrading Psionic Vortex therefore requires:

**240 stones × 5 Elixirs = 1,200 Wisdom Elixirs**

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261001-181924-12uigg.png)

The current Wisdom Well provides a 3% chance to receive 20 Wisdom Elixirs, with a guaranteed jackpot on the 40th Wish if one has not appeared earlier. There is also a 2% chance to receive 5 Elixirs. Under this system, unlocking one Legendary skill takes approximately **323 Wishes on average**, while reaching Level 8 requires roughly **1,290 Wishes on average**, although individual results will vary.

Players should therefore view Psionic Vortex as a major account investment rather than a skill picked up casually during one Wisdom Well rotation.

## 💠Is Psionic Vortex Worth Building?

For a developed Horus main march, Psionic Vortex looks like one of the most important skills to acquire. Horus directly addresses the skill’s greatest weakness by surviving long enough to build its stacks, while his high Energy Regeneration provides another reliable path toward the maximum.

For Medusa or other magical carries, the answer is more account-specific. The damage ceiling remains enormous, but players must consider battle duration, Energy cycles and which existing skill would have to be removed.

This is not necessarily a universal skill that belongs on every magical Immortal. It is a scaling carry skill, and its value depends on whether the formation can create enough time for that scaling to matter.

Players with limited Wisdom Elixirs should prioritise the skill only if it has a clear place in their main march. Unlocking Psionic Vortex simply because 150% looks impressive may leave you with an expensive Level 1 skill and no settled carrier. A completed Horus sustain build is a very different investment case from purchasing the skill speculatively for a secondary team.

## 💠Summary

Psionic Vortex is one of the most ambitious Magical Damage skills introduced to the Tower of Knowledge. At Level 8, it can progress from 30% to 150% increased Magical Damage as the carrier loses HP and casts Ultimate Skills.

Horus is the natural carrier because Royal Sarcophagus protects him from the burst damage that would normally threaten a scaling mage, while his high Energy Regeneration helps him build stacks through repeated Ultimate casts. Cleopatra is recommended by the game as another option, while Medusa and other ranged magical carries deserve further testing.

The skill’s ceiling is enormous, but its real performance will be determined by stack speed, battle length and survivability. If Horus can reach five stacks early and consistently, Psionic Vortex may become one of the defining Legendary skills of the new magical sustain meta.

title: Purification
summary: n the realm of Infinity Kingdom, where strategy and skill intertwine, the \"Purification\" ability emerges as a unique and nuanced skill that can significantly influence the tide of battles. This premium skill, obtainable…
markdown:
### Infinity Kingdom Guide: Understanding and Utilizing the "Purification" Skill

n the realm of Infinity Kingdom, where strategy and skill intertwine, the "Purification" ability emerges as a unique and nuanced skill that can significantly influence the tide of battles. This premium skill, obtainable at the Tower of Knowledge level 38 and available in the Triss Blessing Event shop, represents more than just a tactical advantage; it embodies the historical concept of cleansing and renewal.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/image-94-1024x629.png)

### Mechanics of Purification

In the broader scope of Infinity Kingdom's gameplay, Purification is not just a skill to be used; it's a skill to be mastered. Understanding its intricacies, from its dispel capabilities to its healing nuances, can elevate your gameplay, making you not just a player but a strategist.

- **Trigger and Targeting**: The skill activates swiftly with a 3-second trigger and randomly targets a team member. Its primary function is to clear any debuffs or abnormal effects from the targeted immortal. If no such effects are present, it provides a small amount of healing.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/image-93-1024x599.png)

- **Dispel Abilities**: Purification does not address control effects like Freeze, Stun, or continuous damage types, including Mental Decay. However, it's highly effective against stat alterations like Wound, Attack speed decrease, Energy regen decrease, and increased damage taken. The skill can clear multiple debuffs in a single trigger. You can despell control effects as well as wounds using this skill making it highly effective and sought after for many builds.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/image-92.png)

- **Healing Aspect**: The healing part of Purification is based on the HP of the source and has a recovery rate of 160%. This rate, though modest, ensures consistent healing with each activation.
- **Synergy**: Beyond all the valuable aspects of the skill itself, it has further value for you as a result of its synergy with the skill Wine and Dine. As one of the most frequent healing skills you can get high uptime on Wine and Dine buffs by pairing it with Purification. Very powerful and worth consideration.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/image-91-1024x560.png)

### Strategic Use of Purification

- **Ideal Users**: The skill is best utilized by a support immortal because you will get value from the healing aspect in this way. However, because the healing in raw numbers is not incredibly large, you can also run this just for the despell mechanic on a utility or control based immortal (e.g. Trajan, Cyrus, Tokugawa, Qin or others). For maximizing the healing potential, it's recommended to be used by a backliner rather than a frontliner, whose HP is usually lower.
- **Contextual Relevance**: In the current meta of Infinity Kingdom, Purification is almost a necessity for top-tier teams, especially those using Hybrid Earth/Wind compositions due to the prevalence of Weakening Curse and No Escape. However, for other team types, its necessity may vary.

**Conclusion**
While Purification is a valuable skill in Infinity Kingdom, its effectiveness and necessity are contingent on the specific team compositions and the current game meta. Understanding its mechanics and strategic deployment can enhance your gameplay experience significantly. As you delve deeper into the art of war within Infinity Kingdom, Purification stands as a testament to the game's rich strategic fabric, offering a blend of historical lore and tactical gameplay that continually challenges and rewards its players.

title: Purple Crystal - Maximum Efficiency
summary: Purple Crystals are the most sought after ressource in Infinity Kingdom, simply because you need a metrix ton in order to max out passives on all of your Immortals.
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/Blog-Feature.jpg)

## Most important ressource in Infinity Kingdom

Purple Crystals are the most sought after ressource in Infinity Kingdom, simply because you need a metrix ton in order to max out passives on all of your Immortals.

In this article we shall go over how many crystals you will need, how to get them and most importantly - the most efficient way to obtain them.

## Passive Upgrade Costs

|  | Uncommon | Rare | Elite | Epic |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| lvl 1 (Unlock) | 500 | 2,000 | 8,000 | 20,000 |
| lvl 2 | 720 | 840 | 960 | 1,200 |
| lvl 3 | 1,440 | 1,680 | 1,920 | 2,400 |
| lvl 4 | 2,880 | 3,360 | 3,840 | 4,800 |
| lvl 5 | 4,000 | 6,300 | 7,200 | 9,000 |
| lvl 6 | 10,800 | 12,600 | 1,400 | 18,000 |
| lvl 7 |  | 25,200 | 28,800 | 36,000 |
| lvl 8 |  | 32,000 | 57,600 | 72,000 |
| Total | 20,340 | 83,980 | 109,720 | 163,400 |

Upgrading even just a single march with elite/epic passives will quickly cost you upwards of **2 million purple crystals** (1,960,800).

So how do we earn this high demand ressource? There are many ways of obtaining them, but in the end they come from either destroying immortal fragments or looting in specific events.

### There are many interesting sources of purple crystals:

1. [**Harbor/sailing**](#sail)
2. **[Summons](#summ)**
3. **[Arena Shop](#arena)**
4. **[Mysterium](#mysterium)**
5. **[Contention of Relics Shop](#cor)**
6. **[Legion of Frostborne (SvS) Shop](#svs)**
7. **[Wheel of Fortune](#wheel)**
8. **[Redeem Events](#redeem)**
9. **[Rebel Event](#rebel)**

I know there are many more events that yield immortal fragments, however I will try and go through the most interesting ones that provide the best yields and/or are the ones where you have to choose to spend a game currency in exchange for Fragments or Philosopher Stones. **Knowing which rewards to purchase in an events is crucial to your efficiency.**

## Harbor

The harbor is a great way to earn steady Crystals, and you should **ALWAYS keep your ship sailing.**

There is not much to say about the Harbor, just note that it is a very efficient way to obtain crystals and should be kept going at alle times with no downtime. Go on long sails if you can, but key is to minimize downtime. Simply use 3h, 6h and 12h journeys to best match your windows of playtime.

## Summoning with Philosopher stones

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/贤者之石完整.png)

While you can also summon with the small philosopher stone, the most common summon is the advanced summon which uses the large stones seen on the right here.

You should always save up and summon 9x cost mass summon actually summons 10x giving you 10% cost efficiency. Do remember to use your daily free advanced single summon.

I have been recording my last**513 philosopher stones across 57 mass advanced summons** in an attempt to figure out the **value**of philosopher stones in terms of purple crystals (*If you are interested in the data, you can scroll down and find it on page 2 of this article*).

The average purple crystal value of a single 9x mass summon is =**4,642.86 crystals**

Philosopher Stones can be bought in multiple ways, and gems can be spent in multiplem ways. But we can buy an infinite amount of Philosopher Stones with Gems for 300 each. This means we can calculate the conversion rate of Philosopher Stones to Purple Crystals at a rate of **1:515.88**.

Because we can buy an infinite amount of Philosopher Stones in the Gemshop at 300 gems each, this furthermore means that we can convert to purple crystals at a rate of**1:1.72**.

## Arena Shop

The arena seasons earn you a reward based on your placement (search for the article regarding arena for more info). Besides the seasonal reward, you earn War Insignia with every win and earn daily chests by gaining Victory Points as you win each day. You can gain a total of 100 + 160 + 240 + 300 = 800 War Insignia from daily chests, to unlock these chests you have to win 20x victory points base and in doing so you will earn 10*20=200 War Insignia.

If you cap daily Victory Points, you will earn a total of 1,000 War Insignia every day. With these Insignia you can purchase Epic Immortal Fragments at a price of 200 Insignia each, i.e. **100 Purple Crystals per 200 War Insignia**.

**Via the arena you can earn a total of 500 Purple Crystals / day** + seasonal reward. This is a great steady way of gaining crystals.

## Mysterium

Mysterium is a good place to get ressources and should always be completed before it resets (2 day timer). Rewards from the Mysterium varies both on your luck but also based on the level you are able to complete. There are 2 base floors to complete, then you can choose either normal mode or hardmode for the 3rd floor plus the Evernight Labyrinth (4th). The loot per is greater if you are able to complete hardmode. But either way, the Mysterium drops a lot of gold and speedups and should always be played out. Read more about mysterium in the dedicated article or in the article on gold farming.

In terms of Purple Crystals, an average clear on hardmode will yield around 20 Epic Immortal Fragments = **2.000 Purple Crystals**.

## Contention of Relics Shop

The Shop for Contention of Relics offers multiple options of Immortal Fragments. The purchase options are different based on your Factions Ranking in CoR and come at a varied cost. Luckily, min. 1 option of the cheapest Epic Immortal Fragment is available at any rank. Moreover, the shop offer Philosopher stones! These rewards can be purchased with Valor Marks (read the article on CoR for more info).

We know from the above that Philosopher stones are worth 515.88 Purple Crystals and Epic Immortal Fragments are worth 100 Purple Crystals. Reward efficiency is as follows:

| 1 x Purchase of Reward | Value in Purple Crystals | Cost in Valor Marks | 1x Purple Crystal cost inValor Marks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Expensive Epic Immortal fragment | 100 | 2000 | 20 |
| Medium Epic Immortal fragment | 100 | 1800 | 18 |
| Cheap Epic Immortal fragment | 100 | 1500 | 15 |
| Philosopher Stone | 515,88 | 4500 | 8,7 |

As you can see, purchaseing Philosopher Stones are nearly 2x as efficient as the cheapest Epic Immortal Fragment and near 3x more efficient than the expensive option. **Conclusion: You should always purchase Philosopher stones first**.

## Legion of Frostborne (SvS)

I do not have enought data on the Ancient Remnant Lootboxes available after the Legion of Frostborne to make an educated guess as to the drop rate of Epic Immortal Fragments from these chests. Moreover, with the introduction of new ToS Passive Skills with Patch 1.8 Ability Stones will be a must-purchase for everyone. As such, I will not go into much detail with SvS as a source of Purple Crystals besides stating that it can be a very good source of Philosopher Stones, as the stones are very cheap here. **Only 300 Points per Stone, meaning you will get avg. value = 5,158.83 Purple Crystals** if you purchase all the stones.

More will be added as the first real seasons of SvS plays out. To be continued!

## Wheel of Fortune

For more information on the Badge Redeem Events, see the dedicated article on this topic.

In terms of Purple Crystals, the **wheel should NOT be used to gain Crystals**.

*Why have I chosen to include this you ask? Because a lot of people have been mistakenly giving out the advice for players to spend gems on clearing the Wheel of Fortune Twice in order to earn maximum Purple Crystals from the event. While it is true that the event is most efficiently played by clearing only twice, the conversion rate of Gems to Purple Crystals are horribly low.*

You can gain a maximum efficiency of 14,700 Purple Crystals by clearing the wheel twice. This costs you a total of 14.000 Gems in spins = **0.95 Purple Crystals per Gem**.

Significantly lower than Summoning, read above.

## Redeem Events

For more information on the Badge Redeem Events, see the dedicated article on this topic.

This event is a good source of Purple Crystals. By redeeming the badges you have earned, you can purchase Epic Immortal Fragments and Philosopher Stones. Please see the table below for the costs, value and efficiencies of this event:

| Coin Cost | Purchase Item | Value in Purple Crystal | Coin : Purple Crystal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 100 | 1 Epic | 100 | 1:1 |
| 50 | 1 Elite | 50 | 1:1 |
| 300 | 1 Philosopher Stone | 515.88 | 1:1.72 |

The Philosopher Stone is by far the most efficient item to purchase during this event. **This means you should ALWAYS purchase all 10x Philosopher Stones before you move into the Immortal Fragments.**It is also worth mentioning that the Fragments' conversion rates are identical.
