markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-102-1024x576.png)

## Yawgmoth's Spider Boss Build Guide - the Strongest Boss Build Currently in Infinity Kingdom

## Introduction

Finding a truly exceptional boss march in *Infinity Kingdom* is surprisingly rare. Many builds can produce respectable numbers, but only a handful genuinely push the limits of the game's damage mechanics.

This build, created by **Yawgmoth**, is one of those rare exceptions.

Rather than stacking raw Attack or relying on a single powerful immortal, the composition layers nearly every independent damage multiplier available in the game. Physical Damage Dealt, Physical Damage Taken, All Damage Dealt, All Damage Taken, Ultimate Skill Damage, Critical Rate, Energy Regeneration and multiple below-50% damage effects all work together to create one of the highest sustained single-target damage profiles currently possible.

The results speak for themselves. Against the Level 101 Titanula, Yoshitsune comfortably exceeded **one billion total damage**, while the entire march consistently delivered some of the highest boss damage numbers seen to date.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-101-1024x620.png)

If your goal is maximizing damage against Titanula, Melanthios or other single-target PvE bosses, this is one of the strongest physical compositions currently available.

---

## Team Composition

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-103-1024x164.png)

Every immortal has a clearly defined role. Rather than maximizing individual damage across the entire team, this composition focuses on empowering Yoshitsune and Tutankhamun while ensuring Khubilai Khan maintains his powerful debuffs throughout the encounter.

---

## Why This Build Works

The strength of this march comes from layering multiple independent damage modifiers instead of stacking a single offensive stat.

Throughout the battle, the team simultaneously applies:

- Physical Damage Dealt
- Physical Damage Taken
- All Damage Dealt
- All Damage Taken
- Ultimate Skill Damage
- Critical Rate
- Energy Regeneration
- Below 50% HP damage bonuses
- Dragon damage amplification

Because these effects belong to different damage categories, they multiply together instead of suffering heavy diminishing returns.

As the fight progresses, more of these bonuses become active. Once the boss drops below 50% HP, Yoshitsune's innate damage increase, Fear of Domination and Shadow Dragon all come online together, creating an enormous burst window that allows the team's damage to skyrocket.

---

## Skill Setup

The following setup is the standard version of the build and is recommended if you have access to all of the required skills.

| Immortal | Skills |
| --- | --- |
| Yoshitsune | Energy Mastery , Growl , Anger |
| Mathilda | Weakness , Fountain of Life , Wine and Dine |
| Tutankhamun | Corrosive Power , Time to Shine , Implosion |
| Khubilai Khan | Fear of Domination , Guard , Lightning Strike |

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-104.png)

### Alternative Setup

For bosses with heavy reflected damage, Khubilai Khan can instead run:

- **Absolute Defense**
- **Life Link**

This version sacrifices a small amount of damage in exchange for significantly better survivability. While slightly suboptimal compared to the default setup, it remains a perfectly viable alternative if you lack some of the recommended skills or need additional protection against reflect damage.

---

## Immortal Breakdown

## Mathilda

Mathilda is the support engine that makes the entire march possible.

Her role is not to deal damage. Instead, she continuously supplies **Energy Regeneration** while providing powerful offensive buffs that increase the damage of Yoshitsune, Tutankhamun and Khubilai Khan.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-105.png)

More frequent ultimate casts allow Khubilai Khan to maintain maximum debuff stacks while enabling Yoshitsune and Tutankhamun to spend far more of the battle using their strongest abilities.

Without Mathilda, the team's entire damage rotation slows considerably, making her one of the most important immortals in the composition.

---

## Khubilai Khan

Khubilai Khan provides one of the strongest boss debuffs available.

His ultimate applies **Physical Damage Taken**, stacking up to **90% increased Physical Damage Taken** after reaching three stacks.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-106.png)

Since both Yoshitsune and Tutankhamun deal almost exclusively physical damage, maintaining these stacks throughout the encounter is essential. Few skills contribute more to the team's overall damage.

---

## Tutankhamun

Tutankhamun provides reliable sustained physical damage from start to finish.

While Yoshitsune delivers the massive burst windows, Tutankhamun continuously contributes high single-target damage while benefiting from every offensive buff and debuff applied by the team.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-107.png)

His consistent output makes him the ideal secondary damage dealer for long PvE encounters.

---

## Yoshitsune

Yoshitsune is the centerpiece of the entire composition.

His damage scales exceptionally well in boss encounters because his ultimate gains **50% increased damage once the target falls below 50% HP**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-108.png)

This mechanic rarely reaches its full potential in PvP, where battles often end before the bonus becomes relevant. Against Titanula and other world bosses, however, the fight continues well into the second half, allowing Yoshitsune to repeatedly unleash empowered ultimates.

Combined with Khubilai Khan's Physical Damage Taken debuff, Shadow Dragon's damage amplification and the build's many offensive multipliers, Yoshitsune's damage climbs rapidly.

In Yawgmoth's battle reports, Yoshitsune exceeded **one billion total damage**, making him the clear star of the composition.

---

## Skill Synergies

Every skill in this build has been chosen to strengthen the team's overall damage profile. Rather than stacking the same statistic repeatedly, each skill contributes a different multiplier that combines with the others.

## Energy Mastery

Energy Mastery is one of the core skills of the build.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-109.png)

Every time Yoshitsune casts his ultimate, Energy Mastery restores additional energy while increasing his damage output. This creates a positive feedback loop that allows him to reach subsequent ultimate casts more quickly while amplifying every cast.

---

## Growl

Growl provides one of the strongest temporary offensive buffs available.

Its burst window pairs exceptionally well with Yoshitsune's devastating ultimate, allowing him to capitalize on every major damage phase throughout the encounter.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-118.png)

The downside to Growl's massive damage buff, is that it also lowers initial energy by 100. However, for Yoshi we are mostly reliant on massive damage once we hit the 50% HP treshold on the boss meaning the initial slower ramp-up is perfectly acceptable.

---

## Anger

Anger further strengthens Yoshitsune's already exceptional offensive output.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-119.png)

Since Yoshitsune contributes the overwhelming majority of the team's damage, dedicating another offensive skill slot to him produces excellent returns over the course of the fight.

---

## Weakness

Weakness is one of the strongest aura skills available for dedicated boss hunting.

Rather than directly increasing damage, it significantly boosts the **Critical Rate** of every immortal in the march. Since world bosses have relatively low **Resilience**, the additional Critical Rate translates into an exceptionally high critical hit chance throughout the encounter.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-116.png)

This is particularly valuable for Yoshitsune and Tutankhamun, whose damage scales extremely well with critical hits. In Yawgmoth's battle reports, Yoshitsune's **Total Conquest** landed as a critical hit **95% of the time** in one attempt and **80%** in another, illustrating just how effective Weakness can be against bosses.

---

## Fountain of Life

Fountain of Life is the engine that keeps **Wine and Dine** active.

Every six seconds it heals the entire march. While the healing itself is helpful, the true value comes from repeatedly triggering Wine and Dine's damage buff on every immortal.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-112.png)

The two skills work together to create one of the strongest support combinations available for PvE boss encounters.

---

## Wine and Dine

Wine and Dine 50% chance to increase an immortal's **Damage Dealt** by 30% whenever they receive healing. Note that while you will recieve the permanently wounded debuff once the spider boss hits 50% HP (which negated all healing effects on your immortals) this does not disable Wine and Dine. Wine and Dine can trigger of off attempted healing, even if that attempt is unsuccesful due to wounds debuffs.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-111.png)

Because Fountain of Life heals the entire team every six seconds, the buff is refreshed continuously throughout the encounter, providing excellent uptime on one of the team's strongest offensive effects.

---

## Corrosive Power

Corrosive Power increases **Ultimate Skill Damage**, making it an excellent choice for Tutankhamun, whose sustained damage relies heavily on repeated ultimate casts throughout the fight.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-115.png)

---

## Time to Shine

Time to Shine provides another powerful offensive boost for Tutankhamun.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-110.png)

Combined with Corrosive Power and Implosion, it allows him to maintain consistently high physical damage while Yoshitsune handles the largest burst windows.

---

## Implosion

Implosion increases **Physical Damage Dealt**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-114.png)

Because this modifier is separate from Physical Damage Taken, it stacks exceptionally well with Khubilai Khan's debuffs and substantially increases the damage of both physical DPS immortals.

---

## Fear of Domination

Fear of Domination activates once the boss drops below **50% HP**, increasing the damage enemies take by **20%**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-113.png)

Its timing perfectly matches Yoshitsune's own below-50% damage bonus, creating one of the largest offensive spikes in the entire encounter.

---

## Guard

Guard provides additional survivability for Khubilai Khan, helping ensure Tutankhammun remains alive long enough to maintain maximum Physical Damage Taken stacks for the duration of the fight.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-117.png)

---

## Lightning Strike

Lightning Strike earns its place primarily because of its debuff rather than its own damage.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-120.png)

Whenever it triggers, the boss receives **10% increased All Damage Taken**. Since this belongs to a separate damage category, it multiplies with the build's many other offensive bonuses and increases the damage dealt by every member of the march.

---

## Dragon Setup

Dragon selection is another key part of maximizing this composition's damage. You have two viable options: Fire and Shadow. Preferably you want a shadow dragon for this boss killing build, due to the reliance on below 50% HP execution. However, a shadow dragon at lower upgrade levels in terms of talents, etc. is NOT better than a fully upgraded fire dragon!

## Above 50% HP

**Fire Dragon** performs exceptionally well during the opening phase of the battle, helping Yoshitsune maximize his early damage while Khubilai Khan builds his debuff stacks.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-122-1024x573.png)

## Below 50% HP

Once the boss reaches half health, **Shadow Dragon** becomes the superior option.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-121-1024x518.png)

Its second talent perfectly complements Yoshitsune's own below-50% damage bonus, but the true highlight is **Shadow Breath**.

Shadow Breath causes the boss to take **50% increased damage for approximately 30–45 seconds**. Against Melanthios and Titanula, this window covers a significant portion of the remaining battle, allowing the team to benefit from the debuff for almost the entire final phase.

Combined with Fear of Domination, Yoshitsune's innate damage increase and the team's existing offensive multipliers, this creates an enormous finishing window that is largely responsible for the build's exceptional damage output.

---

## Placement

Correct positioning is just as important as the immortal and skill selection.

Unlike many PvE encounters, **Titanula does not deal full AoE damage**. Instead, her attacks target the **front-left immortal** and damage enemies **in a straight line** behind that target.

This allows you to control exactly which immortals take damage.

For this build, position your march as follows: Mathilda and Khubilaikhan on the **LEFT**and Tutankhamun and Yoshitsune on the **RIGHT**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-128.png)

This setup ensures that **Khubilai Khan** absorbs the boss's attacks while **Mathilda**, positioned directly behind him, shares the line damage. Meanwhile, **Tutankhamun** and **Yoshitsune** remain on the opposite side of the formation where they can deal damage uninterrupted.

Keeping your damage dealers away from the boss's attack line is particularly important because **damage decreases as troop count falls**. Every troop lost reduces an immortal's offensive output, so protecting Tutankhamun and Yoshitsune allows them to maintain maximum damage throughout the fight.

Many players assume Titanula deals full-area damage and overlook positioning entirely. In reality, taking advantage of the boss's line attack is one of the easiest ways to increase your overall damage without changing your march or skill setup.

---

## Battle Results

Yawgmoth's battle reports demonstrate just how effective this composition is.

Some highlights include:

- Yoshitsune exceeding **1 billion total damage**
- Ultimate skills accounting for more than **70% of Total Conquest damage**
- Exceptionally high critical hit rates throughout the encounter
- Consistent battle times of under one minute
- Minimal troop losses despite extraordinary offensive output

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-123.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-124-1024x621.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-125-1024x618.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-126-1024x620.png)

Perhaps most importantly, these numbers are highly consistent. The build performs so well because it relies on reliable mechanical interactions rather than favorable RNG.

---

## Player Perspective

After years of testing PvE marches, it is uncommon to find a composition that genuinely changes how boss damage is approached. Most teams simply stack more Attack or Physical Damage and rely on stronger immortals to carry the fight. Yawgmoth's build takes a far more methodical approach.

Every immortal contributes something unique. Mathilda accelerates ultimate rotations while empowering the entire team. Khubilai Khan continuously increases the boss's Physical Damage Taken. Fountain of Life and Wine and Dine maintain nearly constant Damage Dealt buffs. Weakness pushes critical hit rates to remarkably high levels against bosses with low Resilience. Shadow Dragon and Fear of Domination transform the second half of the battle into an extended burst phase that perfectly complements Yoshitsune's innate 50% ultimate damage bonus.

The result is a composition where every mechanic reinforces the others. Rather than relying on one overpowered interaction, the build achieves extraordinary damage through synergy, timing and a deep understanding of *Infinity Kingdom's* combat mechanics.

---

## Conclusion

Yawgmoth's spider boss build sets an exceptionally high benchmark for physical PvE marches in *Infinity Kingdom*. Instead of relying on raw stats alone, it combines energy generation, powerful support buffs, stacking debuffs and multiple independent damage multipliers into a composition that becomes stronger as the battle progresses.

For players looking to maximize their performance against Titanula, Melanthios and other single-target PvE bosses, this build stands as one of the most refined examples of boss optimization currently available. It demonstrates that the strongest marches are not necessarily those with the highest power, but those that make the most effective use of the game's underlying combat mechanics.

---

## New to Titanula?

Before copying a build, it's worth understanding **[how the Spider Boss actually works](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/spider-boss/strategies/understanding-the-spider-boss-combat-mechanics/)**. Titanula has several unique mechanics—including predictable targeting, line attacks, troop count scaling and a permanent **Wounded** phase—that significantly influence which immortals, skills and formations perform best.

If you're unfamiliar with these mechanics, we recommend reading our **Titanula Spider Boss Mechanics Guide** before choosing a build.

---

title: Top water build Merlin, Artemisia, Ragnar, Hippo - Best cheap build I have seen in patch 2.8.9
summary: So, water teams get clowned on a lot. Some players swear water is the weakest element, others insist it’s only weak because most people run budget setups. Honestly? The truth sits somewhere in the middle. But this…
markdown:
### Crazy Strong Water Team – The Best Budget Water Build I’ve Seen (Patch 2.8.9, Dec 2025)

So, water teams get clowned on a lot. Some players swear water is the weakest element, others insist it’s only weak because most people run budget setups. Honestly? The truth sits somewhere in the middle. But *this* specific build doesn’t just break the stereotype—it straight-up embarrasses teams it has no business defeating on paper.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-5.png)

What makes it fun is that it’s **super cheap**, incredibly consistent, and absolutely punches into big-spender territory. I’ve seen this thing win into enemy marches with **Fountain of Life**, fully maxed immortals, and some of the top tier pay-to-win Tower of Knowledge skills. When a “budget” march does that, you know it deserves its own writeup.

The whole idea revolves around a simple but nasty formula:

**damage mitigation → stable troop count on Merlin → Chill & Frostbite uptime → absurd AoE burst damage**

Let’s walk through it piece by piece.

---

## Core Mechanics Behind the Build

The build leans on three major mechanics water actually does very well when set up properly:

### 1. Energy Control

Between Hippo, Energy Suppression, and No Escape, you’re basically choking out enemy ultimates while speeding up your own.

### 2. Hard Mitigation + Tempo Denial

Resist, Chill’s attack speed slow, Hippo’s attack-speed debuffs, and the frontline talents all stack up into a march that just refuses to die long enough for Merlin to burst down the enemy.

### 3. Chill → Merlin → Frostbite Blow Synergy

This is the secret sauce. Chill isn’t just a soft debuff—it’s what unlocks Merlin’s *real* damage profile. As long as Chill is up, Merlin’s 520% AoE ultimate jumps to **780%**, which is absolutely ridiculous for a non-paywall immortal.

Put all these together and you get a march that doesn’t just scale—it detonates.

---

## Immortals & Skill Setup (With Gameplay Reasoning)

## Ragnar – Frontline Tank / Magical Amp Bot

Ragnar’s job here is *not* to survive forever… though he often does. His real value is his ultimate:

### Frostbite Blow → +30% magical damage taken for 7.5s

That buff has awesome uptime in regen builds. Your entire team is magical, so this is basically cranking Merlin’s volume.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-6.png)

### Talents:

- **Fearless Stance** – you turn Ragnar into an actual brick. The tankiness means he can stay alive to provide debuff uptime.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-7.png)

### Skills:

- **Energy Suppression** – slows enemy energy regen; pairs perfectly with Hippo's energy denial.
- **No Escape** – early silence. Swap this out only when fighting **Fountain of Life** teams (they are immune to the initial silence).
- **Resist** – magical damage reduction for your whole team. Perfect for the current mage dominated meta.

---

## Hippolyta – Disruption Queen / Off-DPS

Hippo is the backbone of the entire control plan. Her energy drain is absurd:

### 7 hits × 100 energy each = 700 energy stolen per ultimate

If you’ve fought Hippo before, you know this is disgusting. And since she reduces attack speed too, she contributes to both the regen control and the mitigation which this build leans into.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-8.png)

### Talents:

- **Destroyer Stance** – she becomes a respectable off-DPS and gets more crit, which means more procs and more damage in early fights.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-9.png)

### Skills:

- **Weakness Aura** – helps Merlin crit more reliably
- **Blessing of Rage** – boosts your immortals energy regen
- **Blessing of War** – early 12-second damage steroid to frontload Merlin’s opening burst

The main point here is: **Hippo sets the tempo.** She helps you ensure that you stay ahead in the energy-game.

---

## Artemisia – Chill Machine/ Utility Support

Arctic Storm’s **9-second Chill duration** is the longest in the game and incredibly consistent in regen builds. You need that uptime because:

### Chill = Merlin’s damage trigger

Other teams run Dido, but Dido’s Chill is RNG-based and with much lower uptimes. Artemisia ensures Merlin always has his buff window available.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-10.png)

### Skills:

- **Assist** – protects Merlin’s troop count, and that’s everything for a burst mage.
- **Malice** – helps you dampen the incomming critical hits in the current crit-centered meta.
- **Absolute Defense** – this is the one choice I also side-eye. Artemisia doesn’t need survival, she needs to stay alive to provide the debuff chill, but her troop count is not important since nothing scales off of it. You could absolutely try swapping this out for **Blessing of Defense** or even something more aggressive depending on matchup.

### Talents:

- **Battle Excitation** – the go-to support talent. It super-charges Merlin’s opening rotation, which this build fully leans into.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-11.png)

Think of Artemisia as the “glue.” Without her, Merlin damage output drops significantly.

---

## Merlin – The Carry

Let’s be real: this entire build exists to let Merlin go nuclear.

Base ultimate damage: **520%**
Damage to Chilled enemies: **780%**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-12.png)

That’s insane for a F2P-friendly immortal. And because it’s AoE, you’re hitting all four enemies for that number. When Chill + Frostbite Blow overlap, the burst is wild.

His unique artifact giving him **50 energy on every ultimate** is the cherry on top; regen builds absolutely abuse this.

### Skills:

- **Fighting Master** – protects him from control
- **Spell Disintegration** – damage and even more magic defense debuffs to stack with Ragnar
- **Annihilation** – huge raw damage, simple and effective

### Talents:

- **Stormeye** – gives the crit and damage he needs. Easy pick.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-13.png)

### Artifact:

- Crit% main
- As much crit rate as you can in secondary attribute rolls (secondaries can be rerolled)
- Annihilation bonus

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-14.png)

---

## Dragon – Water With Inspiration

This part is pretty straightforward:

**Inspiration = more energy regen**, which this entire comp is built around.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/image-15.png)

The recovery buff also stabilizes your frontline and helps keep Merlin’s troop count comfortably high.

Nothing fancy, but it’s exactly what the comp needs.

---

## Optional P2W Upgrades (If You Want to Go Crazy)

If someone wants to take this already-cheap build and turn it into a monster:

- **Energy Master** (god-tier for Merlin)
- **Psionic Tide**/**Corrosive Power**
- **Fountain of Life**
- **Weakening Curse**
- **Energy Shield**

But you don’t need any of this. The beauty of the build is that it already works at a fraction of the cost of meta setups.

---

## Conclusion Summary

This is one of the strongest *practical*, *affordable*, and *high-synergy* water builds you can run right now in Patch 2.8.9. It wins by shutting down enemy energy, stacking mitigation, and letting Merlin’s nukes do all the talking. The way Chill + Frostbite Blow + regen cycles combine is beautiful.

**Bottom line:**
If you want a water team that doesn’t feel like a budget consolation prize, this is the build. Cheap to assemble, high ceiling, and it absolutely deletes teams it shouldn't be able to beat on paper.

title: Touch of Surprise vs. Dazzling Wish – New Scratcher Odds, Level-Ups &
markdown:
![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261121-152720-9setyq.png)

At first glance, Touch of Surprise looks like a more rewarding version of Dazzling Wish. The scratcher has several outfit jackpots, offers up to 60 Eternal Grails from a single result, and promises better winning probabilities as your Wonder Card levels up.

But how much better are those probabilities? How difficult is it to reach the higher levels? And is the scratcher actually better value than the old Dazzling Wish?

We've collected the complete Level 1 reward probabilities, examined the new mechanics, and compared them with our previous Dazzling Wish calculations.

The results are interesting. **Touch of Surprise starts with better Eternal Grail returns, but considerably worse outfit-fragment odds. Its level-up system improves those odds over time, although reaching the higher levels requires a substantial investment.**

## TL;DR – Is Touch of Surprise Better Than Dazzling Wish?

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261121-152522-0zxtfh.png)

These comparisons use the natural reward probabilities, without incorporating the different pity systems or Dazzling Wish's unspecified Surprise Event rewards.

Our initial conclusion is that **Touch of Surprise is worse for outfit fragments at Level 1 but offers approximately 33% more Eternal Grails than Dazzling Wish**.

However, the new leveling mechanic means this comparison changes as players continue scratching.

For players whose main objective is Eternal Grails, we still recommend the dedicated Wish Grail wheel over either event.

## How Does Touch of Surprise Work?

Touch of Surprise replaces the traditional spinning mechanic with Wonder Cards.

Each Wonder Card costs one Token of Light and contains five hidden symbols. Players scratch the card to reveal a combination of symbols and receive the corresponding reward.

The rewards include Eternal Grails and Fu Fei's Night of Terror outfit fragments.

Unlike Dazzling Wish, Touch of Surprise features several different outfit jackpots rather than a single 20-fragment reward.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261121-152755-irssrv.png)

The three major outfit prizes are:

* Five Turkeys: 45 Fu Fei outfit fragments
* Five Meat Legs: 30 outfit fragments
* Five Cakes: 20 outfit fragments

The remaining outcomes primarily reward Eternal Grails.

The event also includes daily ranking rewards, with different symbol combinations contributing different numbers of points.

But the most important new feature is the **UP system**, which allows players to increase their Wonder Card level and improve their chances of receiving grand prizes.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261121-152802-3xewk8.png)

## Complete Touch of Surprise Level 1 Probabilities

The following table contains the complete starting reward distribution, taken directly from the in-game event.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261121-152533-emamrs.png)

These probabilities total 100%.

That allows us to calculate the exact expected rewards at Level 1.

### Expected Eternal Grails per Scratch

Multiplying each possible Grail reward by its probability gives us:

**2.7141 Eternal Grails per scratch.**

This includes the rare 60-Grail UP result, along with the smaller prizes that make up most of the reward distribution.

For comparison, Dazzling Wish's previous probability table produced approximately 2.04 Eternal Grails per draw.

This means Touch of Surprise's starting Grail return is approximately **33% higher**.

That is a genuine improvement over the old system.

However, the number changes as the Wonder Card levels up, because the game increases the probability of grand prizes while reducing the probability of smaller rewards.

Consequently, 2.71 Grails should be understood as the Level 1 expectation, not a guaranteed average throughout an entire event.

### Expected Outfit Fragments per Scratch

The outfit calculation is less encouraging.

At Level 1, the three outfit rewards have the following probabilities:

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261121-152546-w5s94o.png)

That gives an expected return of just **1.65 outfit fragments per 100 scratches**.

By comparison, Dazzling Wish provided a 0.2% chance of obtaining 20 outfit fragments.

That equals four expected outfit fragments per 100 draws.

In other words, at their starting probabilities, Dazzling Wish provided approximately **2.4 times as many expected outfit fragments**.

Of course, players don't actually receive 1.65 fragments from 100 scratches. Outfit rewards arrive in batches of 20, 30, or 45, meaning most players receive none, while a lucky few receive a substantial prize.

The new scratcher therefore starts with significantly worse odds of receiving an outfit reward naturally.

## The UP System – How Do Wonder Card Levels Work?

This is the most important difference between the two events.

Every time you receive the **Five UP** result, your Wonder Card increases by one level.

The maximum level is 10.

The game explicitly states that higher levels increase the probability of obtaining grand prizes while decreasing the probability of receiving smaller rewards.

At Level 1, the chance of receiving Five UP is 1%.

This means players need an average of approximately 100 scratches to obtain one level-up.

Unlike the 1,200-scratch guaranteed prize, **leveling up does not require winning an outfit jackpot**.

The two systems are separate.

### How Many Scratches Does It Take to Reach Level 10?

Beginning at Level 1, players need nine UP results to reach Level 10.

Assuming the reported 1% UP probability remains constant throughout progression, that means:

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261121-152601-uj6i8q.png)

These figures are statistical averages, not guaranteed milestones.

Some players will level up considerably faster, while others will need many more scratches.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261121-152712-ycahsd.png)

The official regional Infinity Kingdom announcement also estimates roughly 1,000 scratches to reach Level 10, which is consistent with our calculation.

### What Are Your Chances of Reaching Level 10?

We can also calculate the probability of obtaining at least nine UP results.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261121-152610-72gt6r.png)

This demonstrates an important distinction.

For players spending 100–200 Tokens, reaching Level 2 or Level 3 is entirely realistic. At 200 scratches, there's an approximately 86.6% chance of receiving at least one UP result.

But reaching the maximum Level 10 is a completely different proposition.

Even after spending 500 Tokens, players have only about a 6.7% chance of reaching Level 10.

The system is therefore designed to reward very deep participation, with its highest levels largely inaccessible to ordinary players.

## How Much Do Outfit Odds Improve at Higher Levels?

This remains the biggest unknown in our complete value calculation.

The game confirms that grand-prize probabilities improve with each level, but the complete probability tables for Levels 2–10 are not currently available to us.

However, community reports from players investigating the new system suggest that the individual outfit-fragment probabilities may increase in small increments as the Wonder Card levels up.

One player reported maximum-level outfit probabilities in the region of **0.10% to 0.21%** across the three different fragment rewards.

That would represent a meaningful improvement over the starting values of 0.01%, 0.02%, and 0.03%.

Unfortunately, we don't yet have a complete screenshot of the Level 10 reward table confirming the exact percentages or their progression across every intermediate level.

For that reason, we won't publish a supposed average outfit return across 900 or 1,200 scratches based on guessed upgrade rates.

What we can say confidently is that the level-up mechanic improves outfit odds, but the overwhelming majority of players will spend much of their event participation below the highest levels.

This makes Touch of Surprise much harder to evaluate than Dazzling Wish.

## The 1,200-Scratch Guaranteed Prize

Touch of Surprise also features a guaranteed grand-prize system.

The in-game counter begins at 1,200 scratches and decreases as players participate.

The rules state that after the required number of scratches, players receive a guaranteed reward randomly selected from the three major outfit outcomes:

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261121-152624-rgx2ql.png)

This is quite different from Dazzling Wish, where 700 draws guaranteed 20 fragments.

The new event requires considerably more participation to reach its guarantee, but the prize can potentially contain more fragments.

However, we don't know whether the three pity outcomes are equally likely or whether their ordinary reward probabilities determine the selection.

We also haven't established how receiving a natural outfit jackpot interacts with the pity counter.

Therefore, the expected outfit-fragment value of the 1,200-scratch guarantee cannot yet be calculated precisely.

One point is nevertheless clear: **a single guaranteed prize does not necessarily unlock Fu Fei's outfit**.

The outfit requires 80 fragments, meaning players may still need additional jackpots or fragments from other sources.

## Touch of Surprise vs. Dazzling Wish – The Actual Value Comparison

We can now compare the two systems more meaningfully.

### For Eternal Grails

At Level 1, Touch of Surprise provides approximately 2.71 Eternal Grails per scratch, compared with 2.04 from Dazzling Wish.

This makes Touch of Surprise the better of the two events at their starting Grail probabilities.

For illustration:

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261121-152631-einffm.png)

The Touch of Surprise figures are hypothetical calculations assuming every scratch used the Level 1 probability table.

Actual players will begin leveling up during longer sessions, which changes the reward distribution.

These figures therefore provide a useful starting comparison, not an exact forecast.

### For Outfit Fragments

The situation is reversed.

At Level 1, Touch of Surprise provides significantly fewer expected outfit fragments.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261121-152640-pqonbx.png)

Dazzling Wish wins clearly when comparing starting probabilities.

However, Touch of Surprise improves its outfit odds through leveling, so we cannot conclude that Dazzling Wish is necessarily better across an entire 1,200-scratch session.

The exact result depends on the higher-level probability tables and the pity mechanics.

### Which Event Has the Better Pity?

Dazzling Wish required 700 draws to guarantee a fixed 20-fragment reward.

Touch of Surprise requires 1,200 scratches for a reward of 20, 30, or 45 fragments.

That means the new pity threshold is approximately 71% higher, but the potential reward is also larger.

If the new event consistently awarded 45 fragments, the increased requirement could be attractive.

If players frequently receive just 20 fragments, however, the guarantee becomes substantially worse.

Without the selection probabilities, we cannot fairly assign an exact winner to the pity comparison.

## What About Wish Grail?

Even with the improved Grail rewards in Touch of Surprise, there's another important alternative.

The Wish Grail wheel continues to provide substantially more Eternal Grails than either system when players select the 300-Grail grand prize and collect its cumulative milestone bonuses.

For example, our previous Wish Grail analysis estimated approximately **1,057 Eternal Grails from 200 spins**, including the 100- and 200-spin milestone rewards.

Compare that with:

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261121-152647-i2xpk4.png)

Wish Grail therefore remains the clear general recommendation for players whose primary objective is Eternal Grails rather than the featured seasonal outfit.

You can read the full calculations in our [Wish Grail October 2026 Guide](https://ik-wiki.com/posts/wish-grail-october-2026-outfit-jackpots-eternal-grail-odds-best-spin-milestones/).

## What Should Players Do?

The practical recommendations depend on how many Tokens of Light you're willing to spend and what you're trying to obtain.

### Free-to-Play and Low Spenders

For these players, Touch of Surprise is generally not an attractive outfit investment.

At Level 1, the natural outfit probability is only 0.06%, and reaching the higher levels requires hundreds of scratches.

A few lucky players will obtain fragments, but most should expect to receive ordinary Eternal Grail rewards.

If your main objective is long-term account progression, saving Tokens for Wish Grail remains the stronger choice.

### Moderate Spenders

For players spending approximately 100–300 Tokens, the UP system begins to become relevant.

You'll likely reach at least Level 2 and potentially progress a few levels further.

However, you remain far away from the 1,200-scratch guarantee and are unlikely to reach Level 10.

This means much of your participation will occur at relatively low Wonder Card levels.

Unless you're specifically collecting Fu Fei's outfit or competing for ranking rewards, I'd generally recommend spending those Tokens on Wish Grail instead.

### Heavy Spenders and Outfit Collectors

This is the group where Touch of Surprise becomes more interesting.

Players willing to spend 900–1,200 Tokens can realistically reach the higher Wonder Card levels, benefit from improved outfit probabilities, and potentially trigger the guaranteed grand prize.

However, the event still contains substantial uncertainty.

Without the complete upgraded probability tables, we cannot determine exactly how many outfit fragments these players should expect.

And because the pity reward is selected from three possible outcomes, reaching the guarantee doesn't provide a fixed number of fragments.

For players determined to collect every outfit, this may simply be the cost of participating.

But for players comparing the purchase against Chaos Immortal fragments, artifacts, and other valuable progression systems, it's difficult to recommend such a large investment without better information.

## Final Thoughts – Is the New Scratcher Actually Better?

Touch of Surprise is an interesting replacement for Dazzling Wish.

Its new mechanics offer more variety, larger potential outfit jackpots, and a progression system that gradually improves the chances of obtaining rare rewards.

The starting Eternal Grail returns are also noticeably better than those of the old Dazzling Wish.

However, that doesn't automatically make Touch of Surprise a better event.

The starting outfit probabilities are considerably worse, and the strongest improvements are locked behind a leveling system that requires hundreds of scratches to develop.

The 1,200-scratch guarantee is also a major investment, particularly when the guaranteed outfit reward can vary between 20 and 45 fragments.

For players who primarily want Eternal Grails, Wish Grail remains the more attractive option.

For outfit collectors, Touch of Surprise may become competitive at higher levels, but the exact value remains uncertain until we have the complete upgraded probability tables.

**Our recommendation: Treat Touch of Surprise as a specialized outfit lottery rather than your main source of seasonal value. Use Wish Grail for Eternal Grails, and only invest heavily in the scratcher when the featured outfit is worth the potentially enormous cost to you.**

We'll update this analysis as more players share the Level 2–10 probability tables and clarify the guarantee mechanics.

title: Tower of Knowledge tier list for level 0-20
summary: Welcome, fellow Infinity Kingdom players! This guide focuses on Tower of Knowledge (ToK) skills from levels 0 to 20. During the early preparation stage, it’s easy to overspend purple crystals on skills that you’ll later…
categoryPath: Beginners guide to Tower of Knowledge - collection of Tier Lists based on level ranges
markdown:
Welcome, fellow Infinity Kingdom players! This guide focuses on **Tower of Knowledge (ToK) skills** from levels **0 to 20**. During the early preparation stage, it’s easy to overspend purple crystals on skills that you’ll later need to replace. Rebirthing skills costs you 20% of the original crystal investment, so it’s crucial to choose wisely and avoid wasting precious resources. I’ll share which skills I recommend upgrading, which to skip, and how to keep your builds efficient while still enjoying a power boost in these early levels.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-25-1024x570.png)

---

### Why Skill Selection Matters at Levels 0–20

In the very first stages of the game, you need to strike a balance between grabbing skills that offer immediate benefits versus saving your purple crystals for high-tier skills you’ll unlock later.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-38-1024x502.png)

Many of the skills available at these lower levels either:

1. **Remain decently strong** throughout the early game (and can later be moved to a secondary team).
2. **Provide short-term power** but will eventually require rebirthing (and thus waste crystals).

You want to avoid the second scenario whenever possible. Let’s take a closer look at the major skill unlocks at levels 1, 5, 10, 15, and 20.

---

### Level 1: Onslaught and Wisdom

Right from the start, you gain access to **Onslaught (green)** and **Wisdom (green)**. Both are extremely cheap to acquire and upgrade:

- **Onslaught** boosts your physical damage output, making it ideal for early-game physical attackers such as Alexander.
- **Wisdom** boosts magic damage, benefiting your magic-based Immortals. If you use Medb (powerful early immortal) Wisdom is quite strong.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-26.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-27.png)

They’re not as strong as higher-level skills like **Anger (lvl 27)** or **Concentration (lvl 24)**, but they still pack enough punch to remain useful well into mid-game. Once you outgrow them on your main march, you can always move them to your second or third team, ensuring you haven’t wasted your crystals.

---

### Level 5: Hold Fast, Fortify, and Thump

At level 5, three more skills appear: **Hold Fast (green)**, **Fortify (green)**, and **Thump (green)**.

- **Hold Fast** provides a physical defense buff, which can help your frontline survive longer, especially early on. Normal attack damage is significant in the first stages of the game, so a cheap defensive buff can go a long way. You can move it to a backup team or rebirth it later if you no longer need it.
- **Fortify** and **Thump** are generally less appealing. They don’t offer enough impact to justify spending purple crystals, so it’s best to skip these if you can.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-28.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-29.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-30.png)

---

### Level 10: Meteor and Instigation

Upon reaching level 10, you unlock **Meteor (blue)** and **Instigation (blue)**.

- **Meteor** can be useful for dealing extra magic damage against bosses if you’re using a magic-based Immortal. Outside of that niche, it’s not particularly impressive, so most players can skip it.
- **Instigation** was once considered powerful for control-focused teams, but the pace of the game has accelerated, reducing its effectiveness. It’s not a terrible choice if you really want extra control, but it’s generally not worth investing a lot of crystals.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-31.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-32.png)

---

### Level 15: Support, Grace, and Silence

Level 15 adds **Support (blue)**, **Grace (blue)**, and **Silence (blue)** to your options.

- **Support and Grace** offer healing or regen capabilities, often popular in Earth-based teams. However, with **Wounds** becoming more common in the current meta, these skills lose much of their effectiveness. They can still be useful for PvE, but unless you have a specific plan, it’s safer to save your crystals for better skills.
- **Silence** stands out as a powerful option because it prevents enemies from regaining energy, effectively shutting down their ultimates. It also deals decent damage. This is one of the best early mid-tier control skills you can pick up, and it can remain relevant on your secondary teams even after you unlock higher-level skills.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-33.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-34.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-35.png)

---

### Level 20: Stray Arrow and Combo

Finally, at level 20, you gain **Stray Arrow (blue)** and **Combo (blue)**.

- **Stray Arrow** focuses on single-target physical damage at a 55% trigger chance. It can be handy if you need more boss damage, but it’s still on the weaker side in most PvP scenarios. If your purple crystals are in short supply, this skill is usually best skipped.
- **Combo** is an excellent pick for any frontline fighter who relies on normal attacks (like **Alexander** or **Hannibal Barca** in Earth, Wind, or hybrid lineups). It scales well and remains competitive for a long time. Even after you move your main march to stronger ToK skills, Combo can find a new home on a secondary lineup.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-36.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-37.png)

---

## Personal Recommendations and Opinions

You’ll unlock higher-level (and generally more potent) skills pretty quickly in today’s fast-paced environment. Therefore, investing heavily in weaker or situational early skills can cost you crystals later. Here’s a general tier list for levels 0–20 based on overall usefulness and longevity:

- **S-Tier**: **Silence**, **Combo**, **Onslaught**
These are the most valuable to acquire and upgrade, and they can remain useful even into the mid-game.
- **A-Tier**: **Wisdom**, **Hold Fast**
Solid picks if you need a cheap magic buff (Wisdom) or defensive support (Hold Fast). They’re easy to rebirth or move to secondary lineups.
- **B-Tier**: **Instigation**
Situational but can be used in a hyper-control setup. Otherwise, you can skip it.
- **C-Tier**: **Meteor**, **Stray Arrow**
Useful in niche scenarios (boss damage), but mostly overshadowed by better options.
- **F-Tier**: **Grace**, **Support**, **Fortify**, **Thump**
These have minimal utility, and you’ll likely regret spending crystals on them once you progress further.

Your main goal is to avoid pouring resources into skills that will quickly become obsolete. Focus on those with lasting impact, and you’ll have a smoother path when transitioning to higher-level skills that truly define endgame strategies.

---

### Summary

Navigating the early levels of the Tower of Knowledge (0–20) can be tricky. You need enough power to compete in Preparation servers without wasting crystals on skills you’ll just rebirth later. **Silence**, **Combo**, and **Onslaught** shine as top choices thanks to their balance of cost-effectiveness and long-term potential. Meanwhile, a few others like **Wisdom** and **Hold Fast** can be decent choices as well for a shorter period of time.

Everything else is largely optional or too niche to be worth your purple crystals. By keeping your spending smart, you’ll have plenty left to invest in the powerful late-game ToK skills that truly make a difference. Use this guide to plan your early ToK path, stay efficient, and lay the groundwork for a formidable army in Infinity Kingdom!

title: Tower of Knowledge tier list for level 21-30
summary: Here is the completed Tower of Knowledge Tier List Guide (Levels 21-30) for Infinity Kingdom!
categoryPath: Beginners guide to Tower of Knowledge - collection of Tier Lists based on level ranges
markdown:
Here is the **completed Tower of Knowledge Tier List Guide (Levels 21-30)** for **Infinity Kingdom**!

Welcome, fellow Infinity Kingdom players! This guide focuses on **Tower of Knowledge (ToK) skills** from levels **21 to 30**. During the early preparation stage, it’s easy to overspend purple crystals on skills that you’ll later need to replace. Rebirthing skills costs you 20% of the original crystal investment, so it’s crucial to choose wisely and avoid wasting precious resources. I’ll share which skills I recommend upgrading, which to skip, and how to keep your builds efficient while still enjoying a power boost in these early levels.

As you progress through **levels 21-30** in the **Tower of Knowledge (ToK)**, you unlock some of the most impactful skills in **Infinity Kingdom**. These abilities shape **PvE boss fights, PvP battles, and hybrid team compositions**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-79-1024x505.png)

This guide will help **new and experienced players** decide **which skills to invest in, and which to avoid** to **maximize their purple crystal efficiency**.

---

## Level 22 Unlocks

### Root

- **Effect:** Deals **single-target damage** and applies a **Root effect** to immobilize enemies.
- **Analysis:** Great for **PvE boss fights** due to its **consistent single-target damage**. However, **not very useful in PvP**, where mobility and cleanse effects diminish its value.
- **Tier:** **B** (Good for PvE, weak in PvP)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-80.png)

### Precision

- **Effect:** Increases **accuracy by 15%**.
- **Analysis:** **Accuracy is rarely an issue**, making this skill **pointless** in most scenarios.
- **Tier:** **D** (Avoid)

### Penance

- **Effect:** Reflects a **small portion of damage** back at the attacker.
- **Analysis:** The **reflected damage is minimal**, making this a **waste of resources**.
- **Tier:** **D** (Avoid)

---

## Level 24 Unlocks

### Rage

- **Effect:** Increases **critical hit rate**.
- **Analysis:** Very strong **if you have a crit-based team**, especially in **fire teams** using **Chase**. However, **it will eventually be replaced** by better skills.
- **Tier:** **A** (Great early on, but will be dropped later)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-81.png)

### Concentration

- **Effect:** Increases **magic damage by 30%**.
- **Analysis:** One of the **best skills for mages**, as **raw damage scaling is incredibly powerful**. A **core skill for any magic-based Immortal**.
- **Tier:** **S** (Must-have for magic teams)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-82.png)

---

## Level 25 Unlocks

### Agile

- **Effect:** Increases **dodge rate**.
- **Analysis:** **Dodge rate is unreliable**, and the **impact is minimal**. **Not worth the investment**.
- **Tier:** **D** (Avoid)

### Retaliate

- **Effect:** **30% chance to counterattack** when hit by a normal attack.
- **Analysis:** Can be **useful in niche scenarios**, such as a **Peter frontline against hybrid teams**. However, its **uses are too situational** to justify investing in.
- **Tier:** **C** (Situational)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-83.png)

### Chase

- **Effect:** Allows follow-up **extra attacks**.
- **Analysis:** **Fantastic early game skill**, especially when paired with **crit-based teams**. It **eventually falls off**, but remains **a strong investment for most of the game**.
- **Tier:** **A** (Strong, but not permanent)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-84.png)

---

## Level 26 Unlocks

### Magic Shield

- **Effect:** Reduces **magic damage taken**.
- **Analysis:** Magic damage **isn't a big enough threat** to justify using **a skill slot for this**.
- **Tier:** **C** (Not useful in most situations)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-85.png)

### Chaotic Blade

- **Effect:** Increases **normal attack damage** with a chance for **bonus damage**.
- **Analysis:** **Very strong in the early game**, especially for **attack-speed-based Immortals**. Over time, it gets **outclassed** but remains **great for secondary teams**.
- **Tier:** **A** (Good early, still useful later)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-86.png)

---

## Level 27 Unlocks

### Physical Shield

- **Effect:** Reduces **physical damage taken**.
- **Analysis:** Unlike **Magic Shield**, this skill **is actually useful** because **most normal attacks and ultimates are physical**.
- **Tier:** **A** (Good defensive skill)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-87.png)

### Anger

- **Effect:** Increases **physical damage by 30%**.
- **Analysis:** A **top-tier skill for physical damage dealers** like **Alexander, Hannibal, and Attila**.
- **Tier:** **S** (Essential for physical teams)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-88.png)

### Absorb

- **Effect:** Provides **lifesteal** (leeching damage for healing).
- **Analysis:** On certain builds, like **Duel Master Alexander**, this skill can **provide crazy sustain**. However, **not useful for most teams**.
- **Tier:** **C** (Situational)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-89.png)

---

## Level 28 Unlocks

### Heavenly Thunder

- **Effect:** Deals **magic damage** based on **attack speed**.
- **Analysis:** **Strong in hybrid teams** where **attack speed is high**. Works well in **specific hybrid builds** but **not a general-use skill**.
- **Tier:** **B** (Good in specific setups)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-90.png)

### Fighting Master

- **Effect:** Grants **control immunity**.
- **Analysis:** **One of the best PvP skills in the game**. Being **immune to crowd control** is **game-changing** in **high-level fights**.
- **Tier:** **S** (Must-have for PvP)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-91.png)

---

## Level 29 Unlocks

### After-Image

- **Effect:** Boosts **dodge rate**.
- **Analysis:** **Not great on its own**, but when paired with **Misleading** (unlocked later), it can create a **dodge-focused team**.
- **Tier:** **B** (Mediocre alone, strong with Misleading)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-92.png)

### Toxin Nova

- **Effect:** Deals **poison damage over time**.
- **Analysis:** **A strong early-to-mid game skill**, but **will eventually be replaced** by better abilities.
- **Tier:** **A** (Good, but temporary)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-93.png)

### Defensive Blessing

- **Effect:** Provides **flat defense boosts**.
- **Analysis:** **Amazing for any team**, as **flat defense reduction is always useful**. Works well **even in late-game setups**.
- **Tier:** **A** (Highly effective)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-94.png)

---

## Level 30 Unlocks

### Adrenaline Rush

- **Effect:** **Increases energy regen speed**.
- **Analysis:** **Absolutely broken on Immortals who rely on ultimates**, like **Richard, Hippolyta, Charles, and Attila**.
- **Tier:** **S** (Game-changing for certain Immortals)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-95.png)

### Garrote

- **Effect:** Increases **bleed damage**.
- **Analysis:** **Good for physical DoT setups**. Works similarly to **Chaotic Blade**.
- **Tier:** **A** (Good, but not core)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-96.png)

### Fire Nova

- **Effect:** Deals **AoE magic damage**.
- **Analysis:** **Solid for magic teams**, but **eventually replaced by stronger skills** like **Annihilation**. Still **great for second and third teams**.
- **Tier:** **A** (Strong early, good later)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-97.png)

### Iron Will

- **Effect:** Provides **resistance to magic damage**.
- **Analysis:** **Just like Magic Shield, this is not necessary**.
- **Tier:** **D** (Avoid)

---

## Final Tier List Summary

### S-Tier (Must-Have Skills)

✔ **Concentration** (Magic Teams)
✔ **Anger** (Physical Teams)
✔ **Fighting Master** (PvP Control Immunity)
✔ **Adrenaline Rush** (Energy Regen)

### A-Tier (Strong & Useful Skills)

✔ **Chase**
✔ **Chaotic Blade**
✔ **Defensive Blessing**
✔ **Fire Nova**
✔ **Garrote**

### B-Tier (Situational but Good)

✔ **Root** (PvE Only)
✔ **After-Image** (Only with Misleading)

### C-Tier (Rarely Useful)

✔ **Absorb**
✔ **Magic Shield**
✔ **Heavenly Thunder**

### D-Tier (Avoid These Skills)

❌ **Precision, Penance, Agile, Iron Will**

This guide ensures you **invest your purple crystals wisely** while maximizing the power of your **Immortals**! 🚀

title: Tower of Knowledge tier list for level 31-35

categoryPath: Beginners guide to Tower of Knowledge - collection of Tier Lists based on level ranges
markdown:
### ToK Tier List and Skill Recommendations (Levels 31-35)

As you progress through *Infinity Kingdom*, choosing the right **Tower of Knowledge (ToK) skills** is crucial. Some skills will carry you well into the **late game**, while others serve as **temporary but efficient choices** for your primary or secondary teams. The goal of this guide is to help you select **strong skills that you won’t need to rebirth later**, ensuring that you don’t waste precious **purple crystals** melting skills unnecessarily.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-110-1024x536.png)

This tier list covers the **Level 31-35 skill unlocks**, a pivotal stage where some of the game’s most powerful skills become available. These skills will define your strategy for a long time, so making the right choices now is essential for **efficiency, longevity, and optimal gameplay progression**.

---

## Level 31 Unlocks

### Will of Angels – F-Tier

This skill is a complete **no-go**. Even against wound-based setups, the healing provided is minimal. By level 31, **wound-heavy enemies are common**, and this skill won’t offer meaningful protection. Avoid it entirely.

### Life-Link – B-Tier

A **decent skill** with some PvP utility. While it won’t last long in your main lineup, it finds continued value in **secondary or third teams**. Additionally, it’s **essential for the Spider Boss** setup when paired with **Absolute Defense**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-111.png)

### Cleave – S-Tier

A **top-tier skill for physical damage dealers**. Works exceptionally well on **Alexander or Hannibal** due to their **high attack speed and high physical damage output**. More attack speed = **more activations = more damage**, making Cleave a **must-have for physical teams**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-112.png)

---

## Level 32 Unlocks

### Blessing of War – A-Tier

A **strong skill** for both **PvE and PvP**. It won’t last into **late game**, but you can get **huge value in the midgame**. Particularly useful in an **Earth-Wind Hybrid setup**, where it plays a key role in boosting effectiveness.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-113.png)

### Demon Body – F-Tier

A **completely useless skill**. There is no scenario where this skill provides real value. Avoid it.

---

## Level 33 Unlocks

### Sacrifice – B/C-Tier

A **situational skill** that can work on specific **support immortals** like **Dido or Cyrus**. It provides an **energy boost** and a **damage increase for allies**, but since it’s not **guaranteed**, it’s an unreliable option. **Not a must-have, but can be decent in niche setups.**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-114.png)

### Duel Master – S-Tier

One of the **best skills in the game**. It offers **wounds immunity**, which is essential for immortals that rely on **lifesteal or healing**. Must-have for:

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-115.png)

- **Alexander in Hybrid teams**
- **Tutankhamun in Shadow teams against Hybrid or Lightning teams**
- **Overall strong damage modifier as well**

### Berserk – B-Tier

A **powerful aura**, but **only effective in specific builds**. If you’re running a **Hybrid team**, it’s a **must-have**. It provides **good value in your main** before transitioning to a **secondary hybrid team**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-116.png)

---

## Level 34 Unlocks

### Rage Blessing – A-Tier

A **very strong regeneration skill**, providing sustained healing over time. While it will eventually be replaced (especially when **mass silence effects** become prevalent), it remains effective **well into late seasons**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-117.png)

### Resist – B-Tier

A solid **magic defense skill**, but not a top-tier choice. **Blessing of Defense** is often the preferred alternative due to its **wider defensive coverage**. Works well in a **secondary team**, providing **value while progressing**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-118.png)

**Note:** At level 34, players unlock access to **Wisdom Well skill-stone skills**, which are locked behind a **paywall**. These will be covered in a **separate guide**, as this guide focuses on **general skill recommendations** accessible to all players.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-119-1024x408.png)

---

## Level 35 Unlocks

### Absolute Defense – A-Tier

A **strong defensive skill**, particularly effective in **backline assist setups**. While **not as dominant in the current meta** due to **fast-paced power creep**, it still provides good value:

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-120-1024x379.png)

- **Effective once you unlock Tier 5 troops**.
- **Essential for the Spider Boss setup**.
- **Can be used effectively in PvP**, particularly in **support-based defensive teams**.

### Malice – A-Tier

An **excellent early-to-midgame aura**, reducing **critical damage received**. **Crit-based builds** are common in **early game and Season 1**, making Malice a **great defensive option**. However, its value declines as **dragon specializations unlock more resilience** (around **Season 2**).

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-121-1024x489.png)

### Oaken Guard – S-Tier

One of the **best physical defense skills in the game**. An **absolute must-have** against any **physical damage setup**:

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-122-1024x475.png)

- **Essential in almost all compositions except Duel Mage builds**.
- **Remains viable well into Conquest servers**.
- **Will stay in your main team for a long time**.

---

## Final Thoughts

Choosing the **right ToK skills** between **levels 31-35** will significantly impact your **progression efficiency** and **long-term resource management**. The best skills are those that **carry you well into late game** or transition smoothly into **secondary teams**, ensuring that you do **not waste purple crystals rebirthing skills**.

### Key Takeaways:

- **Top-Tier (S-Tier) Skills:**  - **Cleave** (Physical Damage Dealers)
- **Duel Master** (Hybrid & Shadow Teams)
- **Oaken Guard** (Physical Defense)
- **Strong (A-Tier) Skills:**  - **Blessing of War** (Strong early game, later Hybrid Compositions)
- **Rage Blessing** (Regen-based setups)
- **Absolute Defense** (Defensive Assist Setups & bosses)
- **Malice** (Anti-Crit Defense, Early Game)
- **Situational (B-Tier) Skills:**  - **Life-Link** (PvP, Spider Boss Setup)
- **Berserk** (Hybrid Teams)
- **Sacrifice** (Specific Support Immortals)
- **Resist** (Magic Defense, Secondary Teams)
- **Avoid (F-Tier) Skills:**  - **Will of Angels** (Weak Healing)
- **Demon Body** (No Competitive Use)

By planning your **skill selection wisely**, you will **optimize growth, avoid wasting resources, and maximize your efficiency** in both **PvE and PvP**. Stay strategic, and your **immortals will remain competitive well into the late game**.
