### Player Guide: Mastering Toxin Nova and Fire Nova in Infinity Kingdom

In the sprawling battlefield of Infinity Kingdom, the Tower of Knowledge skills Toxin Nova and Fire Nova often go unnoticed among the array of flashy and high-profile skills. However, these magic damage dealer skills are not only accessible to all players but also provide a surprisingly robust damage output that can enhance your strategic gameplay significantly.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/image-44-1024x365.png)

#### Skill Overview

**Toxin Nova and Fire Nova** share the same fundamental mechanics, with the only distinction being the type of damage over time (DoT) effect they apply—Toxin Nova inflicts Poison, and Fire Nova inflicts Burn. These skills are described as follows:

- **Official Skill Description**: "Every 6 seconds after battle starts, has a 50% chance of causing Magical Damage (175%) to 3 random enemy units and also inflicting a damage over time effect for 6 seconds dealing Magical Damage to the targets for 75% once every 3 seconds."

#### Analyzing the Damage Output

Despite their simplicity, the damage efficiency of Toxin Nova and Fire Nova is quite notable. Here’s a breakdown:

- **Probability of Activation**: Each skill has a 50% chance to trigger every 6 seconds.
- **Damage Calculation**: Upon activation, these skills not only deal an immediate 175% magical damage but also add a DoT that totals 150% over 6 seconds (75% every 3 seconds).
- **Comparative DPS**: This sums up to a whopping 325% damage per activation. Given the 50% trigger chance, the average DPS (Damage Per Second) contribution from these skills is **approximately 81.25%**.

This DPS is competitive, even **surpassing several higher-tier skills**like Stormeye (68.75% DPS), Spell Disintegration (62.5%), and Poison Thorn (55%). This demonstrates that both Toxin Nova and Fire Nova are not just filler skills; they are potent tools in their own right.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/image-45-1024x617.png)

#### Strategic Deployment

Toxin Nova and Fire Nova are best utilized in teams that can capitalize on sustained damage throughout a fight. They are particularly effective in:

- **Magic-focused Teams**: Complementing immortals with high magical output.
- **Control Teams**: Pairing with control effects to maximize damage during enemy disable periods.
- **Synergy with Chase**: Given that there are a lot of damage instances from both triggering effects and the damage over time effects, these skills pair well with Chase as the high number of damage instance will give you a good chance to land a critical hit quite frequently.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/image-46-1024x570.png)

**Note on Usage with Fire Dragon**: Players using the Fire Dragon should opt for Toxin Nova to avoid overlapping Burn effects, which do not stack and might result in significantly reduced efficiency.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/image-47.png)

#### Acquisition and Utilization

Both skills are freely available and can be acquired without the need for special events or premium currency, making them accessible options for building out your fourth march or reinforcing your existing teams.

#### Conclusion

While Toxin Nova and Fire Nova might not carry the prestige of some higher-profile skills, their effectiveness in the right strategic setup cannot be understated. Their high potential DPS, coupled with the versatility in application, makes them worthy of consideration for any player looking to enhance their magical damage capabilities in Infinity Kingdom. Remember, the best arsenal is one that's fully utilized—don't overlook these gems hidden in plain sight.

title: Trajan versus William Crit rate on Troops versus Immortals
summary: There are many Ultimate Abilities in Infinity Kingdom, one that has a particular intricate mechanic behind it, is the odd differentiation being made between the two Fire Immortal's William and Trajan on the way their…
markdown:
There are many Ultimate Abilities in Infinity Kingdom, one that has a particular intricate mechanic behind it, is the odd differentiation being made between the two Fire Immortal's William and Trajan on the way their Ultimate Ability work.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/williami-1-853x1024.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/trajan-1-1-1-1024x1024.png)

Williams Ultimate Ability reads*".... increases the Crit Rate of all your **troops**by x% for 6s."* whereas the Ultimate Ability of Trajan reads*"... **Immortal's**critical chance will be increased by 10% for 6 seconds, stackable up to 5 times."*

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/image-14.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/image-15.png)

This leads us to a very interesting question. One that a player recently asked me via my YouTube Channel. He asked me **"what is the difference is between "boosting the crit rate of troops" as mentioned in William's skill and "boosting the crit chance of immortals" as mentioned in Trajan's skill? Is there any difference between "boosting the crit rate of troops" and "boosting the crit rate of immortals"? Which one is better?**

This is what today's guide is going to be all about. What the devil is the difference?

## Difference between boosting Troop stats and Immortal stats

So there is a major difference between increasing the attributes/stats of your troops and of your Immortals. First of all, Immortal's Ultimate Ability's are damage scaled based on the attributes of both your Immortals and your Troops. That means that at high troop counts (where we do a lot of damage) boosting troop attributes is a big deal. However, we do not know the precise damage equation and as such I cannot prove that troop boosts are in fact stronger than Immortal boosts. Although I can say with confidence that they are.

Besides this, I asked an employee as the Infinity Kingdom team to comment on what the difference means for players. He had a very interesting reply!

It turns out, that **boosting troops** means that **all troops regardless of troop type and Immortal affinity/element** are affected (makes sense). However **boosting "Immortal's critical chance" ONLY works on fire Immortals!**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/image-14.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/image-15.png)

What this means then, is that **William**is boosting the the Crit Rate of any friendly **troops**whereas **Trajan's**boost to Immortal's Critical Chance only apply to other **Fire Immortal's**.

**This is a big deal if you are doing hybrids.**I have seen many players try and mix fire boosters like Trajan and William with e.g. lightning and shadow. It is very important to stress that you **CANNOT**use Trajan in a hybrid. Turns out he simply dosen't work! However, William does work, making him a very nice card to hold if you need to boost the Crit Rate of one of your marches. Maybe you are doing a Shadow Crit build?

## Which is better then?

**As for which is better. I think it's pretty simply. If you run Fire, Trajan is better.** His skill is simply better as it quickly stacks up providing both 50% Critical chance increase (basically making it near impossible for your Chase and Seon' Ultimate's to not proc constantly. Furthermore, every time it is applied you engage the fire dragon's third skill providing you a nice damage buff. With **Trajan's buff mechanic, you get a reliable and consistent application of this dragon buff.**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/image-18.png)

With the **Unique Artifacts** for both William and Trajan, the same story continues. William becomes stronger and is still very strong. However, Trajan's buffs are boosted a lot more and he becomes extreemly powerful in your fire team - but useless in anything but fire!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/image-17.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/image-16.png)

Ultimately, for the **classic Seon + Wu + Hippo fire build, you want Trajan as the last Immortal**. However, if you are running one of the **dual mage**builds without Seon in it (e.g. Baldwin + Wu), then I would actually **recommend you running BOTH William and Trajan.**These two Immortals do have very nice synergy between them, and provide massive burst potential for a hyper agressive dual mage fire team.

Hippolytta's energy regen control and ability to consistently ensure Seon crit-procs is however just too strong to pass on for a main march pure-fire team. As such, Trajan ultimately wins the fight for last spot.

title: Troop Advantage, Tiers and more - Full Beginners Needs to Know
summary: A practical, systems-focused overview of troop types, troop advantage, barracks tiers, and how to upgrade efficiently.
markdown:
## Beginner’s Guide to Troops in Infinity Kingdom

A practical, systems-focused overview of troop types, troop advantage, barracks tiers, and how to upgrade efficiently.

### Introduction

If you understand **troop types**, **formation rules**, and **how tiers actually upgrade**, you’ll save weeks of wasted speedups and resources. Troops are the “real” stamina of your account: every gnome, every rally, every PvP hit is ultimately a troop trade. New players usually lose the most progress by (1) training the wrong mix, (2) misunderstanding counters, and (3) upgrading barracks in the wrong order.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-142.png)

This guide lays out the troop system clearly, with emphasis on one of the most important recent clarifications from the IK team: **troop advantage is a flat 5% swing in both directions**.

---

## 1) The Four Troop Types and What Counters What

Infinity Kingdom has **four troop types**:

- **Bowmen**
- **Shieldmen**
- **Cavalry**
- **Spearmen**

### The Counter Triangle

Three of the four types form the counter triangle:

- **Cavalry counter Shieldmen**
- **Shieldmen counter Spearmen**
- **Spearmen counter Cavalry**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-141.png)

### Bowmen Are Neutral

**Bowmen do not counter any troop type, and no troop type counters Bowmen.**

---

## 2) Troop Advantage Explained: The Real Value Is a 5% Swing

For a long time, players knew counters mattered but didn’t have the exact number. The IK team has now clarified troop advantage as:

- **+5% damage dealt** against the troop type you counter
- **-5% damage taken** from the troop type you counter

That means the counter relationship is not “just extra damage.” It’s a **two-sided combat modifier**.

### Why this matters more than it looks

A lot of players hear “5%” and shrug. In practice, it’s meaningful because it stacks on top of everything else that affects damage and survivability.

Because the advantage applies to both outgoing and incoming damage, it acts like a **net swing** in combat efficiency. In a clean counter matchup, you’re not only hitting harder—you’re also lasting longer, which increases total damage your march can output before it collapses.

### What troop advantage does not do

- It does **not** override tier gaps. A higher tier often wins through raw stats if the gap is big enough.
- It does **not** change Bowmen matchups (they remain neutral).
- It does **not** replace good march structure. A countered frontline still dies fast if it’s underbuilt.

That means, while troop advantage is a great advantage to have! You should not build your setups around it! Instead, use the knowledge when positioning your immortals against certain enemy players in order to, for example place your spearmen facing enemy cavalry.

---

## 3) How Troops Fit Into a March: Front Row vs Back Row

A troop (march) is composed of **four Immortals and one Dragon**, arranged in **two rows**:

- **Front row (2 Immortals):** can be **Spearmen / Cavalry / Shieldmen** leaders
- **Back row (2 Immortals):** must be **Bowmen** leaders

Because **two of your four Immortals must lead Bowmen**, you naturally consume more Bowmen across your marches. That’s why many veteran accounts prioritize Bowmen upgrades early: not because Bowmen “beat everything,” but because you simply field them **everywhere**. Unless you are build relies exclusively on damage dealt by frontline immortals, you should prioritize upgrading Bowmen to new tiers first.

---

## 4) Troops Are Trained in Barracks, and Barracks Decide Tier

Each troop type has its own training building (barracks). The crucial mechanic for beginners:

You do *not* “unlock tiers” primarily through Academy research. Research supports your army, but **your troop tier is upgraded by the level of the building that trains that troop type**, i.e. the Barracks.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-143.png)

When a barracks hits the required level for the next tier, your troops **automatically convert** from the old tier to the new tier (all trained troops will transform into troops of the new tier, you do not need to train them all over again.

This is one of the most important efficiency mechanics in the early game.

---

## 5) The Best Way to “Upgrade Tiers” Without Wasting Resources

Here’s the veteran habit that saves huge amounts of resources:

### Max your Training Grounds capacity before pushing the barracks tier

Before you upgrade a barracks to the level that triggers tier conversion, try to:

1. **Fill training queues**
2. **Max out Training Grounds capacity** (so you’re holding as many troops as possible)
3. Then upgrade the barracks to trigger conversion

Why? Because converting a large stockpile of older-tier troops into the new tier is generally cheaper than training the new tier from scratch.

If you rush your barracks tier while your troop count is low, you end up having to **train the higher tier directly**, which is much more expensive (and time consuming).

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-145.png)

### A simple rule that works

If you’re not capped (or close to capped) on the troop type you’re upgrading, **either pause or speed up** and train more, then push the barracks level.

---

## 6) Troop Tiers and Season Progression

Troop tiers are not infinite at the start. Your maximum tier depends on available building levels, which expand as you progress through seasons.

A common progression model looks like this:

- **Tier 5 (T5)** is the max during initial seasons when **buildings cap at level 40**
- Later seasons extend building levels and unlock higher tiers:  - **Building level 45 → T6**
- **Building level 50 → T7**
- **Conquest: building level 55 → T8**
- **Legendary: level 60 → T9**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-144.png)

---

## 7) Training Priorities for New Players

This is where practical play matters more than theory.

### Priority 1: Keep Bowmen training consistently

Because back row requires Bowmen leaders, you’ll field Bowmen everywhere. If you ever feel “I can’t make a second march,” it’s often because you’re short on Bowmen.

### Priority 2: Build one strong main march first

Spreading upgrades evenly across everything is a classic beginner trap. One strong march:

- Clears higher-level map content sooner
- Performs better in rallies
- Loses fewer troops per day for the same results

That also means **prioritize the types of troops that your main march uses**: E.g. Cavalry and Shieldmen = then you should neglect upgrading technology and barracks for Spearmen. Delay that and focus on what you use in your main.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-146-1024x536.png)

### Priority 3: Don’t ignore the triangle

Having troop advantage can be quite powerful. Getting both reduced damage taken and more damage dealt can make or break a matchup if you are close to each other on other development parameters. Always looking over formations when trying to beat certain main rivals is always recommended. Changing up your frontline formations so that you gain troop advantage can just make the difference!

---

## Conclusion Summary

- There are four troop types: **Bowmen (neutral), Shieldmen, Cavalry, Spearmen**.
- Counter triangle: **Cav > Shield > Spear > Cav**.
- **Troop advantage is a confirmed 5% bonus to damage dealt and 5% reduction to damage taken** in the counter matchup.
- March structure forces **Bowmen in the back row**, making Bowmen a constant resource demand.
- **Troop tiers upgrade via barracks level and automatic conversion**.
- Best efficiency habit: **max Training Grounds capacity and troop counts before triggering a tier conversion**.

---

title: Tutankhamun changes may 2023
summary: Major changes to the Ultimate ability and energy regen attributes of Tutankhamun!
markdown:
**Major changes to the Ultimate ability and energy regen attributes of Tutankhamun!**

### Before:

Infinity Kingdom has just released a new shadow element Immortal figure, Tutankhamun, with an ultimate ability called "Wrath of Horus" (Unleash 5 waves of energy to random enemies dealing physical damage of up to 250%, if a target has already been damaged, the next energy wave will deal double the damage). In this article, we will explore who Tutankhamun was in real life, what he can do in the game, and how important energy regen is for Immortals.

### After:

Instead of unleasing double damage on ALL damaged enemies, Totankhamun has been nerfed A LOT and not instead has gotten an added leech effect as well as the double damage effect however with a modified trigger condition. Instead of double damage to all damaged, he now deals double damage to a target he has hit within the past 1.5 seconds. A major nerf. To make up for some if the damage loss, they have added a leech efect. When damaging an enemy that is affected by Bleed or Tear, Tutankhamun will have 70% chance to recover 2% of his maximum hp.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/image-101-1024x576.png)

Tutankhamun was an ancient Egyptian pharaoh who ruled from around 1332 BC to 1323 BC. He ascended to the throne at the age of nine and died at the age of eighteen, making him one of the youngest pharaohs to have ruled Egypt. His tomb was discovered in 1922 by archaeologist Howard Carter, and the discovery of the tomb and its treasures made Tutankhamun one of the most famous pharaohs of ancient Egypt.

## Tutankhamun in Infinity Kingdom

In the game, Tutankhamun's ultimate ability, "Wrath of Horus", deals physical damage of up to 250% to random enemies. If a target has already been damaged with 1.5 secdons, the next energy wave will deal double the damage. This ability is still very very powerful and the leech effect works well in tandem with the concept of Bathory and Bjorn.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/image-100.png)

**Before**:

Tutankhamun's energy regen rate is 67.2, which is not the best but should not be a problem for him. Energy regen is an important factor to how powerful an Immortal is, and it is often overlooked by many players when reviewing Immortals. However, it is a crucial element to consider as it determines how quickly an Immortal can use their ultimate ability in battle. A higher energy regen rate means an Immortal can use their ultimate ability more frequently, which can greatly impact the outcome of battles.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/image-107.png)

**After**:

Tutankhamun's energy regen has been SUBSTANTIALLY increased! From 67.2 to a massive 70.4 energy regen as it's base. This is a massive buff that will do a lot to make up for the lost damage. Overall this makes him a much more consistent Immortal and in my opinion making him more interesting for actual PvP leech focused physical shadow marches.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/image-101.png)

## Amazing boss killer

Furthermore, Tutankhamun will be an amazing Immortal for killing world bosses in Norheim and will be absolutely amazing at killing the spider boss. Comparatively, he will likely be above and beyond the best single target Immortals currently in the game. His ability deals significantly more damage than that of e.g. Yoshitsune and Hippolyta and will likely be unrivaled in terms of boss damage dealing potential. In the correct setup, I would not be surprised to see top tier spider builds with Tutankhamun able to reach 6-7% hits!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/image-106.png)

## Conclusion

In conclusion, Tutankhamun is a powerful new Immortal figure in Infinity Kingdom. His ultimate ability, "Wrath of Horus", deals massive amounts of damage to random enemies, and his energy regen rate is sufficient for him to be used in various energy regen focused builds. Energy regen is an important factor to consider when reviewing Immortals, and it is crucial for their effectiveness in battles. Tutankhamun can be applied in various scenarios, such as replacing Siegfried or taking on world bosses. Tutankhamun's arrival in Infinity Kingdom has certainly made the game more exciting, and players are looking forward to seeing what he can do.

title: Tycoon's Club Black Friday 2026 – Fortune Wheel Odds, Chip Shop & Is It
summary: The Tycoon's Club returns for Black Friday 2026 with a new chip shop,
markdown:
![Tycoon's Club Black Friday 2026 – IK Wiki guide](/uploads/screenshot-20261126-222459-k8sb2g.png)

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261127-091855-u2xj37.png)

The Tycoon's Club is back. The casino-themed event from October returns for Black Friday 2026 with a few important changes: a new **chip currency** you earn by spinning the Fortune Wheel, a reworked Private Treasure Gallery, a **daily** points leaderboard, and a set of Black Friday Amethyst packs on GTarcade.

At first glance it looks brutal. The headline rewards in the Gallery cost **34,000 Tycoon Coins**, which is roughly **$2,800** worth of Amethyst. But once you work through the numbers, there is one efficient route through the event that is cheap or even free. This guide explains how the event works, what everything really costs, and where your money (if any) is best spent.

If you missed the October run, start with the [Tycoon's Club – New Event Overview & Beginner's Guide](/posts/tycoon-s-club-new-event-overview-beginner-s-guide) and the [Tycoon's Club Spending Guide](/posts/tycoon-s-club-spending-guide-best-buys-fortune-wheel-odds-value-analysis). This article covers what is different this time.

## Event Dates

* **Event:** 26 November – 3 December 2026 (ends at 00:00 UTC)
* **Private Treasure Gallery:** stays open one extra day, until 4 December 00:00 UTC, so you can spend leftover coins and chips
* **Daily reset:** 00:00 UTC (Limited-Time Rewards, Fortune Wheel Energy and the leaderboard)
* **Requirement:** Castle level 15+

## The Basics: Coins, Chips and Amethyst

There are three currencies to keep track of:

* **Amethyst** – the premium currency you buy with real money.
* **Tycoon Coins** – the event currency. **100 Tycoon Coins cost 50 Amethyst** (1 Amethyst = 2 coins), the same rate as in October. You also earn coins for free from the VIP Pass and Max Bounty.
* **Chips** (the purple token) – **new this time**. You cannot buy chips. You only get them from the Limited-Time Rewards tab by *consuming* Tycoon Coins on the Fortune Wheel.

That last point is the key to the whole event, so keep it in mind.

## What Things Cost in Real Money

Amethyst is sold on GTarcade. During Black Friday you get 25% more Amethyst per dollar than usual on the special packs. Each Black Friday pack can be bought **once per day**.

| Pack | Price  | Black Friday | Normal | Amethyst per $ (BF) |
| ---- | ------ | ------------ | ------ | ------------------- |
| 1    | $2.99  | 25           | 20     | 8.4                 |
| 2    | $4.99  | 38           | 30     | 7.6                 |
| 3    | $9.99  | 75           | 60     | 7.5                 |
| 4    | $19.99 | 150          | 120    | 7.5                 |
| 5    | $49.99 | 300          | 240    | 6.0                 |
| 6    | $99.99 | 600          | 480    | 6.0                 |

Buying all six Black Friday packs costs **$187.94 a day** and gives **1,188 Amethyst (2,376 Tycoon Coins)**. The bonus gems and VIP points are the same as on the normal packs; only the Amethyst goes up. There is also a GTarcade bonus for a single order of $800 or more (100 Amethyst, 20 Stardust, 5 Ultimate EXP Rolls, 5 Superior Resources Optional Chests), which is not worth chasing.

**Rule of thumb for this guide:** at the big-pack rate of 6 Amethyst per dollar, **1 Tycoon Coin ≈ $0.08** and **1,000 coins ≈ $83**.

## VIP Pass (Holiday Battle Pass) – $4.99

![VIP Pass purchase screen: $4.99 for 60 Amethyst, 250 Gems and 3 chests now, and 450 Amethyst, 500 Gems, 23 blue and 5 gold chests by level 30](/uploads/screenshot-20261126-222831-p9jpa3.webp)

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261127-091901-azizqn.png)

The pass has 30 levels. You earn EXP from daily event missions.

* **Free track (Silver Insignia):** 10 Tycoon Coins per level = **300 coins**.
* **Paid track (Gold Insignia, $4.99):** 60 Amethyst, 250 Gems and 3 chests immediately, then 15 Amethyst per level, for a total of **450 Amethyst, 500 Gems, 23 blue chests and 5 gold chests** at level 30.

That is **510 Amethyst (1,020 coins) for $4.99**, about 100 Amethyst per dollar, or roughly 13 times better than the best Black Friday pack. If you plan to spend anything at all, buy this first. Just make sure you will actually do the daily missions; the Amethyst arrives level by level.

## Fortune Wheel – the Real Odds

![Fortune Wheel with Energy bar, spin button and daily points leaderboard](/uploads/screenshot-20261127-083513-q5ubzx.webp)

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261127-091907-5nkonz.png)

One spin costs **10 Tycoon Coins**. You can raise the reward multiplier, which multiplies both the cost and the rewards. When the Energy bar reaches 100% you trigger **Gold Rush**: the next spin costs 10% less. Energy resets daily.

The full reward table:

| Result                     | Reward                            | Chance | Points |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------ | ------ |
| Super Jackpot (3 goblins)  | 100 Midnight Star                 | 0.10%  | 10     |
| Super Jackpot (3 smiles)   | 600 coins                         | 0.15%  | 6      |
| Super Jackpot (3 diamonds) | 450 coins                         | 0.20%  | 4      |
| Lucky Triple               | 80 coins                          | 1.10%  | 3      |
| Super Pair (goblins)       | 45 coins                          | 2.00%  | 3      |
| Super Pair (smiles)        | 30 coins                          | 3.00%  | 3      |
| Super Pair (diamonds)      | 25 coins                          | 4.00%  | 1      |
| Lucky Pair                 | Superior Resources Optional Chest | 23.80% | 2      |
| Surprise Single (goblin)   | 20 coins                          | 4.00%  | 2      |
| Surprise Single (smile)    | 15 coins                          | 6.00%  | 2      |
| Surprise Single (diamond)  | 10 coins                          | 8.00%  | 1      |
| Thanks for Playing         | Medium Speedup Chest              | 47.65% | 1      |

**What this means:**

* On average a 10-coin spin pays back **7.98 coins**. The wheel returns **79.8%** of what you put in, so each spin really costs you about **2 coins** (a little less than in October, where the return was close to 90%).
* Each spin also gives on average **1.48 leaderboard points**, about 0.24 Superior Resources Optional Chests, 0.48 Medium Speedup Chests and a 0.1% shot at 100 Midnight Star.
* The swings are large. Over 120 spins the coin result typically varies by around ±360 coins, mostly decided by whether you hit one of the 450 or 600-coin jackpots.

Because coins you win go straight back into the wheel, a small bankroll can generate a lot of "consumption". That matters for the next part.

## Limited-Time Rewards – Where Chips Come From

Every day you earn chips for the total number of coins you consume on the wheel. Coins you won back and spun again count again.

| Coins consumed (daily) | Chips | Total chips | Expected real cost | Coins per chip (this tier) |
| ---------------------- | ----- | ----------- | ------------------ | -------------------------- |
| 1,200                  | 100   | 100         | ~242 coins         | 2.4                        |
| 3,600                  | 150   | 250         | ~727 coins         | 3.2                        |
| 7,200                  | 200   | 450         | ~1,454 coins       | 3.6                        |
| 12,000                 | 250   | 700         | ~2,424 coins       | 3.9                        |
| 18,000                 | 300   | 1,000       | ~3,636 coins       | 4.0                        |
| 25,000                 | 350   | 1,350       | ~5,050 coins       | 4.0                        |

"Expected real cost" is what you lose on average, after the wheel pays back its 79.8%. The first tier is by far the best value: **100 chips for about 242 coins (~$20 of Amethyst)**, every single day. The higher tiers get steadily worse, and maxing every tier costs about **5,050 coins (~$420) per day**.

(The tab's banner says *"Wir bieten euch erstklassigen Mitgliederservice!"* in German, even on English clients. Someone at the localization desk was busy with Black Friday too.)

## Private Treasure Gallery

The shop has two halves: items bought with chips and items bought with coins.

**Chip items (good value):**

| Item                                                         | Price     | Daily limit |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------- | ----------- |
| Louis IX – Night of Terror Fragment ×30                      | 100 chips | 5           |
| Alexander the Great – Summer Passion Fragment ×30            | 100 chips | 5           |
| Fu Fei – Night of Terror Fragment ×8                         | 100 chips | 25          |
| Athena – Summer Passion Fragment ×8                          | 100 chips | 25          |
| Fate of Chaos Selection Chest VIII ×20                       | 75 chips  | 12          |
| Shadow and Light Selection Chest II ×30                      | 50 chips  | 6           |
| Core Immortals Selection Chest (Earth · Lightning · Wind) ×1 | 50 chips  | 3           |

An Immortal Outfit needs **60 fragments** (extra fragments upgrade its Glamour Level). So:

* **Louis IX or Alexander outfit: 200 chips** (2 purchases)
* **Fu Fei or Athena outfit: 800 chips** (8 purchases, 64 fragments)

**Coin items (mostly terrible value):**

![Gallery coin items: 34,000-coin Chaos chests, Crimson Moonlight and Stardust](/uploads/screenshot-20261126-223114-pgt3n0.webp)

Compare the same items across both halves:

* **Fate of Chaos Selection Chest VIII:** 20 for 75 chips (~180–300 coins of real cost) versus 80 for 34,000 coins. Per chest, the chip route is about **30–45 times cheaper**.
* **Core Immortals Selection Chest:** 50 chips (~120–200 coins) versus 10,000 coins.
* **Shadow and Light Selection Chest II:** 30 for 50 chips versus 60 for 10,000 coins.

In other words, **never buy chests with coins if the same chest exists for chips.** Spin the coins on the wheel instead and buy with the chips.

## Max Bounty

Max Bounty is unchanged from October. Six bounties worth 1–6 stars (21 points per round) refresh every hour, and the progress bar has chests at 80, 110, 140, 170, 200, 230 and 260 points. The chests go from 80 Tycoon Coins + 50 Gems at the start to 220 Tycoon Coins + 450 Gems + 5 Philosopher's Offers at 260. In total the track is worth **roughly 1,000 Tycoon Coins**, free.

## Gilded Club

The Gilded Club tiered shop is back and **refreshes daily**. Tier 1 is free (10 Tycoon Coins, a scroll and potions), tier 2 costs **$0.99 for 10 Amethyst plus chests and 1,000 VIP points** (about 10 Amethyst per dollar, better than any Amethyst pack), and tier 3 costs 200 Gems for 5 Amethyst and more consumables. Further tiers continue the ladder with more cash and gem purchases. Always claim tier 1; tier 2 is a fine impulse buy if you are spending anyway.

## Is It Worth It? Four Budgets

All numbers below are averages. The wheel is random, so your own results will swing up or down.

**Free-to-play (\~1,300 coins: 300 from the free pass + \~1,000 from Max Bounty)**

Spin exactly **1,200 coins a day** (120 spins) to collect the first 100 chips, and stop. That costs about 242 coins a day, so your free coins last around five days, for **~500 chips**. That is enough for the **Louis IX Night of Terror** *and* **Alexander Summer Passion** outfits (200 chips each) plus a Core Immortals Selection Chest or Fate of Chaos chests with the rest. Not bad for zero dollars.

**$4.99 – VIP Pass (~2,300 coins)**

The pass adds about 1,000 coins. Now you can take the first tier every day of the event (\~700 chips) and sometimes the second. That covers both 200-chip outfits with \~300 chips to spare, or puts you most of the way to an 800-chip Fu Fei or Athena outfit.

**~$80–$120 – Pass + small Black Friday packs**

Add the $2.99, $4.99 and $9.99 Black Friday packs on some days (138 Amethyst for $17.97 per day). Taking tiers 1 and 2 on most days gets you to roughly 1,200–1,300 chips: **Louis IX + Alexander + Fu Fei or Athena**. This is the sweet spot for a light spender.

**$400+ a day – Leaderboard and max tiers**

Maxing all six chip tiers costs around **$420 per day**, so roughly **$2,900** over the event, for 1,350 chips a day. Just appearing on the daily leaderboard needs 1,500 points (~1,000 spins, about $170–$210 a day). The top three on my server were at 145,000–163,000 points on day one. That is around 110,000 spins, or very roughly **$20,000+ in a single day**. The leaderboard is strictly whale territory.

## Verdict

The first impression is correct for most of the event. The coin-priced Gallery items are priced for whales, the leaderboard is out of reach for almost everyone, and buying Amethyst to convert straight into coins is poor value even at Black Friday rates.

The chip shop is the exception. Because the wheel pays back almost 80% of every spin and chips are awarded on everything you *consume*, the first daily tier turns about 240 coins into 100 chips. That makes two Immortal outfits reachable for free-to-play players and a third for anyone buying the $4.99 pass and a few small packs.

**Quick plan:**

1. Buy the **$4.99 VIP Pass** if you will spend anything at all, and do the missions every day.
2. Clear **Max Bounty** whenever it refreshes.
3. Each day, spin until the **1,200-coin** tier is done, and stop there unless you have coins to spare.
4. Spend chips on **Louis IX** and **Alexander** outfits first (200 chips each), then **Fu Fei** or **Athena** (800 chips).
5. Never buy chests with coins when the same chest is available for chips.
6. Claim the free Gilded Club tier every day.

title: Tycoon's Club – New Event Overview & Beginner's Guide
markdown:
![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261015-151140-iuq6tf.png)

## VIP Pass – Complete Missions and Earn Rewards

The VIP Pass works much like the familiar seasonal event passes. Players complete gameplay objectives to earn EXP and progress through **30 levels of rewards**.

There are two reward tracks:

* **Free Pass:** Provides resources and a total of 300 Tycoon Coins.
* **Premium Pass ($4.99):** Adds additional rewards, including Amethyst Stones that can be exchanged for 900 Tycoon Coins.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261015-151255-g2yrml.png)

Objectives include training troops, defeating gnomes and gnome bosses, and completing other gameplay activities. Some require substantial resources, so check the objectives early and plan accordingly.

The premium pass offers potentially good value for players who complete all 30 levels. We'll examine that more closely in our separate spending guide.

## Max Bounty – Fight Enemies for Free Rewards

Max Bounty introduces six combat missions, including Hostile Takeover, Riot Suppression, and Asset Recovery.

These missions work similarly to Rebel encounters. Players fight enemies, earn rewards, and progress through a milestone track. Stronger opponents can be tackled with alliance rallies.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261015-151313-dd1ar9.png)

**The important mechanic is that Max Bounty refreshes every hour.**

Completing all six missions awards 21 bounty points. The full milestone track requires 260 points, meaning approximately **13 complete rounds** are needed to finish it.

Completing the milestones rewards players with around **1,000 Tycoon Coins**, making this one of the event's most important activities for free-to-play players.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261015-151345-hjvjsp.png)

Remember that missions consume AP and can cause significant troop losses. AP-reduction talents work on these encounters and can help reduce costs.

## Fortune Wheel – Slot Machine and Energy System

The Fortune Wheel is the casino component of Tycoon's Club.

Players spend Tycoon Coins to spin a three-reel slot machine, with different symbol combinations determining their rewards.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261015-151403-1jop9o.png)

Winning combinations can award additional Tycoon Coins, while less fortunate outcomes may provide only resources or speedups.

A normal spin costs **10 Tycoon Coins**, and players can increase their wager using the Reward Multiplier. Higher multipliers increase the rewards received but do not appear to improve the chance of winning.

### How Does Energy Work?

The Fortune Wheel also features an Energy meter that fills as players use the machine.

When the meter is full, players receive a **10% discount on spin costs**. For example, a 10× spin normally costs 100 coins but drops to 90 with the discount.

Importantly, Energy does not appear to guarantee a jackpot or increase winning probabilities. It is a cost-reduction mechanic, not a traditional pity system.

The Fortune Wheel also includes a competitive leaderboard with additional ranking rewards.

**Be careful:** The coins used for gambling are the same coins needed to purchase guaranteed rewards in the event shop. You can lose coins without receiving anything particularly valuable in return.

## Private Treasure Gallery – Spend Your Tycoon Coins

The Private Treasure Gallery is the event's reward exchange shop. Here, players can purchase specific resources and materials using Tycoon Coins.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261015-151427-brxp7p.png)

Some notable rewards include:

**Crimson Moonlight and Stardust are particularly interesting rewards**, offering potentially excellent value compared with other ways of obtaining these materials.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261015-151438-net5mp.png)

For many players, saving Tycoon Coins for guaranteed shop purchases may be preferable to gambling them in the Fortune Wheel.

## Gilded Club – Additional Shop Offers

The Gilded Club is a separate event-related shop accessible through Infinity Kingdom's regular shop interface.

It contains additional resource bundles, premium purchases, and offers that can be obtained using Gems.

Some rewards are available for free, so remember to check the shop regularly and claim anything available.

## What Should You Prioritize?

For most players, our recommendations are fairly straightforward:

1. **Complete Max Bounty:** Work toward all 260 milestone points to collect the event rewards.
2. **Progress your VIP Pass:** Complete objectives and claim as many of the 30 levels as possible.
3. **Check the Gilded Club:** Don't miss the free rewards.
4. **Choose your Gallery rewards:** Crimson Moonlight and Stardust are worth particular attention.
5. **Be cautious with the Fortune Wheel:** Remember that gambling Tycoon Coins means giving up guaranteed purchasing power in the Gallery.

## Final Thoughts

Tycoon's Club offers a welcome new activity between Infinity Kingdom's regular seasonal events, with opportunities for both free-to-play players and spenders.

The most important activities for casual players are the VIP Pass and Max Bounty, which offer predictable progression and rewards. The Fortune Wheel adds a more exciting but riskier option for players interested in gambling or competing for leaderboard rankings.

For those considering spending money, we'll take a closer look at the **Fortune Wheel odds, VIP Pass value, event bundles, and best reward purchases** in our upcoming Tycoon's Club Spending & Value Analysis.

title: Tycoon's Club Spending Guide – Best Buys, Fortune Wheel Odds & Value Analysis
markdown:
![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261015-151837-yeghcv.png)

## VIP Pass – Is the $5 Purchase Worth It?

The premium VIP Pass costs $4.99 and offers one of the best returns in the entire event.

Completing all 30 levels rewards players with 450 Amethyst Stones, which can be converted into **900 Tycoon Coins**, alongside 500 Gems and various resource chests.

Combined with the free pass and Max Bounty rewards, the total potential currency looks like this:

That's already almost enough for 100 Crimson Moonlight, which costs 2,500 Tycoon Coins in the Private Treasure Gallery.

For comparison, a free-to-play player completing the available activities can collect approximately 1,370 coins, enough to purchase 100 Stardust for 1,000 coins.

**Our verdict: The $4.99 VIP Pass is an excellent purchase for active players who can complete all 30 levels.** The currency alone makes it attractive, even before accounting for Gems and additional resources.

## Gilded Club – The Best Way to Buy Additional Coins

One easily overlooked mechanic is that the Gilded Club shop uses a tiered purchase system.

Buying one offer unlocks the next, and these tiers include free rewards and purchases made with Gems. This makes the shop much better value than simply comparing the prices of individual bundles.

![Screenshot](/uploads/screenshot-20261015-151648-zs584h.png)

Here are the first nine tiers:

The combined cost of reaching tier 9 is **$10.96 plus 1,000 Gems**, rewarding 120 Amethyst Stones from tiers 2–9. These convert into 240 Tycoon Coins.

Because the shop offers free and Gem-purchased rewards between paid bundles, progressing through the tiers gives players considerably more value than purchasing Amethysts from standalone bundles.

### Getting 100 Crimson Moonlight for $15.95

![](/uploads/screenshot-20261015-151438-net5mp.png)

This is where the event becomes particularly interesting.

Players who complete their free activities and purchase the VIP Pass can obtain 2,270 Tycoon Coins. They need just 230 more to purchase 100 Crimson Moonlight.

![](/uploads/screenshot-20261015-151255-g2yrml.png)

By progressing through the first nine Gilded Club tiers, they obtain another 240 coins.

The total monetary cost is:

* VIP Pass: $4.99
* Gilded Club paid tiers: $10.96
* Gilded Club Gem purchases: 1,000 Gems

**Total: $15.95 + 1,000 Gems for 100 Crimson Moonlight**, assuming all event activities are completed.

Players also receive the VIP Pass rewards, additional resources from Gilded Club purchases, and other items along the way.

That makes this one of the most interesting low-spender opportunities in the event.

The calculation assumes seven daily free claims, full Max Bounty completion, and completion of all 30 VIP Pass levels.

## Is It Worth Spending More in the Gilded Club?

Beyond the first few tiers, the Gilded Club introduces increasingly expensive purchases, but also larger rewards.

For example, the later tiers include free Amethyst rewards after paid purchases, alongside additional Gem-based offers.

This means each purchase should be evaluated based on the cumulative rewards it unlocks, not just the Amethysts included in that particular bundle.

However, there are diminishing returns. Once you've obtained enough coins for your target Gallery purchase, additional spending should be justified by the next specific reward you want.

The more expensive Chaos-related rewards require substantially greater investment. For example, a 34,000-coin reward requires the equivalent of 17,000 Amethyst Stones before accounting for event rewards.

![](/uploads/screenshot-20261015-151427-brxp7p.png)

For most players, pursuing these premium rewards through direct purchases will be considerably more expensive than obtaining Crimson Moonlight or Stardust.

**Our recommendation is to take advantage of the early Gilded Club tiers, particularly when they unlock free or Gem-purchased Amethysts, but avoid buying large bundles without a clear reward target.**

## Fortune Wheel – Is Gambling Your Coins Profitable?

The Fortune Wheel allows players to wager Tycoon Coins for a chance to win more coins and additional prizes.

Unfortunately, the expected returns are not particularly attractive.

![](/uploads/screenshot-20261015-151403-1jop9o.png)

Based on the event's published reward probabilities and the initial probability analysis, the expected Tycoon Coin return is approximately:

These are statistical averages, not guarantees. Individual players can win substantially more or lose almost everything they wager.

The key consideration is that **the Fortune Wheel uses the same Tycoon Coins needed for guaranteed Gallery rewards**.

If you gamble 1,000 coins, your expected coin balance after the resulting payouts is approximately 898 coins. You may receive other resources and leaderboard points, but your purchasing power in the Gallery has decreased on average.

### Does Energy Make Gambling Better?

The Fortune Wheel features an Energy meter that provides a 10% discount when fully charged.

For example, a regular spin costing 10 coins drops to 9 coins when the discount is active. A 10× spin costing 100 coins drops to 90.

At the discounted price of 9 coins, the expected return of approximately 8.98 coins is almost break-even.

However, players must first accumulate the Energy required to activate the discount, meaning the overall activity still involves regular-price spins.

The Reward Multiplier also increases both the wager and potential rewards without appearing to improve winning probabilities.

**Our verdict: Gambling is not a reliable way to increase your Tycoon Coin balance.**

The Fortune Wheel can still be worthwhile for players competing for leaderboard prizes or seeking its other rewards, but players targeting guaranteed Gallery purchases should generally save their coins.

## What Are the Best Rewards to Buy?

The Private Treasure Gallery contains a wide range of rewards, but two stand out for ordinary players.

**100 Crimson Moonlight – 2,500 Tycoon Coins**

This is arguably the most attractive purchase for players who need Crimson Moonlight. The relatively low coin requirement, combined with the VIP Pass and early Gilded Club tiers, makes it accessible without enormous spending.

**100 Stardust – 1,000 Tycoon Coins**

Stardust is an excellent alternative for free-to-play players or those who need the resource for their current Immortal progression.

The larger artifact and Chaos-related rewards can be valuable, but their much higher currency requirements make them substantially less attractive for most low and moderate spenders.

## Final Recommendations

Tycoon's Club is an unusual event because its best value appears concentrated at the lowest spending levels.

For just $4.99, the premium VIP Pass supplies substantial currency and additional resources. With a relatively small investment in the Gilded Club, players can reach the 2,500 coins required for 100 Crimson Moonlight.

Beyond that point, the cost of obtaining additional high-end rewards increases significantly.

Meanwhile, the Fortune Wheel offers exciting potential jackpots but is not an efficient method of accumulating coins over time. Its negative expected return makes guaranteed Gallery purchases the more dependable choice for most players.

**Our recommendation: Buy the VIP Pass if you can complete it, take advantage of the early Gilded Club tiers, and prioritize guaranteed rewards rather than gambling your currency.**

For low spenders especially, 100 Crimson Moonlight for $15.95 plus 1,000 Gems looks like one of the standout opportunities in this new event.

title: Understanding Charles’ Ultimate Ability — Clearing Up the Shield Absorption Misconception
summary: Charles’ ultimate ability has been one of the more frequently misunderstood skills in Infinity Kingdom, largely due to how its second clause is worded. On the surface, the description seems straightforward:
markdown:
### Introduction

Charles’ ultimate ability has been one of the more frequently misunderstood skills in *Infinity Kingdom*, largely due to how its second clause is worded. On the surface, the description seems straightforward:

> *“Creates a shield for all units that absorbs damage (400%). Your Shield absorption will increase by additional 150% for 6 seconds.”*

The first part is streight forward: a 400% shield applied to all allied units. The confusion starts with the second sentence. It reads like a general amplification effect, leading many to assume that *any* shield generated by Charles during those 6 seconds becomes stronger, right?

That assumption, however, does not match how the mechanic turns out to actually work. Let's dive in!

---

### What the Ability Actually Does

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-27.png)

Let’s break the skill into its real functional components:

#### Base Effect

- Charles casts his ultimate.
- All allied units (including himself) receive a shield equal to **400% of his relevant scaling stat** (Aptitude-based).

#### Additional Absorption Clause

- The “+150% shield absorption for 6 seconds”:  - **Applies only to Charles himself**
- **Applies only to the shield generated by his ultimate**
- **Does not affect any other shield sources**

In practical terms:

- Allies each receive a **400% shield**
- Charles receives:  - A **400% base shield**
- Plus an additional **150% of that base value**, resulting in a **total of 600% shield**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-29-1012x1024.png)

This is super important to understand, because scaling shield values - if that was possible - would open up to huge synergy builds with multiple shielding effects on Charles like Energy Shield, Jade Barrier, Sturdy Barrier, etc.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-30.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-31.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-32.png)

That however is **NOT**possible, contrary to what I see many thinking and building for both in theoretical forums and in-game.

---

### How the 6-Second Window Works

The timing component is equally important and often overlooked.

- The **extra 200% shield value (600% total vs. 400%) is temporary**
- It lasts for **6 seconds only**
- If that additional portion is not fully consumed within that time, **it expires**

So functionally:

- Charles has a **stronger initial shield buffer**
- But only part of it is guaranteed to remain beyond 6 seconds

This makes the effect more of a niche **front-loaded survivability boost**, not a sustained **scaling mechanic**.

---

### What It Does Not Do

This is where most misconceptions come from.

The 150% increase **does NOT**:

- Amplify **Energy Shield** (Tower of Knowledge)
- Enhance **Sturdy Barrier** (Talent specialization)
- Boost shields from other immortals

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-28-1024x836.png)

Even if Charles triggers another shield effect during that period, it behaves completely normally. This has been verified and confirmed via communication with the development team (through IKVIP discussions).

---

### Conclusion Summary

Charles’ ultimate is often misread, but its real function is quite precise:

- **All allies receive a 400% shield**
- **Charles alone receives a 600% shield (400% + 150%)**
- The extra portion:  - **Lasts 6 seconds**
- **Expires if unused**
- **No other shield effects are amplified**

Understanding this properly helps avoid building around nonexistent synergies and instead positions Charles where he performs best: as a frontline stabilizer with strong early durability.

Once you view the skill through that lens, his role in defensive compositions becomes much clearer—and much more reliable.

---

markdown:
Water without Attila

First of all, water without Attila is like ice cream on a cold winter’s day, you can do it and some might enjoy it, but it’s a lot better when the suns out. Attila is an extremely powerful Immortal (one of the absolute best Immortals in the game) and water marches without him suffers. Since Attila is a semi-paywalled Immortal (available in bundles and through the pearl shop) he can also be collected from the arena, and it should be the goal of anyone running water to build him as soon as possible. In the meantime, however, there are a few alternatives for the free-to-play/low spenders out there.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Skaermbillede-2022-06-08-140942-1024x498.png)

*OBS: Beware, that I cannot do a water guide with any meaning to it without both Merlin and Attila. I would recommend anyone playing IK to at least buy the extra builder and get Merlin from that. But if you are not going to build either one then you should stop building water and focus on Contention of Relics and build fire instead. Fire is a thousand times stronger than water without the two strongest Immortals, Merlin and Attila.*

**Despite the above, I have been getting a lot of requests from players asking for guides on water builds.**This article is for all the many water players out there! **In this article, I will not dive deep into the builds, but instead, explain the logic and present the best options for you to build into.**

## Logic behind composing water builds

Some of you ask for cheap/F2P setups, some for light spending, and some want to beat holy with water. So, I have made a collection of water guides and builds to help you on your way to greatness! *While you run these no-Attila builds, you should really focus on getting as many Attila shards in arena as possible!*

I have gathered a few diferent builds that I think you might find interesting to read more about. They work in very different ways, and therefore they all have their own dedicated article explaining the builds in detail. However, **you must understand the logic behind them in order to choose what you want to do with your water.**

### Logic behind water builds

As an Infinity Kingdom player you are faced with many facets of the game. There is a PvP element in SvS (maybe in Norheim), in Arena and occationally once in a blue moon you will maybe do a real Illusion Battle (non prime league). You also have PvE content in two primary shapes: (1) Fighting gnomes and / or event-gnome-camps where you face a team of gnome Immortals on the battlefield. Here you want consistency to grind it out, making Barca a solid choice. You also have gnome bosses and the spider boss twice a week where you only face a single enemy. This makes Barca utterly useless but also makes Hippolyta extreemly strong.

As such you have to figure out what is important for you. Which elements of Infinity Kingdom are you struggling with the most and how do you like to play the game? Do you want to farm gnomes and compete in PvP with Barca? Do you want to slay bosses like they are wet noodles with Hippolyta? Want to build out a crit-chase march for arena with William?

You have a many different options as a water user for compositions in varying price ranges (incl. alternatives for players unable to max Attila). Below I have outlined the best builds for you who want to run water even **without**Attila. Lastly, I also added the pure-water build which you want to move towards as you get Attila shards from the market. When / if you are looing for some more advanced builds later on, see my other guide on spender water builds where you will find Bathony and Khan can take water to new heights!

## Free to play without farming Attila!

**The cheap 1-dollar builds**: Here we unlock Merlin, but we need someone to fill in while we build out Attila (before we move on to the second build). We want to run one of three combinations:

1. [Merlin, Yoshi, Herald, **Barca** (strongest but requires Barca unique)](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/elements/water/water-with-hannibal-barca/)
2. [Merlin, Yoshi, Herald, **Hippolyta** (best for bosses)](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/elements/water/f2p-water-build-hippolyta-replacing-attila/)
3. [Merlin, Yoshi, Herald, **William** (solid all round)](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/elements/water/water-with-william/)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/merlin-300x300.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/williami-250x300.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/hippolyte-300x300.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/haraldIII-300x300.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/hannibal-300x300.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/minamotonoyoshitsune-300x169.png)

## Free to play with Attila!

- **Water pure**. Here we rely on the core water Immortals Merlin and Attila to nuke and control the battlefield.
- [We run: Merlin, Yoshi, Attila, Herald.](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/elements/water/pure-water-yoshi-merlin-attila-herald/)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Skaermbillede-2022-06-08-141227.png)

If you are a light-spender or have considered spending a little in Infinity Kingdom, you can get a lot of value from little spending by developing into water builds with Genghis Khan or Bathony. Khan can be unlocked free of charge via Golden Path, but realistically you need to spend to have the gem supply and market refreshes to get him to max without building for years... So, if you are a low or light spender you might want to check out my article on low to mid spender water marches here.

title: Understanding Second Wind
summary: In Infinity Kingdom, defeat can sting, especially when your Prosperity drops to zero and you're forced to relocate. However, the game provides a critical mechanic to help soften the blow: Second Wind. This system…
markdown:
In *Infinity Kingdom*, defeat can sting, especially when your Prosperity drops to zero and you're forced to relocate. However, the game provides a critical mechanic to help soften the blow: **Second Wind**. This system rewards you with a significant stash of resources once you've been zeroed, helping you get back on your feet faster. But how exactly does Second Wind work? Is it random? Can it be optimized? In this guide, we dive deep into the mechanics behind Second Wind, using in-game testing, community observations, and real player experiences.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/image-117-1024x575.png)

---

## What is Second Wind?

Second Wind is a compensation system triggered when your Prosperity hits zero and you are forcibly relocated. Once you're zeroed, a 15-minute timer begins, and when it ends, you will automatically "fly" to a new random location on the map. At this point, you'll receive an in-game mail offering a one-time resource compensation package.

This compensation is not random—it is based on ***how many troops have died***since the last time you were zeroed. You can see this in the resources returned. Look at the image above, I get around double food - that is troop production costs!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/image-126-1024x153.png)

### Second Wind serves two purposes:

1. It helps you recover from being zeroed by refunding some of the resources lost in training your troops.
2. It encourages active PvP participation without punishing players into total economic ruin.

---

## How Resource Compensation is Calculated

Through in-depth testing and analysis, it has become clear that Second Wind bases its compensation on the **resource cost of the troops you've lost** since your last zeroing.

A few key points:

- The amount of food is **double** that of the other resources. This directly reflects the training cost structure for troops (e.g. training T5 Bowmen costs 2.1M food and 1.1M of each other resource).
- The compensation doesn't appear to factor in losses from garrison alone—it includes all troop deaths, particularly those in **Training Grounds** and **Hospital**.

This proves that Second Wind is highly correlated with troop losses. It’s not based on your power, troop tiers alone, or a fixed value. That being said, there is also a minimum amount or a default base reward in Second Wind, which you get regardless of troop losses. This seems dependent on your Walls level. **The vast majority of the resources from Second Wind comes from Troop Losses.**

---

## Important Mechanics to Know

- **Triggering Second Wind**: Only when your Prosperity reaches zero and you are relocated by force ("fly") will Second Wind be activated.
- **Cooldown or Accumulation?**: Troop losses seem to accumulate over time until you are zeroed. There does not appear to be a daily reset or clear cap, though older losses seems to decay somewhat in Second-Wind-RSS-Value.

---

## How to Optimize Second Wind

If you're planning to fight a lot or participate in honor-farming, **Second Wind can be a powerful part of your economy**.

Here are some strategies:

- **Farm Yourself**: As seen in tests, an alt that’s been attacked frequently (e.g. for honor farming) accumulates massive troop losses. Zeroing such an account results in a large Second Wind compensation.
- **Time It During Events**: If you're competing in a high-resource-demand event (like City Expansion), getting zeroed at the right time can supply you with tens of millions in resources for upgrades.
- **Avoid Small Zeroings**: A single minor defeat won’t provide much value. Let troop losses build over time if you can absorb the risk, then get zeroed for a much more rewarding Second Wind.

**Tip**: When I need resources on my main, I make sure I sit the night over in the snow in Legion of Frostborne. That takes my Prosperity to 1 meaning I will be zeroed in a single attack. Then I kill myself with an alt. I then gain the Second Wind Resource boost based on the troops I have lost fighting over the course of the last few days or even weeks.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Does Second Wind return 100% of lost resources?** No. The exact amount is unclear, but from player testing, it appears to refund **10–20% of the total value** of lost troops, though this may vary slightly depending on how full your TG was and what troop tiers you lost.

**Do resources from Second Wind go into protected storage?** Yes, they are granted as protected resources. They cannot be stolen by an attacker after you’ve been zeroed.

**What if I haven’t been zeroed in a long time?** You may have a very large compensation stored up. Second Wind remembers troop deaths across days or even weeks if you haven't flown, which means your compensation can become massive if you’ve been fighting hard. Note that there does seem to be some diminishing / decay factor on this. If you are idle for a year dont expect a big Second Wind... but hey, who is.

---

## Conclusion

**Second Wind is not just a backup plan—it’s a smart part of your economy in *Infinity Kingdom***. Once seen as a mysterious or random system, it’s now understood as a strategic tool for resource management and recovery. By keeping track of your troop losses and understanding the mechanics behind Prosperity, troop deaths, and defeat, you can time your zeroing to extract maximum value.

So next time you’re about to be zeroed, don’t panic. Smile, hit that timer, and look forward to your Second Wind.

title: Understanding Spender Water Builds
summary: This article reflects on the logic behind building more advanced water marches. Water has a core problem: Yoshi is very weak. Water have some of the strongest Immortals to choose from: Merlin, Attila, Ragnar, Ramssess…
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Skaermbillede-2022-06-08-140942-1024x498.png)

### Advanced water spender builds

This article reflects on the logic behind building more advanced water marches. Water has a core problem: Yoshi is very weak. Water have some of the strongest Immortals to choose from: Merlin, Attila, Ragnar, Ramssess, Herald. All viable and strong, problem is that there is only really Merlin in the backline to deal damage. We can solve this problem in a number of ways:

## Water with Dido-Merlin

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/dido-1.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/merlin-1.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/attila.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/haraldIII.png)

We run a defensive water where we use Dido to protect and boost the damage output of Merlin. Best combined with Ramssess for defense and Attila for physical damage and control. This is a VERY strong build that will perform well in most all situations. I even seen earth mains being taken down with this.

If you are spending a little on the daily bundles, you accumulate a lot of pearls quite fast. Use these to unlock Dido! She is an awesome support Immortal for water and if you run her right your Merlin can nuke your enemies like there’s no tomorrow!

1. **[Dido, Merlin, Attila, Ramesses.](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/elements/water/diddo-merlin-offense/)**

## Water with Bathony

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/elizabethbathory-1.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/merlin-1.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/attila.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/haraldIII-1.png)

There are three variations of this build:

1. **[Bathony as support:](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/elements/water/water-with-support-bathony/)** This is an extremely powerful build. We run: Bathony, Merlin, Attila, Herald in order to maximize our debuffs and boost the damage of Bathony / Merlin to the absolute max. You should prioritize unique artifact on Attila as quickly as possible. **This is my personal favorite setup and my recommendation to run in most situations.**
2. **[Merlin as support:](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/elements/water/water-with-bathony-and-support-merlin/)** We rely on his strong base damage to get some hits in as we support Bathony with assist. By securing a Bathony on the highest possible troop count, she can kill the entire enemy team by herself!
3. **[We run both Merlin and Bathony nukers](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/elements/water/water-with-bathony-double-dps-backline/)**. Here we use all the strongest magic passives to boost Merlin while leaving Bathony with only absolute defense to protect her troop count.

These variations all work very well. Ultimately, **it is up to the composition of your secondary march which to run**. I personally love fire teams because the damage they are able to dish out in seconds is unrivaled by anything else. Also, fire scales very well off of blessings (of which there are many to spare for a secondary march). Therefore, I recommend doing a defensive Merlin (option 3) and a double mage fire as your secondary team and using all the magic passives here.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/genghiskhan-1.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/merlin-1.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/attila.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/haraldIII-1.png)

Finally, we have a specialist water setup to counter the big whales you undoubtably are meeting in SvS and back when there was still IB's to play... If you want to have a chance versus big holy marches, you need to rally and you need to have Khan. Breaking a holy requires a Khan march up front in a rally. Holy relies on securing a high troopcount throughout the fight, if you are able to take them down to 60-70% HP then anyone can finish the job. By making a dent in the troop count of a holy march right from the beginning, it will die even fighting a more standard main march water/earth/fire/wind/lightning/shadow.

- **[Anti-holy rally team.](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/elements/water/water-with-khan-holy-counter/)** If you want to compete at the highest levels of Infinity Kingdom, you are going to be struggling to fight off holy marches with your water (or any other element for that matter). Fear not! Whilst you might not be able to straight-up win 1-on-1 versus a holy march with 40k more power than your water, this setup will make a hell of a dent and is PERFECT as the first march in a rally.
You will run: Merlin, Khan, Attila, Ragnar or Merlin, Khan Attila, Herald (run Ragnar if you have his unique artifact with the same ToK skills as Herald).

title: Understanding the Spider Boss Combat Mechanics
summary: Titanula is one of the few PvE encounters in Infinity Kingdom where understanding the boss has a greater impact than simply increasing your march power. Players often spend weeks optimizing immortals and skills for…
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-156-1024x565.png)

## Introduction

Titanula is one of the few PvE encounters in *Infinity Kingdom* where understanding the boss has a greater impact than simply increasing your march power. Players often spend weeks optimizing immortals and skills for higher damage, yet many overlook the mechanics that determine whether those damage dealers can actually perform throughout the fight.

Unlike most enemies, Titanula follows fixed targeting rules. Its attacks are completely predictable, allowing you to decide exactly which immortals will absorb damage and which will remain protected. Combined with the permanent Wounded effect introduced halfway through the encounter, those mechanics shape almost every successful Spider Boss build.

Once you understand how the boss works, the reasoning behind high-end Titanula marches becomes much easier to appreciate.

---

## Titanula's Targeting Defines the Entire Encounter

The first mechanic to understand is also the most important: Titanula always attacks the **front-left immortal** with its basic attacks.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-157-1024x444.png)

At first glance this might not seem particularly significant, but it becomes much more important once the boss begins using its ultimate. Contrary to what many players assume, Titanula does **not** deal full area-of-effect damage. Instead, its ultimate attacks in a straight line, striking the front-left immortal and the immortal positioned directly behind them.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-159.png)

That means only one side of your formation is taking meaningful damage throughout the battle.

Once you know this, the positioning of most Spider Boss marches suddenly makes sense. Rather than placing damage dealers across both sides of the formation, experienced players deliberately stack their defensive and support immortals in Titanula's attack lane while keeping both primary damage dealers on the opposite side.

The reason is simple. An immortal's damage gradually falls as troop count decreases, so every attack your damage dealer avoids translates directly into higher damage for the remainder of the battle. Protecting Tutankhamun or Yoshitsune often provides a larger increase in total damage than replacing either immortal with a theoretically stronger alternative.

---

## The Battle Changes at 50% Health

Once Titanula falls below 50% HP, the encounter enters its second phase.

At this point the boss permanently applies the **Wounded** debuff, preventing all healing for the remainder of the fight. Any strategy built around sustaining your march through healing immediately loses much of its value, shifting the focus entirely toward maximizing damage before the battle ends.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/image-158.png)

Interestingly, one of the strongest support combinations in the game continues working despite healing being disabled.

**Wine and Dine** doesn't trigger when healing is successfully restored. It triggers whenever an immortal **attempts** to receive healing. As a result, **Fountain of Life** continues activating Wine and Dine's Damage Dealt buff every six seconds throughout the second half of the encounter, even though no health is actually recovered.

It's a subtle interaction that many players miss, but it's also one of the reasons the combination appears in so many optimized Spider Boss marches.

---

## Building Around the Boss

Once these mechanics are understood, building a Titanula march becomes much less about finding the highest Combat Power and much more about working with the encounter itself.

A good Spider Boss march generally follows a few simple principles. Your toughest immortal occupies the front-left position to absorb Titanula's attacks, with another support immortal directly behind them to take the secondary hit from the boss's ultimate. Both primary damage dealers are positioned on the opposite side of the formation, preserving their troop count for as long as possible, while healing is replaced by buffs that continue providing value after the Wounded phase begins.

Many of the strongest Spider Boss teams may look unusual at first glance, but they're all built around these same underlying mechanics. **[For build guides specifically crafted for the killing bosses, read more here!](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/elements/boss-killing-builds/)**

---

## Conclusion

Titanula rewards understanding rather than improvisation. The boss follows fixed targeting rules, attacks only one side of your formation, and completely changes the value of healing once the battle reaches its second half. Those mechanics explain why successful Spider Boss marches are often positioned differently from standard PvE teams and why certain skill combinations consistently outperform others.

Before experimenting with different immortals or chasing small damage increases through skill changes, it's worth making sure your formation is built around the encounter itself. More often than not, understanding Titanula's mechanics produces a larger improvement than simply adding more power to your march.
