title: Unique Artifacts (added 2.8.7) - are they worth buying? Pricing and value estimates
summary: With patch 2.8.7, the Daily Pearls Shop received a big update: you can now directly buy Unique Artifacts using Mysterious Pearls. For many players, this looks tempting — but is it really worth it? Let’s break it down in…
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/image-44-1024x330.png)

## Infinity Kingdom Guide: Daily Pearls Shop Update (Patch 2.8.7)

With patch **2.8.7**, the **Daily Pearls Shop** received a big update: you can now directly buy **Unique Artifacts** using **Mysterious Pearls**. For many players, this looks tempting — but is it really worth it? Let’s break it down in detail.

---

## What’s New in the Pearls Shop?

There are now **two new artifact purchase options**:

1. **Shadow/Holy Immortal Unique Artifact Chest**  - Cost: **360 Mysterious Pearls**
- Gives a unique artifact for a Shadow or Holy immortal.
2. **Golden Path Season Selection Chest**  - Cost: **240 Mysterious Pearls**
- Lets you pick a unique artifact for one of the Golden Path immortals.
- Immortals included: **Matilda, Yi Sun-Sin (YSS), Seon, Artemisia, Louis IX, Tokugawa, Trajan, Cao Cao, Ragnar, Darius**, and a handful of others.

---

## Why This Is Important

Unique artifacts are **power spikes**. They unlock the full potential of an immortal and are often the difference between a mid-tier build and a meta build. Until now:

- **Holy/Shadow artifacts** have been relatively accessible via events, rewards, and steady progression.
- **Golden Path artifacts**, on the other hand, have been *extremely limited*. Unless you participated heavily in Golden Path seasons, getting them was nearly impossible.

So this change gives players another way to get their hands on **rare season-specific uniques** — but at a steep cost.

---

## Cost Analysis

Let’s break down what these purchases actually mean in gem and dollar terms.

### Golden Path Selection Chest (240 Pearls)

- **Gem value:** ~7,920 gems
- **Dollar equivalent:** $72 if you buy Pearls through Daily Pearl packs
- **Time:** 12 days of buying Daily Pearls packs to accumulate enough currency
- **Comparison:** You obtain the same item for 600 Golden Path coins = 9,000 gems ($81.8)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/image-40-1024x582.png)

💡 Key takeaway: **Similar cost to GP uniques, but without grinding Golden Path.**

---

### Shadow/Holy Artifact Chest (360 Pearls)

- **Gem value:** ~11,880 gems
- **Dollar equivalent:** $108 purchased via Daily Pearl packs
- **Time:** 18 days of Pearl purchases to gather enough currency

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/image-41-1024x724.png)

💡 Key takeaway: **Overpriced compared to how many Holy/Shadow artifacts you can naturally obtain through events and game rewards.**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/image-42.png)

**value estimates are made using the standard 10$ bundles offering 1100 gems.*

---

## Veteran Recommendation

### 1. Do NOT buy the Shadow/Holy Unique Chest

- You’ll naturally collect plenty of Shadow and Holy uniques just by playing.
- Events flood you with Shadow/Holy artifact fragments over time. If you main shadow or holy you likely do not need one more expensive artifact, but if you do - hey, it's here!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/image-43-1024x534.png)

- Spending 360 Pearls here is a **trap for newer players** who don’t yet see how common these will become.

### 2. Golden Path Selection Chest: Only If You Desperately Need It

- This is the **only good reason** to spend Pearls here.
- If you are actively running **Golden Path immortals** (Fu Fei/YSS/Seon/Artemisia builds are still quite relevant for mid-spenders), this can save your build.
- But beware: 240 Pearls is still **very expensive**. Think carefully before pulling the trigger.

### 3. Grind Golden Path for Free Whenever Possible

- Don’t forget you can still earn **Golden Path currency for free** through consistent participation.
- The Daily Pearls option should be treated as a **last resort** if you absolutely cannot wait.

---

## Final Thoughts

The **Daily Pearls Shop update** is a mixed bag:

- The **Shadow/Holy option** is essentially a **Pearl sink** — avoid it.
- The **Elemental Selection chest**, while expensive, is an option for players who wants to rush artifacts for the seasonal immortals, players who missed or skipped earlier seasons or who just need a critical artifact to unlock fast to unluck a new build’s full power.

title: Unique Elemental Specific ToK Skills
summary: Elemental Protection Skills – Are They Worth Using?
markdown:
**Elemental Protection Skills – Are They Worth Using?**

*A breakdown of one of the most underused skill families in Infinity Kingdom*

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-24.png)

---

## 🔍 What Are Elemental Protection Skills?

Elemental Protection Skills are **situational Tower of Knowledge skills** that provide passive effects tied to specific elements (Wind, Lightning, Earth, Water, and Fire). They:

- Have a **55% chance to trigger every 12 seconds**, lasting for 12 seconds.
- Offer a **base effect** usable by any Immortal.
- Provide a **bonus effect** when used on an Immortal that matches the skill’s element.

These effects sound appealing — but they rarely make the cut for serious PvP or high-tier play.

---

## 🧪 Skill-by-Skill Breakdown

### 🌪️ Wind Protection

- **Effect**: 25% dodge rate boost (55% chance every 12s).
- **Bonus**: If a Wind Immortal dodges, it gives a shield to a random ally (120% damage absorb).

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-25.png)

**Verdict**: Too RNG-heavy. Dodge isn't a reliable mechanic, and the shield goes to a random ally. Better to use **Agile** or skip altogether.

---

### ⚡ Lightning Protection

- **Effect**: Grants a 40% chance for normal attacks to stun for 3s (triggered every 12s).
- **Bonus**: If used by a Lightning Immortal, their next ultimate gets +30% damage after a stun.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-26.png)

**Verdict**: Decent base stun, but the chain of effects (trigger → stun → ultimate) is too situational. Can be fun for experimental builds or alt marches.

---

### 🌍 Earth Protection

- **Effect**: Removes Silence/Root and grants 200 energy (55% chance every 12s).
- **Bonus**: For Earth Immortals, every 100 energy regen = +5% ultimate damage.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-27.png)

**Verdict**: Cleanse effect is nice, but bonus is weak. Earth teams rely more on shields and sustain, not burst damage.

---

### 🌊 Water Protection

- **Effect**: Reduces critical damage taken by 21%.
- **Bonus**: If a Water Immortal receives crit damage, they heal for 45% of the damage taken.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-28.png)

**Verdict**: Could work versus crit-heavy teams (e.g. Seondeok), but inconsistent. Could support Merlin builds, but better survivability options exist.

---

### 🔥 Flame Protection

- **Effect**: Increases critical hit rate by 6%.
- **Bonus**: Fire Immortals get +21% crit damage on top.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-29.png)

**Verdict**: The most viable of the bunch. Can make Fire marches hit very hard — perfect for secondary marches focused on burst damage.

---

## ❌ Why They’re Rarely Used

- **Unreliable Activation**: 55% chance means you can go entire battles without effects triggering at the right time.
- **Too Niche**: Bonus effects only work on element-matching Immortals, limiting flexibility.
- **Better Options**: Skills like **Adrenaline Rush**, **Shelter**, **Weakness**, or **Rage Blessing** offer consistent, team-wide value.

---

## ⚔️ When to Use Them (If At All)

Here are some niche cases where Elemental Protection Skills *might* be useful:

| Skill | Niche Use Case |
| --- | --- |
| Wind Protection | Dodge-based PvE setups, alternative shield builds |
| Lightning Protection | Crowd control builds in secondary marches |
| Earth Protection | Silence-heavy matchups (e.g. Mysterium bosses) |
| Water Protection | Anti-crit defense vs burst teams |
| Flame Protection | Secondary Fire burst marches with Wu or Hippolyta |

---

## 🧙‍♂️ What About Holy, Shadow, or Chaos Protection?

These don’t exist yet — but here's what they *could* look like:

- **Holy Protection**: Reduces healing or energy regen for enemies.
- **Shadow Protection**: Reduces magic damage taken and resists Silence.
- **Chaos Protection**: Counters Confusion or random debuffs.

Would they change the meta? Probably not — but they’d be fun tools for creative builds.

---

## 🧾 Final Verdict

Elemental Protection Skills are **themed and interesting**, but rarely provide enough value to be worth a skill slot. Use them:

- For fun or experimentation.
- In lower-tier marches.
- When you’re out of better options.

Otherwise, your skill slots are better spent on **tried-and-true options** that work in all situations, not just when RNG cooperates.

---

Want to test them out for yourself? Try running a **full Protection March** in Arena and see how it feels!

title: Unleash the Arcane Fury: Skills for Magical DPS
summary: In the mystical realms of Infinity Kingdom, mastering the art of magical damage can turn your immortals into formidable forces to be reckoned with. Understanding the skills that enhance magical DPS is crucial for…
markdown:
In the mystical realms of Infinity Kingdom, mastering the art of magical damage can turn your immortals into formidable forces to be reckoned with. Understanding the skills that enhance magical DPS is crucial for crafting a powerful strategy. In this guide, we'll explore the skills designed for magical DPS and the heroes who can harness their arcane might to devastating effect.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-1024x481.png)

### 1. Annihilation

Annihilation is a skill that truly shines when bestowed upon magical backline DPS immortals such as Merlin, Baldwin, and Himiko. These heroes are known for their prowess in dealing magical damage from a safe distance. Annihilation enhances their destructive potential by increasing their magic attack damage, turning their spells into devastating attacks that can decimate enemy forces.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-1.png)

For heroes who rely on the power of their spells to dominate the battlefield, Annihilation is an essential skill to consider. It transforms them into formidable spellcasters capable of obliterating foes with their arcane might.

### 2. Toxin Nova and Fire Nova

Toxin Nova and Fire Nova are skills perfectly suited for magical backline DPS immortals like Wu, Merlin, and Baldwin. What sets these skills apart is their synergy with abilities like Chase. The damage-over-time (DoT) effects from Toxin Nova and Fire Nova provide an excellent opportunity for Chase to trigger, thanks to their continuous damage output.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-2.png)

Chase is especially efficient when paired with skills like Nova or Death Breath, which reliably proc magic damage. Additionally, combining Chase with Weakness can further increase your critical hit rate, making it a potent addition to your magical DPS arsenal.

### 3. Chase

Chase is a versatile skill that can benefit any magical backline DPS immortal, but it truly excels with heroes like Wu. Wu's increased crit rate from William or Trajan, coupled with her high energy regeneration, allows her to cast her ultimate more frequently, increasing the chances of Chase triggering.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-3.png)

Chase becomes especially effective when used in tandem with other skills that reliably proc magic damage, such as Nova or Death Breath. Its three-second cooldown adds an additional layer of strategy to consider when planning your attacks, making it a skill that requires precise timing and coordination.

### 4. Spell Disintegrator

Spell Disintegrator is a skill that finds its place with Wu and any other magical backline DPS immortals. Its effectiveness is further amplified when paired with Chase, thanks to the possibility of a three-second proc.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-4.png)

This synergy ensures that your magical DPS immortals can consistently deal significant damage, wreaking havoc on your enemies.

### 5. Stormeye

Stormeye is a skill suitable for any magical backline DPS immortal. It can be particularly effective when combined with Fighting Will, further enhancing the durability of your heroes.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-5.png)

By increasing their attack and crit rates, Stormeye empowers your magical DPS immortals to unleash devastating spells with precision and efficiency.

### 6. Death Breath

Death Breath is a skill that can benefit any DPS backline immortal, including those specializing in magical damage. It adds an extra layer of versatility to your hero's abilities, making them more formidable in both close and ranged combat.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-6.png)

### 7. Poison Thorn

Poison Thorn is a skill that greatly benefits both the damage output and the utility effect of your magic damage immortals. In addition to providing excellent single-target damage, it also automatically targets the enemy with the highest physical attack attributes. This means that the damage deal carries greater value than random targeted damage, because we are reducing the troop count of one of the most powerful and important enemy Immortals on the playingfield.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-7.png)

Lastly, Poison Thron also applies a healing debuff to the enemy, one which dampens healing recieved by 50%. This can be a significant boost to your combat prowess against powerful sustain setups and it is the only tower of knowledge skill with a healing reduction effect.

In conclusion, harnessing the power of magical DPS skills is essential for conquering the diverse challenges of Infinity Kingdom. Whether you're empowering magical backline DPS immortals with Annihilation, Chase, or Nova skills, or enhancing their survivability with Stormeye and Spell Disintegrator, these skills can turn your heroes into unstoppable arcane warriors.

So, delve into the arcane arts, refine your strategy, and watch as your magical DPS immortals become the champions of Infinity Kingdom, wielding the very forces of magic to shape the battlefield in your favor.

title: Unleash the Auras
summary: In the ever-evolving battlefield of Infinity Kingdom, auras hold the power to tip the scales of battle in your favor. Understanding the auras that can empower your immortals is crucial for crafting a winning strategy.…
markdown:
### Unleash the Auras: Enhancing Your Immortals in Infinity Kingdom

In the ever-evolving battlefield of Infinity Kingdom, auras hold the power to tip the scales of battle in your favor. Understanding the auras that can empower your immortals is crucial for crafting a winning strategy. In this guide, we'll delve into the auras designed to enhance your heroes and the heroes who can best utilize these effects to become unstoppable forces on the battlefield.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-59-1024x582.png)

### 1. Sacrifice

Sacrifice is an aura that shines when assigned to heroes like Trajan, Qin, Dido, or any other immortals who don't rely on dealing damage. These heroes can thrive even if they aren't the primary damage dealers on the field.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-50.png)

Sacrifice becomes especially effective in marches featuring numerous DPS immortals, such as fire-focused teams. It allows your support immortals to take on a critical role by absorbing damage, protecting your more damage-oriented heroes.

### 2. Berserk

Berserk is an aura designed for heroes like Alex and Hannibal. It particularly excels in marches where there are numerous immortals relying on normal attacks or Adrenaline Rush.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-51.png)

The aura boosts the damage output of your immortals, turning them into relentless attackers capable of swiftly dealing with opponents.

### 3. Malice

Malice is an aura that thrives when assigned to heroes like Charles and Theodora. It finds its true potential in sustain-focused marches that aim to avoid sudden spikes of damage.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-52.png)

By reducing the enemy's damage output, Malice ensures your team can outlast your opponents, gradually chipping away at their forces.

### 4. Misleading

Misleading is an aura that shines in wind or holy marches due to their naturally high dodge rates. It becomes especially effective when combined with other evasion-enhancing skills like Afterimage and Wind Protection.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-53.png)

Misleading makes it challenging for opponents to land critical hits, ensuring your immortals remain resilient and hard to defeat.

### 5. Weakness

Weakness is an aura that is particularly effective in fire marches due to their high critical hit rates. It becomes challenging for abilities like Malice, Dido's epic artifact, or the increased resilience from a high-level dragon to negate the aura's effect.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-54.png)

Weakness ensures that your opponents' attacks are less likely to deal critical damage, increasing your immortals' survivability.

### 6. Coercion

Coercion is an aura that excels in full physical marches, such as holy or wind-earth-hybrid teams.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-55.png)

By reducing the enemy's physical damage, Coercion ensures your immortals can endure prolonged battles and outlast your opponents.

### 7. Shelter

Shelter is an aura that finds its place in sustain-focused marches, like earth or holy teams. It shines against opponents whose attacks are consistently low in damage.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-56.png)

Shelter provides additional protection, ensuring that your immortals remain resilient and can withstand enemy onslaughts.

### 8. Paralysis

Paralysis is an aura that becomes especially effective against wind-earth hybrid teams.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-57.png)

It can disrupt the flow of the battle, impairing the enemy's immortals and giving your team a crucial advantage.

### 9. Spring of Life

Spring of Life is an aura that thrives when assigned to heroes like Theodora and Zenobia. It becomes especially potent when combined with other healing skills like Vitality Touch and Purification.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-58.png)

Spring of Life ensures that your immortals receive continuous healing, allowing them to endure longer and maintain their combat effectiveness.

In conclusion, mastering the art of auras in Infinity Kingdom is essential for constructing a resilient and potent team. Whether you're sacrificing for the greater good, enhancing the berserk rage of your attackers, sowing malice among your enemies, or misleading opponents with elusive tactics, these auras can turn your heroes into unstoppable forces on the battlefield.

So, embrace the power of auras, refine your tactics, and witness your immortals become the champions who lead your army to victory in the world of Infinity Kingdom.

Within the magical realms of Infinity Kingdom, the Tower of Knowledge harbors a wealth of powerful skills that can turn the tide of battles. One such skill, known as "Root," often remains hidden in the shadows despite its remarkable potential. In this article, we shed light on the underrated passive ability of Root, exploring its mechanics, benefits, and strategic applications.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/image-45-1024x543.png)

**Unleashing the Power of Root**: Root is a triggered passive skill found within the Tower of Knowledge. When activated, it possesses a 45% chance to deliver a single instance of 350% magical damage while simultaneously applying the Root control effect to the targeted enemy Immortal. Though classified as a rare-quality skill rather than epic, Root's true strength lies in its versatility and cost-effectiveness.

## Strategic Applications:

1. **Low Soul Crystal Costs**: One of the standout features of Root is its ability to be applied at a relatively low cost. By utilizing this passive skill, players can unleash a formidable control effect and deal substantial magical damage without exhausting excessive resources. This makes Root an excellent choice for those seeking to maximize efficiency while keeping their soul crystal expenditure in check.
2. **Boss Battles and Single Target Encounters**: Root's potency truly shines in boss battles and scenarios where single-target control is crucial. The skill's ability to immobilize an enemy Immortal provides a strategic advantage, preventing them from executing devastating attacks or unleashing powerful skills. Whether it's a formidable boss or a high-priority target, Root can be a game-changer, allowing players to gain the upper hand in challenging encounters.
3. **Synergy with Multiple Mages:** For those commanding a force of two or more mages, Root becomes an invaluable asset. The probability of triggering the passive skill increases with each mage equipped with Root, enhancing the overall control potential of the team. By skillfully coordinating attacks, players can stack Root effects on a single target, effectively immobilizing them for extended periods and mitigating potential threats posed by opposing Immortals.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/image-46-1024x584.png)

**Conclusion**: In the realm of Infinity Kingdom, the Tower of Knowledge offers a myriad of skills to wield, each with its unique attributes and strategic applications. Among them, Root emerges as a hidden gem, often overlooked but holding immense power within its grasp. Its ability to inflict substantial magical damage and apply the Root control effect, combined with its cost-effectiveness, makes Root a must-have skill for those seeking to excel in battles with low soul crystal costs, single-target encounters, and multiple mage setups. Unlock the potential of Root, and watch as your enemies become ensnared in its potent grasp.

title: Unleashing the Fury: Skills for Physical DPS
summary: In the battlefields of Infinity Kingdom, the power of physical damage is a force to be reckoned with. Mastering the skills that enhance physical DPS can transform your immortals into relentless warriors. In this guide…
markdown:
### Unleashing the Fury: Skills for Physical DPS in Infinity Kingdom

In the battlefields of Infinity Kingdom, the power of physical damage is a force to be reckoned with. Mastering the skills that enhance physical DPS can transform your immortals into relentless warriors. In this guide, we'll explore the skills designed for physical DPS and the heroes who can utilize them to unleash chaos on the battlefield.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-9-1024x502.png)

Please make note that the Physical Damage skills relating to normal attack immortals can be found **[here](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/combat/tower-of-knowledge-passives/normal-attack-skills/)**. This guide will cover the remaining more diverse set of physical attack skills.

### 1. Chaotic Blade and Garrote

Chaotic Blade and Garrote are skills that excel in the hands of physical backline DPS immortals, with Seondeok being a standout example. These skills come with damage-over-time (DoT) effects, making them particularly effective at reliably triggering Seondeok's ultimate ability. The continuous damage output from Chaotic Blade and Garrote ensures that Seondeok's ultimate ability is unleashed more often than with most other skills.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-10.png)

When paired with a hero like Seondeok, Chaotic Blade and Garrote allow for a relentless barrage of attacks that can quickly wear down enemy defenses and turn the tide of battle in your favor.

### 2. Desire of Life

Desire of Life is a skill tailor-made for Khan, the formidable warrior of Infinity Kingdom. When equipped on Khan, this skill becomes especially potent. Khan's inherent tankiness combined with Desire of Life makes him a formidable force on the battlefield. The skill's effectiveness is further enhanced when paired with Duel Master, allowing Khan to not only endure more damage but also deal out significant punishment to his foes.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-13.png)

Desire of Life turns Khan into a nearly unbreakable bulwark, capable of withstanding the fiercest of assaults while dealing devastating blows to his enemies.

### 3. Blade Vortex

Blade Vortex is a skill that finds its place with physical DPS immortals in marches running Loki. This skill enhances the damage output of physical attackers, making it a valuable addition to their arsenal.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-14.png)

When paired with heroes who rely on physical damage, Blade Vortex ensures that their attacks are even deadlier, decimating enemy forces with precision and power. Being one of only three effects to provide debuffs for Loki, makes this a powerful skill for late-game whales running Loki setups.

### 4. Death Breath

Death Breath is a versatile skill that can benefit any DPS backline immortal, whether they specialize in physical or magical damage.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-15.png)

This skill adds an extra layer of versatility to your hero's abilities, making them more formidable in both close and ranged combat.

### 5. Sniper

Sniper is a powerful and simple skill. You have a good chance to deal a massive blow to your enemy's backrow. As the name suggests, this is a single target snipe that deals massive damage to the enemy troop count and if set up right you can do a lot of harm to one of your enemy's most valuable combat tools.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-11.png)

Perhaps the strongest aspect of this skill is the fact that it deals 50% increased damage against enemies at more than half their troop count. This makes it extreemly powerful at reducing enemy troop count in the critically important fase of any combat: the first 12-18 seconds.

### 6. Spear Impale

Spear Impale is another powerful skill dealing a high amount of damage to the enemy in front of the Immortal. Running this against a frontline of powerful immortals will make quick work of the enemy troop count as well as provide a solid boost to all physical damage.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/image-12.png)

Powerful took in setups like earth and holy.

**In conclusion**, mastering the art of physical DPS in Infinity Kingdom is all about understanding the skills that can amplify your hero's capabilities. Whether you're unleashing the relentless damage-over-time effects of Chaotic Blade and Garrote with heroes like Seondeok, turning Khan into an unbreakable fortress with Desire of Life, enhancing physical attackers with Blade Vortex, or adding versatility with Death Breath, these skills can turn your heroes into relentless warriors on the battlefield.

So, dive into the chaos of battle, refine your strategy, and witness as your physical DPS immortals become the unstoppable force that carves a path to victory in the world of Infinity Kingdom.

title: Unyielding - a crit skill for physical damage dealers
summary: Unyielding is one of the Epic skills available through the Wish Shop, purchased with Cinders earned primarily from Wisdom Well runs. Because Cinders accumulate slowly and are often spent on several powerful options…
markdown:
### Introduction

**Unyielding** is one of the Epic skills available through the **Wish Shop**, purchased with **Cinders** earned primarily from **Wisdom Well** runs. Because Cinders accumulate slowly and are often spent on several powerful options, players tend to ask the same question: *is Unyielding worth unlocking?*

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/image-189-1024x570.png)

The answer depends largely on how your march is structured and which immortal is carrying the damage. Unyielding is best understood as a **situational power spike skill**—one that can be extremely effective in the right context, but inconsistent if used without considering the mechanics behind it.

This guide explains how Unyielding works, when it performs best, and where experienced players tend to find the most value from it.

---

## Skill Mechanics

**Unyielding activates when an immortal’s troop count drops below 70%.**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/image-186.png)

When triggered, it grants:

- **+50% Critical Rate**
- **Healing effect**

The critical rate boost is the main attraction. A 50% increase is extremely large compared to most other skills and can significantly increase burst damage if the immortal is already built around critical hits. For reference, it is not long since it was perfectly valid to run Rage for a meager 15% crit rate buff when doing high crit burst setups. 50% is absolutely massive! But naturally, it does come at a downside - you must loose troops!

However, the skill has one important limitation: **it only activates once the troop threshold is reached.** If the immortal never drops below 70% troops during combat, the skill provides no benefit at all.

The healing component adds survivability, particularly for immortals who remain alive long enough to benefit from sustained fighting.

---

## Strengths of Unyielding

### High Critical Potential

The **+50% crit rate** can dramatically increase damage output, particularly for physical attackers who already stack crit through:

- Immortal specialization bonuses
- Artifacts
- Supporting skills

In optimized builds, the skill can push an immortal close to near-constant critical hits once the threshold is triggered. For example, doing highly defensive Khan or Bathory builds where you are able to stack enough mitigation to lose troops relatively slowly and not in chuncks of 50-80% at a time, then you can get real value out of this skill. That being said, I find the most useful version of this is leaning into also taking advantage of the sustain trigger on a frontline immortal like Alexander or Ares with super high attack speed for high trigger rates on the sustain effect.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/image-190-1024x566.png)

**This is from an IBL battle, hence the low numbers. 1 million healing is quite significant in IBL.*

### Added Sustain

The healing component helps extend survivability during longer fights. This can allow an immortal to remain active long enough to convert their crit advantage into real damage.

### Effective Against Non-Healing Counters

Unyielding performs best when facing compositions that **do not block healing effects**. Against standard damage or support teams, the sustain can noticeably increase staying power.

---

## Weaknesses and Limitations

### Activation is Situational

The biggest weakness of Unyielding is its **conditional activation**.

Modern PvP battles often fall into two extremes:

- An immortal may be **burst down very quickly**, never benefiting from sustained healing.
- Or they may **remain above 70% troops**, meaning the skill never triggers.

This makes Unyielding inherently less consistent than always-active skills. If you are not able to stack enough mitigation to have troop count reduced slowly in a fight (despite being against big burst e.g. Himiko builds) but instead find yourself dead in 15s from the first crit proc on the enemy ultimate which can one-shot many players, well then this skill gives you 0 value.

Frontloaded quick builds that rely on pressure early also struggle to take advantage, as you need all the power you can get in the first seconds not after each side has dealt a couple blows to each other.

### Healing Counters Exist

Certain immortals, such as **King Emperor**, can negate healing effects. In those cases, Unyielding still provides the critical rate boost, but the sustain portion becomes irrelevant.

### Opportunity Cost

Because Wish Shop skills require **large amounts of Cinders**, unlocking Unyielding means delaying other powerful Cinder skills. For many players, it becomes more of a **secondary or optional investment** rather than an early priority.

---

## Comparison: Unyielding vs Time to Shine

A common comparison is **Time to Shine**, another crit-focused skill.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/image-188-1024x138.png)

**Time to Shine** is generally the more reliable option because its bonuses apply immediately.

**Unyielding**, on the other hand, can outperform it **once triggered**, but requires the correct combat conditions.

For this reason, many experienced players treat Unyielding as a **situational alternative rather than a universal replacement**.

---

## Player Perspective: Frontline Alexander in Illusion Battlegrounds

While Unyielding is often associated with backline carries such as **Khan**, experienced players have found strong results using it on **frontline physical attackers**, particularly **Alexander**. Honestly, this is the main use case I personally see for Unyielding, because the IBL format is not as bursty as hyper-regen crit mage builds in the "real game". While IBL battles are quite short, they are not decided by one-shots, which is quite important here! Anyway, here is how I use Unyielding. From testing in **Illusion Battlegrounds**, this setup has proven surprisingly effective.

Alexander naturally occupies the frontline, which means:

- He **reliably drops below the 70% threshold** during combat.
- His **damage output remains strong even while taking pressure**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/image-187-1024x646.png)

Once Unyielding activates:

- The **50% crit rate dramatically boosts his counter and skill damage**.
- The **healing effect adds sustain**, allowing him to win prolonged one-on-one engagements.

Illusion Battlegrounds also tends to favor **crit stacking for frontline attackers**, making the skill’s effect even more noticeable in that environment.

In practice, this combination allows Alexander to function as a **durable duelist**—a frontline immortal capable of sustaining damage while still delivering meaningful offensive pressure.

---

## When to Use Unyielding

Unyielding tends to perform best in the following scenarios:

### Good Use Cases

- Frontline attackers who **regularly fall below 70% troops**
- Physical carries with **crit-focused builds**
- Long fights where **sustain matters**
- Modes like **Illusion Battlegrounds**, where crit stacking is easier

### Less Ideal Situations

- Glass cannon backlines that die too quickly
- Teams that **rarely lose enough troops to trigger the skill**

---

## Conclusion

Unyielding is a **powerful but situational skill**.

When its activation condition is met, the combination of **50% crit rate and healing** can significantly increase both damage output and survivability. However, because the skill depends on dropping below 70% troops, it lacks the reliability of always-active options like Time to Shine.

For experienced players, Unyielding often works best as an **optional build variation**, particularly on immortals who naturally remain in combat long enough to trigger the effect.

In environments such as **Illusion Battlegrounds**, or on frontline attackers like **Alexander**, the skill can become a surprisingly strong dueling tool that combines damage spikes with sustain.

The key takeaway is simple: **Unyielding rewards the right context.** When paired with a build that reliably activates it, the results can be excellent.

---

title: UPDATE Change - Theia's Roulette Rewards Universal Fragment Chests
summary: Theia's Roulette Event has been going on for a long time now. It is the only method of obtaining many of the most powerful Immortals' Fragments in Infinity Kingdom, namely those of the Holy and Shadow elements. While…
markdown:
Theia's Roulette Event has been going on for a long time now. It is the only method of obtaining many of the most powerful Immortals' Fragments in Infinity Kingdom, namely those of the Holy and Shadow elements. While some Shadow Immortals are available elsewhere e.g. in the Sparks of Galaxy event and Gilgamesh is a F2P holy Immortal, the rest of the holy and shadow roster are exclusively Theia's Roulette rewards.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/image-6-1024x462.png)

Untill now, the event has been dedicated to each Immortal on rotation. E.g. event 1 = Himiko, event 2 = Siegfried, event 3 = Theodora, event 4 = Manco, and so on. However, as the roster for both the holy and the shadow element has grown and grown over time we now have a collection of eight different unique Immortals, four of each element.

1. Siegfried (shadow)
2. Himiko (shadow)
3. Theodora (holy)
4. Manco (holy)
5. Bjorn (shadow)
6. Tomyris (shadow)
7. Khubilai Khan (holy)
8. Nebuchadnezzar ll (holy)

What this means for the game and players, is that in order to upgrade an Immortal to max star-ranks you need multiple events and as such wait for months on end for your Immortal to be available again through the roulette rotation. Since Thiea's Roulette comes around roughtly every 2 weeks, even big whales who want to max an Immortal in insanely inefficient 2 or 3 events would have to wait 16-32 weeks! Months on end to get an Immortal.

**The development team has listened to our cried for help and changed the event by breaking the rotation scheme!**

**This is great news for anyone with a hope or a dream of getting any of the Thiea's Immortals. Most importantly, this is a HUGE advantage for the smaller spenders who go for high efficiency in their spending.**

## The change - breaking the rotation cluster f***

What the change did was make the Bonus Event Bar drop Universal Immortal Fragment chests instead of specific Immortal Fragments. Meaning that while before the first 50-spin bonus rewarded 10x Fragments for only the single Immortal on rotation (e.g. ONLY for Manco) it now drops 10x Fragment chests with which the player can choose what Immortal's Fragments they want.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/Skaermbillede-2023-01-03-144227.png)

This means that for spenders of any size, getting the Immortals you need max rank, no longer requires a long wait between events. Instead, you can get whatever Immortal you want in every single event!

## Why this is a big deal for mid-spenders

This is a huge change for all of the mid-spenders out there. Many of you have either not been able to get your holy or shadow team finished simply because the game forced you to purchase the highly inefficient bundles in order to max out on only 2 or 3 events.

Now you can play the roulette efficiently, spreading out your spending across multiple events to take advantage of the fact that the bonus is much more efficient in the low tier.

For instance, spending only 50 spins rewards you 10 bonus fragments. Spending another 50 rewards you another 10 Fragments (from the 100 bonus). However, then you need to spend 100 spins more to get another 10 bonus fragments (from the 200 bonus) dropping the effiency to half value of your first 100 spins. Moreover, from here it gets increasingly more expensive with a 150 jump and a full 200 jump for the last two tiers. However, the last tier is a 60 fragment drop, which makes a bit more sense.

For pure effiency you always want to stop at 100-spins however, but if you want to go a bit faster then that you can opt for the 200 spin bonus or go for a full 900 spin clear.

You should NEVER stop between 200-900. Always get as close to 200 as you can (not leaving a half empty wheel of course) OR make sure you cap 900.

Check out this effiency table

| Bonus Thresholds | Bonus Rewards | Total Fragments for each threshold | Efficiency (Spins per Fragment) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 50.00 | 10 | 10 | 5.00 |
| 100.00 | 10 | 20 | 5.00 |
| 200.00 | 10 | 30 | 6.67 |
| 350.00 | 10 | 40 | 8.75 |
| 500.00 | 10 | 50 | 10.00 |
| 700.00 | 10 | 60 | 11.67 |
| 900.00 | 60 | 120 | 7.50 |

Best of luck on the wheel! For more information on the costs of maxing Theia's Immortals and some ideas for how to do it efficienty, **[check out my guides here](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/events/wheels-roulette/holy-shadow-immortals-roulette/)**. Be ware that they are a bit old and slightly outdated.

title: Updated: Using Rune Factory to buy shadow and holy immortals
summary: With Sparks of Galaxy removed from rotation, many players assumed Holy and Shadow progression would slow to a crawl. For a while, Rune Factory looked like a strict “100-pull pity” replacement — expensive, rigid, and…
markdown:
## Introduction

With *Sparks of Galaxy* removed from rotation, many players assumed Holy and Shadow progression would slow to a crawl. For a while, Rune Factory looked like a strict “100-pull pity” replacement — expensive, rigid, and heavily dependent on hitting guaranteed jackpots.

That is no longer the case.

The recent changes to Rune Factory fundamentally altered how value is generated. Instead of building toward a 100-energy jackpot, the event now pays out Rune Insignias steadily through smaller drops, with energy resetting on any Rune reward.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-100.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-103-1024x542.png)

This guide breaks down:

- How the **new version** actually works
- What Holy and Shadow fragments cost now
- What you should realistically budget
- How this compares to the old 100-draw pity version

I’ll explain it the way I would to another endgame player looking at real progression numbers — not marketing percentages.

---

## How Rune Factory Works (Current Version)

Each Energy Core equals one pull.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-211.png)

### Per pull drop chances:

- **0.5%** → 70 Rune Insignias
- **12%** → 4 Rune Insignias
- **24%** → 2 Rune Insignias
- Remaining % → no Rune Insignia

### Critical rule change:

- **Energy resets on ANY Rune Insignia drop**
(70, 4, or 2)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-209.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-210.png)

There is still technically a pity at 100 energy.
But reaching 100 now requires **100 consecutive pulls with zero Rune drops**.

The probability of that happening is:

- 63.5% chance of **no**Rune on a single pull

In real gameplay terms, you will essentially never see pity trigger. That alone changes how we evaluate this event compared to the previous version which was all about the 100-energy trigger of the pity mechanic for 70 rune insignias.

---

## The Currency Conversion Chain

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-149-1024x553.png)

- **70 Rune Insignias** → 280 Inferno Insignias
- **450 Inferno Insignias** → 60 Holy or Shadow Immortal fragments

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-148-1024x419.png)

## Expected Value: What You Actually Get Per Pull

Instead of thinking in “cycles,” we now think in **expected Rune per pull**.

### Expected Rune Insignias per pull:

(70×0.005)+(4×0.12)+(2×0.24)(70 × 0.005) + (4 × 0.12) + (2 × 0.24)=0.35+0.48+0.48=1.31Runeperpull= 0.35 + 0.48 + 0.48 = 1.31 Rune per pull

### Convert Rune → Inferno

- 1 Rune = 4 Inferno
- 1.31 Rune × 4 = **5.24 Inferno per pull (average)**

This result of on average **5.24 Inferno per core** is the foundation for the next sections covering cost analysis of holy and shadow immortals, intended to help you with your planning and evaluation of if this event is worth spending on for you.

---

## Cost of Holy & Shadow Immortal Fragments

From the Legendary Battle Pass Shop:

- **450 Inferno Insignias = 60 fragments**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-148-1024x419.png)

### Cores required (average)

450÷5.24≈85.9450 ÷ 5.24 ≈ 85.9

Plan around: **86 Energy Cores per 60 fragments (average)**

That is dramatically different from the old version where we could assume 200-cores would basically always get you 60 fragments of holy or shadow immortal.

---

## Real-World Cost (Using Core Shop Limits)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-151-1024x680.png)

For players aiming to buy **all four Holy or Shadow Immortal fragment packs in a Battle Pass season**, an efficient target is **~700 Energy Cores**. This assumes you are planning conservatively around guaranteed pity cycles while allowing for minor Inferno Insignia carryover or supplemental sources.

### Bundle Assumptions

This example assumes you are purchasing **only the $5 and $10 core bundles**, which have identical cost efficiency:

- **$5 bundle:** 12 Energy Cores
- **$10 bundle:** 24 Energy Cores

Both bundles cost approximately **$0.42 per core**, so the goal is simply to reach the required total within daily stock limits.

---

## Buying All 4 Immortals in stock per Battle Pass Season

Each season allows:

- 4 purchases × 60 fragments
- 240 fragments per season
- Total cost = 1,800 Inferno Insignias

### Cores required (average)

1,800÷5.24≈343.51,800 ÷ 5.24 ≈ 343.5

Plan around: **344 Energy Cores per season**.

---

## Real-World Cost (Using $5 and $10 Core Bundles)

### Example purchase:

- 14 × $10 bundle → 336 cores = $140
- 1 × $5 bundle → 12 cores = $5

Total: **348 cores** for **$145**.

### Updated seasonal estimate: around $145 per season to buy all four Holy/Shadow packs (average numbers).

---

## Variance: What to Expect in Practice

Even though we use averages for planning, **Rune Factory is still RNG** and increasingly so.

What this means practically:

- Some seasons you’ll hit 70-Rune jackpots early
- Some seasons you’ll see mostly 2-Rune and 4-Rune drops
- Your actual cost may fluctuate

But because small Rune drops are frequent:

- Progress feels steady
- You are no longer waiting for pity cycles
- Income is smoother than before

This is a major psychological improvement over the old version.

---

## Comparison: Old Version vs New Version

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-212-1024x433.png)

### The key shift:

Old Rune Factory:

- Functioned as a **100-pull cycle event**
- Value came from guaranteed jackpot
- Small chance to get lucky

New Rune Factory:

- Functions as a **steady income event**
- Value comes mostly from frequent 2 and 4 Rune drops
- Jackpot is bonus, not backbone

The event is roughly **twice as efficient now** for Holy/Shadow fragment purchasing.

---

## So Is Rune Factory Good for Holy/Shadow Now?

Compared to the old version? Yes — significantly better. Compared to historical Sparks of Galaxy efficiency? Still generally more expensive.

The biggest difference is mindset:

- You no longer treat this as a “100-core jackpot loop”
- You treat it as a **steady expected-value grind**
- You budget around averages, not pity

If you are planning Holy or Shadow progression:

- Expect **~86 cores per 60 fragments** as your working number
- Expect **~344 cores per season** for all four Battle Pass purchases
- Expect **~$145 per season** if buying cores efficiently

It’s still not cheap. But it is no longer structurally punishing. And that is a meaningful improvement. And most importantly, the cost efficiency has been quite significantly increased with the recent change - which is very good given how many players are missing Galaxy. This is now a quite meaningful replacement with decently prices holy and shadow immortals.

---

title: Upgrade costs of Dragon Portraits
summary: Dragon Portraits are one of those systems that look underwhelming at first glance, especially when you focus on a single level upgrade. The stat gains per level are small—often just a handful of attack and defense…
markdown:
### Introduction

Dragon Portraits are one of those systems that look underwhelming at first glance, especially when you focus on a single level upgrade. The stat gains per level are small—often just a handful of attack and defense points. For many players, especially early on, it’s easy to dismiss portraits as low priority.

That’s a mistake.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-79-1024x473.png)

Portraits are a classic scaling system. Individually weak, collectively powerful. Once you start stacking dozens of levels, the cumulative stat gain becomes significant, especially in prolonged fights where raw attributes matter more than burst mechanics. That said, the real limiting factor isn’t willingness—it’s cost.

*Before we dive on in, special thanks to player **GoldenState** from server 344 who has been most helpful providing key information on the later portrait levels.**Thank you!***

---

## Costs of all portrait levels

Please find complete list of all upgrade costs for dragon portraits level 1 through 50. Note that level 50 seems to remain the max level for portraits, regardless of other level-caps being increased during seasons, portrait level-caps remain the same.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-83.png)

**Note that all dragons have the same portrait upgrade costs - including holy and shadow!**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-82-1024x500.png)

---

### Understanding the Cost Curve

The defining feature of Dragon Portrait progression is how aggressively the costs scale.

- Early levels (1–10) are extremely cheap and accessible
- Mid levels (20–30) begin to demand real crystal investment
- Late levels (40–50) become a serious long-term resource sink

By the time you reach level 50:

- **Total Crystals:** 128,496
- **Total Gold:** 154,020,000

The jump is not linear—it’s exponential in practice. For example:

- Level 10 costs **284 crystals**
- Level 30 costs **2,700 crystals**
- Level 50 costs **7,500 crystals**

That means a single late-game upgrade can cost more than the first 10 levels combined.

---

### Why Portraits Still Matter

On paper, something like:

- +4 Physical Attack
- +6 Physical Defense
- +3 Magic Attack
- +6 Magic Defense

Doesn’t look impactful... but across 50 levels, you're reaching meaningful and quite significant attribute levels.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/image-80-1024x473.png)

### Player Perspective

From experience, the biggest mistake players make is delaying portraits too long because the upgrades “look small.”

In practice, what works best is:

- **Max talents first** (priority system)
- Then steadily invest into portraits without overcommitting

---

### Conclusion Summary

Dragon Portraits are a long-term investment system with heavy scaling costs. While each level offers small stat increases, the cumulative effect is substantial and should not be ignored.

- Early levels are highly efficient—take them quickly
- Mid levels require balanced investment
- Late levels are expensive and should be approached carefully

If you treat portraits as a background progression rather than a primary focus, they’ll quietly become one of the more reliable sources of raw power in your account.

title: Upgrading dragon talents to 6-6-10
summary: Infinity Kingdom, the popular mobile game, has captivated players with its immersive gameplay and strategic elements. One of the game's most sought-after achievements is unlocking level 6 dragon talents, which provide…
markdown:
Infinity Kingdom, the popular mobile game, has captivated players with its immersive gameplay and strategic elements. One of the game's most sought-after achievements is unlocking level 6 dragon talents, which provide significant advantages in battles and overall progression.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/image-14-1024x448.png)

However, a discrepancy exists among servers, with some having access to level 6 talents while others remain stuck at level 5. In this article, we delve into the fascinating world of Infinity Kingdom and explore the relationship between Conquest Season and the unlocking of level 6 dragon talents.

### Dragon talents matter

In Infinity Kingdom, players raise and nurture powerful dragons that become formidable assets in both defensive and offensive scenarios. Dragon talents play a pivotal role in enhancing a dragon's abilities, granting unique skills and attributes. These talents can be leveled up to unlock even greater potential, making them highly coveted among players.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/image-16-1024x420.png)

**The Divide: Level 5 vs. Level 6 Talents**:

Among the vast community of Infinity Kingdom players, a divide exists regarding the availability of level 6 dragon talents. While some servers have the privilege of accessing these higher-tier abilities, others are left with only level 5 talents. This discrepancy has led to debates and discussions within the player base, fueling speculation on the unlocking mechanism as well as some resentment based on the fact that servers with talents 6-6 are matched with servers without it in Server versus Server PvP content (Legion of Frostoborne).

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/image-17-1024x339.png)

**So how do we get it?**

Conquest Season is a recurring event in Infinity Kingdom that introduces intense battles and challenging objectives for players. It is during this time that the determining factor for unlocking level 6 dragon talents comes into play. Once a server reaches Conquest Phase 4 (P4), a significant milestone in the event, level 6 talents are unlocked for all dragons across that server.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/image-15-1024x436.png)

Conquest Season consists of several phases, each escalating in difficulty and offering unique rewards. Conquest Phase 4 is the ultimate goal for players, as it represents a significant milestone in the event. Reaching P4 requires strong coordination, teamwork, and strategic planning. It is a testament to a server's collective effort and serves as a gateway to unlocking the coveted level 6 dragon talents.

Unlocking level 6 dragon talents can have a transformative effect on gameplay. These talents grant dragons access to more potent skills, improved attributes, and additional combat capabilities. Players who have access to level 6 talents gain a substantial advantage in battles, allowing them to dominate opponents and progress more rapidly in the game.

## Conclusion

In Infinity Kingdom, unlocking level 6 dragon talents represents a significant milestone and a powerful advantage for players. The Conquest Season serves as the determining factor, with servers reaching Conquest Phase 4 unlocking these coveted abilities for all dragons. The pursuit of level 6 talents drives players to push their limits, fostering a competitive environment within the game. As players strategize, coordinate, and aim for conquest, the quest for unlocking dragon talents becomes a thrilling adventure in itself, adding an extra layer of excitement to the immersive world of Infinity Kingdom.

markdown:
## Infinity Kingdom Equipment Upgrade Cost Guide (Level 15–40)

Equipment plays a **crucial role** in the strength of your Immortals in *Infinity Kingdom*. While talent setups, artifact upgrades, and Tower of Knowledge skills all matter, it’s **your gear**—especially **epic +1 equipment**—that truly skyrockets your stats as you progress into the mid and late game.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/image-154-1024x557.png)

Recently, a player asked me:
**"How much does it actually cost to upgrade equipment?"**

I didn’t know off the top of my head—so I did the work and **melted down gear** to bring you this breakdown. Based on current testing (Season 1 capped at Level 40), here's **everything you need to know** about **Enchanted Stone costs**, where to get them, and **how steep the curve gets.**

---

## 📊 Equipment Upgrade Cost Table (Level 15 to 40)

| Level Range | Upgrade Cost |
| --- | --- |
| Level 15 | 700 |
| Level 15–20 | 2,500 |
| Level 20–25 | 15,900 |
| Level 25–30 | 41,900 |
| Level 30–35 | 119,100 |
| Level 35–40 | 294,200 |
| Total Cost | 475,390 Enchanted Stones |

> ⚠️ **Note:** This is the **total cost for upgrading a single piece of Epic +1 equipment** from Level 15 to 40.

---

## 🔥 Where to Get Enchanted Stones

As you’ve probably noticed, the **later levels get very expensive**—with **over 400K stones required past level 25** alone. Here’s how to stock up efficiently:

### 1. Defeating Gnomes

- Gnomes regularly drop **small amounts of Enchanted Stones**
- Great for **daily farming**, but won't keep up with late-game costs on its own

### 2. Spider Boss Battles

- Fought **twice a week**
- **Major source** of Enchanted Stones (especially at higher difficulties)
- Your **best method for stacking big amounts quickly**

💡 **Tip:** Make sure you're in an active alliance doing **high-difficulty Spider runs**—it’s by far the best bang for your time.

---

## 📈 Why Equipment Matters

Each upgrade boosts your Immortal’s **core attributes**:

- Physical Attack / Magic Attack
- Defense
- HP
- Speed
- Crit, Dodge, Block, etc.

By the time you're upgrading beyond Level 30+, the stat increases are **massive** and can be the difference between winning and losing PvP fights or boss challenges.

---

## 🛠️ What This Means for You

- Don’t ignore Enchanted Stone farming just because early upgrades are cheap—**you'll need hundreds of thousands** later
- **Prioritize your main Immortals’ gear upgrades first**—don’t spread resources thin
- If you're still in **Season 1 or 2**, it's best to **stockpile Enchanted Stones now** so you’re ready when Season caps increase
- **Level 35–40 alone costs 294.2K**—which is **over 60% of the total upgrade cost**

---

## 🔮 What’s Next?

I’m currently capped at **Level 40** in **Season 1**, but as the server progresses and unlocks **higher level upgrades**, I’ll be updating this guide with:

- Costs for Level 40–50 and beyond
- Full chart for **each level** (not just in intervals)
- Enchanted Stone return values from melting high-level gear

---

## 💡 Final Takeaways

✔ **Total cost to upgrade Epic +1 gear (15–40): 475,390 Enchanted Stones**
✔ Costs ramp up significantly after Level 30
✔ **Spider Boss** = best source of stones
✔ Prioritize **main team gear upgrades**
✔ Stockpile now so you aren’t scrambling later
