title: Upgrading Immortal Affinity
summary: Now that Asteria has returned in patch 2.9.5, the new Immortal Affinity system is starting to make a lot more sense. At first glance the shop looks fairly straightforward, but once you actually test the numbers, you…
markdown:
## Introduction

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-101-1024x529.png)

Now that Asteria has returned in patch 2.9.5, the new Immortal Affinity system is starting to make a lot more sense. At first glance the shop looks fairly straightforward, but once you actually test the numbers, you realize the system is less about finding “better” items and more about understanding how the bonus affinity mechanics work for different immortal factions.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-96-1024x540.png)

After going through the values from every gift item in the shop, the biggest thing that stands out is how differently elemental immortals are treated compared to Chaos, Holy, and Shadow immortals. That distinction is probably going to matter quite a bit long term, especially for players investing heavily into premium factions.

---

## How Affinity Gifts Actually Work

Every gift in the Asteria shop gives a base amount of affinity points that can be used on any immortal. Some gifts also provide bonus affinity when used on the correct elemental immortal.

For example, elemental gifts like Abyssal Pearl or Zircon Ring give a smaller base value to everyone, but provide a large additional bonus when matched to the proper element. In practice, that means Water immortals benefit much more from Water-themed gifts, Fire immortals from Fire gifts, and so on.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-97-1024x635.png)

The system is actually cleaner than it first appears. Once the bonus is applied correctly, all properly matched gifts end up landing at essentially the same crystal efficiency.

That was honestly a bit surprising to me. I expected there to be obvious “best value” purchases, but after testing the numbers, the developers seem to have balanced the entire shop around a very consistent ratio.

---

## The Hidden 10-to-1 Efficiency Pattern

Once you calculate the affinity gained per crystal spent, almost every properly used gift lands at roughly the same efficiency.

The universal gifts:

- Spiritfont Nectar
- Starweave Silk
- Letter of Blessing

all convert at 10 affinity per crystal.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-98.png)

*Special thanks to VictorSeven for sharing the above table with us all!*

The elemental gifts do the same thing, but only if they are used on the correct immortals.

For instance, the purple elemental gifts cost 50 crystals and provide a total of 500 affinity when the elemental bonus activates. The blue elemental gifts cost 30 crystals and provide 300 total affinity under the same conditions. Both still end up at the same 10-to-1 conversion rate.

So the system is not really about hunting for mathematically superior items. The optimization comes from using the right gifts on the right immortals and avoiding wasted bonus potential.

---

## Why Elemental Immortals Have an Advantage

This is where the system gets more interesting. Chaos, Holy, and Shadow immortals do not appear to receive any elemental bonus affinity at all. They only gain the base value from elemental gifts.

That creates a pretty massive efficiency gap.

Take a purple elemental gift as an example. A Water immortal receives the full 500 affinity from an Abyssal Pearl, while a Chaos immortal only gets the base 200 points. The crystal cost stays the same either way. That means elemental immortals effectively gain affinity more than twice as efficiently from those items.

The same thing happens with the blue elemental gifts. An elemental immortal receives the full 300 points, while Chaos, Holy, and Shadow only receive 100.

It is pretty clear that elemental gifts are not worth using on non-elemental immortals unless you have absolutely nothing else available. Especially since you want to unlock bonuses by getting as many insignias completed (affinity lvl 30) as possible. More about that in another guide!

---

## The Best Gifts for Chaos, Holy, and Shadow

Because they cannot trigger elemental bonuses, Chaos, Holy, and Shadow immortals are heavily dependent on the universal gifts instead.

That means:

- Spiritfont Nectar
- Starweave Silk
- Letter of Blessing

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/image-99-1024x626.png)

are currently the best-value affinity items for those factions.

All three maintain the full 10 affinity per crystal ratio regardless of immortal type, which makes them dramatically more efficient than elemental gifts for universal factions.

I suspect this is going to create a long-term bottleneck eventually. Players building Chaos, Holy, or Shadow marches are all pulling from the exact same affinity material pool, while elemental players are spread across separate elemental gift categories.

On larger or older servers especially, I would not be surprised if Nectar and Silk become extremely contested resources later in the patch cycle.

---

## What This Means for Long-Term Progression

Right now the Affinity system still feels new, but the resource economy behind it already tells us quite a lot.

If you mainly run elemental teams, your progression path looks fairly smooth. You can specialize into your own elemental gift pool and maintain strong efficiency throughout.

Chaos, Holy, and Shadow players probably have a rougher road ahead. Since they cannot benefit from elemental bonuses, they are locked almost entirely into universal gifts, which means every player using those factions is competing for the same limited resources.

That does not necessarily make those immortals weaker, but it does make them more expensive to optimize over time.

And honestly, that fits Infinity Kingdom pretty well historically. Premium factions have almost always carried heavier progression costs somewhere in the system.

---

## Final Thoughts

The Affinity system initially looked more complicated than it really is. After testing the numbers, the structure is actually fairly straightforward once you understand how the bonus affinity mechanic works.

At the moment, the most important thing is not finding secret high-value purchases. It is understanding which gifts properly match your immortals and recognizing that Chaos, Holy, and Shadow factions currently operate under very different efficiency rules than elemental teams.

That difference will probably end up shaping long-term account progression much more than people realize during these first few days of the patch.

---

title: Upgrading Immortal Talents and Well of Time Elite
summary: The Elite Well of Time is one of the most important new features for upgrading Immortal Talent Specializations. Normal Well of Time still exists, but Elite adds an entirely new progression path, complete with daily…
markdown:
### How to Upgrade Immortal Talent Specializations using Elite Well of Time

The Elite Well of Time is one of the most important new features for upgrading Immortal Talent Specializations. Normal Well of Time still exists, but Elite adds an entirely new progression path, complete with daily challenges, unique rewards, and long-term talent growth. If you want to maximize your Immortals, this mode is absolutely core to your progress.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/image-101-1024x556.png)

---

### Well of Time Basics (Normal & Elite)

Normal Well of Time is unchanged, but Elite mode is where all the new growth comes in:

- **10 challenges per day** (you can buy more).
- **Elite Pass (30 days = $10)**: **Big recommendation**. It gives +5 extra attempts/day and +6 additional Master’s Insight books/day. Since this content is time-gated, those extra daily books really add up.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/image-85.png)

---

## Rewards system:

First-time clears are where the bulk of your rewards come from. For example, stage 1-1 only gives 8 Marks + 5 Insight Books on first clear. By the time you reach stage 14-5, it’s up to 80 Marks + 18 Books (plus extra from raid reward, so in reality more like 94 Marks + 22 Books on first clear). Raiding after that only gives a fraction (e.g. 14 Marks + 4 Books).

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/image-86.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/image-87.png)

**No penalty for failing.** If you try a tough stage and fail, you don’t lose an attempt. This means you should always push as far as possible — even if it takes 10 retries to crack a stage.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/image-88.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/image-89.png)

Rewards are **Master Marks** (Attack, Magic, Ranged, Defense, and Support types) + Insight Books. Marks are used to unlock and upgrade minor talent nodes, while Insight Books are the big bottleneck for advancing trees.

The trick with higher stages is that you need to adjust your team composition. Some fights punish you with heavy magic damage, others need you to hold dragon skills until the second wave. Think of it like puzzle content — each fight is solvable, but the solution depends on your Immortals and build.

---

### Immortal Selection System

Each Immortal now has a new specialization system. You’ll see a small icon on the portrait — click it, and you can pick between three unique specialization trees depending on Immortal role.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/image-100-1024x568.png)

- **Tank examples**: Shielding, Accuracy, Resilience.
- **Attack examples**: Attack speed, Crit rate, AoE boosts.
- **Support examples**: Healing or damage-boosting options.

Once you pick, you’re locked in unless you reset (500 gems to respec). The talents aren’t “one size fits all” — the best choice depends on your setup. For example:

- Hannibal/Alexander benefit a lot from attack speed if you’re running hybrid.
- Ranged units shine with Deadly Crit Rate.
- Mages usually want Crit Rate Stormeye.
- Tanks almost always want Shielding/Resilience.

I’ll be making deeper guides for each Immortal type, but for now, use these as starting points.

---

### Progression & Costs

Unlocking and upgrading Immortal specialization trees costs **Immortal fragments** + **Insight Books**.

- Unlock costs:  - 200 fragments (first)
- 100 (second)
- 150 (third)
- 200 (fourth)
- 250 (fifth)
- 300 (sixth)
- 350 (seventh)
- 400 (eighth)
- Rank 8 completion = 1950 Books for main nodes + 240 for mandatory minor progress nodes = grant total of minimum **2,190 Insight Books** (only for basic unlocks; you’ll need more later to max out minor nodes).

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/image-99-1024x522.png)

**Flexibility:** You don’t need to max one tree before moving to another. For example, you can go 1-1-1-1 across all trees instead of 5-5-5-5. This is important since Marks drop evenly across all types, but you’ll be book-gated. Best move is to unlock broadly and then prioritize the most impactful nodes (physical damage on DPS, magic attack for mages, defense on tanks, crit rate for burst dealers, etc.).

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/image-97.png)

So while 2,190 is the number you need to upgrade your Immortal talent to rank 8, you will eventually want to max out the entire talent tree since the attribute, boosts, etc. are quite powerful. **In doing so, you are going to need a grant total of 4,750 Insight Books to max a full immortal talent tree.**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/image-96.png)

The two damage nodes alone take 1200 total to max both (600 and 600) - these are the most impactful nodes after main talent ranks.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/image-98-1024x525.png)

---

### Master’s Insight Books

Marks drop for all roles equally, but Insight Books are time-gated from Well of Time. Careful allocation is critical.

- Don’t waste them on niche nodes (like Accuracy on a mage).
- Saving for key upgrades and key immortals to progress (e.g. magical damage boosts for Himiko) is much better than spreading too thin.

---

### Long-Term Considerations

Getting one Immortal to rank 8 specialization is **very expensive**. In addition to the major main talent nodes you are also spendig books and fragments on the minor nodes in between. See progress pattern below.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/image-91.png)

Just to give perspective:

- Epic Immortals need **1,020 immortal fragments** for stars + artifact unlock, then another **2,190 immortal fragments** for talents (and on top of that the 2,190 books).
**Minimum total = 3,210 fragments.**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/image-95-1024x561.png)

- Chaos Immortals are even pricier: 1,640 immortal fragments just for stars/artifacts, luckily for those looking to push chaos immortals, the talent tree is identical to the one for epic immortals (no additional costs). But you will ofc need the added immortal fragments plus the same book requirements.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/image-90.png)

If you don’t have the resources to fully commit, don’t start a Chaos project half-way. Stick to Epic Immortals unless you’re ready to go all in.

---

Honestly, I think this new system is one of the better long-term grinds IK has added. It gives PvE players a puzzle-like challenge (Elite Well stages), while also creating meaningful progression without being tied only to PvP. The Elite Pass is a must-buy if you’re even a light spender, because those extra daily Insight Books stack up over time. Personally I quite like it and I like having to plan out progress on immortal trees across multiple marches. Anything that forces players to think is amazing in my book.

My advice: push Well stages as far as you can every day, don’t be scared of failing, and focus your Insight Books carefully. For me, I’m prioritizing Wu and Qin in my fire march, while spending leftover Marks on secondary marches instead of stockpiling. That way nothing goes to waste.

---

title: Using alts and level 1 alliances to win!
summary: Server versus Server battles are supposed to be the epitomy of battles where raw power and overwhelming force are used to slay hordes of enemies as eight servers are thrown into all out war over supremecy of the Capital…
markdown:
Server versus Server battles are supposed to be the epitomy of battles where raw power and overwhelming force are used to slay hordes of enemies as eight servers are thrown into all out war over supremecy of the Capital Ymir.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/image-2.png)

.... supposed to be. In reality, whilst having the biggest whale is nice and all. The server bringing the most alts are always the most scary! Whales can be rallied and cities can be blocked off completly. As such, if you find yourself in a large power disparity, fear not! You can still very much compete against even the biggest of servers.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/right-way-1024x461.png)

How? By using an army of alts to block in bubbles while they instant build thermals all over the place making it impossible for your enemy to even find space to park. Moreover, you need a ton of useless marches to drain the soul and time from your enemies. Send a 1-troop march to ALL of your enemies thermals. They have no choice but to go around and attack each and every single one. Making them both vulnerable and extreemly stressed on time and resources.

## Abusing level 1 alliance builds

Create 3 Alliances using those 3 characters. Leave the entry access as Join Freely. Enter frost on them using the C15 character you made.

Level 1 alliance gets the same number of Tactical Points as the strongest and most established alliances in game. In the Expansion tree (blue) spec into Indestructible, Demolition, Quick Repair, and Wonder Builder.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/image-3.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/image-4.png)

Start crafting a thermal. The game gives your alliance enough starting RSS to create one extra thermal. Your first thermal is also free and instantly completed (costs no RSS) - giving you 1 free creatable thermal and 1 instantly placeable thermal (2) in total. Once you have placed 2 completed thermals, swap to the Iron Wall tactic (in place of Wonder Builder). Great - you can now fully restore these thermals to full health, twice. This means the enemy must spend 4.5 hours (straight) rotating demolition tactics using 9 different alliances on that thermal to bring it down to low health, then you can restore it, and then they must do that again for another 4.5 hours using 9 different alliance shells demolition rotation to bring them down. This forces players to be available for 9 hours+ straight to take down a thermal tower.

**Once the next chronicle opens, Security Alert tactic grants you an additional 1 hour of defense time - can be used twice, totaling 11 hours of straight demolition needed to bring it down.**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/image-5-1024x820.png)

During this time, the mini alliance can create an Diplomacy Alliance (allies) with the Main Alliance - and the Main Alliance can now place towers off that chain. Once they place one Main Alliance tower, they can place 7+ around your alt alliance towers, securing the area. They can continue to do this regardless of the thermal zone restrictions, allowing them to completely override the existing functionality for thermal placement block zones, even though you shouldn't be able to place in the zone of another alliances thermal zone.

## Recap

Using your 3 characters, place your C15 into these alliances and go into frost with them, then pass lead back off to the low level C2 when you are done in frost for that shell. With this strategy, secure all 3 gates for another servers own zone - locking them from being able to place there if you got to it first - completely stopping them from being able to play the game before the zones even open with just one little C15 account - ruining the entire 45 day event for an entire server full of dedicated players who support the game with their time.

Repeat this strategy on all gates and lock everyone into their own zones, ruining intended gameplay and KvK for the entire bracket without even lifting a finger on your main account.

Collect your prize fighting nobody - a hollow victory but none the less, a win by game design.

title: Methods to farm resources with alts
summary: I am Myrahk and in this article I will share some insights about me and my 14 alts. I have gotten many questions about why I have the number of alts I do, how I manage them and what I get out of it - so here we go!
markdown:
I am Myrahk and in this article I will share some insights about me and my 14 alts. I have gotten many questions about why I have the number of alts I do, how I manage them and what I get out of it - so here we go!

## Relying on your alts to farm is the fastest way to grow!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/image-53-1024x574.png)

## Use your alt's AP to turn it into resources for your main!

First of all, alts are great for farming resources on the map from empty castles (people who left the game) and from the many farm nodes. I try to spend my AP when it is up and keep marches farming nodes when AP is down. Read more about **["Dead Castle Farming"](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/development/resources/dead-castle-farming/)**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Skaermbillede-2022-03-21-130922.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/low.png)

Your alts need resources to grow, but if you are consistent about your farming you will get an abuncance of leftover resources. As these stack up, I '*harvest*' them with my main making sure that every AP-attack my main sends out returns full of resources.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/image-74-1024x503.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/image-73-1024x541.png)

## Excess food for consistent gold production

Your main castle will get a lot more food than you can spend, this is because we are still using some rss from alts to upgrade their buildings. While we are producing troops too, the proportionality is skewered and as such you will most likely get way too much food if you are consistently farming your alts and farming dead castles with alts.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Skaermbillede-2022-03-21-130711.png)

So remember to put on your minting talents and nuke ur foodstock in the Forge every once in a while! An easy way to keep efficiently minting a ton of gold for your dragons!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Skaermbillede-2022-03-21-130648.png)

All in all, this is an extreemly efficient way to mass resources very quickly. The more time you spend keeping your alts AP down, the more value you get. This is also how the people who were very fast to get tier 7 troops (and c50) did it and something you need to do if you have enough speedups to keep yourself growing quickly towards c50 and t7.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/image-75.png)

## Alternative Passive Resource farming

If you do not have the time to spend AP on alts attacking castles all over Norheim, then you may want to simply create a farmvile group of alts where you only do the bare minimum and still achieve quite solid resource income (almost) without moving a finger.

**[Read more here.](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/development/resources/passive-resource-farming/)**

title: Using Bluestacks
summary: Download BlueStacks from the official site here: https://www.bluestacks.com/
markdown:
Download BlueStacks from the official site here: [https://www.bluestacks.com/](https://www.bluestacks.com/)

Boot the program and begin. Honestly, playing in a single window using Bluestacks is so simple it required no guidance. But some people have written me asking how to play multiple instances of Bluestacks at the same time - i.e. "how to play all of my alts at the same time".

**1. Find the multi-instance manager**

![Billede](https://media.discordapp.net/attachments/901162764297441340/930180969288335420/unknown.png)

### 2. Create new instance

**3. Be ware of configurations** - running BlueStacks can be resource intensive on your machine since booting virtual machines with seperate OS's require quite a bit of processing power. This means a strain on your CPU and GPU.

![Billede](https://media.discordapp.net/attachments/901162764297441340/930180277752451122/unknown.png)

Go to configuration options by clicking the cog on your instance - create a configuration that fits your hardware loadout. I would **recommend**for 4-6 instance running **1 / 2 cores, 1 / 2 GB memory and setting FPS to 20**. Infinity Kingdom can run smoothly on 1 core, 1 GB and 20 fps!

Set your **display** according to the size you want. I use 6 instances at a time so I run min. settings at **960x540 with 160 DPI.**

markdown:
### Unlocking and Maximizing "Victorious Pursuit" via the New 5-Day Bundle in Infinity Kingdom

"Victorious Pursuit," a skill previously exclusive to the Legion of Frostborne event, has now been made accessible through a new 5-day bundle, offering a unique opportunity for players to accelerate their acquisition of this powerful skill. This guide will navigate you through the process of obtaining "Victorious Pursuit," its mechanics, optimal usage, and strategies to leverage its full potential.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-51-1024x493.png)

## How to Obtain "Victorious Pursuit"

### Legion of Frostborne

Traditionally, "Victorious Pursuit" could be obtained by participating in the Legion of Frostborne event, requiring players to collect skill stones through event participation.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-52-1024x485.png)

### The 5-Day Bundle Option

For those looking to expedite the skill acquisition or short on required stones, the new 5-day bundle presents an appealing alternative:

- **Offer Details**: For $20 per day, players can purchase a bundle that includes 5 skill stones.
- **Bonus Reward**: Upon purchasing all five $20 bundles (totaling $100), players receive an additional 25 skill stones.
- **Total Acquisition**: Over the five days, players can obtain 50 skill stones towards the 60 needed to unlock "Victorious Pursuit."
- **Supplementary Acquisition**: The remaining stones can be conveniently obtained in Kingdom vs Kingdom (KvK) events or subsequent participations in Legion of Frostborne.

## Skill Mechanics and Usage

"Victorious Pursuit" enhances your Immortals' battlefield prowess by increasing damage dealt with each instance of ultimate skill damage:

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-53.png)

- **Skill Effect**: A 5% increase in damage for 4 seconds after each ultimate skill damage instance, stackable up to 10 times.
- **Optimal Conditions**: The skill shines brightest with Immortals like Manco, whose ultimate skill delivers continuous AoE damage, allowing for rapid stacking and sustained buffs.

### Synergy with High-Frequency Ultimates

- **Hippolyta Example**: With her unique artifact, Hippolyta's ultimate can hit 7 times, translating into a 35% damage increase. However, maintaining this buff is contingent on rapid subsequent casts.
- **Manco's Advantage**: Manco uniquely benefits from "Victorious Pursuit" due to his ultimate's nature, ensuring near-constant buff presence and full stack maintenance.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-54.png)

### Potential with Corrosive Power

The introduction of "Corrosive Power" opens the possibility of achieving high enough energy regeneration (when combined with skills like "Energy Burst") to maintain "Victorious Pursuit" buffs with Immortals like Hippolyta or Tutankhamon, potentially maximizing the skill's effectiveness.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-55.png)

## Strategic Considerations

### Evaluating Against Flat Bonus Skills

When integrating "Victorious Pursuit" into your strategy, it's crucial to assess its effectiveness in maintaining at least a 30% damage increase through stack management. If maintaining such stacks proves challenging, reverting to passive skills like "Anger" or "Concentration," which offer consistent flat damage bonuses, may be more beneficial.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-56.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/image-57.png)

### Team Composition and Skill Synergy

Building a team that capitalizes on "Victorious Pursuit" involves selecting Immortals with rapid, high-frequency ultimates or enhancing energy regeneration to ensure the continuous application and stacking of the skill's buff.

## Conclusion

The introduction of the 5-day bundle for "Victorious Pursuit" skill stones significantly lowers the barrier for players to unlock and utilize this powerful skill, offering new strategic depth and damage amplification possibilities. By carefully selecting Immortals that synergize with "Victorious Pursuit" and strategically managing skill stacks, players can unleash unprecedented damage levels on the battlefield. As always, it's essential to weigh this skill's dynamic benefits against the consistent output of flat bonus skills, ensuring your Immortals' lineup is optimized for victory.

title: VIP system explained for beginners
summary: The VIP system in Infinity Kingdom is a long-term progression feature designed to reward consistent logins, purchases, and gem investments with powerful bonuses. It is one of the most important systems to optimize if…
markdown:
## 🏩 VIP System Guide – Infinity Kingdom

The **VIP system** in *Infinity Kingdom* is a long-term progression feature designed to reward consistent logins, purchases, and gem investments with powerful bonuses. It is one of the most important systems to optimize if you want to get stronger over time — whether you spend money or not.

This guide will cover what VIP does, how to upgrade it, what rewards you get, and why hitting **VIP 15** should be a top goal.

---

## 📈 What Is VIP?

VIP is a **player progression system** with 15 levels in total. Each level offers permanent benefits ranging from extra healing speed to bonus troop stats and exclusive shop items.

There are **three main ways to increase your VIP level**:

1. **Daily logins** – Free VIP points each day
2. **Spending gems** – Exchange gems for VIP points (1 gem = 1 point)
3. **Buying packs** – All purchases include VIP points

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-111.png)

At certain VIP levels, you unlock:

- **Daily VIP chests**
- **Special shop access**
- **Powerful combat stat boosts**
- **Gifting options** (send items to allies and alts)

---

## 🍜 VIP Rewards Overview

### 🎁 Daily VIP Chest

Once you reach VIP Level 10, you start receiving a **daily reward chest**, which includes valuable items like:

- **Field of the First Stone** (from VIP 10+)
- Resource boosts
- Speedups
- Scrolls and potions

These add up over time and provide excellent passive progression — especially helpful in early and mid-game.

### 🍭 VIP Shop

At **VIP 15**, you unlock the **VIP shop**, which lets you spend VIP points you’ve earned over time. Some highly desirable items include:

- **Shadow Dragon Crystals**
- **Holy Dragon Egg** – Extremely valuable
- **Troop consumables**, boosters, and utility scrolls

This shop rotates and evolves, giving ongoing value even after you’ve hit max VIP level.

---

## 🧙 Immortals from VIP Packs

As you progress through VIP levels, you unlock **exclusive chests** that offer strong immortals:

- **Merlin** – Very early game (VIP 1+)
- **Zenobia** – VIP 5 chest (fantastic early support immortal)
- **Elizabeth Báthory** – Available in mid-to-late VIP chests

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-108-1024x411.png)

While once powerful, these immortals are no longer meta-defining. However, unlocking Zenobia early (for ~$5) is still a **smart investment** because it enables you to find her fragments in the market and build her quickly.

---

## ⚔️ VIP Combat Bonuses

VIP isn’t just cosmetics or convenience — the **combat bonuses** it grants are game-changing:

| VIP Level | Bonus |
| --- | --- |
| 11 | +4% Immortal Defense |
| 12 | +4% Immortal Attack |
| 13 | +5% Crit and Resilience |
| 14 | +5% Accuracy and Dodge |
| 15 | +500 Troop Capacity |

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-107-1024x407.png)

The **+500 troop capacity at VIP 15** is especially powerful:

- More damage output
- Greater survivability
- Better scaling in rallies and boss fights

These are **permanent buffs** that apply to all battles, making VIP progression one of the best long-term investments in the game.

---

## 💎 How to Level Up VIP (Even Free-to-Play)

VIP points are earned through:

1. **Daily Login** – +150 VIP points every day for showing up
2. **Gems** – 1 Gem = 1 VIP point
3. **Event Rewards** – Like relic donations and special packages
4. **Alliance Spending Rewards** – Sometimes you get small VIP boosts when others in your island or alliance make purchases

### Free-to-Play Strategy

Even as a **100% free-to-play** player, you can reach **VIP 15** over time If you are free-to-play I would recommend progressing atleast to level 13 for the major combat buffs:

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-109-1024x452.png)

- **Stack your gems** – Save for a major spend push during a **Wonder Journey** or **Spending Reward** event
- Use the gems to buy **VIP levels** and **trigger reward milestones** in parallel

For example:

- VIP 15 costs **1 million total VIP points**
- If done with only gems, that’s **1 million gems**
- You can do this gradually over months, spending during events for **double value**

On F2P alts, this is **extremely efficient**.

---

## 🏰 Gifting Unlocks

At higher VIP levels, you unlock the ability to **gift alliance members and alts**:

- **Attack/Defense/Speed Buffs**
- **Teleport scrolls**
- **Misc. consumables**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-110-1024x572.png)

This makes your **VIP 15 main account** incredibly useful to your other accounts or friends, especially during alliance wars or IB preparations.

Not all items are giftable at lower VIP tiers — the higher your VIP level, the more valuable items you can send.

---

## 🔥 Why You Want VIP 15

VIP 15 is **one of the most powerful milestones** in the game:

- +500 Troop Count is **massive**
- Full access to the **VIP Shop**
- Permanent **combat buffs**
- Maxed **gifting power**
- Passive resource growth from daily chests

If you’re aiming for late-game competitiveness, **VIP 15 is not optional** — it's a core progression goal.

---

## 📌 Final Tips

- **Buy Zenobia at VIP 5** if you're a new spender. Great early support.
- **Don’t waste gems randomly** — wait for **Spending Events** (like Wonderful Journey) to maximize value
- **VIP Shop items rotate** – Check regularly for rare items
- **Prioritize VIP growth over cosmetic purchases** early on

---

## 🧠 Summary

The VIP system in Infinity Kingdom is more than just fluff — it’s one of the **most impactful features** in terms of long-term growth, combat strength, and utility. Whether you’re a spender or a grinder, hitting **VIP 15** will significantly boost your power and unlock important features that give you the edge in both PvP and PvE.

**Free-to-play** players: It’s a marathon, not a sprint. Plan your gem spending wisely, log in daily, and save for key events.

**Spenders**: You’ll hit VIP 15 faster, but still maximize your value by syncing upgrades with reward events.

---

title: Vision Guide: How Fog of War, Scouting and Blind Spots Work
summary: Vision is one of the most important and least explained mechanics in Legion of Frostborne, commonly referred to as KvK. When players first enter the Frozen Realm, most of the map is hidden beneath darkness. Unlike…
markdown:
Vision is one of the most important and least explained mechanics in Legion of Frostborne, commonly referred to as KvK. When players first enter the Frozen Realm, most of the map is hidden beneath darkness. Unlike Norheim, where castles and troop movements are normally visible, the KvK map only reveals enemy activity when one of your sources of Vision reaches it.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-25-1024x431.png)

This is easy to mistake for a visual effect that simply makes the battlefield feel more mysterious. In reality, Vision determines far more than what appears on your screen. It affects whether you can locate and attack enemy castles, inspect objectives, continue a Thermal Tower chain and, in some situations, whether your alliance can attack a city or gate at all. Understanding it properly makes it easier to scout enemies, hide vulnerable castles and recognize why destroying a single Thermal Tower can disrupt an entire defensive position.

Weather adds another layer. Fog and Sunny conditions change the effective range of Thermal Towers, meaning the same tower network can provide different coverage from one day or province to the next. A route that looks safely illuminated today may contain blind spots tomorrow, while a favorable Sunny forecast can create an opportunity to extend a tower chain farther than normal.

## Table of Contents

- What Vision reveals
- Sources of Vision and their ranges
- Shared alliance and Federation Vision
- Understanding the eye symbol
- How weather changes Vision
- Scouting hidden enemies with marches
- Using alternate castles as lamps
- Thermal Towers and objective warfare
- Denying Vision by dismantling towers
- Hiding in an enemy blind spot
- Common Vision mistakes
- Summary

---

## What Does Vision Actually Reveal?

The darkness covering the Frozen Realm conceals enemy territories, troops, troop movements and relocation sites. Resource deposits, Gnome camps, cities and gates may still appear vaguely through the darkness, but you cannot inspect their complete information until you have Vision over the relevant area.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-27-1024x533.png)

Once an enemy enters your Vision, the game reveals the target and allows you to interact with it normally. This can expose a castle that appeared to be sitting in empty space, show marches moving toward a gate or reveal the details of an objective your alliance is preparing to attack. If the source providing Vision moves away or disappears, the area returns to darkness unless another friendly source continues to cover it.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-26-1024x592.png)

This makes Vision temporary and local. Your alliance does not gradually uncover the entire battlefield permanently. Instead, every castle, march, objective and Thermal Tower contributes its own area of visibility, and the map you can see at any moment is the combination of all those overlapping areas.

## Sources of Vision and Their Ranges

The easiest way to understand the system is to treat every friendly object as a light source with its own radius.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-31-1024x234.png)

The tile values above are the ranges observed in current play and demonstrated in community testing. The official game description confirms the different sources of Vision but does not publish their numerical radii, so it is worth rechecking the edge of a tower's coverage after major KvK updates.

In practice, the distinction between the ranges matters. Castles provide a useful local bubble, but objectives and Thermal Towers illuminate a much larger area. Marches only reveal a narrow path, yet their mobility allows them to find targets that none of your permanent sources can currently see.

## Shared Alliance and Federation Vision

Vision is shared between members of the same alliance. If an alliance member teleports into an otherwise dark area, their castle immediately becomes a new source of Vision for everyone else. The same applies to friendly cities, gates and Thermal Towers controlled by the alliance.

Friendly alliances can also share Vision through the relevant diplomatic relationship. In the modern Legion of Frostborne format, Federations connect several alliances from the same faction and allow them to cooperate across the battlefield. This makes Vision a coalition resource rather than something each alliance must always create by itself.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-28-1024x371.png)

Shared Vision is one of the reasons diplomacy has such a practical effect in KvK. A smaller support alliance can illuminate an approach, maintain a tower route or position castles around an objective while the main fighting alliance concentrates its strongest players elsewhere. A castle does not need enough power to defeat an enemy in order to contribute. Sometimes its most valuable purpose is simply allowing everyone else to see.

The opposite is also true. When a diplomatic relationship ends, an alliance may lose access to Vision it had been relying upon. A route that looked completely secure can suddenly contain large patches of darkness because the castles and towers illuminating it belonged to someone else. Alliance leadership should therefore know which parts of the map are supported by its own assets and which are visible only because of Federation partners.

## Understanding the Eye Symbol

When an enemy has Vision over your castle, an eye symbol appears above it. The same warning can appear over allied castles and Thermal Towers. This is the game's way of telling you that the position is currently exposed and can be seen by the opposing side.

If the eye is absent, the territory is sitting in an enemy blind spot. That is useful information, particularly when placing vulnerable players, reinforcement castles or alternate accounts near an active front. A hidden castle is much less likely to attract casual attacks because the enemy cannot simply find it while browsing the map.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-29.png)

The missing eye should not be treated as a guarantee of safety. Enemy Vision can change at any moment. A scout may pass close enough to reveal the castle, a new Thermal Tower may finish construction, or a hostile castle may relocate nearby. Weather can also expand tower coverage into a previously hidden position. The eye is best understood as a live warning, not a permanent status.

This gives players a very simple defensive habit: whenever you relocate in KvK, check the castle for the eye symbol. If your intention was to hide in the darkness and the eye immediately appears, the position is not as concealed as it looked.

## How Weather Changes Vision

Weather in Legion of Frostborne is regional. Every province can have different conditions, and the weather interface shows both the current state and the forecast for the following day. For Vision planning, the two important conditions are Fog and Sunny weather.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-22-1024x200.png)

The weather rules specifically modify Thermal Tower range. They do not state that castle Vision, objective Vision or the one-tile bubble surrounding a march changes at the same time. This distinction matters because castles and moving troops can be used to compensate when Fog reduces the reach of your towers.

Fog can do more than increase the number of towers needed for expansion. If a castle or suspected enemy position is sitting near the outer edge of your normal tower range, a 25% reduction may return it to darkness. A planned attack route may lose visibility, a tower chain may become more awkward to extend, and an area around a choke point may become harder to monitor.

Sunny weather creates the opposite opportunity. The additional range can illuminate positions that were previously outside your coverage and allow an alliance to reach farther with fewer towers. Leadership teams planning a major expansion should therefore consult the forecast before committing their tower stock and construction tactics. If Sunny weather is approaching, waiting may save towers or make a difficult route much easier. If Fog is forecast, building a little redundancy into the route can prevent the entire operation from depending on a single reduced Vision bubble.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-24-1024x377.png)

Weather can differ between neighboring provinces, so it is not enough to check the general conditions around your own castle. The relevant weather is the weather in the province through which the tower chain or military operation will actually pass. For the complete list of conditions and their gathering, combat and territory effects, see the [Legion of Frostborne Weather System Guide](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/legion-of-frostborne/misc-kvk-guides/legion-of-frostborne-weather-system-guide/).

## Scouting Hidden Enemies With Marches

A moving march creates Vision three tiles around itself. This small radius does not look impressive beside a Thermal Tower, but it is one of the most flexible scouting tools available because it travels with the troops.

If you know the approximate location of an enemy castle, send a march toward a resource deposit or Gnome camp close to the suspected position. If there is no suitable target beside it, choose something farther away so the march route passes through the area you want to inspect. As the troops move, their Vision bubble travels along the path and briefly reveals enemy castles, marches or towers nearby.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-30-1024x385.png)

Route selection is the important part. Sending troops to the closest node may not help if the game chooses a path that misses the suspected castle by two tiles. A target behind the location is often better because it forces the march to cross the area rather than stopping short of it.

When the hidden territory appears, an attacker must be ready to act. The scouting march only provides Vision while it is close enough to the target, and the opportunity can disappear quickly as the troops continue along their route. For a coordinated hunt, one player can provide the moving Vision while another keeps a strong march ready to attack as soon as the castle is revealed.

Gathering can also be used to hold a small patch of Vision. If a resource deposit is located beside a suspected enemy position, leaving a march gathering there provides a three-tile observation point until the troops are recalled or removed. It is more persistent than a passing scout, although the gathering march is exposed and should not contain troops you cannot afford to lose.

## Using Alternate Castles as Lamps

For longer-term scouting, alternate castles can be used as what many players call lamps. The idea is simple: place a shield on the alt, teleport it beside the area you want to monitor and use the castle's five-tile Vision range to illuminate the surroundings for the rest of the alliance or Federation.

A lamp can reveal hidden enemy castles, objectives and troop movements without requiring a main account to remain in a dangerous position. Because the castle continues providing Vision while shielded, it can be difficult for the opposing side to remove immediately. This makes lamps particularly useful around gates, contested cities, vulnerable tower chains and likely enemy relocation areas.

The alt must belong to an alliance whose Vision is shared with the players expected to use the information. Simply teleporting an unrelated account into the area will only help that account. Before placing a lamp, check the alliance, Federation and diplomatic setup so the Vision reaches the intended fighting alliance.

It is also worth considering what happens when the shield expires. A lamp placed deep inside hostile territory becomes an easy target once it is no longer protected, and losing the castle removes the Vision at exactly the moment the enemy may be preparing to move. Long operations therefore require either a sufficiently long shield or someone assigned to renew and monitor the account.

Used properly, lamps allow low-power accounts to make a meaningful battlefield contribution. They are not there to win fights. Their job is to remove the enemy's ability to hide and give the main alliance the information needed to choose its attacks.

## Thermal Towers and Objective Warfare

Thermal Towers are the backbone of permanent Vision in Legion of Frostborne. They illuminate a broad area, protect territory from the Frozen Realm's environmental effects and create the network through which an alliance expands.

Vision is directly connected to tower placement. The first Thermal Tower must be placed within existing friendly Vision, commonly supplied by a nearby allied castle. Further towers are then placed within the range of the existing tower network. This is why a single forward castle or lamp can be strategically valuable: it can establish the initial visibility required to begin a new route.

The tower network also affects objective warfare. Cities and gates must be covered by an owned or allied Thermal Tower before an alliance can attack them. It is not enough to know where the objective is located. The alliance needs the required tower coverage to interact with it properly.

This makes a tower an operational asset rather than just an area buff. A defensive tower near a gate may be providing Vision of incoming troops, enabling further tower placement and preserving access to the objective at the same time. Losing it can therefore interrupt several parts of the defense simultaneously.

Vision and geothermal protection should not be confused. They are related because Thermal Towers provide both, but the rules governing overlap are not identical. Vision Proximity can overlap freely, while geothermal zones belonging to different alliances are subject to placement and priority restrictions. When examining the map, it is therefore possible for an area to be visible without receiving the same protection from the Frozen Realm's environmental effects.

## Denying Vision by Dismantling Towers

One of the most important offensive uses of Vision is removing the enemy's sources rather than merely adding more of your own. According to the current Thermal Tower rules, a tower being dismantled stops providing Vision to its owner. Friendly towers also cannot be chained from that tower while the dismantling is underway.

This means an attack on a Thermal Tower can have an immediate effect even before its Durability reaches zero. The defenders may lose visibility over nearby castles and troop movements, while their planned expansion route is temporarily interrupted. If the targeted tower was the only source covering a gate, city or narrow approach, the entire area can become much harder to coordinate.

The demolition force naturally creates some local Vision through its own marches and its interaction with the target. Community testing also describes attackers as gaining the tower's Vision while dismantling it. The exact size and duration of this attacking Vision should be rechecked after major KvK updates, but the confirmed defensive consequence is already significant: the tower's owner loses the wide Vision bubble until the demolition troops are expelled.

This explains why alliances should respond quickly when a critical tower begins flashing under attack. Allowing even a small demolition force to remain inside is not harmless simply because the tower will take time to fall. The attackers may already have blinded the surrounding position and disabled its value as a link in the tower chain.

From the attacking side, tower dismantling should be coordinated with whatever comes next. If the goal is to conceal a larger march, expose hidden castles or disrupt reinforcements around a gate, those movements should begin while the defenders are missing their tower Vision. Destroying a tower and then waiting several hours to use the opening wastes much of the tactical value.

## Hiding in an Enemy Blind Spot

Players usually think about Vision offensively, but the system is equally useful for concealment. A castle positioned just beyond the edge of enemy Vision cannot be seen through ordinary map browsing. This is useful for weaker accounts, rally participants, reserve fighters and alts supporting an operation.

The safest blind spots are not simply places without a nearby enemy tower. You must account for enemy castles, captured objectives, Federation partners and moving troops as well. An area that looks dark from one enemy alliance's perspective may be completely visible to another alliance sharing information with it.

Weather can change the calculation. Fog may pull the edge of enemy tower coverage away from your castle, while Sunny weather can suddenly place the same position inside their Vision. If a castle is relying on a very narrow gap for protection, checking the next day's forecast is just as important as checking the eye symbol when first relocating.

Movement also creates exposure. A hidden castle may be revealed when an enemy sends a march past it, even if the march is travelling toward an unrelated resource node. Experienced players sometimes use apparently ordinary gathering routes precisely because the path sweeps through likely blind spots. Remaining hidden therefore depends partly on avoiding predictable locations beside nodes and common travel lines.

## Common Vision Mistakes

Most Vision mistakes come from treating the darkness as empty space rather than as an area containing information you do not currently possess.

- **Assuming an empty map means there are no enemies:** Castles and marches can be sitting directly in front of you without appearing until you create Vision.
- **Ignoring the eye symbol:** If the eye is visible, the enemy can see the position. A castle intended as a hidden staging point should be moved or protected accordingly.
- **Confusing Vision with geothermal protection:** Thermal Towers supply both, but visibility and protection do not follow identical overlap rules.
- **Planning tower chains without checking weather:** Fog can reduce tower range by 25%, while Sunny can make the same route considerably easier.
- **Scouting without an attacker ready:** A passing march may reveal a castle for only a brief window. The combat march should be prepared before the scout reaches it.
- **Using an unprotected lamp:** An exposed alt is easy to remove, and its Vision disappears with it.
- **Forgetting shared Vision:** An enemy Federation may see far more than the nearest hostile alliance's own towers and castles suggest.
- **Treating tower demolition as a slow, harmless process:** The defender can lose the tower's Vision as soon as dismantling begins, long before the tower is destroyed.

## Conclusion

Vision is one of the mechanics that separates Legion of Frostborne from ordinary fighting in Norheim. Castles provide local visibility, captured objectives and Thermal Towers illuminate larger areas, and marches create small moving bubbles that can be used to search through the darkness. All of this information can be shared through alliance, diplomatic and Federation relationships.

The eye symbol shows when a castle or tower is currently exposed to enemy Vision. When it disappears, the position is in a blind spot, but that safety can change quickly when troops pass nearby, a new tower is constructed or Sunny weather extends an existing tower's range.

For ordinary players, the main lesson is to check whether the enemy can see you and to understand how a scouting march can reveal targets. For alliance leadership, Vision is part of the structure of the entire battlefield. It determines tower routes, objective access, forward positioning and the information available during an attack. Fog and Sunny weather change Thermal Tower coverage by 25%, while dismantling a critical tower can blind its owner and interrupt further expansion before the tower itself has fallen.

Once you begin looking at KvK through Vision rather than simply through power and march strength, many battlefield decisions make more sense. The alliance that controls what can be seen often controls where the next fight happens as well.

## Related Guides and Sources

- [Legion of Frostborne Weather System Guide](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/legion-of-frostborne/misc-kvk-guides/legion-of-frostborne-weather-system-guide/)
- [Thermal Towers: Information and Strategies](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/legion-of-frostborne/thermal-towers-info/thermal-towers-info-and-strategies/)

markdown:
### Player Guide: Mastering the "Vitality Touch" Skill in Infinity Kingdom

"Vitality Touch" is a top-tier skill in Infinity Kingdom, renowned for its significant boost to healing and defensive capabilities in your immortal lineups. Perfect for sustain-focused strategies, this skill can be a game-changer in how you manage your troops during intense battles.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/image-13-1024x281.png)

### Overview of Vitality Touch

**Skill Mechanics**:

- **Activation**: Automatically activates every 6 seconds after the battle begins.
- **Healing**: Heals the allied unit that has lost the most troops by 120% of the Recovery Rate.
- **Defense Buff**: Increases physical and magical defense of the healed unit by 10% for 18 seconds.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/image-14-1024x626.png)

This potent combination not only helps in maintaining your troop's health but also provides a rolling defensive buff that can cover multiple immortals over the duration of the battle, enhancing their survivability against both physical and magical attacks.

## Strategic Implementation

**Optimal Use Cases**:

- **Sustain Setups**: Vitality Touch shines in builds where prolonged combat is expected, such as Earth or Holy setups, where maintaining high troop health is crucial.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/image-16-1024x386.png)

- **Shadow Sustain**: Although traditionally less common, integrating Vitality Touch in shadow setups focused on sustain can provide unexpected durability, especially when combined with other defensive skills.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/image-17-1024x538.png)

- **Hybrid Synergy**: In hybrid teams, particularly those including Zenobia, pairing Vitality Touch with skills like "Purify" and "Wine and Dine" can create a resilient core that supports both offensive and defensive maneuvers effectively.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/image-15-1024x383.png)

**Choosing the Right Immortal**: Since the skill’s healing effect is based on the Recovery Rate, which in turn depends on the immortal's Aptitude Attribute, it’s important to select an immortal with a high Recovery Rate to maximize the healing effect. Healers or support immortals generally make the best carriers for this skill.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/image-22-1024x619.png)

## Acquisition Guide

**How to Obtain Vitality Touch**:

- **Triss Event**: Vitality Touch can be purchased through the Triss shop using Cinders. Cinders can be accumulated by participating in various events like Legion of Frostborne or by selling unused skill stones.
- **Accessibility for Free Players**: Free-to-play players have a pathway to this skill by accumulating rewards from events like Legion of Frostborne and converting other resources into Cinders, making it accessible without direct payment.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/image-18-1024x518.png)

#### Tactical Considerations

- **Timing and Placement**: Given the skill activates every 6 seconds, placement in your lineup is crucial. It should ideally be placed on immortals who are likely to sustain significant damage early in the battle to maximize its defensive utility.
- **Buff Stacking**: Managing the defensive buffs to overlap efficiently can create windows of high resilience against incoming damage, pivotal in turning the tides during critical moments of a fight.

#### Conclusion

Vitality Touch is more than just a healing skill; it’s a comprehensive support tool that boosts the defensive and recovery capabilities of your immortals. Whether you are pushing for dominance in sustained fights or looking to add a layer of durability to your hybrids, Vitality Touch offers a versatile solution that can be adapted to a wide range of strategic needs. By integrating this skill thoughtfully, you can enhance your battlefield effectiveness and ensure your immortals last longer and fight harder in the fierce contests of Infinity Kingdom.

## Training Grounds

The Training Grounds is where you can check your army status like total number of available troops, troops that are already deployed, the number of wounded troops, etc. The higher the level of your Training Grounds, the more troops you can have. You cannot build a real army without upgrading your Training Grounds.

![](https://oss.gtarcade.com/ucms/87759b36-77ea-467d-87e9-2008324fdea8_2020-05-13.jpg)

## Walls

The Walls is what protects your Castle city from harm. When you are attacked by enemies you can place armies at your walls to garrison your city. You can also assist fellow alliance teamplayers by sending garrisons to their walls at a time of need. The high the level of your Walls the more durability they have. If an attacker defeats all garrisoned armies on the walls, they also need to defeat the walls themselves. I.e. killing the durability of your wall whilst they take damage from all of your fortifications. You can train fortifications at the walls.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/image-59-1024x435.png)

### The last line of defense

Upgrading your castle level requires specific buildings to have been constructed first. You can find my comprehensive list of all **[requirements for each castle level here](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/development/buildings/castle-upgrade-requirements/)**.

Every Castle level requires you to have upgraded your walls and for walls your training grounds. Hence these two always go hand in hand and you need to upgrade both continually to unlock new Castle levels. **[See Upgrade Costs of Castle levels here.](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/development/buildings/castle-upgrade-costs/)**

title: Water Bath Fire Gilga Hybrid
summary: I get a lot of players sending me requests for march setups, lately I have been getting a lot of interest in running the earth-wind hybrid as a second or third team. Furthermore, many people seem to be running water…
markdown:
I get a lot of players sending me requests for march setups, lately I have been getting a lot of interest in running the earth-wind hybrid as a second or third team. Furthermore, many people seem to be running water mains where they have spent a little to get Attila and Merlin. Other prefer fire or lightning marches but many players are writing saying they have water main since the beginning of the game, but don’t know what to do with it to make it fit with a second and third march build.

**This is the second build guide in the progression series. As such, we are developing upon the F2P build from last time. We are adding Elizabeth Bathory to the water main march for massive improvment to our main march. In addition, some players may at this point be able to run Seondeok who can replace Gilgamesh in our fire team for a nice improvement.**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/Design-uden-navn-1024x306.png)

For the purpose of this guide I shall use a real player from the community. This player reached out and asked me to setup a complete three-march-setup that fits with what he has going for him at the moment. If you are progressing your setups into something more advanced than pure F2P and is looking for inspiration for how to setup your marches, this guide may just be for you!

Togeather with the community I ended up with this three-march-setup to recommend for our requesting-player: **(1) Water main (2) Fire secondary and (3) Earth/Wind Hybrid third.**

In addition to these builds and collective setup, I will include a link to future work on how these builds can improve and develop if you choose to spend to unlock new Immortals.

## The builds

We are turning the water into a standard control-centric setup with Merlin as our core dps. As for the fire, we are building full offense and maxing its burst crit potention, with a bit of luck you can take down a huge chunck of HP on even marches with much higher power with an offensive fire. Lastly our hybrid will be a standard wind-earth hyrbrid with a few modifications since we are not running it as a main. Basically this hybrid is able to get massive value out of a lot of tok skills which are terrible anywhere else. Running it in this way means that we are using top tower of knowledge skills on all three marches instead of having a third with nothing going on (as is often the case).

As you progress you can swap your Yoshitsune and your Gilgamesh 1:1 with Elizabeth Bathory and Seondeok respectively. The build you want to run is as follows. Furthermore, if you can swap Herald with Ragnar this will give you a nice boost to your Merlin's damage output.

**— WATER —
Merlin**: Concentration + Annihilation + Death Breath
**Bathory**: Assist + Malice + Absolute Defense
**Herald/Ragnar**: Shelter + Energy Suppression + Oaken Guard
**Attila**: Adrenaline rush + Fighting Will + Fighting Master

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/image-98.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/image-99.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/image-100.png)

**— FIRE w. GILGA —**
**Seondeok**: Anger + Chaotic Blade + Flame Protection
**Wu**: Chase + Toxic Nova + Rage (if you have enough crit to consistently proc chase, you can go double nova over rage)
**Hippo**: Energy Burst + Missleading + Garrote.
**William**: Weakness + Blessing of Rage + Resist

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/image-89.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/image-90.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/image-91.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/image-92.png)

**— EARTH-WIND HYBRID —**
**Zeno**: Berserk + Blessing of Speed + Life-link
**Qin**: Coercion + Blessing of War + Blessing of Defense
**Hannibal Barca**: Cleave + Physical Shield + Heavenly Thunder
**Alexander**: Duel Master + Combo + Absorb

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/image-93.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/image-94.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/image-95.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/image-96.png)

## Further development and build progression

Like I said in the beginning of this guide, this is tailored for one particular player and then made into a generalized guide for others to seek inspiration from. Your Immortals roster, willingness to spend, server PvP meta may be a lot different from this player’s and as such you should as always make careful decisions that fit your situation. Use the above as inspiration!

In addition to the three-setup-builds we have gone other in this guide, I have made some progression pathways as part of a broader series on low-spender-three-march-setups: [**Read more here.**](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/elements/full-3-march-comps/concept-ideas-for-low-spender-3-march-setups/)

title: Water build for Conquest Season (v2.8.3)
summary: As players progress into the Conquest season in Infinity Kingdom, the Water element composition gains access to its most refined and powerful form. With top-tier Tower of Knowledge (ToK) skills now unlocked and dragon…
markdown:
### Infinity Kingdom Water Build Guide: Conquest Season Edition

As players progress into the Conquest season in *Infinity Kingdom*, the Water element composition gains access to its most refined and powerful form. With top-tier Tower of Knowledge (ToK) skills now unlocked and dragon talent trees fully available, this is the season where your Water march can truly dominate. This guide builds on our earlier articles on Season 1 and Season 2 water setups and takes you into the final optimized version for competitive PvP in Conquest.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-76-1024x461.png)

---

## Core Immortal Lineup for Conquest Water

The Conquest Water march builds on the core composition from Season 2: Artemisia (or Dido), Merlin, Ragnar, and Bjorn (or substitutes like Attila or Hippo if needed). This lineup provides an excellent balance of burst magic damage, crowd control, support sustainability, and debuff synergy.

### Immortal Skill Setup

**Artemisia** (or **Dido** if Artemisia is unavailable):

- **Assist**
- **Heart of Arcana**
- **Weakness**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-82.png)

Artemisia provides the early energy and chill support required to set up Merlin. Assist ensures Merlin is protected and has the highest troop count, ensuring he receives fewer debuffs. Heart of Arcana gives a massive +35% magic damage boost and is essential to scale your burst output. Weakness increases your critical hit chance, making Merlin's high damage spells even more lethal.

**Merlin**:

- **Corrosive Power**
- **Psionic Tide**
- **Fighting Master**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-83.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-84.png)

Merlin is your nuclear warhead. Corrosive Power triggers a cycle of +60% boosted ultimate casts every 3 activations, and Psionic Tide gives him a rapid +200 energy injection after each ultimate. Fighting Master protects Merlin from critical crowd control effects, particularly from Shadow teams that rely heavily on silence and freezes.

**Ragnar**:

- **Weakening Curse**
- **No Escape**
- **Malice**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-85.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-86.png)

Ragnar is the glue that holds this setup together. With his innate support from his talent tree and his frontline tank synergy, he becomes a powerful utility tool. Weakening Curse lowers enemy resistance, No Escape slows enemy energy regen (stopping opposing ultimates), and Malice reduces the crit rate of enemies — a key counter to crit-focused hybrid and shadow builds.

**Bjorn** (or **Attila/Hippo**):

- **Energy Shield**
- **Rage Blessing**
- **Energy Suppression**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-87.png)

Bjorn provides bonus magic damage reduction and a 20% bonus to magic damage dealt, stacking yet again onto Merlin's burst chain. Rage Blessing boosts early regen (pairing well with Arcana and Psionic Tide), while Energy Shield keeps Merlin healthy. If you are using Attila or Hippo, replace Energy Shield with Oaken Guard or Fighting Master depending on opponent types.

---

### Strategic Considerations

Just like earlier seasons, your build must adapt to the enemy teams in your battlegroup. Conquest is filled with players running optimized shadow, hybrid, fire, and chaos setups, so flexing your skill sets is mandatory.

- **Misleading**: Use against physical-heavy opponents to cause missed normal attacks. Stack this with dodge-based artifacts and talents to create miss-focused defense.
- **Malice**: Essential in metas with high crit setups like Shadow or Chaos. Reducing enemy crits can often be the difference between surviving a nuke or not.
- **Weakness**: A key offensive support skill. Boosts your Merlin’s crit potential substantially. A must in this setup unless you are already crit-capped.

---

## Dragon Talent Tree: Water Dragon in Conquest

In Conquest, Dragon Talents become available, and they play a huge role in maximizing your Water build's effectiveness.

**Coalesce** is your go-to talent specialization. It amplifies the magic damage dealt by your dragon’s breath and scales further with chill effects. This stacks beautifully with Bjorn, Ragnar, and Arcana, resulting in devastating Merlin ultimates.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-81-1024x397.png)

If you are still relying on non-Bjorn backlines, **Inspiration** may be useful instead to boost team energy regen. This is especially valuable if you're using Hippo/Attila to maintain energy uptime.

Thanks to the elemental flexibility of the Water Dragon, you retain your 4-element synergy bonus even when running Bjorn (a Shadow immortal). This allows you to push a maximum burst setup without compromising your elemental cohesion.

---

## Progression Path & Chaos Meta

Once you hit Conquest, the next step is entering the Chaos meta. If you acquire Chaos Immortals, consider transitioning Merlin into a more frontloaded burst role by using **Energy Mastery** in place of Psionic Tide.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-88.png)

In Chaos, Merlin becomes the centerpiece of even more refined compositions. Combining Energy Mastery with the rest of your regen and amplification stacking leads to some of the highest frontloaded damage outputs in the game. Merlin effectively becomes a most dangerous AoE caster.

---

## Final Thoughts

Water marches are all about optimizing your damage amplification and protecting Merlin long enough to get his big spells off. With the build outlined above, you ensure fast and frequent ultimates, constant control over the enemy’s abilities, and incredibly high burst damage potential.

If you've followed this guide series from Season 1 to Conquest, congratulations — you now have a Water march that can match (and defeat) some of the strongest setups in *Infinity Kingdom*. Thanks to players like Hastur for contributing meta-defining builds!

Ready to drown your enemies in blue flames? This Conquest Water build will show them the meaning of devastation.

title: Water Build w/o Yoshi & Attila (C30)

markdown:
Castle level 30 - ToK level 30. Around this time you will have dragon in level 26-28 ish and Immortals in your main around 30-35 (this is very rough, everyone's progression is different). We are beginning to hit a level where composition matter and we are loosing to earth spenders - hence we need to beef up on damage support for Merlin, boost Merlin as much as we can, and rely on control on the battleground.

**Keep in mind, that this is a 100% free to play guide. This means, you can do this build VERY easily and without costing you more than the third builder unlock (let's be honest, you need that if you want to play this game - kind of the cost of the game to get that).**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/image-2-1024x538.png)

## How does it work?

In the beginning, you cannot choose another element than water if you want to be a F2P or light spender. If you want to spend, earth is the way. Later in the game, you want to move into a 100% fire main (level 40+) which coincidentally should be run with Abaoji too unless you can get enough fragments through KoH to get Cyrus.

The idea then is to make water as strong as possible. We do that through Merlin. His ultimate skill "Prophecy" is insanly strong as the numbers are simply higher than anything else and it is in AOE. So we need him to dish out damage reliably. Hence, we want to keep him alive and boost his damage.

We also use Herald for some physical off-DPS'ing, as he is extreemly quick to max (season 1 arena) and deals very nice damage. In fact, he is viable all the way to end game.

I personally like Brynhild for her control. She is Attila just with less damage, the control output is massive, meaing you can get interrupts in on key skills. For instance, fighting an earth spender who is not clever enough to run Fighting Master on Charles = Bryn will keep his healing low.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/image-4-1024x600.png)

## ToK Passive Loadout

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/Skaermbillede-2022-08-01-214030.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/Skaermbillede-2022-08-01-214208.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/Skaermbillede-2022-08-01-214216.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/Skaermbillede-2022-08-01-214223.png)

**Merlin**: Concentration + Fire Nova + Root
**Abaoji**: Defense Blessing + Silence
**Herald**: Anger + Garrote + Physical Shield
**Brynhild**: Fighting Master + Adrenaline Rush

### Alternatives & near-term goals:

- If you are getting controlled on Merlin, run Fighting Master over root.
- As soon as you unlock cleave (**level 31**) you want that on Herald. Move Garrote out.

## Power boosts if you want to spend a little

Spending a little goes a long way with this march. Brynhild is by far the weakest link in the chain. The control is good, but she dosen't deal high damage like Attila does (Epic version of Brynhild). You can do two things:

1. Move into **Attila**. This increases your damage and your control significantly. Attila is very stong and have played a key role in many march combinations, incl. old meta (pre patch 2.0) hard counter to shadow! He is still very strong, and my personal preferred choice.
2. Move into**Ramssess II**. He is one of the most underrated Immortals in the game. His damage output is quite fine and his skill makes high physical Immortals like Alexander the Great into wet noodles slapping on rocks. You want to run him as tank and try to position him in front of enemy Alex's. This is the best choice if your goal is arena competition (make the right setup and positioning and beat earth whales)

title: Water Castle lvl 20 Build (w. Merlin)

markdown:
This guide is part of my article series on water builds. If this build is not to your likeing, have a look at the rest of my builds on the water build page. I have multiple builds for any taste available, IB, PvE, arena/ToS builds and F2P/cheap builds.

**This article is for new developing players and part of my guide series which includes builds for Castle level 20, level 30, level 35 and level 40. These builds are made for the average player who unlocks Merlin and later Attila but is not whaling hard.**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/image-43-1024x500.png)

## A Castle level 20 guide to Water

At Castle level 20, you have limited access to Tower of Knowledge passives. Moreover, you will quite quickly reach level 20 and will not have the most amazing stable of Immortals nor many stars ranks on the Immortals in play. As such, this guide attempts to zero in on the average player and where he or she is at in terms of Immortals and Passives around Castle level 20. It is based on an average player accounts and experiances with where we expect to be at around this progress level. Special thank you to Jessica who has been the primary driver, inspiration and brains behinds all of this!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/image-38-1024x710.png)

## Immortals

At this point in your progress, the best options for Immortal composition is to run**Merlin, Helen, Eulji and Bryn**.

**Note that if you have been able to buy Attila at this early stage or be super lucky and obtain, Hippolytta, Richard or William you want to swap one of these Immortals in to replace Eulji. If you have Attila + one of the other subs swap both Eulji and Bryn to Attila + either of the previously mentioned.**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/merlin-1024x1024.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/helen-1024x1024.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/euljimundeok-1024x576.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/brynhild-1024x1024.png)

## Passive (ToK) setup

At this point in your progress, you most likely have **0 stars on Merlin, 7 stars on Helen, 5 stars on Eulji and 5 stars on Bryn**.

**You should not spend your Purple Crystals on upgrading passive levels just yet. Wait untill you reach higher levels to spend this valuable ressource!**

### You should run the following passive setup at this stage:

**Merlin**: no stars

**Helen**: Wisdom (1) + Meteor (1)

**Eulji**: Onslaught (1) *or Combo (1) if you want to do bosses more efficient.*

**Bryn**: Silence (1)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/Merlin20.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/helen-1.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/eulji.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/bryn.png)

**[Continue to Water Build for Castle level 30](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/progression-builds/builds-castle-level-30/water-castle-lvl-30-build-w-merlin/)** to see what you should be building towards as you continue your journey in Norheim!
