markdown:
***"Navigating Changes in Infinity Kingdom's Legion of Frostborne Season: A Deep Dive into Alliance Dynamics"***

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-79-1024x342.png)

Infinity Kingdom's Legion of Frostborne season has taken an intriguing turn with the recent 2.6.3 update, introducing key changes that promise to shake up alliance dynamics. While the adjustment to the War Declaration system might be considered a minor inconvenience if managed properly, the real game-changer lies in the alterations to alliance diplomacy. This article delves into the substantial impact of these modifications, especially for active servers relying on strategic alliance management.

## War Declaration: A Minor Annoyance with Proper Management

The introduction of the War Declaration system mandates that players formally declare war on a City or Checkpoint before launching a siege.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-81.png)

While this may seem like a minor change, it can become an annoyance if not managed effectively. Players holding the rank of Alliance R6 and R5 now have the exclusive authority to declare war, and a mandatory three-minute waiting period follows each declaration.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-80-1024x561.png)

*Impacts:*

- **Strategic Adjustments:** Properly managing the new War Declaration system becomes crucial to avoid unnecessary delays. Alliances need to coordinate their efforts efficiently, ensuring smooth transitions between diplomacy and war to maintain an active and strategic edge.

## Alliance Diplomacy: A Game-Changing Shift for Active Servers

The 2.6.3 update significantly alters the landscape of alliance diplomacy, limiting alliances to a maximum of nine allies. This has profound implications, particularly for active servers accustomed to utilizing multiple alliances for strategic advantages.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-82-1024x542.png)

*Impacts:*

- **Challenges for Active Servers:** Active servers face substantial challenges with the new alliance diplomacy restrictions. The ability to chain thermals from numerous alliances to expand into new territories becomes a logistical puzzle. The tactic of instantly building a thermal with a fresh alliance, previously offering free placement, now demands more effort as it occupies one of the precious diplomacy slots.
- **Loss of Vision in Occupied Territories:** Perhaps the most significant impact is the loss of vision in territories occupied by the server itself. This change disrupts the traditional strategy of maintaining visibility across various regions, a shift that may hinder active servers in planning and executing strategic moves.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/image-83-1024x480.png)

- **Scaling Mechanic Disadvantages:** The changes in alliance diplomacy seem designed as a scaling mechanic, where the benefits of having numerous active alliances diminish as the count rises. This approach appears to impose disadvantages on active servers, favoring one-color servers. The potential consequences may lead to imbalances in competition, favoring servers with fewer but more powerful alliances.

As the Legion of Frostborne season unfolds, players must adapt to the nuanced challenges posed by the 2.6.3 update. While the War Declaration system may be a minor inconvenience with proper management, the real test lies in navigating the intricacies of alliance diplomacy. For active servers, these changes demand a reevaluation of strategies, resource allocation, and diplomatic maneuvers. The season promises to be an exciting test of adaptability and resilience, revealing whether the advantages conferred on one-color servers can truly stand against the might of larger, stronger, and more active alliances. The quest for a vibrant gaming community must always take precedence over a game dominated by a select few with superior advantages. Let the battle for Frostborne commence!

title: What happens when you are defeated at your own walls?
summary: Infinity Kingdom Guide: What Happens When You're Defeated – Understanding Zeroing, Training Ground Deaths & Second Wind
markdown:
**Infinity Kingdom Guide: What Happens When You're Defeated – Understanding Zeroing, Training Ground Deaths & Second Wind**

## Introduction

Being defeated in *Infinity Kingdom* is a rite of passage—and whether it’s a calculated risk during PvP or an unfortunate surprise while offline, understanding what happens when your castle falls is essential to progressing intelligently. This guide breaks down what happens during a defeat, how troop losses work, what you lose, what you might recover, and how to strategize around the game’s core mechanics of defeat and zeroing.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/image-105.png)

---

## The Mechanics of Defeat: Where Troops Die

When you’re attacked and lose the battle, several things happen depending on where your troops are and what part of your city is impacted.

### Garrisoned Troops (Castle Wall Defense)

- If your castle is attacked, you can have a march defending yourself by setting them as Garrisons on your walls. If you do, then the defending team fights your enemy first. **Some troops die**, and **some are wounded** and sent to the **hospital**. Normal battle just like if you had attacked an enemy.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/image-106.png)

If you loose the fight at your walls.... the following occur:

First of all you loose **Prosperity** based on the power differential, i.e. based on how much you loose. If you are loosing to a much more powerful enemy with a very large troop count you will loose more prosperity. While I cannot figure out the precise equation for it, it seems that the amount of prosperity lost is **based off of two things: 1 the amount of troops lost in training grounds and 2 the enemy winners carrying capacity.**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/image-107.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/image-108.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/image-109.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/image-110.png)

Interestingly, you dont always loose the same amount of Prosperity even against the same enemy. It seems like a loss with fewer troops dead gives you a smaller amount of prosperity loss. BUT there is also a cap on how much Prosperity you can loose per attack which seems to be dependent solely on your Walls level.

### Troop Losses - Training Grounds

- If the enemy defeats your main defense, additional losses occur in your **Training Grounds (TG)**.
- **TG troops are NOT protected** and are **permanently lost** upon defeat.
- This includes any troop tier in the TG regardless of how they were trained.
- You will loose between **2-3% of your current amount of troops in your training grounds**, based on the amount currently sitting around. If your training grounds are **full**you will loose around **3%** of the troops there, and once it gets **below 50%** full you loose around**2.5%** and as it **empties**you get down to around **2%** troops lost per defeat in Training Grounds alone.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/image-111-1024x529.png)

***OBS:** This is only training grounds losses, you also loose from Garrison and Hospital!*

### Troop Losses -Hospital

- Hospitals have a capacity like the Training Grounds does.
- Once you are defeated, the enemy will raid your hospital and you loose a portion of the wounded troops waiting to be healed. These will **die permanently**.

---

## Resource Loss After a Defeat

Losing a battle doesn’t only affect your troops—it impacts your economy.

### Here’s what happens:

- **Farms**: Any **unclaimed resources** on your farms are the first to be taken by attackers.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/image-112-1024x314.png)

- **Storage**: After farms are emptied, your **unprotected stored resources** are raided.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/image-113-1024x556.png)

- **Protected resources** in your storehouse remain untouched.

---

## The Hidden Cost: Honor and Tier Differences

The attacker gains **honor** based on how many troops they defeat—and **which troop tiers they defeat**.

- **Killing higher-tier troops grants more honor**.
- **Killing lower-tier troops grants reduced honor**, even in large numbers.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/image-114.png)

This system prevents honor farming through low-tier units and rewards strategic, fair fights. If you’re zeroed, you give up a lot of honor—but most of that value only benefits the attacker if your troops are strong.

Note: The first Defeats will yield more honor, because we are killing a larger portion of troops in total even given the same Garrisoned units. This is because we are killing A LOT more troops at the Training Grounds and the hospital during the first attacks. This is down to the **maths of losses at the training grounds.**

While a healthy training ground will loose around 3% and an almost empty one will loose 2%, that may not seem like a big difference - but you should remember that its % of current amount of troops. So having 700K troops in training grounds while getting **3% nets you around 21K dead troops**in TG alone whereas **2% on an almost empty TG of e.g. 200K troops gives you just 4K dead troops**.

Ultimately, the amount of losses incurred is huge for large filled training grounds as the death % increase the more troops there are and a percentage of a full training grounds is so much more than a near empty one!

***TIP**: If you are farming honor using the honor talent, you want to always keep the target being garrisoned at full training grounds capacity. The TG losses will expans your honor gain significantly.*

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/image-116.png)

---

## Second Wind: Partial Compensation After Zeroing

Once zeroed, the game provides a one-time partial recovery system called **Second Wind**.

When you “fly” back to your castle (after being defeated and relocated), the system will:

- Refund a **significant amount of resources**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/image-117-1024x575.png)

The amount of resources returned is not clear to me, I believe its somewhere around 10-20% of the troop value killed since last time you whent flying.

I know for certain that the amount of resources returned through Second Wind is a result of two things:

1. The **default base amount** that will be offered to you regardless of losses. This is very small and seems to be based off of castle level.
2. The **variable is the amount of troops lost.** You are getting resources back from second wind based on how many troops have died since you last flew (there seem to be a diminishing timer on this too, but if you fight actively you wont notice). Basically you get back a portion of the resources spent training the troops that have died since last time you flew.

I do not know for certain what the % returned is, but it seems to me in testing it a bit, that we are getting around 10-20% back through second wind. Please do hit me up if you know more!

## Strategic Tips: How to Avoid Defeats entirely or Diminish the losses

### Before a Defeat:

- **Use your shield** consistently if offline during high-risk times.
- **Empty your Training Grounds** if expecting an attack. Send your armies out to farm or build a city. They will not die if not in your castle.
- **Claim all farm resources** regularly.
- Keep hospitals **upgraded and empty** to maximize capacity.

---

## Conclusion

Defeat in *Infinity Kingdom* is painful but manageable—especially once you understand the mechanics.

- Not all troops die in a defeat.
- **TG and hospital deaths are real and permanent**.
- **Honor is earned** based on **tier differences**, making smart PvP vital.
- **Second Wind offers a small safety net**, but don’t rely on it to restore you fully.

By preparing smartly and understanding where your losses come from, you can recover quickly and reduce long-term damage. Whether you're a casual player or a hardcore PvPer, this knowledge can mean the difference between bouncing back—or burning out.

There are a lot of unknowns still when it comes to the precise equations used in calculating troops deaths, etc. If you have any information that I dont, please reach out on Discord and share!

title: What Is a Voucher in Infinity Kingdom?
summary: So this week’s 'question of the week' that I have been getting the most both on Discord and in-game has been: “What’s a voucher, and how does it work?” I think this question is popping up a lot right now because of the…
markdown:
So this week’s 'question of the week' that I have been getting the most both on Discord and in-game has been: *“What’s a voucher, and how does it work?”* I think this question is popping up a lot right now because of the new **Spender Voucher Event** that GTarcade just dropped through their social media channels. The event itself is nothing crazy — you can search for your account via a GTarcade webpage and buy **vouchers at a 5% discount**. While discounts are always nice, its only real value for 1 and 2 $ bundles or if you are desperate for gems. But more on that. In this article we will briefly go over the new spender campaign but mainly focus on the core question of "what is a 'voucher' and how do they work?"

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-77.png)

Before getting into whether it’s worth it, let’s first break down what a **voucher** actually is and how it works inside Infinity Kingdom.

---

### What a Voucher Actually Is

A **voucher** in Infinity Kingdom is basically **a form of in-game payment**. You can think of it as a prepaid credit that you can use in the **in-game shop** to buy bundles, event packs, or any of the regular offers that pop up there.

You can’t earn vouchers inside the game directly — they come from **GTarcade events or bundles** that you buy **outside** the game (like from the official GTarcade website or app store promotions).

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-82-1024x632.png)

Once you buy one, the system automatically sends it to your **in-game mailbox**. From there, it becomes an item you can find in your **inventory**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-81-1024x633.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-80-1024x638.png)

Each voucher has a **specific dollar value**, such as $1, $2, $6, $20, etc. When you go to the in-game shop, you’ll see the option to **pay using a voucher** if you have one available (if your in-game shop is using your local currency, don't worry the vouchers work on the bundles just the same). So if you have a $5.99 voucher and you buy a $5.99 bundle, the voucher covers that cost fully — no real money needed, or well you spent the money on the Gtarcade app instead of the in-game shop.

A few key details worth knowing:

- Most vouchers **expire after 30 days**, so don’t just let them sit there.
- For some reason, **$5.99 vouchers don’t expire**, which makes them possible to hold onto.
- Vouchers can only be **used inside the in-game shop**, **not** in the GTarcade App’s external shop or official website events.

---

### About the Current Spender Voucher Event

The new **Spender Voucher Event** is pretty straightforward: GTarcade gives you a 5% discount on buying vouchers directly. You search for your account name or castle number on their event page, choose the voucher amount, and buy it with the discount applied. **[See campaign here.](https://topup.gtarcade.com/accountLogin?game_id=408&op_id=2758&gameName=Infinity%20Kingdom&gameType=1&isShop=1&tax_type=1)**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-83-1024x431.png)

Now, while 5% off is fine, the event’s**value isn’t amazing**. Here’s why:

- Most players who want vouchers already need them for events like **Stellar Compass**, **Sparks of Galaxy**, **Chaos Roulette**, or **Wisdom Well** — but those events usually give *extra currency or rewards* if you buy directly from the **GTarcade in-game bundles**.
- The **daily bundles** (especially the three Pearl bundles) often come with **extra AP and SP bottles**, making them a better deal overall.
- The voucher event doesn’t give you that kind of bonus — just the small discount itself.

If you are looking to buy 1$ and 2$ bundles OR if you want vouchers to buy in-game items because you favor getting gems over more e.g. event currency you will find value from the event. But in general I would advise you make sure to get the most efficient bundles over in-game bundles that award gems. For example, if you are buying Frosty Orbs for Sparks of Galaxy with the 1$ and 2$ bundles, you get the same amount from Gtarcade and in-game store, but you get gems from the in-game store, and as such you should buy vouchers and redeem in-game. Here this campaign is, well... not good value, but the best value you will get. Beware, that as you enter the 5$ and above tier, you get more value from Gtarcade as the number of Frosty Orbs increases over in-game bundles.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-86.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-85.png)

In general, you will get better value in the Gtarcade store. But always compare for max efficiency!

For example, you can get a 3x 5.99 (3*6=18) voucher plus 9x Major AP and 9x Major SP bottles plus 1,100 VIP and 1 million gold by spending just 15$ in the Gtarcade App, whereas the in-game shop gives you a few gems but no other side rewards and 3x will cost you the full 18$ insead of 15$ plus side rewards.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-78.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-84.png)

The same is true for Gtarcade bundles for events, like buying **8x** Divine Coins (coins for Wisdom Well event) for 5$ on Gtarcade, compared to getting just **4x** Divine Coins for 5$ in-game (plus 520 gems and 500 VIP points and 100K gold).

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-79.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-87.png)

So while it’s technically a “discount,” the **total value per dollar** is usually better if you just stick to the **regular GTarcade bundles** instead of chasing this event.

### Bottom Line

Vouchers are **prepaid credits** you can use in the **in-game shop** to buy bundles in-game. They come from **GTarcade’s website events or bundles**, arrive in your in-game mailbox, and most expire after 30 days.

The current **Spender Voucher Event** gives a small 5% discount, which isn’t bad — but not enough to make it better than the regular GTarcade bundles, which still give more total value.

Always compare bundles across campaigns and stores, the options here are subject to change so always compare across shops when you are planning your spending.

---

---

title: What is Elemental Bond and how does it differ from the old From Triumph
summary: With the release of Patch 2.8.4, Infinity Kingdom has retired the
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/image-56-1024x568.png)

With the release of Patch 2.8.4, *Infinity Kingdom* has retired the long-standing and generally underwhelming **Triumph of Fate** event, replacing it with a completely revamped and significantly improved version: **Elemental Bond**. This new event introduces a modernized structure, rotating Immortal pools, and a cost-effective shard acquisition method for paying players.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/image-60-1024x556.png)

In this guide, we’ll break down how the new Elemental Bond event works, its key differences from Triumph of Fate, optimal spending strategy, and overall evaluation from both a pay-to-play and free-to-play perspective.

---

## What Changed From Triumph of Fate?

Triumph of Fate used to offer:

- 12-card flip board
- Up to 12 Immortal Shards
- 1 Sun Crystal, 2 Artifact Fragment Chests
- Some Dragon Crystals, EXP Scrolls, and Speedups
- 2 free daily flips
- Additional flips at 300 Gems each

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/image-58-1024x573.png)

However, this event was widely criticized for its poor rewards, low Immortal variety, and lack of shard consistency.

With Patch 2.8.4, Triumph of Fate has been retired. In its place stands **Elemental Bond**, with meaningful upgrades that focus on value, predictability, and expanded Immortal choices.

---

## How the New Elemental Bond Works

**Event Duration:** Weekly, from Friday to Monday.

### Event Mechanics:

- You flip cards on a 12-tile board, aiming to match pairs.
- Each flip costs **1 Soulglass Crest**, a new event currency available only via in-game bundles.
- Instead of flipping one by one, you can use a **Flip All** option, which costs 12 Soulglass Crests and instantly gives all the rewards.

### Rewards Per Round:

- **12 Immortal Fragments** of your selected target
- **30 Element Dragon Shards** matching your Immortal’s element

### Rotation System:

- Immortals are split into two-element groups that rotate every two days:  - Water & Earth
- Earth & Lightning
- Lightning & Wind
- And so on
- Only elemental Immortals are available (no Shadow, Holy, or Chaos)
- Immortal pool includes **high-value rares** such as Charles, Han, and Baldwin

### Bundle Pricing:

- All packs offer the same consistent value: **1 Soulglass Crest = $0.25**
- 12 Crests = $3 (cost to complete 1 full flip session)
- No value degradation in higher-priced bundles (a rarity for IK)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/image-59-1024x532.png)

---

## Is Elemental Bond Worth It?

### For Light to Mid Spenders

- **YES.**
- $3 per 12 Fragments of top-tier Immortals like Charles or Khan is excellent.
- Compare this to $99 Epic Return packs or Lucky Spins with lower predictability.
- You also receive a small number of Dragon Shards to help develop dragons.

### For Free-to-Play (F2P) Players

- **NO.**
- Unlike Triumph of Fate, **no free daily flips** are available.
- No way to earn Soulglass Crests through gameplay or gems.
- The event creates a stronger paywall around Immortal acquisition.

---

## Strategic Tips

- **Always use Flip All**: Since the reward is fixed and there’s no RNG advantage to flipping manually, save time and just Flip All for 12 Crests.
- **Choose Wisely**: Pick Immortals that are hard to get elsewhere. Go for Charles, Baldwin, Han, or Wu if available.
- **Bundle Efficiency**: Buying the cheapest bundles repeatedly yields the same value as large packs — buy according to your budget.
- **Dragon Shards**: Don’t expect large shard gains here. This is more about Immortal progress than Dragon growth.

---

## Final Verdict

### Pros:

- Predictable, fixed-price Immortal acquisition
- High-value Immortals in rotation
- Excellent for catch-up and focused spending
- Consistent pack value (rare for IK)

### Cons:

- Fully paywalled; no F2P access
- Limited Dragon Shard gains
- No Artifact rewards or added bonuses

Elemental Bond is a strong addition to the game for low- and mid-spenders. While it does remove free options for F2P players, it makes acquiring some of the game’s best Immortals significantly more affordable and predictable. It represents a step forward in value, though not necessarily in accessibility.

We hope to see future iterations include hybrid mechanics, such as a free daily flip or gem conversion to open it up to more players.

---

Stay tuned for rotation schedules and best picks from each cycle in upcoming guides!

title: What is it and how do I use them?
summary: You downloaded Infinity Kingdom, you have completed the tutorial and now you are fighting gnomes left and right, killing bosses and most importantly of all - you are growing your power and preparing to fight other…
markdown:
You downloaded Infinity Kingdom, you have completed the tutorial and now you are fighting gnomes left and right, killing bosses and most importantly of all - you are growing your power and preparing to fight other players! In Infinity Kingdom, your PvP power is determined by many factors. Element counters, technology, troop tier, Immortal strength, boost level, EXP level, equipment, artifacts and **passives**.

Passive skills from the Tower of Knowledge (ToK) are vital to your ability to fight and win battles. If you study your armies strenths and weaknesses, make strong combinations of skills and focus on getting these to a high rank quicky - then you are able to win battles against players much higher power than you. I personally rely on well crafted earth team with the right passives to win versus holy marches 40k+ more power.

**Passives are the most important aspect of immortal strength in Infinity Kingdom.**

## So what presicly are they?

A ToK skill (also referred to as passive) is a skill which bring unique effect to any Immortal you equip it to. As you can see below, every Immortal has a frame named "Skills".

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/image-1.png)

Here you can see the Immortals Ultimate ability (first one) and the ToK skill slots afterwards (for epic Immortals like Wu = 3 slos).

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/image-2.png)

**For example**: Garrote is a triggered skill, meaning it only activates when its trigger is true. In this case every 6 seconds of fighting there is a 40% chance that Garrote will deal damage to three random enemy units and apply a damage over time effect for the next 6 seconds.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/image-1024x553.png)

## Where do I find all the skills?

While you have been looking around exploring it, you must have noticed this building:

![](https://oss.gtarcade.com/forum/png/2022-04-16/249781_faa81d07-c5d8-4a70-9860-17e6c943b4de_105828.png)

**The Tower of Knowledge.**

Once you clicked on it, you saw lots of colored icons, with lots of different effects.... these are all skills you can choose to develop and equip to your Immortals via the Immortal screen above.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/image-3-1024x516.png)

The Tower of Knowledge will be crucial for developing your marches, here in fact you can learn new skills to add to your Immortals.

### There are four levels of skills:

- green
- blue
- purple
- gold

From green to gold, the green ones will give less power, while the gold ones, will give more power.

This **doesn't mean** though that having all gold skills will give you an advantage over teams with both purple and gold skills.

## So how do we use em?

Step one: Click the Immortal.

Step two: Click on the Passive slot where you would like to set a skill

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/image-4.png)

Step three: Find the skill you think is best for your Immortal and your skill combination, i.e. in this case we want another Nova or Anihilation since we are procing chase for burst damage.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/image-5-1024x590.png)

Step four: Hit Equipment (should be "Equip") and your done.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/image-6.png)

## Costs to unlock and upgrade the skills

Each skill has 8 levels and the costs to upgrade them differ based on the skill's color. **[You can read more about the cost of upgrading in my guide here.](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/combat/passives/tok-passives-upgrade-costs/)**

title: What is it and how does it work?
summary: Throne of the Supreme is a cross-server PvP tournament in Infinity
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-1-1024x568.png)

### What is Throne of the Supreme?

Throne of the Supreme is a **cross-server PvP tournament** in *Infinity Kingdom* that showcases the top players from many servers battling it out in a grand arena. It typically **opens around the same time as a server's first Season 1 of KvK (Conquest Season)** and is one of the most exciting competitive events in the game.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-683x1024.png)

This event lets you test your strength against the best – without risking any troop losses.

---

### How Does It Work?

#### No Troop Losses – Just Glory

In this event, **your own Immortals and troops are used**, but the battles are **simulated** – **no troops are lost**, and healing isn’t required. This means you can go all out with your best builds and strategies without worry.

---

### Stage 1: Ranking Battles (Arena Style)

The first stage plays like the **regular Arena**, but it’s part of the Supreme competition. All participants are placed in a large ranking system and fight each other to climb the leaderboard.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-2-1024x333.png)

- Fight other players to earn points and improve your rank.
- Only the **Top 64 players** will qualify to move on to the next stage.
- This part of the event is **very competitive**, so make sure to use your strongest Immortals, best troop synergies, and optimal relics.

---

### Stage 2: Knockout Bracket

After the top 64 are determined, the event switches to a **bracket-style knockout tournament**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-4-1024x428.png)

- Players are divided into fixed brackets.
- Each round eliminates half the field.
- The format goes from 64 → 32 → 16 → 8 → 4 → 2 → Champion.

This stage tests your consistency and ability to win against top opponents in **best-of matches**.

---

### Cross-Server Competition

Unlike regular Arena, **Throne of the Supreme is cross-server**, so you’ll face top players from many different servers. This increases the challenge and prestige of the event.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-5-1024x471.png)

---

### Side Event: Betting System

Alongside the tournament is a **betting mini-game**, where you can place bets on which players you think will win their matchups.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-7-1024x497.png)

- Use your predictions to earn **valuable rewards** like gems, speedups, and rare items.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-6-1024x519.png)

- Smart betting can make this side event just as profitable as participating directly!

---

### Tips for Success

- Optimize your lineups with strong synergy and well-upgraded Immortals.
- Scout the leaderboard early to understand the competition.
- Participate in the betting system even if you didn’t qualify – it’s worth it!
- Save your strongest teams and relics for the knockout rounds.

---

### Conclusion

Throne of the Supreme is a true test of PvP strength and strategy in *Infinity Kingdom*. Whether you're fighting to be crowned the Supreme Champion or making smart bets on your favorite competitors, it’s an event no player should miss!

title: What is Prime League how does it work?
summary: New with patch 2.0 we have Illusion Battlefield style tournaments aka. Illusion Battle Prime League.
markdown:
New with patch 2.0 we have Illusion Battlefield style tournaments aka. **Illusion Battle Prime League**.

## What is IB Prime League?

It is a free-to-play game inside the IK universe. The battles are styles same as Illusion battles, but there are key differences

1. This is a **tournament**style format. Meaning you have rounds to gather ranking and must fight to progress into the playoffs.
2. This is a free-to-play friendly event where **EVERYONE has the same** pre-defined set of Immortals, dragons, and passive skills to choose from and build any march out of what is provided.
3. **No boosts.** No more playing against solo-alliance servers with all buffs active or trying to rally down a whale with VIP 15 bonuses. No boosts from Alliance Tech, Alliance Terriroty, Academy Research, Lord Talents, Nobility, Well of Time, Official posts, castle skins, VIP level or building level counts. In other words, NO BOOSTS. Only thing you have access to is buffs, which you want to have on for the battle same as always.
4. Slowly increase the strength of your march. We upgrade passives using Violet of the Void. **We get 50 x Violet Void currency every week during Prime League,**meaning for the first battle, we have just 50 to spend!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/Skaermbillede-2022-04-22-212333-1024x551.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/Skaermbillede-2022-04-22-212227.png)

Check your calendar for the Prime League tab where you find info on the game as well as the **schedule**for battles coming up.

## How does it work?

- You register for the battle same as with 'real' IB. You need to talk to your officers or alliance leader.

- You must set your teams and build them out inside the Prime League framework. Since you will not be fighting with your real Immortals or armies, you must build (theorycraft) a march for this specific game content. See below.
- The battles work same as any other IB. Specialization talents, troops allocation (provided free). You must also heal your troops in battle, meaning there will be an advantage for those with many speedups (small P2W advantage). You can speed marches moving to or from a location and you can instant recall. Costs are the same as ourside Prime League.

## Create your marches / setups!

You MUST create your armies yourself. You cannot use your real marches and have to lock in your Prime League marches before battle phase begin.

Click on the Prime League Tab --> Go to Top left --> Set formation --> Set Immortal passives.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/Skaermbillede-2022-04-22-202633-1024x568.png)

**Remember that you can set four marches**. In Pre-league (beginning of Prime League) no one has very strong marches since we are limited to upgrading only a new ranks on our passives. This means, you can build some solid second and third marches.

*I still recommend your fourth as a conserving 1-troop march to poke and confuse the enemy.*

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/Skaermbillede-2022-04-22-202655-1024x579.png)

## How does passives and upgrading work in Prime League?

When you have chosen which marches to build, you need to setup your Immortals with passives.

- You upgrade passives by spending the currency "Violet of the Void". **We get 50 x Violet Void currency every week during Prime League, meaning for the first battle, we have just 50 to spend!**
This means you are able to max 1-2 passives. Therefore, you need to review passive descriptions again to find those that perform well on low levels and those that needs to be high rank to have an impact - e.g. Fighting Will is a very strong max level passive, but as rank 1 the % is so low that the passive is worthless.
- Find marches and guide here: **[Prime League Builds](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/prime-league-illusion-battle/prime-league-builds/)**

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/Skaermbillede-2022-04-22-203813-1.png)

- **Melting/Reborn a passive returns 100% of the Violet Voids you invested**. This means that you can theorycraft a lot and try different things out, and that as we get more Voids available the meta will shift quickly from the strong baseline passives into the strong maxed Epic passives.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/Skaermbillede-2022-04-22-202920-1024x595.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/Skaermbillede-2022-04-22-202847-1024x565.png)

## What is Pre-league and Playoffs?

Pre-league are the beginning matches of the Prime League season. Here we play others and gain ranking to qualify for the playoffs. During the Playoffs we will face off other alliances for 1v1 battles (think of Throne tournament layout).

### Key differences is passive progression

- We gain 50 violets per week, meaning by the time we reach playoffs we have a lot of violets to invest.
- We also gain access to new passive skills when Prime League hits the playoff stage. If you open up your Prime League tab and hit upgrade on a passive you are taken to the Tower of Skills for Prime League. Here you can see the cutoff. The cutoff is the level 40 ToK skills.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/Skaermbillede-2022-04-22-202955-2-1024x687.png)

title: What to buy as a spender in season 1?
summary: Season 1 is where spending efficiently matters the most, because almost everything looks valuable when your account is new. Immortal fragments, skills, AP, resources and event currencies can all provide immediate power…
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-200-1024x512.png)

## What to Buy as a Spender in Season 1?

Season 1 is where spending efficiently matters the most, because almost everything looks valuable when your account is new. Immortal fragments, skills, AP, resources and event currencies can all provide immediate power, but not all of them age equally well once you move into later seasons.

The best way to approach Season 1 spending is therefore not simply to ask what makes you stronger today. You also need to consider whether the thing you are buying will still matter once you reach Conquest.

This guide is aimed at **light and mid spenders who want good long-term value**, rather than players trying to buy every possible advantage in Season 1. Whales competing for the top of the server will naturally have different priorities.

It is also worth noting that the Season 1 shop and event structure has changed considerably. **The old Stardust Wheel recommendation is no longer relevant**, as Stardust has been replaced by Zuma and seasonal events. Some other purchases, particularly Cinders and Divine Well spending, also need to be looked at differently under the current system.

---

## Golden Path — Still One of the Best Season 1 Purchases

The **Golden Path** is still one of the easiest purchases to recommend in Season 1, although the reason it is valuable has changed quite a bit over time. It used to be an exceptional source of Purple Soul Crystals for developing Tower of Knowledge skills, but that is no longer the main reason I would buy it. Seasonal events now provide so many Soul Crystals and Philosopher's Stones that both skill development and normal summoning are considerably easier to sustain than they used to be.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-201-1024x575.png)

The real value of Golden Path today is the combination of **immortal progression, artifacts, AP, SP and additional opportunities to obtain immortals that are otherwise awkward to develop early**. The exact rewards depend on the active pass, but this is one of the better places to pick up useful seasonal immortals such as **YSS**, while also progressing artifacts for both elemental and seasonal immortals. Those are rewards that can directly affect the marches you are actually developing rather than simply adding more generic materials to an already plentiful resource pool.

The **AP and SP** are also more important than they may initially appear. Season 1 is largely a race to develop the account quickly enough to keep farming, upgrading and progressing without unnecessary downtime. Having additional AP supports continued PvE farming, while SP helps maintain the pace of development through the season. For an active spender, those resources translate into faster overall account growth rather than a single temporary power increase.

Another reward I value is the **random Immortal Summon Fragments**. Philosopher's Stones are much easier to accumulate now, but not every useful immortal is sitting conveniently in the normal summon pool. **Genghis Khan**, for example, is still harder to obtain because he is not available through regular summoning. Random summon fragments therefore retain some interesting upside: you are not guaranteed the immortal you want, but they give you additional chances at immortals that normal Philosopher's Stone accumulation cannot solve as easily.

This is also why I would no longer sell Golden Path to new players primarily on Soul Crystals. They are certainly useful, and you will still consume plenty of them while upgrading Tower of Knowledge skills, but scarcity is what determines spending value. With modern seasonal events handing out large quantities of Purple Soul Crystals and Philosopher's Stones, neither resource is the bottleneck it once was.

Golden Path remains a very good Season 1 purchase; **the reason has simply changed**. Buy it for the immortals, artifacts, AP/SP and broader progression it provides, with the random Immortal Summon Fragments offering some additional upside for harder-to-acquire immortals. Treat the Soul Crystals as a useful extra rather than the main reason to spend.

---

## Daily Bundles — Useful, but Don't Overcommit Early

Daily Bundles need a little more nuance than the old recommendation gave them.

Their main attraction is the steady supply of resources, AP and Pearls, but the Pearl side of the equation becomes much more relevant later when artifact empowerment enters the picture. The problem in Season 1 is that a new player usually does not know which immortals they will eventually want to build around.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-202-1024x538.png)

That makes heavy early investment into artifact-related progression somewhat speculative.

For a light spender, **the $1 Daily Bundle is a reasonable stopping point**, and you can continue doing that until Conquest becomes realistically achievable. It gives you some steady account progression without committing much money to a system whose eventual targets may still change.

For larger spenders, the extra AP can certainly be useful if you are farming heavily, but I would no longer describe Daily Bundles as something every mid spender automatically needs to buy every day. Their value depends heavily on how aggressively you are farming and how much you are prepared to spend over an entire season.

In other words, the cheap daily purchase is sensible. Going much further should have a purpose.

---

## Divine Well / Wisdom Well — Strong Rewards, but Now an Expensive Weekly Commitment

The old version of this guide treated Wisdom Well as something you could gradually approach through cheap bundles and save the currency for later. The current system needs to be evaluated differently because **Divine Well is now weekly rather than monthly**, making consistent participation considerably more expensive.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-203-1024x561.png)

There are still very strong skills available through the system, and spending here can absolutely make an account stronger. The issue is efficiency.

Buying into a premium skill system every week adds up very quickly, particularly during Season 1 when you may not even know what your long-term Conquest march will be. A skill that looks essential for your current Water, Earth or Lightning march may end up sitting unused once your account changes direction.

For a player trying to dominate Season 1, there will naturally be cases where buying the correct skill is worth the premium. If one specific skill completes your main march and you are actively fighting for top rankings, short-term power has real value.

For an efficiency-focused spender, however, I would be much more conservative.

The question should not be, **"Is this a good skill?"** It should be, **"Am I confident I will still use this skill later?"**. If the answer is uncertain, there are usually better places to spend your money. Now to determine which skills are worth getting already in season 1, head on over to the IK-wiki discord where veteran players are more than happy to help you figure out the right skill investments for your build!

---

## Cinders — The Source Has Changed

The previous recommendation to simply save Cinders until Conquest also needs updating because the way players obtain them has changed.

With the old Stardust system gone, the Cinders you are seeing in Season 1 are most likely coming through the **1050 Grail Box** rather than the old event structure.

That changes how I would think about them. The Grail Box contains several things you may want depending on the stage of your account, so you should not view the purchase purely as "buying Cinders." You are buying the overall box and then deciding how its value fits into your current development.

For an early-season spender, buying **one or two of these boxes** can make sense if the other available rewards are useful to your account. Beyond that point, the efficiency becomes much harder to justify unless you are specifically spending for short-term Season 1 power.

Cinders themselves still have value, but I would not make Cinder acquisition one of the central goals of an efficient Season 1 spending plan.

---

## GTArcade Shop — Usually Better Than Buying Blindly In-Game

If you are going to spend consistently, it is worth understanding how the **GTArcade shop** interacts with normal purchases. You are generally buying the same underlying game purchases, but spending through GTArcade can contribute toward **cumulative shop rewards**, and the shop also offers **vouchers and discounts**.

That means two players can effectively spend the same amount on the same type of progression while one receives additional value simply because of where the purchase was made. For someone who already knows they are going to spend, this is one of the easier efficiency improvements to make. You are not necessarily increasing your budget; you are trying to extract more from money you were already going to spend.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-204-1024x795.png)

The cumulative rewards are particularly relevant when you are making several purchases across a season. A single small purchase may not make the difference obvious, but repeated spending is where those additional rewards start to matter.

Before making larger purchases directly in-game, I would therefore check whether the equivalent purchase can be made through GTArcade and whether you currently have a useful voucher available.

---

## Seasonal Events and Zuma

The old guide placed the Stardust Lucky Spin at the very top of the Season 1 priority list. That recommendation should now be removed as **Stardust wheel is no longer the Season 1 opportunity it once was. The old system has been replaced by Zuma and seasonal events**, so there is no longer a reason to tell new spenders to build their entire Season 1 budget around the Stardust Wheel.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-205.png)

Seasonal events should instead be judged individually by their current rewards. Do not assume an event is efficient simply because it is limited or because the game presents it as a special opportunity. Look at what you are actually receiving and ask whether those materials contribute to progression you will still care about several seasons later.

For Season 1 in particular, broadly useful account resources are generally safer than paying heavily for temporary access to something you will eventually obtain much more cheaply.

Zuma Tower is a repeatable climbing event that uses **Zuma Visions** (the updated currency replacing Pearl of Finding). Each run begins at Floor 1 and continues until the player chooses to stop and claim rewards. Claiming rewards immediately ends the run and resets progress back to Floor 1.

Movement within the tower is determined by spending Zuma Visions on exploration attempts. Each attempt can:

- Move you up 1 or 2 floors
- Keep you on the same floor
- Drop you down 1 or 2 floors

Your **current floor at the moment you claim** determines the reward tier you receive. You do not earn rewards for every floor you pass, only for the final floor reached when claiming.

At its most basic level, Zuma Tower functions as a **currency conversion system**:

- **1 Zuma Vision ≈ 1 Stardust (minimum)**
- Worst-case outcome: spend 5 Zuma Visions → claim 5 Stardust

This establishes a hard floor value for the event. Even with extremely poor luck, players will not receive less than this baseline unless they overspend chasing higher floors. The cost of Safe Exploration rise quite significantly and as such it is generally not worth doing if you are after Stardust here. Climbing is for players who are after Castle skins.

- Farming **Crimsons**, do the first exploration then claim, repeat.
- If looking for **Stardust,**do the first exploration and then chance a free exploration – since levels 1 and 2 both holds 5 stardust you have nothing to lose! Claim 5 stardust or a bonus if you are lucky on the free attempt.

---

## Legendary Battle Pass — Relevant Later, Not a Season 1 Priority

Once you reach **Castle 40**, the Legendary Battle Pass becomes a different proposition. At that point your account direction is normally much clearer, and progression toward Holy, Shadow and eventually Chaos-related development starts becoming more relevant.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/image-206-1024x561.png)

For mid and higher spenders, the pass can offer good value because you are now buying resources that connect much more directly to your longer-term account plan.

For smaller spenders, however, there is no need to treat it as mandatory. If you are not yet developing the immortals or systems that benefit from those rewards, spending elsewhere can be more efficient.

This is one of the broader lessons of spending in Infinity Kingdom: **a good-value item is not automatically good value for your account right now**.

---

## Conclusion

Season 1 spending should be about building an account rather than buying a Season 1 march.

That distinction becomes increasingly important as Infinity Kingdom's event and shop systems change. The old Stardust Wheel priority is gone, Divine Well is now a much more expensive weekly proposition, and Cinders no longer fit neatly into the old Cinder Wish Shop recommendation.

The safest purchases are therefore the ones that remain useful regardless of where your account eventually goes. **Golden Path, sensible daily progression and taking advantage of GTArcade cumulative rewards and vouchers** are difficult to regret. More specialized spending should come after you understand what you actually intend to play.

For most light and mid spenders, spending a little less in Season 1 and keeping that budget available for Conquest is often better than trying to buy every early advantage.

Season 1 is temporary. Your account is not.

---

title: What to buy from in-game shops
summary: Whether you're a light spender or a whale, knowing where to spend your resources is key to efficient progression in Infinity Kingdom. This guide walks through all the day-to-day in-game shops and outlines what’s worth…
markdown:
## 🛒 Infinity Kingdom In-Game Shops Guide: What to Buy

Whether you're a light spender or a whale, knowing where to spend your resources is key to efficient progression in *Infinity Kingdom*. This guide walks through all the **day-to-day in-game shops** and outlines what’s worth your investment — and what isn’t. We are not going to cover all the standard bundles, since most of them are too expensive to consistently buy for normal players and you should buy from there only if you really need something. We are going to cover the in-game shops which are either free or very cheap and efficient.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-79.png)

---

## ⚔️ Arena Shop

The Arena Shop can be deceptive. While it offers a variety of items, almost all of them are bad value compared to other sources. The two standout exceptions are **Stardust**, which is always in demand for portait levels, and the big 2400 **Wind Dragon Crystals**, which are priced far more rare than other dragon shards. Even if you're not building Wind, it’s wise to collect these for potential future use or to save resources if you ever need Wind (especially with the new buff in patch 2.8.2). Small dragon crystal bundles here are a massive trap — they look tempting but offer extremely poor shard-per-cost ratios.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-80-1024x497.png)

### ✅ Buy:

- **Stardust** – A must-buy every time it appears.
- **Big Gold Bundle Wind Dragon Crystals** – Even if you’re not building Wind, these are great value.

### ❌ Avoid:

- **Other dragon crystals** – Horribly overpriced. For example, 40,000 arena coins may give you 800 shards vs. 6,000 in the Wind pack — over 7x less value.

---

## 🧭 Mysterium Shop

This shop rotates based on Mysterium progress and offers one of the few ways to get **Elite Artifacts (EAs)** without relying on luck or cash. If you're developing an Immortal that's missing their artifact, this should be your top priority.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-81-1024x509.png)

### ✅ Buy:

- **Elite Artifacts (EAs)** for Immortals you actively use.
- Only consider other items **after** you're done with EAs.

### ❌ Avoid:

- **Teleports on Main** – Use alt-account inventories for porting instead and CoR shop.

---

## 🔄 Triss Shop (Skill Recycle Shop)

This shop is critical for developing a strong march. It lets you recycle unwanted skills into a unique currency to buy top-tier ones. Since meta skills like *No Escape*, *Purify*, *Weakening Curse*, define competitive play, you should always prioritize these. Artifacts are a secondary option once your core builds are complete. Avoid using this shop to grab UAs unless in very niche cases like if you cannot obtain e.g. Trajan's elsewhere — they are often freely available from events and not worth the spend here.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-82-1024x534.png)

### ✅ Buy:

- **Top-tier Skills** only (e.g. *No Escape*, *Energy Burst*, etc.).
- **Artifacts only** if you’re done with key skills.

### ❌ Avoid:

- **Low-tier skills** – They offer no real advantage and waste your currency.

---

## 🛡️ Alliance Shop

Simple and essential: **Space Portals** are the only purchase that makes sense in this shop. These normally cost real money, but here you get them free just for contributing to alliance tech or donating during KVK. Even if you don’t currently need to teleport, having a stockpile means you’re ready for war, server merges, or emergency jumps. No other items in the shop come close in value.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-83-1024x553.png)

### ✅ Buy:

- **Space Portals** – Normally $5 each, totally free here with steady coin flow.

### ❌ Avoid:

- **Everything else** – Cost per value is significantly worse than the portals.

---

## 🌟 Golden Path Merit Shop

This shop is a jackpot for mid-to-late-game players. You earn merit through Golden Path missions and can use it for powerful Immortals, AP, dragons, Stardust, and even portals. **Dragon Castle Skins** like Mountain can offer great utility, while Immortals like **YSS** are excellent long-term investments. The shop is very flexible, making it great for plugging resource gaps. You can even buy **Stardust** here in a pinch. Frames and chat skins are purely aesthetic but available for collectors.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-84-1024x533.png)

### ✅ Buy:

- **Important Dragons** – Based on your team comp (Mountain is great early).
- **Core Immortals** – YSS, Trajan, etc.
- **Big AP Pots** – Excellent value for long-term farming or raids.
- **Space Portals** – Backup if you’re short elsewhere. Personally I like to obtain them here too as long as I am below my threshold. When I hit my count I collect only from Alliance shop etc.

### Optional:

- **Stardust** – Rare and useful but expensive pick here.
- **Frames & Chat Skins** – If you care about cosmetics.

### ❌ Avoid:

- **Artifacts here** – Usually more efficient to get elsewhere (Mysterium, Triss).

---

## 💠 Pearl Shop (Daily Purchase)

This is one of the game’s most flexible shops for spenders. You earn **Pearls** from spending and can convert them into valuable resources. **Sun and Power Crystals** are your best value here for building equipment. You can also grab **Dust**, which is rare and needed in large amounts. Occasionally, you can use Pearls to finish key Immortals (like grabbing a few shards for Alex to unlock his specialization). Avoid buying **keys** or **Shadow Crystals** unless you're spending heavily or chasing something specific. Personally I like to stack Pearls to buy Epic Dragon Chest Keys, but only while you are in dire need of crystals as you rapidly progress in e.g. season 1 and 2.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-85-1024x537.png)

### ✅ Buy:

- **Sun & Power Crystals** – Excellent cost efficiency for equipment growth.
- **Dust** – Needed for specializations; hard to farm.

### Optional:

- **Immortals** – Finish specific units if close.
- **Keys** – Only in progress stage.

### ❌ Avoid:

- **Shadow Crystals** – Overpriced for their value.

---

## 💎 VIP Shop

Reserved for long-term or heavy spenders, this shop lets you spend **VIP Points** on premium items. Most notably, it’s where you can unlock **Holy and Shadow Dragons**, but you’ll need to focus on one. Splitting between both is too expensive. Unless you’re a super whale, pick one and commit. Everything else in the shop is filler — some players grab epic chests during dragon rushes, but most regret it later. If you're under VIP 15, you may want to push VIP using gems slowly over time — it’s a long but worthwhile goal!

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-86-1024x532.png)

### ✅ Buy:

- **Holy or Shadow Dragon** – Best investment of your VIP points.  - **Holy Dragon** is top-tier, great synergy and power.
- **Shadow Dragon** has unique combos — niche but strong.

### ❌ Avoid:

- **Epic chests, gear, etc.** – Poor long-term value.
- **Trying to get both dragons** – Focus on one or you’ll stagnate.

### 🪙 VIP with Gems?

If you're not VIP 15 yet:

- Spending gems to reach VIP 15 over time is viable.
- Especially good in big alliances where you get lots of free VIP points.

---

## 🏪 Standard Gem Shop

The “default” gem shop looks like a place to grab quick resources — but in practice, it's just a price anchor. Almost everything here is full price and rarely worth it. Treat it as a reference point to know what’s **overpriced**, and only buy here in one situation: **using gems to push VIP level** when nearing milestones like VIP 15.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-87-1024x560.png)

### ❌ Avoid:

- **Everything** — It’s full price. You’ll find better deals almost anywhere else.

### ✅ Only exception:

- **VIP Points** – If you’re gem-pushing to hit VIP milestones.

title: What to Expect from the New Season 1 format (2.8.2)
summary: Disclaimer: New formats are not released yet and this is my best guess at how the new season 1 format will look.
markdown:
*Disclaimer: New formats are not released yet and this is my best guess at how the new season 1 format will look.*

As *Infinity Kingdom* transitions into a reworked **Season 1**, many players—especially veterans from early release servers—are wondering what has changed. The upcoming version of Season 1 appears to follow the framework of what has traditionally been known as **Season 2**, incorporating multiple new systems and content updates. Here's a breakdown of the key features and what players should prepare for.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-75-1024x576.png)

---

## 🆕 Major Changes in the New Season 1

### 🧙‍♂️ Level 50 Castle Cap

- The maximum castle level increases from 40 to **50**, allowing further progression.
- Players will need substantial **resources** and **speedups** to reach this new cap.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-77-1024x514.png)

Link to all **[building costs](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/development/buildings/castle-upgrade-costs/)** and **[requirements](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/development/buildings/castle-upgrade-requirements/)**.

### 🌀 Chaos Immortals

- All **Chaos-element Immortals** are available through the **Chaos Roulette**.
- Expect them to be **expensive**, priced similarly to how Holy Immortals were on release around 6-9K each depending on speed.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-78.png)

[**Chaos Roulette (2.6.9) - Wiki & Tools | Infinity Kingdom**](https://ik-wiki.com/docs/events/wheels-roulette/chaos-roulette-2-6-9/)

### ⚔️ Immortal Specializations

- Specialization system is added for **Immortals**, granting powerful stat boosts and effects.
- Players will need to collect large amounts of immortal fragments again - begin banking now!
- **Dragons do not get specializations** yet—that feature is introduced in Season 3.

### 💎 Artifact System

- **Elite Artifacts (EAs)** are available, much like in original Season 1.
- Slight improvement in accessibility via **more coins in Mysterium**, but not drastically easier.

### 📘 Skill System Updates

- No Chaos-element exclusive skills yet.
- **Well of Time** skill pool is refreshed or updated.
- Expect tweaks that bring some meta-shifting possibilities.

---

## 🎯 Event & Currency Changes

### 🌌 Galaxy & Theia Changes

- **Holy and Shadow Immortals** are available in the **Galaxy** shop—**A LOT cheaper** than Theia.
- This significantly lowers the cost for completing Holy/Shadow teams.
- Chaos Immortals remain tied to **Chaos Roulette**, with premium pricing.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/image-76.png)

### 👑 King of the Hill (KoH) Updates

- KoH now features **all GP heroes** (including strong options like YSS).
- These previously season-locked Immortals can now be obtained more flexibly.

### 🧭 Improved Event Rewards

- Rewards across events are **slightly better** than old Season 1, though not radically different.

---

## 🧰 Preparation Guide for Players

To prepare for the new Season 1 (Season 2-style), here’s what to focus on:

### Resource Banking

- Save **resources** and **speedups** for pushing to Castle 50.
- **AP (Action Points)** will be valuable for farming new equipment and events.
- Stockpile **EXP scrolls** for new Immortals and specialization leveling.
- Stockpile Enchanted Stones for new levels on Equipment.

### Currency Management

- Save up and bank **Galaxy Crystal Balls**: Save for Holy and Shadow Immortals.
- Spending funds: Prepare for **Chaos Roulette** if aiming for Chaos units.

### Progression

- Aim to reach **Castle 40** before the season update.
- Maximize **tech upgrades**, and build strong **dragon levels** and **equipment** setups.
- **T5 troops** are expected, so complete that progression path where possible.

---

## 💬 Current Meta Snapshot

- **Pure Earth teams** remain strong and popular (e.g., Fu Fei, Alex, Charles).
- **Mixed marches** are still viable, especially for mid-tier or flexible strategies.
- **Whales** dominate with full Chaos setups, but aren’t the only meta-defining option.
- **Apollo specialization** is notable among top players.

---

## 📌 Final Notes

- Transitioning into the new Season 1 may come with **uncertainty**—some players report conflicting info about jump mechanics or update timing.
- As always, **stockpile strategically** and **adapt early** to seize advantages.
- Expect more clarity once the season actually goes live or patch notes are officially released.

title: Which Chaos Immortal Carry to get going from Conquest into Legendary
summary: The seasonal discount chests have changed an important decision for players progressing through Conquest. With Apollo and Medusa both available for 250 Grails, these Immortals are no longer choices reserved almost…
categoryPath: Season Progression - Everything you need to know before a new season
markdown:
![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-26-1024x839.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-27-1024x810.png)

## Apollo or Medusa? What Conquest Players Should Build for Legendary Season

The seasonal discount chests have changed an important decision for players progressing through Conquest. With **Apollo and Medusa both available for 250 Grails**, these Immortals are no longer choices reserved almost entirely for the biggest spenders. A patient mid-spender can realistically build one of them, which naturally leads to the question I have been hearing more often lately: **Should I build Apollo or Medusa?**

If we were only talking about Conquest, my answer would be Apollo. He is easier to get working with the skills available during those seasons and can be remarkably difficult to deal with when built properly.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-28-1024x608.png)

The problem is that Conquest does not last forever.

After Conquest P5 you move into Legendary Season, where the Tower of Knowledge gains another set of skills. One of those skills, **Eternal Battlelust**, changes the comparison considerably. It gives Medusa exactly the kind of scaling she needs to turn from a good Conquest Immortal into one of the more frightening damage dealers available in Legendary.

For someone deciding where to spend 250 Grails today, I therefore wouldn't make the decision based only on which Immortal is strongest in the season you are currently playing. You also need to think about where that investment leaves you several seasons from now.

## Why Apollo Is So Good in Conquest

There is a reason Apollo is tempting.

His ultimate, **Corona Godstrike**, deals physical damage to all enemies at a **750% Damage Rate** when fully upgraded and has a 70% chance to reduce their healing effect by 30% for six seconds. Each time he casts his ultimate, he also gains a stack of Light Blessing, reducing the damage he takes by 10%, stacking up to three times.

With Apollo's exclusive artifact effect active, Corona Godstrike receives another **30% increased damage**.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-29-1024x543.png)

That gives him an unusual combination for a damage dealer. He can pressure the entire enemy march while gradually becoming harder to remove as the fight develops. He doesn't need an elaborate Legendary-only setup before he starts doing his job either, which is an important distinction when we're talking about players still moving through Conquest.

I would run **Energy Mastery** with him. Getting Apollo through his ultimate cycle quickly allows Corona Godstrike to begin applying pressure while building his Light Blessing stacks at the same time. In practice, I've seen him remain extremely effective even when facing **Knife Through Butter** setups that should, on paper, make life uncomfortable for him.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-30-1024x547.png)

This is also where Apollo has a real advantage for a mid-spender. You can build him during Conquest and actually make use of the investment immediately. You aren't buying an Immortal today while waiting several seasons for the pieces that make him relevant.

If your only concern were winning during Conquest, I would be quite comfortable recommending Apollo.

## So Why Do I Recommend Medusa?

Because the question changes once Legendary Season enters the picture.

Medusa is already a capable physical damage dealer, but her real ceiling becomes much easier to reach when Legendary Tower of Knowledge skills enter the game. The important one is **Eternal Battlelust**, and understanding what it does explains most of my reasoning here.

At level 8, Eternal Battlelust reads:

> Upon entering battle, each instance of passive damage or triggered skill damage increases physical damage by 5% and reduces damage taken by 1%, stacking up to 20 times.

At full stacks, we are therefore looking at up to **100% increased physical damage** alongside **20% damage reduction**.

Now look at Medusa's own ultimate.

## Gaze of Silence and Eternal Battlelust

Medusa's **Gaze of Silence** contains both a passive and an active component. Its passive deals **600% physical damage to all enemies every six seconds**, with damage against targets carrying Mark of Revenge increased by another 30%.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-26-1024x839.png)

Its active component removes all debuffs from Medusa and attempts to petrify all enemies for three seconds with a 70% success rate. Targets that resist the petrification receive **Mark of Revenge** instead.

With Medusa's exclusive artifact effect, the duration of Mark of Revenge from Gaze of Silence is extended by another three seconds.

What matters here is how naturally her damage profile works with Eternal Battlelust. Medusa repeatedly produces the kind of passive damage that allows the Legendary skill to build its stacks, and as those stacks accumulate, her physical damage continues climbing while she simultaneously becomes more resistant to incoming damage.

The result is very different from simply giving a damage dealer another offensive skill.

You are building a feedback loop around the way Medusa already fights.

Her passive damage helps develop Eternal Battlelust. Eternal Battlelust makes subsequent physical damage increasingly dangerous. Gaze of Silence continues hitting the entire enemy march, while its petrification and Mark of Revenge mechanics create additional pressure of their own.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-31.png)

Once the march has had enough time to develop those stacks, Medusa can become an absolute damage machine.

## The Important Catch: You Need Eternal Battlelust

There is one warning I would attach to any recommendation of Medusa, particularly for players working with a limited budget.

**Do not plan around Legendary Medusa without also planning for Eternal Battlelust.**

Buying Medusa from the discounted seasonal chest is only one part of the investment. Eternal Battlelust is a Legendary Tower of Knowledge skill, so players approaching the end of Conquest should start thinking ahead about the resources required to unlock and develop it.

That means saving **Wishing Well coins or Skill Stones** rather than arriving in Legendary with Medusa ready but no way to build the skill that makes the setup so powerful.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-32-1024x471.png)

This matters because 250 Grails can make Medusa herself look surprisingly affordable. In reality, the complete Legendary build requires more preparation than the chest price suggests.

Apollo is considerably more forgiving in that respect. He can make good use of Energy Mastery and the skill pool already available during Conquest, whereas Medusa's long-term recommendation assumes you are prepared to make the additional Legendary investment.

## What the Battle Reports Are Showing

The reason I'm comfortable recommending this path isn't based solely on reading the skill descriptions.

We've also been looking at actual Medusa marches being used in Legendary, including a **Medusa, Alexander the Great, Anubis and Fu Fei** setup with Demeter (thanks to play Money for giving insight on this performance). The march is still a work in progress rather than a completely finished T9 build, yet it has already reached the elimination rounds in Legendary and has been able to take consecutive Tower fights without refreshing.

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-33-1024x472.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-34-1024x472.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-35-1024x472.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-36-1024x472.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-37-1024x472.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-38-1024x472.png)

![](https://ik-wiki.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-39-1024x472.png)

That is important context.

A finished whale march proving that Medusa works would tell us very little about whether she is a sensible investment for the players asking this question. Seeing the setup perform while it is still being developed is much more useful, because those are exactly the circumstances many Conquest players will find themselves in when they first enter Legendary.

The player testing the march also described **Eternal Battlelust as essential to Medusa's success in Legendary**, which lines up with what the mechanics suggest. His advice to players still in Conquest was essentially the same conclusion I've reached: build Medusa gradually during Conquest, then have enough resources saved to obtain Eternal Battlelust as soon as Legendary opens.

## Apollo Is Still the Better Immediate Investment

None of this suddenly makes Apollo a bad choice. In fact, there is a slightly awkward truth behind the whole comparison. Apollo is probably the better Immortal for many players at the exact moment they are being asked to choose. A player in early Conquest may have several seasons ahead before Legendary. Apollo can provide value throughout that period without asking you to reserve resources for a Legendary skill that you cannot even access yet. For someone primarily interested in immediate results, that matters.

**Medusa is the recommendation because we're looking further ahead.** If you're in Conquest P1, for example, Apollo could potentially serve you extremely well for several seasons. There is nothing wrong with choosing him if those seasons are your priority. What I would avoid is spending 250 Grails on Apollo simply because he looks stronger today without considering what happens once your account crosses into Legendary.

For mid-spenders especially, these decisions tend to stay with the account for a long time. You cannot approach every discounted Chaos Immortal as though another 250 Grails will be waiting whenever the meta changes.

## Which One Should You Build?

For players who want the simplest answer, I would separate the decision by timeframe. **If your priority is Conquest performance right now, Apollo is the stronger and easier choice.** Build around Energy Mastery and he can become a very effective battlefield Immortal without requiring access to the Legendary skill pool. **If you are choosing one Immortal as a longer-term investment through Conquest and into Legendary, I would build Medusa.** You may have to be patient with her. Apollo can look like the better purchase while both accounts are still sitting in Conquest, and depending on where you are in the progression cycle, he may remain the better performer for several seasons.

Once Eternal Battlelust becomes available, however, the reason for investing in Medusa starts to become clear. That is why my recommendation for players currently working their way through Conquest is to **slow-build Medusa, prepare her for Legendary, and start banking the resources needed for Eternal Battlelust before you get there**.

The 250-Grail seasonal chest makes the Immortal much more accessible. Planning ahead is what turns that opportunity into a march you can continue using after Conquest is over.

## Final Thoughts

Apollo and Medusa being available for only 250 Grails is a significant opportunity for mid-spenders, but I wouldn't treat the two purchases as interchangeable. Apollo gives you more immediate value and is arguably the better pure Conquest choice. Medusa asks for more patience and another major investment once Legendary begins, but the arrival of Eternal Battlelust changes her potential enough that I believe she is currently the better long-term project.

For a player with unlimited resources, there is no real dilemma: build both and use whichever fits the season and march you are playing. For everyone else, the decision deserves a longer view.

Personally **every single day I make sure to spend 250 Grails progressing with Legendary season in mind (despite being in conquest) hence, I spend my chests on Medusa fragments — and I am saving during Wisdom Well events for Eternal Battlelust once I land on Legendary.**
